note: Per-organism visual audit: 141 subagents each OPENED the exported portraits and judged them against the reference row. Covers every non-quadruped organism; the 141 quadruped-routed mammals were excluded because wave 4/5 was rewriting them.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon ant, or a green-bottle fly larva toy — not a cockroach
rows.defect: It is three bright cyan spheres strung in a row (head-ball, thorax-ball, abdomen-ball) with six thin straight sticks poked into the underside. Every mustRead is missing: there are no flat glossy oval wing-covers (just one small pale ellipse pasted on the rear ball's shoulder, floating clear of the outline), no shield-shaped pronotum — the head is a fully separate ball with a big cartoon white-highlight eye completely exposed — and the antennae are three stiff straight rods, not two long backswept threads. The leg/body joins are hard seams: the sticks terminate at the sphere edge with no taper, no coxa, no muscle. Measured silhouette is roughly 1.8:1, not the 2.5 called for, and the colour is a saturated aquarium teal, nothing like a roach's chestnut gloss.
rows.fix: Kill the bead-chain: merge thorax and abdomen into one continuous flattened dorsal shell whose outline is a single unbroken curve, and drop a wide shield pronotum forward over the head so the head is hidden from above. Overlay two long glossy tegmina meeting on a centreline seam that runs the full body length. Replace the three rods with two threadlike antennae longer than the body, curving back over the shell. Legs must emerge from swollen coxal bases inside the shell outline and taper with a visible femur/tibia break plus spines. Recolour to dark chestnut/oxblood with a specular sheen.

rows.readsAs: a tick or a fat orange spider with two seed-pods for pincers
rows.defect: An apricot-coloured smooth oval with faint blotches, flanked by two thin dark stick-legs per side and two claws that are plain tapered ovals with a small hooked notch cut in the tip. The claws are identical in size — the mustRead demands one much larger — and both are visibly stuck ON: they float beside the body with a clear gap and no shoulder, merus or joint linking them. Legs are 2px-wide bent lines with kinked elbows, the opposite of 'long heavy armoured legs'; they do span wide but read as spider legs. No calcified abdomen tucked under is drawn at all, and the two eyes are white pinheads on straight wire stalks rising out of nothing. There is no carapace texture, no segmentation, no shell plates — the body is a lit gradient ball.
rows.fix: Rebuild the claws as a chunky three-segment chelipeds (merus, carpus, propodus) growing out of the carapace edge with overlapping plates at each joint; make the left one roughly 1.6x the right. Thicken the walking legs to armoured segments with visible articulation rings and dactyl tips. Give the carapace a hard ridged outline with a transverse cervical groove and pitted calcified texture instead of the fruit gradient. Add the folded abdomen tucked under the rear of the carapace. Seat the eyestalks in orbital notches on the carapace front margin.

rows.readsAs: a generic aquarium tetra or minnow
rows.defect: A pure lens shape — two symmetric arcs meeting in sharp points at both nose and tail-root — in flat aquarium teal. Two of the three mustReads fail outright: there is NO chin barbel anywhere, and there are only TWO dorsal humps (faint translucent lobes) instead of three separate dorsal fins. A pale line does run the flank, but it is dead straight, not the cod's distinctive high-arched lateral line. The fins are all soft translucent blobs laid over the body with no ray structure and no attachment — the pectoral is a grey smudge, the tail is a detached fan sitting behind a pinched point. Aspect measures about 2.4:1 against the 3.9 called for, so it is far too deep-bodied, and the snout is pointed where a cod's is blunt with a heavy overhung upper jaw.
rows.fix: Stretch to ~3.9:1 and round the snout into a blunt overhung jaw. Hang a single stiff barbel from the chin. Replace the two humps with three discrete dorsal fins separated by clear gaps, and add two anal fins beneath. Arch the lateral line up over the pectoral then down. Give every fin visible rays and a fleshy base that merges into the body wall rather than a translucent overlay. Recolour to mottled olive-brown over a pale belly.

rows.readsAs: the Cod from this same batch, painted grey — a spotted generic fish
rows.defect: This is the Cod render recoloured — the identical lens outline, the identical two translucent dorsal humps, the identical detached fan tail, the identical eye — now pale blue-grey with grey blotches. All three mustReads fail. There are no fleshy lobed fins on muscular stalks; the fins are flat translucent paddles with no stalk at all. The tail is a plain single fan, not three-lobed and with no central spike. The scales are absent — the blotches are soft airbrushed grey circles sprayed on top of a smooth gradient, with no scale relief and none of the white flecking on steel-blue. Body depth is far too shallow for a coelacanth's deep muscular trunk.
rows.fix: Break the shared fish template. Build each paired fin as a thick muscular lobe growing out of the body wall, with the fin web only on its distal end. Rebuild the tail as an upper lobe, a lower lobe, and a small separate central spike between them. Deepen the trunk and give it a heavy rounded head with bony plates. Replace the sprayed blotches with overlapping rough cosmoid scales, each catching a small white speck of light.

rows.readsAs: a green ant with a cocklebur stuck to its back — and structurally the same creature as the Cockroach in this batch
rows.defect: The Cockroach render's exact construction reused in mint green: same three spheres in a row, same stick legs, same cartoon eye — with short yellow-green bristles radiating in a spiky sunburst from the middle ball. Two mustReads fail: the body is a bright pale mint, the opposite of a 'stout dark heat-absorbing body', and the insulating hair is a ring of separate straight spikes standing off the silhouette like a burr, not dense fur that reads as a coat. Wings are absent, which is correct. The abdomen ball meets the thorax ball with a visible hard tangent seam, and the legs are unarticulated wires.
rows.fix: Recolour to near-black/sooty brown so the heat-absorbing read lands. Replace the spike ring with a dense pile that softens and thickens the outline itself — fur must change the silhouette, not sit outside it. Fuse the thorax and abdomen into one continuous body with a waisted pinch rather than two tangent balls, and thicken the legs with visible femur/tibia joints and hairs.

rows.readsAs: a bare autumn bonsai tree or a dead shrub
rows.defect: The colour is flatly wrong: the whole colony is warm amber-orange over chocolate-brown trunks, exactly the tropical palette the note forbids for an azooxanthellate coral that must be bone-white to pale pink. The second mustRead also fails — there are no cup-shaped polyps at the branch tips; the tips just fade out into hairline twigs, and the only pink elements are a scatter of soft blurred dots clustered low around the trunks, i.e. sprayed on behind the structure rather than being polyps at the tips. The five near-parallel vertical trunks rising from a flat base and fanning into a fine twiggy crown read unmistakably as a bare winter tree.
rows.fix: Recolour the whole colony to chalk-white with faint pink flush and remove the brown entirely. Terminate every branch tip in a discrete calyx cup with visible septa and an extruded polyp crown, sized so they read at 440px. Make the branching irregular and dichotomous with thickened nodes at each fork instead of the smooth tapering tree limbs, and merge the trunks into one encrusting holdfast rather than five parallel poles on a flat floor. Delete the loose pink dot cloud.

rows.readsAs: a dark silhouette of a generic fish — at a glance, nearly nothing
rows.defect: The same lens template again, this time in a near-black slate that is barely separable from the background — the image is almost invisible at 440px. Two mustReads fail: the snout is a sharp point, not a blunt rounded snout, and there is no chin barbel. The dorsal fin is a ghost — a faint dark smear above the back with no rays and no discernible edge — and the tail is a small dark triangular notch that is neither clearly forked nor connected; it sits behind a pinched point with a visible gap. The body is not a stout torpedo, it is a flat two-arc lens with sharp bow and stern. Only the white eye ring and one straight pale lateral line have any contrast.
rows.fix: Raise the value of the whole fish well clear of the background and give it a pale belly for tonal separation. Round the snout and add the chin barbel. Round out the ventral profile into an actual torpedo instead of a symmetric lens. Draw the dorsal as a solid soft-rayed fin with a fleshy base, and rebuild the tail as an unmistakably forked caudal joined to the body by a thickened peduncle.

rows.readsAs: a small jellyfish with a striped bell
rows.defect: It reads as a jellyfish, which the note explicitly forbids. The body is a teal DOME — flat-bottomed with a domed top, the classic medusa bell — and two long thin tentacles trail down from its lower corners well past the body, which is precisely the 'stinging trailing tentacles' that must not be there. The jelly is also opaque saturated teal rather than transparent; you cannot see through it at all. The comb rows are painted as flat vertical stripes of pure hue (yellow, green, magenta, cyan) sitting on the surface like decals — the colour bands are sprayed on rather than being refracted light off beating plates, and they run straight down without following the body's curvature into the ends. I count roughly ten stripes across the visible face, and the two outermost 'combs' are separate stiff sticks standing clear of the silhouette.
rows.fix: Change the body to a true ovoid/egg — rounded at BOTH ends, no flat bottom, no bell margin — and delete the two trailing tentacles entirely. Make the jelly genuinely translucent: let the background darkness and the far-side comb rows show through it. Rebuild the combs as eight meridional rows of discrete short paddle plates that wrap the curvature and converge at both poles, each plate carrying a small iridescent spectral glint rather than a full-length flat stripe. Add the faint internal pharynx mass and the apical statocyst.

rows.readsAs: A generic green pond fish — most people would say piranha, tetra or a cartoon goldfish, not a carp.
rows.defect: No barbels anywhere — the mouth is a plain drawn smile line with nothing hanging from the corners, so the single most diagnostic carp feature is absent. The dorsal is a short dark triangular flap sitting on the shoulder, not a long fin running most of the back, and it meets the body along a hard straight seam with a colour step. The caudal fin is a separate flat triangle floating behind the body with a visible gap of dark background between it and the peduncle — the tail is not connected to the fish. Body is far too short and deep: the flank measures roughly 230x130 px, ~1.7 aspect against the specified 2.8, giving a disc-shaped panfish. Skin is a smooth green gradient with one thin lighter lateral line and no scale structure at all.
rows.fix: Grow two pairs of barbels out of the mouth corners (a short upper pair, a longer drooping lower pair) as tapered curves that start inside the lip silhouette. Extend the dorsal into a long low-arched fin spanning ~60% of the back, blended into the dorsal ridge with a soft ramp instead of a hard triangle base. Reattach the caudal: extend the body taper into the peduncle so the fin roots inside the flank outline with no background gap. Stretch the body to ~2.6-2.8 aspect and add overlapping scale rows that follow the flank curvature rather than a single painted stripe.

rows.readsAs: A blue ladybird or a generic cartoon beetle — nothing in the picture says carrion beetle.
rows.defect: Colour is completely wrong: the elytra are a uniform periwinkle-blue gradient with no black-and-orange blotching, so the warning pattern that defines the species is missing entirely. The antennae are missing — the head carries only two dots for eyes and nothing projecting forward, so there are no clubbed knobs. The abdomen tip is not exposed; the elytra cover the whole rear and end in a smooth closed curve. The legs are six thin grey hairline arcs that float clear of the body outline with a gap between the leg and the pronotum — they read as scratch marks, not limbs, and they have no joints, tarsi or thickness taper. The head/pronotum is a separate dark rounded blob stacked on top of the elytra with a hard crescent seam where the two overlap. Elytra silhouette is a plain egg with a single ruler-straight vertical line down the middle for the suture.
rows.fix: Repaint the elytra with irregular black and orange transverse blotches that follow the wing-cover curvature. Add antennae growing out of the front of the head with a thin scape and a distinct 3-4 segment club at the tip. Shorten the elytra so two or three pale abdominal tergites show past the rear edge. Rebuild the legs as tapering jointed limbs (femur/tibia/tarsus) rooted inside the body outline. Blend the pronotum into the elytra with a shared shading ramp instead of a stacked overlapping blob, and break the perfectly straight suture line into a slightly irregular seam.

rows.readsAs: A teal songbird or a crested quail chick — closest to the small birds elsewhere in the set, not a cassowary.
rows.defect: All three mustReads are absent. There is no bony casque — the head carries a small spiky teal feather crest, the kind used for a cockatiel or hoopoe. The neck is the same teal as the body with no vivid blue and no red wattles hanging from it. The plumage is a smooth glossy teal gradient with a large inset oval wing patch outlined by a hard dark line, not black hair-like shaggy feathers. The beak is a tiny orange cone about a third the length a cassowary bill needs. The legs are two thin uniform-width yellow sticks with no thigh mass, no scaling and no dagger claw, and they meet the body belly at a bare butt-join with no feathered thigh transition. Body reads as a small perching bird, not a 60kg ratite.
rows.fix: Add a tall keratin casque rising from the top of the skull, blended into the crown. Recolour the neck to saturated blue with a violet nape and hang two red wattles from the throat. Replace the smooth teal body fill and inset wing oval with matted black hair-like plume strokes so no hard wing outline survives. Thicken and lengthen the legs into grey scaled ratite legs with visible thigh mass rooted under body feathering and a large inner claw. Bulk the torso and drop the tail to a stub.

rows.readsAs: A barracuda or a mackerel — a sleek pointy-nosed pelagic fish, definitely not a catfish.
rows.defect: No barbels at all. In their place there is a detached dark oval blob floating in front of the snout, completely separated from the head by background — an off-body artifact that reads as a bubble or a rendering error, not whiskers. The head is a narrow pointed cone, the opposite of the broad flattened head required, and the eye sits at the very tip of the snout. No stiff leading spine on the dorsal or pectoral — the dorsal is a soft dark triangular flap laid on the back with a hard straight base seam and a colour step, and the pectoral is a small translucent triangle stuck flat on the flank with no root. Body is a smooth cyan lens shape with a machined straight lateral line running the full length; the caudal is a flat forked wedge with a hard join line at the peduncle.
rows.fix: Delete the floating oval and grow four to eight barbels out of the lip and chin, tapering and drooping, rooted inside the head silhouette. Widen and flatten the head into a broad shovel with the eyes set high and back on the skull, then narrow into the trunk. Give the dorsal and pectorals a thick pale leading ray drawn as a stiff spine, and blend all fin bases into the body with a soft ramp rather than a straight-edged triangle sitting on top. Break the perfectly straight lateral line into a slight curve that follows the flank.

rows.readsAs: A maggot, grub or witchetty larva — or literally a string of pearls. Nobody would say cricket.
rows.defect: This is not an insect. The picture is a horizontal row of about nine overlapping perfect cream-white spheres with a single dark round eye disc at the right end. There are no legs of any kind, so the hugely long folded hind legs are absent. There are no antennae, so the whip antennae longer than the body are absent. There is no humped arched back — the spheres form a level tube with a flat top. No head capsule, no thorax/abdomen division, no mandibles, no tarsi. Every segment is a mathematically perfect circle, the clearest possible case of a geometric primitive stack. The one eye is a flat brown disc with a white dot pasted on the last sphere.
rows.fix: Rebuild from scratch as a cricket: distinct head capsule, humped thorax rising well above the head, abdomen tapering down and back so the dorsal line is a strong arch. Add two whip antennae growing from between the eyes at 1.5-2x body length, six jointed legs rooted under the thorax, and a pair of enormous folded hind legs with a bulged femur above the body line and a long thin tibia angled back past the abdomen. Replace the circle stack with irregular tergite plates whose widths vary along the body.

rows.readsAs: An orange minnow or a small goldfish/killifish — a perfectly ordinary sighted surface fish.
rows.defect: It has an eye. A white sclera ring with a black pupil sits at the front of the head, directly contradicting the eyeless smooth head mustRead. The flesh is opaque saturated amber-orange with a dark brown dorsal saddle — not pale pink, not translucent, and no internal organs, spine or gut are visible anywhere. So two of three mustReads fail outright. The dorsal is a dark brown triangular patch laid on the back with a hard boundary that reads as sprayed-on colour rather than a fin growing out of the ridge; the caudal is a separate brown fan whose base meets the pale body at an abrupt colour step with no blending. The snout is drawn out to a long straight needle point.
rows.fix: Remove the eye entirely and close the socket into smooth continuous skin with a faint depression where the orbit would be. Recolour the whole body to a pale pink-white with translucency: let a darker spine line, gill mass and gut shadow show through the flank. Reshape the snout from a needle into a blunt rounded cave-fish head. Root the dorsal and caudal into the body with a soft value ramp instead of a hard brown patch edge.

rows.readsAs: A frog — but a cartoon garden frog or common toad, with nothing to say cave-dwelling.
rows.defect: It reads as a frog, which is the one thing working here, but the skin fails the pale translucent depigmented mustRead: it is a saturated mint-green gradient carrying a scatter of dark grey-green round spots that sit flatly on the surface with no shading interaction, reading as sprayed-on decal dots rather than the animal's own pigment. The hind legs are two flat dark paddle shapes splayed horizontally out of each side of the body — they meet the torso at a hard outline with a visible seam, have no thigh or shank mass and no folded knee, and they read as leaves stuck on rather than folded hind legs. Front limbs are two tiny pale nubs poking below the belly with no arms attached to them. Body is a near-perfect circle and the eyes are two perfect circles with perfect circular pupils.
rows.fix: Desaturate the skin to a pale translucent pinkish-white and let a hint of internal shadow show through; if spots are kept, tint and shade them into the surface so they follow the body curvature. Rebuild the hind legs in profile: a thick femur folded up alongside the flank, tibia doubled back, foot forward, all rooted into the hip with continuous shading and no outline seam. Give the front limbs visible forearms from shoulder to the toes rather than floating nubs. Break the perfect circular torso into a slightly wider-than-tall squat body with a head as broad as the shoulders.

rows.readsAs: A cooked prawn or a crayfish — the right family, but the wrong animal and clearly a sighted surface species.
rows.defect: The glassy translucent colourless mustRead fails completely — the animal is solid opaque orange with brown speckles, the colour of a cooked prawn, and nothing shows through it. It also has a prominent eye: a black bead with a white specular highlight on the front of the carapace, against a spec calling for hidden eyes. The walking legs are three straight black hairlines with no thickness, no joints and no taper, hanging below the carapace and reading as pen scratches. The antennae are correct in length and sweep, and the curved segmented abdomen with tail fan does read, but the abdomen segments are drawn as a stack of near-identical crescents and the carapace is a plain smooth egg with no rostrum. Overall it is small in the frame and floats above a detached ellipse shadow.
rows.fix: Recolour to near-colourless glassy white with faint blue-grey edges, letting the gut line and muscle banding read through the cuticle. Remove or reduce the eye to a pale unpigmented stub with no black pupil and no highlight. Rebuild the pereiopods as jointed tapering limbs rooted under the carapace. Add a pointed serrated rostrum projecting forward from the carapace, and vary the abdominal segment sizes so they narrow toward the tail instead of repeating.

rows.readsAs: An ammonite fossil, or a coiled snail shell ornament
rows.defect: The shell is a flat planispiral coil — a nearly 2D disc of ribbed whorls spiralling to a central knob, seen face-on. There is no spire at all (mustRead 'knobby pointed spire' absent), no broad flared lip (mustRead absent; the only lip cue is a thin pale white outline arc on the right rim that reads as a highlight stroke, not a thickened flared aperture), and no eyes — the two long stalked eyes peering out from under the lip are entirely missing (mustRead absent, and the row calls for 'prominent' eyes). The one soft-body cue is a single dark rust blob at lower right that sits ON the shell as a separate overlapping ellipse with a hard edge — a stuck-on part, not a foot growing out of the aperture. Nothing crawls; there is no substrate contact. Aspect reads about 1.15 (roughly as tall as wide), not 1.5.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a conical gastropod, not a planispiral: draw a turreted spire climbing to the upper-left with 5-6 stepped whorls and knobby nodules on each shoulder, and a large body whorl at lower-right. Cut a real aperture on the right: a broad flared lip painted as a thickened, colour-shifted (pale pink/orange interior) sheet with its own inner shadow, not an outline stroke. Extend a muscular foot out of that aperture with the shell edge overlapping it (no separate ellipse), and grow two long eyestalks out of the foot from under the lip, each with a dark terminal eye. Kill the perfect-circle spiral geometry — vary whorl spacing and add erosion/growth-line noise.

rows.readsAs: A pigeon or a young gull
rows.defect: This is a small, plump, pale blue-white perching bird standing on a shadow, not a soaring condor. Every mustRead fails: the head is fully feathered, smooth and round with a neat glossy black bead eye and a short yellow finch/dove bill — no bare wrinkled unfeathered head; the wings are folded, rendered as a flat grey-outlined lens shape pasted onto the flank with a hard concentric ring where it meets the body — a visible stuck-on seam, and nowhere near 'huge plank-broad wings with splayed fingered primaries'; there is no white ruff at the neck base (the whole bird is white, so no ruff can read). Posture is 'flying' in the row but the render is standing on two thin yellow legs. Aspect reads about 1.4, not 2.4. The tail is a single flat grey wedge with a straight machined lower edge.
rows.fix: Redraw in flight, wings fully spread edge-to-edge across the canvas as broad rectangular planks with 6-7 separated, upcurved finger primaries at each tip. Paint the body near-black/sooty brown so the two required white marks read: a shaggy white ruff collar at the neck base and white underwing coverts along the leading edge. Replace the head: small, bare, wrinkled grey-pink skin with visible folds and a heavy hooked ivory bill, set on a naked neck. Delete the folded-wing lens decal and the perching legs; tuck the feet back against the tail.

rows.readsAs: A cyan rubber-duck / cartoon duckling
rows.defect: A bright turquoise-cyan cartoon duckling floating in a water ring, drawn tiny (occupies well under a fifth of the frame). mustRead 'sooty black rounded body' fails outright — the body is saturated teal with a glossy highlight. mustRead 'white bill running up into a white forehead shield' fails — the bill is a small orange-yellow triangle with no shield and no white anywhere. mustRead 'big lobed grey-green toes' fails — no feet are visible at all. The folded wing is a flat teal lens with a hard dark outline sitting on the flank as a decal, and the head-to-body junction is a plain overlap of two ovals with a visible edge. Head fraction reads about 0.28, larger than the 0.2 called for, which pushes it further toward duckling.
rows.fix: Recolour the whole bird to sooty charcoal-black with a slightly browner back, so the two white features carry the read. Replace the bill with a stubby white/ivory conical bill that continues unbroken up the forehead into a bulging white frontal shield above the eye line. Show at least one big lobed foot — grey-green toes with scalloped paddle flanges — either paddling below the waterline or raised. Blend the wing into the back with feather-tract brushwork instead of an outlined lens, and scale the bird up to roughly fill the frame.

rows.readsAs: A flea, or a Daphnia water flea
rows.defect: A lumpy purple two-lobed creature that reads as a flea or a water flea rather than a calanoid copepod. The body fails the mustRead 'teardrop wider at the front tapering back': it is widest at the REAR — a big bulbous sphere behind the head — so it tapers the wrong way, with a pinched waist and a visible seam line where the rear sphere overlaps the head lobe. mustRead 'long outstretched antennae as wide as the body is long' is only half met: there are three thin dark whiskers, all on the left, asymmetric and hair-thin, not a symmetric pair of long stiff outstretched first antennae. The forked bristly tail is present at lower right and is the one clearly correct feature. Contrary to the note, the eye is a single large glossy black bead with a catchlight sitting near the front of the head — it reads as a prominent insect eye, not a small median ocellus, and the row asks for 'small'. Several small legs hang below as separate stuck-on teardrops.
rows.fix: Reshape the prosome into one continuous teardrop: broadest just behind the head, tapering smoothly back into a narrow segmented urosome that ends in the caudal furca — remove the rear bulb and the waist seam. Draw one symmetric pair of first antennae sweeping straight out sideways, each as long as the body, thickened at the base where they emerge from the head and finely segmented along their length. Shrink the eye to a single small dark red-brown spot on the midline of the forehead (no white catchlight, no paired look). Add faint transverse segment lines across the prosome so the swimming legs read as growing from segment margins rather than being hung underneath.

rows.readsAs: A leafless bonsai or winter shrub
rows.defect: This reads as a bare winter shrub, not a stony coral colony. The branches are hair-thin, smooth, and taper to needle tips in a fine dendritic fan — the opposite of the mustRead 'rough calcified texture' and 'branching stony colony'; nothing is thick, blunt or chalky. mustRead 'surface covered in tiny cup-shaped polyps' is absent — there are a few soft pink smudges near the base but no cup/corallite structures anywhere on the branches. Worse, the fine canopy is separated from a set of five thick vertical grey pillars beneath it by a hard horizontal boundary: the twigs simply start where the pillars end, a blatant stuck-on seam between two unrelated structures, and those pillars read as tree trunks. Overall silhouette is a symmetric semicircular dome (canopy) on legs, which is a plant-family shape with decoration.
rows.fix: Thicken every branch by 3-4x and make them blunt-tipped and irregular so they read as calcium carbonate, not twigs; taper each branch continuously out of its parent so there is no junction line, and let the trunks fatten into the branches instead of butting against them. Stipple the entire surface with small ring/cup corallites — visible rims with darker centres, denser at the branch tips — as the colony's own texture, not an overlay. Break the symmetric dome: let branches grow at uneven lengths and angles, some fusing, and seat the base on rock rather than on five clean pillars.

rows.readsAs: A golden duck or a goose
rows.defect: A golden-yellow bird sitting low in a water ring — it is the same swimming-bird template as Coot in this batch, recoloured, so the two organisms collide directly. Posture is 'swimming', not the required upright heraldic pose, and mustRead 'wings held open to dry' fails completely: the wings are folded and painted as a flat tan lens decal with a hard dark contour where it meets the flank. mustRead 'hook-tipped bill' is not readable — the bill is a short blunt yellow wedge with only a tiny downturn, the same bill family as the Coot's. mustRead 'low-slung body with a stiff wedge tail' fails — there is no tail at all; the body ends in a plain rounded stern that dips under the water ring. The neck is long-ish and S-curved, the only mustRead partly satisfied, but it is a smooth tube overlapping the body with a visible junction line. The all-over golden colour is wrong for a cormorant, which should be near-black.
rows.fix: Stand the bird upright on a rock, body horizontal and low, and spread both wings wide and stiff in the classic drying pose — separate flight feathers visible, wings rotated forward, drawn growing out of the shoulder with covert feathering blending into the back. Add a long stiff wedge tail of a dozen straight rectrices projecting behind. Recolour to oily blackish-bronze with a yellow-orange gular patch at the bill base only. Rebuild the bill as long and slender with a distinct downward hook at the tip. Remove the water ring and the shared swimming-duck body so it no longer duplicates Coot.

rows.readsAs: An earthworm, or a cartoon snake ring
rows.defect: The body is a near-perfect flat torus — a machined doughnut ring of uniform thickness with a clean circular hole in the middle — and it is finely ribbed with close-set transverse segment lines, so it reads as an earthworm rather than a snake. mustRead 'blocky triangular pit-viper head much wider than the neck' fails badly: the head is a small rounded oval, if anything NARROWER than the ring it sits on, with no jaw angles, no pit, and no brow. It is also visibly stuck on — a discrete lighter oval overlapping the end of the ring with a hard boundary line, not a neck tapering into a skull. mustRead 'white mouth lining shown in a gape' is entirely absent: the mouth is closed, only a thin forked red tongue pokes out. mustRead 'thick heavy-bodied build' is nominally there but reads as constant-diameter tubing, not a muscular body that thickens mid-length and tapers to a tail — no tail is visible anywhere. The body has no pattern: a couple of faint darker smudges, no crossbands.
rows.fix: Break the torus: coil the snake in overlapping, uneven loops with one loop crossing over another, the diameter swelling through the mid-body and tapering to a thin pointed tail that shows. Replace the ribbing with overlapping scale texture (larger keeled dorsal scales, broad ventral scutes on the underside of the visible loops) and paint dark hourglass crossbands with jagged edges as the animal's own pigment. Rebuild the head as a broad blunt wedge, clearly wider than the neck, with a heavy brow ridge over a vertical-slit eye, a loreal pit between eye and nostril, and a sharp cheek-to-neck constriction so it grows out of the body. Open the jaws to about 130 degrees and paint the interior chalk-white with a visible glottis and fangs.

rows.readsAs: A speckled blue bird's egg, or a smooth river pebble
rows.defect: A featureless blue-violet ellipse floating on a drop shadow — a pure geometric primitive with a thin pale rim highlight. The glossy egg-smooth no-spire shell (mustRead) is technically satisfied, but that is the only one. mustRead 'long toothed slit running the length of the underside' fails: there is a row of five small round dark dots across the upper face, which read as spots of pigment, not as an aperture, and they are on the top, not the underside, and they have no slit and no teeth. mustRead 'patterned mantle flaps folding up over the shell' is entirely absent — no mantle, no papillae, no soft tissue of any kind. There is no foot, no head, no tentacles, and no eyes despite the row asking for small eyes, and nothing is crawling: the shell hovers over a detached shadow with no substrate contact. The mottled blue cloudiness reads as sprayed-on airbrush noise rather than the shell's own patterning.
rows.fix: Rotate to a three-quarter view so the underside is visible and cut a real aperture: a long narrow slit running nearly the full shell length, curved, with a row of fine interlocking teeth on BOTH lips, painted with interior shadow so it is a hole and not a line. Extend a broad cream foot from that slit onto a substrate, with a head and two slender tentacles at the front. Bring two patterned mantle flaps up over the left and right flanks, meeting near the dorsal midline with a visible gap between them, edged with branched papillae and carrying a different pattern from the shell beneath. Replace the airbrushed cloud with crisp shell markings that follow the shell's growth curvature, and break the perfect ellipse — the anterior and posterior ends should be slightly beaked and asymmetric.

rows.readsAs: a generic turquoise cartoon songbird / a stylized kingfisher — not a corvid of any kind
rows.defect: All three mustRead features are absent. The bill is a short STRAIGHT yellow wedge, not a slender down-curved red bill. The legs are yellow, not bright red. The plumage is bright turquoise/cyan with a paler cyan wing-disc, not glossy all-black — so nothing about the bird says corvid. On top of the ID failure the wing is a flat lens-shaped cyan disc laid on the flank with a hard dark outline around it (a decal, not a folded wing), and the tail is a thin flat dark spike that meets the body at a hard straight seam with no covert transition. Head is a near-perfect circle joined to a near-perfect ellipse body — a two-ball snowman silhouette.
rows.fix: Recolor plumage to near-black with blue-green gloss sheen highlights only (keep the iridescence in the specular, not the base). Replace the straight bill primitive with a long slender decurved bill, ~1.2x head length, in saturated red; recolor legs/feet red. Grow the wing out of the shoulder as a layered feather group with scapular overlap instead of an outlined disc, and blend the tail base into the rump coverts so there is no seam.

rows.readsAs: a pale ant or a termite alate — most people would say 'ant'
rows.defect: The defining feature is missing: there are no broad transparent veined wings tented over the back. The only thing behind the head is a small pale opaque teardrop lobe overlapping the rear sphere — no venation, no transparency, no roof-shaped tent, and it is narrower than the body. The body is two nearly perfect pale spheres in a row plus a small head sphere, so it reads as a three-ball ant, not a short stout barrel. Head is not blunt-and-wide with eyes at the corners — it is a small round ball with one dark ellipse eye on the side. Legs are six uniform straight grey sticks of identical thickness with no femur/tibia taper and no tarsal feet; they attach at hard points on the sphere. Two long thin antennae are drawn, but cicadas have tiny bristle antennae — these read as ant/wasp antennae.
rows.fix: Fuse the two abdominal spheres into one tapering barrel (wide at the thorax, bluntly rounded at the tip) with visible tergite banding. Widen and flatten the head, push two large eyes to its outer corners, and shrink the antennae to short bristles. Add the actual wings: two pairs of long translucent membranes with a branching vein network, angled ~30 degrees down each side into a roof over the abdomen and extending past its tip. Give the legs jointed segments with thicker femora.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon sunfish or an angelfish — and it is geometrically the SAME asset as the Clownfish in this batch, only recolored
rows.defect: The dorsal fin is a strip of five hard grey triangular sawteeth sitting ON TOP of the back as a separate shape with a visible straight baseline seam — it does not grow out of the body, it is a paper crown laid on. It also covers only the front half of the back, so the required single long dorsal that runs spiny-then-soft to the caudal peduncle is missing. The caudal fin is a flat opaque grey circular-sector paddle butted against the body at a hard vertical edge with no peduncle at all, and it is a machined arc, not a fin with rays or pointed trailing tips. The vertical bars are evenly spaced identical translucent stripes airbrushed over the flank, clearly sprayed on rather than pigment in the scales. No thick-lipped sloping face — the head is an unbroken smooth curve with a cartoon white-and-black dot eye and a small etched pectoral scribble. Body is much rounder than called for; measured aspect is roughly 1.6, not 2.4.
rows.fix: Replace the sawtooth strip with one continuous dorsal whose membrane emerges from the back contour: hard rays with pointed tips in the front third, softening into a rounded lobe that trails to a point over the peduncle. Build a real caudal peduncle so the tail fin flares out of the body instead of abutting it, and give the tail visible rays with a slightly forked/pointed trailing edge. Elongate the body toward 2.2-2.4 aspect. Add a steep sloping forehead and a protruding thick lower lip. Derive the bars from the scale field (per-scale darkening) rather than an overlay gradient.

rows.readsAs: a scallop shell, or a folded paper hand-fan on two little stands
rows.defect: There are no concentric growth rings — the shell is covered in RADIAL ribs fanning from the hinge, which is the wrong ornament entirely and turns the clam into a scallop. The two symmetric hinged valves do not read as two valves: the whole thing is one purple bowl shape, and the only division is a faint centre rib. The top edge is a dead-straight machined horizontal line with a white specular streak on it, which looks like a cut edge, not a hinge with an umbo. The bottom outline is a perfect circular arc. The two small purple triangles poking out below are hard-edged geometric wedges with a visible overlap seam against the shell — they read as feet or as a stand, not as a pale muscular foot or a pair of fleshy siphons (they are the same purple as the shell, not pale flesh).
rows.fix: Rotate the ornament: replace the radial rib fan with nested concentric growth lines following the ventral margin, tightening near the umbo. Split the silhouette into two valves gaping slightly along a wavy commissure so the hinge line reads, and give it an umbo bump at the dorsal edge rather than a straight cut. Break the perfect arc of the ventral margin. Recolor the protrusion to pale pink-cream flesh, soften its edges, and either extrude it as a single tongue-shaped foot from the gape or as two fringed siphon tubes — with a soft flesh-to-shell transition instead of a hard overlap.

rows.readsAs: a red cichlid or a red tilapia — a stranger would not say clownfish, and it is visibly the same model as the Cichlid in this batch
rows.defect: The single most identifying feature is entirely absent: there are no white bands and no black band edging anywhere. The fish is a uniform red-to-crimson gradient with evenly spaced airbrushed vertical shading stripes — those stripes are darker, not white, so they read as generic shading, not clownfish bars. The snout is not blunt and stubby; it is a smooth pointed taper. The fins are not rounded paddles: the dorsal is the same stuck-on grey sawtooth crown as the Cichlid, with a hard straight baseline seam over the back, and the tail is the same flat opaque grey circular-sector plate butted onto the body with no peduncle. Body geometry, eye, pectoral scribble and lateral line are pixel-for-pixel the Cichlid asset in a different hue.
rows.fix: Paint three white bars with black margins in the correct clownfish placement — one just behind the eye angled forward, one mid-body with the characteristic forward-pointing bulge, one across the caudal peduncle — as bands in the pigment layer, not overlay stripes. Set the base to true orange, not crimson. Blunt the snout and shorten the head. Replace the sawtooth dorsal with a low continuous dorsal that is only slightly notched, and swap the grey sector tail for a rounded, black-edged, translucent-white paddle caudal that flares from a real peduncle. Give the pectorals and pelvics rounded paddle outlines so the fish is visibly a different build from the Cichlid.

rows.readsAs: a fat orange newt or a cartoon otter — nobody would call this a rock lizard
rows.defect: The head is a separate flat orange ellipse overlapping the body with a visible curved seam and a grey rim highlight along its top — it is stuck on, not grown out, and there is no neck or jaw articulation at all. The tail fails its mustRead: instead of a long tapering tail longer than the body, it is a short thick hook that curls UP and forward, blunt-ended and the same width along most of its length, with a dark brown blotch painted inside the curl; it is shorter than the trunk. The limbs fail their mustRead completely — two stubby dark brown nubs hanging below the belly, no bent elbows, no sprawl, no splayed clawed toes, no hind/fore differentiation. No scale texture and no ear opening; the dark spots are soft airbrushed blobs floating over a smooth gradient skin, clearly sprayed on. The mouth is a single scored line. Overall aspect measures roughly 2.3, well short of the 3.5 called for.
rows.fix: Merge head into a tapering neck and rebuild it as a wedge with a distinct jawline, nostril and a recessed ear opening behind the eye. Replace the hooked stub with a tail that is body-length-plus, thick at the base and tapering continuously to a fine point, held low and slightly curved. Rebuild the limbs as four sprawling legs with the elbow and knee pushed out sideways, forearm and shank visible, and five splayed toes with claws on each foot. Elongate the trunk toward 3.5 aspect. Replace the airbrushed blobs with an actual scale field, darker dorsally, and let the blotches fall on scale groups.

rows.readsAs: a coiled ribbed hose or a fat green caterpillar with a ping-pong paddle for a head
rows.defect: The posture is wrong in the way that destroys the ID: nothing is reared. The entire animal lies flat as a horizontal donut coil, wider than it is tall (measured aspect about 1.3 wide, and the row asks for taller-than-wide). The hood is not spread ribs behind the head — it is a large flat circular disc that the head is drawn ON, with a wedge notch bitten out of its lower right, so it reads as a paddle or a lollipop, and it overlaps the neck with a hard crescent seam rather than flaring out of it. The body is covered in dense, evenly spaced hard ridge lines running the full length, which look like a corrugated vacuum hose or a caterpillar, not scales, and they run straight across the coil without following its curvature at the crossing point. The eye is one white oval with a black slit floating on the disc; there is no brow, no supraocular scale, no fixed reptilian stare structure. The forked tongue is two straight red hairlines with no thickness. The tail end is a blunt cut cylinder with no taper.
rows.fix: Rebuild the pose: lift the front third off the ground into a vertical S, with the head at the top looking forward and only the rear coiled on the ground; target a portrait aspect near 1.1 tall. Make the hood a flare of the NECK — widen the neck skin outward and downward from behind the jaw with the rib struts faintly visible through it, tapering back into the body, no disc outline and no notch. Reshape the head into a blunt wedge with a distinct jaw and a brow ridge over a round lidless eye. Replace the corrugated ridge lines with an imbricated scale field that follows the body's curve and shrinks in perspective around the coil, and taper the tail to a point.

rows.readsAs: a teal quail or a crested pigeon — and unmistakably the same bird model as the Chough in this batch
rows.defect: It is the Chough asset in this same batch with a small tuft added — identical turquoise body, identical flat lens-shaped cyan wing-disc with a hard dark outline, identical yellow legs, identical thin dark spike tail joined at a hard seam. The mustRead bill fails: it is a small STRAIGHT yellow triangle, not a heavy dark hooked bill, and it is far too short for a cockatoo. The crest fails too: it is five thin teal spikes about a fifth of head height, sitting on the crown as a separate outlined shape rather than a raised fan of feathers rooted in the skull — it reads as a punk fringe or a jay's tuft. Feet show three forward toes on a simple Y; the required two-forward two-back zygodactyl grip is absent. Colour is turquoise, which reads as no cockatoo species. Head is a plain circle on an ellipse body.
rows.fix: Recolor the plumage to white/cream with a hint of grey shadow. Replace the bill with a heavy, deep, dark grey hooked bill with a strong downcurved culmen and a visible cere at the base, roughly twice its current mass. Rebuild the crest as five or six long recurved yellow feathers sweeping up and back from the crown, each with a visible shaft and rooted into the skull feathering so there is no outline seam; make it at least head-height. Change the foot to two toes forward and two back wrapping a perch. Replace the outlined wing disc with layered coverts and primaries emerging from the shoulder.

rows.readsAs: A painted Easter egg, or a domino tile — nothing living
rows.defect: The whole render is a single smooth salmon-orange ellipse with a soft white rim highlight and five perfectly round, evenly spaced black dots in a straight line across the upper third. There is no foot, no tentacle fringe, no shell nacre, no crawling posture, no ground contact — the body floats above a detached black shadow ellipse. Every mustRead fails: the shell is not ear-shaped (it is a plain egg oval), the 'row of holes' is five identical machined circles stamped on the surface rather than perforations sunk into a shell edge, the huge muscular foot is entirely absent, and there is no frilly sensory fringe anywhere on the rim. The pale blotches inside the body read as sprayed-on airbrush clouds, not nacre. Silhouette is a perfect geometric primitive.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette as an asymmetric ear/auricle outline — flat spiral apex crowded to one end, wide flaring aperture at the other — instead of a symmetric ellipse. Sink the respiratory pores into the raised left margin as a curved arc of irregular, decreasing-diameter openings each with a shadowed lip and a raised rim, not flat dots on a flat field. Add the cream muscular foot bulging out beneath the shell's whole lower edge so the shell overhangs it, and grow a dense irregular fringe of short epipodial tentacles from the seam between foot and shell so the fringe emerges from the tissue rather than being drawn on. Sit the foot on the ground plane and attach the shadow to it.

rows.readsAs: A bloated newt or axolotl with a plastic dinosaur crest glued on
rows.defect: Construction is visibly three stuck-together primitives: a fat pale-blue ellipse trunk, a separate white egg for the head overlapping it with a hard crescent seam where the two ovals cross, and a thick banana-shaped tail whose base cuts across the trunk with another visible hard outline. The head is a rounded egg, not the large blunt triangular head required — there is no jaw line, no cheek mass, no snout taper; the mouth is a single straight ruled line. A row of identical black triangular spikes is planted along the back like a comb, sitting on top of the body rather than growing from a dorsal crest. Grey spots are airbrushed onto the trunk with no relation to body form. The four legs are plain grey capsules poking out from under the ellipse with no shoulder or hip, and the belly is not held clear of the ground — the trunk bottom sits right on the shadow. Tail is roughly body-length, which is the one mustRead that lands.
rows.fix: Merge head and trunk into one continuous outline with a neck that narrows and re-widens rather than two overlapping ovals; give the head a wedge plan — wide at the jaw hinge, tapering to a blunt snout — and cut a real jaw line. Start the tail as an unbroken continuation of the pelvic mass so no crossing edge exists at its base. Replace the comb of identical triangles with an irregular keeled nuchal crest of decreasing spine height that rises out of the dorsal ridge. Build the legs as three-segment limbs (femur, tibia, splayed foot with toes) angling out and down from visible shoulder/hip bulges, and lift the trunk so a gap of daylight shows between belly and ground.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon rabbit or a purple hamster
rows.defect: A purple pear-shaped blob with two tall narrow ears, three long straight white whisker lines, a round cartoon eye with a white catchlight, and two square white incisors drawn as literal rectangles below the nose. The arched rump is present, but the legs are simply not there: below the body there are only two small dark comma-shaped scribbles, no visible limb, no foot, and certainly no slender delicate legs with hoof-like claws — that mustRead is fully absent. The rear haunch is marked by a hard-edged crescent line stamped onto the flank rather than muscle form. The buck teeth and tall ears push the read to a rabbit; a real agouti has small rounded ears, no rabbit incisors, and long thin deer-like legs holding the body high. Body is essentially a rounded capsule with decoration.
rows.fix: Shorten and round the ears to low fleshy cups set well back on the skull. Delete the rectangular incisors and the straight whisker rays. Most importantly, build four long slender legs — high shoulder and long thigh flowing out of the trunk, thin cannon bones, and small blunt hoof-like nails — lifting the belly clear so the animal reads as a small standing ungulate-like rodent. Replace the stamped crescent on the haunch with a soft form-following value change, and let the coarse agouti-banded coat break the silhouette edge instead of leaving it a clean airbrushed curve.

rows.readsAs: A plump standing pigeon or duck with two brown planks stuck to its chest
rows.defect: Posture is wrong for the reference: the bird is standing upright on two thin yellow legs planted on the ground, not flying. The body is a near-perfect orange circle with a second smaller circle for the head overlapping it — the seam between the two circles is plainly visible as an arc across the neck, and a third lighter oval sits behind the body as an unexplained hump. The wings are long and narrow (correct) but they are two flat brown planks that pass ACROSS the front of the breast and terminate in a hard straight cut where they meet the body, so they read as pinned-on rather than rooted in a shoulder. The bill is a tiny short yellow triangle with a small hook and no tube nostrils at all — the heavy tube-nosed bill mustRead fails. No tail is visible behind the body.
rows.fix: Commit to the flying posture: lose the standing legs, tuck them under, and set the body on a shallow gliding tilt. Fuse head and body into one continuous head-neck-breast line rather than two overlapping circles, and delete the stray oval behind the body. Root each wing in a shoulder bulge that swells out of the back so the leading edge is a continuous curve off the body — never a straight cut across the breast — and taper the wing to a pointed hand with the trailing edge slightly S-curved. Enlarge the bill to a heavy pale hook occupying a real fraction of the head, with the paired horn tubes modelled as raised ridges along the upper mandible. Add the short wedge tail projecting behind.

rows.readsAs: A pink paper arrow or a stylised sawfish weathervane
rows.defect: The head is a hard machined arrowhead — two perfectly straight converging edges meeting at a sharp point, with four identical triangular sawteeth hanging exposed below the jaw line. That is the exact crocodile/V-snout silhouette the reference note explicitly warns against, and it is the opposite of the required broad rounded U-shaped snout with hidden teeth. The trunk is a flat pink plank with a dead-straight top edge and a dead-straight bottom edge running the full length, tapering to a needle point at the tail tip; it has no volume, no belly, no cross-section. The 'armour' is a row of separate identical spikes planted along the top line, plus a few straight ruled cross-lines — no scute rows, no bony texture, no keels. The legs are two thin bent wires. The eye is a single white dot on the flat facet of the head. The whole animal is jammed into the bottom quarter of the canvas with a large empty void above it.
rows.fix: Rebuild the snout as a wide rounded U in plan — parallel-sided, blunt at the tip, wider than the neck — and close the lip line over the teeth so no tooth shows on a shut mouth. Give the trunk real depth: raise the back into a domed ridge and drop a heavy sagging belly so the top and bottom outlines are opposing curves, never parallel straight lines. Replace the planted spikes with two paralleled rows of overlapping osteoderms that swell out of the dorsal skin, each with a keel and shading, continuing without break onto the tail where they merge into a double then single caudal crest. Make the tail thick and muscular at the base, longer than the body, laterally compressed toward the tip. Build sprawled four-toed limbs with real upper and lower segments and a visible elbow/knee. Rescale and recentre so the animal fills the frame.

rows.readsAs: The Agama from this same batch in a different colour — or a generic salamander
rows.defect: Same three-primitive construction as the Agama in this batch, to the point that the two are near-twins with different colours: a separate pale oval head overlapping the trunk with a hard crescent seam at the neck, a smooth banana tail whose base cuts across the body on a visible line, and a trunk that is a plain ellipse. Brown spots are airbrushed on top of a flat blue-grey field with no scale structure at all — the required squared armoured scale rows and the lateral skin fold are both entirely missing, so two of three mustReads fail. Legs are four dark tapered stubs with no joints, feet or toes, projecting from the underside with no hip or shoulder. The tail does exceed the body length, which is correct, but it is a featureless smooth tube with a single ruled highlight stripe rather than a ringed, scaled, tapering tail. Mouth is one straight ruled line; the eye is an almond with a hard white ring.
rows.fix: Fuse head, trunk and tail into one continuous outline — the neck should narrow and the tail base should widen out of the pelvis with no crossing edge. Cut the diagnostic lateral fold as a continuous granular groove running from behind the foreleg to the hind leg, with the dorsal and ventral scale fields meeting it at different angles. Replace the sprayed spots with rectangular scale rows that follow body curvature, ring the tail with them, and let the dark blotches sit inside those rows rather than over them. Keep the legs short but give them elbows, knees and five splayed toes. Differentiate strongly from the Agama render: flatten the trunk, drop the crest entirely, and make the head a narrower wedge.

rows.readsAs: A pale worm or a peeled banana with legs
rows.defect: The single most diagnostic feature of this species — glossy jet-black skin — is absent: the animal is rendered cream/ivory white with pale yellow blotches, which reads as a fire salamander at best and as an albino larva at worst. Two grey ellipses float behind and below the tail with no connection to the body: off-body artifacts sitting on the dark background. The head is a separate pale oval overlapping the trunk with a visible seam, and the tail base cuts across the trunk on another hard line. Only two legs are visible, both plain grey tapered sticks with no joints or toes. The eye is a small flat black dot with no lid, no orbit and no bulge, so the 'bulging prominent eyes' mustRead fails; the mouth is a single ruled line with a small upturn that reads as a smiley. The skin is flat matte with airbrushed spots and no wet specular at all.
rows.fix: Recolour to a deep saturated black with a strong narrow specular running the length of the back and along the top of the tail so the skin reads wet and glossy; delete the yellow blotches entirely. Remove the two grey ellipses behind the tail. Fuse head, body and tail into one continuous outline; widen and round the skull, and set the eyes as hemispherical domes standing proud of the head profile with a bright highlight and a dark orbit crease. Show all four short sprawled limbs with visible elbows and blunt toes, and give the tail a rounded, slightly compressed section that tapers evenly rather than a smooth even tube. Add costal grooves as soft vertical dents along the flank.

rows.readsAs: A flea, or a very small shrimp — close, but a hobbyist's shrimp
rows.defect: The best-formed render in the batch, and the C-curl, the small head with two pairs of antennae, and the spread tail fan all land. What breaks it is that the body is two overlapping smooth golden spheres — a head-thorax ball and an abdomen ball — with a clearly visible crescent seam between them, so the required laterally flattened SEGMENTED body does not read; there is no pleon segmentation, no coxal plate stack, no articulated rings anywhere. The legs are four or five perfectly straight identical hairlines dropping vertically from the underside, which fails 'many segmented legs of differing shapes' — no gnathopods, no chelae, no knees, and all of them the same length and thickness. The eye is a plain black disc pasted on the head. The organism also occupies only about a quarter of the frame width, leaving a large empty canvas.
rows.fix: Replace the two spheres with a stack of overlapping arched segments running the whole length of the curl, each segment's trailing edge visible as an overlapping plate so the curve is built from articulation rather than drawn onto a ball. Hang large flat coxal plates from the thoracic segments. Differentiate the appendages: two enlarged subchelate gnathopods forward with visible propodus and folded dactyl, then pereopods that lengthen and angle rearward, each drawn with a knee bend rather than as a straight line. Give the pleon three pairs of feathery pleopods beneath the curl. Recess the eye into the head capsule as a compound field of tiny facets rather than a solid black disc, and scale the whole creature up to fill the frame.

rows.readsAs: a generic golden sunfish or bream
rows.defect: None of the three mustReads are present. There is no flat straight sloping topline to an upturned mouth — the topline is a smooth convex dome and the mouth is a small terminal point with no upturn. There are no bold black wedge bars: the flank carries soft orange-brown vertical shading bands that read as gradient banding, not black wedges, and they fade out rather than being crisp. The dorsal is not set far back — it is a sawtooth comb of five sharp identical triangles sitting on the highest point of the back, mid-body, and it is stuck ON: there is a hard dark line across the base of the comb where it meets the body, with no tissue continuity. Body aspect is roughly 1.8, not the specified 2.5 — it is a deep disc, not an elongated fish. The pectoral fin is a flat isoceles triangle primitive, and the caudal is a straight-edged bowtie with machined edges.
rows.fix: Rebuild the topline as a straight ramp from the upper lip to the dorsal origin, and place the dorsal origin at ~65-70% of body length so it sits over the anal fin near the tail. Replace the sawtooth comb with a spined dorsal whose membrane rises out of the dorsal ridge (no base line). Draw 4-5 hard-edged black wedges that are widest at the back and taper downward, painted into the silver skin layer so they sit under the specular pass. Cut body depth so aspect is 2.5 and shift the mouth to a superior/upturned position.

rows.readsAs: an unidentifiable dark minnow silhouette
rows.defect: The image is nearly invisible against the background — the body is a dark slate grey at maybe 15% contrast on a near-black field, so most of the render cannot be resolved at all. What does resolve is a pointed lens/almond silhouette with a single straight highlight line running nose to tail, aspect about 2.2 rather than the specified 4. The deeply forked tail is absent: the caudal is a solid dark rounded blob with no fork whatsoever. There is no barbel under the chin. There is no projecting upper jaw — the snout is a symmetrical point. The head is not separable from the body; the eye is a white ring floating on the snout tip with no head mass built around it.
rows.fix: Raise body value substantially (a cod is a pale olive-brown with mottling, not near-black) so the animal reads on the dark card. Stretch to aspect 4 and give the body a distinct nape/head break at ~26% length. Replace the caudal blob with a properly forked tail with two pointed lobes and a concave trailing margin. Add the chin barbel as a short soft filament growing from the lower jaw, and push the upper jaw forward past the lower.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon Easter bunny in the wrong colour
rows.defect: The animal is solid turquoise/teal. The mustRead 'thick white coat with black ear tips' is entirely absent — there is no white anywhere and the ear tips are the same teal as the rest, only slightly darker. The ears are long and upright, i.e. rabbit-proportioned, when the mustRead calls for short ears; and the hind feet are not visible as large at all — the foot is a small teal stub the same size as the forefoot. The coat has no fur texture: the body is a smooth vector gradient with a specular sheen, so it reads as glazed plastic rather than thick pelage. The haunch is a separate teal ellipse laid over the torso with a visible hard crescent seam at its front edge, and the near foreleg is a detached teardrop with a dark gap between it and the chest. The whiskers are four perfectly straight machined white lines fanning from a point. The teeth are a literal white rectangle divided by one vertical line.
rows.fix: Force the palette to white/cream with dark grey-black ear-tip masking on the distal third of each ear. Shorten the ears to about 60% of current length. Enlarge the hind foot to a long plantigrade paw and plant it so the heel shows. Merge the haunch into the torso outline (one continuous silhouette, shading only) and grow the foreleg out of the chest mass. Replace the smooth gradient with a fur-clump noise pass and break the body edge with a fringed outline. Curve and taper the whiskers, and round the incisors.

rows.readsAs: a cream pill capsule or a plain sardine
rows.defect: The silhouette is a capsule — a cream lozenge with parallel top and bottom edges and rounded caps, exactly the failure mode listed. All three mustReads are missing: there is no steeply upturned drawbridge mouth (the mouth is a short horizontal slit near the tip), there are no barbels on the chin, and there are no long ribbon dorsal and anal fins running to the tail — the back and belly edges are completely bare from head to tail. The only fin is one flat grey triangle pasted on the mid-flank with a hard straight hypotenuse. The caudal is a small ragged grey smudge that barely reads as a tail and does not connect to the body. The body has no scale structure at all — a real arowana's huge mosaic scales are its single most recognisable feature. Colour is a flat bone-cream with a plastic top highlight.
rows.fix: Break the capsule: give the body a shallow dorsal taper and a straight ventral profile so the head wedge is distinct. Rebuild the mouth as an oblique, near-vertical hinged jaw pointing up at ~45 degrees with the lower jaw leading, and hang two long chin barbels from it. Run a low continuous ribbon fin along the rear two-thirds of both the back and the belly, merging into the caudal so the three form one continuous margin. Add large overlapping crescent scales in rows with iridescent rim lighting.

rows.readsAs: a small cartoon penguin
rows.defect: The stance, white front and stubby build do read as an auk-type bird, so the basic form works — but the back is bright violet-purple, not black, so the required 'black back and white front' fails as a colour read. The wing is a dark purple oval decal laid on the flank with a continuous hard rim all the way round; it does not grow out of the shoulder and there is no shoulder joint. The white breast is likewise a clean-edged oval patch with a machined boundary, so it reads as a sticker rather than a plumage boundary. The legs are set at the body's midline rather than far back at the rear, which is the specific mustRead, and the feet are three straight yellow sticks with no webbing. The bill is a small flat yellow triangle; a razorbill bill should be deep and blade-like. No feather texture anywhere — the body is one smooth gradient sphere plus a smaller sphere for the head, with a visible neck pinch between them.
rows.fix: Recolour the dorsal surface to near-black with a cool sheen. Move the leg insertion back to about 75% of body length so the bird sits back on its heels. Dissolve the wing outline: keep the wing as a shaded feather tract that shares an edge with the body silhouette at the trailing tip only. Soften the breast boundary with a broken feather margin. Deepen the bill to a laterally compressed blade with a white groove, and web the toes.

rows.readsAs: a teal kiwi or a generic stub-billed shorebird
rows.defect: The defining feature is inverted-to-absent: the bill is straight and if anything angled slightly DOWNWARD, a long flat yellow-orange spike, when the mustRead is explicit that it sweeps strongly upward. That alone makes it not an avocet. The crisp black-and-white pied patterning is absent — the whole bird is turquoise. The legs are pale yellow-tan, not long blue-grey, and they are short: the tibia barely clears the belly, whereas an avocet is a leggy wader. The wing is the worst construction problem — it is a stack of three concentric teal ellipses with hard outlines sitting on the flank, plus a separate dark teal dagger of a primary tract jutting out to the right with a straight machined edge and a visible seam where it crosses the body edge. The head is a plain sphere joined to the body sphere with no neck. No feather texture; smooth gradient plastic throughout.
rows.fix: Rebuild the bill as a fine needle that curves upward through its distal half, thinning to a point, and shorten its base depth. Repaint to white body with a black crown-and-nape cap, a black shoulder bar and black wing tips. Lengthen the legs to at least the body depth again and recolour to blue-grey. Delete the concentric ellipse wing entirely and replace with layered scapular and primary feather groups that emerge from the shoulder and taper past the tail. Add a slender S-curved neck between head and body.

rows.readsAs: a smiling orange tadpole with something brown behind it
rows.defect: The tail is a separate object. A large brown balloon-shaped mass sits behind the orange body at a different hue and value, overlapping it with a hard curved boundary — it reads as a second creature or a rock behind the animal, not as the axolotl's own tail. There is no taper from body into tail and no fin crest along the tail or back, so that mustRead fails. The gill stalks are partly misplaced: the upper cluster sits correctly behind the skull, but a second pink feathery cluster hangs beneath the throat, forward of and below the jaw, where an axolotl has no gills — that is an off-body artifact. Only two clusters are readable, not three pairs. The head is a smooth egg with no wide flat cranium; the body is a plain capsule with a specular highlight stripe. The legs are two thin brown sticks with no feet, and they are drawn in a darker separate colour so they read as pasted under the body.
rows.fix: Rebuild the tail as a continuous laterally compressed extension of the trunk in the same skin material, tapering from the hips, and run a translucent fin crest along its top and bottom edge continuing forward onto the lower back. Delete the throat gill cluster and place three paired stalks along the sides of the neck immediately behind the head, all branching from a common gill arch. Flatten and widen the head so it is broader than the trunk. Rebuild the limbs in body colour with four visible splayed digits on each foot.

rows.readsAs: a snow monkey or a young langur
rows.defect: All three mustReads fail. There are no enormous naked bat-like ears — the head shows only two tiny grey nubs almost buried in the curly fringe. There is no skeletal elongated middle finger; both hands are plain rounded grey mittens with no digits at all. The tail is not huge and shaggy and bigger than the body — it is a thin smooth wire-like arc, roughly the width of a finger, and worse, it exits from the animal's upper left SHOULDER rather than the base of the spine, floating clear of the torso with a gap between the arc and the back. The pelage is a smooth grey-cream with soft round blotches airbrushed on top of the belly and thighs, which reads as sprayed-on spots rather than fur. The face is a flat mask plate with a hard edge against the surrounding fluff. The eyes are small and dark when the row calls for prominent.
rows.fix: Scale the ears up to at least head height, make them naked leathery grey with visible inner ridges, and set them low and wide. Move the tail root to the base of the spine and rebuild it at three to four times its current thickness with a long shaggy fringed outline so it out-masses the torso. Open the hands into five digits with the third drawn as a thin skeletal probe roughly twice the length of the others. Enlarge the eyes and give them the reflective orange tapetum. Replace the airbrushed blotches with directional coarse guard-hair strokes that break the silhouette.

rows.readsAs: a purple spider or an engorged tick
rows.defect: The carapace is a near-perfect smooth ellipse with dark circular spots sprayed over it — a geometric primitive, not a crab shell (no rim, no eyestalk sockets, no front margin, no mouthparts). The 'pincers' are two small featureless ovals floating ABOVE the shell at the upper corners, each joined by a thin dark stick with a hard visible seam where it meets the body; neither has a claw gape or opposing fingers, so no pincer reads at all. They are also raised over the back rather than held forward. Only three thin stick legs per side (a crab has four walking legs plus the chelipeds), all straight dark lines meeting the shell at a hard line. The 'eyes on stalks' are two bare pale filaments rising from the top of the shell with no eyeball on the end — they read as antennae, not eyes. mustRead 'pair of large pincers held forward' and 'eyes on short stalks above the mouthparts' both fail.
rows.fix: Grow the chelipeds forward from the front margin of the carapace as two-part limbs (merus + a split claw with a fixed and a movable finger, gape open), blended into the body edge with no butt-joint stick. Widen the carapace into a fan/hexagonal shell with a raised front margin and a notched rim rather than an ellipse. Add four walking legs per side, thicker at the coxa and tapering to a point, emerging from under the shell rim. Put a dark spherical eyeball on the tip of each short stalk and seat the stalks in orbital notches on the front edge, above a visible mouthfield. Replace the sprayed dot texture with shell-follow tubercle shading.

rows.readsAs: a green finch or a cartoon chick
rows.defect: There is essentially no neck — the head is glued directly to the front of the body ellipse, so the single most identifying crane feature ('long neck carried straight') is absent. The proportion is that of a chick: body ellipse roughly as tall as long, legs short, headFrac far above the 0.24 called for. No drooping bustle of tail plumes over the rump — the rear is a single flat dark wedge. No bare red crown patch; instead there is a bright cyan spiky tuft that reads as a cartoon punk crest. The wing is a hard-outlined concentric ellipse decal sitting on the flank with a clear dark seam all the way round — a sticker, not a folded wing growing out of the shoulder. Legs are plain yellow sticks that meet the belly at a hard point with no thigh, no hock, no feathering.
rows.fix: Extend the neck to roughly half the standing height, held vertical and straight, tapering smoothly out of the shoulders with continuous plumage shading (no join line). Shrink the head to ~0.12 of the height and make the bill a straight spear. Replace the crest with a bare red skin patch over the crown/nape. Build a drooping bustle of long curved tertial plumes over the rump that overhangs the tail. Lengthen and thin the legs into true stilts with a visible backward-bending hock, and dissolve the wing decal's outline into feather-tract shading that flows off the body.

rows.readsAs: a shrimp or prawn
rows.defect: The claws are two flat leaf-shaped paddles with no split, no fixed/movable finger, no gape — they read as leaves or fins, so 'large pincer claws held forward' fails. They hang off a thin straight stick that meets the carapace at a hard butt-joint. The antennae are dead-straight machined lines that cut ACROSS the body and out the far side rather than sweeping out of the head. The carapace is an unmodified ellipse with sprayed dark dots; there is no cervical groove and no rostrum. The abdomen is a chain of scalloped bumps that meets the carapace at a visible step. The walking legs are three near-identical straight hairlines under the thorax. The tail fan is present but is a spray of spiky rays rather than the paired uropods plus telson.
rows.fix: Rebuild the chelae as three-segment limbs ending in a genuinely split claw (open gape, thickened base, tapered tips) growing out of the base of the carapace at the front. Give the carapace a pointed rostrum and a cervical groove so it stops being an egg. Sweep the antennae out from beneath the rostrum in a curve and keep them clear of the body silhouette. Make the abdominal segments overlapping plates that shrink smoothly rearward, and flare the tail into two paired uropod blades either side of a central telson.

rows.readsAs: an ant
rows.defect: Three smooth spheres in a row — head, thorax, abdomen — beads on a string with pinch-points between them; that is an ant silhouette, not a cricket. The legs are uniform hairline sticks that meet each sphere at a hard point; the hind leg has only a thin bent knee, no thickened cranked femur, so 'cranked jumping hind legs' fails. The wings are a single faint pale crescent on the top of the rear sphere — no flat tegmina laid over a rounded back, no wing edge, no venation. The antennae are two short straight lines barely longer than the head, nowhere near 'longer than the whole body'. One large glossy round eye sits on the head like a bead.
rows.fix: Fuse the thorax and abdomen into one continuous cylindrical body with a saddle-shaped pronotum over the front, killing the bead-chain pinch-points. Lay two flat tegmina flush along the top of the abdomen with a visible trailing edge and vein lines that follow the wing. Rebuild the hind legs with a fat pear-shaped femur folded up above the body and a long thin spined tibia cranked sharply back below it. Extend the antennae to at least 1.3x total body length, curving and tapering. Blend every leg base into a coxa bulge on the thorax instead of a hairline touching a sphere.

rows.readsAs: a knife blade or a stylised gar fish
rows.defect: This is a machined object, not an animal. The body is a flat plank with a dead-straight top edge and a dead-straight bottom edge tapering to a point — a wedge/knife blade. The head at the right is a flat isosceles arrowhead with a straight-line snout, so 'long narrow V-shaped snout' does not read as a jaw at all; there is no mandible line, no nostril boss, no eye socket, just a cyan dot pasted on. No enlarged fourth lower tooth — the only teeth are a small row of identical white triangles tucked under the head. The dorsal scutes are seven perfectly identical sharp isoceles spikes standing on the straight back line like a sawblade, spaced evenly, sprayed on top of the plank. The tail is the same flat plank ending in a point — no double crest, no lateral flattening, no depth. Two thin bent wire legs are the only limbs and they meet the plank at a hard line. There is no head/neck/body/tail volume transition anywhere.
rows.fix: Replace the straight-edged plank with a barrel-bodied form that has depth: a wide sprawling torso, a narrowing neck, and a tail that starts thick and tapers over its whole length. Model the snout as a true V in plan with an upper and lower jaw line, nostrils at the tip, and interlocking teeth along the closed jawline including one oversized fourth lower tooth protruding outside the upper lip. Give the tail a double row of scutes converging into a single crest, and flatten it laterally so it is tall and thin, not a flat board. Grow four sprawling legs out of the shoulders and hips with visible upper limb mass and splayed clawed feet. Break every straight edge with osteoderm bumps and scale rows that follow the body's curve.

rows.readsAs: a white duckling or a dove — and it is visibly the same bird as Crane.png and Curlew.png in this batch
rows.defect: The bird is cream/ivory white with a small yellow bill. 'All-black glossy plumage' — the single hardest mustRead — is not merely missed, it is inverted. The bill is short, yellow and duck-like, not a stout black pointed bill. The tail is a grey pointed wedge, not square-tipped. The body is the identical ellipse-plus-stuck-on-wing-decal template as the Crane and the Curlew in this same batch, just recoloured: the wing is a concentric ellipse with a hard dark outline seam around it, and there is a stray white scribble inside it. No neck, head fused straight onto the body, legs are two yellow sticks butt-joined to the belly.
rows.fix: Recolour the whole bird to near-black with a blue-green iridescent sheen on the back and wing coverts, and make the bill black, stout, straight and deep at the base with a visible culmen ridge and a slight hook. Square off the tail tip. Lengthen the body horizontally and add a short but real neck so the head is distinct from the shoulder. Replace the outlined wing decal with layered primaries whose tips extend past the body toward the tail, blended into the flank with no seam.
