rows.readsAs: the same generic chick as Crane.png and Crow.png, in purple
rows.defect: The bill is straight — a plain yellow triangular spike angled slightly upward. 'Very long smoothly downcurved bill' is the defining feature and it is absent, which the reference row explicitly warns destroys the identification. The bill is also short: perhaps a sixth of the profile, not a quarter. The head is not small and round on a neck — it is welded into the body ellipse with no neck at all. Legs are short yellow sticks meeting the belly at a hard point, not long bare wading legs; the bird stands like a chick, not a wader. The plumage is flat purple with no streaking of any kind. The wing is the same hard-outlined concentric-ellipse sticker used on the Crane and Crow, with a visible dark seam separating it from the flank.
rows.fix: Draw the bill as a long, smooth, evenly downcurving arc at least a quarter of the total profile length, thick at the base and tapering to a fine tip. Shrink the head to a small round ball, set it on a short slender neck that grows out of the shoulders. Lengthen the legs substantially with a visible bare tibia above the joint. Recolour to mottled brown and cover the body in fine dark streaking that follows the feather tracts, and dissolve the wing outline into layered coverts.

rows.readsAs: a squid — with a real chance of being called a jellyfish
rows.defect: The mustReads are all present — the two yellow eyes carry a clear dark W-shaped pupil, a fin skirt runs the mantle's full length, and there are several short arms plus two longer ones with teardrop club tips. The problems are execution. The mantle is striped with perfectly straight, evenly spaced, parallel vertical lines that stop dead at the mantle edge — sprayed-on wallpaper rather than chromatophore banding that wraps a rounded body. The fin skirt is a single hard-edged concentric ellipse sitting behind the mantle with a crisp seam all the way round, and its outer edge is a machine-perfect ellipse arc with no undulation whatsoever, contradicting 'undulating fin skirt'. The arms are flat tapered blades of uniform grey that appear from beneath the eyes with no head or arm crown behind them — they hang like ribbons rather than growing from a muscular base. Overall silhouette is a smooth oval dome, which pulls it toward a jellyfish.
rows.fix: Make the fin margin wavy — a rippling sine along the outer edge — and blend the skirt into the mantle with a soft shaded fold instead of a hard concentric outline. Curve the mantle stripes so they follow the body's rounded surface, vary their width, and fade them at the edges. Build a visible head mass between the eyes from which the arm crown emerges, thicken each arm at the base with sucker rows down the inner face, and keep the two tentacles distinctly longer than the eight arms rather than roughly matched.

rows.readsAs: a blue rubber vacuum hose coiled on the floor, or a giant millipede
rows.defect: The coil is a near-perfect torus — a smooth doughnut of constant thickness with a clean elliptical hole punched in the middle, no taper from neck to tail and no sense of one loop lying over another. The whole body is ruled with evenly-spaced dark hatch lines from end to end like a vacuum hose or a millipede's rings; ventral scutes are wrapped right over the dorsal surface. Colour is bright periwinkle blue, not olive-green, and the blotches are three or four faint pale-grey smudges floating inside the blue rather than dark oval saddles. The head is a small separate bean tacked onto the ring at the 4-o'clock position with a visible notch where it meets the coil, and the eye sits on the SIDE of the head, not high on top. Nostrils absent. Thickness reads as garden hose, not thigh — the mustRead 'thick as a thigh' fails.
rows.fix: Rebuild the coil as two or three overlapping loops of DIFFERENT diameter with the body tapering ~40% from mid-body to tail tip, so the silhouette is not an annulus. Restrict the scute hatching to the ventral arc only (the belly side facing the viewer on each loop) and let it disappear over the back; replace the uniform pitch with slight width variation. Repaint base to olive/khaki-green and paint the blotches as dark ovals with pale halos that follow the body's curvature (i.e. compressed along the loop). Grow the head out of the neck with a continuous width ramp — no separate ellipse — widen it to a blunt wedge and move both eye and nostril onto the TOP plane of the skull.

rows.readsAs: a generic orange trout or salmon
rows.defect: No silver lateral stripe anywhere — the fish is a flat orange-to-gold gradient with a single thin pale midline crease. The mouth is a short hairline notch at the very tip of the snout; there is no huge underslung gape reaching back past the eye, so the single most diagnostic anchovy feature is absent. The eye is a tiny perfect white circle with a black dot, drawn ON TOP of the snout tip overlapping the outline rather than set in a socket. Every fin is a flat hard-edged triangle laid over the body: the pectoral is an opaque dark triangle with three straight sides and a visible seam across the flank, the dorsal is a triangular flap with a straight leading edge, and the caudal is a dark wedge butted against a hard vertical line at the peduncle. Body silhouette is a symmetrical almond/lens.
rows.fix: Add the broad specular silver band running the full flank at mid-height with a soft feathered upper edge, and desaturate the base from orange to blue-green dorsal / white ventral. Rebuild the head: extend the jawline back past the eye so the mouth opens as a deep curved gape under a projecting pointed snout. Sink the eye into the head with a lid rim instead of stamping a circle on the outline, and move it back off the tip. Replace all triangular fins with membrane shapes that have ray striations and a soft translucent base blending into the flank over 6-10px — kill the caudal seam by tapering the peduncle into the fin root.

rows.readsAs: a dark ocean sunfish, or a stone pebble with a paper bowtie taped on
rows.defect: The body is a bare charcoal ellipse — essentially an egg — with four faint vertical bands and nothing else: no mouth at all, no gill-cover spine, no scale texture. The caudal fin is a literal geometric triangle, straight-edged, apex touching the body and flaring to a flat vertical back edge, joined by an obvious hard seam; it reads as a paper bowtie clipped onto the disc. The dorsal and anal fins are flat translucent grey sheets sitting BEHIND the body plane with a visible overlap edge instead of growing from the dorsal ridge. The two trailing filaments do exist but they are hairlines of uniform width running off the top and bottom of the canvas, unattached-looking and mechanically straight. The whole thing is near-black on a near-black background — at a glance the portrait is almost empty.
rows.fix: Raise value and hue substantially (marine angelfish are saturated blue/yellow) so the subject separates from the dark plate. Break the ellipse: add a slight anterior forehead ramp and a concave snout notch, and give it a small terminal mouth plus the backward-pointing opercular spine at the gill margin. Rebuild the caudal as a soft-edged rounded/lyre fin with ray striations, rooted in a tapering peduncle so there is no straight seam. Root the dorsal and anal fins IN the body outline — same silhouette, continuous — with the filaments emerging as tapering extensions of the last rays that curve, not ruler-straight lines.

rows.readsAs: a pink balloon fish with a bedside lamp — the lure sells it as an anglerfish, but nothing else does
rows.defect: The jaw is not upturned — the mouth is a dead-straight horizontal line across the middle of the face, and the 'fangs' are ten small identical white triangles evenly spaced along it, reading as a zipper or a saw blade rather than long needle teeth. No lower jaw mass, no gape. The body is a smooth magenta/bubblegum-pink egg with a glossy airbrush highlight — a deep-sea ambush predator painted like a bath toy. The caudal fin is a dark maroon fan sitting to the LEFT of the body with a visible gap and hard boundary where it meets the flank: clearly a separate shape placed behind, not grown out. The illicium stalk is a hairline that emerges from a point on the skull with no base swelling, and the lure bulb is a perfect circle with a perfect circular white dot inside it. No pectoral or pelvic fins at all despite the mustRead calling for tiny fins.
rows.fix: Tilt the mouth line up 25-35 degrees toward the snout and give the lower jaw its own protruding mass, then replace the even triangles with irregular curved needle fangs of varying length that interdigitate and cross the lip line. Recolour to dark brown-black or charcoal with a faint subsurface sheen; kill the glossy egg highlight. Attach the caudal by tapering the body into a short peduncle so fin and flank share one continuous outline. Thicken the illicium base into a fleshy mound rising out of the forehead, add a slight S-curve to the stalk, and make the lure an irregular glowing esca with bloom rather than a circle-in-circle. Add small round pectoral fins low on the flank.

rows.readsAs: a red salamander or newt
rows.defect: No dewlap — the diagnostic throat fan is completely absent, and the throat is a plain smooth curve. Only TWO limbs are drawn: one dark-red peg hanging down at the shoulder and one at the hip, each a plain rounded rod that stops in a blunt stump with no foot, no toes and no adhesive pads, joined to the body by a hard dark seam line. There is no elbow or knee, and no far-side limbs at all, so it does not read as a sprawling posture — it reads as propped on two dowels. The head is a separate rounded blob abutting the trunk with a visible pinch/notch at the neck, and it is a blunt oval, not the long narrow pointed wedge called for. The tail is a fat rod of nearly constant width with a darker inner racing-stripe painted down its centre, and it is roughly the same length as head+body, not longer. Dark spots are sprayed as flat blobs on the back with no relation to the form.
rows.fix: Add the extended dewlap as a semicircular fan hanging from the throat, pink/red, with radial gular-rod striations, growing out of the jaw line. Draw all four limbs with elbow and knee bends and terminate each in five long splayed digits with visibly widened toe pads; splay them laterally for a sprawling stance instead of hanging them vertically. Lengthen the tail to at least 1.5x head+body, taper it to a whip point, and remove the painted centre stripe in favour of banding that wraps around the cylinder. Reshape the head into a long narrow triangular wedge with a distinct snout tip and merge it into the neck with a continuous outline. Recolour to green with a brown wash and replace the sprayed blobs with a fine granular scale texture.

rows.readsAs: a string of amber beads with pins in it, or a generic wasp/bee toy
rows.defect: The antennae are two perfectly straight rigid lines radiating off the head — no elbow, no scape/funiculus break — which the reference specifically names as a mustRead. The three body parts are three smooth tangent spheres with mirror-ball specular highlights; there is no narrow waist petiole between thorax and gaster, the spheres simply touch, so it reads as a string of beads. Worse, the middle sphere is the LARGEST and the head the smallest, which is backwards for a worker. Leg placement is wrong: the visible legs spring from beneath the rear two spheres, including two long ones off the gaster, rather than all six from the thorax; each leg is a straight tapered stick with no femur/tibia joint, no tarsus and no foot. No mandibles. The head sphere carries a single perfect-circle black eye with a white catchlight, like a doll's eye.
rows.fix: Add the elbow: a long straight scape from the head, then a sharp 90-degree bend into a segmented, slightly clubbed funiculus. Pinch a genuinely narrow petiole (with a visible node bump) between thorax and gaster and squash the gaster into an ovoid rather than a sphere; shrink the thorax below gaster size and give it the mesosomal saddle profile. Move all six leg roots onto the thorax and give each leg a bent femur-tibia joint plus a small hooked tarsus. Kill the specular ball highlights in favour of a matte chitin sheen with faint segment striations. Add forward-pointing mandibles at the head.

rows.readsAs: a teal copy of the Ant in this same batch
rows.defect: This is the SAME rig as the Ant in this batch, recoloured teal — identical three tangent spheres, identical straight stick legs off the rear, identical straight unelbowed antennae, identical single circular doll eye. Every one of the three mustReads is missing: the body is three balls, not one soft pear-shaped bulb; there are no cornicles (no tube pair on the rear at all); and there is no needle beak and no stem to stick it into. It also has the ant's petiole problem, which is doubly wrong here because an aphid should have NO waist and NO three-part division.
rows.fix: Stop routing this species through the ant rig. Build a single soft pear/teardrop body, widest at the rear, with a small head fused into it — no thorax/gaster split, no visible seams. Add the two backward-angled cornicle tubes projecting from the rear dorsum and a small cauda between them. Draw the rostrum as a fine needle angled down from under the head into a green stem the aphid stands on, and shorten the legs to stubby six-legged supports gripping that stem. Replace the glossy spheres with a soft matte, slightly translucent cuticle.

rows.readsAs: a generic red dart fish or a large minnow
rows.defect: The body is a symmetrical lens/almond pointed at both ends, uniformly bright crimson from nose to tail — the inverse of the real fish, which is dark olive-grey with red confined to the rear scale margins. No armoured scales anywhere; the only surface marks are one thin pale midline crease and a faint arc. The dorsal and anal fins are dark maroon blobs that sink into the background and sit BEHIND the body outline as separate silhouettes, and they are placed around mid-body rather than far back framing the tail, so the diagnostic paddle-shaped rear end does not read at all. The caudal is a small dark fan butted onto a hard vertical seam and is far too small for a 4.5-aspect body. The head is not flattened or bony and there is no upward-angled mouth — the snout just narrows to a point, with a perfect white circle eye stamped on the outline and a tiny hairline pectoral fin that looks like a scratch.
rows.fix: Recolour to dark olive-grey/bronze along the front two-thirds, then paint large overlapping cycloid scale plates over the rear third with bright red trailing margins so the red is a rear gradient, not the whole fish. Move the dorsal and anal fins right back to sit adjacent to the caudal and root them IN the body outline so the three together form one continuous paddle; enlarge the caudal to a broad rounded fan and blend the peduncle into it. Flatten and broaden the head into a bony plated wedge with visible sutures, and angle the mouth upward with a jutting lower jaw. Sink the eye into a socket back from the snout tip and replace the scratch pectoral with a proper rayed fin.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon teal gecko or a newt-shaped tadpole toy — nobody would say 'blind cave salamander'.
rows.defect: Three of three mustReads are absent. There are NO blood-red feathery external gills anywhere on the neck — the head-to-body junction is a bare smooth taper. The skin is bright teal/turquoise with yellow-green mottled blotches, the opposite of chalk-white unpigmented cave skin. Worst of all it has a large, wide-open, glossy black eye with a white catchlight painted on a white sclera, when the reference explicitly says 'never draw open eyes'. Only two legs are visible and they are hairline dark sticks with hard butt-joints against the belly, no feet or toes. The tail is a big flat dark-teal paddle that overlaps the rear body as a separate darker shape with a visible edge where it crosses, reading as a fin glued behind the animal rather than the body continuing into a tail. The head is a rounded ball, not broad and flat. The mouth is a simple upcurved smile line.
rows.fix: Kill the eye entirely — replace with a faint skin-covered depression the same value as the surrounding head. Recolour body to a translucent pinkish chalk-white (near #ece2df with pink subdermal blush) and drop the yellow blotching. Add the non-negotiable feature: 3 paired plumes of blood-red (#c0202a) feathery gills growing out of the neck sides just behind the jaw, drawn as branching filaments whose bases blend into skin, no outline. Flatten and widen the skull into a spatulate paddle. Give four legs, each with a splayed 4-toe foot, and blend the tail into the body with a continuous dorsal contour instead of an overlapping darker shape.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon red balloon-fish or a smiling cherry-coloured pufferfish.
rows.defect: Zero of three mustReads land. There is no slumped gelatinous face and no bulbous drooping nose — instead there's a small round pink knob on the front with a tiny dot eye and a short straight mouth slit, and the mouth curves UP into a smile rather than the required downturned frown. The body is a hard-edged glossy cherry-red/crimson ellipse with a bright specular highlight streak, reading as inflated rubber rather than pale slack gelatin (real blobfish are pinkish-grey/beige). The tail is a dark maroon flat paddle that sits behind the body with a clear hard seam and a value break — it is a shape stuck on, not a fin growing out of the peduncle. There is a scribbly row of small dark arcs along the lower flank that looks like pen-scratch decoration sprayed onto the surface, plus a stray diagonal hatch cluster near the mouth. Overall silhouette is a clean geometric ovoid.
rows.fix: Desaturate to pale putty-pink/grey (#c9a9a0 range) and cut the specular highlight so the surface reads as soft and matte. Rebuild the face: a large overhanging drooping snout lobe that hangs past the mouth line, brow flesh sagging over the eyes, and a mouth that curves DOWN at the corners. Break the ovoid with slack, asymmetric wobble in the ventral contour. Redraw the caudal fin as a low-contrast translucent membrane whose rays fan out of the body with no seam, and delete the scribbled flank arcs.

rows.readsAs: A purple dolphin or generic porpoise — the pointed snout and clean fin blobs read cetacean but never 'blue whale'.
rows.defect: The mustReads fail. The rostrum is a narrow POINTED cone, not a broad flat U with a single median ridge, and there are no pleated throat grooves at all — the throat is a blank gradient. The dorsal fin is present and roughly three-quarters back, which is correct placement, but it is rendered as a solid dark-plum ellipse sitting on top of the back with a hard elliptical outline and a value jump where it meets the skin: a sticker, not a fin. The pectoral flipper below is the same problem — a detached dark oval with its own closed outline overlapping the flank. There is an off-body artifact: a small pale grey blob floating in empty space above and forward of the back (presumably a blowhole or spout) that touches nothing. The colour is lavender/magenta-purple, not blue-grey, and the flanks are a smooth two-stop gradient with no mottling. Tail flukes are a flat dark notched paddle with a hard seam at the peduncle.
rows.fix: Widen and flatten the rostrum into a broad U seen in three-quarter, with one raised ridge running from blowhole to snout tip. Add 15-25 longitudinal ventral pleats from chin to navel, drawn as soft parallel grooves in the same skin value, not lines on top. Reduce the dorsal to a small falcate nub and, critically, build both fins and flukes with a base that shares the body's fill and gradient so no outline exists at the join. Delete or reattach the floating grey blob to the top of the head. Shift hue to blue-grey (#5a6b7d) with pale mottled dapple.

rows.readsAs: A grey ribbed hose or a shed snakeskin — at best an albino/leucistic generic snake, certainly not a boa constrictor.
rows.defect: None of the three mustReads are present. There are NO saddle-shaped dorsal blotches and nothing reddens toward the tail — the whole animal is uniform pale grey-white with a handful of faint soft grey circles scattered randomly, which read as smudges rather than saddles. There is no dark eye stripe. The head is a smooth rounded bulb barely wider than the neck, not a heavy arrow-shaped head. The body scaling is the biggest problem: it is rendered as dozens of perfectly parallel, evenly spaced, machine-regular light bands wrapping the tube, identical in width from head to tail, which makes the whole thing read as corrugated hose or a vacuum cleaner tube rather than a scaled animal. The body also does not taper — it stays the same diameter through the coil and ends abruptly. The forked tongue is a flat pure-red 2px Y with hard straight lines and no taper, drawn as a graphic symbol.
rows.fix: Add the identity feature: a chain of dark brown/maroon saddle blotches along the dorsal midline, irregular in width, saturating to brick red over the last third of the body. Add a dark bar from eye to jaw angle. Widen the skull into a blunt triangle distinctly broader than the neck. Replace the uniform corrugation with scale rows that vary in width, compress on the inside of curves and stretch on the outside, and fade in scale on the highlight. Taper the last 15% of the body to a short point. Redraw the tongue thinner, tapering, dark red, with a curve.

rows.readsAs: A generic blue mackerel or a small tuna.
rows.defect: Two mustReads land: the tail is genuinely deeply forked and the snout is a pointed cone overhanging the mouth. The third fails hard — the flank is saturated ROYAL BLUE with a bright electric gradient, not a plain mirror-silver. A bonefish's whole identity is that it is a featureless chrome mirror; this reads as a tropical aquarium fish. Secondary issues: every fin (dorsal, anal, pelvic, and the leading half of the caudal) is a nearly transparent ghost-grey shape that barely registers against the background, so the fish appears to have a solid body with vapour attached — the dorsal in particular is a faint quadrilateral hovering over the back with a visible straight leading edge. The eye is a small white ring with a dark centre placed right at the silhouette edge, half hanging off the head profile. The body is also drawn very small in the 440px frame, wasting most of the canvas.
rows.fix: Recolour to a neutral silver: near-white specular band along the lateral line, cool grey-green dorsal fading to white belly, and remove all blue saturation. Raise fin opacity to roughly 0.6 and give each fin visible rays whose bases dissolve into the flank rather than starting at a straight edge. Move the eye inboard so the full orbit sits on the head. Scale the whole organism up by about 1.4x in frame.

rows.readsAs: A kiwi, or a generic purple cartoon songbird/plover — nothing about it says seabird.
rows.defect: The defining feature is missing: the feet are two thin YELLOW stick legs with three hairline toes and no webbing whatsoever — the reference demands vividly coloured blue or red WEBBED feet, and the bright blue foot is the single thing that makes a booby recognisable. The bill also fails: instead of a long tapered dagger running straight into the forehead, it is a thin needle spike attached to a small round head at a clear seam, with the forehead rising in a steep dome above and behind it, breaking the required continuous bill-to-crown line. The eyes are not forward-set flanking the bill — there is one small side-mounted dot eye, giving a lateral, not binocular, stare. Construction is visibly primitive: the body is a near-perfect large circle, the head a near-perfect smaller circle, and there is a hard crescent line where the head circle overlaps the body circle. The wing is a dark violet crescent laid on the flank with a closed hard outline, and the tail is a separate flat dark wedge stuck to the rear at an abrupt angle. Colour is lavender purple throughout.
rows.fix: Replace the feet with large, fully webbed, splayed three-toe paddles in saturated cyan-blue (#1fa8d8), sized comfortably larger than the head. Rebuild the bill as a thick-based tapering dagger whose base is as wide as the skull and whose top line continues unbroken into a flat sloping forehead — no seam, no dome. Move the eyes forward to sit immediately against both sides of the bill base with a dark bare-skin mask. Break both circles: give the body a torpedo taper toward the tail and merge the head into the neck with a shared contour. Rebuild the wing from layered feather groups growing off the shoulder instead of one outlined crescent, and blend the tail wedge into the rump.

rows.readsAs: A generic brown leaf-shaped fish, or a flounder — the double-pointed lens body and floating tail dominate.
rows.defect: The signature mustRead is wrong. The dorsal fin is a tall dark-brown triangular HUMP covering only the middle third of the back with a peaked apex — the bowfin's identity is a very long, low, gently undulating dorsal that runs almost the entire back from just behind the head to the tail. It is also drawn as an opaque separate shape with a hard lower boundary and a distinct value step where it sits on the body, a classic stuck-on part. Worse, the caudal fin is physically DETACHED: there is a visible dark gap of background between the pointed rear tip of the body and the brown fan tail, so the tail floats free. The black eyespot (ocellus) near the tail base, one of three mustReads, is completely absent, and so is the gular plate under the chin — the throat is blank. The body outline is a symmetrical pointed lens/leaf shape, tapering to sharp points at BOTH ends, which is a geometric primitive rather than a fish; the real bowfin has a blunt rounded head. The eye is a white ring sitting on the extreme snout edge.
rows.fix: Replace the hump with a long low dorsal ridge spanning roughly 70% of the back, with a soft wavy upper margin and a base that dissolves into the dorsal skin. Close the gap: attach the caudal fan directly to a thick fleshy peduncle. Add the black ocellus, ringed in orange, on the upper caudal peduncle. Add the bony gular plate as a pale hard shield under the lower jaw. Blunt and round the head end so the silhouette stops being a symmetric lens, and move the eye inboard onto the cheek.

rows.readsAs: A stylised turtle icon or app logo — the family reads, but the floating pill legs and drawn-on web pattern make it a symbol, not an animal.
rows.defect: The legs are DETACHED. Two dark teal ellipses float below the shell with a clear band of background visible between each ellipse and the plastron — nothing connects them to the body, and there are only two of them. They also have no feet, no toes and no claws, so the 'scaly clawed elephantine feet' mustRead is entirely absent. The 'hinged underside that shuts like a box' mustRead is also absent: the plastron is a single flat dark horizontal bar under the carapace with no hinge line, no seam, no forward and rear lobes. The head is a plain teal ellipse butted against the shell rim with a visible hard edge at the join and no neck. The carapace pattern is a set of thin, evenly spaced concentric arcs plus radiating spokes, drawn as uniform-width lines over the dome — it reads as a wireframe or spiderweb sprayed on top of the surface, not as raised keratin scutes with their own thickness and growth rings. Everything is one flat teal hue with a single glossy highlight, and the dome is a clean half-ellipse.
rows.fix: Rebuild all four legs as thick columnar limbs emerging from under the shell margin with continuous flesh — no gap, no closed outline — each ending in a broad elephantine foot with visible overlapping scales and 4-5 blunt dark claws. Replace the flat under-bar with a proper plastron showing the transverse hinge line splitting it into front and rear lobes. Give the head a short thick neck that widens into the shell opening, plus a hooked upper beak and a nostril. Convert the wireframe arcs into discrete polygonal scutes with slightly raised centres, darker seams and yellow-orange radiating starburst markings inside each one. Warm the palette toward brown/olive with orange scute flares.

rows.readsAs: a mayfly or a small damselfly
rows.defect: Two mustReads are absent. The wings are NOT folded tent-like over the back — four translucent leaf-shaped wings are splayed wide to the rear like a mayfly/damselfly at rest, two per side, fanned apart with clear gaps between them. And there are NO long thread-thin antennae held forward at all; the head end is a bare dark bulb with two pale eye dots and nothing projecting from it. The abdomen is a string of four identical beads with visible constrictions between them, which reads as a machined chain rather than an insect abdomen. The only appendages under the head are three short dark hooked strokes. Subject also occupies maybe 15% of the 440px frame, floating high above a detached black ellipse shadow.
rows.fix: Replace the splayed four-wing fan with a single tent: two hairy opaque wings meeting in a ridge along the dorsal midline, tapering to a rounded tip past the abdomen tip, drab grey-brown with a hair fuzz edge rather than glassy transparency. Add two antennae at least 1.2x body length as thin tapering curves growing forward from the head, converging slightly. Smooth the abdomen bead chain into a soft tapered cone with only faint segment shading. Increase subject scale ~1.8x and drop it toward the shadow.

rows.readsAs: an eel, or a small green snake
rows.defect: The single most explicit mustRead — 'no visible eyes' — is violated by a bright white-and-blue glowing eye dot at the head, the highest-contrast pixel in the whole image. The second mustRead, annular grooves, is entirely missing: the body is a perfectly smooth teal gradient tube with a single continuous cream dorsal stripe running its length, no ring texture anywhere. The head is not blunt or bullet-shaped — it tapers to a fine point, and there is no sensory tentacle. The cream stripe is a uniform-width painted line that reads as sprayed on rather than as a colour change in the skin.
rows.fix: Delete the eye highlight entirely; if any eye is drawn it must be a faint skin-covered dimple with no specular. Add 40-60 annular grooves as shallow transverse shading bands wrapping the tube perpendicular to its centreline, tighter near the head, so they compress on the inside of each body curve. Blunt the snout into a rounded bullet with a slight overhang and add one tiny tentacle bud between nostril and jawline. Break up the dorsal stripe so it varies in width and fades in the shadowed curves.

rows.readsAs: a flat cardboard crocodile silhouette, or a small sail-backed dinosaur toy
rows.defect: All three mustReads fail. The snout is a sharp pointed triangular arrowhead, not broad and blunt — the head is literally a dart tip. The teeth are fully exposed as a row of four hard white rectangles hanging below the jaw with a mouth that is not shut. There is no bony ridge between the eyes; there is one flat pale dot for an eye. The 'armoured back' is rendered as ten separate evenly-spaced pale triangular spikes standing on the dorsal line — identical isoceles cones with straight machined edges and a visible hard seam where each meets the back, so they read as stuck on. The body is an extremely flat wedge, far flatter than aspect 4.5 warrants, with a straight-line ventral edge. The legs are two tiny rectangular blocks with squared-off feet.
rows.fix: Widen and round the snout into an alligator-style blunt spatula with the jawline closed and the teeth hidden behind the lip. Add the paired bony ridge as a raised V of shaded skin between the orbits, and give the eye a proper raised orbital dome. Replace the spike row with overlapping keeled osteoderm rows that continue as texture down onto the flanks and neck rather than sitting only on the spine outline, and blend their bases into the back so no seam is visible. Give the belly a curved sagging profile and rebuild the legs as sprawled limbs with visible upper and lower segments and splayed clawed toes.

rows.readsAs: a generic tan spider — a wolf spider or a jumping spider
rows.defect: The headline mustRead — enormous forward-jutting pincer jaws — is completely absent. Nothing projects from the front of the animal at all; the front end is a bare tan sphere with four small black dots on it. The second mustRead, leg-like pedipalps held forward as extra feelers, is also missing: there are exactly eight legs and no forward pair, so the 'appears to have ten legs' read is lost. The body is two near-perfect tan spheres of nearly equal size butted together with a hard seam between them, which is a geometric-primitive silhouette. The abdomen is smooth with soft airbrushed dimples, not hairy or segmented. The legs are thin straight tapered sticks with hard angular knees and they plug into the sphere at a visible join with no coxal mass.
rows.fix: Add the chelicerae as a massive pair of forward-projecting vertical pincers roughly a third of body length, clearly the widest thing on the front of the animal. Add two pedipalps reaching forward past them, thinner than the legs and held clear of the ground. Shrink and elongate the abdomen so it is a segmented ovoid with visible tergite bands, and make the propeltidium narrower than the abdomen rather than equal. Add setae along every leg and on the abdomen edge to break the silhouette. Grow the legs from a shaded coxal bulge so the join is not a butt seam, and reduce the eye cluster to two eyes on a central tubercle.

rows.readsAs: a small pale gorilla or a snow monkey
rows.defect: The mustRead 'small slender body' fails hard — the torso is a large smooth white egg that dominates the figure, wider than the shoulders and with no waist, so the animal reads as heavy and ape-like. The face is pale grey, not pale pink, and it sits inside a helmet-shaped grey cap that has a hard clean edge like a swim cap rather than a hair boundary. The tail is a uniform-width grey tube that arcs up and left from the hip with a visible hard seam at the attachment and no taper along its length; it curls once but reads as a drawn arc laid on top of the body rather than growing out of the rump. The arms are undifferentiated dark grey lumps merged into the torso sides with no elbow or hand, and the legs are two stubby dark paddles. The blotches on the belly and thigh are soft grey clouds that read as sprayed on top of the white fur.
rows.fix: Narrow the torso substantially and give it a chest-to-hip taper so the body is slender; the head should be a larger fraction of the mass. Warm the face to pink-tan and let the dark cap edge break into irregular hair tufts, especially at the temples where capuchins have the characteristic points. Taper the tail from a thick base that blends into the rump shading down to a thin tip, and coil the terminal third tightly. Separate the arms from the torso silhouette with visible shoulder, elbow and small hands, and stand the figure on all fours per the quadruped posture rather than seated frontal. Replace the airbrushed blotches with fur-direction shading.

rows.readsAs: a green guinea pig, or a tailless rabbit
rows.defect: The mustRead 'blunt squared-off brick-shaped head' fails — the head is a small smooth ball with a rounded muzzle, which is the standard guinea-pig head and the reason this reads as the wrong rodent. Body colour is bright mint green, which for an earth-fauna row is simply the wrong animal colour. The haunch is drawn as a hard-edged lighter crescent on the flank with a visible seam line where it meets the body, so the hip reads as a separate shape pasted on. Whiskers are three perfectly straight hairline strokes of even weight radiating from the muzzle — machined lines, not hairs. The incisors are one solid white rectangle with square corners. The ears are two small pointed cones stuck on the crown; capybara ears are small rounded flaps set far back. Legs are near-invisible stubs, so the 'short partly webbed legs' read gets no support at all.
rows.fix: Square the head off: flatten the top of the skull, extend and blunt the muzzle into a broad brick, and set eye, ear and nostril high along the same upper plane. Recolour to a coarse brown-tan. Dissolve the haunch crescent into gradient shading with no boundary line, and let a few fur strokes cross the boundary. Curve and taper the whiskers with varying length. Round the incisor block and reduce its contrast. Replace the pointed ears with small rounded flaps. Bring the legs out far enough to show blunt splayed toes with webbing between them.

rows.readsAs: a red chicken chick, or a robin
rows.defect: The mustRead black face mask is entirely absent — the face is the same pink-red as the rest of the bird, so the single most identifying cardinal marking is missing. The crest is not a pointed swept-back peak: it is a small two-lobed notched tuft sitting on the crown that reads exactly like a chicken's comb, and it has a hard outline where it meets the head. The bill is a small yellow triangle rather than a thick conical orange cone, and its base does not blend into the face. The tail is a short dark pointed stub angled down; a cardinal's tail is long and roughly body-length. The wing is a dark oval drawn onto the flank with a crisp closed outline and no feather structure, sitting on top of the body rather than folding against it. Subject fills only about 20% of the frame.
rows.fix: Add the black mask as a dark region wrapping the bill base, chin and eye. Rebuild the crest as a single tall triangular peak of feather strokes rising from the crown and sweeping back, with the base feathering into the head so there is no outline. Thicken the bill into a short heavy orange cone with a visible culmen ridge. Lengthen the tail to roughly body length as a narrow squared-off fan. Replace the oval wing patch with layered coverts and a few primary tips that break the body outline. Scale the bird up ~1.6x in frame.

rows.readsAs: a generic silver disc fish — a pomfret or a moonfish
rows.defect: The defining mustRead — oversized eyes for the head — fails outright: the eye is a small dot roughly a tenth of head depth, smaller than average for a fish of this shape, when it should be the dominant feature of the head. The two separate dorsal fins are barely legible; there is one small dark triangle at mid-back and a faint smudge behind it, with the second fin not clearly resolved as its own fin. The mouth is a thin drawn curve, not the large oblique mouth called for. The body is a near-symmetric lens/ellipse — an obvious geometric primitive, with the top and bottom curves mirroring each other and no belly-versus-back asymmetry. The caudal fin is a flat grey triangle set off from the body by a visible hard seam at the peduncle with a colour and value jump, so the tail reads as stuck on. The pectoral fin is a small fan drawn on top of the flank with a crisp outline. Aspect reads closer to 1.6 than the specified 2.2.
rows.fix: Enlarge the eye to roughly 30-35% of head depth with a dark iris and a small specular, and pull it forward and high. Draw two distinctly separated dorsal fins: a short spiny anterior fin and a separate soft posterior fin with a clear gap of bare back between them. Widen the mouth into a large oblique gape reaching back under the eye. Break the ellipse — deepen the belly relative to the back, add a nape rise behind the head, and let the caudal peduncle narrow gradually into the tail with the body colour carrying into the fin rays so the seam disappears. Shift the palette off cold silver toward the reddish-copper the name implies.

rows.readsAs: A beaked whale or a long-snouted dolphin — the ID lands, which is why this is the only non-blocker here.
rows.defect: Best render in the batch, but the pectoral fin is a dark, hard-edged ellipse laid over the pale belly — a clean elliptical boundary, no blend into the flank, no leading/trailing edge. The two dark shapes on the back (mid-body and behind the head) are soft grey smudges with no fin outline at all, so the 'small dorsal fin set far back' does not read as a fin. The tail flukes at the far left dissolve into thin wispy strokes rather than a solid fluke silhouette. The rake marks are present but painted as pale hairline streaks that look like motion lines sprayed over the grey rather than healed scar tissue in the skin. The eye is a perfect white circle with a black dot — too clean and too high-contrast for 'small eyes'. Tusks: two small pale triangles do erupt near the beak, but they sit on the upper contour of the beak so they read as upper-jaw fangs, not lower-jaw male tusks.
rows.fix: Re-grow the pectoral from the body: taper its root into the flank over ~15px with a matched value ramp instead of an ellipse edge, and give it a swept trailing edge. Give the dorsal an actual falcate outline (hooked trailing edge) at ~70% body length and delete the second smudge behind the head. Rebuild the flukes as one solid horizontal fluke pair. Move the two tusks to the ventral contour of the beak so they erupt upward THROUGH the lower jaw line, and drop the rake marks to low-contrast, slightly-raised paired scratches that follow the body curvature.

rows.readsAs: A teal ant, or a cartoon garden bug. Nobody would say honeybee.
rows.defect: It is bright cyan-teal from head to abdomen. There is no amber anywhere — the 'banded amber-and-black abdomen' mustRead is absent, the abdomen is a teal cylinder with pale grey rings. It is a chain of two perfect spheres (head, thorax) plus a ringed drum (abdomen), each a clean geometric primitive with a visible overlap seam between them. Only ONE wing is drawn — a flat grey ellipse resting on top of the abdomen with no venation and no attachment point; four clear veined wings are missing. No pollen basket on any hind leg. Posture is standing on six thin stick legs over a cast shadow, not flying. The 'fur' is a fringe of stiff yellow-green bristles poking out of the sphere outlines — sprayed-on spikes, not a fuzzy coat.
rows.fix: Recolour to amber/ochre with true black bands rendered as pigment IN the cuticle. Replace the sphere chain with a single fused thorax-abdomen mass, thorax wider than the head and merging without a seam. Draw four wings: two long forewings, two short hindwings, translucent with visible vein tracery, rooted at the dorsal thorax. Thicken and clump the hind tibia into a loaded pollen basket. Put it in flight — legs tucked, wings blurred, no ground shadow. Replace the bristle fringe with a soft feathered thorax edge that reads as pile.

rows.readsAs: A tick or a plain ladybird with the spots missing — it does read 'beetle-ish', but as a top-view pill, not an insect.
rows.defect: Top-down view of a near-perfect grey-blue ellipse split by a dead-straight, one-pixel vertical line — a machined seam, not an elytral suture. The head is a single black rounded lump overlapping the top of the ellipse; there is no pronotum, so the 'distinct head, thorax and abdomen sections' mustRead fails outright — head and thorax are one blob. The six legs are thin grey arcs that appear from BEHIND the elytra edge with no coxa, no joint, no attachment — they float alongside the body. Silhouette is an egg. Aspect reads ~1.25, not the 2 in the reference. Two tiny white dots on the black head are the only eyes.
rows.fix: Insert a separate pronotum plate between head and elytra, narrower than the elytra and wider than the head. Make the elytral suture a soft shaded valley that follows the dome's curve and stops at the pronotum, not a ruled line to the edge. Anchor each leg with a visible coxa emerging from under the thorax edge, add femur/tibia/tarsus segmentation and taper. Break the ellipse: widen the elytra shoulders and pinch them toward the apex. Lengthen to the ~2 aspect.

rows.readsAs: A golden carp or mullet. It is read as a fish, not a whale.
rows.defect: The animal is GOLD. 'Uniform white body' is the headline mustRead and it is completely absent. There is no bulging melon — the head tapers to a sharp point, the exact opposite of the beluga's overhanging forehead. No neck crease. The 'low ridge along the back' is only a hairline grey stroke that reads as a rim highlight, not a dorsal ridge. The pectoral is a dark brown ellipse pasted onto the belly with a crisp edge and no root. The tail is a two-lobed fork on a thin peduncle that reads as a fish caudal fin rather than horizontal cetacean flukes.
rows.fix: Recolour to warm-shadowed white/ivory. Rebuild the head: a large rounded melon that bulges forward and overhangs a short blunt mouthline, with a soft crease behind it at the neck. Convert the hairline into a broad, low, bumpy dorsal ridge with visible knuckles. Re-root the pectoral as a short paddle whose base blends into the flank. Redraw the tail as flukes — a broad horizontal blade with a notched centre, not a symmetrical fish fork.

rows.readsAs: A purple toy stork or sandpiper. Nothing about it says bittern.
rows.defect: Flat lilac-purple bird. 'Brown-and-buff streaked camouflage' is entirely missing — the plumage carries no streaking of any kind, just a purple gradient. The bill points forward and slightly DOWN, so the defining reed-mimic bill-to-the-sky freeze pose is absent. The neck is a thin smooth tube with a hard seam where it plugs into the perfectly spherical head and another where it enters the body — the opposite of the thick hunched retractable neck. The wing is an ellipse outline drawn on top of the body ball with a hard contour line; it does not grow out of the shoulder. Body is a plain egg on two yellow stick legs.
rows.fix: Repaint in brown/buff/tan with vertical dark streaking running down the throat and breast — the streaks must follow the neck and body curvature, painted as feather tracts, not overlaid. Point the bill vertically and align the head, neck and body into one continuous upward column. Thicken the neck to at least 2.5x its current width and merge it into the breast with no seam. Replace the drawn-on wing ellipse with layered scapular and covert feather groups whose edges break the body silhouette.

rows.readsAs: A blue ant. Directly confusable with the Bee in this same batch — the two are the same model in different colours.
rows.defect: Cornflower BLUE, not 'stubby compact dark body'. It is the same three-perfect-spheres-in-a-row chassis as the Bee in this batch, recoloured — head sphere, thorax sphere, abdomen sphere, each with a visible overlap seam. No strongly humped thorax and no bowed head: the head sits level and forward, the thorax is a plain ball. Wings are ONE opaque olive teardrop lying on the thorax/abdomen join, not short broad clear wings. Two long curved antennae sweep forward off the head — a black fly's antennae are tiny stubs; these read ant/wasp. Legs are straight, unsegmented, uniform-width blue lines with machined ends. It is standing over a shadow, not flying.
rows.fix: Recolour to near-black with a smoky sheen. Fuse the spheres: build the thorax as a pronounced dorsal hump that rises well above the head and rolls forward so the head tucks under it — that hump-over-bowed-head profile IS the black fly. Shorten the antennae to stubs. Replace the single teardrop with a pair of short, broad, translucent wings held out from the thorax with faint venation. Taper and segment the legs. Since Bee and Black Fly share one chassis today, they must be differentiated by silhouette, not by hue.

rows.readsAs: A small yellow pike or barracuda — a generic elongate fish with a spiky fin, not a blenny.
rows.defect: The dorsal is a row of four hard sawtooth triangles sitting on the middle third of the back only — 'single long continuous dorsal fin down the whole back' fails, and the spikes are machined isosceles triangles with straight edges. No cirri tufts above the eyes at all. The head is a pointed wedge, not a blunt bulldog head; the eye is a small white ring at the very tip of the snout instead of high-set and bulging. The ventral contour is a dead-straight line for most of the body length. The pelvic/anal fins are flat brown triangles overlaid on the yellow flank with crisp edges. The whole animal occupies only about 40% of the 440px frame, so it renders tiny and detail-starved.
rows.fix: Run one continuous dorsal from just behind the head to the tail base, with a soft undulating membrane edge and spine ribs showing through — no isolated sawtooth block. Blunt the head into a steep, rounded bulldog forehead and move the eyes up and forward so they bulge off the top contour. Add branched feathery cirri above each eye. Curve the ventral line. Blend the fin bases into the flank instead of overlaying triangles. Scale the render up ~1.6x in frame.

rows.readsAs: A teal aquarium damselfish. It reads as sighted and brightly coloured — the two things a blind cave fish is not.
rows.defect: Two mustReads fail simultaneously. It is bright teal-cyan, not 'pale pinkish unpigmented' — cave-adapted albinism is the entire point of this animal and there is none. And it HAS a visible eye: a white ring with a dark pupil sitting behind the snout, when eyes are specified hidden and the head must be smooth and blank. The body is a sharp lens/almond with two straight converging edges meeting at a hard point at the snout, so the silhouette reads as a folded paper shape. Two flat, hard-edged triangles are laid over the mid-body and back as fins — visible facets, not fin membranes. The caudal fan attaches through a narrow stalk with a hard join line.
rows.fix: Recolour to translucent pinkish-white with subtle blood-vessel warmth and a faint suggestion of internal structure. Delete the eye entirely and cover the socket with smooth skin — a shallow depression at most, no ring, no pupil. Round the snout and curve the dorsal and ventral profiles so the body is a soft fusiform, not a lens. Replace the flat triangles with soft-rayed dorsal and anal fins whose bases fade into the flank, and thicken the caudal peduncle so the tail flows out of the body.

rows.readsAs: a plush toy monkey or a generic cartoon ape sitting down — nobody would say baboon
rows.defect: No muzzle at all — the head is a smooth ball with a flat human-ish face, a tiny button nose and two lips, plus round disc ears pasted flat on the sides. All three mustReads fail: no long dog-like muzzle, the tail is one smooth continuous C-curve with no kink at the base, and there is no shoulder cape (the shoulders are bare). The torso is a hard-edged capsule with a light rim stroke and a STRAIGHT HORIZONTAL LINE across the bottom — a machined edge. Both arms and both legs are plain dark tubes that terminate against that capsule with a visible hard seam; nothing grows out of the body. The orange dappling reads as blobs airbrushed on top of a solid fill rather than fur.
rows.fix: Replace the ball head with a wedge skull: extend a long tapered muzzle forward ~0.5x head length, set the eyes close together high on the brow-ridge, add the deep-set orbits. Build the tail in two segments — a short erect base segment rising ~40deg then a hard break into a hanging distal segment (not a spline). Add a shoulder mane as coarse hair strands overhanging the upper arms so the shoulder silhouette is ragged, not smooth. Kill the capsule: the torso outline must be a barrel that narrows into the pelvis and the flat bottom line must go. Blend limb roots into the torso with shared fur strokes crossing the join so no seam is visible.

rows.readsAs: a teal leaf, or a green pepper with a snake head glued to one end
rows.defect: It is TEAL/cyan, not bright yellow — the single most diagnostic feature of the species is inverted. The body is a flat lens: the entire underside is one perfectly straight horizontal line and the left (tail) end is cut off by a straight diagonal chamfer, so the silhouette reads as a leaf or a chile pepper, not a soft slug. The head is a small hooked nub joined to the mass by a thin neck with a hard seam — it is stuck ON, and it reads as a tiny snake or bird head. Only one indistinct pair of tentacles with a single white dot; no lower oral pair. No pneumostome / breathing hole and no mantle saddle anywhere on the back. The dark blotches are diffuse smudges sprayed over the fill, not skin.
rows.fix: Recolour to saturated banana yellow with olive-brown blotching. Give the foot a rippled, slightly undulating contact line instead of a ruler-straight one, and round the posterior into a tapered point rather than a chamfer. Grow the head out of the body as a continuous swell — no neck, no seam — and put FOUR tentacles on it: two long upper optic stalks with dark eye tips, two short lower sensory ones. Add the raised mantle saddle over the front third with a visible pneumostome hole on its right side.

rows.readsAs: a wastebasket or a nuclear cooling tower
rows.defect: It is a smooth flared cylinder with a perfectly elliptical rim outlined in a uniform grey stroke — a geometric primitive, an industrial cooling tower silhouette. Every mustRead fails. There are no fused plates: the wall is one continuous gradient with soft brown blobs airbrushed on it, zero sutures, zero chalky plate edges. There are no trapdoor/operculum plates — the summit is an open hole showing a flat brown-to-black gradient. There are no cirri; nothing emerges from the opening at all.
rows.fix: Break the cone into 4-6 discrete overlapping wall plates with visible vertical suture lines and slightly mismatched top edges, so the rim reads as a ragged crown rather than a drawn ellipse. Give the wall a chalky, weathered, ridged texture growing with the plate geometry. Seat two beaked operculum plates in the aperture, meeting on a diagonal slit. Sweep a fan of feathery, curled cirri out of that slit past the rim to break the machined circle.

rows.readsAs: a needlefish or a green pike with a comb glued under its nose
rows.defect: The teeth are a row of ~8 identical white triangles hanging entirely BELOW and OUTSIDE the body silhouette, evenly spaced like a comb stamped under the snout. There is no mouth line and no jaw opening at all — the snout is a solid closed wedge, so the underslung jaw does not read. The eye is a perfect white donut ring with a dark centre, sitting half outside the dorsal contour. The second (rear) dorsal fin is a translucent grey-green dome floating BEHIND the body with no attachment — an off-body artifact rather than a fin growing off the back. The pectoral is a hard-edged triangular fan with a straight seam at its root. Body proportion is closer to 6:1 than the specified 7:1 and reasonably pike-like, which is the one thing working.
rows.fix: Cut an actual mouth: split the snout into upper and lower jaws along a long gape line, project the lower jaw forward past the upper so it is visibly underslung, and set the fangs INSIDE that gape at irregular sizes with the largest canines forward. Replace the ring eye with a filled dark iris and a soft highlight, moved fully inside the silhouette. Anchor both dorsals to the dorsal contour with a fleshy base that shares the body's shading, and widen the gap between them so the two-dorsal read is unmistakable. Feather the pectoral root instead of a straight cut.

rows.readsAs: a generic green deep-sea fish wearing an astronaut bubble helmet
rows.defect: The transparent dome is a literal perfect circle with a hard grey stroke, and it extends far past the head into empty background — the right half of the ring encloses nothing but dark space, so it reads as a bubble helmet placed near the fish rather than a fluid-filled chamber that IS the head. Inside it the eyes are two boxy extruded cylinders with straight vertical sides and flat facets meeting at a hard rectangular corner — obvious geometric primitives, and they are green-grey rather than the vivid green the reference calls for. The two dark scent pits at the front of the face are absent entirely; there is nothing where the false eyes should be. The snout below the dome is a hard-edged flat triangular wedge. A row of perfectly identical circles runs along the belly like stamped photophores, and there are stray faint straight hatch lines floating off-body above the head.
rows.fix: Make the dome the head: fit it to the skull so the transparent shell bulges out of the forehead and its lower margin merges into the snout — no free-floating arc over background, no uniform outline stroke (use a refraction highlight and a soft rim instead). Rebuild the eyes as rounded organic barrels with domed emerald lenses on top clearly aimed UPWARD through the dome, no flat facets or box corners. Add the two dark scent pits low on the front of the face. Vary the belly photophores in size/spacing and delete the off-body hatch lines.

rows.readsAs: a mackerel or tuna with a turbine intake bolted to its face
rows.defect: The gaping mouth is rendered as a flat dark ELLIPSE PLATE stuck on the front of the snout, filled with straight horizontal hatch lines and ringed with a hard grey outline — it reads as a jet engine intake or a loudspeaker, not a mouth. The pointed snout wedge visibly pierces through this disc, leaving a hard seam where the two overlap, and the disc's outline juts well beyond the body silhouette on all sides. The gill slits are only five short curved strokes confined to the flank — nowhere near encircling the head as the reference requires. The dorsal fin and pelvic fin are separate translucent grey blobs floating BEHIND the body outline with no connection to it. The eye is the same white donut ring primitive used on the Bass and Barracuda.
rows.fix: Model the mouth as a three-dimensional cavity, not a disc: an irregular oval aperture with a fleshy upper lip continuous with the snout, a distended lower jaw, and dark interior shading with visible gill-raker texture. Its rim must be part of the head silhouette. Push the gill slits into a long vertical series that wraps from the dorsal ridge down to the throat, each one a deep organic slot. Attach the dorsal to the back with a broad drooping base sharing the body's tone, and the pelvics likewise — no detached grey shapes. Filled iris, not a ring.

rows.readsAs: a generic pink cartoon fish with a crown behind it — could equally be the Barracuda or Barreleye from this same batch, they share the identical almond body, donut eye and triangular fan pectoral
rows.defect: The dorsal fin is a dark purple sawtooth crown with a perfectly straight bottom edge, sitting BEHIND the body with a clearly visible gap and seam — it is a shape pasted behind the fish, not a fin rising out of the back. It is one uniform zigzag, so the spiny-front-joined-to-soft-rear mustRead fails outright. The body is a double-pointed almond lens: the head end tapers to a needle point, so there is no head, no jaw hinge, and no large bucket mouth — just a faint dark sliver. It is a lens shape, not a deep laterally compressed body with a rounded brow. The eye is the white donut ring primitive again, half outside the outline, and the pectoral is a hard triangular fan with a straight-cut root. Colour is hot magenta.
rows.fix: Give the fish a head: blunt the anterior into a rounded brow with a real jaw hinge behind the eye and a wide, deep, hinged mouth that clearly hangs open. Rebuild the dorsal as two joined sections growing from the dorsal ridge — sharp straight spines in front, a rounded soft-rayed lobe behind, joined by a low notch — rooted into the back with shared shading and no gap. Deepen the body vertically and give it the compressed slab profile with a broad flank. Filled iris. Feather the pectoral root.

rows.readsAs: a moth
rows.defect: This reads unambiguously as a MOTH, not a bat. The two long tapered spikes on the head curve outward like antennae, not ears. The wings are smooth broad triangular lobes with a scalloped trailing edge and a highlight along the leading edge only — there is not a single finger strut visible anywhere in the membrane, which is the one feature the note explicitly flags as mandatory. Each wing meets the body at a hard straight-cut seam. There is no uropatagium: the legs are two bare thin sticks with nothing between them and no tail. Two short straight hairline sticks poke out horizontally from the wing bases at left and right — stray off-body straight-line artifacts. The body is a featureless olive blob with no fur texture, and the cyan glowing eyes read as insect eyes.
rows.fix: Draw the hand: four elongated finger bones fanning from a wrist near the leading edge to each scallop tip, visible as raised struts with the membrane sagging between them — that alone converts moth to bat. Replace the antennae with broad rounded ears set forward on the skull, with visible tragus and inner-ear folds. Span a tail membrane between the hind legs enclosing a short tail, so the lower silhouette is one continuous sheet not two loose sticks. Blend wing root into the shoulder with fur strokes crossing the join. Delete the two straight sticks at the wing bases. Add fur texture to the torso and make the eyes small and dark, not glowing cyan.

rows.readsAs: A small teal dragonfly toy
rows.defect: No mandibles at all. The head is a plain teal ball with two small dark eye-dots and three tiny hook strokes beneath it (legs) — nothing resembling the huge crossed sickle jaws that ARE the dobsonfly. The wings are four hard-edged grey blades radiating from one point behind the thorax with a visible hard seam where each meets the body, and they read as stiff paddles, not long smoky net-veined membranes folded past the abdomen (no venation whatsoever). The abdomen is a chain of five near-perfect alternating dark/teal circles — a bead string, a geometric primitive repeat, not a soft flabby elongated body. It is also the same template as Dragonfly in this batch, recoloured teal.
rows.fix: Add the defining organ: two long forward-projecting curved mandibles crossing at the tips, at least 0.5x body length in the male, growing out of the head capsule with no seam. Replace the four blade-wings with two pairs of long low-alpha membranes reaching past the abdomen tip, carrying a fine irregular cross-vein net. Replace the bead-chain abdomen with one continuous tapering soft tube whose segment boundaries are shallow shading ripples, not discrete circles. Blend wing roots into the thorax with a shared gradient so no hard line remains.

rows.readsAs: A generic green fish, maybe a mullet
rows.defect: There is no beak. The head just tapers to a blunt point with a tiny black dot eye — no rostrum, no upcurved smiling jawline, no mouth line at all. The dorsal fin is a leaf-shaped dark ellipse sitting on the back with a hard visible seam and zero sickle sweep; the pectoral is an identical detached-looking ellipse pasted on the flank, clearly a separate object rather than a limb growing from the body. The tail is a notched vertical fish caudal fin, not horizontal crescent flukes. A stray pale grey ellipse floats above the back near the shoulder, unattached to any surface — an off-body artifact. The whole silhouette is a smooth green capsule.
rows.fix: Build a real rostrum: pull the snout into a short cylindrical beak set off by a melon crease, and draw the jawline as an upward-curving arc past the eye. Rebuild the dorsal as a backswept sickle with a concave trailing edge, and root both fins with a fillet/gradient that dissolves the seam. Rotate the tail to read horizontally — two crescent flukes with a central notch, seen edge-on wide rather than a vertical fish fin. Delete the floating grey ellipse or attach it as a blowhole on the head crown.

rows.readsAs: A yellow chick or a canary
rows.defect: Reads as a chick, not a dove. The bill is a small orange triangle with no fleshy cere at the base and no dove taper. The wing is a hard-edged dark-brown crescent laid flat on the flank with a sharp boundary line — a decal, not plumage, and the whole flank carries a flat yellow-green oval facet inset inside it that looks like a lit panel. The tail is a single thin dark spike, not a slim tapering fan of feathers. The body is a rounded blob with an aspect near 1.4, shorter and dumpier than the 1.9 the row calls for, and the round head sits on the breast with no neck transition.
rows.fix: Lengthen the body to ~1.9 and pull the tail into a layered tapering wedge of 3-4 feather planes instead of one spike. Replace the crescent decal wing with feather groups that emerge from the shoulder and overlap onto the flank, softening the leading boundary. Remove the flat oval facet. Add a small pale cere bulge at the bill base and slim the bill to a slight downward taper.

rows.readsAs: A red needlefish or a barracuda-like eel
rows.defect: The glowing chin barbel is completely absent — the defining feature of the animal is missing. The needle fangs are present and legible along the jaw, and the photophore row is present, but the photophores are twelve identical evenly-spaced blue ellipses in a perfectly straight line, which reads as a sprayed-on decal stripe rather than the fish's own light organs. The dorsal edge of the body is a dead-straight machined line from behind the head to mid-body, giving a blade/scalpel silhouette rather than an eel-like body. The tail is a tiny frayed brush that barely reads as a fin.
rows.fix: Add the barbel: a long filament hanging from the chin, at least head-length, ending in a glowing bulb with a soft bloom. Break the straight dorsal edge into a gentle undulating curve and thin the body toward the tail. Vary photophore size, spacing and brightness along the row and let them sit slightly below the body midline so they read as organs in the skin. Build the caudal into a small but readable lobed fin.

rows.readsAs: A purple cartoon bug — indistinguishable from the Dobsonfly in this same batch
rows.defect: The eyes fail the mustRead outright — the head is a small purple ball with two tiny dark dots on top, not huge globe compound eyes filling the head. The abdomen is a chain of five discrete alternating light/dark circles, a bead string, not a long slender rod. The four wings are hard grey blades all radiating from a single point behind the thorax and swept backward over the abdomen, contradicting the note that wings stay spread flat; they carry no venation and each meets the body at a hard seam. It is pixel-for-pixel the same template as Dobsonfly in this batch, only recoloured purple.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as two enormous hemispherical compound eyes that meet at the top and occupy nearly the whole head volume, with a faceted micro-texture. Replace the bead-chain abdomen with a single long slender tapering rod ~2x thorax length, segmented by shading only. Reposition the wings out to the sides, held flat and roughly perpendicular to the body, two pairs of distinct lengths, each with a fine net of cross-veins and a pterostigma, rooted into the thorax with no seam. Differentiate the template from Dobsonfly's.

rows.readsAs: A dark grebe or coot, or a wooden decoy
rows.defect: The bill is a sharp yellow cone/wedge tapering to a point — the exact opposite of the flat spatulate mustRead; it reads as a heron or grebe bill. No webbed feet are visible at all (they are hidden under water rings, so the third mustRead cannot read). The body is a plain dark rounded dome, effectively a capsule, with no boat-shaped keel or stern, and the head sits on it as a separate ball with a visible boundary at the neck. The water is three perfect concentric ellipse outlines and a flat elliptical disc — machined geometric primitives sitting under the animal.
rows.fix: Flatten and widen the bill into a spatula: broad, rounded at the tip, with a nail at the end and a slight dorsal dip. Reshape the body into a boat hull — rising breast, flat waterline, upturned stern with tail coverts. Fuse head into neck into body with continuous contour rather than stacked balls. Either raise the pose so the webbed feet read, or drop the biped mustRead for the swimming pose. Break the perfect concentric ripple ellipses into irregular, varying-thickness wave arcs.

rows.readsAs: A grey armoured fish, something like a sturgeon or a whale-shark toy
rows.defect: The body is banded with about ten evenly spaced parallel dark stripes running top to bottom — a sprayed-on segment pattern that makes it read as an armoured or larval animal; a dugong's hide is smooth. Two thin dark whisker-like strokes hang detached beneath the mid-belly, touching nothing — off-body artifacts. The flipper is a plain grey ellipse pasted on the flank with a hard visible outline where it meets the body. The head is a separate paler capsule butted onto the trunk with a clear seam, and the snout, while it does carry a small bristle cluster, is not the big downturned muzzle disc the row asks for. The notched fluke and absence of a dorsal fin both read correctly.
rows.fix: Delete the vertical banding entirely and replace with soft blotchy scarring and broad top-lit shading. Remove the two floating belly strokes. Root the flipper with a shoulder fillet and a gradient so the outline disappears. Merge head into body as one continuous form and enlarge the muzzle into a broad downturned disc that overhangs the mouth, with the bristles growing from its face rather than sitting beside it.

rows.readsAs: A pink ladybird, or a mushroom
rows.defect: The legs are six thin grey hairline arcs floating outside the shell outline with a visible gap at their inner ends — they do not grow from the body, and none of them is a toothed rake-like foreleg; they read as motion whiskers. The head is a dark trapezoid with a flat straight top edge stuck onto the dome with a hard seam, more mushroom cap or bonnet than a flat spade-shaped rake, and there is no horn. The body is a near-perfect magenta egg split by one dead-straight vertical line — the elytra suture is a ruled line, not a seam between two shells, and the dome carries a smooth airbrush gradient rather than a glossy armoured highlight.
rows.fix: Rebuild the legs as thick jointed limbs emerging from under the elytra edge, with the forelegs broadened into flat tibiae carrying 4-5 visible teeth along the outer edge. Reshape the head into a wide flat semicircular clypeal spade projecting forward beyond the pronotum, fused into a distinct pronotum shield rather than butted on, and add a horn. Make the elytral suture two overlapping shell halves with a slight offset and shadow instead of one ruled line, and add a tight specular highlight plus a rim light so the shell reads as hard glossy chitin.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon fish / leaf-shaped aquarium fish — closest to a spiky-backed sunfish silhouette; not identifiable as a damselfish
rows.defect: The body is a symmetric pointed lens/almond — sharp points at both nose and tail joint — not the deep rounded oval of a damselfish. The dorsal fin is a row of five hard-edged dark triangles floating on a separate darker strip laid ON TOP of the back: there is a clear straight seam where the spiky strip meets the teal body, so the fin is stuck on rather than growing out. The tail is a single solid dark triangle wedge with a straight leading edge butted against the body — NOT forked, so the 'forked tail' mustRead fails outright. A second faint triangle sits on the flank as a pectoral fin with the same pasted-on hard edge, and the teal-to-white gradient runs as a flat vertical wash rather than as the fish's own countershading. Only the eye (white ring, black pupil) is convincing.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette as a deep oval with a blunt rounded snout and a narrowing caudal peduncle instead of a two-pointed lens. Replace the triangle-row dorsal with one continuous membrane whose base is drawn from the same body outline path (soft ray lines inside it, no separate strip, no seam). Replace the tail wedge with a true forked caudal: two lobes with a concave notch between them, attached through a tapering peduncle rather than butted flat. Feather the pectoral fin base into the flank with a soft alpha ramp.

rows.readsAs: a bead-bodied toy ant or a cartoon mosquito; several people would say 'ant with a wing glued on' before 'damselfly'
rows.defect: The abdomen is a string of six discrete pink spheres with visible dark gaps between them — a bead necklace, not the needle-thin continuous stick a damselfly must have. The mustRead 'needle-thin stick abdomen' fails; these are literal geometric primitives (perfect circles with specular highlights) rather than a tapering tube. The thorax and head are two more spheres, so the whole animal is seven balls in a row with hard seams at every junction. The wings are a single flat white blade fanned out horizontally behind the thorax, spread and overlapping the abdomen — the mustRead requires wings held closed together over the back at rest, and these read as one paddle, not two pairs. The head is a plain ball with both eyes crowded on the same upper-left surface; there is no hammerhead, no widely separated lateral eyes. Legs are three scratchy pink lines under the head with no attachment structure.
rows.fix: Replace the sphere chain with one continuous tapering stroke of near-constant thin width (about 3–4 px at 440), segmented only by faint darker banding drawn INSIDE the tube, not by gaps. Redraw the wings as four narrow lancet wings held together and angled up over the back, roughly parallel to the abdomen, with visible nodus/pterostigma spots. Widen the head laterally into the classic dumbbell/hammerhead with one large hemispherical eye at each far end. Grow six legs from the thorax with a defined coxa where they meet it.

rows.readsAs: a herring or sardine with LEDs on it — a shallow-water baitfish, not a bathypelagic predator
rows.defect: This is a bright silver, pale-bellied surface fish. The mustRead 'specks of photophores' is the only one satisfied (a neat row of cyan dots along the ventral line). 'Oversized jaw crowded with needle fangs' is entirely absent — the mouth is a thin white hairline at the snout tip with no gape and no teeth at all. 'Large light-gathering eyes' fails — the eye is a tiny dot barely larger than a photophore, smaller in relative terms than the damselfish's. 'Black soft body' fails — the body is light silver-grey with a bright white belly, the palette of a herring. On top of the mustReads: the dorsal fin is a flat grey oval smeared onto the back with a hard boundary, the caudal is a plain dark triangle with a straight butt joint, and the flank triangle (pectoral) is a hard-edged wedge sprayed on. The photophore dots are also a mechanically even, equally spaced row that reads as printed decoration rather than embedded organs.
rows.fix: Recolour the body to near-black/deep charcoal with only a faint sheen, keeping the photophores as the brightest thing in the frame. Enlarge the eye to roughly 3x current diameter with a glassy dark iris. Rebuild the head as an oversized hinged jaw opening well past the eye line, with a comb of irregular needle teeth on both jaws (varied length, slightly curved back). Replace the oval dorsal blob with a low soft-rayed fin whose base blends into the dorsal contour, and jitter the photophore spacing and brightness so they read as organs, not a dotted line.

rows.readsAs: a mushroom on stilts, or a long-legged spider — in this same batch it is easy to confuse with the Deer Tick, which is also a dome on stiff radial legs
rows.defect: Zero of the three mustReads are present. There are no ear-like fins anywhere on the mantle — the mantle is a bare rounded dome. There is no webbed umbrella between the arms; the arms are fully separate. The body is opaque, hard-edged and glossy plum rather than soft translucent gelatinous. On top of that, the reference calls for prominent eyes and the render has NO eyes at all — the face is a blank dome. The arms are the worst failure: four of them are short, straight, blunt-ended cylinders hanging straight down like table legs with flat cut-off tips, and two are long smooth arcs sweeping out to the frame edges at a near-constant width. All of them meet the mantle at an abrupt shoulder with a visible seam, and I count six, not eight. No suckers, no taper.
rows.fix: Add the two paddle fins as soft lobes rising off the upper mantle, drawn from the mantle's own contour so no seam shows. Draw the eight arms from a common web: a continuous skin sheet spanning the upper third of every arm, generated as one filled path with the arms so it cannot separate. Taper every arm from a thick base to a fine curling tip (no flat ends, no constant width) and vary their curvature. Add two large dark eyes on the mantle sides. Drop opacity slightly and soften the rim to sell gelatinous flesh.

rows.readsAs: a red sea fan / gorgonian from a warm shallow reef — the exact opposite of the Lophelia-type cold-water colony specified
rows.defect: The colour is a saturated crimson/scarlet, directly contradicting the mustRead 'pale branching thicket with no algal colour' — this is a tropical red gorgonian palette, exactly the thing the note tells us not to draw. The branching itself is the strongest thing in the batch (good recursive fine twigs, believable fan), but the branch TIPS are bare pointed twiglets with no cup polyps, so the second mustRead also fails. The pink blobs that presumably stand in for polyps are floating in the empty space around the lower trunks, not on any tip — off-body artifacts hovering against the background. The five basal trunks are perfectly uniform-width tubes with identical rounded caps and a straight vertical run — machined capsule primitives that do not taper into the branch network above them, leaving a visible change of drawing language between base and crown.
rows.fix: Recolour to chalky bone/ivory white with faint grey-violet shadow; remove all red. Move the polyp blobs onto the branch tips and redraw them as small flared calyces with a visible cup mouth. Retaper the basal trunks so they thicken toward the holdfast and thin continuously into the branches, with an irregular, slightly knobbly edge instead of constant-width rounded rectangles.

rows.readsAs: a red spider or a cartoon ant — and inside this batch it reads as the same creature type as the Deep-Sea Octopus (rounded dome plus stiff radiating sticks)
rows.defect: The body is two perfect glossy spheres of nearly equal size butted together with a hard crescent seam — a snowman, not a flat unsegmented teardrop. Both spheres carry a bright specular highlight that makes them read as billiard balls. The mustRead 'flat teardrop unsegmented body' fails on both counts (it is neither flat nor unsegmented). 'Barbed spear mouthparts jutting ahead' is missing entirely — nothing projects in front of the head sphere. The reference says eyes hidden, but a cluster of six black dots is painted on the front sphere and reads unmistakably as spider eyes. The legs are thin straight sticks of uniform width, radiating in flat splayed fans from the seam region; several do not touch the body at all, leaving a visible gap, and they have no joints, no taper and no tarsal claws.
rows.fix: Collapse the two spheres into one low flat teardrop with a matte, faintly pebbled cuticle and kill the specular highlights. Remove the eye dots. Add a forward-projecting capitulum: a short dark hypostome with backward-facing barbs plus two stubby palps flanking it. Redraw all eight legs with a thick coxa growing out of the body edge (no gaps), a femur/tibia bend, taper to fine tips, and bunch them all toward the front third as the reference requires instead of fanning evenly front and back.
