rows.readsAs: an owl — correctly — but a dark woodland tawny/screech owl, not a desert species
rows.defect: It does read as an owl — round facial disc, two large forward-facing eyes, small ear tufts and a hooked yellow bill are all legible, and that is the strongest read in the batch. But the mustRead 'pale sandy-buff plumage' fails badly: the bird is dark slate charcoal, almost black-blue, which is a night/tawny colouring with nothing desert about it. 'Feathered legs' also fails — the legs are bare, thin, bright yellow twigs with no feathering at all, and they are the highest-contrast element on the whole bird, pulling the eye away from the face. The proportion is wrong too: the reference asks for 0.8 (taller than wide, perched) and the render is clearly wider than tall, with a horizontally slumped body. The wing is a plain grey-lavender oval pasted on the flank with a continuous hard outline, and the tail is a solid dark triangle projecting off the rear with a straight seam where it meets the body.
rows.fix: Shift the plumage to warm sandy buff/pale ochre with soft cream mottling; keep only the facial disc rim darker. Stand the bird up — narrow and heighten the body so the silhouette is taller than wide, tucking the tail down rather than out. Feather the tarsi (fluffy pale leggings down to small dark toes) and desaturate the feet. Replace the oval wing patch with a folded wing whose covert rows and primary tips are drawn as feather groups blending into the flank, and blend the tail base into the body contour instead of butting a triangle against it.

rows.readsAs: a peeled egg with a hat on, or a generic pale ladybug seen from above — nothing about it says aquatic diving beetle
rows.defect: The elytra are a large flat cream-white perfect egg-oval bisected by a dead-straight, ruler-thin grey line — a machined edge running the full length. There is no pale yellow rim; the whole shell is uniformly pale, so the mustRead rim contrast has nothing to sit against and fails. The head/pronotum is a separate dark grey mushroom-cap blob sitting on the top of the egg with a hard curved seam and a slight overhang — plainly stuck on, not grown out, and it is the only dark mass on the animal so the seam is the first thing the eye finds. The 'silver air bubble under the wing cases' is absent. The legs fail worst: six thin grey arcs of constant width float in the background with a clear gap between each leg and the shell edge — they touch nothing. They are also all identical smooth crescents, so the hair-fringed oar-like hind legs the mustRead demands do not exist; nothing is flattened, nothing is fringed, and the hind pair is the same as the front pair. Colour reads as a pale albino egg rather than a beetle.
rows.fix: Darken the elytra to olive/blackish-brown and add a true marginal band of pale yellow following the shell outline, plus the same band on the pronotum. Replace the straight centre line with a slightly irregular suture and add faint longitudinal striae. Reshape the pronotum into a trapezoid that shares its edge with the elytra base and merges with the body silhouette (no overhang, no seam), with the head narrower in front of it. Attach every leg at a visible coxa on the body edge; broaden and flatten the hind pair into paddles and line their trailing edge with a comb of swimming hairs. Add a bright silver crescent of trapped air at the elytra tip.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon jellyfish or a green alien balloon-head, not an octopus
rows.defect: The mantle is a near-perfect bright-green sphere with two tiny cartoon dot eyes sitting ON its front face, mid-bulb — the eyes are supposed to sit BELOW the mantle where the arms attach, and they read as pupils painted on a balloon rather than bulging eyeballs. No horizontal slit pupil (both pupils are round black dots with a white catchlight). I can count only about five arm strands, all the same hairline thickness with no taper mass, no suckers anywhere, and they emerge from a dark undershadow rather than visibly growing out of the mantle base. A flat dark ellipse floats behind the bulb like a halo with no anatomical role. Two of the three mustReads (suckered arms of unequal length, slit pupil) are absent.
rows.fix: Split the silhouette into two masses: a pear/bag mantle on top, then a distinct visceral hump below it carrying two large bulging eyes with a horizontal bar-shaped pupil in each. Rebuild the arms as eight tapering cones of visibly unequal length whose bases fuse into a webbed skirt (no gap, no shadow join), each with a scalloped inner edge and a double row of sucker discs shrinking toward the tip. Kill the halo ellipse.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon newt or a bath-toy lizard
rows.defect: The tail is a separate smooth cream capsule that overlaps the trunk with a hard visible line across the flank — a textbook stuck-on part, and it is the same width along its whole length so it reads as a sausage laid alongside the body, not a tail growing from it. The head is a rounded ball with a single round dot eye and a drawn-on smiley mouth line; it is not broad, not flattened, not a shovel. The flanks are perfectly smooth with zero wrinkle or skin folds — the only surface interest is a scatter of soft yellow spots that sit on the surface like airbrush. All four legs are identical grey matchsticks with no thigh mass.
rows.fix: Make the body one continuous tapering tube from snout to tail tip with no seam, and flatten the last third laterally into a paddle/rudder with a fin crest. Widen and flatten the skull into a spade with the eyes as tiny dark lidless dots set on TOP of the flat head, and replace the smiley with a wide slit mouth line that follows the head's outer contour. Add a lateral row of loose fleshy fold lobes along each flank so the outline is scalloped rather than smooth. Replace the stick legs with short splayed limbs having a visible upper-limb mass and four splayed toes.

rows.readsAs: a squid, just barely — but at a glance it is the same creature as the Giant Octopus in a different colour
rows.defect: Built from the exact same kit as the Giant Octopus in this batch — vertical glossy egg bulb, two round dot eyes with white catchlights placed on the bulb's face, thin hairline strands below — only the hue (teal) and the bulb's egg-vs-sphere shape differ. It is posed upright/sessile, not swimming. The two clubbed feeding tentacles ARE present and legible (the pale cyan pair with bulb tips), which is the one mustRead that lands. The triangular tail fins are missing: at the mantle's TOP there is only a soft dark blur that reads as an out-of-focus halo, and it is at the wrong end anyway since the mantle tip points up. Eyes are small dots, not dinner plates.
rows.fix: Lay the mantle horizontally into a torpedo and put two hard-edged triangular fins on the pointed tail end, joined to the mantle by a continuous flare rather than pasted on. Enlarge the eyes to at least 3x their current diameter with a dark lidded rim so they read as dinner plates, and move them down onto the head mass between mantle and arm crown. Give the eight short arms visible thickness and sucker rows so they separate from the two long tentacles, and put toothed sucker rings on the club tips. Change the arm-strand construction so it does not share a silhouette with Giant_Octopus.png.

rows.readsAs: a sea anemone, or a stylised cyan mushroom/fountain
rows.defect: The plume is CYAN/teal, not blood-red — the single most identifying feature of this animal is the wrong colour, and the tube is the same cyan rather than white chitin, so the whole organism is one flat monochrome. It is one lone cone, not a cluster of tubes. The cone is a straight-sided machined funnel with a perfectly elliptical rim and a hard dark ring inside the opening; there is no chitin banding or growth ridging. The plume filaments are short stubby flat blades splaying sideways from the rim like a shaving brush rather than a tall soft feathery crown, and where they meet the rim there is a hard cut line.
rows.fix: Recolour the plume deep arterial red with darker crimson in the shadowed filaments, and the tube bone-white/ivory with faint horizontal growth bands and a slightly irregular, non-elliptical rim. Add two or three shorter neighbouring tubes at different heights behind it for the cluster read. Make the plume taller than it is wide, built from many fine barbed filaments that converge into a single stalk disappearing INTO the tube mouth so there is no seam at the rim.

rows.readsAs: an ant
rows.defect: This is an ant. Three separate glossy cream beads in a row (head, then two near-identical ellipsoid segments) with obvious pinch seams between them, six hairline grey stick legs and two curved antennae. None of the three mustReads is present: the body is not a flat oval brown leaf (it is a pale bumpy three-part solid), the front leg is the same thin stick as the others with no raptorial hook or thickened femur, and there is no beak under the head. Colour is cream/white instead of brown. It is also rendered far too small in the 440px frame, occupying maybe a fifth of the canvas.
rows.fix: Replace the three-bead body with a single flattened brown oval shield — head fused into the thorax, folded wing-cases meeting in a centre line down the back, a pale outer margin. Give the front pair thick muscled femora ending in a curved sickle tibia folded back against them, clearly heavier than the four swimming legs, and put flattened hair-fringed paddles on the hind pair. Add a short dark stylet beak tucked under the front of the head. Drop the antennae (they are hidden in this animal) and scale the render up so the body fills the frame width.

rows.readsAs: a gorilla, or a yeti
rows.defect: The arms are shorter than the legs — they are two stubby dark grey paddles hanging at the hips, ending well above the ground, with no hands at all, let alone long hook-shaped ones. The dominant mass is a big pale bulbous torso the shape of a rounded rectangle, with a small round head and a pale cap perched on top; the legs are two short thick grey posts. Grey blotches are sprayed across the belly like stains rather than reading as fur pattern. Both arms and both legs meet the torso as flat overlapping shapes with a visible edge — nothing grows out of the body.
rows.fix: Invert the proportions: arms roughly 1.6x the leg length, knuckles at or below the feet, with a narrow shoulder, a long slender forearm and a distinctly elongated curved hand with four long fingers and an offset thumb. Slim the torso to a narrow tapering chest so the arm span dominates. Merge the limb roots into the shoulder and hip with continuous shading instead of overlaid shapes. Replace the sprayed blotches with directional fur strokes and give the face a pale ring around a dark mask.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon tortoise or a fat gecko
rows.defect: The tail is a flat grey ribbon curled into a hook, hard-edged and clearly a separate shape drawn over the top of the body with a visible boundary where they overlap — it is thin and flat, the opposite of the fat sausage fat-storing tail the reference calls for. The body is a smooth cream egg with an aspect closer to 1.8 than 3.5, so the animal reads squat and round rather than long and low. The skin is not beaded at all: soft grey smudge blotches float on a glossy surface with no bump, no bead, no orange anywhere. Only two grey stick legs are visible, and the head is a small pointed cone with a straight ruled mouth line and one dot eye.
rows.fix: Elongate the trunk to roughly 3.5:1 and continue it directly into a thick tail that is nearly as wide as the hips at its base before tapering — no separate shape, no overlap edge, and lose the cartoon curl. Cover the whole dorsal surface in tightly packed rounded beads (small lit domes with dark interstices) in irregular black and orange bands rather than grey smudges. Broaden the skull into a blunt heavy wedge with a jowl and set it on a thick neck the same width as the head. Show four sprawled limbs with the feet turned outward and clawed toes.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon tree frog
rows.defect: Nothing about it is translucent. The body is an opaque near-perfect teal circle with a hard specular highlight and darker teal blotches sprayed on top; there is no glimpse of heart, gut or bone, and no pale see-through underside — the defining feature of the species is simply absent. The colour is a dark sea-green, not lime. The eyes are large and forward-facing (correct) but they are flat white ping-pong balls with black centre dots, not pale gold. The limbs are flat dark-teal silhouettes overlapping the body disc with a visible edge where they meet it, and the two front legs read as a pair of matched flippers pasted onto the belly.
rows.fix: Make the ventral half genuinely see-through: light the belly to a pale milky green and paint a small red heart, a coiled white gut and the dark liver visible through it, with the skin's own sheen laid over the top. Shift the dorsal green to lime and add fine pale dorsal speckles instead of grey smudges. Recolour the irises pale gold with a fine dark radiating pattern and a small round black pupil. Break the perfect circle into a slightly wider-than-tall frog outline, and let the limbs emerge from beneath the body with shoulder and thigh mass so no overlap edge shows; give the toes visible round adhesive discs.

rows.readsAs: a baby chick or a fat yellow quail
rows.defect: This is a plump yellow songbird/chick, not an eagle. All three mustReads fail: the beak is a tiny pale nub with a slight downcurve and no fleshy cere, there is no bony brow ridge (the eye is a small round black dot on a smooth rounded skull, giving a friendly not a scowling read), and the legs are two thin yellow twigs with three hairline toes — no feathered tarsi, no talons, no grip mass. The body is a near-perfect egg with a dark comma-shaped swirl painted on the flank that reads as a decal rather than folded wing feathers, and the tail/wingtip is a single hard-edged dark shard whose top edge is a straight line meeting the body at a visible seam.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head: enlarge to ~0.24 of body height, give the beak real depth — a deep hooked maxilla with a raised cere block at the base — and cut a projecting supraorbital shelf that overhangs the eye so the pupil sits in shadow. Replace the twig legs with thick feathered thighs that taper out of the belly mass into scaled tarsi and four splayed talons. Delete the swirl decal and build the folded wing as an overlapping covert/primary stack whose leading edge emerges from the shoulder with no boundary stroke; the primaries should reach the tail tip rather than spike past it.

rows.readsAs: a leaf, or a kite with a string
rows.defect: Reads as a green leaf or a paper kite on a stem, not a ray. No duck-bill snout at all — the front of the disc is a plain rounded curve with nothing jutting ahead of the wings. The wings are not sharply pointed; the disc is a soft rounded triangle with a straight machined line along the right trailing edge and an abrupt hard corner at the right wingtip. Two cartoon googly eyes with white sclera and black pupils sit stuck on the top surface like appliqué, in a spot where a real eagle ray has none (its eyes are lateral, on the head, with spiracles behind). The pale blobby spots are soft airbrush circles floating above the skin rather than pigment in it. The tail is a uniform-width green noodle that meets the underside at a visible seam and is barely longer than the disc, not the whip-thin filament several body-lengths long.
rows.fix: Grow a distinct head lobe forward of the wing leading edges and terminate it in a fleshy duck-bill rostrum, with the eyes set on the sides of that lobe and spiracles behind them. Sharpen the pectoral wings to swept falcate points and put a shallow concave sweep in the trailing edge instead of the straight cut. Extend the tail to 2-3x disc width, tapering from a thick base that blends continuously into the pelvic region, with a small barb behind the base. Replace the airbrushed dots with crisp-edged white ocelli that follow the disc's curvature and fade under the wing shading.

rows.readsAs: an earthworm, though the eye makes some viewers say caterpillar
rows.defect: The overall read is right — a ringed, segmented pink tube in an S-curve with no limbs — but two mustReads fail. There is a visible black eye dot on the head end, and the row explicitly requires no eyes or head features. There is no swollen saddle band (clitellum) anywhere; the segment rings run at uniform width from head to tail with no thickened smooth collar near the front. Secondary issue: the segmentation reads as a stack of separate crescent shells laid on top of a tube (each ring has its own highlight and hard lower edge) rather than as annuli of one continuous skin, which pushes it toward caterpillar/grub territory.
rows.fix: Delete the eye dot entirely. Insert a clitellum at roughly 1/3 back from the head: a smooth, slightly swollen, paler collar spanning several segments where the annulation flattens out. Soften the per-ring hard edges into shallow grooves in one continuous surface, and taper the last third to a pointed tail. Tighten the prostomium into a small blunt lobe overhanging the mouth.

rows.readsAs: a hair comb, or half a sea urchin on a stick
rows.defect: This does not read as an animal at all — it is a flat olive ellipse with a fan of straight needles combed along the upper-left arc only, plus a long thin curved stalk trailing off to the lower right. The body silhouette is a mathematically perfect ellipse, an obvious geometric primitive. The spines are uniform straight line segments radiating from a shared arc, all stopping short of the body edge in some places and overhanging it in others — they are drawn on top of the ellipse, not growing out of the skin, and they cover only one quadrant instead of doming over the whole back. Two mustReads are simply absent: there is no short tubular beak-snout (only a tiny featureless nub at the left edge) and there are no legs or digging claws whatsoever — the body sits directly on the ground shadow. The colour is a flat dark khaki with none of the required cream-and-black spine banding.
rows.fix: Replace the ellipse with an asymmetric humped body: high rounded rump, shoulders dropping forward into a low neck. Sprout the spines from the whole dorsal surface, each one thick at the base where it emerges from the fur and tapering to a point, varying length and angle, with cream shafts and dark tips, and let the outermost ones break the silhouette. Add a short cylindrical hairless beak projecting forward and slightly down from the front of the head, with no visible mouth. Add four short splayed limbs with broad flat feet and three to five heavy claws each, the front pair turned outward. Delete the trailing stalk (it reads as a stem, not a tail).

rows.readsAs: a needlefish or a fountain-pen nib
rows.defect: A rigid orange lens/almond shape pointed at both ends, with a hard grey stroke outlining the entire body. That grey stroke is doing duty as the continuous fin fringe, but it reads as an outline stroke, not as a membrane — it has uniform width, follows the body outline exactly, and has a crisp inner boundary against the orange. The head is not blunt-jawed; the front tapers to a sharp point with a tiny white bead eye at the very tip, giving a needlefish/gar read. There is a small triangular flag stuck on the mid-flank with a visible hard seam where it meets the body, which is not any fin an eel has. The body is dead straight and rigid, no undulation, and the aspect measures closer to 5:1 than the specified 12:1. The tail ends in a few stray wispy hairs rather than a fin.
rows.fix: Redraw the body as a long muscular cylinder with at least one sinuous S-bend, aspect ~12:1, round in cross-section at the front and laterally compressed toward the tail. Build a blunt head: broad rounded snout, a wide jaw line running well back past the eye, the eye set behind and above the jaw hinge rather than on the tip. Make the fin fringe a translucent membrane of varying height that rises from the back around a third of the way along, wraps the tail tip and returns along the belly, with a soft feathered outer edge and faint ray striations — and no outline stroke. Delete the mid-flank triangle; if a pectoral is wanted, put a small rounded one just behind the gill and blend its base into the flank shading.

rows.readsAs: a generic purple cartoon stork or crane
rows.defect: Two mustReads fail outright. The plumage is lavender-purple, not pure white. The neck is not S-curved — it is a short straight purple stub barely one head-length long, joining the shoulders at a visible constriction, so the bird has no neck read at all. The bill is a straight yellow spike (right in shape) but it is thin enough to look pinned onto the face rather than continuous with the skull. The legs are yellow-tan sticks, not the required long dark legs, and they are far too short — the tarsi barely clear the body, where an egret's legs should be roughly body-height. The dark wing is a hard-edged blade with a straight upper margin and a machined point, and there is a dark comma swirl painted on the flank that reads as a sticker rather than as feather groups. Body silhouette is a plain egg.
rows.fix: Recolour plumage to white with cool grey shading only. Triple the neck length and put a real S in it — kinked back at the crown, forward at the base — with the throat feathers thickening where it enters the breast so there is no pinch line. Darken and lengthen the legs to roughly the body height, with a visible tibiotarsus/tarsus break, backward-bending hock, and long spread toes; contrast them against the white body. Grow the bill out of the skull with a widening base and a subtle gonys. Replace the wing blade and the flank swirl with layered scapular and covert feather groups whose bases disappear into the back, plus trailing aigrette plumes off the rear.

rows.readsAs: a bath-toy rubber duck
rows.defect: This is the classic rubber-duck shape the note explicitly warns against. The bill is a short orange triangle that meets the face at a sharp step, with a clear notch between bill top and forehead — the opposite of the required unbroken sloping wedge from bill tip to crown, which is the single key read for an eider. The body is a light, high-riding rounded egg, not a bulky heavy duck sitting low in the water. Colour is uniform bright green with a painted-on dark swirl on the flank; none of the required black-and-white blocking is present and there is no pale green nape (the whole bird is green, so the nape cue is meaningless). The water is three concentric perfect ellipses — geometric primitives, not a disturbed surface — and the body simply overlaps them rather than displacing them. The flank swirl and the wing shape both terminate in hard strokes that read as sprayed-on decoration.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head profile as one straight ramp: start the frontal feathering far forward onto the bill so bill and forehead form a single unbroken wedge from tip to crown, with no notch and no rounded brow. Deepen and widen the body, drop the waterline so the belly is submerged and the back sits close to the surface, and lengthen the rear into a low pointed stern. Block the plumage: white back and breast, black flanks and belly, black crown cap, and a distinct pale green wash on the nape behind the cheek. Replace the concentric ellipses with irregular broken ripples that deform around the hull and a soft waterline where the body enters, and delete the flank swirl in favour of a real folded wing whose base merges into the back.

rows.readsAs: the same fish as the Eel in this batch, in a different colour
rows.defect: Near-identical to the Eel in this same batch — same lens body, same grey outline stroke, same stuck-on mid-flank triangle, same white bead eye at the tip — recoloured purple. Every mustRead fails. There is no single long ribbon anal fin along the underside; the underside carries the same uniform grey outline as the back, which means it also fails 'no dorsal fin' since the dorsal fringe is present and equal to the ventral one. The head is not blunt, rounded or flattened — it tapers to a sharp point. The mid-flank triangle has a hard seam where it meets the body and corresponds to no knifefish anatomy. Body is rigid and straight, and the fine hairs at the tail are the same stray-wisp treatment as the Eel.
rows.fix: Fork this away from the eel model entirely. Flatten and blunt the head into a broad rounded wedge with a flat top, small eyes set low and far forward, and a wide terminal mouth. Give the trunk a heavy cylindrical front third that tapers into a laterally compressed rear. Remove all dorsal fringe so the back is a smooth unbroken ridge, and remove the pectoral triangle's hard seam (keep only a small rounded pectoral blending into the gill area). Add the defining feature: one continuous undulating ribbon fin running from just behind the throat to the tail tip along the whole underside, with visible rays and a wavy free edge. Darken the dorsal surface to olive-slate with a yellow-orange throat and chin.

rows.readsAs: Common earthworm / nightcrawler
rows.defect: This is an earthworm, not a planarian. The body is a round tube drawn as ~18 stacked annelid rings — heavy visible segmentation — where the reference demands a ribbon-flat UNSEGMENTED body. The head is a plain rounded bullet tip with one single black dot on the side; there is no arrowhead/triangular head, no pair of cross-eyed spots, and no ear-like auricle lobes at the head corners. Three of three mustReads fail. It also sits in a raised S-curve like a burrowing annelid rather than gliding flat on a surface.
rows.fix: Replace the tubular ring-stack body with a flat ribbon: wide, near-constant-width silhouette with a soft undulating outer edge and NO cross-rings — shade with a broad centreline gut branch instead of segments. Rebuild the head as a wedge/arrowhead with two small backswept auricle lobes at its rear corners, and place two tiny dark eyespots side by side on the dorsal surface angled inward (cross-eyed), not one lateral dot.

rows.readsAs: A paramecium or other ciliated single-celled microbe
rows.defect: Not a fish at all. It is a plain purple ellipse ringed with short straight grey bristles and speckled with flat translucent dots, with two cartoon eyes and a squiggle mouth in the middle of the mass. The silhouette is a mathematically clean oval — a geometric primitive — with no head, no tail, no caudal peduncle, no gill cover and no body/fin distinction. The bristle ring reads as cilia, not as a continuous fin skirt (a flounder's skirt is a soft membrane with rays inside it, not spokes sticking out past the outline). The eyes are symmetric on either side of the midline rather than crowded onto one side, and the mouth is a neutral curve, not a twisted asymmetric jaw. The dots read as sprayed-on decals — no relation to skin form.
rows.fix: Rebuild from the flounder outline: an asymmetric leaf-shaped disc with a discernible snout end and a narrowed peduncle into a rounded tail fan. Draw the dorsal/anal fin skirt as one continuous translucent membrane hugging the outline with internal ray striations, not external spokes. Move both eyes to the upper-left of the head, offset and one slightly higher/forward than the other, and kink the mouth line so it hooks up on the blind side. Replace the flat dot decals with mottled sand-camouflage blotches that follow the body shading.

rows.readsAs: A white ant or termite
rows.defect: The eyes fail outright: there is one tiny black dot on a cream head where the reference requires huge red compound eyes filling the head. The thorax is neither bristly nor grey-striped — it is a glossy off-white sphere. The body is literally three overlapping perfect spheres (head, thorax, abdomen) with visible seams where they intersect; that is a primitive assembly, not an insect. Only one small pale grey wing is present and it sits like a flat leaf pasted on the thorax's top-right with a hard boundary; no halteres. The legs are uniform grey sticks with no femur/tibia taper and no joints, and there are only four of them meeting the body at hard points. Two long antennae stick out where a fly should have short stubby aristae. Despite the 'flying' posture it is standing on legs.
rows.fix: Swap the dot eye for a pair of large dark-red compound domes that consume most of the head volume and meet near the midline. Merge the three spheres into a continuous thorax-abdomen with a pinched waist rather than intersecting balls, add longitudinal grey thorax stripes and short dark bristles breaking the outline. Give it two translucent veined wings swept back from a shoulder that blends into the thorax, plus two small knob halteres behind them. Rebuild the legs as six tapered jointed limbs. Replace the long antennae with tiny stubs.

rows.readsAs: A caterpillar or a stack of golden bread rolls
rows.defect: The colour is wrong for the row: it is saturated orange-amber, not creamy white glossy skin. The head end is a dark brown ball with a bright white-ringed eye clearly stuck on the front — the row calls for eyes hidden and a TAPERED POINTED head end, and this is neither tapered nor eyeless; the dark ball reads as a bolted-on capsule with a hard rim seam against the orange body. The segments are eleven identical perfect overlapping circles of near-equal radius, so the grub has no taper at all along its length — blunt at both ends, and it reads as a stack of coins/bread rolls rather than a soft body. There is also a stray pale crescent on the leftmost segment that looks like a rendering artifact.
rows.fix: Recolour to a pale cream/ivory with a wet gloss highlight. Grade the segment radii so the body narrows to a genuine point at the head end and stays fat and blunt at the rear, and let each segment be a soft asymmetric bulge (varying width, slight overlap shadow) rather than a circle of fixed radius. Delete the dark head sphere and the eye entirely — a maggot's anterior is a translucent taper with two tiny dark mouth hooks. Remove the pale crescent artifact on the tail segment.

rows.readsAs: A flying fish, though the pointed snout pushes it toward a halfbeak
rows.defect: Best in the batch and broadly legible, but three things are off. The tail is a small solid red triangle with no fork at all — the row requires an unevenly forked tail with a much longer lower lobe, and there is no lobe split visible. The snout is drawn as a sharp needle point where a flying fish is blunt-nosed. The upper 'wing' springs from the top of the body near the dorsal ridge rather than low on the flank behind the gill, so the pair does not read as paired pectorals — and there is a dull magenta blob sitting behind the head, overlapped by the wing, that looks like a stray dorsal-fin shape rather than anatomy. The two wings are near-identical mirrored translucent slabs with straight ruled striation lines.
rows.fix: Split the caudal into two lobes with the lower lobe roughly 1.5x the upper and a deep notch between them. Blunt the snout into a rounded, slightly bulbous nose. Drop the upper pectoral's root down onto the flank just behind the head so both wings originate from the same shoulder region and blend into the body with a soft gradient rather than at the dorsal line. Remove or resolve the magenta blob behind the head. Curve the fin ray striations so they fan from the root instead of running as parallel straight rules.

rows.readsAs: A blue-tinted flying fish; in this batch it is plainly the same asset as #5
rows.defect: It is the Flying Fish from this same batch recoloured blue and fattened — same translucent slab wings with straight ruled striations, same white-ringed pinprick eye, same sharply pointed snout. That pointed snout directly contradicts the mustRead 'blunt armoured bony head': there is no bony plate, no ridge, no armour texture anywhere, just a smooth tapered cone. The pectoral fans are pale washed-out lavender-blue with no electric-blue edge band; the outline of the fan simply fades out. The finger-like walking rays read as loose thin blue hairs floating below and left of the body rather than as stiff separate digits rooted in the pectoral base, and several of them cross outside the fin silhouette as stray strands. The spots are flat grey discs sprayed over both body and fin alike, ignoring the form underneath.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as a short blunt box with a hard bony ridge line and a visible cheek plate, ending in a rounded snub, not a point. Add a saturated electric-blue rim band along the trailing edge of each pectoral fan and dot the membrane with the species' blue ocelli. Root the free walking rays at the front-lower corner of the pectoral base as a small set of stiff, jointed, thicker digits touching the substrate, and delete the floating strays. Make the spots follow body shading and stop them at the fin boundary. Widen and square the body so it stops sharing the Flying Fish's torpedo silhouette.

rows.readsAs: A rabbit or a chinchilla
rows.defect: The defining feature is absent: there is NO patagium. Nothing spans wrist to ankle — the flank is a clean unbroken red curve, so the animal cannot read as a gliding squirrel. The tail is a fat round tube with a rounded tip, not flattened or feather-like, and it joins the rump at a hard crescent seam that reads as a separate part pushed into the body. The eyes are a single small dark dot with a highlight, far from 'enormous black eyes'. The limbs are barely present — a couple of short nubs under the belly, no forelegs visible at all, so the quadruped posture does not hold. Two white buck teeth drawn as a flat rectangle with straight vertical dividers plus tall upright ears make it read as a rabbit. The body silhouette is essentially a large circle with a smaller circle head.
rows.fix: Add the gliding membrane as the primary read: a taut skin sheet from wrist to ankle continuing the flank shading, with a slight sag curve and a visible cartilage spur at the wrist. Flatten the tail into a wide horizontally-splayed paddle with hair strands breaking its outline, and blend its root into the rump instead of stopping at a crescent. Enlarge the eye to a big glossy black dome with a single specular highlight. Draw four real limbs with hands and spread digits gripping. Shorten and round the ears, and replace the rectangular incisor block with two small chisel teeth or drop them.

rows.readsAs: A dark round beetle or a spider — barely visible against the background
rows.defect: Leg count fails: I can see only two thin walking legs on each side (four total), where the row demands four pairs. The carapace is not squarish — it is a near-perfect circle flattened slightly at the bottom, a geometric primitive with a hard uniform outline. The two pincers are held UP and outward at 45 degrees like raised arms, not forward, and each is a smooth grey teardrop with no visible split between the fixed and movable finger, so they do not read as pincers. The walking legs are dead-straight ungraded sticks with no knee joint and no taper, meeting the shell at hard points with no shoulder. The eyes are two tiny white ticks on hairline stalks poking above the shell rather than prominent. Finally the whole render is a dark grey-violet on a dark navy field — the contrast is so low the animal nearly disappears; the strongest value in the frame is the drop shadow.
rows.fix: Raise the body value substantially (lighter shell, warmer tone) so it separates from the background. Reshape the carapace to a wider-than-tall rounded trapezoid with a slightly notched front margin. Add the missing two pairs of walking legs and give every leg a real knee bend, taper and a pointed dactyl tip, rooted into a shoulder bulge on the shell edge. Bring both chelipeds down and forward in front of the body and split each claw into two opposing fingers with a visible gape. Enlarge the eyestalks into short thick stalks with dark bulbous eyes seated in orbital notches.

rows.readsAs: a pufferfish, or a generic grey aquarium fish with measles
rows.defect: The mustRead 'rigid armoured box-shaped carapace' is absent. The body is a smooth horizontal rounded rectangle / capsule with soft shoulders — exactly the flagged silhouette — with no angular carapace, no keels or dorsal/ventral ridges, no plate facets, no hexagonal scute grain. The mottling is a scatter of soft blurred grey ovals floating above the surface (they fade out over the belly gradient and none of them follow the body's form) — sprayed on. The caudal fin is a separate darker grey pleated fan butted against a straight vertical body edge with a hard tonal seam and a visible notch gap at top and bottom; the dorsal fin is a small striped triangle sitting on the back line with a hard boundary. The pectoral fin is a tiny quarter-circle fan glued mid-flank. Only the eye and the small pursed lips read as intended.
rows.fix: Rebuild the trunk as a box: a squared-off cross-section silhouette with four soft-cornered edges, a visibly flatter belly and a distinct dorsal keel line running head-to-tail, and a taper toward the tail peduncle. Replace the blur-blob spot layer with a carapace texture that is part of the skin — tessellated hexagonal scute cells with darker cell borders, spots seated INSIDE cells and dimming with the shading. Grow the caudal fin from a narrow flexible peduncle that pinches out of the box (no straight-edge butt joint), and give the dorsal/anal/pectoral fins ray roots that blend into the body value over ~6px instead of an outline.

rows.readsAs: two unrelated objects — a tan tick with legs, next to a floating shrimp tail
rows.defect: The animal is in TWO DISCONNECTED PIECES. The head/thorax blob on the left and the curled segmented abdomen on the right do not touch — there is a clear band of dark background between them, and each has its own closed outline and its own shading. That is the worst possible seam failure: the abdomen is an off-body artifact. Beyond that: no leaf-like paddle limbs (just four straight rigid rods hanging under the head like table legs), no stalked eyes (a single tiny white dot on the head), no forked tail fan (the abdomen ends in a blunt spiked curl), and no translucency — it is an opaque orange plastic. The overall bounding box is roughly 1.5:1, nowhere near the required 3.5 elongation; the pose is hunched and compact rather than a straight upside-down swimmer. Antennae are two long dead-straight sticks.
rows.fix: Make it one continuous body: a single tapering trunk from head through 11 thoracic segments into a slender abdomen, drawn as one path with the segment rings as internal shading only. Replace the four rods with 11 paired phyllopod limbs — broad leaf-shaped lobes with feathery setal fringes, drawn in a metachronal wave so they read as a moving row. Add two eyes on short stalks flanking the head. End the abdomen in a two-lobed forked tail fan with setae. Stretch the silhouette to ~3.5:1 and flip to the upside-down swimming pose. Drop opacity/add rim transmission so the gut stripe shows through.

rows.readsAs: a chrome starfish, or a metal ninja throwing star
rows.defect: This is a starfish, not a brittle star. The arms are straight, rigid, near-uniform-width rods with rounded caps radiating from a fat pentagonal centre; nothing snakes or whips. There is no tiny central disc set off from the arms — the arms merge continuously into the middle, and the two lower arms meet in a shallow V notch with no disc boundary at all. Arm length is only about 2.5–3x the disc width, where the row demands 'many times longer'. Surface is a smooth chrome-blue gradient with a handful of white bokeh dots sprayed on top; no spine rows, no vertebral segmentation, no granular disc plating. The whole thing has a machined, symmetrical, emblem-like quality.
rows.fix: Shrink the central disc to a small distinct button (~12-15% of overall width) with its own scalloped edge and granular plating, and make each arm start at that edge with a visible narrowing so the disc/arm join reads. Redraw the arms at 5-8x disc width, each with a different serpentine curve (S-curves, one coiling back), tapering to a hairlike tip. Add the vertebral ossicle segmentation — regular cross-banding down each arm — with paired lateral spine tufts along both edges. Kill the bokeh dots and the chrome gradient; use a matte banded arm pattern that follows the segmentation.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon smiley-face blob, or a dark spider crouching (from the splayed floating limbs)
rows.defect: Two mustReads are simply missing: there is no tympanum disc anywhere behind the eye, and there are no powerful folded hind legs — the haunches do not exist. The body is a near-perfect dark circle (a geometric primitive), aspect ~1.0 against a required 1.6. The mouth is a thin upcurved arc that reads as a cartoon smile, not a very wide flat mouth line — it stops well short of the body edge on both sides. The two eyes are hemispherical domes stuck on the top of the sphere with a hard dark rim circling each one, a clear stuck-on seam. What hind limbs exist are flat, near-black splayed silhouettes floating OUTSIDE the body outline with no visible attachment to it, plus two thin straight cylindrical forelimbs dangling from the belly. Green mossy patches are airbrushed over the sphere and ignore its form.
rows.fix: Replace the circle with a squat 1.6:1 frog mass: broad flat head merging into a wider sacral hump, mouth line carried right out to the silhouette on both sides and given a slight downturn at the corners. Add the tympanum — a large circle behind and below each eye, larger than the eye, with its own rim highlight and a taut membrane sheen. Build the hind legs as three folded masses (thigh, shin, foot) attached at the sacral hump with the knee peaking above the back line, and connect the webbed feet to them; delete the free-floating dark limb silhouettes. Seat the eyes into raised orbital brow bulges that swell out of the skull instead of ringing them with a dark outline. Make the mottling a wet-skin pattern that darkens along the flank shading.

rows.readsAs: a green ant, or a generic alien bug — one of several three-sphere insects in this batch
rows.defect: Nothing here reads as a bee. The mustRead 'broad bands of black and yellow fuzz' is absent — the whole animal is glossy mint green, and the abdomen's stripes are just darker green shading grooves. 'Fat rounded fully furry body' is absent — it is three separate hard glossy spheres in a row (head, thorax, abdomen) with visible overlap seams at each joint and specular highlights that make them read as plastic beads, not fuzz. The only 'fur' is a collar of straight yellow-green spikes radiating from the thorax equator like a sea-urchin ring — stuck-on decoration confined to one band, with the rest of the body bald. The legs are six thin dead-straight sticks with no joints or pollen basket. The wings are two small grey outlined ovals lying flat on the back with hard edges.
rows.fix: Fuse the three spheres into one continuous fat body with soft waisting rather than gaps and outlines, then coat the ENTIRE silhouette in fur — a fuzzy irregular edge all the way round (broken outline, no clean curve anywhere) plus directional hair strokes over the surface. Repaint as broad black and yellow transverse bands that wrap the body form (bands should bow with the curvature, not sit as flat stripes). Give the legs femur/tibia/tarsus bends and thicken the hind tibia into a corbicula. Redraw the wings as translucent veined membranes hinged at the thorax and angled back over the abdomen, ~60% of body length.

rows.readsAs: a plump bluebird or a cartoon chick
rows.defect: Two mustReads fail. There is no neck: a perfectly circular head sits directly on the body egg with a hard crescent seam where the two circles overlap, so the required 'thick upright neck' does not exist. The legs are short yellow tubes that emerge from the belly with a flat cut end, holding the body low — the opposite of 'heavy horizontal body carried high on long bare legs'; the body's lowest point is barely above the feet. The head is a dome, not flat-crowned. The wing is drawn as three nested concentric ellipse outlines — a bullseye decal pressed onto the flank, with a machined perfect-curve edge and no feather tract structure. The tail is a sharp dark triangular wedge stuck on the rump with a straight leading edge. Fine dark hairline strokes from the wing tip escape the body silhouette and float in the background as loose scratches (off-body artifact).
rows.fix: Insert a real neck: a thick column roughly 0.8x body height rising from the shoulders with a continuous contour into both body and skull, no overlap seam. Flatten the crown and square the rear of the skull, keep the short stout bill. Lengthen the legs to about 1.2x body depth, expose the tibia above the tarsal joint, and rotate the body to horizontal so it sits high on them; give the tarsus scute banding and three forward toes. Replace the concentric-ellipse wing with layered coverts and folded primaries whose feather tips sit inside the silhouette. Build the tail from overlapping rectrices rooted under the rump instead of a triangle wedge. Clip the stray hairlines to the body mask.

rows.readsAs: a winged ant, or an orange bug carrying a folded paper fan
rows.defect: Two of the three mustReads are missing: the antennae are straight tapered bristles with no clubbed knobs (and there are five bristles sprouting from the head, not two), and there is no coiled proboscis anywhere. The body is three hard spheres in a row with a bright white ring outline drawn at each junction — an explicit seam where head meets thorax and thorax meets abdomen. The wings are rooted on the ABDOMEN (the rear sphere), not the thorax, and they attach along a hard white arc. The legs also attach to the head/neck rather than only to the thorax, breaking the note. Wing veins are straight white lines that overshoot the membrane and continue several pixels into the black background — off-body artifacts. The wings themselves are two soft-edged fans with blurred dark smudges floating in them rather than scale-textured patterning, and the whole thing is a flat salmon monochrome.
rows.fix: Move the wing roots to the thorax and grow them from it (no ring outline; blend the membrane base into the thoracic fur over several pixels). Add clubbed antennae — two only, curving up and forward, each swelling into a distinct knob at the tip — and delete the extra head bristles. Add the watch-spring proboscis coiled under the head. Split into four wings with the forewing overlapping the hindwing and a scalloped/angled outer margin instead of a soft blob. Clip veins to the wing mask and taper them from thick at the base to hairline at the margin. Replace the blurred smudges with a scale pattern: a dark marginal border, a vein-following cell pattern and an eyespot, all dimming with the wing's shading. Fuse the head/thorax/abdomen spheres into a waisted body.

rows.readsAs: a discus or angelfish wearing a paper crown, with a giant target painted on its side
rows.defect: The mustRead 'dark bar masking the eye' is absent — the real eye sits fully exposed as a white-ringed dot on plain flank. Instead a large perfect black circle with a crisp white ring is painted mid-body; it is a geometric primitive and, being far bigger than the real eye, it hijacks the read and makes the fish look like it faces the wrong way. The dorsal 'fin' is a rectangular block of identical sharp zigzag triangles sitting on top of the body outline with a straight horizontal seam — a cut-out paper crown, not fin rays growing from the back. The caudal fin is a separate pleated lobe detached from the body with a dark gap between them. The pectoral fin is a perfect quarter-circle pleated fan glued mid-flank. A hard vertical tonal edge splits the body into a light front half and a dark rear half — a sprayed-on seam that follows no anatomy. A stray oval lobe floats beyond the snout tip. The disc shape and pointed snout are the only things working.
rows.fix: Delete the oversized ring; if a false eyespot is wanted put a soft-edged ocellus high on the rear flank and make it smaller than the real eye. Add the true field mark: a dark vertical bar running from the dorsal origin down through the eye to the throat, wider than the eye, with soft edges. Rebuild the dorsal as continuous fin rays — spines of graded length rising out of the back through a fleshy fin base that shares the body's value, with membrane between them. Reattach the caudal via a peduncle (close the gap) and root the pectoral with a fleshy base instead of a clean arc. Replace the vertical light/dark split with the species' own oblique chevron striping that curves with the disc, and remove the floating lobe past the snout.

rows.readsAs: A coiled teal rubber garden hose with a cartoon snake head glued to one end
rows.defect: The head is a separate egg-shaped blob laid ON TOP of the body tube with its own grey/white outline ring visibly closing around it — a hard seam where head meets neck, exactly the stuck-on join that is a blocker. Two of three mustReads are absent: the body is saturated bright teal/turquoise, not 'pale washed-out unpigmented' cave coloration, and there is no blunt wedge head with heat-sensing pits (the head is a plain ovoid with no jawline, no mouth, no nostrils, no pits). The body surface is covered in dense identical transverse hatch ridges that read as a corrugated hose, not scales, and the coil is a near-perfect flat torus (a geometric ring). The tongue is three straight red line segments forming a machined 'Y' sitting off the snout tip. Faint grey speckles float on the body like dust.
rows.fix: Desaturate to a pale pinkish-ivory / translucent unpigmented cave palette (near-white with faint pink undertone). Kill the outline stroke on the head ellipse and blend the head into the neck with a continuous taper — reshape the head into a wedge, wider at the jaw than the neck, with a visible mouth line and a pit row between eye and nostril. Reduce the eye (cave-adapted = small/reduced), replace the uniform transverse hatch with an overlapping scale field that follows body curvature and compresses on the inside of the coil, and break the perfect circular coil into an asymmetric loose loop.

rows.readsAs: A string of red beads, or a caterpillar
rows.defect: The body is a chain of ~16 overlapping perfect SPHERES — shaded balls, i.e. geometric primitives strung on a curve. The mustRead demands a long FLATTENED body of segments; this is emphatically tubular and beaded. Legs are thin dark-red hairlines that tangle in crossing arcs under and even over the body; they do not read as one pair per segment fanned along both sides, they read as scribbles, and several arcs cross the belly in an X. No forcipules, no distinct pair of rear trailing legs. Four appendages sprout at the front (two yellow curls plus two long red arcs) which muddles the antenna read. Head is just another sphere with a black dot.
rows.fix: Replace the sphere chain with overlapping flat tergite plates — each segment a wide, dorsally flattened shield whose rear edge overlaps the next, drawn wider than tall. Anchor exactly one leg pair per plate at the plate's lateral margin, angled progressively rearward, each leg with a visible coxa-femur-tibia break rather than a single hairline arc, and all legs on the same side of the body plane. Add elongated terminal legs trailing behind and a flattened head plate with forcipules under it. Drop the two extra red front arcs.

rows.readsAs: A green chili pepper or a leaf with a curled stem
rows.defect: The mustRead 'cone eye turrets that swivel independently' is entirely missing — the eye is a tiny flat black bead flush with a smooth flank, no turret cone, no lid ring. The legs are two bare hairline strokes with a small T-bar for a foot, hanging off the underside of the blob with no hip, no thigh volume and a hard join; only two legs are drawn for a stated quadruped and there are no zygodactyl grasping feet. The body is one smooth teardrop with a long thin blade drawn back to a point, producing a leaf silhouette; no mouth, no casque texture, no lateral rib/skin detail. Only the tail spiral and the casque spike survive as chameleon cues, and the spiral is a flat stroked scroll.
rows.fix: Build the eye as a raised cone turret: a domed scaly cone with a small central aperture, offset from the head profile so it breaks the silhouette. Give all four legs real volume — a thick femur wedge growing out of the body wall with no outline seam, a bent knee, and two-plus-two opposed toe bundles clamping a perch. Compress the body into a tall leaf with a serrated dorsal crest of individual spines rather than a smooth blade, add a mouth line running back under the eye, and give the skin a granular tubercle field so the tail spiral reads as skin, not a drawn scroll.

rows.readsAs: A generic goldfish or trout clip-art icon
rows.defect: The spot polarity is inverted — the reference is explicit that char are PALE spots on a DARK ground, and this render is dark olive-brown blotches on a light orange ground, the exact pattern the row forbids. 'White leading edges on lower fins' is also missing because the lower fins are missing: there is no anal fin, no pelvic fins. Worse, the dorsal fin is a single large translucent brown ELLIPSE drawn behind the body whose bottom half shows through the semi-transparent flank and protrudes below the belly line as a phantom lobe — a visible render bug. Fin rays are dead-straight machined lines. The eye is a perfect white circle with a black dot, cartoon-scaled and pushed onto the snout tip. The body is a smooth almond/lens with a white outline stroke.
rows.fix: Invert the ground: deep olive-to-slate flank grading to an orange belly, with small round CREAM/pink spots scattered over the dark upper body. Clip or opaque the dorsal fin so it stops at the dorsal line — no ellipse bleeding below the belly. Add pelvic and anal fins growing out of the ventral wall with a bright white leading ray and a thin black stripe behind it (the diagnostic char mark). Curve the fin rays and let the fin membrane taper into skin instead of butting against an outline. Shrink and re-seat the eye behind the maxilla, not at the snout tip.

rows.readsAs: A moorhen, coot or generic dark wading bird — nothing about it says chicken
rows.defect: The tail is a hard-edged QUADRILATERAL SLAB — perfectly straight top, straight bottom, straight angled end, with a rim outline — jutting horizontally backward and meeting the body at a hard vertical seam. That is a machined polygon, and it directly contradicts 'short upswept fan of tail feathers.' The comb and wattles are also missing: the crown carries only a smooth pale crescent arc, there is no serrated red comb and no wattle under the beak at all. The neck is a plain column with a visible notch step where it meets the shoulder. Legs are two thin lines ending in flat bars — no toes, no scale texture, so 'scaly legs' fails too. Plumage is a flat dark oval with a single rim light and no feather groups.
rows.fix: Delete the slab. Rebuild the tail as a short upswept cluster of overlapping sickle feathers, each a separate tapered shape rising above the back line, root hidden under the saddle so there is no seam. Add a red serrated comb (four to six points) on the crown and a pair of red wattles hanging under the beak. Widen the drumstick into the body so the leg grows out rather than plugs in, give the tarsus a scute-scaled texture and three forward toes plus a hallux. Warm the plumage and break it into breast, wing-bow and saddle feather groups so the body is not one smooth oval.

rows.readsAs: An orange plastic toy ape or a person in a mascot suit — closest to a Bigfoot figurine
rows.defect: The mustRead 'large protruding round ears' is completely absent — the head is a bare sphere with no ears at all. Instead the skull carries a hard grey outline arc offset above it that reads as a glass helmet or bald cap. The brow is a flat dark ELLIPSE pasted across the forehead rather than a bony ridge, and the muzzle is inverted: it is a DARKER oval on a lighter face, where the row asks for a pale muzzle, and it does not protrude at all. Eyes are two cartoon googly circles with white sclera. Arms are uniform-width tubes butted against the torso — the torso's grey outline continues visibly behind the shoulder, a textbook stuck-on seam. The whole animal is smooth airbrushed salmon-orange plastic with soft blurry blotches and an orange glow bleeding outside the silhouette at the shoulders; there is no hair anywhere on a species defined by black hair.
rows.fix: Add the ears first — large round flat discs standing well clear of the skull on both sides, breaking the silhouette. Recolour to near-black hair with a pale grey-pink face and a PALE protruding muzzle that pushes forward past the brow, and cut a real prognathic jaw profile. Replace the ellipse brow with a modelled supraorbital torus that casts a shadow into the eye sockets, and shrink the eyes to small dark irises with almost no visible sclera. Merge the arms into the shoulder with a deltoid mass and remove the torso outline stroke so no line survives under the limb. Overlay a directional hair field (long shaggy strokes on forearms, back and flanks) so the surface stops reading as vinyl, and clip the orange bloom to the silhouette.

rows.readsAs: A red squirrel — it also sits uncomfortably close to a generic cartoon rat
rows.defect: There are NO STRIPES. The single most diagnostic mustRead — bold dark and pale stripes along back and face — is entirely absent; the animal is uniform salmon-rust from nose to rump. Cheek pouches are also missing, so two of three mustReads fail. Construction is visibly two overlapping circles: a hard grey arc seam runs where the head sphere overlaps the body sphere, and a second grey arc outlines the haunch ellipse. The tail is a smooth banana tube with one big pale rounded-rectangle decal painted on it — a capsule primitive standing in for fur. The teeth are a literal white RECTANGLE with a vertical divider line floating at the mouth. Whiskers are straight hairlines fanning from a single point. Front legs do not exist; the visible feet are two dark brown blobs stuck under the belly with no leg connecting them.
rows.fix: Paint the five dark dorsal stripes separated by cream stripes running from shoulder to rump, plus the dark eye-stripe and pale cheek stripe on the face — these follow body curvature and must be part of the fur shading, not overlaid bars. Bulge the cheek behind the jaw into a filled pouch. Remove the grey arc seams by drawing head and body as one continuous outline with the neck as a shading transition. Rebuild the tail as a flattened plume of directional fur strands with a dark centre and pale fringe, deleting the capsule highlight. Replace the tooth rectangle with two rounded chisel incisors below a lip, curve the whiskers, and add real forelegs with elbows tucked at the chest.

rows.readsAs: A bread roll or a bar of soap with a snail's eyestalk stuck on one end
rows.defect: The silhouette is a machined slab: the entire underside is a dead-straight horizontal line, the ends are squared with a small radius, and the top ridge is a row of identical circular scallop arcs. I count SEVEN scallops, not the required eight plates, and the arcs are geometric segments rather than valves with a beak, apex and lateral areas. The 'leathery girdle band ringing the plates' is missing — the lower two-thirds is one undifferentiated smooth flat wedge with no band, no bristles, no distinct edge. Worst of all there is a small pale hooked tube on the right end carrying a glossy black bead — an eyestalk with an eye, on an organism whose reference row explicitly says headFrac 0 and eyes hidden. It is an off-body artifact grafted onto the shell. Colour is uniform bone-white with a metallic sheen; the subject also occupies only about a third of the 440px frame.
rows.fix: Delete the eyestalk entirely. Rebuild as eight distinct valves: a wider head valve, six intermediate valves with a raised jugal ridge and sloping lateral areas, and a smaller tail valve — each overlapping the one behind so the shell arches like a segmented back, not a scallop row. Wrap a girdle band of granular leathery tissue all the way around the valves, wider at the ends, with a visible sculptural texture and short marginal bristles, and let the underside deform to the rock instead of running as a straight ruler line. Mottle the colour (olive, brick, cream banding per valve) rather than one bone tone, and scale the body up to fill the frame.

rows.readsAs: a generic small red aquarium minnow — in this batch it is the Goldfish drawn smaller and thinner; the two share the same lens body and the same detached wedge tail
rows.defect: Not one of the three mustReads is present. There is no fused pelvic suction disc on the belly — the underside is a bare unbroken red curve with nothing on it. There are not two separate dorsal fins; there are two tiny triangular nubs sitting on the back line, both the same size, reading as bumps rather than fins. The head is not big or blunt: it is the pointed end of an almond, and the head fraction is nearer 0.15 than 0.30. The single eye is a small white ring with a black dot placed right at the snout tip, not two eyes set high and close together. Beyond the mustReads, the body is a pure lens/almond primitive (two circular arcs meeting in points at both ends), the caudal fin is a separate hard-edged red wedge butted against the body with a visible vertical seam line, and the pectoral fin is a flat triangle drawn on the flank with a hard outline. The whole animal occupies about a fifth of the 440px frame, so it is also badly undersized.
rows.fix: Rebuild the body from a blunt-fronted profile: widen the anterior third into a broad flat-topped head that is ~30% of length, drop the eyes to two bumps on the TOP of the skull set close together, and taper the rear rather than mirroring the front arc. Add the defining organ: a round-to-oval pale suction disc on the ventral midline under the pectorals, drawn as a raised belly structure with its own shading, not a decal. Split the dorsal into a short spiny anterior fin and a longer soft posterior fin with a clear gap. Grow the caudal fin out of the peduncle — narrow the body into a wrist and let the fin rays fan from it so the seam disappears. Scale the whole render up ~2x to fill the frame.

rows.readsAs: a kiwi, or a generic cartoon chick — nobody would say godwit; it also shares its exact body-plus-oval-wing-plate construction with the Goose in this batch
rows.defect: The bill is far too short — it is roughly one head-length, a plain straight orange cone with no upward tilt and no pale base, where a godwit's bill should be two to three head-lengths. The legs are short, stubby and orange-yellow, ending in tiny toes on the ground; the mustRead calls for long dark legs. There is no cinnamon breast and no dark chevron barring — the bird is uniform mint green with a plain paler belly patch. The wing is the worst structural failure: a hard-edged pale oval plate laid on the flank with a continuous dark outline all the way round, so it reads as a sticker on the body rather than a folded wing, and a second thin crescent line above it repeats the same hard edge. The tail is a separate dark triangular blade jammed into the back of the body with a visible straight seam. The body silhouette is an egg with no neck articulation — the head sphere sits directly on the body sphere.
rows.fix: Triple the bill length and give it a faint upward sweep with a pale flesh-toned proximal half fading to dark at the tip. Lengthen the tarsi to at least half the body height and recolour them dark grey-black. Repaint the breast cinnamon with a run of dark V-shaped chevrons that follow the body's curvature (scaled and rotated per row, not stamped). Kill the wing outline entirely: render the folded wing as tonal shading plus a few coverts/primary edges that dissolve into the flank at the leading edge, with only the trailing tip lifting free of the body. Merge the tail into the rump by tapering the body into it instead of abutting a triangle.

rows.readsAs: a green cichlid or piranha — the shape is fish-generic, and stripped of the missing orange it is indistinguishable in construction from the Goby in this batch
rows.defect: The colour is green, not deep orange — the single most identifying feature of a goldfish is simply absent. The tail is physically detached: there is a clear dark gap of background between the rear of the body and the fan tail, which floats as a separate hard-edged pale-green pad with a straight left border. It is a single flat fan, not a flowing double fan, and it has no motion or translucency. The back is not high-arched with a long dorsal — the dorsal is one short low triangular nub near the mid-back. The body is again the lens/almond primitive, symmetric front-to-back, with a straight machined highlight line running its full length. The eye is a plain white circle with a black dot outlined in hard black, floating near the snout. The pectoral fin is a flat scalloped triangle stamped on the flank with a hard edge.
rows.fix: Recolour to saturated orange-red with a paler belly gradient. Reconnect the tail: taper the body to a narrow peduncle and let two overlapping translucent lobes flare from it with wavy rather than straight margins and a soft ray texture. Raise the dorsal into a long continuous fin running most of the back and lift the dorsal profile into a real arch so the deepest point is forward of centre. Break the front-back symmetry of the body outline. Replace the drawn-on pectoral with a small translucent fin whose base fades into the flank.

rows.readsAs: a flamingo, or an inflatable swan ring — the pink plus the thin S-neck plus the concentric rings all push away from goose
rows.defect: This reads as a pink pool-float swan. The neck is thin, tall and S-curved like a swan or flamingo, not the long THICK neck of a goose, and it joins the body at a hard tuck with a visible seam where the tube meets the sphere. The bill is a short pointed yellow cone, not a flat rounded goose bill. The Canada-goose note is entirely unmet: no black neck, no black head, no white chinstrap — the whole bird is magenta-pink. No webbed feet and no legs are visible at all; the bird is floating in water rings, which also contradicts the biped posture in the row. The wing is the same defect as the Godwit: a hard-outlined oval plate on the flank plus a second crescent line, both with continuous dark borders, sitting on top of the body instead of growing from a shoulder. The water is drawn as three thin perfect ellipses — machined concentric rings with uniform stroke width, an obvious geometric primitive rather than a disturbed surface.
rows.fix: Thicken the neck to roughly twice its current diameter and straighten it into the upright goose posture, flaring its base continuously into the shoulders so there is no seam. Reshape the bill to a broad flat-topped rounded bill with a visible nail at the tip. Apply the Canada-goose colourway: black head and neck, crisp white chinstrap patch from cheek to cheek, brown-grey body, pale breast. Either stand the bird on webbed feet per the posture field, or if the swimming pose is kept, replace the elliptical ripple strokes with irregular broken waterline arcs of varying weight and add a partial reflection. Dissolve the wing outline into tonal coverts.

rows.readsAs: a chinchilla or a white pet mouse
rows.defect: The incisors are two small pale cream squares sitting at the mouth, not huge protruding orange incisors outside the lips — wrong size, wrong colour, and they read as teeth-shaped tiles rather than curved chisels. There are no oversized digging claws: the forefoot is a smooth grey nub with no toes and no claws at all, and the hind foot is likewise a rounded stub. The body is not cylindrical and neckless at aspect 2.6 — it is a near-spherical hunched ball roughly 1.2 wide-to-tall, so the proportion is badly off. The pale ice-blue/white colouring is nothing like a gopher. Construction problems: the haunch is a separate lighter oval overlaid on the body with its own visible edge; the tail is a smooth grey tapered tube stuck onto the hip with a hard boundary; both ears are flat grey teardrop cutouts with hard outlines pasted on the skull; the whiskers are five perfectly straight rigid lines of identical weight radiating from one point.
rows.fix: Stretch the body to a low cylinder around 2.5:1, drop the arched back, and run the head straight into the shoulders with no waist. Recolour to brown-buff. Make the incisors large curved orange chisels projecting clearly beyond the lip line, visible even in profile. Build real forefeet: splayed toes carrying long pale curved claws roughly as long as the foot itself. Blend the haunch as a shading mass under the same fur rather than an overlaid oval, and let the tail base widen into the rump. Curve the whiskers with varying length and taper, and origin them from a fleshy muzzle pad.

rows.readsAs: a green cartoon ape mascot in a hoodie, or a Hulk-style figure — the helmet seam is the first thing the eye lands on
rows.defect: The sagittal crest is rendered as a separate hard-edged dome arc over the skull with a clear continuous seam line across the brow — it reads unmistakably as a helmet or a hood pulled over the head, not as a peaked skull. There is no heavy brow ridge under it; the face is a flat pale-green oval with two round white cartoon eyes and a small pink nose, closer to a frog or a plush toy than a gorilla. The arms are two dark green rounded capsules butted against the sides of the torso with visible vertical seams — no shoulder mass, no deltoid, no taper, and they end in blunt rounded stubs with no hands, so knuckle-walking is completely absent; the figure is standing squarely, not resting on folded knuckles, and the shoulders sit level with the hips rather than higher. The torso is a rounded rectangle — a capsule with straight parallel sides — so the barrel chest and pot belly do not read; the only belly cue is a lighter oval overlay with a visible edge. The dark blotches on the chest are soft grey stamps that sit on top of the surface with no relation to any fur direction.
rows.fix: Delete the helmet arc and instead sculpt the crest as a ridge continuous with the skull, casting its own shadow into a deep overhanging brow that shades the eyes; sink the eyes small and dark under it and enlarge the muzzle forward. Rebuild the arms from a broad trapezius-shoulder mass that flows into the upper arm, thickest at the shoulder, and terminate them in visible folded fists with the knuckles contacting the ground so the shoulders ride clearly above the hips. Replace the capsule torso with a wide barrel chest narrowing slightly then bulging into a low pot belly, so the outline has real inflection. Convert the blotches into fur-direction shading that follows the chest and abdomen contours.

rows.readsAs: a coiled length of corrugated garden hose, or a large teal earthworm — the perfectly round ring reads as an object, not an animal
rows.defect: The pose is a near-perfect flat torus — a geometric ring/donut with an even inner hole — not the loose S-curve the row asks for; it reads as a coiled hose. There is no pale yellow collar behind the head, the defining grass-snake mark. The body is bright teal-cyan, not olive-grey. The eye shows a vertical yellow iris with a dark slit-like pupil, the opposite of the round pupil in the row, and the head is a small bulb with no cheek mass. Body diameter is dead uniform all the way round with no taper toward a tail — the tail simply disappears under the coil, so the animal has no visible end. The surface is a run of identical parallel ribs of constant spacing and constant width, which reads as corrugated rubber tubing rather than overlapping scales; four small pale ovals sit on the flank as sprayed-on spots unrelated to the rib pattern. The forked tongue is a flat two-line V of uniform stroke.
rows.fix: Break the ring: lay the body in an asymmetric S with unequal loop radii and let a visibly tapered tail exit the composition. Recolour to olive-grey-brown with darker dorsal flecking. Add the yellow-and-black collar as a band immediately behind the jaw, wrapping with the body's curvature. Change the pupil to round and black in a paler iris. Replace the uniform ribbing with imbricated scale rows that compress on the inside of each curve and stretch on the outside, and vary scale size from large mid-body to small at the neck and tail. Widen the head slightly at the jaw and let the neck narrow behind it.

rows.readsAs: a mosquito or a small ant — the thread legs and thread antennae read dipteran, and nothing about it says jumper
rows.defect: The body is three separate spheres in a row — head, thorax, abdomen — each with its own highlight and a visible pinch seam where they meet, so it reads as strung beads rather than one insect. The abdomen is a short egg, not a long tapered abdomen; it is barely longer than the thorax and ends bluntly with no ovipositor or segmental banding. The hind legs fail the primary mustRead: they are hairline strokes of constant one-pixel-ish weight, with no femur mass at all, and their apex reaches only about the level of the back rather than rising clearly above it — a grasshopper's most recognisable feature, the swollen jumping femur, is simply not drawn. The legs also attach with no joint whatsoever, terminating at the body edge. The wing is a hard-outlined pointed leaf shape laid over the abdomen with a continuous dark border and two straight internal veins. The antennae are long thin curved threads where the row calls for short stout antennae, and the face is a round ball with no slant at all. Overall the creature is small in the frame with a lot of dead space.
rows.fix: Fuse the three spheres into one continuous body: a slanted wedge-shaped head running into a saddle-shaped pronotum which flows into an abdomen at least twice the thorax length, tapering to a point and carrying visible tergite segments. Rebuild the hind leg as a thick tapering femur with real width and an internal herringbone stripe, bent sharply at a knee that rises well above the dorsal line, then a thin spined tibia angling down to a foot — and root it in a visible coxal bulge on the thorax. Shorten and thicken the antennae to stubby tapered rods. Replace the outlined wing with a translucent tegmen whose base disappears under the pronotum and which shows fine cross-venation instead of two straight lines. Angle the face backward to give the slanted profile and enlarge the render in frame.

rows.readsAs: a rabbit / bunny
rows.defect: The ears are tall, narrow, upright and pointed — rabbit ears — where the row demands "drooping petal ears". The whole animal reads as a small rabbit: egg-shaped magenta loaf, one dark stick-thin foreleg and one dark hind paw poked into the underside as separate strokes, a hard crescent seam arcing across the rear haunch where the haunch meets the body, and a white machined rectangle for incisors sitting under the muzzle. There is no guinea-pig cue anywhere: no broad flat-topped head, no short blunt roman nose, no rosette/coarse fur texture, no wide low stance. Body is a smooth featureless gradient egg with no hair reading at all. It is pixel-for-pixel the same drawing as Hamster in this batch, only hue-shifted magenta instead of green.
rows.fix: Replace the upright pointed ear shape with the guinea pig's small drooping petal ear — a wide, low, forward-flopping lobe set on the side of the head, not on top. Widen and flatten the skull so the head is a broad wedge continuous with the shoulder (guinea pigs are neckless and the head is as wide as the body), and shorten the muzzle to a blunt roman curve. Delete the white incisor rectangle or replace it with a soft dark lip line. Grow the legs out of the belly mass with a fur-edged join instead of drawing dark sticks over it, and remove the arc seam on the haunch by blending the haunch into the flank. Add short coarse fur strokes / rosette whorls to the coat so it is not a bare gradient. Most importantly, this and Hamster must not share one mesh — give the guinea pig a longer, lower, more brick-like body (aspect ~2.2 as specced; it currently measures ~1.5).

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon chick or budgerigar
rows.defect: None of the three mustRead features are present. There is no bare blue-and-red skin head and no bony helmet casque — instead the head is the same pink as the body wearing a small feathery punk crest of three spikes. There is no white speckling anywhere: the plumage is a plain pink gradient with a single dark comma-swirl on the flank that reads as a painted-on decal, not as a feather tract. The neck is not a thin naked stalk; head and body merge into one continuous pink blob. The head is also not comically small — it is a normal songbird proportion. The tail is a flat dark triangle stuck onto the rump at a hard angle rather than a drooping fan of feathers, and the bill is a tiny yellow finch cone.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as a bare skin knob in blue and red, distinctly different in colour and texture from the feathered body, topped by a smooth bony horn casque leaning back — and shrink it to roughly half its current size. Run a thin naked neck down from it that visibly narrows before flaring into the heavy body. Cover the entire body in dense small white dots in rows following the body contour (this is the single most identifying feature of the species and it is entirely absent). Delete the crest spikes and the flank swirl. Replace the triangular tail with a short downward-drooping feather fan.

rows.readsAs: a green duckling or generic songbird — indistinguishable from the Guineafowl in this batch
rows.defect: This is the identical drawing to Guineafowl in this same batch — same body outline, same flank comma-swirl, same tail triangle, same yellow legs and toes, same tiny cone bill, same eye — recoloured green. Every mustRead fails: the bill is a small straight finch cone with no heavy hooked tip; the plumage is solid green with no white body, no grey mantle and no black wingtips; and the wings do not cross beyond the tail — there are no wings drawn at all, just a swirl on the flank. Silhouette is a plump perching songbird, not a long-winged seabird.
rows.fix: Give it the gull silhouette: a long horizontal body, a flat back, and long pointed wings whose tips cross over each other well past the tail tip. Redraw the bill as a heavy deep yellow bill with a distinct downward hook at the tip and a red gonys spot. Recolour to a white head/breast/tail, a clean grey mantle over the back and folded wing, and solid black wingtips with white mirrors. Straighten the legs into pink webbed feet. This must stop sharing a mesh with Guineafowl — they are currently the same bird twice.

rows.readsAs: a lanternfish or a small barracuda
rows.defect: The defining feature is missing entirely: there is no enormous pelican pouch mouth. The head is a small pointed snout with a row of tiny sawtooth notches for teeth, no larger than the rest of the body, so the animal's whole identity is gone. The body is a symmetrical pointed lens/leaf shape roughly aspect 3, not a whip-thin aspect-7 ribbon, and the tail is a short straight dark spike with no taper and no luminous tip.
