The photophores are a perfectly regular row of evenly spaced identical oval dots — a machined dotted line, not organic light organs. The dorsal fin is a dark grey triangle laid over the back with a hard straight edge where it meets the body, clearly stuck on rather than growing out.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as a huge hinged pouch: an upper jaw as long as a third of the animal, a lower jaw of loose distensible skin bagging far below the body line, and a gape wider than the body is deep. Move the pinhead eyes right onto the tip of the upper jaw. Then replace the lens body with a true whip: mass concentrated behind the jaw and tapering continuously over a long ribbon to a hair-fine tail carrying a small glowing bulb. Vary the photophore spacing and size and let them fade rather than punch out as identical ovals. Blend the dorsal into the back with a soft membrane rather than a hard-edged triangle.

rows.readsAs: a generic orange fish — could be a bass, a snapper, or a perch
rows.defect: The identifying thumbprint is not readable — instead of a dark, sharply bounded oval smudge sitting above the pectoral fin just behind the gill cover, there is a diffuse olive-green cloud in the middle of the flank that reads as a discolouration or a bruise. The black lateral line is essentially absent: there is one faint pale (not black) hairline. Only two dorsal fins are drawn, not three, and the first one is a low rounded brown triangle rather than the tall pointed sail the row calls for. The body is a symmetrical pointed lens, aspect ~2.6 against the specced 3.5, with no separation between head and trunk — no gill cover line, no cheek, no jaw. Both dorsal fins and the pectoral are flat opaque brown triangles that terminate on a hard straight line against the body.
rows.fix: Move and tighten the blotch: a small, dark, hard-edged oval directly above and slightly behind the pectoral fin base. Draw the lateral line as a distinct black line curving from the gill cover along the upper flank to the tail. Add the third dorsal and make the first one a tall pointed triangle noticeably higher than the other two. Lengthen the body to aspect 3.5 and break the lens symmetry — deeper forward, tapering toward a slim caudal peduncle. Add a gill cover line and a small chin barbel. Let the fins emerge with a soft translucent ray membrane fading into the flank instead of butting against it as opaque solids.

rows.readsAs: a paramecium or a single-celled microbe with cilia
rows.defect: This does not read as a fish at all. It is a plain dark grey ellipse with a ring of short, straight, evenly-spaced bristles radiating from the rim, two round dots for eyes and a tiny curved mouth. The "continuous fin fringe" has been rendered as discrete straight hairs — literal machined line segments — rather than as a soft rippling membrane. There is no tail, no gill cover, no pectoral fin, no head at all: the eyes are simply painted onto an undifferentiated oval, so the required "both eyes on the same upper side of the head" cannot read because there is no head to read them on. The outline is a perfect symmetrical ellipse, not the diamond-elongate flatfish outline specced. The mottled grey spots look sprayed over the surface rather than sitting in the skin.
rows.fix: Replace the ellipse with a true flatfish outline: a long asymmetric diamond, deepest just behind the head, tapering to a narrow wrist and then a broad fan tail. Build an actual head at the leading end — jaw line, gill cover, and the two eyes crowded together on the upper side above the mouth, one visibly migrated and slightly out of line with the other. Replace the bristle ring with a continuous soft dorsal-plus-anal fin membrane running unbroken around the whole silhouette, its rays visible only as faint internal striations inside the membrane, its outer edge undulating rather than spiked. Give the skin the flatfish's fine speckle-over-mottle so it looks like camouflaged skin, and add the pale blind-side edge where the body turns over.

rows.readsAs: a tuna or mackerel
rows.defect: There is no hammer. The head is a plain pointed fish snout with a single small eye set behind the tip — no lateral cephalofoil, no T shape, no eyes at outer tips. That is the entire identity of the species and it is absent, so this is unshippable regardless of anything else. The "very tall sickle first dorsal" is a dull rounded dark hump that appears to float behind the back rather than rise from it — it is a separate darker blob visible through/behind the body with no continuous join. The body is the same symmetrical teal lens used for the Gulper Eel in this batch, aspect ~2.8 not 4.3, with a forked tuna tail. Gill slits are five identical straight parallel scratches — a machined comb, not skin openings.
rows.fix: Build the cephalofoil: widen the front of the skull into a flattened wing that projects well beyond the body on both sides, with the eyes placed on the extreme outer tips and the nostril grooves running along its leading edge. Because the pose is broadside, the hammer should read as a wide flat blade seen edge-on-plus-perspective, distinctly wider than the body. Replace the floating hump with a very tall, backward-curving sickle dorsal that grows out of the back with a continuous skin fillet at its base. Lengthen and slim the body to aspect 4.3, add the second dorsal, the pelvic and anal fins, and a strongly asymmetric heterocercal tail with a long upper lobe. Give the gill slits slight curve and varying length so they are not a comb, and stop sharing the lens mesh with the bony fish in this batch — sharks read from the fusiform, cartilaginous silhouette.

rows.readsAs: a green rabbit — the same animal as the Guinea Pig in this batch
rows.defect: Same drawing as Guinea Pig in this batch, recoloured green — identical body egg, identical haunch seam, identical stick legs, identical whisker fan and white incisor rectangle. It reads as a rabbit: tall, narrow, upright pointed ears dominate the head, and a hamster has small round ears. The required bulging cheek pouches are entirely absent — the cheek is a plain smooth gradient with no swelling. The muzzle is a small pointed snout rather than a blunt short one. The white rectangle under the mouth is a hard machined shape. There is a hard crescent line across the rear haunch and both feet are dark strokes pushed into the underside rather than limbs emerging from it.
rows.fix: Swap the pointed rabbit ears for small, round, thin-skinned hamster ears set low on the sides of a wide domed skull. Add the cheek pouches as genuine volume — swell the lower cheek outward and downward so the widest point of the head is at the jaw, catching its own highlight, not as a painted patch. Shorten the muzzle to a blunt stub with a small nose pad. Round the body into the neckless barrel the row describes and let the short legs grow out of the belly fur with a soft join, deleting the haunch seam. Remove the incisor rectangle. Critically, this must not be a recolour of Guinea Pig — the hamster is shorter, rounder and more upright (specced aspect 2.0 vs the guinea pig's 2.2, but the difference has to come from silhouette, not hue).

rows.readsAs: A red robin or a cartoon bluebird recoloured crimson
rows.defect: This is not an emu in any respect. It is a small plump perching bird — cherry-red, roughly as tall as it is wide, with a round head sitting directly on a fat round body, a short yellow triangular finch/robin bill, a smooth glossy folded-wing ellipse with a scribed outline, a pointed tail spike, and two thin yellow stick legs. Every mustRead fails: there is no long bare blue-grey neck (the head is jammed onto the shoulders with no neck at all), there is no shaggy drooping double plumage (the body is a flat airbrushed gradient with two hard-edged lens-shaped highlights sprayed on top), and the wing is plainly VISIBLE and drawn as a big scored ellipse when an emu shows none. The feet are bare wire with no three-toed structure. The head/body join is a hard crescent seam where two ellipses overlap. Critically it is the SAME generic bird body as Falcon, Finch and Flamingo in this batch — identical body ellipse, identical wing scribe, identical bill wedge, identical two-stick legs — only the fill colour differs.
rows.fix: Emu needs its own morphology, not the shared songbird body. Set aspect tall-ish with the mass HIGH: a deep egg-shaped trunk whose top narrows into a genuine long neck (neck length ~0.45 of total height) that grows out of the shoulder as one continuous silhouette path, not a stacked circle. Kill the wing ellipse entirely. Replace the smooth gradient fill with a shaggy plumage edge — perturb the body outline with 40+ downward-hanging hair strokes so the silhouette itself is ragged, and drop the two lens highlights. Neck and head skin = blue-grey bare, body = dusty grey-brown, never cherry red. Legs must be ~0.4 of height, thick-thighed, with three forward toes. Remove the pointed tail spike.

rows.readsAs: A curled-up pink prawn or a krill
rows.defect: Rendered at maybe a quarter of the frame — a tiny pink comma floating in a 440px field, so it reads as a thumbnail mistake before it reads as an animal. Aspect is wrong: the row asks 4.5 (a long slender ribbon) and the render is a curled-up ball roughly 1.4 wide-to-tall. The mustReads all miss. It is NOT upside down — the legs are on the underside and the back is up, standard prawn orientation. The eyes are two dark dots pressed flat into the head globe, not on stalks. The abdomen is drawn as a hard armoured segmented tail with crisp raised overlapping plates and a fan — that is a carapace, and a fairy shrimp has none; the body should be a bare translucent tube. Legs are about six short pink nubs, not eleven pairs of broad leaf-like phyllopods in a wave. Body is opaque saturated pink with a specular sheen, no translucency at all. The head sphere meets the thorax at a visible circular seam.
rows.fix: Uncurl it: lay the body out as a near-straight horizontal tube at aspect ~4.5 filling ~75% of the frame width, and FLIP it so the leg row faces up (upside-down swimming is the single most recognisable fairy-shrimp cue). Delete the segmented armour plating and the tail fan; redraw the abdomen as a smooth soft-walled tube with faint internal gut line visible through it, alpha ~0.65 so the background reads through, grading to orange-pink only at the posterior third. Add eleven paired broad flat leaf-shaped limbs along the thorax, each phase-offset so they form a visible metachronal wave. Put the eyes on two short stalks that project clear of the head outline. Merge head into thorax with one continuous path — no circle-on-circle seam.

rows.readsAs: A grey pigeon or a dove
rows.defect: Reads as a slate-grey pigeon, not a raptor. The bill is a short straight yellow cone with no hook and no tomial notch — it is the same seed-eater wedge used on the Finch and the Emu in this batch. There is no dark malar moustache stripe anywhere; the face is one flat grey wash. The wing is a broad rounded ellipse tucked against the body with a scribed outline, the exact opposite of the required narrow scythe-like swept wingtip, and the only pointed element is a short dark tail wedge that stops well short of reading as a primary. Head fraction is under-scale for the row's 0.24 and there is no heavy raptor brow — the eye is a plain black bead with a white catchlight. Posture is a plump upright pigeon squat, not a falcon's flat-backed alert stance. Body silhouette is a smooth capsule of two overlapped ellipses with a hard crescent seam at the head/shoulder junction, and the wing highlight is an obvious lens shape sprayed on top of the gradient rather than feather structure. Shares its entire skeleton with Emu, Finch and Flamingo.
rows.fix: Give the bill a hooked cere: short, deep, curving down to a sharp downward point with a notch on the cutting edge, coloured blue-grey with a yellow cere at the base — not yellow overall. Paint the malar stripe as a dark vertical wedge dropping from below the eye onto the cheek, blended into the head shading (skin, not decal). Replace the round tucked wing with long narrow primaries that sweep back past the tail tip in a scythe; the wingtip must be the rearmost point of the silhouette. Deepen the brow so the eye sits under a shelf. Flatten the posture — horizontal back, shoulders forward. Break the capsule by making head, breast and back one continuous painted path.

rows.readsAs: An orange piranha or a generic goldfish with spiky teeth
rows.defect: Bright glossy orange-gold, which is flatly wrong — the row and the animal both call for a short stocky dark-brown body. The head is not distinguishable from the body at all: the whole animal is one smooth ellipse, so the required 0.4 head fraction and the 'huge blunt head' do not exist, and there is not one deep pitted groove or ridge on the skull — the surface is a clean airbrushed gradient with a specular sheen, machine-smooth. The eye is large, white-ringed and prominent when the row specifies small eyes (a real fangtooth's eye is a tiny dot lost in the skull). The teeth are wrong in kind: instead of two absurdly oversized lower fangs they are a ring of eight or nine near-identical thin white spikes arranged evenly around the jawline, some pointing up and some down, which reads as piranha dentition. The tail fin is a flat brown triangle with straight machined edges butted onto the body at a hard vertical seam, and there is a small brown nub on the dorsal line that looks stuck on rather than grown out.
rows.fix: Recolour to near-black dark brown with only a dull sheen. Rebuild the head as a separate deep blunt block occupying the front 40% — tall, squared-off forehead, jaw hinged far back behind the eye so the gape is enormous. Carve the skull with deep dark pitted grooves and bony ridges as painted geometry (shadowed troughs), not surface texture. Shrink the eye to a small dark bead with no white ring. Replace the tooth ring with two dominant lower fangs so long they rise outside the upper jaw beside the snout, plus a few much smaller uppers — the size disparity is the whole animal. Blend the caudal fin into the peduncle with a tapered wedge and rayed translucent edge instead of the straight-cut triangle, and grow the dorsal fin out of the back contour rather than sitting a nub on it.

rows.readsAs: A blob of dough with a smaller blob beside it, or a two-headed amoeba
rows.defect: The defining feature is absent: the two claws are not grossly unequal. The right side has a small white pincer of two blades; the left side has a second pincer of almost the SAME blade size, merely mounted on a big pale sphere. A stranger reads that sphere as a head, not as a claw. Worse, the sphere is a separate, obviously detached ball — a full circular seam where it abuts the carapace, no arm, no joint, no merus or carpus segment connecting them, so it looks like a second body stuck on. The carapace itself is a bare cream ellipse with a soft airbrush highlight and zero shell structure: no eye orbits, no front margin, no lateral spines, no texture. The eyestalks are two tiny grey pins standing on the shell with black tips — correct in idea but so short they read as antennae stubs. There are only about four hair-thin grey wire legs total, all identical arcs, where a crab needs eight jointed walking legs with visible knees, and they float off the body edge with no attachment point. Overall silhouette is smooth blobby ovals — no crustacean anywhere in it.
rows.fix: Make the major claw enormous: the closed cheliped should be roughly the size of the entire carapace or larger, brightly coloured (orange/red) against a duller body, held up and forward, and connected by a visible jointed arm — merus, carpus, then the swollen propodus with a fixed finger and a curved dactyl. Shrink the minor claw to a delicate feeding pincer under a quarter that size. Delete the free-floating sphere; the claw must grow from a shoulder socket on the carapace with shading continuity across the join. Rebuild the carapace as a broad flattened trapezoid, wider than deep, with a defined front margin, orbital notches the eyestalks rise out of, and a granular shell texture. Lengthen the eyestalks so they stand well clear of the shell. Give it eight legs in four pairs, each with a real elbow and a pointed dactyl, all rooted at the shell margin.

rows.readsAs: A small white gull or a generic sparrow
rows.defect: The single mustRead that defines a finch — the thick triangular conical seed-cracking bill — is missing. The bill drawn is a slender narrow yellow spike, the same wedge reused on Emu, Falcon and Flamingo in this batch, and it reads as a gull or a sparrow's probe rather than a nutcracker. The tail also fails: it is a long dark pointed spear projecting well past the body, where the row requires a short notched tail. Body is compact and rounded, which is right, but it is achieved with the identical generic bird ellipse plus a scribed folded-wing lens sprayed on top; the wing marking is a hard-edged crescent decal, not plumage. Additionally the whole animal is rendered tiny — roughly 90px in a 440px frame — so it sits as a speck in the middle of the canvas while the other birds in this batch fill their frames. Colouring is a flat cream with grey wash; no finch's face pattern, cap, or wing bars. Head-to-shoulder junction is the same hard overlap crescent seen across the batch.
rows.fix: Rescale to fill ~70% of frame height. Replace the bill with a short, deep, wide-based cone — depth at the base roughly equal to its length, culmen slightly curved, pale horn or silver-grey — and set it high on a rounded forehead so the head reads bull-headed. Cut the tail to about 0.9 of body length and notch the tip into a shallow V instead of a spear point. Turn the wing decal into actual layered coverts and folded primaries with a wing bar, painted as part of the body shading so no hard crescent survives. Give it a real finch palette (warm brown back, streaked flanks, or red/rose crown and breast) rather than blank cream.

rows.readsAs: A glowing ladybird, or a luminous alien egg with a cap
rows.defect: Thread-like antennae are entirely absent — nothing projects from the head at all, and that is a stated mustRead. The legs are six thin grey arcs that DO NOT TOUCH the body: each floats in the dark with a visible gap between the leg and the elytra edge, a straight-up off-body artifact, and all six are the same featureless curve with no coxa, femur, tibia or tarsus. The head shield is drawn as a smooth dark-green dome with two eyes sitting on TOP of it, so the head is not hidden under the pronotum, it is replaced by it — and that dome joins the elytra along a hard flat straight line, a machined seam across the full width. The elytra are one perfect smooth ovoid with a single dead-straight vertical line down the middle; no leathery texture, no punctation, no separate left/right wing-cover edges, no scutellum. The glow is wrong in extent: the entire body luminesces mint green, whereas the note specifies the light comes only from the rear underside segments — here the whole insect is a lamp. Aspect is ~1.2 (a round egg) against the required 2.6, and the dorsal top-down view kills the 'crawling' posture. The rounded ovoid silhouette plus dome is a geometric primitive stack.
rows.fix: Stretch the body to aspect ~2.6 — a long narrow beetle, not an egg. Add two long thread-like antennae arcing forward off the head, each rendered as a tapering multi-segment line. Reattach the legs: root every leg at the thorax margin with a visible coxa and give it two bends (femur/tibia) plus a claw tip; they must overlap the body outline, never float. Reshape the pronotum into a flat semicircular shield that extends FORWARD over a hidden head, tucking the eyes underneath its rim rather than painting them on its crown, and blend its rear edge into the elytra with a soft shadow instead of a straight cut. Split the elytra into two separate leathery covers with a visible suture and a small triangular scutellum, add fine punctate texture and dull the sheen. Confine the emission to the last two abdominal segments at the tail tip — a bright pale yellow-green lantern with a falloff bloom — and desaturate the rest of the body to soft brown-black with the classic red-and-black pronotum marking.

rows.readsAs: A chubby white gull chick or the same generic bird as the Finch, recoloured
rows.defect: Nothing about this is a flamingo. It is a squat cream-white bird whose head sits almost directly on the shoulders — the 'long S-kinked neck' does not exist; there is a stubby thumb of neck maybe a fifth of the required length and it is straight, not kinked. The bill is a small straight yellow triangle with no downward bend at all, where the whole point of a flamingo bill is the sharp keel-break halfway along. The legs are two thin yellow sticks of very ordinary length with a single simple forward bend, no exaggerated backward-bending ankle, and they are nowhere near 'extremely long' — the body still occupies most of the height. It is not pink. Aspect fails badly: the row asks 0.55 (tall and narrow) and the render is roughly square, wider than tall through the body. And it is a straight recolour of the batch's shared bird template — the same body ellipse, same scribed folded-wing crescent with a lens highlight sprayed on, same pointed dark tail wedge, same yellow stick legs and same hard crescent seam at the head/shoulder overlap as Emu, Falcon and Finch.
rows.fix: Rebuild from proportion outward: total height should be ~1.8x width, with the trunk compressed into the top third and legs occupying the bottom half. Draw the neck as a long continuous S — forward sweep out of the shoulder, back-curve at the mid-point, forward again into the head — at least 0.35 of total height, painted as one path continuous with the breast so there is no stacked-ellipse seam. Rebuild the bill: thick and deep at the base, running level for half its length then angling sharply down to a black tip, held nearly horizontal (or inverted) rather than pointing forward. Give the legs a pronounced backward-bending ankle joint at mid-leg and stretch them to at least 0.45 of total height, with webbed feet. Palette to salmon-pink body, deeper carmine wing coverts, black primaries. Delete the shared folded-wing lens decal.

rows.readsAs: a generic teal reef fish or a small dolphin toy
rows.defect: This is not a whale at all — it is a teal-and-green fish. Zero of the three mustReads are present: the back is a single smooth unbroken arc with no knuckle bumps, the skin is a clean saturated teal-to-dark-green gradient with no mottling, no barnacle crust, no lice patches, and the snout is a sharp point rather than a narrow arched rostrum with a bowed jaw. The tail is a small VERTICAL forked fish caudal fin — a whale's flukes are horizontal and broad. The single pectoral is a flat dark-teal ellipse laid over the belly with a hard closed elliptical outline: a stuck-on paddle, not a flipper growing out of the flank. There is also a small pale grey blob floating ABOVE the head, detached from the silhouette (an off-body artifact — presumably a blowhole spout that never attached). Measured body is roughly 3.5:1, not the specified 5.5.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a cetacean: replace the vertical caudal fin with wide horizontal flukes on a tapered peduncle; delete the elliptical pectoral and grow a long sickle flipper from the shoulder with a shared contour; replace the dorsal-less smooth back with a low hump followed by 8-10 knuckle bumps in the rear third; desaturate to mottled grey-brown and stipple irregular pale barnacle clusters on the rostrum, jawline and flukes; bow the jawline and arch the rostrum; delete the detached grey blob above the head or anchor it to the blowhole.

rows.readsAs: a magenta cartoon minnow with a shadow behind it
rows.defect: The dorsal fin does not grow out of the back — it is a dark maroon shape sitting BEHIND the body layer, poking above the dorsal line with a hard straight leading edge and no shared contour with the back; a matching dark blob hangs below the belly the same way, so the fish looks pasted over its own fin sheet. That sail also carries no spots at all, so the single most diagnostic grayling feature (tall spotted sail dorsal) fails twice. No adipose fin is present. The body is a pure mandorla — two circular arcs meeting in sharp points at nose and tail base — a geometric primitive, not a trout profile. The pelvic fin is a flat isosceles triangle drawn on the flank. Colour is hot magenta on plum.
rows.fix: Grow the dorsal from the back contour itself (share the outline, taper the base into the dorsal ridge) and paint 3-4 rows of dark ocelli with an orange-red trailing edge on it; add a small fleshy adipose fin between dorsal and tail; break the mandorla by giving the head a blunter rounded snout and a deeper belly so the profile is asymmetric fore-to-aft; move the lower dark blob to a real pelvic/anal fin attached at the ventral line; pull the saturation down toward grey-lilac with a metallic flank sheen.

rows.readsAs: a teal piranha or fanged tropical fish
rows.defect: Reads as a piranha, not a shark. The teeth are seven separate white triangles floating along the jawline OUTSIDE the head silhouette, with no mouth line, no gape and no gum arc — spikes stuck on, not teeth in a mouth. The dorsal is a dark rounded lens sitting behind the body layer (same defect as Grayling in this batch), not a tall triangular fin rising from the back; a second dark lens hangs below the belly. The tail is a thin frayed fan with visible radiating spokes — a betta/fancy-goldfish tail — where the mustRead calls for a broad lunate crescent. There is no sharp grey/white countershading line: the whole animal is one teal gradient, belly included. The snout is a sharp point, not a conical rostrum.
rows.fix: Replace the fanned tail with a stiff lunate crescent, upper lobe longer; grow a tall triangular dorsal out of the back contour at mid-body and add the small second dorsal and anal fin; cut a real crescent mouth into the underside of the head with the teeth INSIDE it as a serrated arc, and shorten them; blunt the snout into a cone; and add the hard countershading break — grey above, chalk white below — as an actual silhouette-following boundary along the flank.

rows.readsAs: a small white egret or heron sitting on water
rows.defect: The bill is far too long — a straight yellow dagger roughly as long as the head plus neck, reading as an egret or heron rather than a grebe. It also meets the head at a flat abutment with a visible join line. The body is a smooth pale egg with two hard dark bands wrapped across it that read as painted stripes rather than plumage. The neck is a thin uniform-width white tube joined to the egg with a visible outline seam. The lobed-toe mustRead is entirely absent (feet hidden under the waterline, which is defensible for a swimming pose but leaves the feature unshown). The head tuft is a small spray of white spikes that reads as loose bristles rather than the grebe's tippet/horns. Positives: the puffy rounded tail-less rear is correct, and the water rings sell the swimming pose.
rows.fix: Shorten the bill to roughly head-length and taper it into the face rather than butting it on; blend the neck into the shoulder with a widening base instead of a constant-width tube; convert the two painted bands into soft feather-mass shading that follows the body's curvature; broaden the crest into a paired chestnut/black tippet fanned back from the cheeks; and let one lobed foot break the surface behind the body so the diagnostic toe shape actually appears.

rows.readsAs: a white chinchilla or a hamster figurine
rows.defect: Fails the primary mustRead outright: the body is a near-perfect cream circle, not a long low tubular body — overall aspect reads about 1.5:1, nowhere near 2.4. The tail is the opposite of what the row asks for: a thick smooth arched tube swept high over the back, and it contains an inset rounded-rectangle white highlight that looks like a moulded plastic handle. It joins the rump at a hard crescent seam. A separate grey disc sits on the hip as a pasted circle. The limbs are two small grey nubs with no structure. There is no fur texture anywhere — the whole animal is a glossy vinyl gradient. Whiskers are three perfectly straight rays.
rows.fix: Stretch the torso to a low horizontal tube on short legs with the shoulders and haunches read as separate masses; replace the arched tube tail with a short, thin, flat, sparsely-haired tail held low and roughly a third of body length; delete the rounded-rectangle highlight; dissolve the hip disc into a haunch that shares the body contour; add real limbs with a visible elbow/hock and clawed forefeet; and break the vinyl gradient with directional short-fur stippling and a paler belly.

rows.readsAs: a spiky cartoon reef fish with a paper-crown fin
rows.defect: The dorsal is a row of five hard-edged isosceles triangles sitting on a dead-straight baseline across the back — a paper crown laid over the fish, with a dark lens shape visible behind the body as a second detached layer. The tail is a hard-edged quadrilateral fan set off from the body by a visible gap at the peduncle, so it looks clipped on. None of the head mustReads are met: the snout tapers to a sharp point, the mouth is a single thin scratch with no gape, no cavernous jaw and no jutting lower jaw, and the head is neither blunt nor heavy. The spots are uniform soft grey ellipses scattered evenly like an airbrush stencil, sitting on top of the skin rather than in it. The pectoral is a flat fan of straight lines.
rows.fix: Replace the triangular crown with a continuous spiny dorsal membrane whose base merges into the back contour and whose spines curve; close the gap between tail and peduncle and round the fin into a soft paddle with rays; rebuild the head as a heavy blunt wedge with a large downturned gape and an underslung protruding lower jaw; vary the blotch sizes, edge softness and density (denser on the head and dorsal, following body curvature) so the pattern belongs to the skin; and give the pectoral a fleshy rounded base.

rows.readsAs: a purple fantail dove or a wren
rows.defect: The feathered-legs mustRead fails: the legs are bare thin yellow sticks with scaly toes, like a songbird's. The barred tail mustRead also fails — the tail is six separate pointed lozenge feathers radiating with dark gaps between them and no barring at all, which reads as a fantail dove rather than a grouse's broad fannable tail. The wing is a dark purple crescent band swept across the flank with a hard outer edge and no feather structure — sprayed on top of the body rather than a folded wing mass. Positives: the plump chicken-like body and the short yellow conical bill are right, and the posture is convincing.
rows.fix: Feather the tarsi down to the toes with shaggy pale plumage; close the gaps between the rectrices into a solid fan and cross it with 3-4 dark bars plus a terminal band; replace the crescent swoosh with a folded wing that has a scapular mass, coverts and primaries reading as separate layers tucked along the flank; and add cryptic mottled barring across the breast and back instead of the flat purple gradient.

rows.readsAs: a kiwi or a small penguin
rows.defect: The white front is a hard-edged cream oval decal pasted onto the teal body — a closed ellipse with a crisp seam all the way round, not a breast that blends into the flanks. The tail is a small dark triangle jutting from the lower right with straight machined edges and a visible abutment against the body. No wing is indicated anywhere, so the bird has a featureless flank. The bill is correctly long, slender and dagger-pointed but it is bright yellow (a guillemot's is black) and it meets the face at a visible line rather than growing from it. The head is a small ball that does sit smoothly into the neck, which is right. Body colour is teal rather than chocolate brown, so the specified two-tone contrast is only half present.
rows.fix: Feather the breast/belly boundary so the white rises up the flanks in a soft irregular edge and blends at the throat; replace the triangular tail wedge with a short rounded tail that emerges from the rump contour; add a folded wing along the flank with a visible primary tip crossing the tail; darken the bill toward black-grey and blend the base into the facial feathering; and shift the body toward warm dark brown so the countershading contrast matches the reference.

rows.readsAs: a generic minnow or a small barracuda
rows.defect: No beak. The mustRead "long narrow toothed beak snout" is absent — the right-hand end is a plain rounded fish head with a tiny purple eye and no elongated rostrum at all; the whole animal is a smooth spindle with a single continuous outline. The "teeth" are five white sawtooth triangles painted along the lower belly/jaw line, floating on the surface rather than set in a jaw, and they read as a decal. No diamond ganoid armour anywhere — the flank is a flat mint-green gradient with two lighter lengthwise streaks and nothing else. Fin placement is wrong: the one visible dorsal is a small dark triangle at roughly mid-body, not set far back near the tail, and there is no anal fin. The caudal is a dark green paddle blob attached to the body by an abrupt narrow neck with a hard colour break — a visible seam where the tail is stuck on. The creature also occupies only ~40% of the canvas width, floating in empty space.
rows.fix: Extend the head into a true rostrum: at least 30-35% of total length, near-parallel-sided, tapering only at the tip, with the tooth row set INSIDE the jaw line as small interlocking spikes along both upper and lower edges rather than as belly decals. Move the dorsal and anal fins back to ~80-85% of body length so they sit opposite each other just ahead of the tail. Replace the flank gradient with an interlocking rhombic ganoid scale field that follows body curvature and shrinks toward the tail. Kill the tail seam — carry the body taper continuously into the caudal peduncle with the same skin tone and scale field, so the fin grows out of the flesh instead of butting against it. Scale the whole animal up to fill ~85% of frame width.

rows.readsAs: a giant pink earthworm coiled into a ring
rows.defect: The single most important mustRead is not just missing but inverted: instead of long pale stripes running the body length, the entire animal is ringed with dense TRANSVERSE ribs running perpendicular to the axis, top to bottom, all the way around the coil. That cross-banding plus the fat uniform tube reads as annuli, not scales. The coil is close to a perfect torus — a near-circular ring with an even bore hole in the middle — a geometric primitive, not a snake's asymmetric loose loop. The body is far too thick for aspect 8: the tube diameter is roughly a quarter of the coil diameter, so it looks like a fat doughnut rather than a slender serpent. Colour is a saturated hot magenta with no belly/dorsal value split, so the form is only readable from the rib shading. The head does read correctly — small, barely wider than the neck, with a yellow-ringed eye and a red forked tongue — and it is the only part that says "snake".
rows.fix: Replace the transverse ribbing entirely with three longitudinal pale stripes — one mid-dorsal, two lateral — that follow the coil around every bend and stay continuous through the curves; keep only a faint scale texture crosswise, subordinate to the stripes. Thin the body by about 40% and break the torus: make the coil an irregular S-loop with one overlap crossing over itself and a visible tapering tail tip, so no part of the outline is a circular arc of constant radius. Add a paler ventral tone on the underside of the loop to give the tube roundness independent of the ribs, and desaturate the magenta toward an olive-with-pink base so the stripes have something to contrast against.

rows.readsAs: a salamander or an axolotl
rows.defect: Two of the three mustReads fail. The eyes are not huge and lidless: there is one tiny dark eye barely larger than the spots on the back, with a thin vertical slit, set on a smooth blank face — it reads as a dot, not the dominant feature of the skull. The feet have no toes at all: each limb is a plain grey rounded capsule ending in a blunt stub, so there are no broad splayed digits and no lamellae pads. The construction is visibly primitive-based — a light ellipse for the body, a separate slightly overlapping oval for the head with a soft but readable seam at the neck junction, four identical grey capsules for legs, and a hook-shaped capsule for the tail with a grey stripe painted down its middle. The mouth is a single straight ruled line. The dark blotches are flat grey ovals of uniform edge softness scattered on top of the gradient — they do not wrap the body's curvature or cluster the way real gecko tubercles do, so they read as sprayed on. Skin has no granular bumps, just an airbrushed sheen. In this batch it is far closer to a salamander than to any lizard.
rows.fix: Blow the eye up to at least 3x its current diameter so it bulges past the head outline in silhouette, give it a full round golden iris with a narrow vertical pupil and a fixed clear spectacle highlight, and remove any eyelid line. Rebuild the feet: five splayed toes per foot, radiating and slightly upcurved, with visible transverse lamellae bands on the undersides and widened toe tips. Merge head into body with a continuous outline — no overlapping second oval — and widen the head into a triangular skull that flares behind the eyes. Replace the flat spot decals with a granular tubercle field of small raised bumps whose highlights follow the body's light direction and whose density varies over the back, and thicken the tail into a plump segmented carrot with fat rings rather than a smooth grey-striped hook.

rows.readsAs: a house mouse
rows.defect: The tail fails its mustRead on both counts: it is a bare thin curved filament of even width with no fur texture and, critically, no dark tuft at the tip — it just tapers to nothing, which is the exact feature that separates a gerbil from a mouse. The hind foot is a short stub, not the elongated jerboa-like foot called for; the haunch is there but the foot below it is barely a nub. There is no fur anywhere — the entire body is a single smooth mint gradient with an airbrushed highlight, so it reads plastic. The ear is a flat leaf shape laid over the head outline with a lighter inner leaf inside it, sitting on rather than growing from the skull. The incisors are two white rectangles with a hard straight edge. The eye is a single small black dot with a highlight; "large dark eyes on a pointed face" is only half satisfied because the muzzle is quite blunt. The one clearly good passage is the rear leg and the rounded rump, which have believable mass.
rows.fix: Add a black or dark-brown tuft occupying the last 15-20% of the tail, and give the whole tail a fine fur nap — short strokes angled backward — instead of a bare line, thickening it toward the base where it leaves the rump so there is no pin join. Lengthen the hind foot to roughly the length of the head, sole flat on the ground with a visible ankle above it. Break the plastic surface with a directional fur field over the body edges — a slightly ragged silhouette rather than a clean gradient boundary. Sharpen the muzzle to a point and enlarge the eye by about 50%. Replace the rectangular incisors with two chisel-shaped teeth with a slight bevel.

rows.readsAs: a flat cutout crocodile or a toy dinosaur
rows.defect: All three mustReads fail. The snout is a solid flat triangle — an arrowhead about 15% of body length — instead of an extremely long needle-thin tube; there is no thin rostrum, and the teeth are four little triangles hanging under the arrowhead like a sawblade rather than interlocking rows along a slender jaw. There is no ghara knob on the snout tip. The tail is a long thin flat wedge tapering to a point at the left, low and blade-like — the opposite of a tall laterally flattened paddle. The whole render is built from flat facets and ruled straight lines: the dorsal line from head to tail is one straight edge, the belly is another, the eleven dorsal scutes are identical perfect isoceles triangles pinned along the back at even spacing, and the two legs are straight machined sticks with hard corners at the ankle. Head and body meet at a hard chevron colour break, so the head reads as bolted on. It sits in the bottom fifth of a 440px canvas with the upper 70% empty.
rows.fix: Rebuild the snout as a long parallel-sided tube at least 40% of total length, only a few pixels tall, with a slight downward set and a bulbous rounded ghara swelling at the very tip; run fine interlocking teeth along the top and bottom of that tube so they mesh. Make the tail deep: expand it vertically to at least twice body depth over the last third and compress it laterally, with a paired dorsal crest of soft keeled scutes fading into it. Replace the identical triangular scutes with irregular keeled osteoderms of varying size and angle that emerge from the skin with rounded bases. Curve the dorsal and ventral lines, thicken and bend the legs at elbow and wrist with splayed clawed feet, and eliminate the chevron at the neck so head, jaw and body share one continuous surface. Recentre and enlarge to fill the frame.

rows.readsAs: a centipede, correctly, but a short fat bead-bodied one
rows.defect: The body is explicitly wrong against the reference note: it is a string of round beads, each segment a fully spherical bulb with its own specular highlight, so it reads tubular and knobbly rather than flattened. Real centipede terga are wide flat plates; here nothing is flat. Aspect is badly short — the animal measures roughly 4:1, not 9:1, so it looks like a stubby grub rather than a long ribbon. The legs are uniform hairline strokes all swept back at nearly the same angle with no joints, no femur/tibia articulation and no tarsal claw; they read as drawn hairs rather than limbs, and because they all sweep back identically the required long trailing REAR legs are indistinguishable from the rest. The forcipules do read — two yellow hooks under the head — and the red antennae are present, which is the strongest passage in the picture. The animal occupies about a third of the canvas.
rows.fix: Flatten the segments: replace each sphere with a broad low tergite plate that is wider than it is tall, overlapping the one behind it, with a keeled centre and a defined side margin so the dorsal surface reads as a series of shields. Stretch the body to at least 8:1, adding segments rather than scaling, and put an S-curve through it. Give every leg two visible joints and a claw, and vary the angle along the body — front legs angled forward, mid legs lateral, rear legs raked back — then make the final pair 2-3x longer than the rest and clearly separated as trailing sensory legs to mirror the antennae. Enlarge to fill ~85% of frame.

rows.readsAs: a scallop shell, or a folded paper hand fan
rows.defect: Both mustReads fail. There is no wavy zigzag meeting lip: the two valves meet along a single almost perfectly straight horizontal ruled line across the top, with only a hairline of pale grey on it — no interdigitating scalloped teeth. There is no iridescent fleshy mantle bulging between the valves either; that pale grey hairline is all the flesh there is, and it is flat, unpatterned and inside the outline rather than swelling out of it. The shell itself is a single fan, not two heavy fluted valves — radiating rays are perfectly straight lines converging on one geometric point at the bottom, evenly spaced, with no flute depth, no growth-ring cross-banding and no thickened rim. The silhouette is a symmetrical circular-arc fan sitting on two small stuck-on grey triangles that read as feet or a stand rather than as shell. Proportion is wrong too: the reference calls for aspect 1.5 wide, but the render is roughly as tall as it is wide.
rows.fix: Give the aperture a deep zigzag: 6-8 large interlocking wave crests where the valves meet, with the upper valve's crests fitting the lower valve's troughs, and thicken the lip so it casts its own shadow. Push a bulging mantle out through that gap — a fleshy lobe that swells ABOVE the shell line, mottled with iridescent blue-green-gold vermiculation and darker eye spots, wet-looking with soft specular highlights. Rebuild the shell as two valves seen from the front, each with 4-6 broad rounded flutes that are three-dimensional ridges and valleys, not lines, crossed by concentric growth bands and ragged frilly growth edges at the margins. Widen the whole thing to roughly 1.5:1, drop the two triangular feet, and seat it on a byssal base or substrate instead.

rows.readsAs: a shrimp or a krill
rows.defect: The defining mustRead — overlapping armoured segment plates like a giant pill bug — is entirely absent. The body is one smooth featureless pale-green balloon with an airbrushed highlight and a few soft blotches; there is not a single tergite edge, no overlap, no armour line anywhere on it. Leg count also fails badly: instead of seven pairs down the sides there are four or five tiny pale paddle shapes bunched under the front of the head and a fan-shaped cluster at the rear right, leaving most of the body's length with no limbs at all. The eye is a single dark bead — it reads as a simple round eye, not a large fixed compound eye, and there is no facet structure. The two long antennae are present and are the only convincing feature, but they are hairline strokes with no segmentation and one of them is far longer than the other. The head is a separate small oval abutting the big body oval with a readable junction between them. The rear fan plus the smooth curved back make it read as a shrimp rather than a woodlouse.
rows.fix: Segment the body: 7-8 broad overlapping tergite plates arcing across the back from side to side, each with a raised centre and a lipped trailing edge that casts a shadow onto the plate behind, plus flared epimeral side flanges — the plates must define the silhouette, giving it a scalloped outline rather than a smooth curve. Attach exactly seven pairs of jointed pereopods, one pair per plate, spaced evenly along the whole body length and visible on both sides, each with femur, tibia and a hooked claw. Enlarge the eye substantially, place a matching one on the far side of the head, and render both as flat dark hemispheres with a faint facet grid and no highlight sparkle. Add the second pair of antennae, segment all four, and match the two long ones in length. Fuse the head into the first body segment as a broad cephalon with a curved front margin so there is no oval-on-oval seam, and replace the shrimp-like rear fan with a pleotelson shield flanked by two short uropods.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon seagull or shorebird chick — nobody would say ibis
rows.defect: The bill is a short STRAIGHT yellow spike angled slightly upward — there is not a trace of the ibis's long smoothly downcurved decurved bill, which is the one feature the whole animal is known for. There is no bare facial skin: the face is the same white as the body with a small black bead eye. There is no long neck at all — a perfect white circle head is butted directly onto the top-left of a white egg body, and you can see the seam arc where the circle overlaps the ellipse. The wing is a separate flat grey lens shape laid on top of the body with a hard outline, and the tail is a grey triangle poking out the back with a straight machined edge. Legs are two plain yellow tubes with no thigh, knee or feathering — they enter the body with no hip.
rows.fix: Rebuild the bill as a single long tapering arc sweeping down ~90-120deg to a fine tip, length roughly 1.2x the head diameter; render it as one stroke that widens into the skull rather than a cone stuck to a circle. Extend the neck to a genuine S-curve that is drawn as part of the body silhouette (one filled path head->neck->breast), and make the head an egg, not a circle. Add bare dark-red/grey facial skin from the bill base around the eye. Replace the lens-shaped wing decal with a folded wing whose leading edge is continuous with the shoulder contour.

rows.readsAs: a gold mealworm or a cartoon earthworm
rows.defect: It is bright GOLD-YELLOW. The reference says black-brown; a glacier ice worm rendered in canary yellow reads as the opposite animal. It is also nowhere near thread-thin — the body is a fat tapering sausage about 1/12 of its length in width, more mealworm than annelid. The segmentation is a stack of identical hard-edged discs of uniform pitch, like a machined bellows hose or a coil spring, rather than soft annuli that vary along the body. The head end is a smooth ball with a single black dot eye stuck on it, and the reference explicitly calls for hidden eyes.
rows.fix: Recolour to a near-black brown (#241a12 to #3a2a1c) with a faint cold sheen instead of the gold ramp. Thin the body to roughly 1/25 of its length and taper both ends so the head is only slightly blunter than the tail. Replace the uniform disc stack with irregular soft annuli whose spacing compresses on the inside of each curve and stretches on the outside. Delete the eye dot entirely.

rows.readsAs: a red barracuda or a bloodied salmon
rows.defect: The fish is opaque CRIMSON RED. The icefish's entire identity is that it is bloodless — translucent white with visible internal structure — so this is a direct inversion of the must-read feature, and there is no internal structure visible anywhere. The head is not oversized: it is a small narrow point that is if anything smaller than the body depth, and the jaws are a thin dark wedge line, not wide pike-like gaping jaws. The pectoral fin is a single small dark triangle stuck flat on the flank with a hard straight edge — not a large fan. Dorsal fins are two little maroon bumps sitting on the back contour like blobs of putty; the tail is a flat symmetrical dark-red arrowhead with straight edges.
rows.fix: Recolour the body to a translucent bluish-white with alpha so the substrate darkens through it, and paint a visible spine, gill arches and a dark gut shadow inside the outline. Enlarge the head to ~0.3 of total length and open the jaws into a broad crocodilian pike gape with the lower jaw projecting. Rebuild the pectoral as a large translucent ray-veined fan attached at a shoulder that grows out of the flank, and give the caudal fin lobed, ray-striated edges instead of a solid arrowhead.

rows.readsAs: a blue plastic lizard toy, or the same body-plan as a newt
rows.defect: No dewlap — the throat is a clean ellipse edge with nothing hanging under the chin, so a required feature is simply absent. The tail is long but completely unbanded: it is one flat blue tube with a single dark stripe painted down its length. The dorsal spines are a row of solid black isoceles triangles sitting ON the back line with a visible hard seam where each meets the body; they read as glued-on spikes, not scales growing from the nape. The four legs are identical featureless capsules with rounded ends, entering the belly with no shoulder or hip mass at all — pure stuck-on primitives. The head is a perfect ellipse with a single ruler-straight horizontal line for the mouth. The grey blotches are soft airbrush blobs sprayed over the top of the body with no relation to any scale pattern.
rows.fix: Add a large thin semicircular dewlap hanging from jaw to chest, with a scalloped lower edge and its own shading. Band the tail with alternating dark rings that wrap the cylinder in perspective (narrower on the far side). Replace the triangle row with a soft-edged serrated crest whose base blends into the dorsal ridge over several pixels, tallest at the nape and shrinking down the tail. Rebuild the limbs with a thick upper segment, an elbow/knee break and splayed five-toed feet, and blend the shoulder into the ribcage. Break the mouth line into a jaw curve with a tympanum and a subtympanic scale behind it, and replace the sprayed blotches with tessellated scale texture.

rows.readsAs: a honeybee or a small wasp
rows.defect: This is not a bat — it is an insect. The render shows three yellow spheres in a row (head, thorax, abdomen), two large translucent amber VEINED INSECT WINGS fanned off the rear sphere, four thin bristle legs, and a single black dot eye. There is no fur, no membrane stretched over elongated finger bones, no ears of any kind let alone large upright ears with a tragus, and no hooked clinging feet. Every one of the three must-read features is absent. The generator appears to have keyed off the word 'Insect' in the name and built the prey instead of the predator.
rows.fix: Route this to the chiropteran builder, not the insect builder. Build a furred body with a dog-like muzzled head roughly 0.3 of the figure, two tall upright ears each with an internal spike tragus, and wings as a single dark membrane spanning four elongated splayed finger bones from a thumb claw at the leading edge to the ankle, with the interfemoral membrane enclosing the tail. Add tiny hooked feet. The wing must be one continuous membrane whose root is the shoulder muscle, not a pair of separate lobes.

rows.readsAs: a shrimp, or a flea
rows.defect: There are no overlapping armour segments anywhere — the body is two smooth yellow spheres (a big front ball and a smaller rear ball) with a faint seam between them, which is the exact rounded-blob silhouette an isopod must never have. It is not flattened; it is spherical and read as tall. I count roughly four thin hair-like legs under the front ball, not seven pairs of similar walking legs. The rear ends in a spray of pale feathery quills that reads as a shrimp's tail fan rather than a pleotelson plate flanked by two uropods. The two antennae are absurdly long — the lower one is nearly the width of the whole canvas and is a single unarticulated line. The faint olive smudges on the back are airbrushed on top of the sphere and follow none of the body's form.
rows.fix: Rebuild the dorsum as seven overlapping pereonite plates plus a head shield and a rear pleotelson, each plate a flattened arc that laps over the one behind with a soft shadowed lip, so the segmentation IS the silhouette (a scalloped outline, not a smooth ball). Flatten the aspect so the body is wide and low. Draw seven pairs of jointed legs of similar length fanning out from beneath the plate edges. Replace the feather spray with a single triangular pleotelson flanked by two short two-branched uropods. Shorten the antennae to about half the body length and articulate them into 4-5 tapering segments.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon rabbit — the closest to shippable in this batch, but a cottontail rather than a jackrabbit
rows.defect: The ears and head are good, but there are no long powerful hind legs — the rear of the animal is just the body ellipse with a small dark stub of a foot poking out at the bottom, so the defining jackrabbit feature is missing. The haunch is indicated only by a painted-on darker arc across the flank, and that arc is a hard visible seam line rather than muscle mass. There is a second hard seam at the front where the shoulder ellipse overlaps the body. The incisors are a literal white RECTANGLE with a straight vertical split down the middle, sitting on the muzzle as an obvious geometric primitive. The ear openings are a flat pink lens shape with a crisp outline and no fur transition into the head.
rows.fix: Build a real hind limb: a large thigh mass that grows out of the rump contour, a strong angled hock, and a long foot planted from heel to toe on the ground — the hind foot on a jackrabbit should be about as long as the head. Delete the painted haunch arc and the shoulder seam; let the mass changes come from shading on one continuous body path. Replace the tooth rectangle with two small chisel incisors with a rounded outer face and a soft shadow under the lip. Soften the ear-interior lens with a fur-fringed edge.

rows.readsAs: a small white dove or a chick — and specifically it reads as the Ibis from this same batch with the bill shortened
rows.defect: None of the three must-read features are present. The bill is a small short orange cone — a finch/chick bill, not a stout crow-like bill. There is no blue anywhere on the bird and no barred wing patch: the wing is a single flat grey lens laid on a white body with a hard outline. The tail is a short dark grey triangle wedge sticking out the back, not a long broad tail. Head is a perfect circle butted onto the egg body with a visible overlap seam, and the crest is three thin white spikes stuck on the crown. The figure is also tiny in frame — it occupies maybe a third of the canvas, so it reads as a chick. Critically, this is built from the same parts as the Ibis in this same batch: identical white ellipse body, identical circle head, identical grey lens wing and grey triangle tail, identical yellow tube legs.
rows.fix: Recolour to jay plumage — pinkish-buff body, black moustachial stripe, white rump, and a wing panel of alternating black-and-blue bars painted as individual covert feathers rather than a solid patch. Thicken the bill into a deep conical corvid bill about as long as the head is wide, with a slight hook. Lengthen the tail to roughly body length and square it off with visible rectrices. Merge the head into the body with a proper nape curve so no seam is visible, and scale the whole bird up to fill the frame. Vary the wing/tail geometry from the Ibis builder so the two birds do not share a silhouette.

rows.readsAs: a generic teal cartoon bird — a quail or a bluebird
rows.defect: A generic teal cartoon songbird standing on the ground — the 'flying' posture is absent (it is perched, feet planted, with a cast shadow under it). None of the three mustReads land: the crest is a tiny 4-spike tuft of the same cyan as the body, not a spiky rufous punk fan; there is no bare blue face and no red eye (the eye is a plain black bead with a white catchlight on a fully feathered cyan head); the tail is a small dark triangular wedge poking out to the right, not long and broad, and the chest is a plain egg with no heavy-chest/slim-neck contrast (head sits directly on the body with no neck at all). The wing is a flat lens-shaped decal with a hard dark outline pasted onto the body side rather than plumage growing out of the flank, and the body silhouette is a smooth featureless ovoid. Critically this is the SAME body template as the Hornbill in this batch — identical ovoid, identical lens wing with the same outline, identical tail wedge, identical two-toe orange legs, recoloured.
rows.fix: Recolour to olive-brown body with a rufous belly; replace the tuft with a tall ragged rufous crest of 6-8 splayed shafts of unequal length rising from the crown and leaning back; carve a bare skin mask around the eye in saturated blue with a red iris; extend the tail to ~45% of total length as a broad fan of separated rectrices with pale terminal band; add a visible slim neck by narrowing the head-body join and raising the head; switch posture to airborne (feet folded, wings extended, drop the ground shadow); and fork the body template away from Hornbill's so the two are not the same mesh in two colours.

rows.readsAs: a pale white ant or a termite
rows.defect: An off-white/pale-grey insect on a dark ground that reads as a pale ant or a termite, not a honeybee. The banded amber-and-black abdomen is missing entirely — the abdomen is silvery white with two faint light-grey bands and no black, no amber anywhere on the animal. The 'furry thorax' is rendered as a ring of stiff straight yellow spikes radiating outward from a perfectly smooth glossy white sphere — the spikes are stuck onto the sphere's outline with a visible hard boundary rather than being fuzz emerging from a fuzzy surface. Only ONE small grey wing is visible, and it has no venation and is opaque, not clear; the second pair is absent. No pollen baskets on the hind legs — the legs are plain thin dark hairlines with no corbicular load. Head, thorax and abdomen are three separate glossy spheres/ellipsoids butted together with visible seams, so it reads as assembled beads rather than one body. Aspect is also far short of 2.4 — the animal is roughly 1.6 wide-to-tall.
rows.fix: Repaint the abdomen with 4-5 hard alternating amber/black bands wrapping the volume (band edges curving with the form, not straight); make the thorax fuzz a soft irregular halo in ochre-brown that dissolves the sphere's edge instead of spiking off it; add two pairs of translucent wings with a visible vein tracery, forewing longer, held out from the thorax; add a bulging orange-yellow pollen pellet on each hind tibia; blend the head/thorax/abdomen joins with tapered waist and petiole so no seam shows; and lengthen the body to hit aspect 2.4.

rows.readsAs: a generic purple cartoon bird with a yellow beak — a kingfisher or a toucan
rows.defect: The single most identifying feature of a hornbill — the hollow casque on top of the bill — is completely absent. The bill is a smooth straight yellow cone angled slightly UPWARD with no downcurve, closer to a kingfisher's or a toucan's dagger than a hornbill's heavy decurved sabre. There is no bare coloured throat or eye skin and no lashes: the eye is a plain black dot with a catchlight sitting in solid purple feathering. Head fraction reads about 0.22, not the specified 0.45 — the head is a small ball on a big body. The tail is a short dark wedge, not long and broad. The bill meets the face at a hard flat seam where the yellow cone abuts the purple head. This is the identical body template as the Hoatzin in this batch (same ovoid torso, same lens-shaped outlined wing decal, same tail wedge, same orange two-toe feet, same magenta crest tuft) simply recoloured purple.
rows.fix: Scale the head up to ~0.45 of body length; rebuild the bill as a long heavy decurved sabre whose base fairs smoothly into the skull and add a hollow casque ridge riding along its top surface; paint a bare wrinkled throat and orbital patch in red/blue with long dark eyelashes over the eye; extend the tail into a long broad graduated fan with pale banding; drop the punk crest tuft (hornbills do not have one); and give it a body silhouette distinct from Hoatzin's.

rows.readsAs: a spiky grey tortoise
rows.defect: Reads as a spiky tortoise, not a lizard. The body is a tall DOMED egg standing on end, not the flat wide pancake disc the reference requires — the outline is essentially an upright ovoid and the whole animal is taller than it is deep. A huge thick grey banana-shaped tail curls up and forward over the left side, roughly a third of the animal's mass, directly contradicting the 'very short tail' note; it also joins the body with a hard grey-on-grey edge and reads as a separate part laid over the shell. The horn crown is a small scruffy fan of pale spikes clustered right behind the head only, and they point up and back like a tuft of hair rather than a heavy bony crown of thick backward-pointing spikes ringing the rear of the skull. The flank fringe is present but appears only as a row of white triangles along the BOTTOM belly line between the legs, reading as teeth under the body rather than a fringe on the flanks. The dark spots are uniform soft ellipses scattered over the dome like sprayed-on polka dots with no relation to the animal's form or scale texture. Legs are two grey sausages with no feet or toes.
rows.fix: Flatten the body to a wide low disc — widen it and cut the height by half so the outline reads as a pancake from any angle; delete the curled tail and replace with a short blunt stub under 15% of body length; rebuild the horn crown as 6-8 thick tapered bony spikes fanning backward from the whole rear rim of the skull, the two central pair longest, growing out of the skull silhouette; move the fringe scales to the left and right flank edges so they break the disc's outline in profile; replace the polka dots with a mottled beige/rust desert camouflage that follows the dorsal ridges and add keeled scale texture; add splayed sprawling limbs with visible toes.

rows.readsAs: a grey flying saucer with a needle spike, or a jellyfish
rows.defect: The overall gestalt is close, but the front shield is a near-perfect symmetrical ELLIPSE rather than the horseshoe's forward-bowed crescent with swept-back trailing genal spines — as drawn it is a geometric primitive and the piece reads as a flying saucer with a needle under it. The mustRead 'all legs concealed beneath the shell' is violated: a fan of four hard straight bristle-lines protrudes from each side of the small rear body segment, clearly visible outside the shell outline. Two thin white arcs are laid across the left and right of the carapace as straight-ish machined lines rather than the shell's own moulted ridges. The eyes are two identical perfect black ellipses stamped on the surface with no lid, socket or surrounding sculpture. The telson is a flawless isoceles triangle needle with a hard butt-join to the body and no taper variation — it looks machined and glued on. The speckling is a uniform sprayed dot field that ignores the dome's curvature and the ridge lines.
rows.fix: Reshape the prosoma into a true crescent — pull the front edge forward into a rounded bow and sweep the two rear corners back into pointed genal spines so the outline is a horseshoe, not an oval; delete the protruding side bristles entirely (or tuck them fully inside the shell footprint); replace the two white arcs with soft raised ridge highlights that curve with the dome; sculpt the compound eyes as raised kidney-shaped bumps with a surrounding bevel instead of flat black ellipses; taper the telson organically from a wide fairing at its base and add a slight curve and surface facets; and drive the speckling with the shell's cuticle so it stretches over the curvature.

rows.readsAs: a generic pink cartoon monkey or a small ape
rows.defect: No swollen bearded throat pouch anywhere — the throat is a plain pale pink area with no bulge and no beard, so the defining howler feature is missing. The tail is a THIN uniform dark whip curving up behind the left shoulder, not a thick prehensile cable, it has no bare gripping tip, and it emerges from behind the upper back near the shoulder rather than from the base of the spine — a clear anatomical mis-attachment. The head wears a hard-edged darker pink cap that cuts a straight line across the skull like a helmet, a visible sprayed-on seam rather than a change in fur. The face is a flat pink oval with two circular white-and-black button eyes and no muzzle projection at all — the reference calls for a short muzzle but there is zero snout. The arms are featureless dark magenta sausages with no hands, no fingers and no elbow, meeting the torso at an abrupt darker boundary. The blotchy magenta patches on the chest are soft airbrushed clouds floating on the surface, unrelated to fur direction. Posture is a seated frontal biped, not the specified hunched quadruped.
rows.fix: Add a large rounded hyoid bulge under the jaw, covered in long shaggy fur that overhangs the chest, in a contrasting darker tone; thicken the tail to at least the diameter of a forearm, root it at the base of the spine, taper it, and strip the last third to bare pale wrinkled skin curled into a grip; delete the helmet line and replace with graduated fur-length change; push a short blunt muzzle forward with nostrils and a downturned lip; give the arms hands with opposable thumbs and a defined shoulder mass that flows into the torso; replace the airbrushed blotches with directional fur strokes; and reset to a hunched quadrupedal stance on a branch.

rows.readsAs: a tiny distant sparrow with a long twig in its mouth
rows.defect: Rendered at roughly one-sixth the linear scale of everything else in the batch — the bird occupies about 70x40 px of a 440x440 canvas and is mostly empty frame, so at card size it is a smudge. Content-wise: the needle bill is there and is correctly long, but the wings are NOT blade-like or blurred — there is a single small solid dark-purple wedge lying flat along the back with a hard edge, no motion blur, no narrow sickle shape, and no second wing. There is no iridescent gorget; the throat is the same flat dull mauve as the rest of the bird. The feet are drawn as three bright yellow straight lines dangling below the body — the note explicitly says the feet are tiny and tucked, and these are the most conspicuous colour in the whole image. The body is held fully HORIZONTAL like a perched sparrow, not near-vertical as a hovering hummingbird. The bill is a flat straight brown stick that butts against the head with no facial fairing.
rows.fix: Scale the render up 4-5x so the bird fills the frame; rotate the body to about 60-70 degrees from horizontal for a hover; replace the flat wedge with two narrow sickle wings swept forward and rendered as a translucent blurred arc on each side; paint an iridescent gorget across the throat with a hard-edged saturated colour shift (magenta/emerald) that reads as structural colour; shrink and tuck the feet up into the belly feathers and desaturate them; and fair the bill base into the skull with a smooth taper.

rows.readsAs: a grey shark, or a generic dolphin
rows.defect: Reads as a shark. The pectoral flippers — 'enormously long white wing-like' and the single most diagnostic humpback feature — are not delivered: there is one pale narrow paddle lying flat against the belly, roughly a quarter of body length, with a hard dark outline where it meets the torso, plus a second tiny grey stub protruding from the mid-flank that looks like a separate part glued on. Neither is long, neither is wing-like, neither is white against a dark body in a readable way. The tail flukes are a small notched shark-like caudal fin with a perfectly smooth, straight trailing edge — no scalloping at all — and the peduncle narrows into it with a visible hard step. The dorsal fin is a tall triangular shark fin rather than the humpback's low stubby hump on a raised ridge. The tubercles are the one thing that works, but they are rendered as a scatter of identical soft white dots (a sprayed dot field) rather than raised knobs with their own shading, and they spill in a stripe along the flank well behind the jaw. Two loose dark wavy squiggle strokes float over the jaw and over the flipper root, unattached to any anatomy. The body itself is a smooth torpedo capsule with no ventral pleats on the throat.
rows.fix: Rebuild the pectorals as two enormous scythe-shaped flippers at ~30% of body length, white on top, held out and away from the body so they break the silhouette, with the base swelling smoothly into the flank rather than outlined; delete the mid-flank stub; rebuild the flukes wider and add a deep scalloped/wavy trailing edge with an S-curve notch at the centre; replace the shark dorsal with a low blunt hump set on a raised ridge two-thirds back; convert the tubercles to raised bumps with individual highlight and shadow, sized irregularly, confined to the rostrum and lower jaw; delete the two floating dark squiggles; and add long ventral pleat grooves running from chin to belly.

rows.readsAs: a purple anchovy or a swimming slug — the eye is the only cue that it is a fish at all
rows.defect: The mustRead 'thread-like filamentous limb fins' is entirely absent — there is one small translucent grey pectoral flap near the head and nothing else; no filaments anywhere. The silhouette is a symmetric pointed lens/capsule with a soft grey halo outline around it, so there is no head at all: the front end and rear end are the same shape and the only thing telling you which is the head is a white bead eye stuck near the right tip. The 'pointed continuous tail fin' is a tiny dark whisker tuft poking off the left tip, disconnected in value from the purple body — it reads as a stray hair, not a fin continuous with the body. Body is a flat purple gradient lozenge with no scale texture. Aspect measures about 4.5, short of the specified 6.
rows.fix: Grow 4 long thread-like filamentous fins (2 pectoral, 2 pelvic) out of the body wall as tapering strands that share the body's purple and darken toward the tip, rooted with a widened base rather than butted on. Break the fore/aft symmetry: widen and blunt the head third, add a jaw/gill line, and taper the rear third into the continuous lance-shaped tail fin so the tail is the body narrowing, not an appended tuft. Stretch to aspect 6 and add fine overlapping scale mottle.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon monkey or a small orangutan — not specifically a macaque
rows.defect: Posture is wrong: the reference says quadruped and this is a front-facing squat/sit, with both arms hanging straight down at the sides. Every limb is stuck ON: the two arms are separate brown tubes whose tops butt against the orange torso with a hard dark outline seam at the shoulder, and the thighs are two brown ovals overlapping the torso with the same visible edge — nothing grows out of the body. The torso itself is a rounded rectangle with parallel vertical sides. No bare pink or red face: the face is a flat brown oval with a lighter cap band and no muzzle projection whatsoever, just two eyes floating on it. The tail is a long C-curve sweeping up above shoulder height on the left — far too long for the 'short to medium tail' called for, and it too meets the hip as a butt joint.
rows.fix: Repose to true quadruped side-on with the spine horizontal. Merge the arms and legs into the torso silhouette with a shared outline — no per-limb stroke at the joint; let the shoulder and hip mass swell out of the trunk. Reshape the torso from a rounded rectangle to a barrel that narrows to the waist. Repaint the face as a bare pink/red mask with a projecting short muzzle and brow ridge, distinct from the fur ring. Cut the tail to roughly one third of body length and root it as a taper off the rump.

rows.readsAs: a dark pigeon or grackle with two wires stuck in its tail
rows.defect: All three mustReads fail. The beak is a small yellow triangle about a fifth of the head — not a huge pale hooked beak; there is no hook and no curve. There is no bare white facial patch or feather tracery; the head is uniform charcoal. The tail is two thin straight rods projecting horizontally to the right, dark grey, with a visible gap where they meet the rump — stuck-on wires, not a streamer, and they hang horizontally rather than the vertical drape the note describes. The wing is a hard-edged teardrop plate laid on the flank with its own dark outline and a lighter inner facet, reading as a decal rather than folded feathers. The whole bird is monochrome charcoal, which for a macaw is a colour blocker. Aspect is landscape (~1.3 wide) where 0.5 tall was specified. This is the same base render as the Magpie in this batch, recoloured.
rows.fix: Replace the beak with an oversized pale hooked bill that occupies a third of the head, with the cere and the down-curved upper mandible. Paint a bare white facial patch around the eye with fine dark feather lines across it. Rebuild the tail as two long tapered streamer feathers, rooted inside the rump silhouette and hanging steeply so the render is taller than wide. Dissolve the wing plate outline into overlapping covert and primary shapes. Give it saturated macaw colour.

rows.readsAs: a generic striped baitfish — a juvenile striped bass or a convict cichlid
rows.defect: The finlet row before the tail is missing entirely — the body runs smooth from the last fin to the peduncle. The bars are straight vertical grey stripes evenly spaced down the whole flank, not the wavy dark tiger bars over the dorsal half, and the fish is greyscale white/silver with no steel-blue back at all, so two of the three mustReads read wrong. The tail stalk is a plain narrow pinch with no keel. The dorsal fins are two translucent grey ghost blobs sitting on top of the back — you can see the body's stripes straight through them and their circular edges overlap the outline, so they read as separate semi-transparent discs floating above the fish rather than fins growing from the spine. The bars are also uniformly spaced and hard-edged, reading as sprayed on over a plain gradient body.
rows.fix: Add the row of 5-6 small finlets between the second dorsal and the tail on both dorsal and ventral margins, and add the lateral keel to the peduncle. Repaint the back steel-blue-green with the bars as irregular wavy dark stripes confined to the upper half and fading at the lateral line, painted into the skin gradient rather than over it. Make the dorsal fins opaque, triangular and continuous with the back contour instead of translucent circular blobs.

rows.readsAs: a purple pigeon — indistinguishable from the Macaw entry in this batch
rows.defect: This is the identical render to the Macaw in this same batch — same body, same teardrop wing plate with its hard outline, same yellow feet, same tiny yellow triangular beak, same two thin tail rods — only recoloured purple. Consequently every mustRead fails: no black-and-white pied blocks (it is uniform purple), no heavy straight crow bill (the beak is a small yellow cone a fifth of the head), and no graduated wedge tail (two straight thin rods projecting horizontally with a seam at the rump, not a broad wedge of stepped feathers). Aspect is roughly 1.4 wide against the specified 2.6. The wing plate again reads as a decal laid on the flank.
rows.fix: Differentiate it from the Macaw base entirely. Give it a heavy straight black crow bill roughly the depth of the head. Rebuild the tail as a single broad graduated wedge, longer than the body, made of stepped overlapping feathers rooted inside the rump silhouette, with the iridescent green-blue sheen. Repaint the plumage as hard-edged pied blocks: black head/breast/back, clean white scapular patch and belly. Replace the wing decal with folded primaries reading as feather groups.

rows.readsAs: a goldfish or a small orange piranha
rows.defect: The blunt vertical forehead is missing — the head is a smoothly rounded nose that curves gently into the back, exactly the opposite of the mahi's sheer forehead wall. The dorsal fin does not run from behind the eye to the tail: there is a dark brown patch on the upper back that starts near mid-body, stops well short of the peduncle, and above it a spray of fine loose hair-like rays that project past the body outline into empty space near the head — a floating off-body artifact. The body is a deep symmetric leaf/discus, widest at the middle and tapering equally at both ends, so it does not 'taper hard to the rear'; measured aspect is about 1.7 against a specified 3.4. The forked tail is a flat brown triangle joined to the body by a thin stalk with a visible hard seam.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head profile with a near-vertical blunt forehead rising straight off the mouth. Run the dorsal fin as one continuous ribbon from just behind the eye all the way to the peduncle, rooted into the back contour with no gap and no rays escaping the silhouette. Stretch the body to aspect 3.4 and shift the mass forward so it tapers hard to a slim rear. Merge the tail into the peduncle so the fork grows out of the narrowing body. Add the electric blue-green dorsal wash with gold flank speckling.

rows.readsAs: a barracuda or a small golden tuna
rows.defect: This does not read as a shark.
