The body is a gold/yellow spindle with a fine dark dorsal edge — no metallic indigo-blue back, and the eye is a small white bead with a black dot, not the large black eye specified. The tail is a swept-back two-lobed fork with a longer lower sweep, not a nearly symmetric crescent, and there is no keel on the stalk. The dorsal fin is a rounded brown hump sitting on the back with a clear hard seam line where its base meets the body outline. There are two sets of short dark tick marks near the head, and the lower diagonal row projects past the snout outline into empty background — off-body strokes floating in the water. The snout is pointed but shallow, and there is no mouth or gill structure beyond those ticks.
rows.fix: Repaint as metallic indigo-blue back with a hard countershading break to a white belly. Enlarge the eye to a big black orb. Replace the fork with a lunate crescent tail of near-equal lobes on a keeled, laterally flattened peduncle. Reshape the dorsal into a tall triangular fin whose base blends into the back with no seam stroke, and add matching pectorals. Clip the gill strokes inside the body silhouette and render five clean gill slits on the flank rather than loose ticks.

rows.readsAs: a purple ribbed hose or a giant earthworm coiled in a ring
rows.defect: The coil is a geometrically perfect flat torus — an almost exact circle with a clean circular hole in the middle and constant tube thickness all the way round, so the silhouette is a machined donut rather than a snake's overlapping loops. The skin is covered in tight, evenly spaced transverse ribs running the whole length, which reads as a corrugated vacuum hose or an earthworm's annuli, directly contradicting the mustRead 'smooth uniform scales'. There is no coffin-shaped head: the head is a small bulb barely wider than the neck with one eye and no jawline, and no fixed grin mouthline is drawn. The body never tapers to a whip tail — the tube keeps its diameter and simply tucks under itself. It is not rearing.
rows.fix: Break the perfect ring: overlap the loops at different heights so one coil crosses in front of another, vary the tube diameter, and taper the last third to a fine whip tip. Replace the corrugated ribbing with fine overlapping diamond scales that follow the body's curvature and catch light along the spine. Rebuild the head as a narrow elongate coffin wedge, distinctly wider than the neck at the jaw hinge, with the long straight grin mouthline running back past the eye. Raise the front third off the coil.

rows.readsAs: a teal earthworm or caterpillar
rows.defect: Not a lancelet at all — it is an opaque teal tube coiled in an S-arch, built from ~20 overlapping ring/scallop plates, with a single black dot eye near the left tip. Every mustRead fails: the body is not translucent and not blade-shaped-pointed-at-both-ends (the left end is a blunt rounded knob, the right end a rounded taper); there are no V-shaped muscle chevrons (the segmentation is transverse rings, i.e. earthworm annuli, running perpendicular to the axis instead of nested Vs); there is no oral tentacle fringe anywhere; and the reference says eyes hidden but a black eyespot is painted on. No notochord line. The rings are stamped overlapping discs with hard outer edges — machined repetition, not skin.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a flat translucent lanceolate blade: single tapered lens silhouette pointed at BOTH ends, low-alpha body fill so the interior reads see-through. Replace the transverse ring stack with ~40 nested chevrons whose apex points forward (myomeres), drawn as soft interior shading not outline strokes. Add a dark notochord line running tip-to-tip at mid-height, a pale gut streak below it, and a short radial fringe of 8-12 fine cirri at the mouth end. Delete the eyespot entirely (eyes: hidden). Straighten the pose — a shallow single swim-wave, not a two-lobe worm arch.

rows.readsAs: a dark salamander or a small grey monitor lizard — not a Galápagos land iguana
rows.defect: The whole animal is desaturated grey-blue, near-black, against a near-black field — barely legible. The mustRead 'heavy jowly yellow-orange head' is absent twice over: it is not yellow-orange (it is a pale bone-white/light-grey ellipse) and it is not jowly (a smooth flat oval with no cheek mass or jaw line). Worse, that pale ellipse is a hard-edged separate shape butted against the dark body — a clean seam at the neck where the value jumps from near-black to near-white with no blend, the classic head-stuck-on defect. The tail is a straight machined taper with an abrupt dark band across it, another hard seam rather than a colour that grows out of the body. Legs are four stubby flat stumps with no visible claws or knee/elbow articulation. The dorsal spines are a row of identical thin triangles sitting on the back outline rather than emerging from the nape ridge. Body spotting is a scatter of soft dark blobs sprayed over the flank with no relation to scale rows.
rows.fix: Recolour the whole animal to the reference yellow-orange (warm ochre dorsum, brighter rust on the head) and raise overall value ~40% so it reads on the dark plate. Merge head into body: widen the skull into heavy cheek jowls, add a dewlap sagging under the jaw, and blend the head-to-neck value over 15-20px instead of a hard boundary. Vary the crest spines in height (tall at the nape, shrinking down the back) and root each one in a continuous nape ridge that is part of the back silhouette. Thicken the tail base into the pelvis and give it a round taper with lateral spine rows; drop the banded segment. Rebuild legs as stout bent limbs with visible upper/lower segments and 5 splayed claws.

rows.readsAs: an ammonite fossil or a cinnamon roll
rows.defect: The shell is planispiral — a flat coil wound in one plane, seen face-on, like an ammonite or a cinnamon bun. A land snail shell is HELICAL (conical, spire offset to one side); this one has no spire and no apex axis. It is also drawn as a near-perfect circle with concentric ridge arcs of machine-even spacing, plus a hard aperture line that reads as an inscribed circle on top of the disc. The mustRead 'two pairs of tentacles, upper pair tipped with eyes' fails: at the right there is only a tiny yellow spray of 3-4 short straight spikes, no long upper stalks, no eye beads at their tips, no distinct lower pair. The 'muscular gliding foot with a rippling sole' is a thin flat orange lozenge peeking under the shell with a straight bottom edge and zero sole ripple, and the head/foot mass is almost entirely hidden behind the shell. The shell dominates ~80% of the figure so the animal is missing.
rows.fix: Rebuild the shell as a helicoid: 4-5 whorls decreasing in diameter toward an off-centre apex, aperture opening low-right toward the head, growth lines running across the whorls rather than concentric circles, and the whorl suture as a curved groove not an inscribed ring. Shrink shell to ~55% of figure. Grow the foot out to the right and forward — a long muscular sole with a wavy lower margin and transverse pedal ripples, its front lifted into a head. Give the head two LONG upper tentacles arcing up and forward with a dark eye bead at each tip, and two SHORTER lower feeler tentacles below. Blend the mantle collar into the shell aperture so the body emerges from it instead of the shell sitting on a flat slab.

rows.readsAs: a young orangutan or a generic plush monkey
rows.defect: Squat, front-facing, golden-yellow ape with a pear-shaped smooth torso and short dark stumpy limbs — reads as an orangutan or a plush toy, not a langur. mustReads fail: (a) 'tail far longer than the body' — the tail is roughly 0.7 body lengths, a thin brown crescent curling up beside the left hip, and it meets the hip at a hard join with a visible seam where a dark line abuts the yellow torso; (b) 'black face and hands framed by pale grey fur' — the fur is saturated orange-gold, not pale grey, and the face is a mid-brown mask with no black; the hands are indistinguishable dark blobs; (c) 'slender long-limbed build' — the build is the opposite: broad heavy torso, arms barely longer than the torso is wide, legs reduced to two dark rounded lobes tucked under. The reference posture is quadruped; the render is a squared-on seated pose. The torso is a smooth gradient egg with soft brown patches sprayed on it in no anatomical pattern, and the limbs read as separate dark shapes overlaid on that egg rather than muscle continuing out of the shoulder and hip.
rows.fix: Change palette to pale silver-grey body fur with a jet-black face, hands and feet. Turn the figure to a three-quarter/side quadruped stance on all fours. Rebuild the tail at 1.5-1.8x body length, thick at the base where it must taper out of the pelvis (no dark line at the join) and whipping up in a long S. Lengthen all four limbs to langur proportion (arms and legs both clearly longer than torso depth), with visible shoulder, elbow, hip and knee, and slim them down. Narrow the torso — a lean chest and tucked belly, not a pear. Add the crown crest as a raised tuft of fur breaking the head outline, and a pale fur ruff framing the black face.

rows.readsAs: a generic purple minnow strung with fairy lights
rows.defect: The one thing that works is the photophore row, but it works too mechanically: 14 identical perfect circles of the same diameter, same glow, evenly spaced in a straight line along the ventral edge — a string of LED beads laid on the fish rather than organs in its skin. Two mustReads fail: the eye is small (a tiny white ring roughly 1/10 of head height) where the reference demands 'oversized eyes', and the snout is pointed/wedge-shaped rather than blunt and short. No adipose fin is present between dorsal and tail. The body is a smooth symmetrical almond/lens with the dorsal and anal fins as thin flat triangles butted onto the outline; the tail is a small dark triangle that reads notched rather than clearly forked. The purple flank gradient is a soft airbrush with no scale texture. Overall the figure occupies only ~30% of the frame, so it also reads undersized.
rows.fix: Enlarge the eye to 25-30% of head height — a dark pupil with a silvery reflective ring — and blunt the snout so the head front is near-vertical with a steep upturned mouth. Break the photophore row: vary diameter, cluster them in species-typical groups with gaps, run a second short row up onto the flank behind the pectoral, and sink each one into a slight skin depression with a rim so it reads as an organ. Add a small fleshy adipose fin on the dorsal midline just ahead of the caudal peduncle. Deepen the caudal fork into two clear lobes with a concave notch. Add loose deciduous scale texture and a silvery ventral counter-shade so the belly is not the same purple as the back. Scale the whole fish up ~35% in frame.

rows.readsAs: a duckling or a canary chick
rows.defect: A small plump uniformly golden-orange bird with a smooth gradient body and no markings — it reads as a duckling or a canary. All three mustReads are missing: (a) no streaky brown ground-bird plumage — the body is one flat warm gradient with a single darker teardrop outline for the folded wing and no streaking, spotting or feather breakup anywhere; (b) no peaked crest at the back of the crown — the head is a perfectly smooth dome; (c) no long straight hind claw — the feet are two thin yellow scratch-lines with three forward toes and nothing behind. The wing is an inset teardrop drawn as an outline on the flank, a decal rather than folded primaries; the tail is a single flat dark wedge stuck to the rear at a hard angle. The proportion is also wrong for the note's 'horizontal, long-bodied songbird': this is a round, near-1:1 upright ball. The whole figure is tiny in frame (~20% of the plate) so none of the detail has room to exist.
rows.fix: Recolour to buff-brown with dense dark streaking on the crown, nape, breast and back — irregular vertical dashes, not a uniform fill — and a pale unstreaked belly. Raise a short peaked crest at the rear crown so it breaks the head silhouette. Rebuild the foot with a long straight backward-pointing hind claw as long as the toe. Lengthen and lower the body to a horizontal ground-bird posture (aspect ~1.6 as specified), with a slimmer neck and a short conical bill. Replace the wing decal with layered scapular/covert/primary groups whose tips overlap the tail base. Enlarge the whole bird to fill ~55% of the frame.

rows.readsAs: a pink bead-toy ant or a termite
rows.defect: Three near-perfect pink spheres in a row on stick legs. The defining mustRead — 'spined thorax carrying a leaf fragment overhead' — is entirely absent: there is no leaf, no mandible grip, nothing above the ant, which removes the only feature that makes this species readable. The thorax has no spines at all, just a smooth ball. 'Pinched narrow waist' fails: the spheres simply abut, with no petiole node and no constriction between thorax and gaster. The antennae are two straight rigid lines radiating from the head with no elbow bend. The head is the SMALLEST of the three segments, the exact inverse of the note's 'head is oversized with big cutting jaws' — and there are no jaws/mandibles at all, only a single glossy black dot eye. Legs are four straight hairline strokes with no femur/tibia joint, no tarsi, and they poke out of the sphere edges at hard tangent points rather than growing from thoracic sockets. Silhouette is pure geometric primitives.
rows.fix: Add the leaf: a large cut leaf fragment held above and forward, gripped in the mandibles, tilted like a sail, with visible venation and a scalloped cut edge — it should be roughly as wide as the ant's body length. Enlarge the head to the biggest segment and arm it with a pair of curved serrated mandibles. Deform the thorax off-sphere into an angular alitrunk carrying 2-3 pairs of backward-pointing spines. Insert a two-node petiole so the waist visibly pinches to ~20% of gaster width. Elbow the antennae: a long straight scape from the head, then a sharp bend into a segmented funiculus. Rebuild all six legs with coxa/femur/tibia/tarsus segments, joint bends, and tapering thickness, socketed into the thorax underside. Add cuticle texture and setae so the surface is not a plain gradient sphere.

rows.readsAs: a dark grey earthworm, and specifically the same creature as this batch's Lancelet in another colour
rows.defect: Almost invisible: the animal is a near-black grey (value only a few steps above the near-black plate) so the silhouette barely separates from the background. Content problems: only ONE sucker reads — a small dark cap at the left/anterior tip — while the posterior end simply tapers to a fine point with no caudal sucker at all, failing the 'sucker at each end' mustRead. The body is a round tube, not a flattened ribbon; there is no dorso-ventral flattening or lateral margin. The ring segmentation is a stack of ~25 identical overlapping discs with hard outer edges — machined repetition, and far too coarse for 'fine ring segments' (a leech has many annuli per segment). Critically, this is the SAME morphology and the SAME pose as Lancelet in this batch: identical S-arch, identical disc-stack ring treatment, identical blunt-left/tapered-right terminals — only the hue differs. Two different phyla are sharing one asset.
rows.fix: Raise the value substantially (mid olive-brown or grey-green) so it reads on the dark plate. Flatten the body: widen it dorso-ventrally into a ribbon with a visible thin lateral margin, and let the width swell mid-body and narrow at both ends. Add a distinct posterior sucker — a broad flat disc clearly wider than the tail it attaches to — and enlarge the anterior sucker into an oral cup at a downturned head. Replace the 25 coarse discs with 60+ fine annuli drawn as soft surface shading, not stamped outlines, and let them compress on the inside of the arch and stretch on the outside so the segmentation responds to the pose. Change the pose to a true inchworm loop — both suckers planted on the ground with a high tented arch between them — so it stops sharing Lancelet's swim-wave silhouette.

rows.readsAs: a grey caterpillar-banded tadpole, or a dugong at best
rows.defect: No front flippers read at all — the only thing on the flank is a small pale capsule-shaped smudge that looks like a scar or a sticker, not a limb, so the mustRead 'barrel body with front flippers' fails. The body is a smooth grey ellipse wrapped in ~8 evenly-spaced transverse ring lines that read as insect/caterpillar segmentation sprayed over the surface, not manatee skin. The tail is a fan with radiating spoke lines like a bony fish caudal fin rather than a fleshy rounded spatula paddle, and it meets the body at a pinched waist with a hard visible seam where the fan overlaps the ellipse. The muzzle is a plain rounded lump — no split upper lip, no downturned bristly pad; there are only a few stray hair strands.
rows.fix: Delete the transverse ring banding entirely and replace with sparse wrinkle folds concentrated at the neck/shoulder only. Grow two paddle flippers out of the forward third of the body as continuous lobes sharing the body fill (no separate shape, no outline), angled down and back. Rebuild the tail as a single wide spatula that widens continuously out of the peduncle — kill the radiating spoke lines and the waist seam. Add a blunt downturned muzzle mass with a vertical cleft in the upper lip and a dense whisker field, not 3 stray hairs.

rows.readsAs: a blue cartoon langur or a blue-painted gibbon with a wig
rows.defect: Three mustReads fail. (1) The tail is a long thick curling S-tail sweeping out to the left, longer than the torso — the reference explicitly says tiny stub tail held upright. (2) No scarlet nose stripe and no ridged blue cheek flanges: the face is a tiny flat pale-mauve heart-shaped muzzle with no ridging, no red, no paranasal ridges. (3) No olive mane over hunched shoulders — instead there is a fluffy white/grey afro halo ringing the head like a cotton-ball wig. The whole animal is uniform electric blue including the torso, arms and legs. Construction is stuck-on: the arms and legs are separate dark navy capsules laid over a lighter blue torso with hard overlap edges, the head is a separate lighter blue oval sitting on the torso with no neck integration, and the torso has cloudy pale blotches that look like airbrush overspray.
rows.fix: Cut the tail to a 10-15px upright stub. Recolour: body olive-brown/agouti, restrict blue to the two cheek pads with 4-6 carved parallel ridges each, and paint a saturated scarlet stripe down the nose bridge into a red nose pad. Replace the white afro with a longer olive mane flowing from the crown over the shoulders. Extend the muzzle forward into a deep dog-like snout instead of a flat face. Merge the limbs into the torso silhouette with the same fill and shared shading so no capsule edges show.

rows.readsAs: a blue mushroom cap or a jellyfish bell
rows.defect: The silhouette is a smooth semicircular dome — a mushroom cap or jellyfish bell — with NO wings at all. There are no triangular pointed wingtips; the outline curves continuously and the lower-right edge is a perfectly straight machined line that cuts the dome off flat. Both cephalic lobes are missing and there is no mouth of any kind. Two eyes sit on TOP of the dome facing the viewer like googly eyes rather than at the outer corners of the head. The tail is a thin uniform-width curved wire attached under the centre of the dome with a visible junction. The pale round blobs scattered on the surface read as sprayed-on bubbles, not manta spot pattern.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette from scratch: a wide shallow diamond, wingspan clearly wider than body length, with each wing sweeping back to a sharp point and a concave trailing edge. Remove the straight cut edge. Add two forward-projecting horn lobes flanking a wide rectangular terminal mouth at the leading edge of the head. Move the eyes to the outer sides of the head between lobe and wing. Taper the tail from a thick base out of the body mass to a whip point.

rows.readsAs: a red fire ant
rows.defect: This is built as three stacked spheres — a small round head ball, a round thorax ball, a larger round abdomen ball — which is ant anatomy, not mantis. No triangular head: the head is a circle with one oversized black bead eye. No long slender prothorax raising the front of the body; the front is the same height as everything else, and there is no neck, which the note calls the one thing only a mantis has. The raptorial forelegs are a single thin bent red hairline V floating near the head — no thickness, no spines, no folded prayer posture, and it does not visibly connect to the thorax. All the legs are 1px straight lines with no taper, no joints and no visible attachment sockets. Posture is horizontal, not upright.
rows.fix: Replace the three-ball body with a mantis plan: triangular wedge head with two eyes at the outer corners, a narrow tubular prothorax at least 1.5x the head length raising the front of the body, then a slender tapered abdomen. Draw the forelegs as thick two-segment claws with a row of spines on the inner edge, folded closed under the head. Give the four walking legs taper and femur/tibia joints and root them in the thorax with a widening base. Tilt the whole body to a raised-front upright stance.

rows.readsAs: a pink rabbit
rows.defect: This is a squat pink rabbit — exactly the shape the note says not to draw. The legs fail the primary mustRead: the visible limbs are two short stubby pegs under a heavy hunched hindquarter, roughly 1/6 of body height, nothing like long slim deer-like legs; the animal sits low with its belly near the ground. The hind leg is a hard dark crescent laid onto the flank with a clean seam line where it overlaps the body fill — a part stuck on, not growing out. The ears are correct (tall) but they are a separate darker pink shape planted on the skull with a visible overlap edge rather than emerging from it. The nose is a literal white rectangle with a grid of ruled lines in it — a machined primitive on the face. The body is a plain gradient balloon with no fur texture.
rows.fix: Raise the body on four long slim legs — each at least 40% of body height, with a clearly defined thigh, a narrow cannon and a small hoof-like foot — and lift the belly line well clear of the ground. Slim the hindquarter so it is not a rabbit's crouch. Remove the crescent leg decal and let the thigh mass emerge from the flank with continuous shading. Delete the white rectangle nose and replace with a small dark tapered nose pad. Add a short agouti fur break-up and a white rump patch to pull it away from bunny.

rows.readsAs: a generic purple lizard or a small salamander
rows.defect: The snout fails the mustRead: it is a smooth rounded ovoid bulb, not a blunt square salt-crusted face, and there is no salt crust anywhere. The tail is a round-section tube of near-constant thickness for most of its length — not laterally flattened or paddle-like — and it carries a dark purple stripe painted down the inside that reads as a decal floating inside the tail rather than shading. The body is bright lavender-purple rather than dark sooty. The dark spots are uniform soft ellipses scattered over the back like airbrush overspray. The head is a separate ellipse overlapping the body with a visible arc seam at the neck, and the four legs are plain untapered cylinders that butt into the underside with no shoulder or hip mass and no visible claws. The dorsal spines are correct in placement but are identical straight-sided black triangles in a regular row, machine-repeated.
rows.fix: Square off the snout into a short blunt box with a flat rostral face and add pale crusted salt speckle around the nostrils. Flatten the tail vertically — deepen it top-to-bottom, thin it side-to-side, and taper it continuously from a thick base; remove the internal stripe decal. Recolour the body dark sooty grey-black with only a hint of rust. Blend the head into the neck so no seam shows. Give the legs shoulder and hip mass where they meet the body, taper them, and add long curved claws. Vary spine height and lean so the crest is not a repeated stamp.

rows.readsAs: a pink centipede or a bristly caterpillar
rows.defect: The parapodia mustRead is only half met — the fringe exists on both sides but each bristle is a perfectly straight uniform-width red pin of near-identical length, planted in a regular picket-fence rhythm, so it reads as spines skewered through the body rather than fleshy lobes growing out of the segments; many pins visibly start inside the body and poke out both faces. The head mustRead fully fails: the front end is a smooth featureless bulb with one black dot and no tentacles and no palps at all. The segments are drawn as a stack of discrete overlapping discs with hard leading edges, which gives it a millipede/centipede exoskeletal read rather than an iridescent soft body — and there is no iridescence, just a flat pink-mauve gradient.
rows.fix: Replace the straight pins with short fleshy paddle-shaped parapodia that share the body fill, widen at the base where they meet each segment, and carry a small tuft of finer bristles at the tip; vary length so the fringe is not uniform. Terminate the pins at the body edge, never through it. Build a tapering head with 2 long antennae, a pair of palps and 4 short peristomial tentacles. Soften the disc edges so segments read as annuli in one continuous skin, and add a green/blue iridescent sheen along the dorsal midline.

rows.readsAs: a marlin or a swordfish — the one image in this batch a stranger would name correctly
rows.defect: Best of the batch — the spear bill, lens-shaped body and forked tail all read correctly — but the cobalt vertical bars mustRead is entirely missing: the flank is a plain smooth light-purple gradient with no bars of any kind. The dorsal fin is the other problem: it is a dark near-black crescent that sits above the back as a separate flat shape with a hard boundary line against the body and a straight upper edge, so it reads as a sail pasted on rather than growing out of the back. Same for the pectoral, which is a small dark triangle decal sitting flat on the flank with no base and no thickness. The eye is a perfect white ring circle — a geometric primitive bead rather than an eye set in an orbit.
rows.fix: Paint 12-15 soft cobalt vertical bars down the flank, brightest dorsally and fading toward the belly, following the body curve. Rebuild the dorsal so its base blends into the back fill over several pixels with no hard line, make the leading edge tall and sharply pointed then drop away, and give the membrane fin-ray striation instead of a flat black fill. Root the pectoral in a small shoulder pocket and angle it off the body so it has a base. Replace the ring eye with a dark pupil in a shaded orbit set into the head.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon duckling or fledgling songbird
rows.defect: The two headline mustReads are inverted. The head is SMALL (roughly 0.22 of body, not 0.4) and sits on a clearly pinched neck — you can trace the concave notch between the head ball and the body ball. The orange bill is a short stubby cone, maybe 0.8 head-lengths, nowhere near a disproportionately long straight dagger. The tail is a hard-edged dark wedge pasted onto the rear right with a clean straight boundary line where it meets the body, and the wing is a flat lighter ellipse with a crisp outline stamped on the flank rather than a feather mass growing from the shoulder. Body is a two-circle snowman: small head sphere + big body sphere, with a tiny crest tuft glued on top. The whole creature occupies only about a third of the 440 frame, so all the detail is undersized. It is also built from the same template as the Kookaburra in this batch — identical body oval, identical wing ellipse, identical tail wedge, identical yellow stick legs — only the hue differs.
rows.fix: Scale the head up to ~0.4 of the body height and delete the neck constriction so the skull merges straight into the shoulders in one continuous contour. Rebuild the bill at 1.5-2x head length, straight, with parallel-ish edges tapering to a sharp point (kingfisher is nearly all bill). Replace the pasted tail wedge with a short tail that emerges from the body outline itself — sample the body colour at the join and feather the boundary. Kill the outlined wing ellipse; use a soft coverts shading pass with no stroke. Give it a distinct silhouette from the Kookaburra rather than a palette swap, and increase render scale to fill the frame.

rows.readsAs: a kiwi — correctly and immediately
rows.defect: Best render in the batch — the round tailless body of scribbled hair-like feathers and the very long slender decurved bill with a dark nostril dot at the tip both land, and the wings are correctly invisible. Two real problems. First, the head is an obviously separate smooth green sphere overlapping the shaggy body, with a visible arc seam where the clean sphere edge cuts across the hair strokes; the hair simply stops at that arc instead of carrying up over the skull. Second, the legs are set at roughly 45% and 60% of the body length — mid-body, almost under the centre of mass — where a kiwi's stout legs sit well back in the rear third. They are also smooth flat tan tubes that terminate in a hard horizontal line against the body underside with no fur overlapping them.
rows.fix: Continue the hair-stroke pass up and across the head so the same scribble texture crosses the head/body boundary and the seam disappears; keep the head slightly smaller and let it merge, not overlap. Shift both leg roots back to roughly 60-75% of body length so the bird has the correct rear-slung tripod stance, and overlay a few fur strokes across the top of each leg root so the plumage hangs over the thigh instead of ending in a straight cut.

rows.readsAs: a generic minnow or an anchovy — or with the flat capsule shape, a green torpedo
rows.defect: All three mustReads fail. There is no ribbon fin anywhere along the underside — just a thin uniform outline stroke around the whole body, the same weight top and bottom. The body does not taper to a blade-thin point; it ends in a blunt rounded stub with a small wispy black tuft stuck on the end, and there is a visible gap/seam between that tuft and the body. The silhouette is a plain capsule — parallel top and bottom edges with hemispherical caps, exactly the rounded-capsule shape flagged as a defect. Rendered aspect is roughly 4.5:1 against the specified 6. Surface is a flat mint-green gradient with no scale or muscle information, the eye is a perfect small circle with a white dot, the mouth is a single drawn arc line, and the one pectoral fin is a small hatched triangle sitting on top of the flank rather than emerging from a fin base.
rows.fix: Add the defining feature: a long anal/ribbon fin running the full length of the underside as a rippling sinusoidal membrane with visible fin-ray striations, its base blending into the belly. Reshape the body so the dorsal line arches over the head and the posterior tapers continuously to an actual blade point — no terminal tuft, no capsule caps. Push aspect to 6. Break up the flat gradient with body banding or a subtle scale pass, and root the pectoral fin in a shaded socket.

rows.readsAs: a guinea pig, a marmot, or a tortoise that lost its shell
rows.defect: This does not read as a monitor lizard at all. The body is a fat spotted egg with the long axis nearly vertical, and the head is a second smaller egg overlapping it on the right with a plain visible seam where the two ovals cross — no neck, no loose scaly neck skin, just two shapes intersecting. The tail is a smooth uniform-width banana stroke that curves UPWARD off the rear, joined at an abrupt hard boundary and with an inner darker banana shape nested inside it that reads as a painted highlight, not anatomy; it is also a smooth tapering tube with no lateral compression or scale keel. The four limbs are short brown rounded blobs hanging straight DOWN under the belly — the exact opposite of heavy limbs splayed out sideways — and each meets the body at a hard edge. No forked yellow tongue anywhere; the mouth is a single flat horizontal line. The spots are flat dark ellipses of uniform opacity sprayed over the top of the body gradient, ignoring its form.
rows.fix: Rebuild on a horizontal axis: long low body, aspect 3.2, tail carried level and making up half the total length, thick at the base and tapering with a visible keel. Splay the limbs — elbows and knees out to the sides, feet planted wide of the body outline, with clawed toes, and grow each limb from a shaded shoulder/hip mass rather than butting it against the belly. Add the forked yellow tongue flicking from the mouth (it is the single most identifying feature) and give the neck loose hanging skin folds that connect head to shoulders continuously. Convert the sprayed spots to an osteoderm/pebbled-scale pass that follows the body curvature and fades over the shaded flank.

rows.readsAs: a generic red cartoon robin or cardinal — a recoloured copy of the Kingfisher in this same batch
rows.defect: Two mustReads are simply absent: there is no dark brown eye stripe and no whitish head — the entire bird is one flat crimson, head included, so the most diagnostic marking on a kookaburra is missing. The posture is a standing biped on two yellow legs, not flying as specified. The head is not oversized (about 0.24 of the body against the 0.34 spec) and the yellow bill, while decently dagger-shaped, is short of the huge bill the reference calls for. Construction faults: the wing is a hard-outlined lighter ellipse stamped flat onto the flank, and the tail is a dark maroon wedge butted onto the rear with a clean straight seam. It is the same base template as the Kingfisher in this batch — same body oval, same wing ellipse, same tail wedge, same leg pair — so the two birds are indistinguishable except for hue.
rows.fix: Paint the head and throat off-white/cream, then add the broad dark brown band running back through the eye — that pair of marks alone will make it read. Enlarge the head to 0.34 and lengthen the bill to roughly 1.5 head-lengths, heavy and slightly hooked. Either render it flying with spread wings per the posture spec or correct the reference row to biped. Replace the outlined wing ellipse with a shaded wing that has visible primaries, and grow the tail out of the rump with a feathered join instead of a butted wedge. Differentiate the silhouette from the Kingfisher: kookaburra is bulkier and squarer-headed.

rows.readsAs: a small opaque shrimp, or at this size just an orange insect
rows.defect: Rendered far too small — the animal occupies maybe a fifth of the 440 frame with a large empty margin, so almost nothing is legible. Of the three mustReads, only the leg fan partly lands: there is a row of small pale appendages under the abdomen. The body is fully opaque flat orange with no translucency at all, and there are no feathery external gills anywhere — that is the feature that distinguishes krill from any shrimp and it is missing. The eyes are not stalked: a single dark bead with a white glint sits flush in the head, no eyestalk. Structurally the head/carapace and the abdomen read as two separate overlapping blobs with a visible seam between them, and the abdomen is angled upward off the head rather than continuing the body line, so the animal looks kinked/broken. The abdomen also just ends — no tail fan, no telson or uropods. The two long antennae are bare uniform-width brown lines with no taper.
rows.fix: Scale the render up to fill the frame. Make the carapace genuinely translucent — a lower-alpha shell over a darker visible gut line — and hang the branched feathery gills outside and below the carapace where they belong. Put the black eyes on visible short stalks projecting from the head. Realign the abdomen so it continues the head's axis as one flexed body, resolving the seam into a continuous chain of overlapping segment plates. Terminate the tail in a proper fan of uropods. Taper the antennae.

rows.readsAs: a ladybug — recognisable, but with the legs visibly floating loose beside it
rows.defect: Top-down view, and the shell/spot/split-line read is fine — but the legs are detached. All six grey leg arcs float clear of the body with a visible dark gap between each leg's inner end and the elytra edge; nothing connects them to the animal. That is an off-body artifact and it is the first thing the eye catches. They are also thin uniform grey arcs with no joints, no femur/tibia articulation, and they are drawn in a desaturated grey that belongs to no other part of the creature. Secondary problems: the head is a separate mushroom-shaped blob sitting above the pronotum with a hard seam between the two, and it protrudes clear of the shield rather than tucking under it as the reference requires. The spots are flat perfect circles at uniform opacity sprayed over the shell gradient, ignoring the dome's curvature — they do not compress toward the rim as they would on a real hemisphere. No antennae. The dome also reads as a flat oval rather than a strongly domed hemisphere; the highlight is a broad soft wash with no specular pop at the crown.
rows.fix: Anchor every leg root inside the body outline, under the elytra rim, and add a coxa/femur/tibia bend so they are jointed limbs rather than arcs. Recolour them to a dark body-consistent tone. Slide the head back so it is partly hidden under the pronotal shield and merge the two shapes into one continuous front mass — no seam. Project the spots onto the dome so those near the edge foreshorten into ellipses. Add a tight specular highlight near the top of the shell to sell the hemisphere, and add short clubbed antennae.

rows.readsAs: a lamprey, or to a non-specialist an eel with a suction cup on its face
rows.defect: The strongest read after the Kiwi — sucker mouth, gill pores and finless eel body are all present — but the head is built wrong. The oral disc is a geometrically perfect circle attached to the body by a narrow pinched stalk, with a hard boundary at the junction, so it reads as a plunger or a lollipop stuck onto the end of the ribbon rather than the head flaring open into a funnel. The teeth inside are concentric rings of identical small dots, machine-regular. The seven gill pores are equally perfect, identical, evenly spaced circles on a dead-straight line — sprayed on, not set into the skin with any shading or spacing variation. The posterior end is cut off by a straight flat vertical edge (a machined edge, not an anatomical one) and there is no tail fin fold at all. The body itself is a flat two-tone purple ribbon with a uniform darker stripe along the top; it has no roundness, no myomere segmentation, no thickness cue where it curves.
rows.fix: Reshape the disc into an oval funnel that flares continuously out of the head — widen the neck and blend the join so there is no stalk and no seam — and vary tooth size, largest near the centre. Vary the gill pore diameters and spacing slightly, and give each one a shadowed rim so it sits in the skin. Taper the posterior into a low continuous caudal fin fold instead of the flat cut. Add subtle myomere banding and a rounded value falloff across the body so it reads as a cylinder rather than a flat ribbon.

rows.readsAs: A jellyfish — the one silhouette in this batch that names itself correctly, but a diagram of a jellyfish rather than an animal.
rows.defect: The bell is a mathematically perfect hemisphere whose bottom edge is a dead-straight horizontal rule — a machined chord, not a subumbrellar margin. Every tentacle is a uniform 1-2px hairline of identical width and identical teal, and they all terminate abruptly ON that straight line, producing exactly the hard seam the brief calls a blocker. The mustRead 'frilled oral arms under the centre of the bell' is entirely absent — there is nothing under the centre of the bell at all, only rim tentacles. 'Translucent' also fails: the bell is opaque flat teal with a single soft airbrush hotspot near the apex, no sense of seeing water or the oral mass through it. The organism also occupies only about a third of the 440px frame, floating small and lonely.
rows.fix: Replace the semicircle with an ellipse whose lower margin scallops (8-12 lappets) so the rim is wavy, not a chord; drop the tentacle origins slightly INSIDE the bell so they emerge from under the margin rather than butting against a line. Vary tentacle thickness, length and opacity per strand and let 2-3 be thick oral arms with a ruffled, ribbon-like edge hanging from the centre. Composite the bell at ~0.55 alpha with a brighter rim-light ring so the tentacle roots read faintly through the dome, and scale the whole animal up ~1.5x in frame.

rows.readsAs: A pink cartoon bunny or a Pokemon-style mouse. Nobody would say jerboa.
rows.defect: This is a quadruped standing on four stubby nubs. The mustRead 'stilt-like hind legs several times the front legs' is flatly absent — the visible hind limb is a short pink stub the same length as the front one, and the posture is not bipedal. The tail is a thin curved tube shorter than the body with NO tuft of any kind, black-and-white or otherwise, failing the second mustRead. The ears are tall pink rabbit ears, not a jerboa's rounded ones, and both meet the skull as flat teardrops laid on top with a visible hard outline. The body is a single smooth pink egg with a soft airbrush shadow standing in for a haunch; the tail springs from a point on that egg with a hard join. Whiskers are three straight white rulers of equal length radiating from a small white square muzzle.
rows.fix: Rebuild the pose: torso pitched forward over ONE pair of long hind limbs with a clear femur-tibia-metatarsal chain roughly 2.5-3x the forelimb, feet elongated and flat on the ground, forelimbs shrunk to tucked nubs at the chest. Extend the tail to ~1.4x body length, thin along its run, and terminate it in a painted black band followed by a white brush tuft. Grow the haunch out of the torso as a continuous swelling rather than an internal shadow ellipse, shorten and round the ears, and give the whiskers per-strand curvature and length jitter.

rows.readsAs: A mackerel or small tuna. In this same batch it is a colour-swap sibling of the Killifish — same lens body, same construction.
rows.defect: The caudal fin is a symmetrical forked tuna tail — two equal lobes above and below the axis. The mustRead 'asymmetric tail with a long upper lobe' is not merely weak, it is the wrong tail. The five gill slits ARE present as short dark dashes behind the head, which is the one thing that works. The dorsal is a soft rounded blob rather than a stiff triangle, and I can find no stiff pectoral wing — only a faint dark smudge low on the flank. The body outline is a lens: the dorsal and ventral contours are near-straight lines converging to sharp points fore and aft, with a hard straight lateral line ruled down the middle of the flank like a panel gap. No ventral mouth, no snout overhang — the head just tapers to a point with a small ring eye stuck near the tip.
rows.fix: Replace the caudal with a heterocercal fin: upper lobe roughly twice the lower, upswept, with the body axis visibly bending up into it. Add a real triangular first dorsal with a straight trailing edge and a swept apex, plus horizontally-held pectoral wings with a broad root that blends into the flank. Curve the ventral contour into a belly rather than a straight line, undercut the snout so the mouth sits below and behind the tip, and soften or remove the ruled lateral line in favour of a countershading gradient.

rows.readsAs: A duckling or a generic orange finch/chick.
rows.defect: Three mustReads, three misses. Plumage is warm orange-yellow, not moss-green mottled with black and yellow, and it carries no mottling at all — just a smooth gradient. There is no owl-like whiskered facial disc; the face is a plain rounded cheek with a small black bead eye. The bill is a tiny pointed yellow-orange passerine cone, not the heavy pale hooked parrot bill. The wing is drawn as a flat outlined ellipse sitting on the flank — a decal with a dark rim line, painted ON the body, not a folded feather mass growing out of it. The tail is a thin brown spike stuck to the rear at an angle with a hard join, and the legs are two thin twig strokes that appear from under the belly with no thigh or feathered tarsus.
rows.fix: Recolour to mossy green with a black-barred, yellow-flecked mottle broken up per-feather-group. Build the bill as a large pale grey hook with a curved culmen overhanging the lower mandible. Add the facial disc: radiating fine bristles forward of the eye, a flattened owl-like face plane, and vibrissae at the bill base. Delete the ellipse decal and replace it with an overlapping covert/scapular feather mass whose lower edge is scalloped and whose upper edge dissolves into the back. Thicken and shorten the tail into a broad, worn, frayed paddle and give the legs visible grey zygodactyl feet with heavy tarsi.

rows.readsAs: A squirrel or marmot sitting up, silhouetted at night. The upright blob plus big sweeping tail says rodent, not macropod.
rows.defect: The mustRead 'massive muscular hind legs and long feet' is missing — where the thigh should be there is only the smooth continuation of the torso blob, and the only leg is a thin dark stick at bottom right ending in a flat foot. The tiny forearms held against the chest are not visible at all, a second mustRead miss. The tail IS long and tapering and does reach the ground, but it meets the body along a hard visible edge — a clean crease where the wedge-shaped tail shape is laid over the torso — and there is a second hard horizontal seam ruled across the middle of the torso where two body shapes overlap. Rendering is also nearly unreadable: the body is dark brown at almost the same value as the navy background, with the whole animal described by a thin lime rim-light. Head is small with two short ears and a stubby muzzle.
rows.fix: Grow a real hindquarter: a deep, forward-bulging thigh mass continuous with the lower back, a visible ankle high off the ground, and a long flat foot with 4+ toes carrying the weight. Add the tucked forearms with small clawed hands at the chest. Blend the tail root into the rump with a shared silhouette curve instead of an overlaid wedge, and remove the horizontal torso seam. Raise the body's base value 30-40% and add a broad key light on the flank so the animal reads without relying on the rim.

rows.readsAs: A red robin or generic garden songbird — and an obvious duplicate of the Kakapo in this same batch.
rows.defect: This is the Kakapo asset in red. Identical egg body, identical flat outlined wing ellipse decal, identical two-twig legs, identical thin spike tail, identical small pointed yellow beak. Against the reference it fails everything: posture is perched and standing, not flying; the bill is a straight passerine cone with no hook and no dark moustache stripe; the back is flat crimson with no rufous ground and no black spotting; the tail is a bare pointed sliver with no barring; and there are no pointed falcon wings at all, because the wings are not extended and are represented only by that painted-on ellipse. Head fraction is far too large and round for a falcon — the brief explicitly asks for slim and small-headed.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a flying pose: wings extended and swept to sharp points with visible primary separation and a broad root growing out of the shoulder, tail fanned and long. Give the head a hooked grey-blue bill with a yellow cere and paint the dark vertical malar stripe under the eye. Recolour the back to rufous with scattered black chevron spots and band the tail with black bars plus a broad subterminal band. Slim the torso and shrink the head to roughly 0.2 of body length. This must not share the songbird base mesh with Kakapo.

rows.readsAs: A golden minnow or a small tetra; at a glance it is the Juvenile Shark recoloured.
rows.defect: The rounded paddle tail is genuinely there and is the best feature, but it is joined wrong: the caudal fin is a separate brown fan butted against a straight vertical body edge, leaving a hard visible seam line across the peduncle — no taper, no fin rays running out of the flesh. The mustRead 'flattened topped head with an upturned mouth' fails in the opposite direction: the head is a sharp downward-angled wedge with a pointed, slightly drooping snout and no mouth line at all. The dorsal fin exists only as a very low ridge on the back, so 'set far back near the tail' reads as ambiguous rather than diagnostic. Flank spots are soft airbrushed dark ovals floating over the gradient — sprayed on, with no relation to scale rows or body contour. Body is the same straight-edged lens shape as the Juvenile Shark.
rows.fix: Flatten the dorsal profile of the head into a horizontal plane from eye to snout and tilt the mouth upward at the tip with a visible jaw line. Taper the body into a narrow peduncle and let the caudal fin grow out of it with radiating rays and a soft root, deleting the vertical seam. Raise the dorsal into a distinct rounded fin sitting above the rear third. Rework the spots so they sit in staggered rows that follow the flank curvature and pick up the lighting, and round the ventral contour so the outline stops reading as two straight lines.

rows.readsAs: An earthworm or a caecilian with a snake head grafted on — the ring segmentation dominates and defeats the reptile read.
rows.defect: The mustRead 'bold repeating bands or rings of colour' is completely absent — the body is one uniform terracotta from head to tail with only a lighting gradient. What IS repeating is dense fine parallel cross-ridges wrapping the whole coil, which read as annelid segmentation, so 'smooth glossy scales' also fails; the surface looks corrugated and matte, not glossy. The head is a distinctly wider ovoid bulb attached to the neck with a visible hard join, contradicting 'narrow head barely wider than the neck'. The coil itself is a near-perfect circular spiral of constant diameter — no taper toward a tail tip, and in fact no tail tip is findable in the picture. The forked red tongue and the vertical slit pupil are correct and are the only species-specific cues present.
rows.fix: Paint bold saddles or full rings — black/cream or the red-black-yellow tricolour — repeating along the body at roughly 1.5 body-diameters apart, wrapping around the coil so they compress on the far side. Replace the corrugated cross-ridges with an overlapping scale field at a much finer scale plus a strong specular sheen along the top of each coil. Narrow the head to barely exceed neck width and blend the jaw line into the neck instead of a bulb-on-stick. Taper the body over the last third and show the tail tip resting somewhere readable in the coil.

rows.readsAs: an ant or an engorged tick — a bulbous segmented abdomen behind a smooth round head with straight wire feelers
rows.defect: Two separate blobs pushed together: a plain smooth egg-shaped carapace and, behind it, a segmented abdomen that OVERLAPS it with a hard crescent seam, with a bright rim-light stroke painted straight down the join — the abdomen does not grow out of the thorax, it is parked on it. The carapace has no rostrum at all (no spike, no serrations) and no eyestalks — the eye is a single detached white speck floating in the gap to the left of the head. The antennae are four rigid straight dark lines; the lowest one starts in empty space below and left of the body, attached to nothing. Four legs are straight jointless dark sticks with no pincers, and they stop in midair well above the ground shadow. The tail fan is the one genuinely correct feature. mustRead fails: no spiked rostrum, no pincered front legs. Also rendered at roughly 25% of frame and so dark it is nearly invisible at 1:1.
rows.fix: Fuse carapace and abdomen into one continuous swept outline — carry the abdomen's segment ribs forward onto the rear of the carapace so the seam becomes a suture, not a butt-joint, and delete the rim-light stroke that currently traces the overlap. Extend the carapace front into a serrated rostrum spike and hang the antennae off ITS tip so they share one origin; clamp antenna root points to the body outline so none can spawn off-body. Give the front two legs a two-segment bend ending in a small chela, and lengthen all legs so the tips land on the shadow ellipse. Curve the antennae instead of ruling them straight. Raise base albedo/exposure ~2.5x and grow the subject to fill ~65% of the frame.

rows.readsAs: a coiled millipede, or a rolled-up length of ribbed hose sitting on a saucer
rows.defect: There is no animal, only a shell on a plank. The coil is drawn as a heavily ribbed TUBE — evenly spaced transverse bands all the way round — so it reads as a coiled millipede or a wound rubber hose, not a molluscan shell (a real shell is a smooth continuous whorl surface broken only by a sutural line). At the coil centre sits a perfect white specular sphere primitive. No head lobe emerges from the aperture anywhere. The 'tentacles' are three white spikes floating clear of the shell on the right with two grey balls hovering beside them — detached off-body eyespots. The 'foot' is a separate flat lens-shaped plate with a hard straight top edge that the coil merely rests on, with a visible gap and no membrane joining them. A stray thin arc line floats above the upper-left of the shell, touching nothing.
rows.fix: Delete the ribbed-tube treatment and paint the whorl as one smooth spiral surface with a single incised suture and fine growth lines running perpendicular to it; remove the specular ball at the apex. Build an actual body: a muscular head-foot extruded from the aperture, its dorsal surface continuous into the shell lip, with the two thin tentacles growing out of the head tip (eyespots ON the tentacle tips, not free-floating). Replace the flat plate with a foot sole whose top edge is the body's own underside — same material, no straight cut. Cull the stray arc (off-body artifact filter).

rows.readsAs: a robin or a plump garden thrush standing on a lawn
rows.defect: Every mustRead is missing. Posture is 'flying' in the reference but the bird is standing on two thin yellow legs. The wings are not long crooked M-shapes — they are a flat crescent decal lying on the flank, drawn as concentric hard-outlined ovals like a badge. The bill is a short blunt yellow cone, not hooked. There is no scarlet throat pouch and no throat feature at all. The tail is a small flat triangular wedge with two machined straight edges; the fork is a shallow notch, nothing like a scissor tail. The body is a plain plump egg and the head is a separate ball joined by a short neck with a visible tonal break at the junction. It is also the SAME body/wing/tail/leg template as the Gannet in this batch, recoloured red — the two are interchangeable.
rows.fix: Re-pose to soaring: horizontal body, wings extended full span with a sharp carpal kink so the outline reads as a flattened M, and a tail split into two long narrow streamers separated by a deep V (not a notch). Replace the decal wing with a wing whose root disappears under the scapular feathers — no closed outline crossing the body. Hook the bill tip downward and slim the whole bill. On the male, inflate a scarlet gular sac under the chin so it bulges the neck silhouette. Blend the neck ball into the torso so there is no value step. Give the frigatebird a distinct silhouette rule from the gannet so they cannot resolve to the same template.

rows.readsAs: a slice of lime, or a paper fan on a stick — nobody would call it an animal
rows.defect: The frill is pure geometry: a mathematically perfect circle with one pie-slice wedge cut out of the upper-left, and eight straight white radial spokes all converging on one geometric vertex. It looks like a sliced lime, or a Pac-Man, or a folding paper hand-fan. There is no head — the eye bead simply sits on the flat green disc, and the 'mouth' is a single ruled straight white horizontal line from the vertex to the disc rim; no snout, no jaw, no gaping pink gape (mustRead fail). The body is a flat-shaded tapering slab that meets the disc at a hard straight cut with no neck. Legs are two thin unattached-looking sticks plus one tiny stub under the belly. The tail is long, which is the only mustRead that lands.
rows.fix: Break the circle: make the frill an irregular scalloped membrane, wider at the top than the bottom, with a wavy notched rim and a slight bilateral asymmetry from the 3/4 view; replace the ruled radial spokes with cartilage rays that taper, curve, and fade before reaching the rim. Model an actual head IN FRONT of the frill — a wedge skull with a snout, a jaw line, and a pink open gape — so the frill is clearly behind it, not the face itself. Sink the neck into the frill's centre with the frill folding around it rather than the body wedge butting into a disc. Give the four limbs sprawled two-segment geometry with feet on the shadow line.

rows.readsAs: a toad — correct, and the only one in the batch a stranger would name right
rows.defect: The best render in the batch — bulging lidded eyes on top of the head, a clean wide curved mouth line, no tail, correct toad proportions. What breaks it is the limbs: all four are flat dark-brown silhouettes with zero shading, a completely different value from the golden body, and they pass behind the torso as hard-edged cardboard cut-outs. The hind haunches are featureless rounded blobs with no knee and no folded-Z geometry, so 'folded haunches with long hind legs' only half reads. The front legs are tiny stubs poking out of the belly's bottom edge with an abrupt colour break at the join. The dorsal spots are soft airbrushed blurs that sit on top of the surface rather than following its curvature, and the head is not differentiated from the body at all — the silhouette is one plain ellipse.
rows.fix: Re-light the limbs with the same key as the body so they share a material, and let the value graduate INTO the torso at the shoulder and hip instead of stepping. Add a knee break to the hind limb so the haunch folds into a Z and the thigh mass bulges above the body's waist line. Lengthen the forelimbs to prop the chest up. Warp the spots along the body's UV so they compress toward the silhouette edges, and vary their edge hardness. Add a tympanum disc behind each eye and two nostril dots to break the plain ellipse.

rows.readsAs: a moth, or a cartoon ghost with wings — the cyan eyes and earless-muzzleless face read alien, not mammal
rows.defect: Directly violates the reference note. The face is a flat pale disc with no muzzle whatsoever — no snout, no nose, no mouth, no jaw — topped by two tall thin pointed spike ears, i.e. exactly the crinkle-faced insect-bat head the note says to avoid. The eyes are large glowing cyan discs, which pushes it further toward alien/owl. mustRead fails: no fox-like long muzzle, and no finger bones anywhere in the wing membrane — the wings are blank grey sheets with a scalloped trailing edge and a bright painted stroke along the leading edge. The wing roots meet the torso at a hard bright-lined vertical edge, so they read as stuck on. The torso is a smooth featureless grey column with no fur and no neck. A single thin spur at the left wing bend is the only trace of a thumb claw.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as a fox: extend a long tapering muzzle forward with a wet nose pad and a visible lip line, shrink and round the ears down to short fox-ears, and drop the eyes to a warm dark brown iris (kill the cyan glow). Draw the four elongated finger bones radiating across each membrane and let the scallops of the trailing edge fall BETWEEN those fingers rather than being a decorative wave. Put a clear clawed thumb at each wrist bend. Dissolve the wing/body seam by carrying shoulder fur over the membrane root. Add fur texture to the torso so the body is not a smooth column.

rows.readsAs: a pebble, or a fat chick — a smooth grey bean with one eye dot
rows.defect: A featureless grey teardrop. All three mustReads are missing: no external ear flaps, no fore-flippers propping the chest (there is only a tiny nub under the belly), and no dog-like whiskered muzzle — in fact no muzzle, no mouth, no nostrils and no whiskers at all, just one small dark bead for an eye on an unbroken curve. The head is not separated from the body by any neck or brow. The posture is not quadrupedal; the animal is a resting blob with a small forked tail flipper at the rear. The silhouette is a plain capsule/teardrop. Two soft dark circular blurs on the flank read as airbrush smudges sprayed on top of the surface, not as anatomy or fur. The rim light is a hard yellow-white painted stroke tracing only the top edge.
rows.fix: Push the head out of the mass: build a brow, a taper into a dog-like muzzle with a dark nose pad, a mouth line, and a spray of whiskers; add the small external ear pinnae behind the eye — they are the diagnostic that separates fur seal from true seal. Rotate to the quadrupedal stance: long fore-flippers planted and straightened to lift the chest well clear of the ground, hind flippers rotated forward under the hips and visible. Delete the two flank smudges and replace them with fur direction that follows the body's curvature. Soften the rim stroke into a gradient and wrap it around the form instead of stopping at the top edge.

rows.readsAs: a canary, or a wooden rubber-duck toy — a yellow ball with a spike beak
rows.defect: The whole bird is one saturated canary yellow. mustRead fails on two of three: no white body (nothing is white), no jet-black wingtips (the wing and tail are the same yellow as the body), and no dark facial mask — the buff-yellow head wash is the only colour cue and it is meaningless when the body matches it. The long straight dagger bill does read, but it is an unshaded flat triangle with perfectly straight ruled edges. The head is a separate ball on a short neck with a visible tonal step where the neck meets the torso. The wing is a hard-outlined crescent decal of stacked concentric ovals lying on the flank like a badge. The tail is a flat triangular wedge with machined straight edges emerging abruptly from the body. Body silhouette is a plain circle on two wire legs. Same template as the Frigatebird in this batch.
rows.fix: Fix the palette first: body, wing coverts and tail to clean white, the outer primaries to hard-edged jet black, and confine the buff-yellow wash to the crown and nape with a soft gradient into the white — then add the dark bare-skin mask around the eye and bill base. Give the bill a subtle culmen ridge, a value gradient, and a fine dark line along the gape rather than a flat triangle. Replace the decal wing with a wing whose root is hidden under the scapulars — no closed outline on the body. Round the tail into a tapered wedge with feather separations instead of a straight-edged plate. Blend the neck into the torso. Differentiate the silhouette from the Frigatebird's.

rows.readsAs: a nudibranch, but a toy one — a gold pebble with a pink feather-duster stuck on
rows.defect: The cerata read as a flat 2D comb of pink brush-strokes planted along a hard top edge of the body — there is a crisp unbroken line where every plume meets the gold, so they sit ON the slug rather than growing OUT of it. The body itself is a smooth glossy gold lozenge with an airbrushed highlight and no skin texture, papillae or mantle rim; it looks like a plastic almond. The rhinophores are a barely-visible yellow nub at the right end, far too small to read as a pair of club-shaped horns.
rows.fix: Root each ceras with a swollen base that shares the body's gold gradient for its first ~20% of length before going pink, and stagger them in two or three overlapping rows at varying depth so the boundary is a broken tuft, not a line. Give the mantle a visible flared skirt/edge frill and low-frequency mottling so the gold is skin, not enamel. Scale the rhinophores up ~2.5x into two distinct clubbed, annulated horns standing clear of the head.

rows.readsAs: a sardine or small herring with a red slice of watermelon on its back
rows.defect: Almost nothing of the reference survives. The body is a short stubby grey fish about 2.5:1, not a ribbon 18x longer than deep. The crimson dorsal is a single solid opaque semicircular slab laid across the back like a red hat — no individual elongated rays, and no crest rising over the head. There are no oar-like pelvic streamers (only a small black wisp at the tail end), and the body ends in a normal blunt fish tail rather than tapering away. The red slab meets the grey body along a hard clean line with no interpenetration.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette at true aspect ~18:1 — a thin laterally-compressed silver ribbon with a wavy dorsal margin. Replace the solid red slab with a fringe of separate crimson rays whose bases attach individually along the entire dorsal ridge, and extend the first 4-6 rays into a tall plume over the head. Add two long single-ray pelvic streamers with paddle tips trailing well behind the body, and taper the posterior to a point with no caudal fin.

rows.readsAs: a plaice or a generic round flatfish; without the fins it could also be a scallop
rows.defect: The two mustRead towering fins are absent: the dorsal is a tiny ribbed nub on the top edge and there is no anal fin at all on the underside, so the whole vertical-cross silhouette that defines a mola is gone. The rear does not end in a frilled clavus rudder — it just curves shut as a smooth arc. No puckered beak mouth is visible; there is only a thin curved gill line and a round dot eye. The outline is close to a plain circle and the pectoral is a small fan stuck flat on the flank with a visible seam.
rows.fix: Add a tall dorsal and an equally tall anal fin, each roughly as long as the body is deep, growing out of the disc with a thickened muscular base. Truncate the rear vertically and cap it with a scalloped clavus of short rounded lobes. Add a small round protruding beak-like mouth at the front. Break the circular outline with the leathery lumpy irregularity of real mola skin.

rows.readsAs: a jellyfish, or a cartoon squid; the thin threadlike strands push it toward a hydrozoan
rows.defect: The arms are uniform-width wire threads with no taper, no thickness at the base, and no suckers anywhere — the sucker mustRead is entirely missing. I count only about six strands, not eight, and they hang as loose loops rather than reading as a crawling animal. The eyes are two plain round black dots with no horizontal slit pupil (second mustRead missing). The mantle is a near-perfect egg/circle primitive with a flat airbrushed gradient and no mantle-to-head constriction; the arms simply appear beneath it with no web, no arm crown, no interbrachial mass.
rows.fix: Give each arm a thick muscular base that merges into a proper arm crown under the mantle, tapering to a fine tip, and draw a double row of suckers along the inner curve. Bring the count to eight. Replace the dot eyes with a wide horizontal rectangular-slit pupil in a domed eye bulge. Add a web between the arm bases and a slight waist between mantle and head so the bulb is not a free-floating oval.

rows.readsAs: an axolotl — the bright pink, chubby body and big friendly eyes are pure axolotl
rows.defect: The eyes are large, open, glossy black-and-white cartoon eyes with a smiling mouth line — the reference is explicit that an olm's eyes are skinned over and invisible. Colour is a saturated hot magenta with yellow spots, not pale pink translucent flesh. Aspect is roughly 3:1, nowhere near 8:1 — the animal is a fat sausage, not eel-like. Worse, the red frond cluster is duplicated: there is a gill tuft behind the head AND a second identical red frond bundle hanging off the mid-belly where a limb should be, so the limbs have been rendered as gills. No spindly three-toed legs are legible anywhere.
rows.fix: Skin over the eyes — a faint darker patch under smooth skin, no sclera or pupil, and remove the smile. Desaturate to pale translucent flesh-pink with a hint of internal shading, drop the yellow spots. Stretch the body to ~8:1 with an even-diameter eel trunk and a laterally flattened paddle tail. Delete the mid-body frond bundle and replace it with four vestigially thin limbs, three tiny toes on the front pair, and keep the bushy red gills only at the head.

rows.readsAs: a person in a fur-trimmed parka hood, or at best a chimp mascot costume
rows.defect: Reads as a person in a fluffy hooded coat, not an ape. The torso is a flat tan rounded-rectangle shield with a hard continuous outline seam where it overlaps the darker body — a garment, not a chest. The arms are short dark capsules barely longer than the legs, so the enormous arm span mustRead fails outright. The hair is not shaggy long orange-red: the head is ringed by a tight curly brown wig-halo with a hard hairline band across the forehead like a cap brim, and the body is smooth airbrushed tan with soft blob spots. No cheek flanges. The whole figure sits upright and symmetrical, not in a quadruped knuckle-walking posture.
rows.fix: Lengthen the arms to roughly 1.5x body height, bowed outward, with knuckles planted on the ground ahead of the short bent legs. Replace the shield-torso with a body whose contour is broken by long directional hair strands crossing the silhouette edge — the outline should be ragged, never a closed rounded rect. Swap the curly halo for long straggly orange-red locks hanging past the shoulders. Add two broad flat cheek flanges flanking the face and a throat pouch below.

rows.readsAs: a teal mackerel or a generic cartoon dolphin — the vertical forked tail makes it a fish
rows.defect: The animal is uniformly cyan/teal. There is no black-and-white anywhere — no crisp saddle patch, no white eye patch, no white ventral field. Two of the three mustRead features are simply absent. The dorsal fin is a small backswept triangle, not tall. The tail is a vertically-oriented forked fish caudal fin, not a horizontal cetacean fluke, which alone removes it from the mammals. The pectoral is a soft teal blob overlapping the belly with a visible edge and no shoulder integration. A thin light rim-line runs along the whole back like a decal outline.
rows.fix: Repaint to glossy black dorsally with a hard-edged white ventral field, a white oval eye patch behind and above the eye, and a grey saddle behind the dorsal fin. Rotate the tail to a horizontal fluke seen edge-on with a notched centre. Raise the dorsal to a tall near-vertical triangle roughly a fifth of body length with a thick base that swells out of the back. Reshape the pectoral into a large rounded paddle emerging from a shoulder mass rather than sitting on top of the flank.

rows.readsAs: an ant, or a teal-painted honeybee; the spiky yellow ruff and grey stripes dominate
rows.defect: The head and thorax are one big cyan sphere ringed by a spiky yellow-green fringe of hairs — exactly the fuzzy look the note forbids — and the abdomen is a grey-and-white banded segment, so despite the teal it still reads as a striped, hairy bee. The long trailing tongue is completely absent, and there is no swollen polished hind tibia; the legs are four thin uniform teal sticks with no thickening anywhere. The metallic mustRead is only half met: the thorax has a plastic gradient rather than a hard specular jewel sheen, and the abdomen is not metallic at all. Posture is standing on the ground with wings folded, not flying.
rows.fix: Remove the yellow hair fringe entirely and give the whole body a hard chitinous specular highlight with a coloured rim, so the green-blue reads as polished metal. Make the abdomen the same metallic green-gold as the thorax, banded only by faint segment ridges, not grey-white stripes. Add a long dark proboscis trailing back under the body past the abdomen tip. Swell one pair of hind tibiae into large glossy paddles. Separate head from thorax and pose in flight with blurred outstretched wings.

rows.readsAs: A deep-sea anglerfish / footballfish
rows.defect: This is not a monkfish at all — it is a plump red ovoid balloon with a glowing bulb on a wire, i.e. a deep-sea footballfish. The single biggest mustRead, 'enormous flattened head far wider than the tapering body', is completely absent: there is no head region whatsoever, just one smooth egg with an eye near the right edge. Aspect measures roughly 1.35, not the specified 1.9. The frilly jaw skin flaps are missing entirely. The teeth are a row of identical white triangles marching along a straight line, like a zipper decal laid on the surface rather than teeth sitting in a jaw — and the 'mouth' is a single straight scored line, not an upturned gape. The tail is a hard-edged brick-shaped paddle floating at the left with a visible dark gap between it and the body — a stuck-on part, not a caudal fin growing out of a peduncle. The lure is a perfect circle with a perfect circular glow halo. Body blotches are soft airbrush puffs sprayed over the red gradient with no relation to any skin structure.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette as a dorsoventrally flattened wedge: front 50% a wide flat pancake head with the jaw as the leading edge, rear tapering to a narrow tail stalk. Replace the straight mouth line with a genuine concave gape opening upward, teeth of varying length slanting inward from the jaw margin. Delete the detached rectangular tail and grow a caudal fin continuously out of a tapering peduncle. Add a fringe of irregular fleshy lappets along the jaw and body margin. Break the perfect-circle lure into an irregular fleshy esca and taper the illicium out of the snout rather than butting it against the outline. Recolour from saturated red to mottled sand-brown.

rows.readsAs: A green rubber duck or a duckling
rows.defect: Renders as a bright mint-green bathtub duck occupying only about a third of the 440px frame. Every one of the three mustRead features is missing: the bill is uniformly orange-yellow with no red and no yellow tip, there is no red frontal shield on the forehead, there is no white flank streak, and there is no cocked tail with white undertail flashes — the rear is a blank rounded stub. The body is a plain green ovoid decorated with two concentric arcs that read as a sprayed-on swoosh rather than folded wing coverts. Head and neck form one smooth continuous green blob with no perceptible neck. The water is a flat perfect ellipse with a second perfect ellipse ring inside it — a pure geometric primitive with a hard rim, not a waterline. The bill is a plain isoceles triangle stuck onto the head.
rows.fix: Scale the subject up to fill the frame. Repaint the bill as a red base with a distinct yellow tip and carry that red up into a shield plate over the forehead. Add the bold white lateral flank stripe as a broken line of white feather edges along the waterline. Cock the tail up and split the undertail into two white patches with a dark centre. Darken the plumage to slate-black/olive with a bluish head. Replace the concentric arcs with actual scapular and wing-covert feather groups whose shapes follow the body curvature. Replace the elliptical water ring with an irregular, softly-broken waterline that clips the body rather than sitting under it.

rows.readsAs: A barracuda or needlefish
rows.defect: Reads as a purple barracuda or needlefish. Aspect measures about 5:1, not the specified 9:1, and the body is a rigid straight spindle rather than a sinuous ribbon. Two explicit mustRead prohibitions are violated: there IS a pectoral fin — a small grey fan stuck onto the flank just behind the head with a hard boundary against the body — and the tail terminates in a separate notched/forked caudal fin at the left instead of the dorsal ridge continuing unbroken to a pointed tail tip. The mouth is not gaping: it is a closed straight line, and the 'needle teeth' are a row of white tick-marks hanging BELOW the lower jaw outline as detached strokes floating in the background, not teeth inside an open mouth. The dorsal ridge is only a faint translucent grey outline, not a ridge of body wall. Spots are uniform grey airbrush blobs sprayed over the purple gradient with no scale or mucous-skin texture.
rows.fix: Delete the pectoral fin entirely and replace it with a single small round gill pore. Delete the forked caudal fin and run the dorsal ridge continuously over the tail tip and forward along the underside. Open the jaw to a genuine wedge-shaped gape with the teeth inside it, sized irregularly and curving backward. Stretch to a true 9:1 and put an S-curve through the body so it swims. Give the dorsal ridge real thickness and let it emerge from the back with no outline seam. Replace the sprayed spots with a reticulated mottling that deforms with the body curve.

rows.readsAs: An orange ant
rows.defect: Reads unambiguously as an ant. The body is three tangent orange spheres in a row with visible seams where each sphere overlaps the next — a bead-chain of geometric primitives, exactly the failure mode this audit is looking for. None of the three mustRead features survives: there is no long needle proboscis jutting forward (the only forward structure is a plumose antenna; the mouthparts are absent), the legs are short stiff brown sticks with a single hard elbow kink — nowhere near 'six very long dangling legs' and I count only five clearly — and the wings are two plain grey rounded ovals lying flat on top of the abdomen like pebbles, with no venation, no narrowness, and no scale fringe. The note's posture requirement also fails: the body sits level with the legs standing on the ground, rather than hanging at an angle with the hind legs kicked up. Every leg meets the body at a hard butt joint with no coxa.
rows.fix: Fuse the sphere chain into a single continuous head-thorax-abdomen with a humped thorax and a long slender tapering abdomen; kill the tangency seams. Add the defining needle proboscis projecting straight forward from the head, longer than the head. Lengthen the legs to roughly two body-lengths, make them thread-thin with a gentle catenary droop and taper to the tarsus, and show all six with the hind pair raised behind. Narrow the wings to long slender blades held over the abdomen, add longitudinal veins and a fringe of scales along the trailing edge. Tilt the whole body head-down 30-40 degrees.

rows.readsAs: A green lacewing or a green fly — and clearly the same creature as this batch's Mosquito
rows.defect: Uses the identical three-tangent-sphere body chassis as the Mosquito in this same batch, only recoloured mint-green — the two images are visibly siblings, which is the 'different organism in the same batch' failure. The mustRead 'thick furry body' fails: the body is glossy smooth spheres with specular highlights, and the only nod to fur is a handful of stiff yellow spikes poking out of the seams between the spheres, which read as bristles stuck into the joints rather than a pile of scales covering the thorax. The mustRead 'broad dusty wings held roof-like over the back' also fails: the wings are two flat leaf-shaped green paddles fanned out horizontally behind the body, with straight radial lines that read as leaf venation, and they butt against the thorax sphere with a hard edge instead of emerging from it. Eyes are specified 'prominent' but the head carries a single small black dot. The feathery comb antennae are the one mustRead that lands.
