rows.fix: Replace the sphere chain with a single furry fusiform body, thorax noticeably wider than the abdomen, and give it a real fur pelt — dense short strokes over the whole thorax, not spikes at the seams. Rebuild the wings as broad triangular forewings with a scalloped, slightly ragged margin, held tented over the back in a roof so the hindwing is mostly hidden; join them under the thorax fur so no seam shows. Swap the leaf veins for the moth's own branching vein pattern plus a dusty scale mottle and an eyespot or band. Enlarge the compound eyes into two prominent hemispheres. Shift the colour off the mosquito's palette to a dusty brown/grey so the two are not read as the same animal.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon gecko or a mango-coloured newt
rows.defect: An orange oval body with a separate orange ellipse dropped on the right as a head — the overlap is visible as a hard crescent seam, so the head is stuck on, not grown out. The dominant mustRead, 'tail longer than head and body combined', fails badly: the tail is a short fat curled club roughly 60% of the body length, and it too meets the body at a visible seam. Measured aspect is about 2.4 against a specified 4.5, so the animal is far too dumpy. 'Splayed sprawling legs with long clawed toes' fails completely — there are two featureless brown pegs pointing straight down beneath the body, no toes, no claws, no splay, no elbow or knee, and the front pair is barely visible. There is no granular scale texture; the skin is a smooth airbrush gradient with a scatter of soft brown blobs sprayed over it. The mouth is one straight scored line.
rows.fix: Stretch the body to 4.5:1 and flatten it. Grow the head out of the neck as a continuous taper with no overlapping-ellipse seam, and widen it into a lizard's wedge with a distinct jawline. Replace the club tail with one longer than head+body, whip-thin at the tip, growing seamlessly out of the pelvis. Rebuild all four legs sprawled sideways — upper limb out, lower limb down, elbows and knees visible from above — with five long spread clawed toes on each foot. Add a granular pebbled scale texture that follows the body form, plus a proper dorsolateral band instead of sprayed blobs.

rows.readsAs: A coiled earthworm or a red vacuum hose
rows.defect: The coil is a near-perfect torus — a machined donut of constant thickness with a clean circular hole in the middle. Real coiled vipers taper and stack; this reads as an extruded tube bent into a ring. The body is covered edge to edge with evenly spaced transverse ribs of identical pitch, which reads as annelid segmentation or the ribbing on a vacuum hose, not as snake scales. Two mustReads fail outright: there is no zigzag dorsal band anywhere (uniform red with only the ribbing), and the head is a small rounded ellipse only marginally wider than the neck rather than a broad triangular head much wider than the neck — the required viper wedge is absent. The vertical slit pupil is present and correct, and the forked tongue reads. There is no taper from a thick midbody to a slimmer neck; the tube is one gauge from tail to head.
rows.fix: Break the perfect torus: vary the coil radius, let loops overlap at different heights and taper visibly toward the tail so it is a stacked coil, not a ring. Replace the uniform ribbing with overlapping keeled scales that shrink toward the head and change size on the flanks versus the spine. Rebuild the head as a broad arrow-shaped triangle, distinctly wider than the neck, with a pinched neck behind the jaw angle and a visible supraocular ridge over the eye. Paint the dark zigzag dorsal band running the length of the spine and following the coil, plus a dark postocular stripe. Desaturate off pure red toward a grey-brown alpine morph.

rows.readsAs: A yellow cartoon rabbit
rows.defect: Reads as a small yellow rabbit. The mustRead 'large round thin ears' fails — the ears are tall pointed leaf shapes angled back, unmistakably lagomorph, not the mouse's big round discs. The mustRead 'naked tail as long as the body' also fails on both counts: the tail is roughly 60% of body length and it is opaque brown with the same fur shading as the body, not naked pink, and it terminates in a blunt hook. The head is a separate ellipse overlapped onto the body egg with a visible boundary arc where the two shapes cross. On the flank there is a hard-outlined dark thigh blob that sits on the surface like a painted patch rather than a haunch under the skin. The muzzle carries a small white rectangle with a flat top edge as teeth — a machined primitive. The legs are two smooth brown stumps with no feet, no toes. Measured aspect is about 2.0 against the specified 2.8, so the animal is too round.
rows.fix: Swap the pointed ears for large round thin ears with visible inner pinna and a translucent edge. Redraw the tail as long as the head+body, thin, tapering, pink and naked with fine annulations, growing out of the rump with no seam. Merge the head ellipse into the body with a continuous neck-shoulder line and pull the muzzle out to a real point with a dark nose. Replace the white rectangle with a pair of chisel incisors that follow the lip line. Dissolve the outlined thigh patch into shading that reads as musculature under fur. Give the feet long splayed toes and add a hind foot with the elongated mouse sole. Lengthen the body toward 2.8:1.

rows.readsAs: A blue pigeon or a bluebird standing on the ground
rows.defect: This is not a raptor and not in flight. It is the generic perched songbird/pigeon template: fat round blue body, small round head, short conical yellow finch bill, two flat yellow stick feet planted on the ground. Every mustRead is absent — no white underside, no dark mask stripe through the eye (the eye is a plain black dot on flat blue), no crooked M-shaped wings (the wing is a dark crescent stroke plus a lighter lens shape painted flat ON the flank, with a hard outline — sprayed-on decoration, not a wing growing out of the shoulder), no hooked bill, no talons at all. Spec says aspect 2.2 / posture flying; the render is roughly 1:1 and standing. The tail is a flat dark triangular wedge butted onto the rear with a straight seam. Identical body to Ostrich, Owl, Oystercatcher and Parrot in this same batch, recolored.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a flying silhouette: horizontal body axis, two long wings swept from the shoulder mass with a downward kink at the wrist (the M), spread tail fan, aspect ~2.2. Paint the underside white with a dark carpal patch and run a dark stripe from the bill through the eye to the nape. Replace the conical bill with a short deeply hooked black bill and hang two outsized talons with curved claws below the belly. Wings must be built as continuations of the body mass, not lens shapes drawn over the flank.

rows.readsAs: A green finch or duckling standing on stilts
rows.defect: A small green chick on long legs, not an ostrich. The defining mustRead — an extremely long bare neck carrying a tiny flat head — is missing entirely: the neck is a short thick stub and the head is ~0.2 of the body, far above the 0.12 spec. No fluffy plume wings (again the flat crescent-plus-lens wing decal glued on the flank) and no tail bustle — the tail is the same hard dark triangular wedge as every other bird here. The legs are two thin yellow lines with a visible hard join where they enter the belly and end in three thin toes, not two powerful toes. The bill is a small yellow cone, not the broad flat ostrich bill.
rows.fix: Change the proportion first: neck length ~1.5x body height, bare and tapering, head reduced to ~0.12 with a wide flat bill. Give the body a high egg-shaped mass with a fluffy plume bustle over the rump instead of the pointed tail wedge, and reduce the wings to drooping plume tufts. Thicken the legs into muscled thighs that emerge from feathering, and cut the toes to two, with one large nailed toe.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon owl, but a stranger would more likely say 'a bird with owl eyes drawn on'
rows.defect: Closest of the birds but still the shared pigeon template with owl parts stuck on. There is no flat round facial disc — just two large white circles floating on a normal small bird head, and the head is ~0.2 of the figure against the 0.35 spec. The body is a horizontal side-profile pigeon body with a clearly visible neck (spec: upright barrel, no visible neck), and a dark pointed tail wedge projects well past the rump. The two ear tufts are hard-edged straight-sided triangles with a visible seam at the skull — parts stuck ON. Same crescent-plus-lens wing decal painted flat over the flank. The eyes are perfect circles with perfect circular pupils, an obvious geometric primitive.
rows.fix: Rotate the body upright into a barrel and merge head into shoulders so no neck reads. Grow the head to ~0.35 and build an actual facial disc: a broad flattened concave heart of radial feathering with a rim, eyes set inside it and a small hooked beak between them. Break the eye circles with a soft feathered lid and an off-round iris. Fold the wings flat down the body sides as feather tracts and shorten the tail so it barely clears the rump. Root the ear tufts as feather clumps whose base blends into the crown rather than triangles landing on it.

rows.readsAs: A scallop shell, or a small ceramic bowl / desk lamp
rows.defect: A perfectly bilaterally symmetric smooth pale fan with straight radial ribs converging on a single point — that is a scallop, not an oyster, and the ribs are machined straight lines. Every mustRead fails: the shell is smooth and clean, not irregular, ruffled or rough-layered; the two valves are not unequal (there is one fan body with a dead-straight dark line across the top acting as the hinge, no cupped-versus-flat pair); there is no pearly interior distinguished from an exterior. Two mid-grey straight-sided triangles sit under the shell touching nothing — off-body artifacts that read as fangs or a stand. The whole object also floats clear above its cast shadow ellipse.
rows.fix: Replace the symmetric fan with an asymmetric outline: one deep cupped valve, one flatter lid, unequal in size and outline, hinged at a narrow ragged umbo. Build the surface from stacked irregular growth laminae with chipped, wavy, overlapping edges instead of straight radial ribs, and dirty the exterior. Reserve the smooth pearly nacre for the open interior only. Delete the two grey triangles and reseat the shell onto its shadow.

rows.readsAs: A generic pink wading bird — a sandpiper or a toy flamingo chick
rows.defect: The long straight chisel bill is the one thing that lands, but it is yellow, not orange-red. The other two mustReads are absent: the plumage is uniform hot pink with no black-and-white blocking anywhere, and the legs are two thin pale-yellow sticks, not stout pink ones, with no red eye ring (the eye is a tiny dark dot). Same shared template as the rest of the batch — same crescent-plus-lens wing decal painted on the flank, same hard dark triangular tail wedge, same hard seam where the leg lines meet the belly.
rows.fix: Recolor to the real bird: solid black head, neck and upper back against a clean white breast and belly with a hard boundary at the waterline, plus a white wing bar. Push the bill to saturated orange-red and thicken it slightly toward the base. Thicken the legs into short stout pink shanks. Add a red orbital ring around a visibly enlarged eye. Rebuild the wing as a feather tract growing off the shoulder rather than a lens laid on the side.

rows.readsAs: A goldfish or a discus
rows.defect: The deep coin-shaped compressed body does read, but the identity features do not. The mouth is a single thin upward-curving smile line — no underslung jaw and, critically, no flat square human-like teeth, which is the entire reason anyone recognizes a pacu. The forehead is a smooth continuous arc rather than a blunt steep rise. The caudal fin is a flat dark triangular facet with dead-straight edges joined to the body across a visible hard line at the peduncle — a part stuck on, not a tail growing out. Small hard-edged triangular slivers at the ventral edge serve as fins. The eye is a perfect white circle with a perfect black pupil, a geometric primitive. Body is a flat yellow gradient with no scale texture.
rows.fix: Cut a real mouth: a short blunt gape with the lower jaw pushed forward past the upper, and paint a row of flat square incisor-like teeth visible in the gap. Break the forehead into a steep straight-ish rise from the snout to a nuchal hump. Rebuild the caudal fin with a soft forked outline and blend the peduncle into it so no seam shows; give the fin visible rays. Add rounded scale mottling over the flank and a dusky red-orange wash on the lower belly. Replace the circular eye with a slightly ovoid one carrying a lid line.

rows.readsAs: A needlefish, barracuda or gar
rows.defect: The rostrum is a sharp needle-like spear that tapers to a point, not a long flat paddle — it reads as a needlefish or gar snout. That is the defining mustRead and it is wrong, not merely weak. The mouth is a thin smile line, the opposite of a cavernous gaping toothless maw. The tail is a small hard-edged forked wedge with straight facet edges meeting a very thin peduncle across a visible seam; it does not read as a shark-like heterocercal tail. A dorsal fin sits on the back as a flat dark triangle with a hard boundary against the body. The dark speckling on the snout is a scatter of dots sprayed on top of the gradient rather than skin.
rows.fix: Rebuild the rostrum as a broad flattened blade — wide in silhouette, rounded or squared at the tip, roughly a third of total length — and taper it into the skull with no seam. Open the mouth into a large rounded toothless gape under the rostrum, with a visible gill flap sweeping back. Make the caudal fin large and asymmetric with a longer upper lobe, blended smoothly out of a thicker peduncle. Root the dorsal fin far back with a soft trailing edge. Drop the sprayed dots for smooth scaleless skin with a soft sheen.

rows.readsAs: A dove or a young seagull
rows.defect: Nothing here says parrot. It is the same pigeon template again, in pale grey-white, with a small yellow conical bill that has only a faint downward tick — no short deeply hooked beak and no fleshy cere. The feet are the standard three-thin-toes-forward stick feet shared with every other bird in this batch, so the zygodactyl mustRead fails outright. The tail is the recurring flat dark grey triangular wedge, and the body is a horizontal fat oval rather than a compact upright stocky parrot. Same crescent-plus-lens wing decal painted flat over the flank with a hard outline.
rows.fix: Give it a genuinely hooked bill: a deep, short, strongly downcurved upper mandible closing over a squared lower one, with a raised fleshy cere at the base carrying the nostrils. Rebuild the foot with two toes forward and two back, gripping. Square off the tail into a short blunt fan instead of the pointed wedge. Tilt the body upright and shorten it to a stocky compact mass with a large rounded head. Recolor away from dove grey — an Amazon green body with a colored face patch — and give the folded wing distinguishable primaries growing off the shoulder.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon guinea pig or a green rabbit toy
rows.defect: No fur anywhere — the body is one smooth mint-green egg with a glossy airbrush gradient and a thin light rim-stroke, so the 'furry' mustRead fails outright. The head is a separate sphere laid ON TOP of the body: its outline arc is visible crossing the flank as a hard seam, and a second pasted-on disc (the haunch) shows its own stroke on the side. Ears are two small pointed leaf shapes standing clear above the skull with their own outlines — the opposite of 'ears buried in the coat'. Incisors are a literal white RECTANGLE with square corners, and the four whiskers are perfectly straight ruled grey lines. Feet are dark green nubs stuck under the hem.
rows.fix: Replace the gradient fill with a real pelt: dense short-stroke fur across the whole silhouette and a fur-broken outer contour instead of the clean egg edge. Delete the separate head sphere and the haunch disc — build one continuous crouched mass whose neck and rump are implied by fur direction and shading, not by overlapping outlines. Sink the ears to two small fur-fringed bumps barely breaking the head contour. Kill the white rectangle teeth (a tiny dark mouth line is enough) and either drop the whiskers or draw 2-3 fine tapering curved hairs.

rows.readsAs: a baboon or a generic teal monkey
rows.defect: The signature mustRead is entirely absent: the tail has NO black-and-white rings — it is a plain flat teal tube of uniform width, it is roughly the same length as the body (not longer), and it exits the LEFT side of the torso at waist height as a hard-edged pipe rather than growing from a rump. The face is a flat ape/baboon face — no fox muzzle, no black mask, and the eyes are small white discs with black pupils, not bright orange-gold. A thin pale perfectly-even arc is stroked across the forehead like a machined headband. Fur exists only as a frizzy halo around the head; the torso, arms and legs are smooth tubes and the two thigh ovals are pasted flat on the front of the belly with visible edges.
rows.fix: Rebuild the tail: longer than head+body, thicker at the base, tapering, with 12-14 alternating dark/pale rings that wrap the cylinder (rings compress on the far side of curves) and a dark tip; root it in a fur-blended rump mass. Give the head a projecting tapered muzzle with a black mask over eyes and snout, white cheek and brow patches, and large amber-gold irides with small pupils. Carry the head's fur texture down over the torso and limbs so nothing reads as a smooth tube, and delete the forehead arc stroke and the separate thigh ovals.

rows.readsAs: an abalone shell, or a speckled egg / a slice of salami
rows.defect: This is not a limpet at all — it is a flat salmon-orange ellipse with a soft airbrush gradient and blurred pale blotches sprayed over the surface. All three mustReads fail: there is no cone and no apex (the form is a flat oval seen face-on, with zero height), there are no radiating ribs, and it is not clamped to anything — there is no rock in the frame and the shell floats above a detached elliptical drop shadow. Five perfectly round black dots march in a straight line across the upper face, which reads as abalone respiratory holes and belongs to a different animal.
rows.fix: Redraw in profile-three-quarter as a low cone: an oval base footprint with the apex raised and pushed slightly forward of centre, so the silhouette shows real height. Add 16-20 ribs radiating from the apex to the rim, each catching light on one side and shadowing the other, with the rim scalloped where the ribs meet it. Seat it on a rock: a stone plane under the shell with the rim in hard contact, no floating gap and no free-standing drop shadow. Remove the five black dots and the sprayed pale blotches; replace with concentric growth banding crossing the ribs.

rows.readsAs: a sea urchin, or a spiky pill-bug / caterpillar
rows.defect: Reads as an invertebrate, not a fish. There is no head, no mouth, no gill line, no caudal peduncle and NO TAIL FIN — just a purple ellipse. Around 18 straight tapered needles radiate in every direction including forward past the snout and straight down, each sitting on the body outline with a hard flat base — stuck-on primitives, not fin rays growing from a fin membrane. The two remaining mustReads fail with them: there is no dorsal FAN (the spines are omnidirectional, not a row along the back) and no feathery separated pectoral rays. The banding is a row of evenly spaced dark lens/leaf shapes painted flat on the surface, uniform in width and spacing, sprayed on rather than skin.
rows.fix: Start from a real fish silhouette: tapered head with a large mouth and gill cover, deep body, narrowing peduncle, fanned caudal fin. Confine the long spines to a single dorsal row along the top edge, each rising from a shared fin base with translucent membrane webbing between the lower thirds. Build the pectorals as two broad wing-like fans of separated rays sweeping back and out from the shoulder. Replace the painted lens stripes with irregular red-brown bars that widen and narrow, wrap the body's curvature, run onto the head and continue across the fin rays as banding.

rows.readsAs: a purple salamander or newt
rows.defect: The tail fails its mustRead: it is shorter than or equal to the body, uniform thick and blunt (no taper at all), curls upward like a beaver's, and carries a painted dark stripe inside it. Only TWO legs are drawn, they are plain tapered cylinders hanging straight down UNDER the body like a mammal's — no elbows out, no sprawl, no feet or toes. The head is a separate ellipse with its own outline stroke visibly crossing over the body ellipse — a hard seam at the neck — and it is a blunt rounded oval, not wedge-shaped. There are no scales anywhere: a smooth purple gradient with soft dark blotches sprayed on top. The mouth is a perfectly straight ruled horizontal line.
rows.fix: Extend the tail to at least 1.5x body length, thick at the vent and tapering to a fine point, held out behind with a gentle S-curve; remove the interior stripe. Draw all four limbs, upper arm and thigh projecting horizontally out to the side and the lower segment dropping to splayed five-toed feet — the classic sprawl. Merge the head into the body with a continuous tapering neck and reshape it into a wedge: broad at the jaw hinge, narrowing to the snout. Replace the airbrush with overlapping scale rows that shrink over the snout and ring the tail, and curve the mouth line to follow the jaw.

rows.readsAs: a prawn or a crayfish
rows.defect: The strongest render in the batch, but it reads as a shrimp or prawn, not a lobster: the abdomen is curled up and forward under the body and the whole animal is short and hunched rather than long and low. The claws are the weak point — they are flat dark-brown blades, much darker than the body so they look like separate objects pasted on, both the SAME size (mustRead calls for unequal), and neither shows an opposed pincer with a real gap between fingers. The walking legs are four straight brown sticks of uniform width with no joints and no feet. Cephalothorax and abdomen are two smooth ovals with a visible gap and seam where they meet.
rows.fix: Straighten and lengthen the abdomen so it extends back level with the body and lift the aspect toward 3:1. Rebuild the claws as three-dimensional pincers in the body's own colour family: a swollen propodus with a visible movable dactyl and an open gap between the fingers, one crusher noticeably bulkier than the cutter, each carried on a jointed arm that grows out of the carapace. Give the legs jointed segments with taper and small pointed dactyls. Close the thorax/abdomen gap with an overlapping carapace edge rather than two abutting ovals.

rows.readsAs: an ant, or a generic long-legged bug
rows.defect: The defining mustRead — hugely enlarged folded hind jumping legs — is completely missing. Every leg is the same thin uniform-width polyline with a sharp angular kink; the hind leg is a bare stick 'Z' with no femur bulk whatsoever, so nothing about this animal says jumper. The body is three smooth spheres in a row (head, thorax, abdomen), each with its own hard outline, meeting at visible seams — an ant's construction, not a grasshopper's continuous tapering body. The single dark wing blade floats above and behind the thorax, overhanging the abdomen with no visible attachment point, and carries a straight ruled white line as its only detail. The head is a plain ball, not tall and flat-sided.
rows.fix: Give the hind legs a massive pear-shaped femur, roughly as deep as the thorax, folded in a tight inverted-V above a long thin spined tibia — that mass is the whole read. Replace the three spheres with one continuous form: tall flat-sided head, saddled pronotum sloping into a long tapering abdomen with segment ridges. Anchor the wings at the thorax and lay them flat along the back reaching the abdomen tip, as two long narrow overlapping panels with fine venation instead of one dark blade with a ruled line. Thicken and taper the front and middle legs and add tarsal feet.

rows.readsAs: a duckling or a generic cartoon waterbird
rows.defect: The checkerboard black-and-white back is absent — the back carries one flat dark crescent band pasted across the dome plus a pale lens patch scribbled with three or four straight white lines, which reads as a random highlight, not plumage. The other two mustReads do land (the straight dagger bill is held level, and the body sits low in the water), but the body is a short dome, aspect closer to 1.6 than the specified 3, so it lacks the long low cigar profile. The head is a perfect circle with a hard rim and the neck is a uniform-width tube whose outline crosses onto the body as a visible seam. The water is three perfect concentric ellipse outlines plus a flat elliptical shadow — machined primitives, not disturbed water.
rows.fix: Lay a real checkerboard over the back and folded wing: rows of crisp white rectangular spots on black, largest across the scapulars and shrinking toward the rump, following the body's curve; add a white-striped collar band on the neck. Lengthen the waterline body so the rear extends well behind the wing and the aspect reaches ~3, with the tail just breaking the surface. Taper the neck so it thickens into the shoulders with no crossing outline, and flatten the head crown with a slight forehead peak instead of a circle. Break the water rings into irregular ripple arcs of varying weight, cut where the body occludes them, and drop the free-floating drop shadow.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon Easter rabbit — a domestic bunny, the exact thing the reference note says it must not be
rows.defect: This is a fat Easter bunny, not a hare. The body is a single wide egg with a small egg head overlapped on it — measured silhouette is roughly 1.15 wide vs tall, nowhere near the specified 1.9, and there is nothing lean or angular about it. The mustRead 'very long black-tipped ears' fails: the ears are uniformly dark maroon from base to tip with a pink inner panel, so there is no tip contrast at all, and their bases vanish behind the head with no attachment — they float over the skull. The mustRead 'long rangy hind legs' fails outright: the hind limb is a short dark-maroon sausage and the foreleg a dark-maroon peg, both butt-joined to the pink body with a hard colour break and a visible seam, no fur transition. The haunch is a drawn crescent OUTLINE arc sitting on the flank rather than a form in the shading — a sprayed-on line. A bright hard rim-light stroke traces the whole body/head overlap, printing the seam where the head ball meets the shoulder. Teeth are two white rectangles with square corners; whiskers are four perfectly straight rulered lines.
rows.fix: Rebuild as one continuous body mass: stretch the torso to ~1.9 aspect, drop the chest, and pull the hind limb out as a long tapering thigh-hock-foot chain that grows from the rump silhouette (shared contour, no butt-join, no colour break at the junction). Delete the crescent haunch outline and read the haunch out of shading only. Paint the last ~25% of each ear as a near-black tip, and anchor the ear bases into the skull with a widening fillet. Replace the rectangle incisors with two soft chisel wedges and give the whiskers a curve and a taper.

rows.readsAs: A blue jay or a crested blue quail — a generic perching songbird
rows.defect: All three mustReads fail. 'Split double crest raised on the grey head': the crest is a ragged spray of about six thin filament strokes, not two raised horns, and the head is the same blue as the body with no pale/grey mask. 'Enormous grey talons thicker than a human finger': the feet are hair-thin yellow stick toes, three forward, identical to a songbird's — no thickness, no scaling, no curve, no talons. 'Black chest band over a white belly': the body is one flat blue gradient, no band, no white. The beak is a small yellow triangular wedge with no hook and no cere. Construction defects on top of that: the wing is a lens shape pasted on the flank with a hard dark outline that crosses the body silhouette on the left, and the head is a separate ball with a dark curved seam arc printed where it overlaps the shoulder. Body reads wider than tall (~1.1) against a specified 0.85 upright.
rows.fix: Give it a raptor head: hook the beak down over the mandible tip and add a distinct yellow-grey cere block at the base; lighten the whole head and nape to pale grey. Replace the filament spray with two thick tapered crest feathers splitting into a V. Rebuild the feet at 3-4x current stroke width with visible scute banding and hooked black talons that curl past the perch line. Add the black chest band and white belly as skin regions in the body shader. Fold the wing as a shape that shares the back contour instead of a hard-outlined lens on the flank, and dissolve the neck seam.

rows.readsAs: A pink two-lobed spider or a tick
rows.defect: The single most important mustRead — 'single pea-like body with no waist' — is directly contradicted: this is TWO near-perfect spheres with a pronounced pinched waist between them, and the front sphere's overlap is printed as a bright hard crescent seam. That is a spider's cephalothorax-plus-abdomen, exactly what the note says it is not. 'Tiny eye turret on top of body' also fails: there are four flat black dots in a 2x2 grid airbrushed onto the FRONT face of the head sphere, no raised ocularium, and four eyes reads as spider, not harvestman (which has two on a turret). The eight legs are present and count correctly, but they are constant-width rulered polylines with one sharp machined knee, no taper, no foot, and they terminate in mid-air well above the ground shadow — several run straight off the frame edge. They are also only about 2.5x body length, not 'many times'. No leg attaches visibly: the joins are hidden under the sphere edges.
rows.fix: Collapse the two spheres into one slightly ovoid body with no waist and no seam crescent, then break the perfect-circle silhouette with a subtle dorsal saddle. Move the eyes to a small raised bump on TOP of the body, two eyes facing outward on opposite sides of the turret. Rebuild the legs at 3-4x current length with a taper from a thick coxa to a hair-fine tarsus, at least three joints each, curving up over the body and back down to touch the ground plane where the shadow sits, and blend each coxa into the body with a fillet so the attachment is visible.

rows.readsAs: A pigeon or a white dove
rows.defect: This is the same body kit as Harpy Eagle and Heron in this batch, re-coloured pale blue-white, and it reads as a dove. All three mustReads fail. 'Hooked raptor beak with yellow cere': the beak is a small straight yellow wedge, no hook, no cere block. 'Heavy scaled feet with curved talons': thin yellow stick toes, unscaled, no talons, no grip. 'Broad rounded wings folded over the back': the wing is a bright white lens with a hard grey outline stuck on the FLANK, and its outline runs off the body silhouette on the left edge — pasted on, not folded over the back. Proportion is also wrong: the silhouette is a wide fat oval about 1.15 wide vs tall against a specified 0.75, and the body sits level rather than at the steep perched buteo angle the note calls for. The head is a ball with a dark curved seam printed where it meets the shoulder.
rows.fix: Steepen the perched axis so the breast is forward and the tail drops behind, and narrow the body to ~0.75 aspect. Hook the beak with a real cere. Thicken the tarsi, add scute banding and four heavy curved talons. Re-cut the wing so its upper edge IS the back contour with the primaries crossing over the tail base, and delete the hard outline stroke. Add red-tail buteo cues — a dark belly band and a warm rufous tail — so it stops reading as a dove.

rows.readsAs: A pink cartoon cat or mouse with straw stuck in its shoulder
rows.defect: The mustRead 'dense cape of spines over the back' fails: the spines are a bale of pale straw strokes clustered on the SHOULDER only, spraying backwards and horizontally past the silhouette into empty space, while the entire rump and lower back are bare pink. It reads as hay stuck to the animal, not as its own coat. 'Pointed pink snout poking out in front' also fails — the face is a round ball with a soft rounded muzzle and, worse, two pointed triangular CAT EARS on top of the skull. The body/head/limb kit is identical to the Hare in this batch: same crescent haunch outline arc drawn on the flank, same dark peg limbs butt-joined with a hard colour break, same two white rectangle teeth, same four straight rulered whiskers.
rows.fix: Replace the shoulder tuft with a spine field that covers the whole dorsal surface from the crown of the head back over the rump, quills short and dense and following the body curve, with a clean spine/bare-skin boundary line low on the flank — no quills projecting outside the silhouette. Swap the cat ears for small low rounded ears half-buried in the spine cape. Extend the face into a long narrow cone snout with a dark nose leather at the tip. Delete the haunch outline and the rectangle teeth, and grow the feet out of the body instead of pegging them on.

rows.readsAs: A blue tick or spider standing next to a cinnamon roll
rows.defect: The spiral shell is present and legible, which is the one thing that lands — but it is a perfectly flat 2D disc pasted BEHIND the body with no volume and no aperture, and the abdomen never enters it; the blue body just sits in front of it. The mustRead 'one enlarged claw that plugs the shell mouth' fails: both claws are the same size, same teardrop shape, mirrored left and right, and neither is anywhere near the shell mouth. 'Two pairs of antennae' fails: I can find only the two eyestalks (hair-thin straight black lines with a white dot on top) and no antennae at all. The walking legs are dark navy rulered polylines with square butt ends floating in mid-air below the body, no feet, no taper — the left pair forms a literal rectangular ladder with a straight rung across it. The body is a near-perfect circle with soft grey spots airbrushed on top of the gradient rather than sitting in the skin, and a hard bright rim outline traces the whole circle.
rows.fix: Enlarge the right claw to roughly double the left, thicken its manus and set it across the shell aperture so it plainly plugs it. Give the shell a three-dimensional cone with a visible dark aperture and tuck the rear of the body into that opening so the two shapes interlock instead of overlapping. Add two pairs of antennae — a long thin pair and a short feathered pair — from the front margin. Rebuild the legs as tapering multi-jointed chains with pointed dactyls that reach the ground plane, joined to the body with a fillet. Break the circular carapace silhouette and push the spot pattern into the shading so it curves with the shell.

rows.readsAs: A sandpiper or a plover — a neckless short wading chick
rows.defect: The defining mustRead — 'long neck kinked into an S' — is entirely absent. The head ball sits directly against the shoulder mass with a hard overlap seam and there is no neck of any length, straight or kinked. Without it this is not a heron at any distance. The dagger bill is good (long, straight, tapered) and the stilt legs are good, but the toes are two small forward stubs rather than long trailing toes. Everything else is the shared bird kit from Hawk and Harpy Eagle in this batch: same ball body, same lens wing with a hard grey outline pasted on the flank whose stroke crosses the silhouette, same short pointed tail wedge. Head fraction reads about 0.2 against a specified 0.3.
rows.fix: Build a real neck: a long tapering column, roughly 1.5x the body height, folded into the resting S with the kink at the third vertebra so the head sits back over the shoulders — and blend the base of the neck into the chest and back contours so there is no seam ring. Lengthen the toes into three long forward digits plus a hind toe that trail on the ground. Grey the body, add the black eye stripe and the loose breast plumes, and re-cut the wing to share the back contour instead of being an outlined lens on the flank.

rows.readsAs: A generic blue baitfish or sardine — close enough to pass as a herring, but the mouthless pointed snout is the giveaway
rows.defect: This is the strongest render in the batch and it does read as a fish, but the body is a pure geometric lens — two circular arcs meeting at hard points at the snout and the tail peduncle — so the silhouette is a primitive rather than a body. The pectoral fin is a flat isosceles TRIANGLE with three straight machined edges pasted on the flank. Two mustRead sub-features are missing: the belly is a smooth convex arc with no keel or scute serration, and there is no mouth or upturned jaw drawn anywhere — the head simply ends in a point. The eye is large and prominent, but it is placed right at the very tip of the snout, forward of the gill line, which is where a mouth should be. Aspect measures around 3.0 against a specified 4.2, so it is noticeably deeper-bodied than a herring. The lateral line is a dead-straight stroke and the tail attaches at a hard pinch with a visible notch.
rows.fix: Slim the body to ~4.2 and replace the arc-on-arc lens with an asymmetric profile: deepest just behind the head, tapering to a slender peduncle. Cut the ventral edge into a shallow keel with a fine sawtooth of scutes from throat to vent. Draw the mouth as an oblique upturned slit with the lower jaw projecting past the upper, and slide the eye back behind it onto the cheek. Replace the triangle pectoral with a soft fan of rays whose base is buried under the operculum. Curve the lateral line and blend the tail root so the peduncle flows into the fin instead of pinching.

rows.readsAs: A small tamarin/monkey — and specifically the same animal as the Monkey render in this very batch (identical egg torso, identical squat, identical uniform-tube tail, identical dark limb lumps); the only difference is the head ruff.
rows.defect: Two of three mustReads are absent. The tail is a plain uniform-width teal tube with NO banding whatsoever, and it does not grow out of the rump — it starts as a stroke laid on the left flank at mid-body height, with a visible hard join where the tube meets the torso. The animal is squatting flat on a ground shadow, not clinging upright to bark; there is no bark, trunk or grip anywhere in the frame. The ear tufts read as a continuous dark-teal curly afro/mane ringing the entire head (a fringe of small blobs all the way round from cheek to cheek), not as two white fan-shaped tufts flanking the ears — and they are not white, they are the same teal as the body plus a thin pale rim, so they read as hair volume, not as the marmoset's signature. Arms are invisible: the torso is a smooth teal egg with two dark rounded lumps at the bottom front doing duty as hands/feet, no shoulder, elbow or digit anywhere. Body blotches are soft grey ovals that sit on top of the surface like airbrushed decals rather than pelage. Silhouette is essentially a capsule with a head on top.
rows.fix: Regrow the tail from the rump as a tapering, slightly curving cone that begins inside the body mass (no start-cap seam), and paint 8-12 alternating dark/light bands as chevron rings that wrap the taper rather than as flat stripes. Replace the all-round ruff with two discrete white fan tufts anchored at the ear positions only, keeping the crown fur short and dark. Add a vertical bark substrate and rotate the pose to an upright cling: forelimbs extended and hooked onto the trunk, hind feet gripping below, tail hanging free. Build actual forelimbs with a shoulder mass, forearm and separated digits instead of the two front lumps.

rows.readsAs: A rabbit or a guinea pig — the pointed ears, whiskers and buck-tooth block push it to lagomorph, and nothing about it says marmot.
rows.defect: Missing mustRead: there is no tail at all — the rear of the body ends in a bare smooth curve, no short furry stub. Missing mustRead: 'blunt rounded head with small ears' — the ears are two tall, dark, sharply pointed triangles standing well clear of the skull, reading rabbit/cat, and the head is not distinguishable as a head at all, it is just the right-hand end of the egg with a face painted on. The quadruped posture is unreadable: I count two small dark nubs under the belly, not four limbs. The buck teeth are a literal WHITE RECTANGLE with straight machined edges and a hard vertical divider line — a pure geometric primitive stuck onto the muzzle. Whiskers are three perfectly straight hairline strokes fanning off the face with no follicle base. A hard crescent seam arcs across the flank (the haunch line) and reads as a drawn contour on top of the body, not as a muscle boundary. Aspect measures roughly 1.5, not the specified 2 — the animal is too tall and round, more egg than barrel.
rows.fix: Replace the rectangular incisor block with two small rounded chisel-shaped teeth whose top edges disappear under the lip. Swap the pointed triangular ears for small, low, rounded ear discs set close against the skull. Add a short conical furry tail growing from the rump silhouette. Model four short legs — two visible near-side limbs with a foot each, plus offside limbs suggested behind — rather than two nubs. Stretch the body to aspect ~2.0 and lower the back so the profile is squat rather than egg-shaped, and dissolve the flank crescent into a soft value shift instead of a line.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon dragonfly, or a bead-and-string bug toy — nothing in it says mayfly without the filaments or the upright sail wings.
rows.defect: Missing mustRead: there are ZERO tail filaments — the abdomen simply stops at the last bead. Missing mustRead: the wings are not triangular and not held upright over the back; they are two flat, back-swept, feather-like blades lying horizontally behind the thorax at the same height as the body, with visible straight rib lines, so they read as fletching or dragonfly wings, and they butt-joint against the first bead with a visible seam. Missing mustRead: the abdomen is not slender or upcurved — it is a chain of five DISCRETE PERFECT CIRCLES (separate green balls, each with its own highlight, dark gaps between them) strung in a straight horizontal line. Beads on a wire, not a body. Legs are four identical small hooked strokes clustered under the head, all the same length and curve, stamped rather than grown. The head is a sphere with two large black spheres for eyes.
rows.fix: Replace the bead chain with a single continuous tapering abdomen that curves upward at the rear, with segment boundaries rendered as soft ring creases in one surface rather than gaps between separate circles. Add two or three hair-thin filaments at least as long as the abdomen trailing from the tip. Rebuild the wings as two large triangles held vertically and pressed together above the thorax, with translucent venation, rooted into the thorax mass so no seam shows. Differentiate the leg pairs in length and angle, with longer forelegs reaching forward.

rows.readsAs: A curled centipede, or a string of white pearls with pins pushed into it — the splayed needle legs actively read as the wrong myriapod.
rows.defect: Missing mustRead: 'two pairs of short legs per segment in a rippling fringe' is not what is drawn. The legs are sparse, long, straight, needle-thin spikes splaying radially OUTWARD well clear of the body — roughly one thin spike per two segments — sticking out sideways exactly like a centipede's splayed legs, which the reference note explicitly says to avoid. They are perfectly straight machined pins with no joints. Missing mustRead: 'cylindrical tube body of many identical rings' — the body is a string of PERFECT SPHERES, each bead with its own specular highlight and a dark crevice between it and the next, so it reads as a pearl necklace rather than a ringed cylinder. The antennae are not short clubs: they are two long thin wires that arc up and over the head into a closed loop/halo, which reads as a wire artifact rather than anatomy. The C-curl pose leaves several beads on the upper arc with no legs at all. The bone-white value is uniformly flat with no chitin sheen along the length.
rows.fix: Convert the bead chain into a continuous cylindrical tube with ring segmentation cut as shallow grooves in one surface. Replace the sparse pins with a dense fringe of many short, jointed legs tucked close under the body so only the tips show below the silhouette, two pairs per ring, phase-offset for the metachronal ripple. Replace the looping antennae with two short forward-pointing club-tipped antennae no longer than the head. Add banded value variation so the tube reads as chitin.

rows.readsAs: A generic small silvery river fish — sardine, dace or minnow. This one would pass unlabelled.
rows.defect: MISSING mustRead: there is no dark lateral stripe. The flank carries only a faint translucent triangular patch mid-body and a soft midline value change; nothing reads as a band. The body is saturated green rather than silvery, so 'small slim silvery body' also lands weakly. The dorsal fin is present but is a flat dark blob with no ray structure and it sits well behind mid-back, roughly two-thirds along. There is a faint hard line at the caudal peduncle where the tail fin butts into the body. No pelvic or anal fin, and the dark wedge behind the gill line is ambiguous as a pectoral. Otherwise this is the strongest render in the batch: correct fusiform lens shape, correct aspect (~3.5), a properly forked caudal fin, and a seamless head-to-body transition with a credible gill line.
rows.fix: Paint a dark lateral stripe from behind the eye to the tail base, following the body's curvature and fading into the belly countershading rather than sitting as a straight overlay bar. Cool the flank toward silver with a warm-dark dorsal and pale belly. Move the dorsal fin forward to mid-back and give it soft ray structure with a base that melts into the dorsal ridge. Blend the caudal peduncle so no join line shows, and add small pelvic and anal fins.

rows.readsAs: A spider or a tick — four eyes, a waist and long splayed legs put it firmly in arachnid-with-a-head territory, not a mite.
rows.defect: This contradicts almost every line of its reference. The reference demands a featureless bag-like UNSEGMENTED body with no waist, no separate head, no visible eyes; what is drawn is two distinct orange SPHERES joined at a pinched waist — a clear cephalothorax plus abdomen — with FOUR black eyes in a 2x2 grid painted on the front sphere. Missing mustRead: the legs are not 'eight short legs bunched at the front'; I count six visible legs, they are long straight tapered sticks, and they are spread front AND rear (two reach forward from the front ball, the rest splay down and back from the rear ball), giving a wide spider stance. Missing mustRead: no mouth cone anywhere. Two sharp triangular points sit on top of the rear sphere and read as cat ears — off-body decoration with no anatomical justification. Both body masses are perfect circles with mirrored highlights, and every leg meets the body as a hard butt-end against the sphere edge.
rows.fix: Collapse the two spheres into a single soft irregular unsegmented bag with no waist, and break the outline so it is not a circle. Delete all four eyes and the two triangular points on the abdomen. Move all eight legs to the front third, shorten them to about a third of body length, thicken them, and root them into the body wall with a fleshy coxa so no butt-join shows. Add a small protruding gnathosoma/mouth cone at the front. Velvet-mite fur texture would sell the bag body.

rows.readsAs: A newt or salamander, or a small plesiosaur toy — smooth skin, tube tail, two stub legs and no neck read amphibian, not varanid.
rows.defect: Missing mustRead: no tongue at all, let alone a long deeply forked one — the mouth is a single straight horizontal line. Missing mustRead: no claws and no muscular sprawled limbs. Only TWO limbs are visible and they are plain dark cylinders of constant width pointing down-and-out, ending in blunt rounded caps with no foot, no toes, no claws; each meets the torso at a hard visible seam where the cylinder overlaps the body oval. Missing mustRead: the tail is not laterally flattened — it is a fat uniform-diameter tube with a rounded blunt tip and a dark stripe along it, and there is a straight cut line where it joins the body. The reference note calls for a long snake-like neck; there is NO neck — the head is a second oval simply overlapped onto the body oval with the join arc plainly visible across the shoulder. The dark spots are soft blobs sprayed on a flat grey surface with no scale texture beneath. The overall silhouette is two flat lens shapes plus a hose.
rows.fix: Root the head on a long muscular tapering neck that grows continuously out of the shoulder mass so no overlap arc remains. Flatten the tail laterally — deep top-to-bottom, thin side-to-side, low dorsal keel, tapering to a point instead of a rounded cap. Rebuild all four limbs in a true sprawl (humerus out to the side, forearm down, splayed five-toed foot with long hooked claws) and blend shoulder and hip into the torso. Add a long forked tongue flicking from the mouth. Replace the sprayed spots with an ocellated scale pattern that follows body curvature over visible skin granulation.

rows.readsAs: A generic cartoon monkey — and indistinguishable from the Marmoset render in this batch apart from that one's face-ringing ruff.
rows.defect: Missing mustRead: the tail is not as long as the body — it is roughly half the torso length, a uniform-width teal tube that starts abruptly on the left flank at mid-body with a visible hard join, so it reads as a handle stuck on rather than a tail growing from the rump. Missing mustRead: no grasping hands or feet and no thumbs — the limbs are four dark rounded lumps (two at the chest, two at the base) with no arm, wrist or digit anywhere. The posture is a hunched upright squat, not the specified quadruped. The torso is a smooth teal egg/capsule with soft grey blotches airbrushed on top and no chest, shoulder or rib structure. The head is a small dome carrying a lighter cap band that reads as a painted stripe, sitting on the torso with a faint seam and no neck. The one mustRead that lands is the flat forward-facing face with large round white eyes. Critically, this is near-identical to the Marmoset in the same batch — same egg torso, same squat, same tube tail, same limb lumps — differing only in the head ruff.
rows.fix: Extend the tail to full body length, taper it, and grow it out of the rump so the base sits inside the body silhouette. Build real limbs: arm with shoulder, elbow, forearm and a hand with four fingers plus an opposable thumb, and a foot with a grasping hallux, with the hands visibly contacting the ground. Reset the pose to a quadruped stance on all fours with a roughly level back. Break the egg silhouette with chest and shoulder mass. Differentiate the head from the Marmoset with a projecting muzzle and short flat crown fur instead of the painted cap band.

rows.readsAs: a squashed olive toad or a generic frog blob — nobody would say 'poison dart frog'
rows.defect: The single mustRead that defines this animal — bold contrasting warning blotches on vivid colour — is entirely absent. The body is one flat mustard-olive tone from nose to rump with no marking of any kind, so nothing on it says 'aposematic'. The only dark shapes are the two eye patches and a smudged saddle under them that reads as a bruise, not a pattern. Worse, the left hind limb is a thin flat quadrilateral wedge with two dead-straight machined edges pasted against the flank — it is a polygon laid over the body, not a leg growing out of it, and there is a hard line where it meets the torso. The two tiny nubs under the right belly are the only other limbs, far too short and stuck on as separate pills. Overall silhouette is a smooth rounded blob/capsule with no amphibian crouch.
rows.fix: Give the skin its own 2–3 colour aposematic scheme painted into the body gradient (e.g. cobalt-blue limbs against a lemon-yellow dorsum, or black blotches over orange) so the pattern wraps with the form rather than sitting flat. Rebuild both hind limbs as tapered curved masses that share the torso's fill and silhouette-merge at the hip (no straight-edge polygon, no seam line); bring the folded thigh up alongside the body in the sprawling crouch. Raise the head slightly so the blunt snout reads as a snout and not as the front of an egg.

rows.readsAs: a generic orange aquarium fish, closest to a trout or goldfish
rows.defect: Fin count fails the mustRead: I count two rounded dorsal lobes and one ventral lobe, not three dorsals and two anals, and the lobes are soft brown humps rather than distinct separate fins with rays. The lower jaw does not protrude — the snout closes to a single sharp point with the mouth line running straight to the tip, so the diagnostic pollock underbite is missing. Colour is warm orange-tan, not olive-green. The pectoral is a flat translucent triangle sprayed over the flank with a visible hard edge, clearly a decal rather than a fin rooted in a shoulder. The eye is a perfect white circle with a black dot — a machined primitive, cartoon-sticker in feel. The body is a pointed lens/leaf shape that comes to sharp corners at both ends. The pale lateral line is present and correct, the one mustRead that lands.
rows.fix: Split the dorsal mass into three discrete fins along the back (short first, longer second, tapering third) and two anals below, each with faint ray striation. Extend the lower jaw past the upper so the mouth line ends in a visible underbite. Reflow the base colour to olive-green over the dorsum fading to silver-white ventrally, keeping the existing lateral line as the boundary. Replace the circular eye with a slightly ovoid iris set into an orbital socket shaded from the head fill. Round the caudal peduncle so the tail joins through a narrowing rather than a corner.

rows.readsAs: a bright green caterpillar or a centipede
rows.defect: Two mustReads are missing outright. There are no paddle lobes (parapodia) — the bristles spring straight out of the smooth body wall, so the segments have no lateral projections at all. And the head is a featureless green ball with a single dot eye: no palps, no antennae, no eversible proboscis, nothing that distinguishes front from back except the dot. The chaetae themselves are pin-straight uniform needles of nearly identical length, evenly spaced, drawn as hairlines — machined bristles, not organic ones, and they read as spray applied over the outline. The segment ridges are a stack of crescent scallops that look like a drawn overlay on a smooth tube rather than the tube's own annulation. Colour is a flat highlighter green with no dorsal/ventral difference.
rows.fix: Add a paired parapodial lobe on every segment — a small fleshy paddle bulging out of the body wall in the body's own colour — and root each chaetal bundle in that lobe so the bristles fan from a base instead of piercing the outline. Vary bristle length, curvature and angle per segment. Build a real prostomium: two or four antennae, a pair of long palps, and a hint of the everted proboscis with jaw tips at the very front. Shade the ventral side darker and let the segment boundaries be pinches in the body silhouette, not drawn crescents.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon tortoise, or at a glance a red beetle with a striped shell
rows.defect: The head is a detached salmon ellipse floating alongside the shell with no neck whatsoever — you can see it overlap the carapace edge as a separate shape. That fails the 'head extended forward on a wrinkled neck' mustRead and is a textbook stuck-on part. The two legs are likewise separate dark brown lozenges hanging below the shell with clear air/seam between them and the body; there are no feet at all, so 'webbed clawed feet' is missing too. The shell is a near-perfect semicircle with a dead-straight horizontal bottom edge and concentric arc lines radiating from a point — that is a sliced-orange geometric primitive, not a scute mosaic; real scutes are polygonal plates (vertebral, costal, marginal), not nested arcs. Only two limbs are visible for a quadruped. Shell is also high-domed, contradicting the note's low streamlined slider profile.
rows.fix: Grow a neck: a wrinkled tapering column emerging from under the front shell lip, with the head continuous with it in fill and outline. Replace the concentric arcs with an actual scute layout — a central row of vertebrals flanked by costals, edged by a marginal band, each plate a slightly irregular polygon with its own growth rings. Flatten the dome and let the carapace rim curve, replacing the straight bottom edge with a plastron seam. Add four limbs, each with a splayed webbed foot and visible claws, joined to the body under the shell rather than dangling.

rows.readsAs: a green hedgehog, or a cartoon sea-urchin-mouse hybrid
rows.defect: The quills are wrong in placement, form and colour. They erupt from a patch on the shoulders and mid-back and point up and forward — the mustRead calls for long quills laid back over the rump, and the rump here is completely bare. They are dead-straight pale sticks of uniform width, several with visibly flat rectangular tips, and there is a distinct dark arc line across the shoulder marking where the quill patch begins — a seam between 'quill zone' and 'body'. No banding on any quill. The body is a green sphere; a porcupine should be brownish-grey and low-slung, and the green makes it read as an amphibian. The eye is a perfect circle, the mouth is a small hard white rectangle, and the whiskers are straight hairlines — all machined primitives. Legs are two tiny dark nubs stuck under the sphere with no shoulder or haunch. Tail is not readable as a short quilled tail.
rows.fix: Lay the quill field back along the spine so it is longest and densest over the hips and tapers forward to a low crest on the neck, with quills following the back's curve rather than radiating from a hub. Band each quill light/dark/light along its length, taper the tips to points, and vary length and splay. Dissolve the shoulder arc so the quills emerge through the fur gradient rather than out of a bounded patch. Recolour to dark brown-grey with a paler quill contrast. Replace the circular eye and rectangular mouth with organic forms and rebuild the legs as stubby columns with haunch mass merging into the torso.

rows.readsAs: a bloated dolphin or a beluga; the belly reads almost manatee
rows.defect: The dorsal fin is a separate rounded triangle sitting on the back with its own complete pink outline all the way around its base — there is a visible seam and a slight gap where it meets the body, so it reads as a shape parked on top rather than a fin rising out of the spine. The pectoral is likewise a dark hook that starts below the belly line with no shoulder attachment. A bright pink-magenta rim stroke runs around the whole animal; on a porpoise this reads as neon sticker outlining, not as a lit edge. Two soft dark ovals sit on the flank like sprayed stains with no anatomical justification. The belly is grossly bulbous and drops well below the tail stock, making the animal look bloated rather than 'stocky short body'. The blunt beakless head and the low triangular fin shape are otherwise correct — the fin's form is right, its attachment is not.
rows.fix: Fuse the dorsal fin into the dorsal line: no outline across the base, the fin's fill continuing the back's gradient, with a subtle fairing where it rises. Same for the pectoral — root it in a shoulder bulge behind the head. Drop the magenta rim to a narrow cool highlight only on the upper lit edge. Remove the two flank blotches or replace them with a soft counter-shading transition to the pale belly. Reduce the belly bulge and raise the ventral line so the body tapers evenly into the caudal peduncle.

rows.readsAs: a jellyfish — an ordinary blue moon jelly
rows.defect: This is the exact failure the note warns against: it reads as a jellyfish with a bell. The float is a smooth near-perfect slate-blue ellipse with a flat underside, and the only nod to a sail is a thin pale hairline arc laid across the top — a single stroke sitting on the surface, not a crimped, pleated crest growing out of the pneumatophore. There is no crimping, no pink-violet iridescence (colour is a dull grey-blue), and no asymmetric S-curve to the float. The tentacles are uniform thin teal lines all terminating within the same narrow band, so there is no 'extremely long' trailing curtain and no distinction between the short dactylozooids and the long fishing tentacles. Where the tentacles meet the float they simply start at the flat underside edge, giving a hard boundary line across the bottom.
rows.fix: Rebuild the float as an asymmetric elongated gas bladder with a tall pleated sail crest growing off its top ridge — the crest should be a scalloped, translucent fin with visible crimps, continuous with the float body. Shift the palette to translucent blue-violet with pink at the crest and along the lower margin. Extend the longest tentacles far past the current band, to two or three float-lengths, with wide variation in length and a coiled/kinked quality; cluster a dense polyp mass right under the float so the tentacles emerge from tissue instead of from a flat edge.

rows.readsAs: a hamster, or with those ears a chubby rabbit
rows.defect: The ears fail the mustRead: instead of small rounded ears flat to the head, there are two erect pointed dark triangles standing straight up off the crown, which immediately pushes the animal toward rabbit/hare. No stubby tail is legible at all — the only rear protrusions are two dark foot nubs. A conspicuous darker swirl/whorl spirals across the flank; it does not follow any muscle or fur direction and reads as a sprayed-on decal over the golden body. The mouth is a hard white rectangle (a machined primitive), the eye is a perfect circle, and the whiskers are three straight hairlines. The limbs are two dark pills stuck under the body with no shoulder or haunch mass, and the silhouette is otherwise a plain rounded blob with no neck or cheek definition. Plump cylindrical body is the one mustRead that lands.
rows.fix: Replace the pointed triangles with small low rounded ears set close against the skull, barely breaking the head outline. Add a short stubby tail at the rump — a thick tuft no longer than a third of the head. Delete the flank swirl and let the fur read through directional shading from the dorsum to a paler belly. Turn the white rectangle into a soft muzzle with incisors implied rather than a block, and give the eye an ovoid iris in an orbital shadow. Rebuild the legs with visible haunch and shoulder volume merging into the torso, front paws tucked as prairie dogs sit.

rows.readsAs: a lemon or an egg yolk with spider legs
rows.defect: The carapace is a near-perfect CIRCLE with a soft airbrush gradient and blurry dark spots sprayed on top - not a broad flattened fan-shaped crab shell (no anterolateral margin, no eye orbits, no front edge, no abdomen). All eight legs are thin brown STICKS of uniform width with sharp machined elbow bends; two of them are stray rods lying flat ACROSS the front of the carapace, connected to nothing - off-body artifacts. The rear legs end in thin points, so the mustRead 'flattened paddle-tipped rear legs' is entirely absent. The claws are two smooth pale EGG shapes with a thin brown wire loop drawn over them - no pincer gap, no dactyl, no crusher mass, and they are equal in size, so 'heavy unequal crusher claws' also fails. Eyes are two hairline stalks each capped by a single white pixel.
rows.fix: Replace the circular body with a wide low fan carapace (aspect ~1.7 wide, front margin toothed, rear tapering, eye notches at the leading edge). Rebuild claws as two-part pincers with a visible gap between propodus and dactyl, and make the right claw ~1.6x the left. Give the rearmost leg pair a flattened oval paddy dactyl. Delete the two rods drawn over the carapace and root every leg in a coxa lump that swells out of the shell margin instead of butting against it.

rows.readsAs: a generic pale minnow-shaped fish; nothing identifies it as a mudminnow
rows.defect: The snout is a SHARP point - the body is a symmetrical lens/almond pointed at both ends - so the mustRead 'blunt rounded snout with an upturned mouth' fails outright (there is no mouth drawn at all). The dorsal fin is a grey slab with a straight top edge and straight vertical ray lines laid ON the back like a separate plate, and it sits forward of centre, not 'far back close to the tail'. The caudal fin is a distinct grey square-ish fan butted against the body with a visible dark boundary and a small gap - a hard seam where fin meets body. A small triangular striped fan floats free in the middle of the white flank, touching no edge of the body.
rows.fix: Blunt the anterior: round the snout into a short dome and add an upturned terminal mouth slit. Slide the dorsal fin back so its origin sits at ~0.75 body length, directly above the anal fin. Fair the caudal peduncle into the tail fin - taper the body into the fin base so there is no boundary line or gap. Re-anchor the floating mid-flank fan to the ventral edge as a pectoral, or delete it.

rows.readsAs: a yellow cartoon submarine or a slug with googly eyes
rows.defect: Best read in the batch - eyes on top, out of water on mud, two dorsals - but the mustRead 'arm-like pectoral fins propping the body up' fails: there is ONE scallop-shaped fan DANGLING below the belly, supporting nothing; the body lies flat on the mud. The torso is a flat SLAB with near-parallel straight top and bottom edges, and where the tail joins there is a literal square vertical STEP in the outline (~20px drop) - a machined seam. Thin white fin rays extend ABOVE both dorsal tabs into empty black space, unattached to any fin membrane. The eyes are two perfect yellow circles with black pupils sitting on the snout like glued-on goggles. The mud mound is a perfect ellipse.
rows.fix: Rotate the pectorals forward and downward into two muscular arm-like props that lift the front of the body clear of the mud, with the body angled head-up. Curve the dorsal and ventral profiles so the torso is a tapering cylinder, not a slab, and blend the caudal peduncle into the tail to remove the square step. Clip the fin rays to the fin membrane. Sink the eye turrets into paired bony sockets that bulge out of the skull rather than drawing free-standing discs. Break the mud ellipse with an irregular edge.

rows.readsAs: a generic green torpedo fish - a mackerel or a small tuna, not a mullet
rows.defect: Head is a sharp cone tapering to a needle point - the mustRead 'blunt flat-topped head with a tiny triangular mouth' fails (no mouth is drawn). 'Faint stripes' are absent; the flank is a flat green gradient with a single dead-straight machined light line running its whole length. The two dorsal fins are DARKER than the body and sit behind the dorsal outline, so they read as shadow blobs floating behind the fish, not fins rising off the spine; the same dark blob is mirrored under the belly. A striped triangular fan floats free in the middle of the flank, touching no body edge. The caudal fin is a separate darker triangle butted to the body along a hard straight seam. The eye is a perfect white ring circle with a black dot, planted almost on the tip of the snout.
rows.fix: Flatten and blunt the head - square the top of the skull, shorten the snout, add the small triangular terminal mouth. Draw both dorsals in body colour or lighter and root them in the dorsal contour so they interrupt the silhouette. Move the floating fan down to the pectoral position on the ventral flank. Taper the peduncle into the caudal so there is no seam. Move the eye back behind the mouth by ~8% of body length and replace the ring with a soft-edged eye set in an orbit. Add 5-6 faint horizontal scale-row stripes.

rows.readsAs: a scallop shell, or a paper hand fan
rows.defect: This is not a mussel - it is a SCALLOP. The shell is a wide fan with straight dark ribs radiating from a point at the BOTTOM centre and the widest, straight hinge edge at the TOP, which is the inverse of the mustRead 'wedge-shaped hinged shell narrow at the hinge end'. Colour is bright orange, not 'dark blue-black glossy'. Growth lines (concentric, perpendicular to the ribs) are completely absent - the ribs are straight lines drawn on a flat orange gradient, a sprayed-on pattern with no shell relief. The byssal beard is represented by two brown TRAPEZOIDS with perfectly straight machined edges sitting under the shell like little plinths - no threads. A few stray dark hairlines poke past the top edge at both corners. The overall silhouette is a rounded square.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette as an elongated teardrop wedge: narrow pointed umbo at one end, broad rounded margin at the other, aspect ~1.8 along that axis. Delete the radial ribs entirely and replace with concentric growth lines parallel to the margin. Recolour to blue-black with a violet specular sheen. Replace the two trapezoids with a spray of fine curved byssal filaments emerging from a gape near the umbo. Remove the stray hairlines outside the shell outline.

rows.readsAs: a green beluga or a small pilot whale - no viewer would say narwhal
rows.defect: THE TUSK IS MISSING. Magnified 4x at the head there is no tusk of any kind - the thin grey line I first took for one is a rim-light stroke hugging the dorsal contour, running up and BACKWARD over the skull, and nothing projects forward from the snout. The defining feature of the species is absent, so the primary mustRead fails, as does the note about left-jaw placement. The head is also a pointed beak rather than the required 'blunt rounded head'. The body is a flat bright-green gradient with no mottling. The pectoral flipper is a flat dark-green ellipse laid over the flank with a hard edge and no shoulder - a part stuck on, not grown out.
rows.fix: Add the tusk: a long forward-projecting spiral emerging from the LEFT upper jaw, offset from the midline, length ~0.5 of body length, with a visible helical twist and a tapering ivory tip. Round the rostrum into a blunt melon-shaped forehead. Add grey-white mottling patches over the dorsal surface. Root the flipper in a shoulder mass that swells out of the body wall and taper its trailing edge.

rows.readsAs: a coiled millipede, or a green pinecone spiral
rows.defect: Three mustReads fail at once. There are NO tentacles - the only appendage is a single flat dark-green ELLIPSE sitting at the lower right, detached from the shell aperture, hard-edged and untextured. There is no leathery hood. There are no red-brown flame stripes; the shell is uniform green. The coil itself is built from dozens of identical repeated bumpy lozenges, so it reads as a coiled segmented arthropod rather than a smooth chambered shell. Worst, a thin white PERFECT CIRCLE arc is drawn across the whole shell and continues off the shell into empty black space at the bottom right and top - a machined geometric primitive floating over the art.
rows.fix: Delete the white circle overlay. Smooth the coil into a continuous logarithmic spiral with a clean rolled whorl surface, and paint radial red-brown flame bands that fade toward the umbilicus. Replace the ellipse blob with a dense fan of 40+ short slender suckerless tentacles spilling out of the aperture, and cap the head with a wrinkled leathery hood folded over them. Add a pinhole eye with no lens at the base of the tentacle crown.

rows.readsAs: a red cartoon worm with two toothpick legs, or an axolotl toy
rows.defect: The tail is a fat ROUND hose of near-constant diameter that curves up and left and just stops - not 'laterally flattened paddle'. Behind it sits a large flat dark-maroon disc that reads as a detached smudge floating clear of the animal rather than a tail fin. Only TWO limbs are visible against the required four, and both are thin dark sticks butt-jointed to the belly with a hard seam, no shoulder or hip mass, ending in a small club with no toes. The head is a separate rounded bulb overlapping the torso along a visible boundary line - a neck seam. The skin is glossy and smooth with a handful of blurred yellow dots sprayed on, the opposite of 'moist granular'. The eye is a cartoon white sclera with a black bead, and there is a drawn smile line.
rows.fix: Flatten the tail laterally into a taper-to-a-point paddle with a translucent dorsal and ventral fin fringe fused to the tail body, and delete the free-floating maroon disc. Draw all four limbs, splayed outward from the body at the elbow and knee, with toed feet and a hip/shoulder swelling that emerges from the torso mass. Blend the head into the trunk - no boundary line - and narrow the skull to a rounded wedge. Replace the gloss with a matte stippled granular texture. Remove the smile and shrink the eye into a lidded socket.

rows.readsAs: a small purple songbird or a cartoon chick with a topknot
rows.defect: The bird is plump and has a nice two-feather topknot, but the mustRead 'very short tail' is violated — a dark pointed tail wedge projects back roughly a third of a body length past the rump, longer than the whole head. The wing is a hard-outlined darker teardrop laid on the flank with a crisp boundary line rather than feather groups growing out of the body, and the neck notch keeps the head from reading 'tucked close'. Body is also only ~90px in a 440px frame, so all the quail-specific cues (scaled breast, stubby cocked tail) are below resolution.
rows.fix: Cut the tail wedge to ~10% of body length and angle it down 20-30 degrees so it reads as a stub, not a streamer. Delete the wing outline stroke and replace the teardrop with 3-4 overlapping covert lobes whose tips break the body silhouette. Sink the head lower and forward so the neck notch closes. Scale the whole bird up ~1.4x in frame.

rows.readsAs: a green finch with three wires stuck to its rear
rows.defect: The mustRead 'metallic emerald green plumage over a crimson belly' is entirely absent — the bird is uniform mint green from throat to vent, no red anywhere. The tail plumes are wrong in count and behaviour: THREE straight strands, not two, all emerging from a single point at the rump with a visible junction, held out horizontally like stiff wires and only about one body length long instead of 'far longer than the body'. Posture is listed flying but the render is a perched bird standing on a shadow. It is the identical body, wing teardrop, crest, bill and legs as Quail in this same batch, recoloured green with strands bolted on.
rows.fix: Paint a crimson belly panel from the throat down over the breast to the vent with a soft gradient boundary against the green. Reduce to two streamers, make each 2.5-3x body length, and hang them in a slow downward S-curve below the perch line. Root them under the covert feathers so no point-junction is visible. Differentiate the body from the Quail template: longer neck, rounder helmet-shaped crest covering the crown rather than two spikes.

rows.readsAs: a rabbit — this one is the closest in the batch, but a tailless one
rows.defect: The mustRead 'short round powder-puff tail' is missing — the rump is a smooth unbroken curve with no tail of any kind. Two hard geometric artifacts: a white RECTANGLE with straight machined edges floats under the nose as the incisors, and the front haunch is a perfect dark circle with a hard stroked outline sitting on top of the flank rather than muscle reading through the fur. The hind and fore legs are featureless dark nubs. The far ear's base is a hard line where it meets the skull.
rows.fix: Add a cottontail: a light-value puff, ~12% of body height, breaking the rump silhouette. Replace the white rectangle with two rounded chisel incisors with a gap between them, tucked under the lip line. Delete the haunch circle stroke and suggest the thigh with a soft value shift plus a few fur strokes crossing the boundary. Blend the ear bases into the skull with feathered value, and give the hind foot an actual elongated rabbit foot shape.

rows.readsAs: a generic spotted disc reef fish with a crown, closest to a spiky triggerfish
rows.defect: The dorsal spines are a separate, darker purple sawtooth crown sitting ON the back with a dead-straight horizontal base line — an obvious stuck-on part, exactly the seam case. The caudal fin is worse: a translucent triangle separated from the body by a visible vertical hard edge and a gap, so the tail does not connect. The snout is a rounded pill lozenge butted onto the front of the head with its own outline. The body is a near-perfect symmetrical lens/almond, and the grey blotches are uniform soft ellipses that read as sprayed on top rather than as pigment in the skin.
rows.fix: Redraw the dorsal as spines emerging from a fin membrane that rises out of the dorsal contour — no straight base, vary spine length front-to-back, share the body's colour ramp. Attach the caudal by tapering the caudal peduncle into the fin rays with overlapping value, killing the gap. Grow the snout out of the head profile as a continuous curve; a rabbitfish muzzle is a short blunt taper, not a tube. Break the lens symmetry (deeper forward, shallower aft) and vary the blotch sizes and edges so they follow body curvature.

rows.readsAs: a large green earthworm or a rubber hose with a snake head glued on
rows.defect: Two mustReads fail outright. 'Very slender whip-thin body in a fast S-curve' — the render is a thick, uniform-diameter tube coiled into a near-perfect circular torus with a single inner return; there is no S and the body is roughly 1/6 the coil diameter, heavy not whippy. 'Smooth glossy uniform scales' — the entire body is covered in dense transverse ribbing/annulation running edge to edge, which is worm or millipede segmentation, not snake scales. The head bulges wider than the neck at a visible pinch. Posture is listed crawling; this is coiled. Identical asset to Rat Snake in this same batch apart from hue.
rows.fix: Drop body diameter to about half and lay it in an open S-curve with the head raised and forward, tail tapering to a fine whip. Replace the annular ribbing with a fine overlapping dorsal scale lattice plus a strong specular highlight running the length for the glossy read. Taper the neck into the head so there is no pinch. Give Racer a distinct pose from Rat Snake so the two are not the same picture twice.

rows.readsAs: a kiwi, or a small plump sandpiper
rows.defect: Three mustReads fail. The bill is a straight yellow dagger with no downcurve at all. The body is a plump round ball — the opposite of 'narrow laterally flattened for slipping through reeds'. The feet have no outsized toes; they end in tiny two-stroke tips, and the tail is a dark wedge pointing back and slightly down rather than cocked up. It is the Quail/Quetzal body template again with a longer bill and longer legs. The wing is the same hard-edged teardrop patch with a visible outline where it sits on the flank.
