rows.fix: Curve the bill downward over the last third and thin it. Compress the body laterally: narrower, deeper, with a keeled breast so the silhouette reads slab-sided. Cock the tail up 40-50 degrees and shorten it. Give the feet three long splayed forward toes plus a hind toe at proper rail scale (nearly as long as the tarsus). Merge the wing into the flank with feathered edges instead of an outlined patch.

rows.readsAs: a hamster or a guinea pig; a stranger would not say rat
rows.defect: The signature mustRead fails: the tail is short (about 40% of body length, not 'about as long as the body'), thick at the base, furred in the same colour as the coat, and curled — it reads as a mouse-toy tail, not a long naked scaly rat tail. The snout is not pointed; the head is a rounded dome with a tiny nose, so 'pointed twitching snout' is missing too. Overall aspect is roughly 1.8 including the tail against the specified 4.4. Same white RECTANGLE incisor artifact as Rabbit — straight machined edges floating under the nose — and the same hard-outlined perfect-circle haunch stuck on the flank. This is the Rabbit asset with the ears shortened.
rows.fix: Lengthen the tail to full body length, taper it to a fine tip, strip the fur colour for a pale pink-grey naked value with faint annular scale rings, and lay it in a lazy trailing curve rather than a curl. Draw the muzzle out into a wedge with the nose at the point and the eye set back. Replace the white rectangle with two rounded incisors. Remove the haunch circle outline. Differentiate the body from the Rabbit template — longer, lower, more arch over the shoulders.

rows.readsAs: a purple earthworm coil; indistinguishable from the Racer in this same batch
rows.defect: Pixel-for-pixel the same asset as Racer in this batch, recoloured purple — same circular torus coil, same inner return, same head. The mustRead 'large round eyes with round pupils' fails: the eye carries a narrow vertical slit pupil, which is the viper cue the reference note explicitly rules out. 'Flat-bottomed loaf cross-section' fails — the body is a perfectly round tube with a centred cylindrical highlight. And the dense transverse annular ribbing reads as worm segmentation rather than snake scalation. The head is noticeably bulbed wider than the neck with a visible pinch at the junction.
rows.fix: Change the pupil to a large round black disc with a warm iris ring. Flatten the ventral side and add pale rectangular belly scutes so the loaf cross-section reads; move the highlight off the centreline onto the upper flank. Replace the ribbing with an overlapping dorsal scale pattern, and for a rat snake add faint saddle blotches fading toward the tail. Slim the head so it is barely wider than the neck and blend the junction. Give it a coil pose distinct from Racer's — a stacked coil with the head resting on a loop rather than the same flat ring.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon songbird or duckling — a canary in violet
rows.defect: Three of the three mustRead features fail. The legs are ochre-yellow, not red. The tail is not a broad fan — it is a solid dark pointed wedge sticking out backwards with straight edges that meet the rump at a hard vertical seam, more pheasant/swallow than pigeon. The bill is a short bright-yellow cone with no white cere, i.e. a finch/chick bill, not a slender grey pigeon bill. The wing is a light teardrop crescent with a hard dark rim arc laid ON the back — a separate scoop shape, not plumage growing out of the body. Head is small and the whole bird is the generic songbird template. It is pixel-for-pixel the same geometry as Plover.png in this same batch, recoloured violet.
rows.fix: Recolour legs to coral-red and shorten/thicken them; replace the pointed dark tail wedge with a short broad fan of overlapping rectrices whose base is hidden under the coverts (no straight seam at the rump); rebuild the bill as a slender dark grey taper with a raised white cere bulge at its base; dissolve the wing crescent's hard rim into feather-tract shading so the folded wing reads as part of the back; add the iridescent green/violet neck patch to break the shared-template look and separate it from Plover.

rows.readsAs: a rabbit — specifically the Rabbit/Hare entry, not a pika
rows.defect: This is a rabbit. The ears are tall, narrow and pointed, standing well above the skull with a pink inner tapering to a tip — exactly the long rabbit ear the reference row explicitly forbids. Two square white buck teeth hang below the muzzle, another rabbit cue. There IS a visible tail: a brown lobe protruding from the rear haunch, which the row says must not exist. The whiskers are four perfectly straight machined lines radiating from the cheek. The hind foot/tail region is an ambiguous brown flap with a hard seam where it meets the flank.
rows.fix: Replace the ears with short, broad, near-circular ears set low on the sides of the skull with a pale grey rim, height no more than ~0.35 of head height; delete the buck teeth and the rear tail lobe entirely so the rump is one continuous egg curve; shorten the visible legs so the belly sits on the ground; replace the straight whisker lines with a few curved, fading strokes; break the flat orange gradient with grizzled agouti fur flecking.

rows.readsAs: a barracuda or a needlefish
rows.defect: The dorsal fin is not set far back near the tail — the only dorsal mass is a darker translucent hump across the MIDDLE of the back (roughly the middle third of the body), and it barely protrudes above the dorsal line, reading as a shading patch rather than a fin. The snout is a narrow round cone, not the flattened duck-bill of a pike. The teeth are a row of seven identical white right-triangles hanging BELOW and OUTSIDE the jaw outline like a sawblade decal pasted onto the head, not teeth set into a mouth. No pale bean markings are present anywhere — the flank is a plain red-brown gradient with a single lateral line. The eye is a big white bullseye at the extreme tip of the head, far too prominent for the 'normal' spec.
rows.fix: Move the dorsal fin back so its leading edge sits at ~0.75 body length, directly opposite the anal fin, and give it real height above the back profile; flatten the snout vertically into a broad shovel/duck-bill with a slight upper-lip overhang; redraw the teeth as irregular sizes seated inside the jaw line with the gum line visible, so nothing extends past the head silhouette; add rows of pale cream bean-shaped blotches running along the flank in the creature's own pigment; move the eye back off the snout tip and shrink it.

rows.readsAs: an unlabelled dark fish or a generic dolphin silhouette
rows.defect: The signature dorsal fin is effectively missing — there is only a tiny dark nub on the back; the row calls for a long, low, broad-based swept-back fin set well forward, which is the animal's single most diagnostic feature. There is no bulbous melon: the head tapers to a rounded point with no forehead overhang at all. There is no pale anchor patch on the throat. Two off-body artifacts: a thin pale hairline arcs over the back and detaches from the silhouette near the head, and a small pale grey ellipse floats free above the back just behind the blowhole. The pectoral flipper is a flat dark blob with a hard straight upper edge overlapping the belly — a stuck-on shape, not a limb growing out. The body is otherwise an untextured dark capsule.
rows.fix: Build a wide-based, low, strongly swept-back dorsal at ~0.35 body length whose base blends into the back over a long chord; add a rounded melon that bulges forward and overhangs the short mouth line, with the mouthline curving up behind it; paint the grey anchor/saddle patch on the throat as skin pigment; delete the stray pale arc stroke and the floating ellipse; reshape the pectoral as a long narrow sickle whose root fairs into the flank with no straight edge; lift the overall value so the form reads against the dark background.

rows.readsAs: a needlefish or a blue plastic dart
rows.defect: The body has no rings. It is a perfectly smooth airbrushed blue spindle with a single specular highlight running its length — a machined lens/almond shape, not a segmented bony-plated pipefish. There is no seahorse head: the head is not differentiated from the body at all, it just tapers into a thin straight needle with no distinct tube snout and no pinhole mouth, and no jaw or cheek plate. The mid-body fin is a hard-edged flap of a slightly different blue laid over the flank with a visible boundary. The tail is a tiny dark fan tacked on the left end.
rows.fix: Cut the trunk into visible bony rings — a regular series of raised annular ridges with shading in each groove, running the whole length and getting finer toward the tail; build a proper head: a short deeper block with a horse-like cheek/eye bulge, then a narrow tube snout with a dark pinhole at the tip; fair the dorsal fin's base into the ridges so no boundary line shows; break the single glossy highlight into per-ring facets so the surface reads as armour, not plastic.

rows.readsAs: a piranha, correctly — but a toy one with a sticker mouth
rows.defect: The teeth are a row of eight identical white triangles strung along a straight diagonal mouth slash — a sawblade decal rather than a dentition, and they read as the same tooth stamp used on the Pike in this batch. The lower jaw does not jut: the profile is one straight cut, so the undershot bite the row calls for is absent. The caudal fin is a flat, uniformly darker triangular blade with a straight leading edge that overlaps the body at a hard seam — clearly a separate shape stacked on the flank rather than a tail growing from a caudal peduncle. The body silhouette is close to a perfect ellipse/disc, deeper than the 1.8 aspect specified. The dorsal is only a couple of faint hairline spines.
rows.fix: Give the teeth irregular sizes and slight angle variation, seat them in a visible gum line and let the lower row overbite the upper; push the chin forward so the mandible juts and the mouth line kinks upward; introduce a narrow caudal peduncle and blend the tail root into the body with matching pigment and a soft transition instead of a straight overlap edge; flatten the top and bottom of the ellipse slightly and steepen the forehead into a distinct blunt brow so the outline is not a pure oval; give the dorsal real area with rayed structure.

rows.readsAs: a horseshoe crab or a beached manatee — an unidentifiable dark blob with two paddles
rows.defect: Badly framed and badly scaled: the animal is enormous, shoved against the bottom of the 440px canvas with two-thirds of the frame empty above it, and the tail paddle runs almost to the left edge. It renders as a near-black featureless lozenge with a tan rim-light — no fur, no internal form, no volume. The webbed clawed feet are absent: there are two thin dark sticks under the belly with no webbing, no claws, no foot shape at all. The eye is a bright magenta/pink sphere that reads as a gem set into the surface. The aspect is closer to 3.5-4 than the specified 2.6, and the body is a low flat dome rather than a sleek rounded animal. The bill and tail paddle do read as flat and fused rather than stuck on, which is the one thing working.
rows.fix: Rescale and recentre so the animal occupies the middle of the frame with balanced margins; lift the base value several stops and paint dense wet-fur strokes so the body has form rather than being a silhouette; replace the leg sticks with short splayed limbs ending in broad webbed forefeet with the web visible between distinct claws; recolour the eye to a small dark bead sunk into a fur groove; raise the back's arch and shorten the body to bring the aspect toward 2.6.

rows.readsAs: the same generic songbird as the Pigeon in this batch, in yellow — a canary
rows.defect: This is the identical render to Pigeon.png in this same batch, recoloured gold — same silhouette, same teardrop wing crescent with a hard dark rim, same long dark pointed tail wedge seamed to the rump, same leg placement, same bill. Against its own reference row it fails every mustRead: the head is SMALL, not large and round; the bill is a pointed yellow cone, not a very short stubby bill; the eye is a tiny dot, not a big dark eye; and the body is horizontal and slouched, not compact and upright. The pointed tail wedge is wrong for a plover as well.
rows.fix: Branch the plover off the shared bird template: inflate the skull to a distinctly round dome roughly 0.22 of body length, cut the bill to a stubby dark peg no longer than half the head depth, enlarge the eye to a large glossy black bead set high and forward, rotate the body to a more upright stance on medium straight legs, and replace the pointed tail with a short square-ended one. Add the breast band and pale supercilium so it cannot be confused with the pigeon at a glance.

rows.readsAs: a corrugated grey vacuum-cleaner hose coiled on the floor, with a toy snake head on one end
rows.defect: The body is a near-perfect grey torus — a closed donut ring of uniform diameter, ribbed with evenly spaced hard ridges that read as corrugated plastic vacuum hose, not scales. None of the three mustReads land: the head is a smooth white EGG/sphere (no broad triangular arrow shape, no thin neck), there is no reared S-curve anywhere (the neck simply exits the ring horizontally), and the rattle is a small tan segmented lump on the lower-left that abuts the grey body at a hard colour seam — it looks like a mealworm laid against the coil rather than a keratin tail tip growing out of it. The head also joins the tube at a visible seam where the sphere meets the ribbing. The only snake cue is the red forked tongue.
rows.fix: Rebuild the coil as overlapping loops of varying diameter (thick mid-body tapering to a thin neck and thinner tail) instead of one constant-width ring; raise the front third off the coil into an S with the head lifted. Replace the spherical head with a wedge — wide at the jaw hinges, narrow at the snout, wider than the neck behind it — and blend neck-to-body with a continuous width ramp. Redraw the rattle as 6-8 nested keratin segments that taper OUT of the tail's own colour ramp (same hue family, desaturating), not a separate tan object. Swap the uniform ribbing for overlapping dorsal scale rows with a blotched diamond dorsal pattern so the skin is the creature's own.

rows.readsAs: a teal budgie or a generic cartoon songbird
rows.defect: It is bright TEAL. A raven is the archetypal black bird and the colour alone destroys the read. Every mustRead fails: the bill is a small yellow cone about a fifth of head length (a raven's is a massive, deep, downcurved black dagger); there are no shaggy throat hackles — the throat is a smooth unbroken curve into the breast; and the tail is a thin dark triangular spike, not a wedge of layered rectrices. The wing is drawn as an inset teardrop with a hard dark outline sitting ON the flank like a decal, with a second concentric arc inside it — a sticker, not folded primaries. Body silhouette is a plain egg. Head fraction reads far under the specified 0.3.
rows.fix: Force the plumage to near-black with blue-violet iridescent specular sheen. Replace the bill with a heavy downcurved black one roughly equal to head length and as deep as the eye is high, blending into the forehead with no seam. Break the throat contour with 5-8 overlapping lanceolate hackle lobes that read as separate feather shafts. Rebuild the tail as a broad wedge of layered feathers with a pointed centre, attached under a covert layer. Delete the concentric wing decal and replace it with 3-4 overlapping feather groups (coverts, secondaries, primaries) whose tips cross the tail base.

rows.readsAs: a paper dart or a folded kite with a string tail
rows.defect: The disc is a hard-edged triangle with a dead-STRAIGHT trailing edge and two straight converging leading edges meeting at a sharp apex — a machined geometric primitive, no wing shape at all. Real ray pectorals are undulating and rounded/rhomboid; nothing here reads as a fin fused to the head. Gill slits and mouth are entirely absent from the underside (a mustRead), and the two grey ovals on top plus the two black dots are just spots on a shell. The tail is a uniform grey stick that meets the disc at a hard butt-joint seam under the body with no base thickening, and terminates in a pale flat arrowhead that looks glued on. A large white specular blob in the disc centre makes it read as glazed ceramic.
rows.fix: Replace the triangle with a rhomboid disc whose leading edges bow forward and whose trailing edges sweep back in a shallow S, with visibly thin, slightly wavy fin margins (thickest at the midline, feathering to translucent at the edge). Show the snout as a soft point continuous with the disc, not a corner. Add 5 gill slits and the arc mouth on the visible underside edge. Grow the tail out of a thickened muscular base that is continuous with the disc's rear midline, tapering to a whip; kill the arrowhead tip or turn it into a small barb set on the tail's dorsal surface. Soften the central highlight into broad wet-skin sheen.

rows.readsAs: a dark blue leaf, or a surfboard seen from above
rows.defect: The shell is a symmetric LENS — pointed at both ends, bulging in the middle — so the mustRead 'parallel edges' fails outright; a razor clam is a straight-sided blade with squared ends. The colour is dark navy-purple, not glossy olive-brown periostracum. There is no digging foot anywhere: nothing protrudes from either end. The growth lines are drawn as short straight line segments perpendicular to the long axis, evenly spaced like ruler ticks — machined, and they stop before reaching the edges. Measured aspect is roughly 3.5:1, well short of the specified 6:1. The object is a flat blue blade floating over its own shadow with no orientation cue.
rows.fix: Straighten the two long edges to genuinely parallel and square off the ends (slightly rounded posterior, obliquely truncated anterior) at 6:1 length. Recolour to warm olive-brown with a darker chestnut band and a wet glossy specular streak running the length. Replace the ruler ticks with fine curved concentric growth lines that follow the shell's own curvature and run all the way to the margin. Extend a pale muscular foot from the anterior end, wider than it is long, with a soft blunt tip and a visible gape between the two valves it emerges from.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon goldfish with a detached fin
rows.defect: The tail is a rounded-rectangle paddle floating in FREE SPACE with a clear dark gap between it and the caudal peduncle — it is not attached to the fish, and it is not forked (mustRead fail on both counts). The dorsal fin is a row of five identical hard-edged sawtooth triangles sitting on the back like a machined comb; real spiny dorsals share a connecting membrane and vary in spine height. Colour is monochrome amber-on-amber: the vertical bands are faint tonal darkening of one hue, so 'bright banded colour' does not read. Body outline is a plain smooth ellipse with no forehead, no caudal peduncle narrowing, and the pectoral is a single flat triangle stuck on the flank.
rows.fix: Reattach the caudal fin: narrow the body into a real peduncle and grow the tail from it, then cut a V notch into the trailing edge to fork it, with visible ray striations fanning from the base. Join the dorsal spines with a translucent membrane and vary spine heights, with the fin base blending into the dorsal contour rather than sitting on a line. Introduce a genuinely contrasting second colour for the bands (e.g. deep indigo or white bars over the orange) so they read as pattern, and add a dark eye-band. Give the profile a steep forehead and a small terminal mouth so it reads deep-bodied damselfish rather than an oval.

rows.readsAs: a barracuda or a small tuna
rows.defect: This is not a shark. It is gold/amber, not grey; the snout is a long POINTED spike, not the required rounded short snout; and there are no black or white fin-tip markings anywhere (mustRead fail). The dorsal and pelvic fins are flat brown blobs that sit BEHIND the body silhouette with no continuity of surface — a hard occlusion edge where each meets the back, so they read as pasted-on shapes. The body is a straight-edged almond with a sharp crease line running its length rather than a rounded torpedo. The tail is a symmetric swallowtail (tuna-like), not the strongly heterocercal, long-upper-lobed shark caudal. Only the 5 gill strokes are correct, and they float on the flank as tick marks.
rows.fix: Recolour to grey with a countershaded white belly and a clear lateral tone break. Blunt and round the snout, moving the mouth to the UNDERSIDE as a crescent. Rebuild the body as a rounded torpedo — widest just behind the pectorals, tapering to a slim peduncle with a lateral keel — and remove the axial crease. Grow the first dorsal out of the back with a thickened base and a swept-back trailing tip; add a strong black or white cap to the first dorsal, pectoral and lower caudal tips. Replace the swallowtail with a heterocercal caudal whose upper lobe is roughly twice the lower and carries a subterminal notch. Add pectorals that project from the shoulder rather than being absent.

rows.readsAs: the same small amber mackerel as the Reef Shark in this batch, with a brown smudge on its back
rows.defect: The sucker plate does not read: instead of a ridged, hard-edged oval disc on the crown, there is a soft brown airbrush smudge spread along the mid-BACK, well behind the head, with no lamellae, no rim and no defined outline — a shadow, not an organ. The jutting lower jaw is absent; the jaw line is straight and the mouth terminal. Fins are barely present: no low-set dorsal or anal fin far back, just a single small triangle mid-belly. Measured aspect is about 3.5:1 against a required 5.5:1, so the body is not slim, and it is amber-gold rather than dark. Critically it is a near-DUPLICATE of the Reef Shark in this same batch — same amber lens body, same axial crease, same swallowtail — differing only by the loss of gill strokes.
rows.fix: Move the sucker forward onto the top of the head and draw it as a distinct flattened oval plate with 14-18 transverse lamellae ridges and a raised fleshy rim, its posterior edge fading into the nape so it grows from the skull. Extend the body to 5.5:1 and darken it to slate/charcoal with a paler belly. Push the lower jaw forward past the upper so the profile is underslung. Add long, low, soft-rayed dorsal and anal fins mirrored in the rear half of the body, plus small paddle pectorals. Differentiate the silhouette from Reef Shark's by flattening the head dorsally and using a squared/truncate caudal rather than the same swallowtail.

rows.readsAs: a pink cartoon chick or a recoloured version of the Raven in this same batch
rows.defect: It is bright PINK and it is the Raven's body reused — identical egg torso, identical concentric-oval wing decal with a hard dark outline, identical tiny yellow cone bill, only recoloured and given a longer neck. Against the reference: the neck is short and THICK (feathered, with a shaded ring seam where it meets the shoulder) rather than long and bare; there IS a prominent visible tail, a dark pointed spike jutting from the rump, which the row explicitly forbids; the bill is a small pointed cone, not broad and blunt; and the wings are a flat inset decal, not shaggy drooping plumes. The legs are thin yellow polylines with hard machined angles at the joints, meeting the body underside at an abrupt seam with no thigh mass, and the feet are two-toed forks rather than three-toed. Proportionally the round body dominates the frame; height is not carried by neck and legs.
rows.fix: Recolour to grey-brown. Roughly double neck and leg length and shrink the torso so neck+legs own about two thirds of total height. Render the neck as bare pinkish skin with a fine down fuzz, widening smoothly into the shoulders with no seam ring. Delete the tail spike entirely — the rump should end in a shaggy rounded mass of loose plumes. Replace the wing decal with large drooping shaggy plumes whose tips hang past the flank and break the body outline. Rebuild the legs with a visible feathered thigh flowing into a long bare tarsus, soft joint curves instead of hard angles, and three forward toes on each foot. Widen and blunt the bill to a flat duck-like tip on a small flat crown.

rows.readsAs: four blue-grey rugby balls or hooped barrel-shaped beads strung on an invisible line
rows.defect: The mustRead 'small coloured gut nucleus inside' is simply absent — each barrel is empty navy with a few pale lengthwise streaks and nothing resembling a gut. The four zooids are also identical clones of one perfect ovoid, evenly spaced along a straight diagonal with clear DARK GAPS between them, so it is four separate floating footballs rather than a linked chain — the aggregate has no connective tissue. Colour is opaque dark navy against a near-black field, which kills the 'transparent gelatinous' read; the barrels are darker than water, not clearer than it.
rows.fix: Add a small warm-orange/amber gut nucleus offset toward one end inside each zooid (visible through the wall). Close the gaps: overlap successive zooids by ~15% and add a short soft gelatinous bridge where they join so it reads as one colonial chain. Lift the body value well above the background and drop opacity to ~0.45 with a rim-light on the open ends so the barrel reads as glass, not steel. Vary each zooid's length/tilt by 10-15% instead of stamping the same ovoid four times.

rows.readsAs: a red corrugated hose or a giant ringed earthworm looped into a donut, with a bead for a head
rows.defect: The head is a separate glossy ellipsoid butted onto the end of the tube with a hard visible seam — the fine ring segmentation stops dead and a smooth bulb begins, no jaw, no neck taper, no continuity of skin. It is a bead stuck on a hose. The body is coiled into a near-perfect torus (a machined donut), evenly ribbed with uniform concentric rings that read as corrugated vacuum hose rather than scale. Colour is fire-engine red with a plastic specular sheen — no sand boa cue at all, and no blotching. mustRead fails on all three: no 'blunt wedge snout' (it is a rounded bulb with a big side-facing slit eye, not tiny upward-facing eyes), the thick stubby cylindrical body reads as a uniform tube, and the 'very short abruptly blunt tail' is nowhere visible — the tail end vanishes under the coil so there is no stub to read.
rows.fix: Grow the head out of the body: continue the scale rows onto the skull, widen the last two body diameters into a shallow wedge, cut a mouth line and set the eyes small and high on the dorsal surface. Break the torus — make the coil an asymmetric S or a loose overlapping pile with varying radius, never a closed ring of constant thickness. Replace the concentric hose ribs with overlapping keeled scales that follow the body's curve. Recolour to sandy tan/ochre with irregular darker saddles. Bring the blunt tail stub out of the coil and show it beside the head so the 'both ends look alike' gag lands.

rows.readsAs: a green starfish / sea star — a stranger would name starfish with total confidence
rows.defect: This is not a sand dollar — it is a five-armed sea star. The mustRead 'flat circular disc like a coin' does not exist in the picture: there is no disc at all, just five tapering mint-green arms radiating from a tiny centre with deep V notches of empty background between them. The 'five-petal flower pattern on the upper face' is absent (the petals ARE the silhouette here instead of being a pattern inscribed on a solid disc). No velvety spine fuzz — the surface is smooth with a few random pale speckles that look sprayed on. Arms are flat slabs with near-straight parallel sides and rounded caps.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette as a solid, slightly pentagonal flat disc with a gently scalloped rim — no gaps between the lobes. Inscribe the five-petal ambulacral pattern INTO the upper face as a faint depressed relief with a paired pore-row texture per petal, radiating from a small central point. Add fine short spine fuzz over the whole surface with a slight velvet rim silhouette. Recolour to bleached bone-white or purple-brown; drop the mint green.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon duckling or a green songbird — nobody would say sandgrouse
rows.defect: The wing is a hard-edged crescent lens laid ON the flank with a bright outline and a clean uninterrupted boundary — a decal, not a folded wing growing from the shoulder. The tail is a solid dark-green triangular slab with two straight machined edges spiked into the rear of the body at a hard seam. Both parts are stuck on, not grown out. Legs fail the mustRead 'very short feathered legs' — they are bare thin orange sticks of ordinary length with no feathering to the ankle. The 'long pointed pin tail' is a short wide wedge, not a pin. Colour is flat emerald green with no sandy cryptic mottling, and the body is a smooth capsule-ish oval with a glassy highlight.
rows.fix: Grow the wing out of the body: break the outline with feather-tip separations at the trailing edge, overlap scapular feathers over the shoulder junction, and remove the continuous bright rim line. Replace the triangular tail slab with two or three narrow elongated central pin feathers extending well past the body, tapering to a point, with the coverts blending into the rump. Shorten the legs and cover the tarsus in feathering down to the toes. Repaint the plumage as mottled buff/ochre/grey vermiculation instead of a single green wash with a specular.

rows.readsAs: a long-billed cartoon bird — kiwi or a blue recolour of the Sandgrouse in slot 4
rows.defect: Same rig as Sandgrouse in a different colour — identical lens-shaped wing decal with a bright outline pasted on the flank, identical dark triangular tail slab with straight edges jammed into the rump, identical thin yellow stick legs and identical plump oval body. In this batch it reads as the same organism as the Sandgrouse, recoloured blue. On its own terms: the bill fails the mustRead 'about head length' — it is roughly twice head length, giving a snipe/godwit, and it is a perfectly straight yellow cone with a hard join to the face. Posture also fails: the body is upright and plump with the breast forward, not the horizontal crouched carriage the row calls for.
rows.fix: Differentiate the model from the Sandgrouse — this cannot ship as the same bird twice. Shorten the bill to head length, taper it to a fine dark tip and blend the base into the feathering of the face. Rotate the body to horizontal, drop the head low and forward on a short neck so it reads as a crouched prober. Grow the wing out: feather-tip separations at the trailing edge, primaries projecting past the tail, no continuous rim outline. Replace the tail wedge with a short squared fan of individual rectrices. Lengthen and thin the legs, and repaint in mottled grey-brown above / white below rather than flat blue.

rows.readsAs: a green leaf, or a generic lure-shaped fish — not a sardine
rows.defect: Two mustReads fail outright. There is no 'mirror-silver flank under a dark blue back' — the whole fish is a flat uniform emerald green with a single soft gradient, no countershading, no metallic flank, no scale detail whatsoever ('large loose scales' also absent). The tail is not 'deeply forked' — it is a small dark triangular flag with at most a shallow nick. The single dorsal fin is not a fin but a vague dark hump smudged behind the head. The body is a pure pointed almond/lens, symmetric top and bottom about the midline, with sharp points at both nose and tail root — it reads as a leaf, not a fish with a head. All fins are flat dark triangles overlapping the body edge with no ray structure and no base blending.
rows.fix: Repaint as countershaded: dark steel-blue dorsal surface breaking along a hard lateral line into a bright specular silver flank with a white belly, plus a row of faint dark shoulder spots. Add overlapping cycloid scale texture reading strongest on the flank. Cut the caudal into two long sharply-pointed lobes with a deep central V. Give the dorsal a real triangular ray-fin at mid-back, and add pectoral, pelvic and anal fins with visible rays and soft bases. Break the top/bottom symmetry: raise the dorsal profile, round the snout and give the head a distinct operculum line and a large silver eye.

rows.readsAs: a caterpillar or millipede carrying a stack of coins, with a pink picket fence floating around it
rows.defect: Off-body artifacts: the 'bristles' are perfectly straight uniform pink line segments and a large number of them are DETACHED, floating in clear black space above and below the body with a visible gap — the dense picket fence in the upper-right sits well clear of any tissue. They also do not emerge from between the scales; they emerge from nowhere. The mustRead 'two rows of overlapping scale plates' is a SINGLE row of identical perfect circles stacked like a run of coins down the spine. The body is a smooth round tube, not a 'flattened oval segmented body'. The head is a featureless white sphere with one black dot, butted onto the front of the tube with a hard seam — a ball on a stick.
rows.fix: Anchor every bristle: originate each tuft from a parapodial lobe on the body wall, in fanned groups of 4-6 with varying length and a slight curve, and clip anything not touching the body. Split the scale row into two overlapping lateral rows of oval elytra with irregular edges and pigment mottling, leaving a visible dorsal midline between them. Flatten the body cross-section so the silhouette is a wide oval, not a tube. Grow the head out — taper the anterior segments into a small prostomium with palps and antennae rather than seating a sphere on the end.

rows.readsAs: a teal handbag or a bucket with a fluted front — a clam at best, not a scallop
rows.defect: Two of three mustReads are entirely missing: there is no 'row of tiny bright blue eyes along the mantle edge' and no 'fringe of sensory tentacles between the valves' — the shell is drawn shut as one solid teal object with no gape, no mantle, no soft tissue at all. The silhouette is wrong: a bucket / rounded square with a nearly STRAIGHT horizontal top edge capped by a hard white rim line, where a scallop is a fan whose margin is a broad curved arc. The 'flat wing-like ears at the hinge' are two dark triangular wedges sitting at the bottom apex reading as little feet the object is standing on, plus two stray dark spikes at the top corners that attach to nothing. Ribs are dead-straight tapering lines converging on a mathematical point.
rows.fix: Reshape the outline to a true fan — narrow at the hinge, flaring to a wide semicircular margin with a scalloped/crenulated edge following the rib crests; kill the straight top edge and the white rim line. Open the valves slightly and paint the mantle in the gap: a soft pleated fringe of tentacles with a row of tiny bright blue eyespots along it, brightest where light catches them. Move the ears to the hinge as flat asymmetric wings continuous with the shell (one larger than the other), and delete the two floating top-corner spikes. Give the ribs slight curvature and irregular width, with growth-line banding crossing them.

rows.readsAs: a purple spider or a tick with a bead necklace draped over its back
rows.defect: The pincers are not pincers — each foreleg ends in a solid lilac oval blob with no split chela, no fixed/movable finger, no gap. The metasoma is a string of five separate shiny balls with visible dark gaps between them, sprouting from the SIDE of the body-ball rather than from a rear segment, and it trails up-and-back to the right instead of arching over the back; the sting is a flat brown wedge floating at the end of the chain with a colour and shading that belong to no other part of the animal. The prosoma is a smooth glossy purple sphere, not a flat broad carapace, and the eight legs are uniform hairline sticks that terminate abruptly against the sphere with no coxa, no thickening, no shadow — poked in, not grown out.
rows.fix: Replace the terminal oval with a two-part chela (fixed finger + opposed movable finger, visible gap) on each pedipalp and hold both forward past the head. Build the tail as one continuous tapering tube with overlapping segment bulges (no inter-bead gaps), rooted at the rear of a distinct abdomen and curled forward over the carapace so the sting points over the head; render the aculeus in the body's own chitin colour, not brown. Flatten the prosoma to a broad low shield (widen x ~1.6, drop specular highlight) and give each leg a thickened basal joint that shares the body gradient at the join.

rows.readsAs: a blue bead-chain wasp, or a damselfly
rows.defect: None of the three mustReads are present. The head is a plain blue sphere with two black eye-domes and NO downward beak — there is no rostrum at all, only a few thin hooked leg-lines below the thorax that could be mistaken for one. The abdomen is a chain of six discrete overlapping balls ending in a plain round ball — no bulbous upcurled genital bulb, no upturn whatsoever. The wings are clear grey-white with fine veins and zero black blotches, and both attach along a single hard straight line at the top of the thorax rather than emerging from wing bases. Body construction is the same bead-chain used on the Scorpion in this batch.
rows.fix: Add a long tapering rostrum dropping vertically from the front of the head to about 0.6 head-lengths, with small dark jaws at the tip. Curl the last three abdominal segments upward and swell the terminal one into a rounded genital bulb. Paint 3-4 irregular dark blotches across each wing membrane and taper the wing root into a fleshy base that shares the thorax gradient. Fuse the abdominal beads into a continuous tapering tube with segment ridges instead of separated spheres.

rows.readsAs: a white dove or pigeon
rows.defect: There is no horn — the forehead is a clean unbroken white curve with nothing projecting from it. There are no wing spurs; the wing bend has no bony projection. The body is a small round dove body, not goose-bulky, and the wing is rendered as a flat grey-white oval plate laid on the flank with a hard dark outline all the way round it — a sticker, not plumage growing out of the shoulder. The bill is a small straight yellow cone with no hook. The tail is a separate dark-grey wedge butted against the rear of the body along a visible straight seam.
rows.fix: Add the thin forward-curving forehead horn (length ~0.5 head height, springing from the crown skin with a soft base blend). Add a short sharp bony spur at each wing bend. Bulk the body up to goose mass (increase chest depth, lengthen neck slightly) and hook the bill tip downward. Kill the outlined oval wing: draw layered covert and flight-feather groups whose bases dissolve into the flank shading, and blend the tail wedge into the rump instead of butting it on.

rows.readsAs: a green pike or barracuda
rows.defect: Fails every mustRead. The head is small and sharply pointed with a tiny eye at the very tip — the opposite of an oversized broad flattened head; headFrac reads more like 0.15 than 0.35. There are no huge fan-like pectorals — only one small dark translucent tab under the belly, half hidden behind the body. The body is a symmetric almond/lens pointed at both ends, not a tapering tadpole. The dorsal is a row of six identical perfect isoceles triangles sitting on a hard straight baseline along the back — a machined comb dropped on top. The caudal fin is a separate fan joined to the body by a pinched neck with a visible hard seam. It is the same silhouette and skeleton as the Sea Bass in this batch, recoloured green.
rows.fix: Rebuild with a wide bluntly-rounded head that is a third of the body length and visibly flattened dorsoventrally (widen head, lower its profile, add preopercular spines). Grow two large rounded fan pectorals from the sides just behind the gill cover, splayed downward as props, with rays fanning out of a fleshy base. Taper the body strongly behind the head into a thin tail stock. Replace the triangle comb with a continuous spiny membrane whose rays vary in height and whose base sinks into the dorsal ridge, and blend the caudal rays out of the peduncle instead of attaching a detached fan.

rows.readsAs: a white cooling tower with frost growing out of the top; anemone only at second glance
rows.defect: The column is a straight-sided truncated cone with a machined-looking hard rim at the top — a lampshade or cooling-tower profile, not a soft fleshy trunk. It has no basal disc: the base is a flat horizontal cut with no flare, no grip, and no rock. The tentacles are stiff white antler-like branched sprigs radiating from that hard rim, reading as frost or bleached staghorn coral rather than soft waving tentacles, and their bases stop dead at the rim line instead of emerging from an oral disc. The mouth is a plain black void hole rather than a slit in fleshy tissue.
rows.fix: Give the column a soft convex bulge and irregular vertical wrinkles, then flare the bottom outward into a spreading basal disc gripping a rock lump. Make the tentacles smooth unbranched tapering fingers of varying length with S-curves, and set their bases in a domed oral disc that sits inside the column rim so they grow out of tissue instead of perching on an edge. Replace the black hole with a slit-shaped mouth on the raised disc, shaded rather than pure black.

rows.readsAs: a generic orange cartoon fish, near-identical to the Sculpin in this batch
rows.defect: There is only ONE dorsal fin — a row of five identical perfect triangles on a hard straight baseline sitting on the back like a stuck-on sawtooth comb; the soft second dorsal is absent entirely. There is no large mouth: the snout is a sharp point with a single hairline scratch. The body is a pointed lens/leaf shape, sharp at nose and sharp at the tail stock, not a robust deep-bodied perch. The caudal fin is a small separate fan joined by a pinched waist with a visible seam. The colour is a flat orange gradient with a specular sheen and no scale texture. It is the identical skeleton to the Sculpin in this batch with an orange palette.
rows.fix: Split the dorsal into a spiny anterior fin (rays of graded height inside a continuous membrane, base sunk into the back) and a separate lower soft posterior fin. Round out the nose and open a large oblique mouth with a visible jaw line running back under the eye. Deepen the belly into a perch profile instead of a symmetric lens. Blend the caudal rays out of the peduncle and square/slightly fork the trailing edge. Add scale texture so the flank is skin, not a gradient.

rows.readsAs: a shiny mango or a polished orange seed with a whisk stuck in one end
rows.defect: The body is a perfect glossy orange ellipse with a bright specular highlight down its top — a hard geometric primitive, reading as a mango or a polished seed. Aspect is roughly 2, not the 4 called for, and there is no sag, no wrinkle, no soft slump anywhere. The tentacles are seven straight unbranched hairline sticks radiating from a single point at the left tip, floating off the body with a hard junction and no mouth structure between them. There are no tube feet on the underside at all; the underside is a clean unbroken curve. A few pale grey smudges float on the upper edge, unattached to anything.
rows.fix: Stretch the body to ~4:1 and break the ellipse: give it a sagging bottom that flattens where it meets the ground, irregular bumps and transverse wrinkles along the top, and matte skin with no specular highlight. Rebuild the tentacles as short thick branched (dendritic) plumes clustered around a visible mouth opening on a raised oral cone whose base blends into the body wall. Add two or three rows of stubby tube feet along the flattened underside. Remove the floating grey smudges.

rows.readsAs: a brown potato or a kiwi fruit with an eye; at best a beached seal pup
rows.defect: All three mustReads are missing. There are no external ear flaps — the head end is a bare smooth curve with a single black dot for an eye. There is no muzzle at all: no snout, no mouth line, no whiskers, no nose; the head is simply the fat end of the blob. The fore-flippers do not lift the chest — the chest lies flat on the ground and the only fore-limb is a tiny three-pronged tab at the lower LEFT, i.e. at the tail end, with a matching nub at the lower right; the animal has no working limb geometry. The whole thing is one featureless brown teardrop with two soft airbrushed dark ovals sprayed on the flank, and a hard bright cyan rim stripe outlining the back that reads as a drawn contour line, not light.
rows.fix: Add small furled external ear pinnae behind and below the eye. Sculpt a blunt dog-like muzzle projecting from the head with a dark nose pad, a mouth line and radiating whisker dots. Move the fore-flippers to the chest just behind the head, lengthen them to about a third of body length, and rotate them under the body so the shoulders and chest are raised clear of the ground with the neck arched up; rotate the hind flippers forward under the hips. Break the teardrop into distinct neck, chest and hip masses. Remove the sprayed-on flank ovals and soften the cyan rim into a broken specular highlight rather than a continuous outline.

rows.readsAs: a pond ram's-horn snail, or a decorative ammonite fossil sitting on a slab
rows.defect: The shell is a flat planispiral (ram's-horn / ammonite) coil seen face-on, not a turreted sea-snail whorl, and no aperture is readable anywhere on it. The foot is a flat grey-purple slab with a hard straight lower edge — the shell rests ON it like a hat on a plank rather than the mantle growing out of it. The only 'head' is a tiny 3-pronged fan at the right edge that reads as a leaf frond; there is no siphon tube and no eyestalks. There is also a pale translucent arc that starts outside the shell at upper-right and crosses down through the foot at lower-left — an off-body stray stroke.
rows.fix: Rebuild the shell as a conic helical spire (apex up-back, body whorl swelling forward) so the aperture is a real opening facing the head. Replace the slab foot with a curved muscular sole whose top edge blends into the shell's aperture lip (shared gradient, no boundary line). Grow two long upper eyestalks + two short lower tentacles and one open siphon tube from the head mass. Kill the stray arc.

rows.readsAs: two pink bubblegum balls with pencil lines drawn out of them — a doodle of a spider, not a pycnogonid
rows.defect: The body is two pink spheres — literal geometric primitives, one with a tiny dark cross scribble for eyes — and the eight legs are 1px perfectly straight lines that meet the spheres at a hard seam with no coxa, no taper, no joint mass. Legs are dead-straight from body to tip with a single kink, so they read as drawn sticks, not limbs. There is no proboscis at all. The body is a fat bulb, the exact opposite of the required shrunken stick.
rows.fix: Reduce the trunk to a thin segmented rod with four lateral processes; the leg bases must be the widest part of the animal and taper over 7 tapered segments to a claw, each with a knee and a slight curve. Give the legs volume (stroke width 6→1 with shading), not hairlines. Add a long tubular proboscis projecting forward, roughly trunk-length. Put four eyes on a small dorsal turret instead of the scribble.

rows.readsAs: two industrial smokestacks, or a pair of frosted-glass milk bottles on a dome
rows.defect: Both sacs are truncated cones with straight sides and the surface pattern is a perfectly regular brick grid sprayed on top — it does not follow the body's curvature. The four siphons are hard-edged cylinders with perfect circular rims, cut off flat, and each meets the tunic at a visible ellipse seam like a pipe socketed into a tank. The substrate is a perfect half-ellipse dome with a dead-straight bottom edge. The greyscale-metallic palette pushes it further from flesh.
rows.fix: Make the sac silhouette irregular and bulged (wider at the cemented base, asymmetric lumps), and let the siphon walls flare continuously out of the tunic — same gradient, no ring seam. Replace the brick grid with a soft translucent tunic through which a vertical pharyngeal basket with fine gill slits shows, warped to the body's curve. Break the rock's straight bottom edge and give the base a spreading holdfast skirt.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon garden tortoise, or a wooden pull-along toy turtle
rows.defect: The carapace meets the brown body along a dead-straight horizontal line across the whole width — a hard machined seam, the single worst artifact in the batch. The head is a plain ellipse abutting the shell edge with a visible boundary and no neck, and the eye is a perfect white circle with a black dot. The front flippers are short rounded paddles about a third of shell length, not long wing-like blades, and they too are stuck under the straight seam rather than emerging from shoulder sockets. Scute lines are thin concentric arcs drawn over the dome, sprayed on, and there is a translucent grey halo rim outside the shell.
rows.fix: Curve the plastron/carapace junction and let the marginal scutes scallop it; no straight edge anywhere. Extend the front flippers to roughly 1.2x shell length as tapering, backswept blades with a thickened leading edge, rooted in a shoulder bulge that shares the body gradient. Grow a short thick neck out of the shell opening and give the head a blunt keratin beak with a slit mouth; replace the dot eye with a lidded almond. Emboss the scutes as raised plates with depth, not line art. Remove the halo.

rows.readsAs: a green firework burst, or a chestnut husk — the urchin family is legible but the animal's defining pentaradial anatomy is absent
rows.defect: The test is a mathematically perfect circle with a smooth radial gradient and no five-part radial pattern of any kind — instead there are three amorphous dark smudges clustered off-centre that read as mould or a bruise. The spines are uniform straight bars of near-identical length and width that stop with blunt square-ish ends, all the same green, giving a firework/starburst rather than a graded spine forest.
rows.fix: Stamp real pentaradial geometry on the test: five petaloid ambulacral bands of paired tube-foot pores alternating with five interambulacral bands of tubercles, converging on an apical disc with the madreporite. Vary spine length, thickness and hue by band (long primaries on tubercles, short secondaries between), taper every spine to a fine point, and let near-side spines overlap the test with cast shadow so the sphere reads as a volume the spines are anchored in. Break the circle with slight polar flattening.

rows.readsAs: a kiwi chick, or a sandpiper hatchling — nobody would say gull
rows.defect: No webbed feet — the feet are two bare forked twigs with three thin toes and no membrane. Body is a fat round ball, not streamlined, and the 'folded wing' is a stuck-on lens outline with a hard dark contour sitting on the flank like a decal, ending in a thin pointed spike for the tail. The bill is a flat needle triangle, neither stout nor hooked nor dagger-thick, and it joins the head at a hard corner. Head is a small circle on the ball with a dot eye and no neck.
rows.fix: Elongate the body into a horizontal teardrop with a long neck-shoulder line; make the folded primaries a stack of overlapping feather blades whose bases disappear under scapulars (no closed outline). Broaden the bill into a stout laterally-compressed gull bill with a nail hook, a nostril slit and a gonydeal angle. Give the feet three forward toes joined by continuous webbing and a proper tarsus. Add a squared tail rather than a spike.

rows.readsAs: a green cartoon snake reared up in a question-mark, or a Loch Ness plush
rows.defect: The whole body is a smooth glossy tube with zero ringed bony armour — no rings, no ridges, no spines, just a plain dark-green S-worm with a single pale highlight stripe. The snout is a stubby round-capped cylinder stuck onto the side of the head at a hard seam, reading as a peg or a duck bill rather than a fused tubular jaw. There is no dorsal fin at all and no pectoral fin; a small hook-shaped tab floats near mid-body doing neither job. The tail curls forward but has no taper and no prehensile grip on anything.
rows.fix: Segment the entire trunk and tail into stacked bony rings with raised lateral ridges and small tubercle spines at each ring junction — the armour is the animal's identity. Taper the snout continuously out of the head into a long thin tube (roughly head-length) with a tiny terminal mouth, no seam. Add the fluttering dorsal fin at the trunk/tail junction and a small fan pectoral behind the gill. Give the tail a real taper and wrap it around a stalk so the prehensility reads.

rows.readsAs: a garden slug, or a beached manatee calf
rows.defect: It is a featureless grey blob. There is no dog-like head — the front simply bulges and stops, with one tiny black dot eye, no muzzle, no whiskers, no mouth line. There are no fore-flippers whatsoever, only two faint grey smudges on the flank. The hind flippers are a single thin two-pronged fork the size of the eye, far too small to read as trailing hind flippers. A hard-drawn golden contour stroke runs along the entire back and down to the tail, an outline rather than a form. The silhouette aspect is roughly 1.4, not the specified 3, so it reads squat and lumpy.
rows.fix: Stretch the body to a true torpedo about 3x long, with a distinct neck taper into a rounded dog-like head: broad muzzle, nostril slits, a mouth line and a full fan of long vibrissae. Enlarge the eyes to big dark liquid domes. Sculpt two short clawed fore-flippers emerging from shoulder bulges, and enlarge the hind flippers to broad webbed fans trailing straight back with visible digit rays. Delete the gold outline and carry the highlight as a soft dorsal sheen inside the silhouette; add fur/pelage mottling.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon purple flamingo-chicken hybrid, or a stylised toy roadrunner
rows.defect: The mustRead "eagle head with a bare orange-red face" is entirely absent — the head is a small lavender ball with a plain yellow beak and a black dot eye, no bare facial skin of any colour. The crest is four tiny magenta tines flicked off the top of the skull, not a fan of long black quills trailing behind the head. The legs are yellow drinking-straws of uniform width with a hard kink and no thigh mass at all — they simply terminate at the underside of the body egg with no feathering or hip, a visible seam where limb meets body. The wing is a hard-edged dark ellipse outline stamped onto the flank: a closed oval loop with a paler fill, plainly a decal laid over the body rather than a folded wing emerging from the shoulder. Body is a smooth capsule/egg with an airbrush gradient and no plumage texture. Tail is two straight ruler-like streamers. Whole bird is purple.
rows.fix: Replace the head with a raptor skull: deep hooked black bill and a bare orange-red mask of skin around the eye reaching to the bill base. Rebuild the crest as 6-8 long black quills sweeping BACKWARD past the nape, not upward. Give the legs a feathered black "trouser" over the upper half, taper them, and blend the thigh into the belly contour so no seam is visible; lengthen so the tarsus is roughly 40% of total height. Delete the ellipse-outline wing and replace with an overlapping covert/primary group whose leading edge merges into the shoulder with no closed outline. Recolour to the grey body / black flight-feathers scheme.

rows.readsAs: A white cartoon chicken or a generic pale gamebird
rows.defect: This is the same body build as the Secretary Bird in this batch, recoloured cream — identical egg torso, identical hard-edged ellipse "wing" decal stamped on the flank, identical yellow straw legs with the same kink, identical head ball and dot eye. Two of the three mustReads fail: the legs are pale yellow-tan and only moderately long, not "very long red legs"; and the tail is a short stubby grey wedge poking off the back, nothing like a long trailing tail (on the reference row aspect 1.2 the tail should be a major part of the silhouette). The frontal bristle spray is present but tiny and sits on the forehead rather than at the base of the bill. Body surface is a flat airbrush gradient with no feather texture whatsoever.
rows.fix: Differentiate the mesh from the Secretary Bird — lower, longer horizontal torso. Recolour the legs to strong coral-red and lengthen them. Replace the grey wedge with a long, broad, banded tail at least as long as the body, tapering off the rear and blended into the rump instead of butted onto it. Move the bristle spray forward to sit directly above the bill base and make it a stiff fanned tuft. Remove the closed-outline ellipse wing.

rows.readsAs: A tuna or mackerel — a generic torpedo-shaped bony fish, not a shark
rows.defect: None of the three shark cues survive. The first dorsal fin is a barely-visible dull maroon lump behind the back that is nearly the same value as the background — not a tall triangular fin. The caudal fin is a near-symmetrical black fan with equal upper and lower lobes; the heterocercal longer upper lobe is absent. There is no crescent underslung mouth — the only mouth marking is a straight horizontal line running along the flank midline, a machined ruler-straight stroke. The gill hatching is a set of five identical parallel tick marks stamped on the cheek. The eye is a perfect white circle with a black pupil, oversized and cartoonish, while the row calls for a small eye. Overall value is so dark against the navy background that the animal is almost invisible.
rows.fix: Add a tall, backswept triangular first dorsal at roughly 20% body length rising from the back with a blended base. Rebuild the tail as heterocercal: upper lobe about twice the lower, with the spine visibly bending up into it. Move the mouth to the ventral surface as a broad down-turned crescent set well behind and under the pointed snout. Replace the perfect white eye disc with a small dark eye and a nictitating lid. Add pectoral fins as long scythe blades. Lift the body value to mid grey with a hard countershading break to white on the belly so it separates from the background.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon orange mouse or a small hamster; the triangular ears push it toward a kitten
rows.defect: The defining mustRead — the long mobile pointed proboscis-like snout — is not there. The face ends in a short blunt muzzle with a pair of white square teeth and three straight whisker lines. The eye is a large white-and-blue prominent eye with a highlight, directly contradicting "tiny bead eyes" and being the single most attention-grabbing feature of the picture. Ears are two triangular flaps that read as a cat's. The body is a plain orange egg with a hard-edged darker ellipse stamped on the flank for the haunch — a closed shape sitting ON the body, not a muscle growing out of it. The legs are two dark stubs barely emerging from under the belly with a hard boundary. No velvety fur texture anywhere; the surface is a single airbrush gradient.
rows.fix: Extend the muzzle into a long tapering flexible proboscis reaching well past the jaw line, tipped slightly downward, with the nostrils at the very end. Shrink the eye to a tiny black bead almost buried in fur, no white sclera and no highlight. Reduce the ears to small rounded lobes half-hidden in the pelt. Delete the flank ellipse and model the haunch with a soft value shift that has no outline. Add short dense fur stippling for the velvety coat, and expose four small pink feet.

rows.readsAs: An insect larva or a tadpole with an egg sac — two separate blobs rather than one shrimp
rows.defect: The animal is drawn as two disconnected lumps. The cephalothorax is one spotted egg on the left; the segmented abdomen is a separate ellipse to the right that merely overlaps it, with a hard crescent seam where the two meet and a clear value discontinuity — it reads as two organisms, or as a shrimp carrying an egg sac. The abdomen also points down-and-right at an angle unrelated to the head's axis, breaking the continuous curve a shrimp's body must have. The serrated rostrum spike is completely absent; the front of the head is a bare rounded dome. The eyes are two flat dark dots painted on the carapace, not stalked eyes standing off the head. The walking legs are four straight identical dark tick marks hanging below the body with no joints and no attachment.
rows.fix: Merge head and abdomen into one continuous tapering curve — a single arc from the rostrum tip through the carapace into the tail fan, with the abdominal segments as overlapping plates whose edges ride over one another rather than a separate blob. Add a long serrated rostrum projecting forward between the eyes. Put the eyes on short stalks that grow out of the head with visible bases. Rebuild the pereiopods as jointed limbs attached at identifiable segment boundaries, and add the long antennal scales; keep the antennae but make them curve rather than run straight.

rows.readsAs: A purple cartoon newt or salamander; a toy gecko
rows.defect: The head is an oversized ellipse butted against the front of the body ellipse with a visible constriction seam — it reads as a separate balloon stuck on, not a skull continuous with the neck. The mouth is a perfectly straight horizontal machined line across the whole side of the head. The mustRead "smooth glossy overlapping polished scales" is unmet: the surface is a plain purple airbrush gradient with dark blotches sprayed on top; there is no scale tiling and no specular sheen. The tail carries a dark internal stripe that is a closed shape with a rounded cap floating inside the tail rather than a marking following the body form, reading as a decal. Only two legs are visible and each is a plain dark cylinder joining the belly at a hard edge with no shoulder or hip mass.
rows.fix: Blend head into body — narrow the neck junction and carry the dorsal contour through unbroken, then reshape the skull to a wedge with a slightly protruding snout. Replace the straight mouth with a subtle curved jaw line that follows the skull. Add fine overlapping cycloid scale rows that wrap the cylinder and shrink toward the tail, with a hard glossy specular streak down the spine. Convert the tail stripe into a series of scale-row-aligned bands that fade, and drop its hard cap. Show all four limbs, each with a visible shoulder/hip mass that merges into the torso.

rows.readsAs: A plump golden chick or a quail standing on the ground
rows.defect: The posture is wrong outright — the reference row calls for flying, and the bird is standing on two yellow legs with a ground shadow under it, wings folded. Beyond that, the mustReads fail: the bill is a short stubby yellow triangle with only the faintest tip curve, not a heavy hooked pirate bill; there is no white flash at the base of the primaries anywhere; and the build is not a barrel-chested bulky gull but the same rounded egg torso used for the Secretary Bird and Seriema in this same batch, complete with the identical hard-edged ellipse "wing" decal on the flank and the same yellow straw legs. Tail is a short dark wedge butted onto the rear. Colour is a uniform honey-gold gradient with no feather texture.
rows.fix: Redraw in flight: wings extended, body horizontal, legs tucked, no ground shadow. Give the bill real mass — thick, dark, with a pronounced hooked nail at the tip. Paint a bold white crescent across the base of the outer primaries on each wing, the field mark the row demands. Broaden and deepen the chest for the bulky gull build and shorten the neck. Replace the ellipse decal with real spread wings whose coverts and primaries emerge from the shoulder without an outline.

rows.readsAs: A small salmon or trout
rows.defect: The mustRead "simple streamlined silvery body" is not met — the fish is a saturated orange-red with a dark dorsal wash, which reads as a salmon or trout, not a silvery baitfish. The single dorsal fin is present but so small and so close in value to the back that it barely registers. The body is drawn with ruler-straight machined lines: a dead-straight lateral line runs the full length, and two more straight crease strokes cut across the flank. The eye is a perfect white ring with a black dot, geometrically exact and pasted on the snout. The caudal fin is a small triangular fan joined at a thin peduncle with a visible hard seam. Structurally this is the same geometry as the Shark in this batch — same torpedo outline, same eye construction, same fin attachments — just recoloured and shrunk.
rows.fix: Recolour to a cool silver body with a darker olive back and a bright reflective flank stripe so it reads as a baitfish. Enlarge the dorsal fin and give it visible rays, blending its base into the back. Replace the straight lateral line with a slight downward-bowed curve that follows the body form, and delete the extra straight crease strokes in favour of soft scale shimmer. Redraw the eye as a slightly irregular dark pupil with an offset highlight rather than a perfect ring. Widen the caudal fork and merge the fin base into the peduncle so no seam shows.

rows.readsAs: a generic green sunfish or a cartoon tropical reef fish
rows.defect: The caudal fin is fully DETACHED — a dark-green rounded paddle floating in open background with a visible ~12px gap of bare dark blue between it and the body tip, and a stray thin diagonal dark line runs straight through it off-body. No fused beak: the mouth is a thin curved smile-line with a soft lip, no dental plates at all. No blunt bulging forehead — the head tapers to a point, so the silhouette is a symmetric almond/leaf lens, aspect ~1.5 not 2.6. The pectoral is a tiny hard-edged fan glued over a separate dark leaf shape rather than a large rowing paddle. Body markings are five blurry airbrushed grey blobs sprayed on top of the flat green fill, floating clear of the outline.
rows.fix: Reattach the caudal: extend the body outline into a narrowing peduncle that the fin flares out of, sharing fill and shading, and delete the stray off-body stroke. Replace the smile-mouth with a hard fused beak — two pale keratin plates, upper overlapping lower, with a faint median suture. Push the forehead into a steep convex bulge above the eye and shorten the snout so the profile is blunt, not pointed. Enlarge the pectoral into a broad rounded wing-like paddle angled down-back, with rays fanning from a fleshy base. Swap the sprayed blobs for scale-following mottling that respects the body curve and clips to the outline.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon duckling or a generic small songbird
rows.defect: The mustRead 'short stubby tail held low' is violated: the tail is a long dark-green pointed TRIANGLE with straight machined edges projecting horizontally about a third of a body-length past the rump, meeting the body at a hard seam. The wing is not a wing — it is a decal: a hard-edged C-shaped grey-green ring with a flat pale-green ellipse inside it, the same stamp reused on Pelican, Petrel and Pheasant in this batch. Body is a plain sphere with no breast/rump distinction; head is a smaller sphere set on it with a visible outline seam, no neck. Legs are two flat yellow sticks with no feathering. A small scribble of stray hatch marks sits below the wing near the flank.
rows.fix: Cut the triangle back to a short blunt fan of 3-4 rounded coverts angled downward, no longer than a quarter of the body, with barbs breaking the outline. Delete the C-ring decal and draw a real folded wing: scapular, coverts and primaries as overlapping soft-edged feather groups whose leading edge emerges from the shoulder mass with no ring outline. Merge head into body with a short feathered neck taper. Add the partridge's rufous face and grey barred flanks so it is not a plain single-hue bird. Remove the loose hatch strokes.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon bird with a paper party fan taped to its rear
rows.defect: The train is neither extremely long nor trailing — nine flat teal lozenge feathers fan out stiffly behind the bird and stop about one body-width away, so the whole render is aspect ~1.5 against the required 2.2. Each 'eyespot' is a single perfectly flat yellow-orange DISC — a geometric primitive, identical nine times, and it sits near the middle/base of each feather rather than at the tip; there is no ocellus ring structure (no blue-black core, no bronze halo). The feathers themselves are hard-edged flat capsules with rounded caps and no barbs, stacked as overlapping facets. The crest is a small spiky teal tuft with no wire stems and no disc tips. There is no iridescent blue neck or breast — the whole bird is one uniform teal, and the wing is the same C-ring-plus-ellipse decal as Partridge/Pelican.
rows.fix: Lengthen the train to at least twice the body, running low and dragging behind and below the feet rather than fanned upward, with feathers overlapping into a soft mass. Rebuild the ocellus at each feather TIP as a layered target — blue-black centre, cyan crescent, bronze-gold outer ring — not a flat disc. Give every train feather loose barb texture so its edges are feathery, not capsule outlines. Redraw the crest as ~6 bare wire stems each ending in a small racket tip. Recolour neck and breast to saturated iridescent blue distinct from the green-bronze body, and replace the wing decal with real folded coverts and primaries.

rows.readsAs: a green kingfisher or a generic long-billed wader
rows.defect: The single most identifying feature is absent: there is NO throat pouch. The bill is a flat yellow-orange cone with two straight machined edges converging to a sharp point, no hook at the tip and nothing slung beneath it. It joins a spherical head at a visible hard outline seam. 'Long neck kinked back onto the shoulders' is also absent — the head ball sits directly on the body ball with no neck whatsoever. Posture is standing biped on yellow stick legs, not the specified swimming. Body/wing/tail/legs are the same reused stamp as Partridge and Petrel (C-ring wing decal, hard dark triangular tail), differing only in bill length and hue. Stray hatch scribbles sit under the wing.
rows.fix: Rebuild the bill as a long straight-sided mandible with a distinct downward hook at the tip, and hang a deep elastic gular pouch from the lower mandible that swells and connects continuously into the throat with no seam. Insert an S-kinked neck folded back onto the shoulders so the head rests over the breast. Set the bird low in water for the swimming posture (waterline across the body, legs hidden) or, if kept standing, shorten the legs to very short and set them far back under a heavy body. Replace the C-ring wing decal with real folded primaries and the triangle tail with a short rounded fan. Remove the hatch scribbles.

rows.readsAs: a fat orange robin chick or a generic round garden bird
rows.defect: Wrong colours and wrong parts. The bird is orange-tan and cream, not black-backed; the belly is a hard-edged perfect cream ELLIPSE pasted onto the orange body with its own visible outline — that is a sticker, not countershading, and it fails the mustRead. There are no flipper wings at all: only a dark brown crescent that reads as body shading, nothing stiff or flat held at the sides. The tail is a hard brown triangle with straight edges spiking out to the right — a stuck-on wedge with a seam at the rump. Silhouette is a near-circular ball, roughly as wide as tall, so it does not read as the tall narrow aspect 0.45 required, and the feet are two small yellow sticks set centrally at the bottom rather than rear-set. The bill is a small yellow cone, not a penguin bill.
rows.fix: Recolour to true countershading: matt black head, back and outer flipper faces, white front, with the boundary as an irregular soft feather margin that runs up the throat and around the face — never a clean ellipse. Add two stiff flat paddle flippers, narrow and blade-like, growing out of the shoulders and held pressed to the sides with a slight outward flare at the tips. Stretch the body vertically into a tall bowling-pin torso and move the feet to the rear so the bird balances back on tail and heels. Replace the triangular tail with a short stiff wedge of downcurved rectrices touching the ground. Give it a stout dark tapered bill instead of the yellow cone.

rows.readsAs: a gold sunfish or piranha wearing a paper crown
rows.defect: The spiny dorsal is an OFF-BODY artifact — five sharp triangles float above the back with clear dark background visible between their bases and the body outline, so it reads as a crown balanced on the fish, not a fin. Only one dorsal is present; the required second soft dorsal is missing entirely. The caudal fin is also detached, separated from the body tip by a visible gap of background. No orange-red pelvic or anal fins — the pelvic is a small dark brown nub the same hue as the body and there is no anal fin. The dark vertical bars are soft airbrushed stripes floating inside the body that fade out before reaching the outline, so they read as sprayed on rather than as pigment in the skin. The colour is uniform gold-brown with no green back. Silhouette is a symmetric pointed almond, aspect ~1.6 not 2.8.
rows.fix: Drop the spiny dorsal down so its membrane base is continuous with the dorsal ridge, and give it curved membrane webbing between spines instead of free-standing triangles. Add a second, separate soft-rayed dorsal behind it with a short gap of back between the two. Reattach the caudal via a narrowing peduncle carrying the body fill. Recolour pelvic and anal fins to saturated orange-red and enlarge them so they read at thumbnail size. Redraw the bars as hard-edged wedges that start on the dark olive-green dorsal ridge and taper down the flank all the way to the outline. Lengthen the body and flatten the ventral line so aspect approaches 2.8.

rows.readsAs: a small orange sandpiper or snipe standing on mud
rows.defect: Posture is wrong at the top level: the reference calls for flying and the bird is standing on two yellow stick legs on the ground with a cast shadow beneath it. There are no spread wings at all — just the same hard C-ring-plus-ellipse wing decal used on Partridge, Pelican and Pheasant, so 'narrow angled swept-back wings' is entirely absent. No tubular nostrils: the bill is a plain flat yellow needle cone with straight edges and no tube ridge, no hook, no nail. The tail is the same stuck-on brown triangle with a hard seam at the rump. Head is a ball with a visible outline seam and no neck. Loose hatch strokes sit under the wing.
rows.fix: Rebuild as an airborne bird: body horizontal, legs tucked, no ground shadow, and two long narrow wings swept back in a shallow M with a distinct hand/arm bend, the primaries splayed and each wing root blending into the shoulder with no ring outline. Redraw the bill as short, stout and dark with a hooked nail and a paired tube ridge sitting on top of the culmen, clearly modelled. Replace the triangle tail with a short wedge of rectrices. Give the plumage a dark upper / pale under split so it reads as a seabird at distance.

rows.readsAs: a white wagtail or a generic pale bird with three grey streamers
rows.defect: None of the three mustReads survive. The tail is three flat grey BATONS — uniform-width capsules with rounded caps, no barbs, no barring at all — that begin inside the wing shape and sweep right, overlapping the body at a visible seam rather than growing from a rump. There is no red bare facial wattle: the face is plain white with a single black dot eye. There is no iridescent green-black head and no white neck ring — the entire bird is one pale grey-white, so a white ring could not read even if drawn. The wing is again the hard C-ring outline with a flat white ellipse inside, which at a glance looks like a magnifying glass laid on the flank. Head is a ball seamed onto the body with no neck; legs are flat yellow sticks. Small stray hatch strokes hang below the wing.
rows.fix: Replace the batons with a single long tapering tail of overlapping pointed rectrices, longest in the centre, carrying strong dark cross-barring, and root them in a rump mass so the join is continuous. Recolour the head glossy green-black, add a bare scarlet wattle patch wrapping the eye plus small ear tufts, and paint a crisp white collar separating the dark head from a coppery-orange scaled body. Delete the C-ring wing decal in favour of real overlapping coverts and primaries with a soft feathered trailing edge. Add a neck taper between head and body and remove the loose hatch strokes.

rows.readsAs: A chrome ammonite fossil or a coiled spring mounted on a flat metal base plate
rows.defect: The head end is only a tiny white 3-prong fleck about 12px wide clipped to the right edge of the shell — there are no long eye tentacles at all, so the mustRead 'two long eye tentacles plus two short feelers' fails. The foot is a separate flat grey slab with a straight bottom edge and two sharp machined corner points; the shell and the ribbed body lobe simply sit ON that slab with a hard horizontal seam rather than the body being one continuous mass that the foot flares out of. A thin stray hairline arc floats across the top-left of the shell, unattached to any surface (off-body artifact). Whole render is desaturated chrome blue-grey with a specular bead at the coil centre, so it reads as metal, not moist flesh.
rows.fix: Grow two tapering eyestalks out of the head mass — length ~0.45 of shell diameter, swelling to a dark ocellus bulb at the tip — plus two shorter oral feelers below them, all sharing the body's gradient with no seam at the base. Rebuild the foot as a low sole whose top edge blends into the body mantle (soft alpha ramp, not a butt-joint line) and whose front/rear ends round off instead of terminating in points. Delete the floating arc stroke. Recolour body to a warm damp grey-ochre with a wet sheen instead of the cold metallic ramp.

rows.readsAs: A generic cartoon fish icon — closest to a teal pufferfish or a clip-art guppy
rows.defect: The body is a mathematically perfect teal ellipse, aspect roughly 1.5 not the 3 the row calls for — it is a capsule/egg silhouette with no tadpole taper. The tail is a separate dark fan wedge stuck on the left with a visible vertical seam and a colour discontinuity at the join; the fan itself is a flat triangle with straight radiating spokes. No sucker disc anywhere on the belly (mustRead missing). No translucency — the body is a flat opaque teal gradient with one straight highlight line running its full length like a machined bevel. The pectoral fin is a small triangle with spoke lines painted on the surface. Eye is a perfect white circle with a black dot.
rows.fix: Rewrite the outline to a real snailfish: bulbous rounded head occupying the front third, then a continuous taper along ~3x body length into a fine point, with dorsal and anal fin membranes running unbroken into that point (one path, no separate tail primitive and no seam). Add the ventral sucker disc as an oval pucker on the belly under the pectorals with concentric soft rings. Drop opacity to ~0.6 with a faint interior shadow so the body reads gelatinous, and remove the straight full-length highlight line.

rows.readsAs: A ribbed vacuum hose or a giant earthworm with an eye painted on
