rows.defect: The body is a constant-diameter tube bent into one flat closed loop, not S-curves, and it never tapers toward the tail. It is covered end to end in dense transverse ribbing that reads as annelid segmentation or a vacuum hose, not scales. The head is a rounded bulb knob on the end of the tube with a big spherical eye, not a wedge, and the tube visibly pinches then re-swells where it meets it. Two pale grey ellipse patches on the upper-left of the coil and one on the right sit flat on the surface like decals, ignoring the tube's curvature. The forked tongue is a thin stick-figure red Y with uniform line weight.
rows.fix: Taper the body radius from ~1.0 at the neck to ~0.15 at the tail tip and lay it in at least two opposing S-bends so one loop crosses over another. Replace the transverse annular ribs with overlapping imbricated dorsal scales that shrink with body radius and follow the curve. Reshape the head into a flat-topped wedge, widest at the jaw hinge and narrowing to the snout, continuous with the neck. Make the surface patches follow the tube's shading gradient (multiply blend, curved edges) instead of sitting flat. Give the tongue a thicker base tapering to two fine tips.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon fish wearing a paper crown; essentially the Snailfish from this same batch with a spiky fin added
rows.defect: Same perfect teal ellipse as the Snailfish in this batch — aspect ~1.5 against the required 2.8, and the head is just the pointed right end of the ellipse with a line for a mouth. No sloping forehead, no pointed snout, and zero canine teeth (mustRead missing entirely). The dorsal fin is a zigzag sawtooth crown sitting on top of the back with a hard straight baseline seam and a darker fill that never blends into the body — it reads as a paper crown laid on. The caudal fin is a detached triangular fan separated from the body by an actual visible gap. The pectoral is the same triangle-with-spokes decal used on the Snailfish.
rows.fix: Lengthen and stoutly deepen the body to ~2.8 aspect, then build a real snapper head: a straight sloping forehead from nape down to a pointed snout, large jaw line, and two visible canines at the front of the upper jaw. Replace the crown with a single continuous dorsal membrane whose spine bases emerge from within the dorsal contour (feather the fill alpha into the body over ~8px, no baseline stroke). Attach the caudal via a narrowing peduncle so there is no gap. Differentiate the palette from the Snailfish — snappers are red-pink, not teal.

rows.readsAs: A cute pet tortoise, or a green glass dome on two rubber feet
rows.defect: There is no tail at all — the mustRead 'long saw-toothed crested tail' is entirely absent. No hooked beak and no oversized head: the head is a small smooth green egg with a single dot eye, and it is joined to the shell by a stubby cylinder neck. Only two legs are drawn, and both are featureless rounded blobs hanging below a flat horizontal plastron bar with a hard straight seam at the top of each — no feet, no toes, no claws. The carapace is a smooth glossy dome scored with a regular radial grid of thin arcs and spokes, which reads as a geodesic greenhouse rather than rough keeled scutes, and it is far too tall and roomy for the 'too small to withdraw into' requirement.
rows.fix: Add the tail: as long as the carapace, thick at the base, with a dorsal row of triangular saw-tooth crests. Enlarge the head to roughly 1.5x current diameter, flatten the skull, and give it a hooked upper mandible overhanging the lower jaw. Replace the two blobs with four splayed limbs ending in clawed feet, with the thigh mass emerging from under the shell rim rather than butted to a straight bar. Flatten the carapace profile, break the radial grid into three irregular keeled ridges of lumpy scutes, and shrink the shell so head and legs visibly do not fit inside.

rows.readsAs: A generic teal wading bird — most people would guess kiwi or a stylised sandpiper
rows.defect: No cream back stripes anywhere — the body is one flat teal gradient (mustRead missing). The wing is a concentric ring of lighter teal ellipses painted onto the flank, clearly a decal that ignores the body's form and has no feather edge or shoulder attachment. The tail is a dark triangular wedge poking out the right side with a hard straight seam against the body. The bill, while long and straight, is a flat opaque orange triangle with a hard boundary against the head and no culmen ridge or shading. Legs are two thin yellow sticks that meet the belly at a hard point with no thigh mass, and the toes are a flat splayed fan.
rows.fix: Paint four bold cream longitudinal stripes down the mantle and scapulars over a barred brown-buff base — snipe cryptic pattern is the whole point of this bird. Rebuild the wing as a folded feather group with a scapular shoulder that emerges from the body contour and layered primary tips overlapping the tail; drop the concentric ellipse decal. Blend the tail base into the rump with short covert feathers. Give the bill a subtle taper with a soft-tipped darker end and shade its base into the facial feathers. Add feathered thigh mass where the legs leave the body.

rows.readsAs: A small blue songbird or kiwi on legs — visibly the Snipe from this batch in a different colour
rows.defect: It is BLUE, not white — the 'entirely pure white plumage' mustRead fails outright. The bill is a long straight ORANGE dagger, the opposite of the required short black hooked bill with tube nostrils. The posture is standing on two yellow stick legs on the ground, not flying, and there are no long narrow pointed seabird wings — just the same concentric-ellipse wing decal on the flank and a small dark tail wedge with a hard seam. Structurally this is the identical rig to the Snipe in this same batch, recoloured blue and scaled down about 30%.
rows.fix: Repaint the entire bird pure white with only soft blue-grey shadow in the undersides; keep the eye as a small black bead. Replace the bill with a short, deep, black hooked bill roughly one third of the head length, with the raised tubular nostril ridge along the top of the culmen. Change the pose to flying: legs tucked, body horizontal, and two long narrow wings swept out to a pointed tip with a span of ~2.5x body length, the shoulder mass growing continuously out of the back. Differentiate the silhouette from the Snipe rig entirely.

rows.readsAs: A generic orange Easter-card bunny
rows.defect: The coat is warm orange-tan, not the required white winter coat. The ears have brown backs with pink inners and no black tips (mustRead missing). There are no oversized furry hind feet — the only thing below the body is a small dark stub at the lower right and a rounded dark lobe at the lower left, neither of which reads as a foot; no front legs are drawn at all. The haunch is a hard-edged darker crescent laid flat over the rump with a clean vector curve as its border, an obvious decal rather than a muscle mass emerging from the body. The body outline is a smooth featureless egg with no fur silhouette. Whiskers are four perfectly straight uniform-width lines fanning from a small white block on the muzzle, and the eye is a perfect white-ringed circle.
rows.fix: Recolour to white with faint blue-grey shading and keep only the ear tips and eye ring dark — black tips on the ears are the identifying mark. Shorten the ears to about 0.8 of head length (jackrabbit ears are longer) and blend their bases into the skull with fur tufts instead of a butt-joint. Build the signature hind foot: a long, broad, splay-toed pad extending forward under the belly, clearly larger than the forefoot, drawn as part of the leg. Replace the crescent decal with a shaded haunch whose edge is broken by fur strokes, add a visible forelimb, and break the whole outline with short irregular fur tufts. Vary whisker length and taper them.

rows.readsAs: a beluga or a pilot whale — an unlabelled viewer would say generic small toothed whale, not a right whale
rows.defect: None of the three mustReads land. There is no arched jawline at all — the mouth is a single thin straight pencil line running horizontally from a sharply pointed dolphin snout, and the head takes maybe 0.2 of the body with no bulk. No callosity crust anywhere; the only white on the head is one tiny pale grey oval sitting on the crown (reads as a blowhole, not a patch of crusty growth). The flipper is a flat mid-grey ellipse pasted onto the belly in a completely different flat colour from the body's silvery gradient, with a hard unblended edge, and it hangs below the belly outline — stuck ON, not growing out. There is also a thin dark curved stroke over the forehead that runs off the head outline into the background at the upper left — an off-body line artifact. Flukes join the peduncle at a hard pinch. Body is a pure recolour of the River_Dolphin in the same batch.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head: bow the mouth line into a deep arch that starts at the snout tip, rises above the eye and returns — the jaw should own the front third of the silhouette, and the upper lip must be a high narrow rostrum sitting inside that arch. Replace the single grey crown oval with a cluster of irregular lumpy off-white callosity blobs of varying size on the rostrum tip, above the eye and along the lower lip. Grow the flipper out of the body wall — start it inside the silhouette, sample the body's gradient at the attachment and blend across ~15px, and make it a broad paddle, not an ellipse. Delete the stray forehead stroke that escapes the outline. Fork the body mesh away from River_Dolphin so the two are not the same shape.

rows.readsAs: a generic orange fish or a red-painted porpoise — nobody would say river dolphin
rows.defect: The defining feature is simply absent — there is no beak. The snout is a short plain taper straight to a point, no tweezers, no length, no teeth of any kind. No melon bulge either: the forehead is a straight unbroken diagonal from snout tip to back, and there is no neck crease. The dorsal hump is present but is a hard-edged dark triangle in a flat different brown from the body, with a visible seam where it meets the back — stuck on. The flipper is the same flat dark ellipse problem as Right_Whale: pasted on the belly, hard edge, hanging past the outline. A small pale grey oval floats in the background above the head, fully detached from the silhouette — an off-body artifact. Geometry is identical to Right_Whale, only the palette differs.
rows.fix: Extend the rostrum to roughly 20-25% of total length as a slender near-parallel tube, and score fine tooth ticks along both jaw edges. Put a rounded melon dome above and behind the beak base so there is a clear stop between beak and forehead, and pinch a shallow neck crease behind the head. Reblend the dorsal hump: make it a low rounded ridge sampled from the back's own gradient with no colour break at the join. Attach the flipper inside the body outline and blend it. Remove or re-seat the floating pale oval so the blowhole is on the head. Give the body a different profile from Right_Whale.

rows.readsAs: a hoopoe, or a generic gold songbird with a broom stuck to it
rows.defect: The tail is three separate straight brown sticks fanning off the rump with black gaps between them — they are rigid machined lines, not connected to each other and not connected into a tail, and they read as broom straws taped to the bird. The crest is a tiny yellow spiky tuft of five thin spikes sprouting from the crown, not a shaggy black crest, and it is the wrong colour entirely. The bill is a very long thin needle like a hummingbird's, not a heavy pointed dagger. The legs are short thin yellow wires with tiny feet — the whole point of a roadrunner is long strong bare legs, and these are shorter than the body is deep. The wing is a stack of three nested concentric almond outlines, a drawn-on decoration rather than feather groups. There is a small scribble of hatch marks at the rump where the sticks attach, which reads as an artifact. Body is a plain egg.
rows.fix: Rebuild the tail as one continuous graduated feather fan — overlapping tapered vanes sharing a common base that grows out of the rump, cocked upward at ~20 degrees, with dark brown-black outer feathers and white feather tips. Recolour the crest black and make it a ragged raisable spray of unequal feathers, not five even spikes. Thicken and shorten the bill to a heavy pointed dagger about head-length. Roughly double the leg length and thicken them into strong scaled tarsi with two-forward-two-back zygodactyl toes. Replace the concentric almond rings with overlapping covert and primary shapes. Delete the hatch-mark scribble.

rows.readsAs: a duckling or a baby chick
rows.defect: No orange-red breast — the mustRead is missing. The whole bird is one uniform tan-gold, and the belly is actually the palest part of the render, so the breast is lighter than the back rather than a saturated brick-orange block against a grey-brown mantle. The bill is a fat wide yellow triangle, not thin. The posture is squat and round with the head sunk onto the shoulders, not the upright large thrush the note asks for; head fraction reads well over 0.3 on a ball-shaped body. The head is a separate circle joined to the body with a visible seam at the throat. Wing is the same nested concentric almond rings as Roadrunner. The render also sits very small in the 440px frame with a lot of dead space.
rows.fix: Paint a distinct breast field: saturated brick orange-red from the throat down over the chest and flanks, with a hard-ish boundary against a slate grey-brown back and crown, plus a white lower belly and undertail. Narrow the bill to a thin straight yellow spike about half its current width. Lengthen the legs and lift the body to a standing upright thrush stance with the head clear of the shoulders and the tail angled down. Blend the head-to-body join so the neck reads continuous. Scale the whole bird up in frame.

rows.readsAs: a kiwi or a dark shorebird with a plank attached
rows.defect: The tail is a literal rectangle — a hard-edged parallelogram slab with a perfectly straight top edge, a straight bottom edge and a square corner where it butts into the body. It is the single worst geometric primitive in the batch and does not read as feathers in any way. There is no red comb and no wattles at all; the head carries only a thin pale crescent rim over the crown and a small dark cone bill. No hackle cape, no puffed chest — the body is a plain dark oval. The neck is a narrow tube with a visible seam ring at the shoulder where it enters the body. The eye is a bright cyan cartoon disc that belongs to a different art language than the rest of the batch. The whole bird is near-black with a pale rim light, so no rooster colour reads.
rows.fix: Delete the rectangle. Build the tail from long curved sickle plumes — three or four arcing feathers sweeping up and back over the rump, plus a bundle of shorter graduated coverts underneath, all originating from a common base inside the body outline. Add a tall serrated red comb on the crown and two long red wattles hanging below the bill. Add a hackle cape: a ruff of pointed narrow feathers flowing from the nape down over the shoulders, which also hides the neck seam. Puff the chest forward and raise the stance. Replace the cyan eye with a small amber-orange eye. Lift the overall value so the plumage is not a silhouette.

rows.readsAs: a swordfish or a marlin — the sail is too small to name the species
rows.defect: The sail fails the mustRead. Instead of a fin taller than the body is deep, the dorsal is a low dark grey slab hugging the back at roughly a third of body depth, with a near-straight top edge and evenly spaced vertical ray lines. It reads as a comb or a saddle laid on the back, and its flat charcoal fill breaks against the pale silver body along a hard seam with no blending. Thin dark hair-strokes stick up out of it into the empty background above the fish — off-body artifacts. No thread-like pelvic fins anywhere. The pectoral is a flat grey triangle with straight radial spokes and a hard edge, pasted on. The bill is present and correct in length but is a flat uniform grey bar with a squared-off blunt tip and its own colour, seamed against the head at the eye.
rows.fix: Triple the sail height so its peak exceeds the body's maximum depth, run it from just behind the head to near the tail, and give it a curved scalloped upper margin rather than a straight one. Tint it deep cobalt with darker spots and make it translucent at the trailing edge; sample the back's colour where it attaches and blend the first ~10px so there is no seam. Delete the hair-strokes escaping into the background. Add two long thin thread pelvic fins trailing back from just behind the pectorals. Taper the bill to a needle point and blend its base into the upper jaw.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon caterpillar or a grub mascot
rows.defect: There is a large dark-green disc floating behind the animal, roughly the size of the whole torso, overlapping nothing and attached to nothing — a huge off-body artifact that a viewer reads as a second blob or a bug. Only TWO limbs are drawn, one front and one rear, and both are plain cylindrical sticks that end in blunt rounded stumps with no feet and no toes at all. The body is a smooth capsule and the head is a separate rounded bean joined to it at a visible pinched seam. The tail is a uniform-width sock tube with a rounded blunt end, meeting the body at a hard elliptical seam line rather than tapering out of the hips. Skin markings are soft airbrushed yellow-green smudges sprayed over the capsule, not spots that follow the form. The face has a big white googly eye and a curved smile line — cartoon mascot, not amphibian. Small brown blobs also float loose around the body.
rows.fix: Delete the detached green disc and the loose brown blobs. Draw all four limbs, splayed out sideways from the flanks at roughly equal size, each ending in a soft blunt four/five-toed foot planted on the ground. Merge the head into the body with a continuous jawline and only a slight neck narrowing — no pinch seam. Rebuild the tail so it starts at full hip width and tapers continuously to a rounded point, growing out of the body silhouette with no join line. Replace the airbrushed smudges with discrete irregular spots that sit on the skin and wrap around the body's curvature, and darken the base body so it reads as moist skin with a wet specular highlight rather than flat plastic. Remove the smile line and shrink the eye.

rows.readsAs: a generic silvery trout or a spotted sea bass
rows.defect: No adipose fin — the back between the dorsal and the tail is completely bare, and that is one of the three mustReads. No kype either: the snout is a plain symmetrical point with no hook on the lower jaw. The spots are soft grey airbrushed ovals that float on the surface, all roughly the same size and evenly distributed, and they do not continue onto the fins or wrap the body's curvature — classic sprayed-on pattern. The dorsal fin is a flat charcoal slab with a hard straight-ish top edge and evenly spaced straight rays, meeting the pale body along a hard colour seam. Thin dark hair-strokes rise off the dorsal into the background — off-body artifacts. The pectoral is a flat grey triangle fan with straight spokes, pasted on. Body, tail, dorsal and pectoral are the same construction as Sailfish in this batch minus the bill.
rows.fix: Add a small fleshy adipose fin as a low rounded nub on the midline between the dorsal and the caudal peduncle — it must be soft-edged and rayless, the opposite of the dorsal. Hook the lower jaw upward into a kype so the mouth cannot close, and lengthen the snout. Make the spots irregular in size and shape, denser above the lateral line and sparse below, and carry them onto the dorsal and tail. Blend the dorsal's base into the back and give it a curved trailing edge. Delete the hair-strokes in the background. Differentiate the body silhouette from Sailfish — salmon should be a deeper-bellied fusiform with a thicker peduncle.

rows.readsAs: a hunched cicada nymph or a shrimp larva — most people would say 'some kind of bug', not 'prawn'
rows.defect: The mustRead rostrum is entirely absent — there is no spike of any kind in front of the eyes, just a smooth bald dome. The animal is built from two separate spheres: a big speckled cephalothorax ball and a second abdomen ball jammed against its right side, with a hard crescent seam and a highlight rim running down the join. The abdomen's 'segments' are drawn as thin arc lines painted on the sphere, not real overlapping plates. Worst of all the abdomen curls the WRONG way — it tucks forward and DOWN under the head, so the spiky tail fan hangs beneath the body like a hand of claws rather than spreading behind. Aspect measures roughly 1.3 (a squat lump), not the specified 2.6. Legs are straight stick strokes that stop dead at the carapace, and the upper antenna starts in empty space a few pixels clear of the head — a detached line.
rows.fix: Add a long serrated rostrum blade projecting forward past the eyes from the top of the carapace. Replace the two-sphere build with one continuous tapering body whose abdomen curves BACKWARD and upward, ending in a spread telson fan at the rear; stretch total length to ~2.6x depth. Build the abdomen from real overlapping segment plates with silhouette scallops rather than arcs painted on a sphere. Anchor every leg and both antennae inside the body outline so no stroke begins off-body.

rows.readsAs: a snow-white plush gorilla or a cartoon ghost-ape — nobody would say proboscis monkey
rows.defect: The single defining feature — the huge drooping pendulous nose — is completely missing. At 4x the face is a flat white disc with two tiny nostril dots and a smile line; there is nothing hanging over the mouth. Colour is also inverted from the reference: the whole animal is pale grey-white with grey limbs, with no orange-brown back anywhere. Construction is stuck-on: the head is a grey ball resting on a white egg torso with a visible seam, the two thighs are separate grey ovals overlapped onto the belly with hard edges, and the tail is a uniform-width grey noodle that meets the body at a blunt butt-join. A grey rounded-rectangle band sits across the brow like a machined visor, and the ears are two plain ellipses pasted on the skull sides. The silhouette overall is a capsule with an ellipse on top. Posture reads seated/upright, not the specified quadruped.
rows.fix: Model the proboscis as an actual fleshy pendulous lobe drooping from the brow past the mouth line, part of the head silhouette. Repaint the dorsum orange-brown with pale grey confined to limbs, tail and face ruff. Grow the thighs out of the torso mass (shared outline, no overlapping ovals), taper the tail from a thick base, and delete the grey brow rectangle in favour of a modelled browridge.

rows.readsAs: an ant or a generic six-legged toy bug — the pincers do not register as pincers at all
rows.defect: First, it is barely visible: at full size it is a tiny dark-grey smudge lost in the background, so I had to brighten it 3x to judge anything. Brightened, the mustRead pincer arms are not pincers at all — they are two plain pale eggs on the ends of straight brown sticks, with no chela, no finger-and-thumb split, no claw shape, and they read as detached floating blobs because the stick arms pass behind them. The abdomen is a smooth SPHERE, not the required flat teardrop with segments — there is no segmentation of any kind on it, only a brown smeared stain. The body is two spheres butted together, each carrying its own hard white rim-light arc so a bright crescent line marks the seam exactly where the join should be hidden. Eyes are four black dots stamped in a 2x2 grid on the front of the ball, obviously sprayed on. Legs are straight tapered spikes.
rows.fix: Raise overall value/exposure so the animal reads against the dark plate. Rebuild the pedipalps as real chelae — a swollen palm with an opposed fixed and movable finger — connected by tapered segmented arms that emerge from the carapace outline. Replace the abdomen sphere with a flattened teardrop carrying transverse tergite bands and a blunt end (no tail, correctly). Kill the per-sphere rim highlight so the cephalothorax/abdomen junction is one continuous form, and drop to two lateral eyes rather than a 2x2 dot grid.

rows.readsAs: a white dove or a duckling — a generic cartoon bird, not a ptarmigan
rows.defect: Two of the three mustReads fail. There is no red comb above the eye — the crown is plain white. The feet are bare thin yellow sticks with three spindly toes, the exact opposite of the required densely feathered feet. The wing is a decal: a perfect grey ellipse OUTLINE stroked onto the flank with a hard uniform-width line, plus a second grey band arcing over the shoulder — it sits on the surface rather than being a folded wing with feather edges. The tail is a flat grey triangle wedge with straight machined edges, butt-joined to the body with a visible hard line and no covert transition. The head is a sphere overlapping the body sphere, seam visible. The bill is a solid yellow cone, too long and pointed for a grouse.
rows.fix: Add the red supraorbital comb. Replace the stick legs with the feathered 'snowshoe' — feathering carried all the way down over the tarsus and toes. Convert the ellipse-outline wing into a folded wing shape with layered primaries breaking the silhouette, and grow the tail out of the rump with covert feathers over the join. Shorten and thicken the bill into a short grouse bill.

rows.readsAs: a lemon-yellow sunfish or a fat goldfish — the detached slab tail is the first thing you notice
rows.defect: The caudal fin is physically detached: a brown rounded-rectangle slab floats to the left of the body with a clear gap of dark background between it and the fish — an off-body artifact with straight machined edges and ruler-straight ray lines inside it. The body is not the required inflated balloon; it is a smooth flat ovoid finished with a hard white stroked outline all the way around, which reads as vector line art rather than paint. The mustRead small beaked mouth is absent — at 4x there are only two faint hairline curves near the snout, no beak, no lips. The eye is a small flat circle, not big and protruding. The pectoral fin is a tiny fan glyph drawn ON the flank as a decal rather than emerging from it, and the dorsal is another straight-edged slab pasted on the back. The dark spots are soft airbrushed blobs floating over the gradient, clearly sprayed on top of the skin rather than being it.
rows.fix: Re-attach the caudal fin so its base merges into the peduncle with no gap and give it a soft membranous trailing edge instead of a rectangle. Add the parrot-like fused beak with a visible mouth line. Enlarge and dome the eye so it bulges past the head contour. Round the body far closer to a sphere and, if inflated, break the outline with spine bumps; drop the uniform white stroke and let the form read from value. Bed the spots into the skin with edge variation.

rows.readsAs: a tan chick or a quail — and it is unmistakably the same bird as the Ptarmigan in this batch, just tinted orange
rows.defect: All three mustReads fail and the render is the Ptarmigan template recoloured. The bill is a small solid tan cone — there is no huge triangular laterally flattened bill and no orange/blue-grey striping. There is no black cap and no big white face patch: the entire bird, head included, is one flat tan-orange. The feet are the same thin bare yellow sticks as the Ptarmigan, not bright orange webbed feet. The wing is the identical stroked-ellipse decal with the same grey shoulder arc, the tail is the same flat triangle wedge butt-joined to the rump, and the head is the same sphere with the same seam. Nothing here identifies the species.
rows.fix: Replace the cone bill with the deep laterally compressed triangular puffin bill, banded orange / blue-grey / yellow with a pale rictal edge, occupying a large fraction of the head. Paint the black crown, nape, back and collar against a white face disc and white underparts. Swap in wide orange webbed feet. Break the shared bird template — the body needs the upright auk posture and a stubbier wing, or it will keep reading as the Ptarmigan.

rows.readsAs: a pink glass vase or a paper lampshade — at best a tube sponge; the pink kills the deep-sea read
rows.defect: The tube reads and the zooid pimpling is genuinely good — hundreds of small raised lozenges bumping the silhouette along both edges, which is the right idea. But the glow colour is wrong: it is hot magenta/pink where the mustRead calls for a cold blue bioluminescence, and there is no light spill into the surrounding water at all, so nothing actually glows. The closed end is not sealed — it is chopped flat, a straight horizontal cut across the bottom with two sharp corners, so the object reads as a cut-off vessel rather than a rounded blind end. The two side walls are near-perfectly straight machined lines, giving a lampshade taper instead of an organic soft-bodied tube, and the mouth rim is a clean geometric ellipse of uniform stroke width.
rows.fix: Recolour to cold cyan-blue and add an outward bloom/halo so the colony is a light source. Round and seal the lower end into a soft blind cone tip with no straight cut. Introduce gentle waviness and thickness variation along the side walls so the tunic reads as gelatinous, and make the rim ellipse irregular with zooids interrupting its edge.

rows.readsAs: a rubber snake toy or a cartoon cobra — the flat yellow and stuck-on head make it read as a prop, not a python
rows.defect: Two of three mustReads are simply not drawn: there is no net-like reticulated blotching anywhere (the snake is one flat mustard yellow with a couple of faint smudges) and there are no heat-sensing pits along the lips. The head is a separate object — at 4x it is a flat-shaded ellipse with a hard white outline, and the ribbed body tube visibly TERMINATES behind it, leaving a pinch and a seam where neck should flow into skull. There is no mouth line at all; the forked tongue is a flat pink stick that sprouts from a bare point on the ellipse. The body is a constant-diameter hose with no taper toward the tail and no thickening at midbody, coiled into a near-perfect flat circle with a small hook inside — the coils lie side by side and never overlap, so there is no mass or weight. Ventral scales are rendered as evenly spaced parallel ticks the whole length, like the ribbing on a machined vacuum hose.
rows.fix: Paint the reticulated pattern — irregular dark net lines enclosing tan saddles with pale centres — following the body's curvature so it deforms with the coil. Add labial pits as notches along the upper and lower lip. Merge the head into the neck as one continuous form: widen the temporal region, add a mouth line, and root the tongue inside it. Taper the body toward the tail, thicken midbody, and let at least one coil cross over another with a cast shadow so the animal has heft. Vary the scale rows in size and spacing instead of uniform ticks.

rows.readsAs: A generic plump shorebird or a kiwi — nobody would say stork
rows.defect: There is no neck at all — the round yellow-billed head is glued straight onto a fat egg-shaped body, so the single most stork-defining feature (a long neck held straight out) is absent. The legs are short-to-medium and YELLOW, not the required very long red legs; the tibia is barely longer than the body is deep, and the bird's belly nearly touches the ground shadow. The wing is a flat lighter-blue lens shape with a hard dark outline pasted onto the flank — a visible seam, not a wing growing out of the body. The tail is a solid dark navy triangular wedge that reads as a separate cut-out stuck on the rear. Body silhouette is essentially a capsule/egg.
rows.fix: Add a real neck: extend a tapering column ~0.45 of body height from the shoulder to the head, held straight and forward, blended into the breast with the same gradient (no outline where they meet). Lengthen the legs to ~0.55 of total height with a clear tibia/tarsus break and recolour them to the required coral red, keeping the bill yellow-to-dark. Replace the outlined wing lens with a feather-group shaded from the body's own gradient and no stroke, and let the tail taper out of the rump rather than butt against it.

rows.readsAs: A generic torpedo-shaped fish with a broken nose; closest read is a needlefish or a barracuda
rows.defect: None of the three mustReads are present. There are no bony scutes anywhere — the back and flanks are a smooth untextured purple gradient. There are no barbels under the snout. The tail is a symmetric two-lobed fork with straight ray lines, not the shark-like upturned asymmetric heterocercal tail. Worse, the snout is broken: a dark plum blob sits off to the right of the head, separated from the body outline, so it reads as a detached lump floating in front of the fish rather than a long pointed rostrum. The eye is a hard-edged perfect white circle with a black dot, a geometric primitive sitting on top of the paint. The body is a plain lens/almond shape with one straight pale highlight line down the midflank.
rows.fix: Draw the rostrum as an actual continuation of the head — a long shallow wedge tapering from the skull, merged into the same silhouette path, and delete the detached blob. Hang four barbels as thin tapering filaments from the underside of that snout. Add the five scute rows: a dorsal ridge of raised keeled plates plus lateral rows, each plate lit on its upper edge so the ridging is topographic, not painted stripes. Rebuild the tail as heterocercal — upper lobe roughly twice the lower and swept up, with the body's caudal peduncle running into the upper lobe. Replace the circular eye with a small dark iris shaded into the surrounding skin.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon aquarium fish — bluegill is a plausible guess only because of the deep round body
rows.defect: The tail is physically detached — there is a clear dark gap of background between the rear of the body and the fan-shaped caudal fin, which floats as an isolated leaf shape with its own outline. The dorsal is a row of five sharp isosceles triangles sitting on the back like a paper crown, a machined zigzag rather than a spiny fin membrane, and it has a hard seam where it meets the back. The required dark ear-flap tab on the gill cover is missing entirely — there is only a thin scribed arc for the operculum. Spots are uniform soft grey blobs sprayed evenly over the surface with no relation to body contour or lighting. The eye is a perfect white circle with a dot.
rows.fix: Reattach the caudal: extend a peduncle out of the body so fin and body share one silhouette, and shade the fin from the body's own colour. Replace the triangle crown with a continuous spiny dorsal — a membrane spanning graduated spines, rooted in a soft base that fades into the back with no outline. Add the diagnostic black ear-flap as a dark oval tab on the trailing top corner of the gill cover. Make the mouth tiny and terminal on a smaller head. Turn the spots into vertical bar-and-mottle patterning that follows body curvature and dims into the belly.

rows.readsAs: The Sunfish from this same batch, recoloured pink
rows.defect: This is the same picture as Sunfish in a different colour. Identical deep round body outline, identical five-triangle crown dorsal, identical detached fan tail with a background gap between it and the body, identical circular white eye, identical scribed gill arc and pectoral fin. On its own merits it also fails every mustRead: there is NO scalpel spine at the caudal peduncle, the dorsal is a spiky crown rather than a long low fin running the whole back, and the forehead is a smooth round curve with none of the steep vertical profile of a tang.
rows.fix: Differentiate it from Sunfish outright: flatten the body toward an oval that is longer than tall, raise a steep near-vertical forehead over a small protruding grazing mouth, and run a single low continuous dorsal from just behind the head all the way to the peduncle (matched by a mirroring anal fin). Add the scalpel — a small hard yellow or white blade lying in a slot on the peduncle, the feature the animal is named for. Reattach the caudal as a lunate crescent joined to the body.

rows.readsAs: A generic small perched songbird — a finch or a sparrow
rows.defect: Posture is wrong: the bird is standing/perched on two visible yellow legs with a rounded upright body, not flying. The tail is a single thin dark wedge poking straight back with no fork and no outer streamers. The wings are not extended at all — just a scribed teal lens on the flank with a hard outline, so there are no long narrow swept-back wings. The bill is a small orange triangle with no wide gape. On top of all that the render is drastically undersized: the organism occupies roughly a fifth of the 440px frame, so it is a fraction of the resolution of the other birds in this batch and the detail is unreadable. Aspect reads near 1.0, nowhere near the specified 2.2.
rows.fix: Rebuild in a flying pose: horizontal body, wings spread and swept back into long narrow points, so the silhouette spans wide and gives the 2.2 aspect. Split the tail into two long tapering streamers with a deep V between them. Widen the bill into a short flat triangle with a visible gape line at the corner. Scale the whole drawing up to fill the frame like the Swan and Swordfish do.

rows.readsAs: A swan-shaped pool float or a decoy — the species reads, but as an object, not an animal
rows.defect: The neck is a straight, uniform-width white pipe angled forward — no S-curve anywhere, which is the swan's single defining line. It plugs into the body at a hard junction: the tube's edge crosses the body's edge with a visible seam and no shoulder or breast transition, so it reads as a straw stuck into a dumpling. The head is a near-perfect sphere with a perfect white circular eye. The bill is uniformly orange with no black knob or dark tip at the base. The body is a plain white dome with a grey lens pasted on it for the folded wing, again hard-outlined. The water is three concentric thin ellipse strokes — perfect geometric ovals, not water.
rows.fix: Redraw the neck as a true S: a thick base swelling out of the breast, curving back, then forward and up to the head, tapering the whole way. Blend the base into the body by widening it into the chest so there is no crossing line. Add the black basal knob/lore mask against the orange bill. Make the folded wing a raised feathered mass rising off the back rather than an outlined patch. Replace the concentric ellipse rings with irregular broken waterline strokes and a soft reflection.

rows.readsAs: The Swallow from this same batch, recoloured orange — reads as a small perched songbird
rows.defect: Same drawing as Swallow in this batch, recoloured orange — identical perched body, identical leg pose, identical flank lens with a hard outline, identical rear wedge. It fails every mustRead: no scythe-shaped crescent wings (the wings are folded and invisible), no enormous gape (small orange triangle bill), and the legs are prominently drawn and clearly visible when the reference explicitly calls for almost no visible legs. Posture is perched, not flying. The body is a plump round ball, not a cigar. Like Swallow it renders at roughly a fifth of the frame, far smaller than everything else in the batch.
rows.fix: Make it a flight silhouette and nothing else: horizontal cigar body, wings out as two stiff backswept sickles with a concave trailing edge, tail short and only shallowly notched, legs omitted entirely. Open the bill into a wide gape wedge across the front of the face. Enlarge the render to fill the frame, and make the wing geometry visibly different from the Swallow's — straighter, stiffer, no streamers.

rows.readsAs: A marlin or a sailfish-less billfish — close to swordfish but the spear shape says marlin
rows.defect: The bill is a thin round tapering spike, i.e. a marlin's spear, exactly what the note warns against — it needs to be a flat broad blade. The dorsal is a low rounded brown hump lying on the back, not a tall stiff crescent sail, and it is a separate darker shape with a visible edge where it overlaps the body rather than rising out of it. A matching brown hump sits on the belly, making the fish oddly mirror-symmetric top-to-bottom and blunting the read. The eye is a hard perfect white circle with a black pupil sitting on the surface. The body is otherwise a clean fusiform lens with a single straight pale midline highlight — smooth and scaleless as required, but flat and untextured. The forked tail is reasonable, though lobes are near-symmetric rather than crescent.
rows.fix: Widen the bill into a flattened blade — broad in side view, with a slight taper and a subtle depressed centre line — and give it a rougher edge than the polished body. Replace the dorsal hump with a tall rigid sickle rising to roughly a third of body depth near the shoulder, its base flaring into the back so there is no overlap seam. Reduce the belly hump to a small anal fin so top and bottom stop mirroring. Sink the eye into a socket with surrounding shading instead of a stamped white disc, and curve the caudal into a proper lunate crescent.

rows.readsAs: A purple cartoon budgie or baby chick
rows.defect: Three mustReads fail. (a) The bird is lavender-purple with a slightly paler face disc — there is no white plumage anywhere, and the eyes are white sclera with tiny black pupils, not brilliant yellow. (b) The feet are two bare thin yellow sticks with three splayed toes, i.e. the standard passerine leg — no feathering at all. (c) The wing is a hard-outlined lavender ellipse laid on the flank with a continuous dark stroke around it and a second dark stroke sweeping over the shoulder; it is a decal, not a wing growing out of the body — a seam blocker. The tail is a sharp dark triangular wedge poking out to the right, again with a hard edge against the body. Head is a near-perfect circle stuck on a near-perfect egg.
rows.fix: Repaint base to broken white with sparse dark barring driven by the same noise field as the body shading, not an overlay. Recolour iris to saturated chrome-yellow with a small black pupil and sink the eyes into a soft facial disc rather than ringing them with a hard outline. Replace the stick tarsi with thick feather-trousered legs that taper into a fluffy toe mass. Delete the ellipse-wing stroke entirely: build the wing as a shading gradient plus a few primary tips that break the body outline, so there is no closed contour inside the silhouette.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon tortoise on wheels
rows.defect: All three mustReads fail. The shell is a tall domed half-circle — not a flat pancake — and it is covered in concentric radiating arcs that read exactly as growth scutes, the one thing a softshell must not have. There is no tubular snorkel snout: the head is a plain orange circle with a round white eye, joined to the body by a short straight neck bar with a visible hard seam on both sides. The feet are two flat brown semicircular blobs sitting under the body like wheels — no toes, no webbing, no paddle shape. A dead-straight horizontal line runs the full width of the body where the shell meets the plastron, a machined edge.
rows.fix: Flatten the carapace to aspect ~1.8 with a soft leathery rim skirt that ripples, and delete every concentric arc — replace with a faint mottled leather grain. Extend the snout into a narrow tube roughly one head-length long with nostrils at the tip. Rebuild the feet as broad three-lobed webbed paddles whose skin is continuous with the leg. Replace the straight shell/plastron line with an irregular soft-shadowed boundary.

rows.readsAs: A generic small white bird — a dove or finch chick
rows.defect: Two mustReads fail and the render duplicates another organism in this batch. The tail is a long pointed grey wedge extending well past the body, not a short square-ended tail. The bill is a thin pointed orange triangle — a warbler/insect-eater bill, not a stout deep conical seed-cracker. Body plan, ellipse-wing-with-hard-outline, shoulder stroke, tail wedge and three-toed yellow stick legs are pixel-for-pixel the same template used for Snowy Owl and Spoonbill, only recoloured pale blue-white. The wing ellipse has a closed dark contour inside the silhouette — a stuck-on part. The whole creature also occupies only about a quarter of the 440px frame, far smaller than every other card in the batch.
rows.fix: Deepen and shorten the bill into a triangular cone as tall at the base as the eye is wide. Cut the tail to a short blunt rectangle with a squared-off end. Repaint to streaked brown/buff with a grey crown and a dark bib rather than pale blue-white. Break the shared bird template: vary body mass, wing insertion and posture per species, and remove the closed outline on the wing. Scale the subject up to fill the frame like the other cards.

rows.readsAs: A teal dolphin or a large fish
rows.defect: The defining mustRead is absent: there is no enormous square blunt head. The front of the animal tapers smoothly to a narrow point, so the head is indistinguishable from the body and reads as roughly 0 of the length rather than a third. The knuckled dorsal hump is also missing — the dorsal line is one unbroken smooth curve with no hump and no knuckles down the caudal peduncle. The blowhole is present as a small pale dot near the front-left of the top, which is correct. The lower jaw is only a faint thin line, not a narrow underslung rod. The pectoral flipper is a solid dark teal blob with a hard closed edge stamped onto the flank — a visible seam where it meets the body.
rows.fix: Rebuild the front third as a vertical-fronted box: a flat blunt leading wall with the profile dropping almost straight down, and a slight overhang above the mouth. Set a thin pencil-narrow lower jaw underslung well below and behind the head front, with a visible gape line. Replace the smooth dorsal line with a low triangular hump followed by four or five knuckles into the tail stock. Blend the flipper root into the flank with shared shading instead of a closed dark shape.

rows.readsAs: A pink tick or mite — two beads on wires
rows.defect: The explicit note is violated: legs spring from the abdomen. The two rightmost legs emerge from beneath the large spotted rear sphere, well behind the front body. Leg count is wrong — I count six visible legs (three left, one mid, two rear-right), not eight. The legs are dead-straight thin rods with no joint and no arch-up-then-down; they read as wires, not limbs, and each meets the body at a point with no coxa or muscle mass. The two body parts are two smooth spheres abutting with a visible seam rather than a waisted pedicel. The abdomen spots are flat dark blobs sprayed on the surface, unaffected by the sphere's shading.
rows.fix: Attach all eight legs to the cephalothorax only, in four pairs fanning forward and back. Give each leg a real bend: rise from the body, peak above the abdomen line, then angle down to a fine tarsus tip, with the femur visibly thicker than the tibia. Narrow the join between the two body sections into a pinched waist. Make the abdomen markings follow the sphere's curvature and lighting so they sit in the skin.

rows.readsAs: A pink gorilla or macaque
rows.defect: Two of three mustReads fail. The limbs are short stubby blobs, not extremely long spindly limbs — the arms are stumps barely clearing the hip and the legs are two rounded lumps under a barrel torso. The tail is thick, curls up to the left, and is at most body-length, not longer than the whole animal. The build is a bulky heavy-shouldered ape with no pot belly distinction, and the hands are not visible at all, so the hook-not-thumb note cannot read. The pale ventral streaks look airbrushed on top of the magenta rather than being a fur colour change, and there is a hard-edged pale patch between the legs. The tail meets the hip at a hard join.
rows.fix: Rescale limbs to roughly 1.5x torso length and thin them to spindles with visible elbow and knee bends; end each arm in a curved four-finger hook with no thumb. Lengthen the tail to about 1.3x head-plus-body, taper it, and add a bare pale gripping patch on the underside of the distal third. Slim the shoulders and add a distinct rounded belly beneath a narrow chest, with the head kept small. Make the pale ventral fur a gradient in the fur shader following body curvature, not an overlaid patch, and blend the tail root into the rump.

rows.readsAs: A terracotta plant pot or a cooling tower
rows.defect: The 'no symmetry of any kind' mustRead fails outright: this is a perfectly bilaterally symmetric truncated cone with smooth machined flaring sides and a flawless elliptical rim finished with a clean grey lip — an obvious geometric primitive. The 'large osculum holes on the surface' mustRead also fails: there is one osculum (the top opening) and the surface carries only small speckled dots that read as sprayed-on freckles, not as openings — they have no rim, no depth and no shadow. The orange gradient is even and machined, top-lit uniformly.
rows.fix: Break the silhouette: bow the walls unevenly, add one or two secondary tubes budding off at different heights, and make the rim an irregular wavy lip rather than a true ellipse. Delete the grey rim stroke. Replace speckles with actual osculum holes — dark interiors with a lit upper rim and a cast shadow inside each — of varying size, plus a fine irregular pitted texture between them. Randomise the wall thickness so no two sides mirror.

rows.readsAs: A dark chicken with a spoon in its beak
rows.defect: The 'long neck' mustRead fails: the head sits directly on the shoulders with no neck whatsoever — the profile goes straight from crown to back. 'Bare face skin' also fails: the face is the same flat charcoal as the body with no bare patch or colour break. The bill is the one good element — flat, flaring to a rounded spatula tip — but it is a solid yellow shape butted against a dark round head at a hard seam, so it reads as a wooden spoon held in the mouth rather than bone growing from the skull. The body is the same shared template as Snowy Owl and Sparrow: identical ellipse wing with a closed dark outline, identical shoulder stroke, identical pointed tail wedge, only recoloured grey. Colour is wrong too — spoonbills are white or pink, not charcoal.
rows.fix: Insert a neck of roughly 1.5 head-lengths in a shallow S, thickening smoothly into the chest. Give the face a bare skin mask around the eye and bill base in a contrasting flesh tone, with the bill's colour and texture continuous into that skin so there is no seam. Slim the body and lengthen the wing so the folded primaries reach the tail base, and drop the closed dark ellipse outline. Repaint white-to-rose rather than charcoal, and stop reusing the passerine body template for a long-legged wader.

rows.readsAs: a small pink prawn or brine shrimp
rows.defect: Renders as a tiny generic pink prawn floating in the middle of a mostly empty 440px frame (the animal occupies barely 25% of the width). None of the three mustReads are present: there is no broad flat shield carapace over the front half — just a rounded pink blob head-lump; the two long thin filaments are drawn at the FRONT sweeping forward like prawn antennae rather than as forked caudal filaments off the tail; and instead of dozens of wriggling leaf legs there are four short dark hair-strokes under the belly. The rear ends in a curled fan/telson (a caridean shrimp tail), not a tapered abdomen with a forked furca. The eyes are a single dark spot on the side of the head, not the paired dark eyes sitting close together on top of a shield that the note calls out. Body reads as two smooth gradient balloons with hard-edged fin flaps stuck to the back end.
rows.fix: Rebuild the front half as one wide, low, dorsally-convex shield plate whose outline is a flattened D — widest across the middle, edges thin and translucent, overhanging the leg mass so the legs are seen THROUGH/under it. Sink the two dark eyes as a close-set pair on the top surface of that shield. Move the two long filaments to the rear as a symmetric fork trailing off the last abdominal segment and delete the forward-sweeping antennae. Replace the four hair-strokes with a dense phyllopod rank — 30+ overlapping translucent leaf paddles in a graded row under the shield, each fading into the body rather than terminating at a line. Kill the fan tail. Scale the whole animal up ~1.8x to fill the frame.

rows.readsAs: a grey langur or macaque sitting facing the viewer
rows.defect: The body is a smooth white egg/capsule with grey blotches airbrushed on top — the blotching does not follow any fur direction and reads as sprayed decal, not pelage. Both arms are flat dark-grey tubes stuck onto the sides of the egg with a visible hard seam at the shoulder, and the two thigh blobs are separate lighter ovals overlaid on the belly rather than growing out of it. The mustRead 'clawed fingers gripping a thin branch' is entirely absent — there is no branch anywhere in the frame, and the limbs end in blunt rounded stumps with no fingers or claws at all. The mane reads as a ring of identical small circles laid in a perfect arc around the head, a bead necklace rather than hair. Posture is a front-facing seated blob, not the quadruped the row asks for. Tail is present and long but attaches at a hard dark line on the hip.
rows.fix: Pose it quadrupedally in profile on a thin diagonal branch and give it real hands: four slender digits plus a claw wrapping the branch, with the branch passing behind the far hand. Replace the egg silhouette with a narrow-chested, long-limbed squirrel-sized body — shoulders narrower than hips, spine slightly arched. Grow the arms out of the torso by carrying the fur gradient across the shoulder joint and breaking the seam with overlapping fur strokes. Convert the blotches to directional fur lanes that follow the body contour. Rebuild the mane as irregular radiating hair tufts of varying length (or a drooping white moustache) instead of a circle of beads.

rows.readsAs: a generic small mint-green finch or sparrow
rows.defect: The wing is a hard-edged dark-teal teardrop laid flat on the flank with a crisp outline all the way round — it reads as a sticker on the body, not a folded wing growing from the shoulder. The tail is a single flat dark-green triangle wedge that meets the body at a straight machined line, and it is pointed rather than the squared tail the row asks for. Plumage is a soft mint/seafoam gradient, which fails 'brilliantly saturated block-coloured' — there are no colour BLOCKS at all, just one wash from mint to dark teal. The bill is short and conical, which is correct, but it is a flat orange triangle with straight edges and no culmen curve or gape line. Head-to-body is right and the yellow scaly feet are convincingly done.
rows.fix: Split the plumage into hard-bounded saturated blocks (scarlet body against a jet-black wing-and-tail, or a tanager's black bib/back) instead of a single gradient. Redraw the wing with feather groups — coverts, then a stack of primaries — whose leading edge tucks under the flank contour so there is no closed outline. Square off the tail into 4-6 overlapping rectrices of near-equal length and let the upper-tail coverts overlap the base so the join disappears. Round the culmen of the bill slightly and add a gape line.

rows.readsAs: a silvery pomfret or moonfish
rows.defect: The dorsal fin is a row of five identical sharp-cornered triangles — a machined sawtooth crown — sitting on top of the back with a straight baseline, clearly a geometric primitive stuck on rather than a membranous fin. The pectoral fin is likewise a hard-edged folded fan with straight radiating creases and a visible outline against the flank. The caudal fin is detached: there is a clear dark gap between the body and the tail, so the tail floats behind the fish. The mustRead 'sharp tail-base spine' is missing entirely — the caudal peduncle is bare with no scalpel. The snout is blunt and rounded with no visible mouth, failing 'small pointed grazing snout'. Colour is pale silver-blue gradient rather than a tang's saturated blue or yellow.
rows.fix: Replace the triangle row with one continuous dorsal membrane whose spines are internal ribs under a translucent web, running from just behind the head and merging smoothly into the dorsal contour. Close the caudal gap: build a real peduncle that narrows out of the body and carries the crescent tail, and set the scalpel spine as a small forward-pointing blade on that peduncle. Pull the snout forward into a short blunt-pointed grazing muzzle with a small terminal mouth. Recolour to a saturated royal-blue body with a black-and-yellow tail, or an all-yellow tang. Soften the pectoral into a translucent lobe fading into the flank.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon tick or a toy spider
rows.defect: Two perfect pink spheres in a row with thin bare sticks for legs — this is a geometric primitive assembly, not an animal. The legs are dead-straight bald lines of uniform width with no taper, no joints, and above all NO HAIR, which fails the 'eight thick densely hairy legs' mustRead outright. Legs sprout from the ABDOMEN (the rear sphere clearly carries three of them, two rising off its top edge), contradicting the note that the front section carries all eight; and I count six legs, not eight. There are no fangs and no pedipalps of any kind — the front of the cephalothorax is a blank sphere with four small dark eye dots painted on the smooth surface. The abdomen carries a few soft airbrushed darker patches that read as sprayed-on shading rather than skin markings.
rows.fix: Rebuild with eight legs, all eight attaching to the cephalothorax in two ranks of four, each leg tapering through femur-patella-tibia-tarsus with a visible knee bend and a downward-hooked foot. Cover every leg and both body sections in dense radiating setae so the silhouette is fuzzy, never a clean line. Deflate both spheres: make the cephalothorax a low domed disc with a fovea dimple and the abdomen a soft egg with a hairy fringe, not a ball. Add two short leg-like pedipalps flanking the front and a pair of downward-stabbing chelicerae with visible fangs below the eye cluster. Set the eight eyes as a graded cluster of two sizes on a raised ocular tubercle.

rows.readsAs: a water bear / tardigrade — recognisable, but a teal plastic one
rows.defect: Silhouette and leg count are broadly right, but the colour is flatly wrong: saturated opaque teal instead of the specified translucent amber-tan with darker gut contents showing through — nothing shows through, the body is a solid slab. The two dark circles on the head lobe read as a pair of EYES on a face, not as the round tubular sucking mouth; there is no terminal mouth at the front of the snout at all. The head is a separate rounded lobe joined to the barrel by a visible seam line where the two shapes overlap. Segmentation is six thin straight vertical scratch-lines sprayed across the flank; they do not bulge the outline, so the silhouette stays a smooth featureless dome instead of a lumpy segmented barrel. The stubby legs are plain cones with tiny notches and no bunch of curved claws. The rearmost pair points down like the others rather than backward.
rows.fix: Recolour to translucent amber-tan and paint a mottled darker green-brown gut mass visible through the cuticle. Move the mouth to the very front of the snout as a round protruding tube ringed by a lip, and delete the two face-circles (or shrink them to tiny lateral eyespots). Make each of the four to five segments push the dorsal outline into a distinct lobe so the barrel is visibly bumpy in silhouette, and let the transverse folds wrap the body in curves rather than straight lines. Terminate each leg in a splayed bunch of four to six curved claws. Rotate the rear pair to point backward. Blend the head lobe into the first body segment so the seam disappears.

rows.readsAs: a tuna or mackerel
rows.defect: A smooth purple torpedo with a flat gradient flank and ZERO scales — the 'huge silver-dollar plate scales' mustRead, which is the single most identifying feature of a tarpon, is completely absent; the body has no surface texture whatsoever. The 'upturned bulldog lower jaw' is also absent: the head tapers to a sharp forward-pointing cone with the mouth line running straight and horizontal, giving a mackerel profile rather than a scooping upturned mandible. The 'long trailing filament off the rear of the dorsal fin' is missing — the dorsal is a barely-visible dark smudge on the back with no ray extension at all. The pectoral fin is a hard-edged triangle with straight crease lines stuck on the flank. The forked tail joins the body across a straight vertical seam. Overall aspect and the large eye are right.
rows.fix: Tile the flank with large overlapping circular plate scales, each catching a specular highlight, big enough to count across the body depth. Rebuild the head: shorten and blunt the snout, drop the jaw hinge back under the eye, and angle the lower jaw up and forward past the upper so it juts. Draw a proper triangular dorsal fin at mid-back and extend its last ray into a long whip filament trailing well past the caudal peduncle. Grow the pectoral out of a fleshy base with translucent rays fading into the flank, and taper the peduncle into the tail so the vertical seam disappears.

rows.readsAs: a teal cartoon newt or salamander
rows.defect: None of the three mustReads land. The head is a plain smooth teal oval with no jowls, no cheek mass, no jaw definition — the opposite of a 'massive jowled blocky head' — and it is joined to the body by an obvious hard seam where the oval overlaps the torso. The body is a featureless egg with grey dots airbrushed onto it in a random scatter; there is no banding whatsoever and no beaded scale texture, the dots read as sprayed paint on a smooth surface. Only two legs are drawn and they are short blunt cylinders stuck under the belly with visible attachment seams, ending in no feet or toes — the sprawling posture is not readable. The tail is a fat uniform-width tube with a dark racing-stripe painted down its centre, and it attaches to the body at a hard line. The whole thing reads as three overlapping ovals plus two pegs. It is also the same saturated teal as the Tardigrade in this same batch, and at a glance the two could be mistaken for each other.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as a wedge-shaped block, deep at the jaw with bulging masseter jowls, tapering to a blunt snout, and merge it into the neck so no seam shows. Replace the sprayed dots with a beaded scale field — small raised granular scales catching individual highlights — organised into transverse dark bands running down the body and continuing onto the tail. Draw all four legs in a proper sprawl: elbows and knees out to the sides, feet flat on the ground with five splayed clawed toes each. Taper the tail from a thick base to a fine tip, band it, and drop the painted centre stripe. Shift the palette off teal toward black-and-white or olive tegu tones so it stops colliding with the Tardigrade.

rows.readsAs: A pale maggot or a woodlouse grub with wire legs and one loose wire at the back
rows.defect: The furcula mustRead is not delivered: instead of a forked spring latched flat under the abdomen there is a single unforked white wire that loops out from behind the rear of the body and hangs in open space below/behind it — it reads as a stray hair or a detached wire artifact, not an organ. The six legs are identical thin grey hairpin sticks with no femur/tibia taper, planted on the underside with a hard butt-joint where each meets the pale body; nothing grows out. The antennae are two straight grey rods with no beads/segments. The head does not exist as a form — there is no cranial mass, just a single black dot placed on the front of an egg. Body is a smooth pale egg with four evenly spaced arc lines painted across it, which read as sprayed-on stripes rather than segment overlaps (no thickness, no shadow at each segment edge).
rows.fix: Replace the trailing wire with a genuine forked furcula: two short prongs from the 4th abdominal segment, tucked FORWARD under the belly and clipped by a tenaculum, so it sits inside the silhouette rather than trailing. Build the head as a separate rounded capsule narrower than the thorax with a visible neck constriction, and put the eye patch (ocelli cluster) on it. Give antennae 4 visible beads with slight droop. Rebuild segment lines as overlapping tergite plates with a dark under-shadow and a highlight lip on each, and taper the legs (thicker at the coxa, hairs at the tarsus) with the body wall bulging into them.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon alien jellyfish or a standing octopus mascot
rows.defect: Three mustReads fail. (a) No triangular fins at a pointed rear — the mantle is a blunt vertical egg and the 'fins' are a single flat dark translucent ellipse pasted BEHIND the mantle like a halo/disc, symmetric and detached-looking, reading as a hat brim or a jellyfish bell rim rather than two muscular triangular fins on a pointed tail. (b) The rear is rounded, not pointed, so there is no torpedo. (c) The two long clubbed tentacles are indistinguishable in kind from the arms — they are two thin lines that shoot out almost horizontally to the far left and right frame edges with no club paddle, while two other arms end in small round knobs at the bottom, so the club is on the wrong pair. Arms attach as tubes butted onto the mantle base with a visible hard boundary; there is no arm crown, no web, no funnel. Both eyes are placed frontally like a cartoon face with white catchlights instead of a single large lateral eye. Posture is upright and standing on its arms, not swimming, and the aspect reads ~0.9 tall not 3.2 long.
rows.fix: Rotate to a horizontal swimming attitude. Rebuild the mantle as a true torpedo that narrows to a point at the rear, and grow two triangular fins directly out of that point as continuations of the mantle wall (shared gradient, no outline). Put ONE large lateral eye at the base of the arms in true profile with a horizontal-slit or W pupil. Make eight arms of graduated length forming a cone with a webbed base merging into the mantle collar, and give the TWO longest tentacles a widened spatulate club with sucker rows. Add the funnel under the collar. Kill the dark ellipse behind the head entirely.

rows.readsAs: A blue cartoon rabbit or chinchilla
rows.defect: The signature feature is wrong: the tail is a smooth blue banana/comma of solid gel with one lighter highlight stripe down it and a perfectly clean silhouette — no fur strands, no plume flare, no breakup at the edge. A squirrel without a bushy tail is not a squirrel. Posture also fails the mustRead: the animal is on all fours in a crouch, not sitting on its haunches, and there are no forepaws and no food — the front limb is a tiny blue nub. There is a hard dark arc seam across the shoulder where the head sphere is welded to the body sphere; the head is a separate ball stuck on. Ears are two flat grey triangular slivers pasted on top of the skull with no ear base or pinna bowl. Whiskers are three straight lines emerging from a small white rectangle at the muzzle — a literal white box for a nose/teeth. Body is two smooth spheres, entirely furless.
rows.fix: Rebuild the tail as a plumed mass: an S-curve armature arched up and over the back with fur tufts breaking the outline on both edges and a lighter fringe, wide at the middle, not a solid tube. Sit the animal upright on its haunches with the spine vertical, big hind feet flat, and two small forepaws held at the chest gripping a nut. Merge head into body with a fur-broken cheek/shoulder transition instead of the arc seam. Replace the white rectangle with a rounded dark nose plus incisors, and root the whiskers in whisker pads. Give the ears a bowl and a tuft. Add a fur-shaded coat with a pale belly instead of flat gradient.

rows.readsAs: A five-pointed starfish — the family reads, but as a flat cut-out sticker rather than a live animal
rows.defect: The radial structure is fake: the five arms are five straight flat wedge strokes laid down independently and they visibly CROSS each other in the middle — the lower-left and lower-right arms overlap in an X over the central region, and the upper-left arm passes over the disc — so there is no central disc that the arms grow from, just intersecting paint strokes. Each arm terminates in a squared-off chisel tip with a hard straight cut across it and a small bevel corner, a machined edge rather than a rounded taper. Arms barely taper at all — they are near constant-width bars. The 'pebbled granular skin' is a scatter of soft white dots airbrushed on top of the flat orange gradient, uniform in size and unrelated to the arm axis, reading as sprayed bokeh. No tube-feet grooves anywhere, no madreporite, and the arms are unnaturally thin and long relative to a near-absent disc.
rows.fix: Construct from a central pentagonal disc first, then grow five arms as continuous outward swells of that disc so the outline is one closed curve with concave notches between arms (no crossings). Taper each arm to a rounded, slightly upturned tip — remove the flat cut ends. Replace the dot spray with an ossicle pattern: paired rows of raised granular plates following the arm's long axis, densest along the ridge, plus a shallow ambulacral groove line down each arm underside. Add the off-centre madreporite spot on the disc.

rows.readsAs: A robin or a generic red songbird chick
rows.defect: Two of three mustReads are absent. The plumage is flat salmon/brick red with a smooth gradient — no glossy iridescent black, and not one pale spot anywhere. The bill is a short blunt yellow triangle wedge, not a sharp straight pointed bill; it is a solid facet with a straight top edge stuck onto the front of the head with a visible colour boundary. Posture is standing on two thin yellow stick legs on the ground, not flying — no wings extended, no triangular wing shape. The wing is a single smooth teardrop plate outlined on the flank by a hard dark seam, sitting on the body like a decal; there are no coverts, no primaries, no feather groups. The tail is one dark solid spike, not a short square tail. Legs are bare yellow lines with a hard joint at the belly. The whole bird occupies maybe a quarter of the 440px frame, so it renders tiny and undersubscribed.
rows.fix: Recolour to the dark iridescent base with green/purple sheen and stipple pale buff-tipped spots across mantle, breast and flanks (spots as feather-tip terminations, aligned with feather tracts, not random dots). Lengthen and sharpen the bill to a straight fine dagger, yellow, merged into the face with feathering over the base. Put the bird in flight per the row: swept-back triangular wings with visible primaries, short square-cut tail fanned, legs tucked. Dissolve the wing outline into overlapping covert rows. Scale the subject up to fill the frame.

rows.readsAs: A blade of grass or a green leafhopper with a bead for a head
rows.defect: It is not twig-like at all: the body is a single smooth flat lance/leaf blade, widest just behind the head and tapering to a needle point at the right, with a uniform glossy green gradient and one continuous unbroken outline — it reads as a blade of grass or a leaf, not a cylindrical segmented stick. There is no thorax/abdomen division, no segmentation whatsoever along its whole length. A perfectly spherical ball head is welded to the blunt front end with a hard circular seam and a bulging silhouette step where sphere meets blade. The legs mustRead fails: there are only about four short green bristles hanging straight down under the front third, all the same length, with no femur/tibia/tarsus joints — nowhere near the long spindly legs stretched in line with the body, and the rear half of the animal has no legs at all. The antennae are two short forked hairs, not long thin straight antennae. A single black dot serves as the eye.
rows.fix: Rebuild the body as a cylinder with visible node/internode segmentation and slight irregular kinks so it reads as a twig, uniform in width rather than blade-tapered, with bark-like mottling in the skin itself. Attach six long legs at the thorax only: the front pair extended FORWARD alongside the antennae in the classic stick pose, mid and hind pairs swept back along the body, each with a clear femur-tibia elbow and thin tarsus. Extend the antennae to at least head+thorax length, straight and fine. Replace the ball head with an elongated head capsule flowing into the prothorax with no circular seam.

rows.readsAs: A green paper kite or a lily pad with eyes
rows.defect: Off-body artifacts: two small grey-white blobs float in empty space clear of the silhouette, one left of the disc and one at the right wingtip, attached to nothing. The cast shadow is also badly misregistered — the ellipse sits low and far to the RIGHT of the body, so the ray appears to hover detached from its own shadow. The disc is not a kite of fused pectorals: it is a hard triangle with two straight machined leading edges meeting at a sharp apex and two sharp corner points at the wingtips, with a visible straight highlight line along the top-left edge like a folded paper kite. The tail is a thin dark line that meets the disc bottom at a hard T-junction with no tail base or pelvic fins, and the barb is a flat cream arrowhead/spearhead pasted at the extreme tip — a separate colour, no serration, no continuity with the tail. The two eyes are cartoon face dots with catchlights placed on the flat top plane; there is no spiracle behind either eye and no hint of the snout. Pale spots are uniform soft dots airbrushed over the gradient.
rows.fix: Delete the two floating blobs and re-anchor the shadow directly beneath the disc centroid. Redraw the disc as a single continuous curved outline — convex leading edges sweeping from a rounded snout, rounded wingtips, concave trailing edge — so the pectorals read as fused and flexible, with a subtle wing-flap undulation. Grow the tail out of a thickening tail base continuous with the disc (no T-joint), with the barb as a serrated keratin spine emerging from the tail's own material at mid-tail, same colour family. Add spiracles behind the eyes and set the eyes as raised bumps on the dorsal surface. Replace dot spray with a skin-denticle mottling that follows the disc curvature.

rows.readsAs: A wasp or hoverfly with fan-blade wings
rows.defect: The defining mustRead is inverted: the wings are NOT folded flat and overlapping down the back — three separate translucent grey blades splay outward and backward from a single point on the thorax like fan slats, well clear of the body, showing daylight between them and the abdomen. They read as glass shards pinned on, each with a hard straight leading edge and a sharp point. There are also no tail cerci at all, and no long antennae — the head carries only a large black eye with a catchlight and a couple of tiny curls. The legs are three short hooked bristles crowded under the thorax, all on the front, none behind. The abdomen is a string of four flat orange lozenge segments with black gaps between them, reading as a painted stripe pattern on a sausage rather than tergites. The head is a plain round ball, not a flat squarish head, joined to the thorax by a hard colour boundary. Finally the body floats: the cast shadow ellipse sits roughly a body-and-a-half BELOW the insect with a large empty gap, so nothing is grounded despite the crawling posture.
rows.fix: Lay the wings flat and overlapping down the back so the hindwing pleats fold under the forewing and the pair sits inside the abdomen silhouette, with visible cross-vein network rather than blank glass. Add two short stout cerci projecting straight back from the abdomen tip. Give long multi-segmented antennae at least half body length forward from the head. Flatten and squared the head, widen the pronotum into a distinct rectangular plate, and spread six sprawling legs — two forward, two lateral, two rearward — with real joints. Re-seat the shadow directly under the tarsi so the crawling pose contacts the ground, and rebuild the abdomen banding as overlapping segment plates with edge shadow.

rows.readsAs: A kingfisher, or just a generic teal garden songbird — nobody would say woodpecker
rows.defect: It is a small teal ground-perching songbird standing side-on on a flat cast shadow — none of the three mustReads are present. There is no trunk anywhere in the frame, so nothing is being clung to; the two thin yellow stick legs are planted horizontally on the ground in a perching stance, not splayed against bark. The tail is a single thin dark wedge streaming backwards and slightly DOWN off the rump, soft and drooping — not a stiff, spread, pointed prop braced against anything. The bill is a smooth yellow CONE that tapers to a needle point, not a straight-sided chisel with a blunt cutting tip. Proportion is also inverted against the reference: the painted bird is clearly wider than tall (body oval roughly 90px wide by 70px tall, ~1.3 aspect) where the row asks for 0.6, i.e. a tall vertical clinger. Two further paint problems: the wing is a set of concentric teal crescent outlines sitting on the flank like a sticker — a closed swirl with its own hard outer edge that never merges into the body shading — and the whole body is a plain rounded egg with a smoothly appended neck bulge, so it reads as a generic-bird primitive with decoration rather than a woodpecker. The only thing that gestures at the reference is a tiny cluster of dark spiky tufts on the crown.
rows.fix: Repose entirely: rotate to a vertical trunk-clinging pose (long axis vertical, aspect ~0.6) and paint an actual bark trunk column behind the bird so the pose has something to grip. Replace the perching leg pair with two short zygodactyl feet gripping the trunk at chest height, toes wrapping the bark edge. Rebuild the tail as a stiff, fanned wedge of stacked pointed rectrices angled DOWN-and-IN so its tip contacts the trunk and takes weight (visible bend/compression at the contact). Rebuild the bill from a cone to a straight-sided chisel: parallel dorsal and ventral edges, blunt chisel tip, and set it dead horizontal into the skull with feathering carried over the bill base instead of a clean join. Delete the concentric crescent wing decal and repaint the wing as folded covert rows whose feather tips overlap the flank shading with no closed outer contour. Add the red nape/crown patch called out in the note in place of the grey tuft.

rows.readsAs: A generic minnow or small herring — a plain striped baitfish, not a wrasse
rows.defect: Two of the three mustReads are absent. There are NO buck teeth: the snout ends in a bare pointed spike with no mouth line, no lips and no protruding incisors at all — the head just tapers to a point like a leaf tip. The pectoral fin is a small dark triangular sliver tucked low behind the gill, roughly a tenth of the body length; it is nowhere near a large fan doing the swimming, and it is painted as a flat darker triangle laid ON the flank rather than a translucent rayed fan emerging from a socket.
