Body shape is also wrong for the row: it is a flat almond/lens — pointed at BOTH ends, widest exactly at mid-length — not a cigar, so it has no rounded blunt head mass and no distinct caudal peduncle. The construction shows: the dorsal fin is a separate dark triangle dropped on the topline with a visible straight seam where its base meets the back, and the tail is a fan joined to the body across a hard vertical cut with a step in the silhouette — both read as parts stuck on. The flank markings are three or four flat, perfectly straight horizontal bands running the full length and terminating abruptly at the outline, which reads as spray-on striping rather than scale-borne pattern. The eye is a hard white circle with a black dot, a geometric primitive with no lid, socket or surrounding tissue. Aspect (~2.9 measured) and head fraction are acceptable; everything else is not.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head: give it a blunt rounded wrasse forehead and a thick-lipped terminal mouth, then paint the protruding buck incisors as two forward-jutting ivory teeth breaking the lip line in silhouette so they show at thumbnail size. Fatten the body from a lens to a cigar — move the widest point forward to just behind the gill, keep the depth roughly constant through the mid-body, and taper to a narrow peduncle so the tail no longer needs a straight cut. Scale the pectoral to 25-30 percent of body length and repaint it as a translucent rayed fan in mid-oar sweep, with its base disappearing under overlapping flank scales instead of ending on a triangle edge. Remove the dorsal fin's straight base seam: run a fin membrane down from the spines into the dorsal ridge with the body colour bleeding up into it. Break the stripes so they follow scale rows, vary in width, and fade before the outline. Replace the circular eye decal with an eye set into a shaded orbital, with an iris ring and a highlight offset from centre.

rows.readsAs: a generic purple fish — the same fish as the Tuna next to it, with spots
rows.defect: No adipose fin anywhere between the dorsal and the tail — I scanned the whole dorsal margin and it is a clean unbroken curve, so a mustRead is simply absent. The tail is a deep symmetric V (the fork cuts nearly a third of the way back into the caudal peduncle), not the squared-off shallow-forked trout tail the row calls for. The 'speckles' are ~12 soft grey-brown ellipses of wildly different sizes airbrushed on top of the purple flank — one of them sits partly over the pectoral fin, which proves they are an overlay layer and not skin. Body is a symmetric almond/lens: the dorsal and ventral curves mirror each other, so there is no belly and no head taper — the snout is a point, not a jaw. Strip the spots and this is pixel-for-pixel the same hull as the Tuna in this batch.
rows.fix: Add a small fleshy adipose lobe on the dorsal midline about 80% back, growing out of the back with no outline. Recut the caudal to a shallow notch (fork depth ~10-12% of fin length) with squared lobe tips. Replace the airbrushed ellipses with dense small spots that follow the body's shading — vary density (packed above the lateral line, sparse on the belly), give the darker ones a pale halo, and clip them out of the fins. Break the lens symmetry: raise the dorsal profile behind the head, drop and round the belly, blunt the snout.

rows.readsAs: a white sea anemone or a bundle of twigs sitting in a plastic funnel / eggcup
rows.defect: The tube is a truncated cone with dead-straight sides and a perfect elliptical rim — a lathed funnel, an obvious geometric primitive. Its base is a flat horizontal cut floating above the shadow ellipse with nothing joining it to any substrate, so the 'anchored to the substrate' mustRead does not read; it looks set down on a table. Proportion is wrong for aspect 0.3: the tube is squat (roughly as wide at the mouth as it is tall) instead of a long stiff tube. The plume is a fan of white branched sticks of uniform width that spring out of the black opening with no visible crown or attachment — they read as twigs stuck in a cup rather than gills on a radiole stalk.
rows.fix: Give the tube an irregular, slightly bowed profile with a few growth-collar bulges and a chipped/uneven rim instead of a clean ellipse; extend it to roughly 3x its current height so the silhouette is tall and narrow. Splay the base into an irregular calcareous foot that merges into the substrate. Taper each radiole from thick base to fine tip and hang short side-barbs off it so the plume reads feathery, and let the radioles converge into a visible stalk sitting in the tube mouth.

rows.readsAs: a generic purple fish — indistinguishable from the Trout in this batch with the spots removed
rows.defect: No finlets at all — the dorsal and ventral margins between the second fin and the tail are smooth, so the row of small yellow finlets (a mustRead, and the single most diagnostic tuna cue) is missing. The tail is a wide symmetric V with straight trailing edges, not a stiff lunate crescent, and it meets the body through a thin unmarked pinch with no keel. The fins are flat semi-transparent dark triangles laid over the flank — the dorsal one visibly darkens the body beneath it, so it is a stuck-on decal, not a fin growing out of the back. The body is the same lens/almond as the Trout: mirror-symmetric top and bottom, no deep-chested shoulder, no thickest-point-forward taper.
rows.fix: Add 7-8 small triangular finlets stepping down the dorsal and ventral margins to the tail, in a warm yellow that reads against the body. Recut the caudal into a swept crescent (curved trailing edge, tips raked backwards past the fin root) and add the keel: a thin horizontal ridge on the peduncle either side of the tail base. Sink the pectoral and first dorsal into shallow grooves so they emerge from the flesh instead of sitting on it. Deepen the body just behind the head and taper hard to the peduncle so the mass sits forward.

rows.readsAs: a chick or a small quail — a generic round yellow bird
rows.defect: The head is a smooth golden ball with a tiny triangular beak and one dot eye — there is no bare warty skin, no red-and-blue caruncling, no snood, no dangling wattle, and no bristly beard on the breast. Three of the three mustReads are absent. The wing is drawn as a concentric ring/spiral oval outlined in hard dark brown pasted flat on the flank; it reads as a painted snail shell or a target decal, and its outline cuts a hard closed seam across the body rather than a wing folding against the ribs. The tail is a flat spray of separate blade-shaped feathers projecting sideways from a single point behind the body, with a visible junction where they all meet the rump. Head-to-body proportion and the plain round body read as a chick.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head: bare knobbly skin in red/blue, a fleshy snood hanging over the beak, a lobed wattle under the chin, and caruncles down the throat, all in a different surface treatment from the feathered body. Hang a coarse black bristle tuft from the mid-breast. Replace the concentric-ring wing with layered coverts and primaries whose tips overlap and break the body outline, and drop the hard outline. Fan the tail upright behind the bird as an overlapping semicircle of banded feathers whose quills disappear under the rump coverts. Thicken the neck so the head sits on a heavier body.

rows.readsAs: a computer mouse, or a toy armadillo on wheels
rows.defect: The legs are two flat grey rounded blobs floating below the shell in a completely different colour and material from the body, with no join to it at all — they read as caster wheels under a computer mouse. Only two legs exist and neither has a foot, toe or scale. The head is an egg-shaped ball that abuts the shell rim at a hard vertical seam with no neck between them; nothing emerges, it is butted on. The shell pattern is a machined radial grid — perfectly concentric arcs crossed by evenly spaced spokes, drawn in uniform thin lines that ignore the shell's shading, so it reads as an engineered dome or a stadium roof rather than keratin scutes. There is no plastron line, no tail, and the shell's lower edge is a dead-straight horizontal cut.
rows.fix: Grow four scaly legs out from under the shell rim: thicker at the shoulder, elephantine, with overlapping scale plates and blunt clawed feet, in the same skin material and palette as the head. Add a wrinkled neck of a few visible folds between head and shell so the head is clearly extended out of the carapace, and let the shell rim overhang it. Replace the radial grid with irregular polygonal scutes — a central row of five, costals either side, a marginal ring at the rim — of unequal sizes with soft seams that follow the dome's curvature. Curve and scallop the lower shell margin and add a short tapered tail.

rows.readsAs: a moth
rows.defect: This is a moth, not a bat. The two long thin tapered spikes rising from the head read as insect antennae, not ears — they are needle-thin and curve outward like a moth's. The face is a blank teardrop with two round glowing eyes and nothing else: no nose pad, no muzzle, no mouth, no fangs — all three mustReads (pig nose pad, pointed ears plus conical muzzle, long thumbs) are missing. The wings are two smooth triangular blades with a scalloped lower edge, containing no arm, no wrist and no finger struts; each meets the torso along a hard straight seam so it is pasted on, not an arm membrane. There is a thin stray stick projecting left from the left wing at mid-height that connects to nothing — an off-body artifact. The two legs are bare wires with no feet.
rows.fix: Replace the antennae with broad triangular ears set on the crown, thick at the base and merging into the skull. Build a face: a short conical muzzle projecting forward, a flat wrinkled nose pad with two slit nostrils and explicitly no nose-leaf, and small paired front incisors. Rebuild each wing around visible bones — humerus to elbow to wrist, then four long finger struts fanning to the tips with the membrane sagging in scallops between them — and put a hooked thumb claw at each wrist leading edge. Anchor the membrane's trailing edge to the ankle so wing and leg are one continuous animal. Delete the stray spur on the left wing.

rows.readsAs: a feathered dart or a crossbow bolt — or an insect pupa with two antennae
rows.defect: Nothing in this picture is a cephalopod. It is a horizontal brown spindle with a gold rim light, a large pointed dart-shaped fin assembly on the left end, and on the right two thin bare stalks each capped with a small ball. There is no webbed cloak, no arms, no eyes of any kind, and no ear-like flap fins on the mantle — all three mustReads are absent, and the 'prominent eyes' spec is unmet because there are no eyes drawn at all. The two stalks join the body at abrupt hard seams and taper to knobs, reading as antennae or insect legs. The body is a smooth featureless capsule with a single seam ring around its middle, and the left-hand point is a flat faceted arrow with straight machined edges. Posture is horizontal like a fish, not the bell-shaped cloaked posture of the animal.
rows.fix: Start over from the animal's shape: a short bell-shaped mantle with a pair of large rounded ear-flap fins set high on its sides, then eight arms of even length descending from under it, all joined by a continuous dark web so the whole lower body is one cape with the arm tips just breaking its scalloped edge. Line the inner web with paired cirri. Put two very large spherical eyes with red-glowing pupils on the head between mantle and web, sized to roughly a sixth of body height. Kill the horizontal dart silhouette and the two ball-tipped stalks entirely.

rows.readsAs: a green spider or a tick
rows.defect: The carapace is a mathematically perfect circle — the most obvious geometric primitive in this batch — with three or four soft grey smudges airbrushed on it that do not follow the sphere's shading. It is bright saturated green, not the ghost-white unpigmented carapace the row requires. Only four walking legs are drawn (two per side, should be eight), and each is a straight rigid stick with evenly spaced ladder rungs painted across it, meeting the circle at a hard point contact with no shoulder or coxa. The two claw arms are hook shapes that likewise butt onto the circle's edge at a visible seam. The eyes are two hairline stalks with dots, which reads as insect antennae rather than reduced crab eyes, and there is no mouthparts region, no abdomen, no front margin teeth.
rows.fix: Deform the carapace into a broader-than-tall shield with a slightly notched front margin and an irregular pitted surface; if the palette allows, drop the pigment toward a chalky off-white with faint pink joints. Add the missing four legs so there are eight, and rebuild each as three tapering segments with knuckled joints and a fine curved dactyl, angled down and out so the animal stands on them. Grow every limb out of a visible bulge on the carapace rim rather than touching it at a point. Replace the ladder rungs with joint shading and a few bristles. Set the eyes in shallow orbits on the front margin, small and clouded, on short thick stalks not hairs.

rows.readsAs: A chrome-and-glass radar dome or a stylised transit-app tortoise logo; the two grey circles read as wheels, so the silhouette says 'toy car with a shell' more than 'reptile'
rows.defect: The four legs are TWO free-floating dark-grey perfect circles hanging in the gap under the shell — they touch nothing, have no thigh, no foot, no toes, and no join to the body at all. Nothing columnar, nothing elephantine, nothing scaly. The shell bottom is terminated by a dead-straight horizontal machined line, and the carapace pattern is a set of perfectly regular concentric arcs radiating from one hub — it reads as a radar sweep / spiderweb decal laid over a dome, not pyramid growth scutes. The head is a smooth pale ovoid butted against the shell edge with a hard seam and no neck at all, let alone a wrinkled retractable one. Whole animal is icy white-blue with zero keratin warmth.
rows.fix: Delete the two floating circles and grow four legs out of the shell opening: a tapered column per leg, wider at the shoulder where it emerges under the carapace, ending in a stumpy club foot with 4-5 blunt claw nubs (no webbing, per the note). Give the leg surface overlapping polygonal tubercle scales. Replace the concentric-arc overlay with 13 discrete polygonal scutes, each an independent plate with its own stacked growth rings and a raised centre boss, separated by dark sulci. Raise the dome apex ~25% for a tall tortoise profile. Insert a real neck: 3-4 accordion skin folds between head and shell so the head reads as retractable. Repalette to olive/ochre/horn brown.

rows.readsAs: A herring gull or a white duck; the small yellow cone bill plus white body says 'seabird' — nobody would say toucan
rows.defect: The bill is a short, straight yellow cone about one-quarter of the body length — the single most diagnostic feature of the species is absent. No banding on it, no downcurve, no dark tip. The body is white/pale-grey with grey wing shading; the required black body with vivid yellow-white bib is entirely missing, so there is no colour block at all. No bare blue eye ring — just a plain black dot on white. The wing is a grey swoosh with a hard-edged crescent boundary sitting on top of the body like a sticker, and it tapers into a sharp dark spike of a tail.
rows.fix: Rebuild the bill at ~0.9x body length, deep at the base and slightly downcurved along the culmen, with a serrated tomium and colour bands (orange/green/black) plus a black tip and a defined black cere line where it meets the face. Repaint the body glossy black and drop in a saturated yellow-white bib across throat and upper breast with a crisp red or black boundary band beneath it. Add a ring of bare blue-teal skin around the eye. Re-root the wing: dissolve the crescent seam into overlapping covert rows so plumage emerges from the shoulder instead of being pasted on. Give it the short square toucan tail, not a spike.

rows.readsAs: A generic cartoon toad or a rubber bath-toy frog — the family is readable but the species is not, and the twig limbs make it read as a sticker-assembled mascot
rows.defect: The toe discs — called out in the row as THE diagnostic feature — are absent. Every digit ends in a bare thin point; the fore and hind feet are splayed sets of tapering sticks with no terminal pad of any kind. The hind legs are not folded into Z-shapes either: they stick straight out sideways as two thin bent twigs, so the animal has no coiled jumping power in the pose. The limbs join the body as thin dark strokes that overlap the belly edge with a visible hard line — no thigh mass, no hip. The body is a plain yellow egg with soft brown blotches airbrushed over it that read as sprayed-on stains rather than dermal pigment. Eyes are prominent and set high, which is right, but they are two identical flat white circles with a black disc — perfect circles, no lid, no lower eyelid fold.
rows.fix: Add large round adhesive discs at the tip of every digit, clearly wider than the toe shaft, with a visible pad rim and a slight underside shadow. Refold the hind legs into a tight Z — femur back and up, tibia forward and down, tarsus back — so the knee sits above the body line and the foot tucks under the flank; that pose alone will say 'tree frog'. Grow real thigh mass out of the flank so hip and body share one continuous contour with no overlap line. Replace the airbrushed blotches with irregular-edged pigment patches that follow body curvature and break at the flank fold. Add a lower lid arc and a horizontal or vertical pupil to the eyes, and consider the red iris of the hylid reference.

rows.readsAs: A red squirrel or a chipmunk — the ball body plus smooth banana tail plus white front teeth is the squirrel cartoon, not a tree shrew
rows.defect: No long pointed squirrel-like snout — the head is a rounded ball with the merest bump at the front, and where the snout should be there is a HARD WHITE RECTANGLE (two flat-topped blocks with straight machined edges) standing in for teeth, plus four dead-straight hairline whiskers radiating like drawn rays. The tail is a smooth tapered orange cone with a lighter highlight stripe — glossy and bare, not bushy in any way, and no hair breaks its outline. The body is a fat round ball rather than a slim low body; the aspect reads ~1.3 not 2.2. Ears are two small hard triangles set on the skull outline. The hind leg is a separate orange lobe overlapping the body with a visible boundary arc, and the forelimbs/clawed grasping feet are essentially not depicted.
rows.fix: Extend the rostrum into a long tapering snout roughly a third of head length, ending in a small dark rhinarium; drop the white block entirely (incisors should not be visible in a closed mouth). Rebuild the tail as a bushy plume — fur tufts breaking the silhouette along its whole length, widening past the base, roughly body-length. Slim and lengthen the trunk to a low horizontal body around 2.2 aspect with a visible shoulder and haunch rather than one sphere. Give the whiskers curvature and varying length. Add four small clawed grasping feet with splayed digits gripping the ground. Re-root the hind limb so the haunch swells out of the flank instead of overlapping it.

rows.readsAs: A coiled red earthworm or a cartoon serpent charm — the ribbing plus even thickness plus perfect coil says 'annelid' or 'rope', not 'whip-thin tree snake'
rows.defect: The body is thick — roughly the same diameter as the head, drawn as a heavy hose coiled into two nearly perfect concentric rings. The row demands 'startlingly thin — pencil-width'; this is the opposite, and the perfect toroid geometry reads as machined. The snout is a blunt round ovoid, not long and pointed, and the head is joined to the body by an obvious narrowing seam where a separate head shape has been butted on. Scales are rendered as uniformly spaced dark ticks marching along the body at identical pitch — a stamped hatching pattern sprayed over a tube, not scales that shrink toward the tail and wrap around the curvature. The coil is a flat spiral floating in space, not draped in loose loops over any branch or support. Colour is bright fire-engine red where the reference is a green vine/tree snake.
rows.fix: Reduce body diameter by roughly two-thirds so it is visibly slimmer than the head, and taper it continuously to a whip-thin tail tip. Break the concentric-ring geometry: give it uneven, overlapping loops with a branch or two passing behind and in front of the loops so it reads as draped, with sag between supports. Reshape the head into a long wedge with a pointed snout and a defined but continuous neck — the widening from neck to jaw should be a smooth flare, not a butt joint. Replace the tick hatching with proper dorsal scale rows that foreshorten around the tube and diminish toward the tail. Repalette to vine-snake green with a paler ventral stripe.

rows.readsAs: A generic silvery fish, closest to an ocean sunfish or a plain bream — and its body shape, palette and eye treatment are near-identical to the Tripod Fish in this same batch, so the two read as the same base asset with different fins bolted on
rows.defect: There is no erectile trigger spine on the forehead — the head profile is a plain smooth curve, so the feature the animal is NAMED for is missing. The eye is set forward and low, sitting almost directly above and beside the mouth; the row requires it far back and high, which is the other signature triggerfish trait. The body is a soft smooth white-grey oval, not a leathery diamond, and it carries no scale texture at all — just two vague grey smudges airbrushed on. Every fin is a flat grey geometric wedge butted against the body with a hard straight boundary line: the caudal is a fan of dead-straight radial rays, the two dorsal lobes are separate triangles overlapping the back outline, and the pectoral is a tiny striped triangle sitting on top of the flank. There is also a visible straight vertical line behind the head standing in for a gill slit.
rows.fix: Add the first dorsal spine: a stout erectile spike rising from the forehead just behind the eye, with the smaller locking second spine behind it. Move the eye far back and high on the skull, well clear of the mouth, and shrink the mouth to a small terminal beak with visible incisor-like teeth. Reshape the body into an angular rhomboid/diamond with a steep forehead slope and a flattened lateral profile. Give the whole hide the coarse plate-like non-overlapping scale texture triggerfish actually have, following body curvature. Re-root every fin: soft rays should emerge from a fleshy base that blends into the flank over several pixels, with membrane between curved rays rather than straight ones. Convert the second dorsal and anal into the long symmetrical undulating rowing fins that run most of the back and belly.

rows.readsAs: A deep-sea stilt fish or a water strider — the species reads correctly, which is rare in this batch; it is the manufactured line-work that lets it down
rows.defect: The strongest image in the batch — the three stilts and the forward-swept feeler pectorals both read immediately — but the construction is machined. The three stilts are uniform-width hairline strokes with zero taper along their entire length and no root swelling where they reach the body; they simply stop at the belly outline with no fairing, and the two rear ones are near-parallel identical strokes. The caudal fin is a hard flat grey triangle with three perfectly straight edges — an obvious geometric primitive butted against the body. The feelers spring from beside the head as bare unattached curves with no base or muscle. The eye is not the tiny useless dot the row asks for: it is a large white-ringed circle with a black pupil, the same eye used on the Triggerfish. The body is a smooth featureless lens with no taper toward the tail and no skin texture.
rows.fix: Taper each stilt: noticeably thicker where it leaves the body and thinning toward the tip, and fair the top of each into a fleshy fin base so it grows out of the flank rather than terminating at the outline. Vary the two rear stilts in angle and length so they do not read as a copied pair. Rebuild the caudal as a soft-rayed fin — curved trailing margin, individual rays with membrane, upper lobe elongated into its own filament as in the real animal. Give the pectoral feelers a fleshy root at the shoulder. Shrink the eye to a tiny dark vestigial dot with no white ring. Taper the body toward the tail and add fine deep-sea skin sheen with a faint lateral line.

rows.readsAs: A perched robin or a small brown songbird with two long tail feathers; nothing about it says seabird, and the perched pose puts it in the same visual family as the Toucan in this batch
rows.defect: Posture is wrong outright: the row calls for flying and the render is a bird STANDING on two yellow feet with a ground shadow beneath it and wings closed — no spread wings, no flight silhouette. The body is salmon/rust red where the reference is a white pigeon-like body. No black wedge stripe through the eye; the eye is a plain yellow-ringed dot on an unmarked head. The bill is a thin yellow needle, not stout, and not red. The two tail streamers are present but only extend about half a body length past the tail, not doubling the body length. The folded wing is a dark crescent laid over the flank with a hard boundary line and a lighter lens-shaped panel inside it that reads as an applied decal rather than covert and primary feather groups. Aspect reads ~1.5 against the required 3.
rows.fix: Re-pose to flight: wings fully spread and swept, feet tucked, body horizontal — that alone fixes the aspect toward 3. Repaint the body and wings white with black outer primaries and black bars across the upper wing coverts. Add the black wedge stripe running back through the eye toward the nape. Thicken and shorten the bill into a stout slightly decurved dagger and colour it coral red. Lengthen the two central streamers to at least the full body length again so they double the total, and give them a thin ribbon taper with a slight wave rather than a straight rod. Dissolve the crescent wing seam into layered feather tracts emerging from the shoulder.

rows.readsAs: a pink tick or mite sitting next to a separate discarded shrimp tail
rows.defect: The animal is rendered as TWO disconnected bodies with a visible dark gap between them. In front sits an opaque pink egg-shaped blob with four thin straight rod legs and two long antennae; behind it, not touching, floats a separate segmented shrimp abdomen with a tail fan. Nothing bridges them — no thorax, no seam, just background. The front blob is also a plain smooth ovoid with sparse dimples: no arched hump-back, no translucency (it is fully opaque), no pale dorsal light-sensing patch, and no feeding claws. Legs are perfectly straight pin-strokes of uniform width stuck onto the underside of the ovoid rather than tapering out of it. Overall aspect reads ~1.5, not the 2.8 called for.
rows.fix: Build the shrimp as ONE continuous body: a single arched dorsal spline running from rostrum to telson, with the carapace swelling and the pleon segments narrowing along the SAME outline, so cephalothorax and abdomen share a silhouette. Delete the separate abdomen primitive. Add the pale dorsal eyespot patch as a lighter region inside the carapace shading (not a decal), give the shell 10-20% translucency with a warm inner glow, taper each pereiopod from a thick base blended into the body to a fine tip, and add two small chelae at the mouth. Stretch to aspect 2.8.

rows.readsAs: a generic purple cartoon snake, or a coiled length of ribbed hose
rows.defect: This is a thick fat rope coil, not a vine snake. The body is roughly 28px wide against a ~340px path — nowhere near the pencil-thin whip the note demands, and there is no taper at all: the tube is the same diameter from coil to neck. The head is a small round bulb barely wider than the neck with NO dart-shaped pointed snout; it reads as a blunt nub. The eye is a plain vertical-slit dot, not a horizontal keyhole pupil. The ventral scale rungs are a repeating hatch of identical parallel ticks sprayed evenly along the whole tube including over the dorsal surface, which reads as a machined thread rather than scalation. The coil is two perfectly concentric flat rings — a geometric spiral, not a snake settling on itself.
rows.fix: Cut the tube diameter by at least 60% and hold it constant to sell the whip; extend the total path so aspect approaches 12. Replace the bulb head with a long wedge: a narrow elongated snout at least 3x the head's width, widening slightly at the jaw. Redraw the eye with a horizontal keyhole/dumbbell pupil on a gold iris. Vary the scale-rung spacing and confine the ventral hatch to the belly-facing side of the coil only. Break the concentric rings with an S-kink so the coil is not two circles.

rows.readsAs: the same snake as Vine Snake, just teal — a generic cartoon snake
rows.defect: This is pixel-for-pixel the SAME image as Vine Snake in this batch — identical coil geometry, identical body thickness, identical ventral hatch, identical head bulb, identical forked tongue, identical shadow — recoloured teal instead of purple. Beyond the duplication it fails every mustRead: the head is a small round bulb the same width as the neck, so there is NO broad triangular head and NO sharply set-off thin neck; the body is a uniform slim tube, not short thick and heavy; and the dorsal surface carries only the same uniform scale hatch, with NO zigzag or diamond chain pattern anywhere. The coil is two flat concentric rings rather than a low heavy pile.
rows.fix: Fork the viper off the colubrid model entirely. Widen the head into a spade/triangle roughly 2x the neck width with the venom-gland bulges at the rear corners, then pinch a distinctly narrow neck behind it. Thicken the trunk to roughly 2.5x the current diameter and shorten it to aspect 2. Paint a true zigzag dorsal chain that follows the body's curvature and deforms with the coil (dark V-bands alternating along the spine), not a repeating tick pattern. Stack the coil in overlapping loops of differing radius so it reads low and heavy.

rows.readsAs: a pale minnow or an oversized tadpole with a toothy grin
rows.defect: There is no lure at all — the first dorsal ray whip that must arc over the head is completely absent, and the dorsal region is only a faint grey smudge. The fangs are a row of tiny even white triangles sitting inside the jawline like a zipper; nothing closes outside the mouth or reaches past the eye. The body is a fat pale teardrop, aspect ~3 against the required 6, and it is light silver-blue rather than a slim dark body. The caudal peduncle is a straight-sided narrow bar that meets the fat body at a hard vertical step — a clear seam where two primitives butt together — and the tail fin is a small flat chevron stuck on its end. Photophores read as four evenly spaced identical cyan rectangles airbrushed along the flank rather than organs set into the skin.
rows.fix: Add the defining lure: a single long ray rising from just behind the skull and curving forward over the snout, with a small glowing tip. Replace the tooth row with 4-6 elongated curved fangs, the front pair long enough to project outside the closed jaw and pass the eye. Halve the body depth and lengthen to aspect 6, darken to near-black with a blue sheen so the photophores read as emitters. Blend the peduncle into the trunk with a continuous taper instead of a step, and enlarge the caudal fin with visible rays. Vary the photophore spacing and size and sink each into a small dark socket.

rows.readsAs: a teal rabbit or bunny
rows.defect: This is a rabbit. Two tall pointed ears stand fully clear of the head — the exact opposite of ears half-buried in fur — and a pair of large white square incisors juts from the muzzle like a cartoon bunny's. No tail is visible anywhere, so the stubby short tail mustRead is simply absent. The body is a smooth teal capsule blob with a hard-edged dark crescent gouged into the flank where the haunch is meant to be; that crescent is a pasted overlay with a visible outline, not a muscle mass growing out of the body. The limbs are three little brown/teal stumps poking from under the blob with no shoulder or hip integration and no feet. The head is an ellipse overlapping the trunk ellipse with a faint arc still visible where they intersect.
rows.fix: Shrink the ears to small rounded flaps set low and partly sunk into the neck fur, with fur strokes crossing their base. Replace the protruding incisors with a blunt closed rounded muzzle. Add a short thick tail, roughly a quarter of body length, emerging from a fur-blended base. Delete the crescent decal and model the haunch as a raised volume in the same shading pass as the trunk. Give the four legs visible shoulders/hips that flow from the body, plus small feet. Remove the head/trunk intersection arc by unioning the silhouette before shading.

rows.readsAs: a purple pigeon or dove
rows.defect: Nothing about this reads as a vulture. The head and neck are FULLY feathered in the same purple as the body — the bare unfeathered head and neck mustRead is entirely missing. The beak is a small straight yellow triangle with a slight droop, not a heavy hooked tearing beak; it is the size and shape of a dove's bill. There is no feather ruff at the neck and no hunched shoulder mass: the neck is thin, upright and forward, giving an alert perched posture rather than a head drawn down into a collar. The wing is a hard-edged lens shape laid over the body with a dark outline all the way around it and a second dark crescent above — a decal, not a folded wing emerging from the shoulder. The tail is a flat pointed dark wedge stuck onto the rear at a sharp angle with a visible join line.
rows.fix: Strip the feathers from the head and upper neck: render them as bare wrinkled skin in a desaturated flesh tone, with the plumage line ending in a distinct ruff collar at the base of the neck. Enlarge the beak substantially, deepen it, and hook the tip sharply downward with a visible cere. Shorten and thicken the neck into an S so the head sits low between raised shoulders, and build a thick ruff volume around the neck base. Redraw the wing as coverts and primaries layered from a shoulder that shares the body's shading, with no closed outline. Blend the tail base into the rump with overlapping covert strokes.

rows.readsAs: a barracuda or a young pike — right family, wrong species
rows.defect: The row of finlets running to the tail is absent — the caudal peduncle is a bare smooth taper with nothing on the dorsal or ventral edge, so a required mustRead is missing. The second dorsal and anal fins are also missing entirely; the only dorsal element is a soft translucent grey blob hovering over the back with no rays and no defined base. The pectoral fin is a hard-edged translucent triangular flap laid flat on the flank with a distinct outline, reading as pasted glass rather than a fin folded against the body. The vertical bars are evenly spaced identical soft stripes that stop abruptly at the belly line rather than wrapping the body's curvature. Body aspect measures closer to 4.5 than the specified 6.5. Head, pointed jaws and the stiff forked tail are good.
rows.fix: Add 8-9 small finlets along both the dorsal and ventral edges between the last fin and the tail, decreasing in size toward the peduncle. Replace the grey dorsal blob with a defined ray-supported first dorsal plus a small second dorsal, and add the matching anal fin. Rebuild the pectoral with visible rays and blend its base into the flank shading instead of outlining it. Make the bars vary in width and taper as they curve over the dorsal ridge and fade under the belly. Lengthen the body about 40% to reach aspect 6.5.

rows.readsAs: a plush cartoon lizard, or from a distance a bent banana
rows.defect: The construction is visible as stacked primitives: a large speckled ellipse for the trunk, a separate lighter ellipse for the head laid over it with its outline clearly crossing the trunk, and a hooked banana shape for the tail joined at a hard diagonal seam on the left flank. The tail is roughly the same length as the body, nowhere near twice it, and it curves up and away rather than trailing. Only two legs are drawn, as featureless brown tapered stumps with NO toes at all — the long splayed toes mustRead is entirely missing — and each stump meets the trunk at an abrupt edge with no shoulder or hip. The body is not flattened or pressed to a surface; it is a plump raised oval sitting high on its stumps. The dark speckling is a scatter of identical blobs sprayed across the top of the ellipse, ignoring the body's curve, and it stops dead at the head boundary. The mouth is a single straight ruled line across the head.
rows.fix: Union head, trunk and tail into one continuous outline before shading so no intersection arcs survive; taper the head out of the neck instead of overlapping an ellipse. Double the tail length, straighten it into a long trailing whip with a smooth base blend and fine ring scalation. Draw all four limbs, each with a defined upper and lower segment splayed out sideways, ending in five long separated toes with claws. Flatten the trunk vertically and drop it so the belly nearly touches the ground. Redistribute the speckling to follow the dorsal curvature, vary the blob sizes, and carry it across the head and onto the tail base. Replace the ruled mouth line with a curved jaw seam.

rows.readsAs: An ant — specifically a small golden garden ant. The pinched three-ball silhouette and the visible eye both say ant, not termite.
rows.defect: This is the generic three-bead ant chassis: three separate near-spherical golden blobs (head, thorax, abdomen) strung together with visible pinch-constrictions between them, which is exactly the wasp waist the reference note says must NOT be there. The body is a saturated egg-yolk gold, not pale/soft/translucent — a worker termite is unpigmented cream. A hard black pupil dot sits on the head even though the row says eyes: hidden (workers are blind). The six legs are hairline sticks that terminate at the sphere outline with no coxa, no thickening, no shading transition — stuck on, not grown out. The antennae are two thin curved wires with no visible beading.
rows.fix: Replace the 3-sphere chain with a single continuous soft-bodied tube: head + thorax + abdomen as one merged silhouette with a BROAD unpinched junction at the thorax/abdomen (no waist narrower than ~85% of the abdomen width). Recolour to pale translucent cream/ivory (low saturation, high value, slight subsurface warmth) and overlay soft transverse tergite bands instead of sphere shading. Delete the eye highlight entirely. Redraw the antennae as a visible string of 9-11 discrete round beads held straight forward, not curved wires. Fair the leg roots into the thorax with a wedge base so no hard line survives at the meeting point.

rows.readsAs: A generic perching songbird — a finch or a small thrush. Nobody would say tern; the standing pose, round body and hidden wings all point away from a seabird.
rows.defect: Posture is standing on two yellow legs on the ground, not flying — the row calls for flying and that is the whole read of a tern. The long narrow pointed wings are absent; instead a dark violet ellipse with a hard crescent outline lies flat on the flank like a decal, plus a second dark stripe over the shoulder that also ends in a hard edge. No black cap: the crown is the same lavender as the rest of the bird and the only dark on the head is the pupil. The body is a fat round egg (roughly 1.2 aspect, nothing like the stated 2.4). There IS a small forked tail, but it is a flat dark wedge pasted at the tail base with a visible seam and no feather structure. The legs are two bare yellow wires meeting the belly at a point.
rows.fix: Rebuild in flight: body as a slim horizontal spindle, both wings extended and swept back, each a long narrow taper about 1.6x body length with a pointed tip and a visible primary-feather trailing edge. Extend the tail into two long thin streamers reaching well past the wing trailing edge rather than a stubby V. Add a solid black cap covering crown and nape down to eye level against a white face. Recolour the body white/pale grey with a light grey mantle and make the bill a slim red-orange dagger. Fair the wing root into the shoulder with a shading gradient so no outline separates wing from body.

rows.readsAs: A generic small green aquarium fish — closest guess a young piranha or a silver dollar. Nothing identifies it as a tetra.
rows.defect: The caudal fin is detached — there is a clear gap of dark background between the rear point of the body and the leading edge of the tail triangle, so the tail floats behind the fish. The pectoral is a small pale wedge dropped on the flank with a hard outline, and the dorsal is a small triangle sitting on the back edge rather than rising out of it. No adipose fin anywhere behind the dorsal (required mustRead). No bright lateral stripe from eye to tail — the flank carries only faint horizontal green striations that read as brushwork, and the fish is uniform green rather than silvery with a stripe. The silhouette is a symmetrical almond/lens with top and bottom mirror-identical, a geometric primitive rather than a fish profile.
rows.fix: Weld the caudal peduncle: extend the body into a narrowing peduncle that physically overlaps and blends into the tail root with no background gap. Add the tiny adipose nub midway between dorsal and tail. Paint one high-contrast lateral stripe (iridescent cyan or red) running from the eye straight to the caudal base, sitting in the scale layer with soft edges rather than on top. Break the top/bottom symmetry by raising the dorsal profile and flattening the belly. Shift the base colour to silver with a green-gold sheen.

rows.readsAs: An ant with a tiny backpack. It is visually a palette swap of the Termite in this same batch — the two would be indistinguishable if you swapped their colours.
rows.defect: This is the SAME three-sphere ant chassis as the Termite in this batch, recoloured mint green with one small grey oval wing pad added over the abdomen. Aspect is roughly 2.0 in lumpy beads, not the required 3.5 slender cigar. The wings are a single flat grey blob with a hard elliptical edge and zero hair fringe — the fringed strap wings are the defining feature of a thrips and they are absent. No asymmetrical cone mouth: the head is a plain ball with a black pupil dot and two thin curved wires. The legs are hairline sticks meeting the spheres at a hard tangent line.
rows.fix: Discard the three-ball body and draw one slender cigar: a single continuous elongate abdomen at ~3.5:1, gently tapered at both ends, with fine transverse segment lines. Replace the grey pad with two pairs of very narrow strap wings held straight back along the body, each strap edged with a visible comb of long fine setae that reads at 440px. Add a short asymmetric downward-pointing cone under the head for the rasping mouth. Shorten and thicken the legs and fair them into the thorax. Eyes small and dark red, not a cartoon pupil dot.

rows.readsAs: A barracuda. The needle snout, exposed sawteeth and symmetrical fork are all barracuda or gar cues; nobody would say shark.
rows.defect: Not a shark. The snout is a long sharp needle point — the mustRead calls for a blunt square-fronted snout and this is the opposite. The tail is a symmetrical forked tuna tail with equal lobes; the long trailing upper lobe is absent. Teeth are drawn as a sawblade of hard white triangles projecting OUTSIDE the head silhouette along the jaw line — a geometric zigzag rather than a jaw. The dorsal is a detached dark teal hump floating above the back with a visible seam where it meets the spine, and the pectoral is a flat wedge pasted on the flank. There are no gill slits at all. The pale vertical banding reads as a sprayed light gradient over the flank rather than dark tiger bars in the skin.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head broad, blunt and squared-off at the front, with a wide crescent mouth set UNDERSLUNG beneath the snout and the teeth contained inside the mouth line instead of protruding as external triangles. Make the tail heterocercal — upper lobe about 1.8x the lower and swept into a long trailing tip. Add five gill slits ahead of the pectoral. Fair the first dorsal into the back as a continuous ridge with no gap and no outline. Repaint the flank as DARK vertical bars and blotches on a grey-brown dorsal surface fading to a pale belly, with soft broken edges.

rows.readsAs: A barracuda or a small mackerel. Nothing says tigerfish — no stripes and no big fangs, the only two things anyone knows about the animal.
rows.defect: The horizontal dark stripes along the flank are simply not there — the body is plain silver-white with a couple of soft grey smudges. The fangs are a row of small white triangles hanging below the lower jaw, not huge interlocking daggers; nothing interlocks and they read as a fringe. The tail is grey and only shallowly forked, with no red tinge. The two dorsal fins are translucent grey ghost-blobs hovering over the back with a visible edge crossing the spine — they overlap the body like semi-transparent stickers instead of rising out of it. The snout is a long point and the whole silhouette is the identical elongate chassis used for Tiger Shark in this batch.
rows.fix: Paint 6-8 crisp horizontal dark stripes running the full length of the flank, following the body curvature and sitting under the scale sheen. Enlarge the dentition dramatically: 8-10 conical daggers per jaw, upper and lower interdigitating outside the closed lip line so the closed mouth still shows them. Deepen the caudal fork and tint the lobes and anal fin red-orange. Make the dorsals opaque and rooted — a solid triangular first dorsal continuous with the dorsal ridge and a small adipose second dorsal behind it. Deepen the body and blunt the head so it stops sharing a silhouette with the Tiger Shark.

rows.readsAs: A bluegill or pumpkinseed sunfish — a generic saw-backed disc fish. The floating tail also makes it read as a paper cutout rather than an animal.
rows.defect: The caudal fin is a detached brown paddle floating a clear gap behind the body — background shows through between the body point and the fin, and the fin itself is a hard-edged rounded rectangle with straight radial spoke lines, a machined shape. A second small brown blob hangs under the belly, also disconnected. The dorsal is a perfectly regular row of six identical sharp isosceles triangles — a sawtooth zigzag primitive, not a spiny fin with a membrane. The head is neither blunt nor steep: the front of the fish tapers to a lens point, and the body is a symmetrical almond with top and bottom mirrored. The vertical bars are soft airbrushed bands laid over the whole flank.
rows.fix: Weld the tail: taper the body into a real caudal peduncle that merges into a fan-shaped caudal with soft feathered rays — no gap, no straight edges, no spoke lines. Replace the sawtooth with a continuous dorsal fin running from just behind the head to the peduncle: one translucent membrane with embedded spines of varying length, shorter at the front, rooted into the back with a soft transition. Give the head a steep blunt forehead by raising the nape into a convex slope and shortening the snout to a small terminal mouth. Break the top/bottom mirror symmetry by deepening the belly, and attach the pelvic and anal fins instead of floating them.

rows.readsAs: A frog. The smooth glossy skin and missing parotoid glands push it toward frog rather than toad, but a viewer would name the family correctly.
rows.defect: Best read in the batch — recognisably an anuran in a front-on sprawl with correct squat proportions, no neck and no tail. But the mustRead parotoid glands are absent: behind each eye the head surface is smooth and unbroken, so nothing separates it from a frog. The skin is not warty in silhouette — the outline is a clean smooth ovoid and the 'warts' are soft airbrushed dark blotches that read as pigment sprayed on top of the surface rather than bumps in it. The two hind limbs are near-black flat cutouts at a completely different value from the mid-purple body, so they read as shadow shapes lying behind the animal rather than limbs continuous with its skin, with a hard value step where each meets the flank. The forelimbs are thin sticks meeting the body edge at a tangent line.
rows.fix: Add a raised kidney-shaped parotoid gland behind each eye, catching a highlight on its dome so it reads as swollen mass. Make the warts structural: perturb the body outline with 20-30 small irregular bumps and give each interior wart a lit top and a shadowed underside instead of a flat dark blob. Raise the hind-limb value to within one step of the body colour so they read as the same animal, and fair each thigh into the flank with a shaded transition instead of a hard edge. Thicken the forelimbs and root them into the shoulder mass.

rows.readsAs: A sitting rabbit or a squirrel
rows.defect: The mustRead 'deep folded hind legs' is simply absent — the animal is one large smooth egg-shaped mass from shoulder to ground with no thigh, no knee fold, no hock, no leg articulation of any kind. The only lower-limb evidence is a small pale horizontal sliver poking out at the bottom-right of the mass (the flat foot), which appears to emerge from nowhere. The tail is a separate tapering wedge laid across the lower-left of the body with its own pale rim highlight running as a hard crease over the torso — it reads as stuck on, not grown out. A tiny dark nub on the right flank is presumably a forearm but is unreadable. On top of that the whole render sits at near-black value against a near-black field; the head, ears and eye are the only legible parts.
rows.fix: Build the hind limb as real geometry: a broad thigh mass bulging out of the rump, a sharply folded shank angling forward-down, and the long flat foot flat on the ground under the body — silhouette must show the Z-fold, not a smooth curve to the floor. Fuse the tail root into the rump so the rim-light is one continuous contour (no highlight line crossing the body), and lift the whole body's base value ~2-3 stops so the form separates from the background.

rows.readsAs: A generic green mackerel or trout
rows.defect: Two mustReads are missing outright. There is no white tip on the lower lobe of the tail — the caudal fin is uniform dark green top to bottom. And the eye is a small beady white bead with a hard dark pupil dot, not the large cloudy glassy reflective eye the species is named for. The two dorsal fins are also not attached: they appear as two soft dark translucent humps floating BEHIND the body silhouette, overlapping it like a shadow layer, with no join to the dorsal ridge and no spines in the front one. The body is a clean symmetrical almond with a faint sprayed-on horizontal streak for flank markings.
rows.fix: Paint the lower caudal lobe with a distinct pale/white tip. Enlarge the eye to ~1.5x and render it as a milky, low-contrast glassy disc with a diffuse reflective bloom rather than a white bead with a pupil dot. Rebuild the dorsals as fins rising from the dorsal contour in the same paint layer as the body — front one a spiny membrane with visible ray spikes, second one soft and separate.

rows.readsAs: A winged fire ant
rows.defect: No yellow-and-black banding anywhere — the whole insect is uniform burnt orange with barely-darker faint arcs on the abdomen. No pinched thread-thin waist: the head, thorax and abdomen are three touching ovals of similar diameter and the thorax-abdomen junction is a wide blunt butt-join. The abdomen is a fat rounded oval with a blunt round end, not a pointed sting-tipped taper. The wings are broad, rounded and paddle-shaped with visible cross-veining and they overlap the abdomen as a stuck-on grey sheet. Legs are straight uniform-width red sticks with no joints and no visible attachment to the thorax.
rows.fix: Cut a genuine petiole — a thread-thin dark stalk of a few pixels' width between thorax and abdomen. Retaper the abdomen to a sharp point with a sting. Repaint with alternating saturated yellow and true black bands that wrap the abdomen's curvature (not sprayed arcs). Narrow the wings to long slender hairless blades and root them into the thorax top. Give the legs a femur/tibia bend and taper.

rows.readsAs: A ladybird with the spots left off, wearing a hat
rows.defect: The head is a dark grey mushroom-cap/sombrero shape sitting ON TOP of the elytra with a hard elliptical seam where it meets the pale dome — it reads as a separate hat, not a tucked head growing from the pronotum. Both mustRead leg features fail: the legs are six thin uniform-width grey hairline arcs that float in the background, starting in empty space and never touching the body outline; none of them is flattened, none has an oar blade or a hair fringe. There are no clubbed antennae at all — just two black dots on the grey cap. The elytral suture is a perfectly straight, perfectly vertical 1px machined line down the exact centre.
rows.fix: Replace the cap with a pronotum wedge that shares an unbroken contour with the elytra, and tuck a small head under its front edge. Anchor every leg into the body under the elytra margin and rebuild the hind pair as broad flattened paddles with a comb of stiff swimming hairs along the trailing edge. Add short clubbed antennae. Curve and soften the elytral suture and let it follow the dome's foreshortening.

rows.readsAs: A tiny shrimp or a copepod
rows.defect: Almost every mustRead fails. The shell is opaque dark grey-blue with no transparency, so no gut and no brood pouch are visible inside. There is not one large dark compound eye — there are two small pale dots side by side, which reads as a paired-eye animal. The antennae are two long straight unbranched hairlines (one up-forward, one down-back) rather than big branched rowing antennae. The rear of the animal carries a fan of feathered swimmerets, which no Daphnia has and which pushes it straight into shrimp territory. Proportion is also wrong: it is clearly wider than tall (roughly 1.4 aspect) when the row calls for 0.8, taller than long. The render is also so dark it is barely visible against the background.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a tall teardrop carapace with real internal transparency — dark gut tube and an egg-filled brood pouch showing through a translucent shell. Replace the paired dots with a single large black compound eye near the top of the head. Delete the rear swimmeret fan. Make the antennae the dominant feature: two thick biramous limbs that fork into feathered branches, swept back mid-stroke. Raise overall luminance substantially.

rows.readsAs: A nautilus or ammonite shell sitting on a blue slab
rows.defect: The shell is a mathematically perfect circle drawn face-on, filled with evenly spaced concentric ribs of identical width — it reads as a machined clock spring or a cinnamon roll rather than a grown shell; there is no whorl expansion (the coil does not widen as it unwinds) and no aperture opening. The foot is a flat slab with a straight lower edge and a hard notch where it meets the shell. The head at right is a small angular blue shape carrying three short stubby spikes — a spiky crown rather than the required pair of slender tentacles, and it sits in front of the foot with a visible break rather than flowing out of it.
rows.fix: Make the coil a true logarithmic spiral: each whorl visibly fatter than the last, ribs widening with it, and cut a real aperture on the head side. Give the foot a soft undulating sole and merge it into the shell with a continuous mantle rather than a notch. Replace the spike crown with exactly two long slender tapering tentacles growing smoothly out of the head, with eye spots at their bases.

rows.readsAs: A coiled millipede or a segmented worm
rows.defect: The coil is a near-perfect torus — a donut of constant diameter with a clean elliptical hole in the middle. There is no slender tapering tail: the tube is the same thickness at every point, and no tail tip is visible anywhere in the silhouette. The 'keeled banded body' mustRead fails too — instead of dark and light bands the whole length is covered in hundreds of fine, evenly spaced transverse comb ribs, which read as insect segments or a ribcage, not snake scales. The head is a bulbous white ball noticeably wider than the neck, joined by a visible pinch/seam, so it looks socketed on. Only the forked red tongue sells the animal.
rows.fix: Break the torus: vary the tube diameter along its length and let the last third taper to a fine whip tip that lies visibly on top of or beside a coil. Replace the comb ribs with overlapping keeled scales and paint broad alternating dark/light saddle bands across the back. Reshape the head to a narrow wedge that flows out of the neck with no diameter jump, eyes set high on the skull.

rows.readsAs: An ant — and specifically the same creature as this batch's Wasp with the wings removed
rows.defect: The defining mustRead — extremely long splayed middle and hind legs — is absent. The legs are short thin sticks roughly as long as the body is tall, angled steeply downward like an ant's; the animal's total leg span barely exceeds its own body length when a strider's should be several times it. There are also no dimples denting the water surface: the ground contact is a single soft elliptical drop shadow with no meniscus, no rings, no surface at all. The body is not narrow and boat-shaped either — it is a spherical head, a spherical thorax and a smooth capsule abdomen, three glossy orange blobs in a row, and the abdomen's outline is a plain rounded rectangle. Structurally it is the same three-ball-plus-sticks build as the Wasp in this batch, minus the wings.
rows.fix: Lengthen the middle and hind legs to 2-3x the body length, splay them nearly horizontally out to the sides with a shallow knee bend so the silhouette is a wide X, and keep the front pair short and folded under the head. Draw a water plane with four to six pressed dimples and light rings under the foot tips. Slim the body into a long narrow tapering boat hull and remove the capsule outline.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon rabbit or a pink guinea pig
rows.defect: Fails two of three mustReads and the colour is wrong. The ears are two tall pointed leaf-shaped spikes standing clear above the skull — the reference demands 'small ears almost buried in fur', and these read as rabbit ears. There is no furred tail at all: the only thing at the rear is a short dark comma-shaped hook the same width as a leg, no fur, nowhere near half the body length. The animal is bright crimson-pink, not any vole colour. Construction is stuck-on rather than grown: the head is a separate smaller ellipse butted onto the body ellipse with a visible tonal seam under the jaw, the two hind stubs are dark peg shapes with hard edges pasted under the belly with no haunch or thigh mass connecting them, the whiskers are four perfectly straight machined 1px lines radiating from a point, and the teeth are a literal white rectangle with a vertical divider. The silhouette is a fat egg with no shoulder, rump or spine — no fur texture anywhere, just a smooth airbrushed gradient.
rows.fix: Shrink the ears to low rounded semicircles set into the fur line so only the top arc clears the head, and drop them back toward the crown. Replace the rear hook with a real tail: a tapering furred cylinder about 0.5x body length, rooted in a rump mass that flows out of the back contour rather than starting at a hard edge. Recolour to warm chestnut/umber brown with a paler grey-buff belly. Merge head and body into one silhouette — thicken the neck junction so the jaw line is a soft value shift, not an outline. Give the hind limbs a haunch: a rounded thigh bulge continuous with the body, foot below it. Curve the whiskers and vary their length; replace the tooth rectangle with two small rounded off-white incisors. Add directional fur breakup along the back and rump edge so the outline is not a smooth ellipse.

rows.readsAs: a duckling or a generic yellow chick
rows.defect: All three mustReads fail. There is no black face mask — the head is uniform pale gold with a plain dot eye. The bill is a small narrow triangular wedge, thin and pointed, not a thick conical seed-cracker. There is no woven grass nest anywhere in the frame and the bird is not clinging upside down; it is standing upright on two feet on the shadow, which also contradicts the 'flying' posture field. The plumage is flat amber-orange, not the bright lemon yellow of a breeding male weaver. Construction: the wing is a separate darker ellipse laid on the flank with a hard crescent edge and its own outline — pasted on, not emerging from the shoulder. The tail is a single flat dark triangle spliced onto the rump at a hard diagonal seam. The feet are stick-figure yellow lines with three splayed toes, no tarsus mass. Whole silhouette is two overlapping ovals (head ball + body egg) with a visible notch where they meet.
rows.fix: Repaint the plumage saturated chrome yellow and add the black mask: solid black over face, chin and throat, cut off cleanly at the crown and nape so a yellow cap and collar surround it. Rebuild the bill as a short deep cone — depth at the base nearly equal to its length, culmen slightly curved, pale horn or black. Add the nest: a woven straw globe with a downward entrance tube, and hang the bird head-down on its underside gripping with both feet, body angled off vertical. Delete the wing ellipse and instead paint the folded wing as layered coverts/primaries whose outline IS part of the body outline, with a dark barred edge. Replace the triangular tail with a short fanned set of rectrices growing from the rump. Fill in the neck so head and body share one contour.

rows.readsAs: a dark grey generic fish or a whale-shaped balloon
rows.defect: The single explicit prohibition in the note is violated: the tail is VERTICAL. At the left end sit two wedge lobes stacked one above the other in the plane of the page, exactly the fish caudal fin the row says a whale must never have. There are no horizontal notched flukes. There is no blowhole — the top of the head is a bare unbroken curve. The body is a plain grey-brown ellipse of roughly 2.5:1, far short of the 5:1 aspect, so it reads stubby rather than streamlined. Every appendage is a stuck-on cutout with its own pale outline stroke: the dorsal fin is a hooked shape sitting on top of the back with a clear line across its base, the flipper is a long flat blade hanging below the belly with a hard-edged root and no shoulder swelling, and the tail wedges likewise butt onto the caudal end with a visible seam. The pale outline stroke running along the entire back and around the fins makes the whole thing read as a sticker rather than a body. There is no baleen jawline, no throat pleats, no mouth line at all, and the eye is a tiny glossy bead placed high with no eye-patch modelling. Two vague dark blotches on the flank look sprayed on top of the gradient.
rows.fix: Rotate the tail into perspective: a wide horizontal fluke pair with a central notch and swept trailing edges, seen slightly from above/below so it reads flat-plane, and taper the peduncle into it with no seam. Add the blowhole as a small paired crescent depression on the top of the head with a shallow bulge around it. Stretch the body to about 5:1 and reshape it: broad head that is roughly a third of the length, a long straight jawline running back past the eye, throat pleats as soft parallel grooves on the underside, tapering to a narrow peduncle. Delete the pale outline stroke entirely. Root the dorsal and the flippers in a swelling of the body mass so their bases disappear into the flank. Move the eye down to just above and behind the corner of the mouth. Replace the sprayed blotches with subtle mottling and callosity/scar texture that follows the body form.

rows.readsAs: a spotted trout or a generic aquarium fish
rows.defect: None of the three mustReads are present. The head is not boxy or flattened — it narrows to a sharp point like a mackerel, and the mouth is a thin line at the very tip of that point rather than a huge flat slot spanning a broad squared-off snout. There is no checkerboard: the markings are irregular soft grey blobs of varying size scattered over the flank, clearly airbrushed on top of the pale gradient rather than being skin, and there are no white lines/grid between them. There are no flank ridges. The gill slits are five perfectly straight equal-length parallel strokes ruled at a uniform angle — machined lines, not gill openings in flesh. The eye is a large glossy cartoon eye with white sclera and a black pupil sitting right at the snout tip, where a whale shark's eye is tiny and set at the corner of a wide head. Fins are grey cutouts overlapping the body with hard seams — the dorsal is a triangle whose base line is visible across the back, the pectoral is a blade hard-edged at the root, the caudal is a symmetrical forked fish tail with straight edges instead of the big asymmetric upper-lobed shark tail.
rows.fix: Rebuild the head as a wide flattened box: blunt squared front, mouth as a very wide terminal slot running the full width of that front edge, slight overhang above it. Move the eyes to the extreme outer corners of the head and shrink them to small dark beads with no white sclera. Replace the blob spray with the real pattern: pale spots laid on a regular grid separated by pale vertical and horizontal lines, wrapping around the body form and shrinking toward the tail so it follows the surface. Add the three prominent longitudinal ridges along each flank, running from behind the head to the tail base and casting their own shading. Redraw the caudal as a large asymmetric shark tail, upper lobe clearly longer. Replace the ruled gill lines with five curved slits of graduated length that follow the head contour and sit in soft creases. Sink every fin base into the body mass so no straight seam is visible.

rows.readsAs: a fat green python or a coiled rubber worm
rows.defect: The defining mustRead — 'extremely thin whip-like body' — is inverted. The rendered body is a thick uniform teal tube coiled into a fat closed doughnut; the tube diameter is roughly a quarter of the coil's outer width, so it reads heavy-bodied like a python. There is no tapering tail at all: the coil closes on itself and the tail end is nowhere to be found, so the 'very long tapering tail half the total length' is entirely absent. The head is a slightly larger rounded blob at the end of the tube, wider than the neck, blunt rather than narrow, with a visible tonal seam at the jaw where it joins — and it carries a big glossy eye that is fine, but the head shape is a lozenge, not a slim arrowhead. The ventral scutes are ruled as dozens of identical evenly-spaced parallel hatch lines of constant width — machined striping rather than scales, and they run right around the curve at uniform pitch instead of foreshortening. The dorsal surface is a flat teal gradient with a few sprayed lighter dots and no scale texture whatsoever. The forked tongue is two straight red 1px lines from a single vertex, geometric.
rows.fix: Thin the body dramatically — target a tube no more than about a tenth of the coil width — and taper it continuously from mid-body to a hair-fine tail tip that is left visible outside the coil, roughly half the total length. Open the composition: an S-curve or a loose loop with the head raised and the fine tail trailing off, so the whip proportion is legible instead of a closed ring. Narrow the head into an elongated wedge, wider at the jaw hinge and drawn out to a pointed snout, with the neck slightly thinner than the head but no seam. Replace the ruled ventral hatching with belly scutes that vary in width with the body curve and compress on the inside of bends. Add dorsal scale texture — small overlapping diamonds following the body axis — instead of the flat gradient and sprayed dots. Curve and taper the tongue tines.

rows.readsAs: a pale newt or salamander
rows.defect: The tail length is right — that mustRead passes. The other two do not. There are no pale stripes running the length of the back; the back carries scattered round grey spots instead, and they sit as flat decals on the gradient with no interaction with the body form. The snout is not slender or pointed: the head is a near-perfect circle butted onto the front of the body ellipse, so blunt it reads as a separate ball, with a hard tonal seam at the neck and a mouth drawn as a single straight horizontal line across it. The four legs are identical grey rounded pegs of equal length pushed under the body with visible hard edges at the root — no shoulder, no hip, no knee, no feet or toes, and no sprawling stance despite the posture field. The tail itself has a dark grey stripe painted along its upper half that stops abruptly partway down, an obvious decal edge that does not follow the taper. The body is a plain capsule with no dorsal ridge or flank fold.
rows.fix: Swap the spots for the correct pattern: six to eight continuous pale cream stripes running unbroken from behind the head to the tail base, separated by darker brown fields, each stripe narrowing with the body. Rebuild the head as a tapered wedge — widest at the jaw hinge, drawn out to a narrow pointed snout — and merge it into the neck so there is no circular outline. Give the limbs real structure: angled upper arm and forearm with an elbow, splayed toes, hind limbs noticeably longer and heavier than the fore, feet planted wide of the body for a true sprawl. Delete the painted tail stripe or continue the dorsal striping down the tail so it tapers with it. Add a subtle keeled dorsal line and granular scale texture so the body is not a smooth capsule.

rows.readsAs: a red salmon or a generic red aquarium fish
rows.defect: The fish is painted saturated crimson red from nose to tail — a whitefish is a silver fish, and the mustRead calls explicitly for 'large silvery scales'. Nothing silver is present and there are no scales at all, only a smooth red gradient with two thin lighter streaks. The snout mustRead also fails: instead of a small blunt overhanging snout above a tiny inferior mouth, the head narrows to a sharp point with a straight line running to the tip, a terminal pike-like snout. I cannot find an adipose fin — behind the dorsal the dorsal contour is unbroken, so that mustRead is missing too. The tail is forked but shallowly, and it is a flat dark-red triangle spliced onto the caudal end at a hard vertical seam with a colour discontinuity across it. The dorsal fin is a separate darker wedge sitting on the back with a visible base line, and the pelvic fin is a small fan cutout with a hard root. The eye is a large white-ringed bead at the very tip of the snout, cartoon-scaled and too far forward. The body outline is a smooth symmetrical lens shape with no operculum, no lateral line and no gill cover.
rows.fix: Recolour to pale silver-white with an olive-brown dorsal fading through a bright silver flank to a white belly, and add large overlapping cycloid scales that catch a soft specular sheen and shrink toward the tail. Blunt and round the snout so it overhangs a small mouth set low and slightly behind the snout tip. Insert the adipose fin: a small fleshy lobe on the midline between the dorsal and the caudal peduncle. Deepen the caudal fork and root it in a narrow peduncle with rays continuing out of the body so there is no seam. Sink the dorsal and pelvic fin bases into the flank. Shrink the eye and move it back behind the snout. Add the operculum edge as a curved crease behind the head and a faint lateral line running the length of the flank.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon toad
rows.defect: The two identifying mustReads are both missing. There is no black robber's mask — the area through and behind the eye is the same plain orange-tan as the rest of the head, with no dark band, so the one feature that names this species is absent. There are no pale dorsolateral ridges; the back is smooth with a few soft brown blotches that read as airbrushed spray on top of the gradient rather than skin markings, and the ridges that should run as two raised pale lines from behind each eye down the back are nowhere. The 'long folded jumping legs' also fail: all four limbs are thin uniform-width curved sticks of about the same length splayed sideways, with splayed hands at the ends; there is no bulky thigh, no acute knee, no folded shank, so the hind legs are indistinguishable from the forelegs and the frog has no coiled spring look. The body is close to a perfect circle. The eyes are two spheres sitting entirely on top of the head outline as separate balls with a visible seam where each meets the skull, and there is no tympanum behind either. The mouth is a single thin curved line.
rows.fix: Paint the mask: a solid dark brown-black patch starting at the nostril, running through the eye and back over the tympanum, ending in a sharp edge at the shoulder, with the pale upper lip stripe below it. Add the two pale raised dorsolateral folds as continuous light ridges from behind each eye to the hip, each with a shadow on its lower side so they read as raised flesh. Rebuild the hind limbs: heavy thigh angled forward, sharply folded knee sitting high beside the body, shank folded back, long foot with webbed toes — clearly larger and thicker than the forelimbs, which should be short with four unwebbed fingers. Bed the eyes into the skull so the lids are part of the head contour rather than balls with a seam, and add the round tympanum behind each. Break the circular silhouette with a snout and a visible sacral hump, and replace the sprayed blotches with skin texture that follows the back's curvature.

rows.readsAs: a generic lollipop tree with brown balls on it — an olive or cherry tree
rows.defect: The trunk is a flat-sided green capsule of uniform width with a visibly rounded cap that just plugs into the bottom of a soft grey-green cloud blob — no taper, no root flare, no branches at all, and a hard edge where trunk meets canopy. The canopy is an airbrushed fog puff with tiny narrow leaf slivers sprayed around its rim rather than leaves attached to twigs. Two mustReads fail outright: the harvest is four smooth glossy brown SPHERES with no spiny green burr anywhere, and there are no creamy catkin tassels. The leaves are short blade slivers, not long saw-toothed lance leaves. It is also the identical asset to Cinnamon and Clove in this same batch, recoloured.
rows.fix: Replace the capsule trunk with a tapering trunk that forks into 3-4 boughs carrying the canopy so foliage grows out of wood instead of sitting on a stick; drop the fog-puff canopy fill and build the crown from leaf clusters. Redraw the fruit as a spiky green burr (radial spine ring) cracked open to show 2-3 brown nuts inside, not bare balls. Add drooping cream catkin strings. Lengthen the leaf primitive to a long lance with a visible saw-tooth margin edge.

rows.readsAs: a cornflower or a single blue aster on a fern frond
rows.defect: A single perfectly straight thin stem with leaves in an exactly regular opposite ladder up its whole length, topped by one lone blue daisy. That is the opposite of chicory: no branching, no stiff wiry near-naked stems, no basal rosette of toothed dandelion leaves, and only ONE flower where chicory carries several sessile flowers spaced along the stems. The ray tips are rounded, not squared and fringe-toothed. The stem is a mechanically straight line of constant width and the leaf pairs are evenly spaced like a template repeat.
rows.fix: Rebuild as 2-3 stiff wiry stems branching at wide angles with almost no leaf on them, put a toothed dandelion-like rosette at the base, and set 3-4 flowers sitting directly against the stems (no stalks). Cut each ray petal square at the tip and notch it with 4-5 small teeth. Add kink/curve variance to the stems so they stop reading as drawn lines.

rows.readsAs: a bunch of cherries or rose hips on wire stems
rows.defect: The harvest is five round red BALLS perched on top of stem tips — perfect spheres with a highlight, not glossy tapering pods, and they sit on the stem ends like beads on wires rather than hanging from a green calyx cap. No white star flower with a purple-black anther ring exists anywhere. The leaves are tiny pale silvery-grey slivers, not dark glossy pointed ovals, so the leaf colour is inverted from the reference. The habit is a fan of straight rods from one point, not a many-branched bushy shrub.
rows.fix: Redraw the fruit as an elongated cone tapering to a point, hanging from a small green five-lobed calyx, ripening green through red. Add small white five-petal star flowers with a dark purple anther cluster. Recolour leaves dark glossy green and widen them to pointed ovals. Give the stems real secondary branching instead of a radial fan of equal rods.

rows.readsAs: a thistle or knapweed clump
rows.defect: The four fruit heads are round bristly pompoms sitting upright on stem tips — they read as thistle heads. The defining mustRead, a long drooping bottlebrush CYLINDER of flowers/cherries, is completely absent; nothing hangs. Leaves are violet-purple slivers, not dark glossy green toothed ovals, so the whole plant is the wrong colour family. The stem base is a flat grey wedge with straight sides. It is also the same fan-of-rods skeleton as Chili Pepper and Cliff Rose in this batch with only the tip ornament swapped.
rows.fix: Build an elongated pendulous raceme: a hanging axis 3-4x longer than wide, densely packed with small round cherries along its length, drooping under its own weight. Recolour leaves dark glossy green with a paler underside and widen them to ovals with an abrupt drip point and fine teeth. Give the shrub woody forking branches instead of a wedge base with straight rods.

rows.readsAs: an olive tree in autumn colour
rows.defect: Identical construction to Chestnut and Clove — an olive-yellow flat-sided capsule trunk with a rounded top cap plugged into a fuzzy airbrushed canopy cloud, hard seam at the join, no branches. Every mustRead fails: the leaves are short scattered slivers with no visible venation at all, let alone three full-length veins, and they are not in opposite pairs; there is no scarlet flush of young foliage anywhere (the whole plant is one yellow-olive tone); and the trunk shows no peeling pale inner bark, it is a plain flat yellow shape. The four pink flower rosettes floating in the canopy are the only feature and they are not the harvest.
rows.fix: Draw leaves as leathery ovals in opposite pairs with three strong veins running the full leaf length. Add a flush of bright scarlet young leaves at the shoot tips. Replace the flat capsule trunk with a tapering branched trunk showing a strip of pale inner bark peeled back and a curled bark quill. Break up the fog canopy into leaf masses on visible twigs.

rows.readsAs: an ox-eye daisy or chamomile clump
rows.defect: The flowers are many-petalled white daisies with a yellow disc — 10+ narrow rays each — not cream FIVE-petalled rose blooms.
