The foliage is a mass of grey-blue feathery pinnate combs that read as fern or yarrow leaves, so the mustRead 'tiny three-lobed wedge leaves' is absent, and there are no curling feathery seed plume tails (the combs read as leaves, not plumes). Same fan-of-straight-rods armature as Chili Pepper and Chokecherry.
rows.fix: Cut the flower to exactly five broad rounded overlapping cream-yellow petals around a yellow stamen boss. Replace the pinnate combs with tiny thick wedge leaves notched into 3-5 blunt lobes, clustered tight along twiggy branches, dull green above with a white-woolly edge. Then add the actual harvest as separate long S-curled silvery plume tails on the seed heads so plume and leaf are visually distinct.

rows.readsAs: an edelweiss, or a frosted bottlebrush conifer sapling
rows.defect: A tall dense white-blue column of stacked overlapping leaves running the full height of the picture, topped by one white flower. Cloudberry is a short herb with one or two rounded five-lobed crumpled leaves — this has dozens of pointed white bracts in a repeating vertical stack, and the proportion is a tall spike rather than a low squat plant. The single amber-orange berry, which is the entire harvest and the plant's identity, does not appear at all. Leaf colour is white-frost, not mid green. The stacking is mechanically regular, each tier the same size and spacing as the last.
rows.fix: Strip it to one short stem carrying one or two large rounded, deeply wrinkled five-lobed green leaves, and put a single golden-amber compound berry (clustered drupelets, raspberry-like) on top of the stem. Keep one small white five-petal flower. Recolour green with deep vein creasing. Delete the vertical bract stack entirely.

rows.readsAs: a generic broadleaf tree with orange caterpillars in it — an alder or mulberry
rows.defect: The crown is a wide rounded mushroom cloud clearly broader than tall — the exact opposite of the mustRead 'narrow conical evergreen crown', and it contradicts the 0.6 aspect in the row. The trunk is the same flat brown capsule with a rounded cap seen in Chestnut and Cinnamon, meeting the canopy at a hard line with no branching. The buds are rendered as lumpy orange vertical strings hanging inside the canopy that read as caterpillars or catkins, not as clusters of nail-shaped buds at the BRANCH TIPS. Leaves are scattered slivers, not opposite glossy lance pairs.
rows.fix: Narrow and heighten the crown into a cone/spire silhouette to match aspect 0.6. Replace the capsule trunk with a tapering branched trunk. Move the buds to the outer tips of branches as small upright sprays, and redraw each bud as a nail shape — a slim pink-red shaft with a small rounded four-lobed head — instead of a bumpy string. Set the leaves in opposite pairs, glossy lance-shaped, with a bronze flush at the shoot tips.

rows.readsAs: a generic lollipop tree with a green popsicle stick for a trunk
rows.defect: The defining cauliflorous feature is absent. The pods are five tiny dark-brown slivers floating INSIDE the green canopy blur, not ribbed melon-sized pods erupting from the trunk — and two of them overlap leaves with no attachment at all, reading as dead twigs or insects stuck to the canvas. The trunk is a flat mid-green capsule with a perfectly rounded bottom cap, uniform width top to bottom, no taper, no root flare, no bark texture, and it meets the canopy at a hard horizontal cut-off line. Leaves are small pointed almond blades pointing outward/upward in a radial spray — the opposite of 'big limp drooping oblongs' — and each floats free of any twig inside a soft green fog. Canopy is a circular airbrushed blob with a bright hot spot in the middle.
rows.fix: Move pods onto the trunk and thick lower limbs: 4-6 fat ellipsoids attached to short thick cushions on the bark, longitudinal ribs, yellow-to-red gradient, none inside the leaf mass. Rebuild the trunk as a brown fissured taper with a flared base and limbs that swell where they leave the trunk. Swap the leaf primitive for long broad oblongs hanging tip-down from visible petioles. Drop the radial-spray canopy layout and the centre glow blob.

rows.readsAs: a sheaf of ripe wheat or goldenrod with a few asters tucked in
rows.defect: Entirely the wrong colour and the wrong leaf. Leaves are small narrow golden-amber pointed blades — wheat/autumn gold — where the row calls for huge thick chalky pale grey-green ovals. They alternate in a dense feathery ladder up a dozen thin stalks rather than sitting as large opposite pairs clasping one thick stem. The inflated balloon pods are entirely missing. All the stalks erupt from a single solid tan trapezoid cone at ground level with a hard seam where they enter it. The lilac five-point star flowers are the one correct element, but they sit as flat stickers on top of the foliage.
rows.fix: Recolour foliage to chalky pale grey-green with a dusty bloom. Replace the narrow blades with large thick oval leaves in true opposite pairs, base clasping a single visible thick stem, 6-8 pairs total. Add 2-3 inflated curved grey-green balloon pods. Collapse the multi-stalk sheaf into one stout stem and delete the tan cone base — let the stem widen into the soil.

rows.readsAs: a dusty olive tree with clusters of blackberries or fungus balls
rows.defect: Two of three mustReads fail. The bark is a flat solid mid-brown capsule — one uniform colour, dead straight parallel sides, a perfectly rounded bottom cap, zero vertical fissures, zero grey. The leaves carry no venation at all and no pale underside; they are flat khaki-olive pointed ovals, the same dull yellow-brown as the canopy fog, nothing like glossy deep green. The berries are the worst element: three clusters of pale bluish-white lumps peppered with dark dots, which read as blackberry aggregates, fish eggs, or dice — not small round black berries in shallow cups. Trunk meets crown at an abrupt line with no branching visible.
rows.fix: Give the trunk grey-brown vertical fissure striping, taper, and a flared base. Recolour leaves to glossy deep green with a visible pale blue-grey flipped underside on some blades and draw the three basal veins. Replace the spotted lump clusters with small glossy black spheres, 5-8 per loose spray, each in a tiny pale cup. Show branches leaving the trunk into the dome.

rows.readsAs: a fern frond or a young conifer sprig with a yellow bud on top
rows.defect: This is not a brassica. It is one dead-straight vertical stem carrying twelve identical mirrored pairs of narrow teal blades in a perfectly regular ladder — a machined pinnate frond, every pair the same size, the same angle, the same shape. Leaf colour is cyan-teal, not waxy blue-green. The 'flat-topped mass of vivid yellow flowers' is a single yellow arc smaller than one leaf, perched on the stem tip like a hat. No clasping leaf bases with rounded ears, no pods at all. The whole silhouette is a narrow spike where the row asks for aspect 0.6 (wider than tall).
rows.fix: Build a branched herb, wider than tall: lobed stalked lower leaves, narrow upper leaves whose bases wrap the stem with visible rounded ears. Replace the tip arc with a broad flat-topped corymb of many four-petalled yellow flowers spanning most of the width. Add slender upright pods angling up from the stem below the flowers. Randomise leaf size/angle down the stem and recolour to dull waxy blue-green.

rows.readsAs: a string of blueberries or a bunch of grapes
rows.defect: The leaves are perfect spheres. Eight identical blue-violet balls with a specular highlight and a faint seam line, strung along a thin wavy green thread — geometric primitives, not foliage of any kind, and blue rather than glossy deep green. The 'thick woody rope stem' is a hairline green wire with no bark and no thickness. Tendrils are literal tiny perfect circles stuck onto the stem at four points. There is no host trunk, no twining grip, and leaves are spread evenly along the whole length rather than concentrated at the top. Nothing hangs or loops — the stem is a shallow S floating in the middle of the frame.
rows.fix: Replace the spheres with large heart-shaped leaves, asymmetric, glossy deep green, each on a short petiole with a visible midrib and lateral veins. Thicken the stem into a woody rope with bark shading that loops down and hangs free. Concentrate the leaves in the top third and leave the lower rope bare. Redraw tendrils as spiral coils, not circles, and give them something to grip.

rows.readsAs: an agave, yucca, or dwarf fan palm
rows.defect: All three mustReads fail. There are no canes — thirteen straight rigid pointed blades radiate in a symmetric starburst directly from one point at soil level, forming a low fan much wider than tall (the row asks 0.8, taller than wide). Nothing arches; every blade is dead straight and stiff. There is no separate low flowering shoot along the ground. The only harvest element is a single small dark grey sliver sitting on one leaf near the centre, which reads as a dead twig or an insect landed on the plant, not pale green three-sided pods — and it is the same off-body sliver primitive used for Cacao's pods in this same batch.
rows.fix: Build a clump of 3-5 tall vertical canes, each carrying long lance leaves in two opposite ranks that arch over at the tips. Aspect must be tall. Add a separate thin shoot snaking horizontally across the soil away from the clump, carrying a row of small pale three-sided pods at ground level. Delete the sliver on the leaf entirely.

rows.readsAs: a mimosa or tree fern
rows.defect: Reads as a mimosa, not a carob. The leaflets are tiny narrow serrations packed along thin rachises like a fern or acacia frond — the exact opposite of 'rounded coin-like glossy leaflets in pairs'. Everything is washed pale sage-grey rather than dark glossy green. The pods are two short dark smudges floating inside the canopy fog, horizontal, unattached, and nowhere near long, flat, leathery or hanging in bunches. The trunk is a flat sage capsule with a rounded bottom cap and no bark, forking into a Y whose two limbs are the same width as the trunk with a hard V seam at the join. The crown is a soft airbrushed cloud with a bright hot spot rather than a dense dome.
rows.fix: Replace the serrated fronds with 6-10 large rounded coin leaflets in opposite pairs on a stout rachis, dark glossy green with paler backs. Hang 4-6 long flat dark brown leathery pods in bunches from the lower limbs so they dangle below the foliage. Recolour trunk to grey-brown bark, taper it, and let the limbs thin and swell where they leave the fork. Kill the canopy glow blob.

rows.readsAs: an ice cream cone under a chain-link fence
rows.defect: Two hard stuck-on defects. First, the root's 'side hairs' are five straight beige sticks that pass clean THROUGH the root body and stick out both sides, drawn over and behind it rather than growing out of it. Second, the foliage is a floating lattice: a diamond grid of identical green X-marks, machine-regular, with an obvious empty gap of dark background between the bottom of the leaf mass and the top of the root — the tops are not attached to the plant. The root itself is a hard-edged cone with dead-straight sides and a perfectly flat horizontal top cut, more ice-cream cone than taproot, and it is pale tan-wheat rather than orange. No green shoulder. The two ring marks are perfect straight horizontal lines across the cone.
rows.fix: Reroot the leaves: converge the petioles into a tight crown that physically sits on the root shoulder, no gap. Replace the X-grid with irregular feathery umbellifer foliage of varying scale and droop, fresh bright green. Redraw side rootlets as thin tapering hairs emerging from one edge of the root only, curving away, never crossing the body. Recolour the root to orange with a green shoulder, curve the sides, round the top into the crown, and make the ring marks shallow curved arcs following the taper.

rows.readsAs: A white water lily or lotus flower with a tiny pink daisy growing out of its centre
rows.defect: This is not clover in any respect. The plant is a single large cream-white many-petalled rosette — a water lily / lotus bloom — with roughly 20 long pointed petals radiating from a central point, and one thin bare green stalk running straight up through the middle of it to a tiny 20-pixel pink daisy with visible separate ray florets. There are no trifoliate leaves, no three rounded leaflets, no pale V/chevron watermark, no green foliage at all. All three mustRead features are missing. The flower head is a flat daisy with rays, not a globe pompom, and the stalk pierces the rosette rather than rising from a leaf clump.
rows.fix: Rebuild from scratch as a low herb: draw 3-5 clover stems each terminating in THREE rounded heart-shaped leaflets meeting at a common point (petiole splits into three short petiolules), leaflets mid green with a pale crescent band across the upper third of each. Replace the lotus rosette entirely. Replace the daisy with a spherical pompom head built from many tiny tubular florets packed on a ball, pink-white, on its own bare stalk taller than the leaves. Aspect must be a squat clump, not a single tall bloom.

rows.readsAs: A clump of dried golden reed or wheat-coloured bamboo with white bottlebrush flowers
rows.defect: Colour is completely wrong — the entire bush is saturated orange-gold/amber, not dusty grey-green, and nothing is woolly or whitish. The leaves are flat isoceles triangles and sharp diamond facets with straight machined edges, pinned onto the stems at a hard angle with a visible seam at every attachment; they are neither oblong, puckered, nor rolled-under, and they are not in opposite pairs. The flower clusters are five white cylindrical bottlebrush spikes standing vertically on top of the stems, reading as fluffy pipe-cleaners rather than whorled ball-clusters spaced along a stem. The silhouette is a tight vertical vase-bundle of near-parallel canes rising from a single trapezoidal base, not a mounded shrub.
rows.fix: Recolour foliage to desaturated grey-green (#8f9c86 range) with a paler whitish underside pass on the down-facing leaf halves. Replace the triangular facet leaf with a small oblong blade drawn as a filled curve with a rolled dark edge and a stippled/dimpled surface texture. Set leaves in opposite pairs at each node with a short curving petiole that widens into the stem so there is no seam. Change flowers from vertical bottlebrush cylinders to 3-4 discrete spherical whorls encircling the upper stem at intervals, each ball made of small two-lipped pale lavender florets. Spread the stems outward into a wide mounded dome instead of a parallel vertical bundle.

rows.readsAs: A white feather duster or a dead fan palm on a forked wooden post
rows.defect: The fronds are cream-white/bone coloured, not green — the whole crown looks dead or made of feathers. The trunk is a flat olive-green FORK: it rises straight then splits into a Y with a second stubby arm, which palms never do; both arms are drawn as constant-width slabs with perfectly straight parallel machined sides, flat colour, no ring scars, no taper, no lean. The crown sits as a separate fan pasted on top of the fork with an obvious hard boundary — the fronds do not emerge from a crownshaft. Leaflets are drawn as identical rigid comb teeth at a fixed angle, so each frond reads as a saw blade rather than an arching feather. Only ONE small brown nut is present, tucked at the fork, instead of a cluster of nuts.
rows.fix: Recolour fronds mid green with yellow-green midribs. Delete the Y-fork and draw a single leaning trunk that tapers upward, curved, grey-brown, with horizontal ring scars spaced up its length and a widened flared base. Grow the fronds out of a crownshaft so the frond bases converge into the trunk top with no seam; give each rachis a real arch that droops at the tip, and vary leaflet length along it (short at base and tip, long at mid) instead of uniform comb teeth. Add a cluster of 5-8 green-to-brown husked nuts wedged where the frond bases meet the trunk.

rows.readsAs: A bunch of dried golden grass stems with red berry heads — essentially the same plant as Coastal Sage in this batch, recoloured
rows.defect: Nearly identical in construction to Coastal Sage in this same batch — same amber-gold vase-shaped bundle of near-vertical canes from a single trapezoidal base, same flat pointed leaflets stuck on at hard angles. Leaf colour is orange-gold, the opposite of the specified dark glossy green, and there is no gloss highlight anywhere. There are no tiered horizontal branch layers at all — the plant is strictly upright, so the defining coffee silhouette is absent. Leaves are small pointed lozenges alternating up the canes rather than large opposite waxy blades with wavy margins, and they are attached with a visible hard seam. The red berries sit in four rounded terminal bouquets at the very tops of the canes, like a flowering herb, instead of being clustered tight against the stem in the leaf axils.
rows.fix: Recolour leaves dark green with a specular highlight strip along each blade. Restructure the branching: one central vertical trunk with 4-5 pairs of near-horizontal branches at spaced heights, foliage held in flat horizontal sprays. Draw leaves in opposite pairs, large, elliptical, with a scalloped wavy outline and a visible midrib, joined to the branch by a short thickening petiole. Move the cherries off the tips and pack them in tight 3-6 berry clusters pressed against the branch at each leaf axil, with a small dimple/calyx dot on each berry.

rows.readsAs: A closed tulip bud or a soft orange tube sponge / sea anemone
rows.defect: The render is a small smooth salmon-orange bundle of about eight fat rounded tubes converging to a single point at the base and flaring open at the top with two dark holes visible in the opening. Every surface is soft, glossy and rubbery with a smooth gradient — it reads as a soft-bodied animal or a closed tulip, which is precisely the opposite of the required stony brittle look. There is no segmentation whatsoever: the tubes are continuous unbroken cylinders, so the jointed bead-like branchlets mustRead is entirely missing. There is no branching (the tubes never fork), no chalky pink-lilac colour (it is warm salmon-orange), and no rock and no hard crust plating anything. All three mustRead features fail.
rows.fix: Recolour to chalky pale pink-mauve with a matte, slightly dusty surface and white bleached tips. Break every branchlet into a chain of short bead segments with a visible constriction/joint between each, and make the branchlets fork dichotomously two or three times. Kill the glossy gradient — use a flat mineral shading with fine granular speckle. Add a dark rock substrate at the base and plate it with an irregular hard pink crust that spreads over the rock with a scalloped raised margin, so the crustose form reads alongside the branching form.

rows.readsAs: A corn plant — but with the leaves and cob visibly pinned onto a bamboo cane
rows.defect: The overall silhouette does read as a maize plant, but the construction is assembled rather than grown. The stalk is a bamboo cane: straight, constant width, with hard pale horizontal node bands drawn across it, and every leaf springs from one of those bands with a visible seam — the leaf base does not clasp or sheathe the stem the way a corn leaf does. The leaves are smooth pointed lozenges with no white midrib and no rippled margin. The cob is an isolated brown ellipse floating against the stem with no husk leaves wrapping it and a hard outline where it overlaps the leaf behind it; its silk is drawn as a flat radiating fan of straight lines that reads as a second tassel rather than a soft tuft. The terminal tassel is likewise a small flat fan of straight spokes instead of a feathery drooping panicle, so the top and the cob look like the same object at two sizes.
rows.fix: Give the stalk a slight sway and taper, soften the node bands into subtle swellings, and grow each leaf out of a sheath that wraps the stem for a short distance below the node so there is no hard join. Add a white midrib line down each blade and a slight wave to the margin. Rebuild the cob: wrap it in overlapping green husk leaves whose tips splay open, angle it up out of a leaf axil rather than pasting it flat on the stem, and replace the straight-line fan with a soft mass of fine curling pale-gold silk threads at the tip only. Make the top tassel taller, multi-branched and drooping with fine anther beads so it cannot be confused with the silk.

rows.readsAs: A stem of cotton buds or a cluster of white mushrooms / gumballs on a bare twig
rows.defect: The plant has no leaves at all. It is a bare dark-olive stem, straight for the lower two thirds, splitting into two branches, each tipped with a clump of five or six perfect white spheres. The broad 3-5 lobed palmate leaves are completely absent, so one mustRead fails outright. There is no split brown boll husk anywhere — the white fibre is rendered as clean smooth circles with no burst capsule, no dry brown carpel valves, no fibre texture, so the second mustRead fails. There is no cream-yellow hibiscus-like flower with a dark centre, so the third fails as well. The bolls are geometric primitives: each is a flat-shaded perfect circle with a soft highlight, overlapping its neighbours with a hard edge, reading as gumballs.
rows.fix: Add the plant: a bushy branching frame carrying alternate broad palmate leaves with 3-5 pointed lobes, mid green with reddish veins, and reddish stems. Rebuild each boll as a brown woody capsule split into 4-5 pointed valves that curl back, with a ragged irregular puff of white fibre bulging out between them — silhouette must be lumpy and fibrous, never circular. Add at least one open cream-yellow five-petalled hibiscus-type flower with a dark maroon throat and a protruding staminal column. Move the bolls into the leaf axils along the branches rather than bunching them all at two branch tips.

rows.readsAs: A generic cartoon lollipop tree with three cherries stuck on the side
rows.defect: A lollipop tree. The trunk is a single flat brown slab with straight parallel sides that runs from the ground to the middle of the canopy and simply stops — there is no branching, no twigs, no spur shoots, so the twiggy irregular crown mustRead is missing entirely. The canopy is a soft yellow-olive blur blob with about twenty pointed lozenge leaves scattered on top of it like confetti; the leaves have no teeth and no visible attachment to anything, and the blur reads as a glow rather than foliage. There is no blossom at all — not one petal — so the abundant pink-and-white five-petalled flower mustRead fails. There are only THREE apples, stacked in a near-vertical line at the left edge, each a perfectly circular glossy red ball sitting directly against the canopy with no stalk; the spec calls for masses of small apples on long slender stalks, and neither the quantity nor the stalks are present. Overall colour is sickly yellow-brown rather than mid-green.
rows.fix: Recolour foliage mid green. Replace the slab trunk with a tapering trunk that forks into 3-4 main limbs which subdivide into visible twigs reaching the canopy edge, with short knobbly spur shoots along them. Delete the blur blob and build the canopy from actual leaf clusters attached to those twigs: oval leaves with a pointed tip and a finely serrated edge, each on a short petiole. Add 15-25 small apples distributed through the whole crown, each hanging on a long thin stalk so it sits clear of the foliage, sizes varied and colours ranging red to yellow with a slight matte bloom rather than a hard specular dot. Add a scatter of five-petalled pink-and-white blossoms with visible yellow stamens across the crown.

rows.readsAs: A fern frond or a sprig of bamboo with a white berry spike — nobody would say mint
rows.defect: It is a single erect frond, not a mint. One straight round green stem carries ~14 smooth-edged lanceolate leaves in near-opposite pairs down its whole length — no teeth on any margin, no square stem, no branching, and no compact low cushion habit at all (it is a tall narrow single shoot, aspect reads ~0.5 not 1.1). The 'flower' is a stack of ~10 white spheres glued in a vertical column at the stem tip, uniform white with hard round outlines — not lilac whorls clustered at shoot tips. No purple tint anywhere; the green is one flat mid-green with a soft gradient. Every leaf is the identical shape rotated, joined to the stem with a visible hard butt-joint where the ellipse meets the stalk.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a low branching cushion: 5-8 short stems fanning from a common base, each ridged with visible flat faces to read as square in section and washed purple at the nodes; leaves half the current length, ovate not lanceolate, with 4-6 saw teeth cut into each margin and a paired node so the pairs are unmistakably decussate; replace the white bead column with 2-3 tight lilac whorl rings encircling the top nodes (petals, not spheres); blend the leaf base into the stem with a short tapered petiole instead of butting the ellipse against it.

rows.readsAs: A cluster of turquoise soap bubbles, or a coral/fungal mass — not a plant at all
rows.defect: This does not read as a plant. It is a mound of roughly nine overlapping near-perfect turquoise SPHERES with strong specular highlights, stacked like soap bubbles, each separated from its neighbour by a hard crescent seam. The colour is saturated cyan/teal, nowhere near 'bright fresh green', and there is no red flush on any margin. The two largest spheres on the right are cut by a single straight ruled line across them, which reads as a rendering artifact, not a leaf vein. The leaves are not kidney-shaped — they are balls; no stalks are visible at all, so the rosette is missing. A single thin green stick rises dead-centre carrying a short column of coral-pink beads; the stick passes IN FRONT of the mound with no attachment point, so the seed spike is floating on top of the blob rather than growing from the crown.
rows.fix: Scrap the sphere stack. Draw 6-9 genuinely reniform blades — wider than long, with a notched heart-shaped base and a smooth undulate margin — each on its own visible arching petiole radiating from one crown point, overlapping in plan view so the rosette reads as flat and ground-hugging. Recolour to fresh yellow-green with a red flush bleeding inward from the margins and running down the petioles. Anchor the seed stem into the crown behind the leaves and rebuild the spike as loose papery three-winged valves in crimson-pink, not beads.

rows.readsAs: A dead or frost-killed fern frond with a pink bud on top; possibly a grey bottlebrush
rows.defect: Same template as Alpine Mint, recoloured. A tall narrow single stem with ~9 pairs of identical dull grey-lavender lanceolate leaves — but the reference asks for aspect 0.5 (broad) and BIG SOFT BROAD oval-diamond leaves; these are narrow, hard-edged, and desaturated purple-grey, closer to dead foliage than to green flushed crimson. The stem is thin and olive, with no crimson and no grooving or veining. The harvest is a tiny 12-bead pink column at the very tip, maybe 5% of the plant's height — the mustRead calls for a HEAVY plume-like drooping tassel, which is the single defining feature of amaranth and it is absent. Leaves butt into the stem at a hard angle with a visible joint line.
rows.fix: Widen the whole plant to aspect ~0.5: fewer, much larger leaves, broad rhomboid/ovate with a pointed tip and a wavy soft edge, alternate not opposite. Recolour foliage mid-green with crimson bleeding along the midrib and into the petiole, and make the stem thick, crimson-flushed and vertically grooved. Replace the bead column with a massive branched panicle occupying the top third of the frame — many drooping filiform tassels of tiny crimson florets, some arching over and hanging down past the upper leaves.

rows.readsAs: A rusty broccoli head, a smoke plume, or an autumn shrub — not a flowering plant
rows.defect: An amorphous orange cloud of ~20 fused blobs sitting on top of three thin straight purple sticks. There is not a single trumpet flower anywhere in the image — no funnel, no flared recurved rim, nothing pendulous. There are no identifiable leaves either: the whole crown is one undifferentiated lumpy mass with soft airbrushed spheres embossed into it, so no oval wavy-edged foliage reads. The colour is rust/terracotta throughout, not mid-green foliage plus white/apricot flowers. The stems are pale lilac straight tapers that vanish into the underside of the blob with no branching and no visible join into the crown mass. As a shrub it fails: no multi-stemmed woody frame is legible, just three matchsticks under a cloud.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a small multi-stemmed tree: 3-4 woody grey-brown stems that fork visibly and carry a loose crown of large, individually drawn ovate leaves with wavy margins and asymmetric bases, in mid green with a downy soft edge. Then hang 5-8 genuinely pendulous trumpets from the branch undersides — long tapered corolla tubes pointing straight DOWN, each ending in a wide flared mouth with five recurved points, in cream to apricot with visible longitudinal pleats. The flowers must be the largest single elements in the picture; right now the plant's signature feature does not exist.

rows.readsAs: A golden fern or an ear of wheat with a mushroom on top
rows.defect: A tall narrow golden-yellow frond, and the entire plant is the wrong colour — bright gold/ochre instead of mid green with purple stems. The leaves are drawn as long feathery pinnate ranks of tiny identical leaflets, i.e. a fern, not the broad toothed twice-divided leaflets of angelica. The stem is a thin uniform green-gold line with no thickness, no ridging, no purple, and there are NO inflated sheaths where the leaf stalks meet it — that mustRead is entirely absent, and the leaf ranks simply intersect the stem line. The umbel is a single flat white HALF-DISC — a perfect geometric semicircle with a straight bottom edge — perched on the tip like a mushroom cap; it is a primitive, not a globe of tiny flowers, and its ruler-straight lower edge is the most machined thing in the batch.
rows.fix: Recolour to mid green with a strongly purple-flushed stem, and make the stem thick and visibly hollow-ridged (parallel grooves, a cut-tube feel) rather than a hairline. Add the inflated papery sheaths: a swollen balloon-like collar clasping the stem at each node with the petiole emerging from it. Redraw the foliage as few, large, twice-divided leaves of broad toothed leaflets, not fern-fine ranks. Replace the half-disc with a true compound umbel — dozens of individual rays radiating from one point, each tipped with a small cluster, forming a hemispherical dome with an irregular outer edge and visible gaps between rays.

rows.readsAs: A frosted fern, or a fossil imprint of one — and it is plainly the same plant as Angelica two rows up
rows.defect: Structurally identical to Angelica in the same batch — same tall narrow frond silhouette, same rank-and-file pinnate leaflets, same flat white half-disc primitive stuck on the tip — just recoloured pale silver-white instead of gold. The mustRead 'two clearly different leaf shapes on one plant' fails completely: every leaflet in the image is the same tiny hooked flake repeated top to bottom, with no rounded long-stalked lower leaves at all. Colour is near-white grey, not bright yellow-green. The flower head is one semicircular disc with a straight bottom edge, not several small loose white umbels. The stem is a plain smooth line with no ribbing.
rows.fix: Differentiate the two leaf zones hard: at the base, 3-4 rounded, coarsely toothed, long-stalked leaves splayed low; above, thread-fine dissected foliage — the contrast is the whole identity of the plant. Recolour to bright yellow-green. Give the stem visible longitudinal ribs and a slight zig-zag between nodes. Replace the disc with 3-5 separate small flat-topped umbels on diverging peduncles, each made of individually visible tiny white florets with gaps between rays, and add a few ripening ribbed grey-brown seeds. Most urgently, break the shared silhouette with Angelica — as shipped these two are the same asset in two palettes.

rows.readsAs: A lollipop tree icon or a broccoli floret on a stick — a generic 'tree' pictogram, not specifically an apple
rows.defect: The trunk is a machined primitive: a perfectly straight, parallel-sided olive capsule with rounded ends, identical width top to bottom, no taper, no bark texture, no root flare, and no branches whatsoever. Where it meets the canopy there is a hard horizontal cut-off line — the foliage mass simply sits ON the stick. The canopy is a flat-bottomed mushroom cap with a soft airbrushed green haze behind scattered leaf ellipses, so the crown is a domed blob rather than the low wide CROOKED crown the reference asks for; the trunk is also far too tall relative to the crown for an apple. The four apples are flawless circles with a single specular dot, floating in the leaf layer with no stalk attaching them to anything, and there is no blossom anywhere. Leaves are identical smooth ellipses with no teeth, scattered like confetti rather than borne on twigs.
rows.fix: Taper and bend the trunk, flare it into the ground, and — critically — split it into 3-4 crooked primary limbs that fork upward and carry the leaf mass, so the crown grows out of the wood instead of resting on it; kill the horizontal seam. Widen and lower the crown, break its outline into irregular lobes with sky gaps. Give the leaves fine marginal teeth and cluster them along visible twigs. Hang the fruit in twos and threes from short visible pedicels off those twigs, deform the circles slightly and add a calyx dimple and a stem well; add a scatter of pink-white five-petal blossom.

rows.readsAs: The same tree as Apple with orange fruit — a generic orange/citrus tree at best
rows.defect: The same asset as Apple with a different leaf stamp and orange fruit — identical parallel-sided olive capsule trunk, identical rounded-rectangle profile, identical hard horizontal seam where the trunk disappears into a flat-bottomed dome of foliage, identical branchlessness. The leaves are near-circular pale grey-green paddles with a single ruled midrib line, so they read as coins, not as broad heart-shaped leaves with an abrupt drip-tip and fine teeth; the mustRead red stalks are absent (no petioles are visible at all). The three orange fruit are perfect circles with a specular dot, floating unattached, with no suture groove and no velvet texture — they look like glass marbles. No blossom on bare twigs.
rows.fix: Fork the trunk into real limbs with a taper and bark grain, and dissolve the trunk/canopy seam. Redraw leaves as broad cordate blades — wide at the base, notched heart base, sharp abrupt tip, fine serrations — each on a short RED petiole clearly attached to a twig. Make the fruit slightly ovoid rather than circular, add the shallow vertical suture groove, a red blush on the sunward side, and a soft velvety edge rather than a hard rim; hang them tight against the twigs. Add a few five-petal pale-pink blossoms sitting directly on bare wood. Above all it must stop being the Apple silhouette recoloured.

rows.readsAs: A bleached cycad or a feather-duster on a green slingshot
rows.defect: The trunk is a flat olive-green Y — two straight-edged capsule limbs of uniform width fused into a fork, with a hard silhouette line and zero bark texture. Palms do not fork, and the required 'rough diamond-patterned trunk' is entirely absent (it is a solid single-tone green fill, not even brown). The fronds are bone-white/cream, not the specified blue-grey green, and read as bleached feathers. The fruit bunch is a tiny 20px cluster of brown speckles wedged into the crotch of the fork — it does not hang, there are no orange strands, and nothing about it is 'heavy' or 'massive'. Where the frond fan meets the trunk there is a visible seam: the white fan simply sits behind the green Y with no crownshaft, no leaf-base scars, no transition. Fronds also radiate as a flat 2D fan with no arch or droop.
rows.fix: Replace the forked capsule with a single unbranched trunk that tapers slightly upward and carries overlapping diamond leaf-base scars painted into the trunk body (not overlaid). Recolour fronds from #f2efe4 white to a blue-grey green (~#7d8f78) with a darker rachis. Grow each frond from the trunk apex with a thickened swollen base so the join is a widening, not a butt-joint. Rebuild the harvest as 3-4 pendulous strand-clusters of amber-brown ovals hanging BELOW the crown on visible orange rachillae, scaled to at least a third of the crown width.

rows.readsAs: The same bleached cycad as the Date card — an indistinguishable duplicate
rows.defect: Essentially the same broken asset as Date — same forked olive capsule trunk, same white feather fan, same speckle-cluster in the fork. The 'shaggy trunk patterned with old leaf-base diamonds' is not present in any form; the trunk is one flat green shape with a straight left edge and a hard-cornered fork. The 'heavy date bunches hanging under the fronds' are not hanging at all — the fruit is a single small brown lump sitting on top of the fork junction, above the lowest fronds. Frond leaflets are drawn as identical mirrored spikes off a straight rachis, machine-regular with no length gradation toward the tip, so the crown reads as a graphic starburst rather than foliage. The crown is also symmetrical about the vertical and sits like a decal in front of the trunk.
rows.fix: Same trunk rebuild as Date (single tapering trunk, painted diamond scar texture, brown-grey not green). Then differentiate this card from Date so the pair is not a duplicate: give Date Palm a taller trunk with a fibrous shaggy skirt of old frond bases under the crown, and taper leaflet length along each rachis (long mid-frond, short at tip). Recolour fronds blue-grey green and hang the date bunches on visible stalks emerging from between the frond bases, drooping below the crown line.

rows.readsAs: A generic autumn lollipop tree with orange baubles — a stock apple/orange tree
rows.defect: A textbook lollipop tree. The trunk is a rust-red rounded rectangle of constant width with a rounded bottom cap — no taper, no root flare, no branches at all, and no 'dark blocky bark'; it is a flat orange-brown gradient with straight parallel sides. It terminates abruptly inside a soft brown airbrush blob that is the crown, and there is a clear seam where the hard-edged trunk enters the soft-edged glow. The crown is a circle, not the required 'upright oval'. Leaves are tan/khaki with pale highlights rather than dark green above and grey-green beneath, and they float in a ring around the blur with no twigs connecting them to anything. The four fruits are perfect circles with a single hard specular dot each — plastic beads — and none of them carries the four-lobed papery star calyx that is the species' signature must-read.
rows.fix: Split the trunk into a tapering bole with at least 3-4 diverging scaffold branches that carry the leaves, so leaves attach to wood instead of hovering in a fog. Kill the radial airbrush blob and let the crown silhouette be defined by leaf clusters. Recolour leaves to dark green with grey-green backs on the turned ones. Make the crown taller than wide (aspect 0.8 means upright oval). Re-render the fruit as a slightly flattened globe with a visible four-lobed calyx star cupping the top and a short stalk, and remove the perfect-circle specular dot in favour of a soft broad terminator.

rows.readsAs: A purple clematis or passionflower vine climbing a trellis
rows.defect: Almost nothing in the reference survives. The habit is a vertical S-curve climbing UP the canvas — the must-read 'long trailing runners flat on sand' and the 2.6 landscape aspect are both violated; this is portrait and ascending. There are no leaves whatsoever: not one deeply lobed, rough, grey-green leaf appears. Every green mass has been replaced by huge violet star-shaped flowers, four of them, at roughly a third the canvas height each. The flowers must be 'yellow five-lobed' and are instead purple with eight to ten pointed petals. The only correct element is a single striped green-yellow melon, and it sits at 40px diameter half-hidden behind a petal. The two tendrils are perfect spiral curls of uniform stroke width, drawn like a clock spring rather than a grabbing organ, and they attach to the stem at a hard T-junction.
rows.fix: Re-lay the whole plant horizontally: two or three runners spreading left and right from a crown near the bottom-centre, hugging a sand line. Add the lobed bristly grey-green leaves as the dominant mass. Recolour the flowers from violet to pale yellow and rebuild them with five broad fused lobes and a green calyx. Promote the melon to a prominent hard mottled sphere resting ON the ground plane, and add a second one. Make tendrils taper to a hair at the tip and vary the coil radius so they read as organic rather than as a drawn spiral.

rows.readsAs: A stalk of wheat or a dried fern frond
rows.defect: This is a wheat stalk, not a mint. A single perfectly straight vertical stem carries ten pairs of gold-orange lance leaves in flawless herringbone — identical size, identical 45-degree angle, evenly spaced, mirrored exactly left and right. That regularity is machine output, not growth. The leaf colour is amber/gold, the reference calls for grey green, and mint leaves are not lance-shaped darts. The 'square stem' must-read is invisible — the stem is a plain tapered line with no facet, no edge highlight, no corner shadow. Worst of all, the 'rings of lavender tube flowers up the stem' are reduced to one 15px column of pale beads perched at the very top like a caterpillar; there are no whorls at the leaf axils anywhere down the stem, and the beads are spheres, not tubular lipped flowers. Aspect is roughly 0.35 (tall and thin) against a specified 0.9.
rows.fix: Widen to a shrubby multi-stem habit at aspect ~0.9 — three or four woody-based stems, not one wand. Give the stem a square section by painting a lit left facet and a shadowed right facet with a visible corner ridge. Recolour leaves to grey-green, shorten and round them into small opposite ovals, and break the mirror symmetry (stagger pair spacing, rotate alternate pairs 90 degrees so you see some edge-on). Move the flowers into 4-5 dense whorled rings sitting at the leaf axils up the upper half of each stem, rendered as lavender-pink two-lipped tubes with visible corolla mouths rather than beads.

rows.readsAs: A small columnar cactus with a flower stuck on top — could be swapped with any cactus in the set
rows.defect: The single defining feature of Adenium — the hugely swollen bulbous grey caudex — is completely absent. Instead the plant is a tall narrow green cone that is WIDEST AT THE BOTTOM only in the way any cone is, with straight machined ribs running floor to tip and a perfectly pointed apex. It reads as a cactus. There are no 'few thick stubby branches' — there is exactly one axis and no branching at all. There are no glossy spoon-shaped leaves anywhere in the image. The 'trumpet flowers with pale throats clustered at the tips' are one small flat pink daisy, drawn as a circle with eight identical radial petals and a darker circle centre, stuck on the cone's point like a pin. The rib lines are dead-straight parallel strokes of constant width, the classic flat-facet tell, and the teal-green body colour belongs to a cactus, not to a grey succulent trunk.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette from the ground up: a fat bottle/onion-shaped caudex occupying the lower 55% of the frame at 2-3x the width of anything above it, in warm grey-brown with soft wrinkled shading and no straight edges. From its shoulder grow two or three short thick tapering branches that fork once, ending bluntly. Add tufts of glossy dark-green spoon leaves at those tips only, leaving the stems bare below. Replace the daisy with a cluster of 3-5 deep-pink five-lobed trumpets seen at varied angles, each showing a pale throat and a visible corolla tube receding into the cluster.

rows.readsAs: An ornamental purple grass or a bundle of Japanese maple twigs in a pot
rows.defect: The colour brief is inverted. The must-read is 'silver-white foliage with intense blue flower whorls'; the render gives magenta-pink foliage with pale grey-white flower spikes. The leaves are sharp pointed slivers, some bent into hard chevrons, not small spoon-shaped hairy leaves. Habit is wrong too — instead of a 'rounded low woody bush' this is a tall upright vase-shaped broom, six or seven near-straight canes fanning up from a solid brown cone that sits on the ground like a plant pot. That base cone has a hard triangular silhouette and the canes emerge from its top rim as separate strokes, giving a visible seam between base and stems. The flower spikes are undifferentiated stacks of grey beads on bare stem tips, so the 'stacked rings' read as vertebrae rather than as whorls of lipped flowers, and there is no reddish bract anywhere.
rows.fix: Swap the palette: leaves become silver-grey with a soft hairy edge glow, flowers become saturated blue-violet with reddish-purple bracts behind each whorl. Reshape leaves into small rounded spatulas clustered densely along the lower stems. Compress the habit into a low mound wider than tall, with the canes arching outward rather than standing parallel. Dissolve the brown pot-cone into a splayed woody root crown whose bark texture continues up into the stems so there is no line where they meet. Build each flower spike as 3-4 discrete rings with a gap of bare stem between them, each ring made of small two-lipped corollas facing outward.

rows.readsAs: A generic frost or moonlight herb sprig — structurally the same plant as Desert Mint in this batch
rows.defect: The one feature the whole species is named for is missing: there is no woody seed pod and no pair of long recurved grappling hooks anywhere in the image. There is also no trumpet flower. What is rendered is a rigid dark-purple vertical stem with five tiers of paired pale ice-blue almond leaves — directly contradicting 'sprawling flat-to-the-ground habit' and the 2.0 landscape aspect, and contradicting 'mid green, clammy-hairy' with a frosted white-blue. The leaves are perfectly mirrored ellipses, identical at every tier, evenly spaced, attaching to the stem at a hard point with no petiole and no swelling. A small orange glow sits at the stem tip standing in for a flower but has no petals, no throat, no spots. Critically, this is the SAME template as Desert Mint in this batch — one straight stem, evenly stacked opposite leaf pairs, a small bright thing at the apex — recoloured.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a sprawler: two or three sticky stems running low and outward across a ground line at wide aspect, carrying large rounded shallowly-lobed mid-green leaves of varying size and angle, some overlapping and foreshortened. Add the hero element — one or two blackened woody capsules split into two long inward-curving horns, tapering to needle points, resting on the ground where they are unmistakable at thumbnail size. Add at least one pinkish-purple trumpet flower with a flaring five-lobed mouth and a dark-spotted throat. Give leaves visible petioles that thicken into the stem, and break the mirrored tier spacing entirely.

rows.readsAs: A small ornamental autumn shrub — burning bush or a nandina in fall colour
rows.defect: It is an upright vase-shaped bouquet standing on a solid brown tapered trunk — the single most important mustRead, 'a wiry creeping mat over bog moss', is completely absent. Nothing creeps, nothing trails, there is no ground mat and no moss. The leaves are salmon/orange-red pointed ovals, not tiny dark evergreen ovals, and they sit on thick visible stems rather than hair-thin runners. The pink 'crane's head' backswept flowers are rendered as flat five-dot red-pink pinwheel rosettes at the stem tips with no backswept petals. All the stems converge into a hard-edged brown trapezoid at the base with a visible seam where the green/red stems terminate and the flat brown wedge begins.
rows.fix: Rebuild the form: kill the upright vase skeleton and the trunk entirely. Lay down a low horizontal mat filling the bottom third of the frame — long near-horizontal hair-thin runners crossing each other over a mossy hummock — with only the berry stalks rising vertically (short, 15-20% of frame height). Recolour leaves to dark evergreen (#1e3d24 range) with bronze tips, and shrink them to 1/3 current size in two opposite ranks. Redraw the flower as four narrow petals swept fully backward from a protruding central style.

rows.readsAs: A lavender or Russian sage with sunflowers stuck on top
rows.defect: The foliage is BLUE-VIOLET. Every leaf spray is a bright periwinkle/lavender feather, nowhere near 'dark olive green, glossy with resin'. The leaves are also the wrong architecture: long multi-pinnate feathery sprays with a dozen-plus opposed leaflets, not tiny paired two-lobed V leaflets. Aspect is specified 1 (as broad as tall) but the render is a narrow upright plume roughly 2:1 tall. The cotton-white fuzzy seed balls — an explicit mustRead — are entirely missing. The flowers are flat sunflower-style discs with rounded untwisted petals and a dark centre, not five twisted yellow petals. Branching is a dense converging bundle, the opposite of 'open airy widely spaced'.
rows.fix: Fix the palette first — the leaf hue is off by ~180°; force dark olive (#3f4a22) with a hot specular resin highlight. Replace the pinnate spray primitive with paired teardrop leaflets joined at the base into a V, two per node only. Widen the crown to aspect 1 and cut branch count by half so sky shows between branches. Add the cotton seed balls as soft white fuzz spheres — they are the recognition cue. Give the yellow petals a twist/propeller offset.

rows.readsAs: A bundle of dried straw or a sheaf of wheat stalks
rows.defect: There is no foliage at all. The whole plant is a sheaf of straight mustard-yellow sticks radiating off yellow stems — literal straight machined line segments with flat ends, no taper, no curve. Colour should be dark evergreen; it is gold/straw. Form should be 'a flat creeping heather-like carpet' and it is an upright bundle rising from a flat yellow-green trapezoid trunk. The black berries are three or four tiny grey-brown dot clusters confined to the very top, not glossy black berries nestled tight against foliage. Nothing here reads as a plant surface — it reads as construction material.
rows.fix: This one needs a rebuild, not a tune. Recolour to dark evergreen. Replace the straight stick primitive with short curved needles that have rolled-edge shading and pack them densely (5-10x current count) along the stems so the stems disappear under them. Flatten the whole form to a low spreading carpet (wide, height under 30% of width), remove the trunk. Move the black berries down into the needle mass and give them a specular dot so they read as glossy.

rows.readsAs: An autumn squash or watermelon vine with orange blossoms
rows.defect: The leaves are ORANGE-GOLD star-shaped fans with pointed radiating lobes — they read as flowers, not leaves, so the picture appears to be a vine of orange blossoms. Leaf colour should be mid green and bristly; there is no bristle texture anywhere, the fans are smooth gradient-filled. The fruit is a single small ROUND striped sphere — a watermelon — not 'a long ridged dark green fruit with bumpy warted skin'. No warts, no elongation, no ridges. The yellow star flowers are indistinguishable from the leaves. The tendrils are present as small coils but they are tiny decorative curlicues sitting beside the stem rather than springing from the leaf nodes.
rows.fix: Recolour leaves to mid green and swap the radiating-star primitive for a broad heart-triangular blade with 3-5 shallow lobes and a serrated bristly edge. Redraw the fruit as an elongated cylinder ~3.5:1, dark green, with longitudinal ridges and scattered raised warts plus a specular sheen, hanging DOWN under a leaf. Then add small five-petal yellow flowers as a separate element so the flowers and leaves are visually distinct. Root each tendril at a node so it grows out of the junction.

rows.readsAs: An edelweiss or white chrysanthemum bouquet in a vase
rows.defect: The leaves are WHITE/pale silver star-shaped fans. Currant leaves must be mid green and maple-like with 3-5 lobes; there is not a single lobed green leaf in the image. The berries are dense red pom-pom clusters sitting UPRIGHT at the tips of the topmost stems — the exact opposite of the mustRead 'berries hang in a drooping string (raceme)'. Nothing droops. Aspect is specified 1 but the render is a narrow upright plume near 2:1. All stems converge into a flat green tapered trapezoid at the base with a hard seam at the junction. This shares its exact skeleton with Cranberry, Crowberry and Curry Leaf in this same batch — only the decoration colour differs.
rows.fix: Recolour leaves to mid green and replace the star-fan primitive with a palmate maple-like blade, 3-5 lobes, toothed margin, visible palmate venation. Replace the terminal pom-pom with a pendulous raceme: a thin arching stalk hanging downward off the underside of a cane, with 8-12 small round berries spaced along it. Broaden the crown to aspect 1 and give the canes an outward arch instead of a vertical bundle. Dissolve the trapezoid base into individual cane bases entering the soil separately.

rows.readsAs: An asparagus fern or a young acacia sapling
rows.defect: Structurally the closest in the batch — the pinnate sprays are legible — but the mustRead 'flat heads of tiny white flowers' is entirely absent; instead there are a few small brown-grey berry blobs. Aspect is specified 0.7 (wider than tall) and the render is a narrow upright plume near 1.8:1 tall. The leaflets are an identical chevron mark stamped at perfectly even intervals along every rachis, mirrored left/right — machined repetition, not grown foliage; no leaflet varies in size, angle or overlap. Colour is a bright acid green rather than 'glossy mid to dark green'. The base is again the flat green tapered trapezoid with a hard seam where the stems meet it.
rows.fix: Add the flat-topped white flower heads — they are a mustRead and the fastest fix. Widen and squat the crown to aspect 0.7. Jitter leaflet size, angle and spacing along each rachis by ±25% and let some leaflets overlap the rachis so they stop reading as stamps. Deepen the green and add a specular highlight along the upper half of each leaflet for the gloss. Replace the trapezoid base with several separate stem bases.

rows.readsAs: A stylized wheat frond or a heraldic fern motif
rows.defect: The form is wrong at the root: this is a single tall vertical stalk with leaves running the full height of it, when the mustRead demands 'ground-hugging spoon-leaf rosette' and 'single flower on a BARE stalk'. There is no rosette at all and the stalk is anything but bare. The leaves are white/bone coloured pointed lances, not mid-green spoons, and they are placed in perfectly mirrored opposite pairs at mathematically even intervals — eight identical rungs up a ladder. The flower is a tiny disc at the very top, far too small relative to the plant, and shows no pink-tipped rays.
rows.fix: Rebuild: drop every leaf off the stalk. Build a flat ground rosette of small spoon-shaped (rounded-tip, narrow-base) mid-green leaves radiating outward at near-horizontal, overlapping each other. From its centre send up one bare thin stalk carrying one flower head at roughly 3x its current diameter, white rays with pink flushing on the underside/tips and a flat yellow disc.

rows.readsAs: A purple agave, or a water lily with a buttercup in the middle
rows.defect: The rosette form is right in principle but executed as a PURPLE agave. The leaves are broad mauve triangular spear blades with dead-straight machined edges and sharp points — no 'deeply backward-toothed' jagged margin anywhere, and the colour is nowhere near mid green with a pale midrib. Each blade is a flat gradient wedge with radiating crease lines. The flower is a tiny yellow disc with a dark centre on a hair-thin stalk — it reads as a miniature sunflower, not a dandelion's shaggy dense many-rayed head — and it is far too small for the leaf mass beneath it. The spherical white seed clock, an explicit mustRead, is absent.
rows.fix: Recolour the rosette to mid green with a pale midrib stripe down each leaf. Replace the straight-edged spear blade with a narrow lance carrying deep backward-pointing (retrorse) triangular teeth cut into both margins — that toothed silhouette is the whole recognition. Narrow each leaf to about half its current width and let the outer ones flop toward the ground. Enlarge the flower head 2.5x and rebuild it from many thin overlapping strap rays rather than a disc, and add the white seed clock as a translucent sphere of radiating pappus on a second stalk.

rows.readsAs: a golden forsythia or olive sprig with blueberry pom-poms glued on
rows.defect: It is drawn as an UPRIGHT vase-shaped bush on a single thick tapering trunk, clearly taller than wide — the exact opposite of the required low sprawling mat that is wider than tall. The leaves are bright saturated GOLD-YELLOW, not the specified blue-grey green, and every one of them is the identical pointed-ellipse primitive stamped at a different angle, alternating in perfect metronome pairs up each wand — machined repetition, not foliage. The berries are not scattered singly: they sit in tight 3-5 berry pom-poms at the tips of bare stalks, reading as elderberry/viburnum umbels, and each berry is a flat perfect circle with a hard rim and no waxy bloom. The stems all converge into one solid trunk with a hard edge where the fan of wands meets it.
rows.fix: Rebuild the armature as a prostrate/decumbent mat: several low stems radiating sideways from an off-centre crown, canvas wider than tall (invert the 1.6 aspect so width dominates). Recolour the leaf fill to a dull blue-grey green with a paler underside, and jitter per-leaf length, width, tip-angle and edge noise so no two are congruent. Break the berry clusters apart — place berries singly in leaf axils, drop the hard circle outline, and give each a soft off-centre highlight plus a dusty pale-blue bloom overlay instead of a specular dot. Dissolve the single trunk into 3-4 sprawling woody runners so no stem-to-trunk seam exists.

rows.readsAs: a bunch of purple grapes, or a cluster of soap bubbles with a wire through it
rows.defect: There is no plant here. The body is a heap of eight or nine overlapping PERFECT SPHERES, purple, each with its own radial-gradient sheen and visible hard crescent seams where they overlap — geometric primitives, not leaves. Not one long-stalked basal leaf is present; there is no leaf shape, no blade, no petiole, no vein anywhere in the image. Rising from the centre is a dead-straight machined grey-brown 2px line with zero taper and zero curve, which passes BEHIND the sphere mass and simply terminates — a stalk stuck on, not grown out. On top of it is a tiny stack of orange-red blobs about 40px tall; the reference calls for a dense rose-pink papery seed spire, and this is neither dense, nor pink, nor papery, and it is far too small against the body mass. The colour is fluorescent violet, nowhere near 'fresh mid green'.
rows.fix: Scrap the sphere-cluster generator entirely for this species. Build a basal clump: 6-10 oblong-to-arrow-based blades, each on its own visibly reddish tapering petiole that emerges from a shared rootstock, blades at varied lean and foreshortening, mid-green with a paler midrib. Replace the straight line with a thickened, slightly S-curved reddish stem that tapers from base to tip and is drawn in FRONT of nothing it should hide. Enlarge the seed spire to roughly a third of total height and build it from overlapping translucent rose-pink discs so it reads as papery, not as a chain of orange beads.

rows.readsAs: a silver-leaved ornamental shrub — Russian olive or a small sagebrush
rows.defect: The note says in so many words 'never draw it as an upright tree', and this is an upright shrub roughly twice as tall as it is wide, standing on a stout vertical trunk with a cast shadow beneath it. Nothing about it creeps. The leaves are narrow silvery-white LANCE spikes with sharp points, repeated as one identical primitive in mirrored pairs; the reference asks for small ROUNDED oval leaves, glossy dark green above. The catkins are five pale-yellow bumpy sausages standing on bare vertical sticks, with no red tint and no fuzz — and they float above the foliage on stems that show a hard butt-join where they leave the crown. Construction is identical to Arctic Blueberry in this same batch: same converging-wand armature, same trunk, same stamped-ellipse leaf, only the palette differs.
rows.fix: Force the form to prostrate: render a mat whose width is ~2.8x its height, with woody stems running near-horizontally left and right across the ground plane and rooting at intervals, and remove the trunk and the standing shadow. Swap the lance leaf for a small near-circular oval with a blunt tip, dark glossy top face and a silvery-hairy underside on the leaves that flip over. Redraw the catkins short and upright, red-flushed at the base, with a soft fuzzy stippled edge rather than a clean sausage outline, and grow each one out of a visible leafy node instead of butting it onto a bare stick.

rows.readsAs: an agave or aloe with a stray daisy sticking out of it
rows.defect: The rosette is a symmetric fan of ~15 sharply POINTED lanceolate blades; the reference calls for oval untoothed leaves, and 'oval' and 'dagger' are not the same read. The colour is glowing turquoise-cyan with an internal light source, not mid green, and the whole leaf mass is bilaterally mirrored about the stem like a heraldic device. The flower head is far too small — maybe 45px across against a 300px leaf fan — and it is a perfectly regular geometric rosette of identical triangular petals around a stippled disc, i.e. a stamped sunflower icon, with no ragged tips and no droop at all. The stem is a dead-straight 2px line of uniform width running the full height, and it is drawn OVER the leaf fan rather than emerging from within it, so it reads as a wire laid on top. No stem leaf pairs are present.
rows.fix: Reshape the rosette leaves to blunt-tipped ovals with soft undulating margins, recolour to a matt mid green with fine hair fuzz on the rim, and break the mirror symmetry (vary count, length and splay per side). Enlarge the flower head to ~3x its current diameter, then irregularize it: uneven ray-petal lengths, notched and split tips, several rays drooping below horizontal, and a domed textured orange-gold disc. Give the stem taper and a slight lean, occlude its base behind the front leaves so it grows out of the rosette, and add the 1-2 opposite stem-leaf pairs the reference requires.

rows.readsAs: a cluster of soap bubbles, or a bunch of white mushroom caps on a wire
rows.defect: The single most identifiable feature of this plant — the arrowhead leaf with two backward-pointing lobes — is completely absent. What is drawn is a pile of overlapping cream-white PERFECT SPHERES with visible hard overlap seams, the exact same generator output as Arctic Sorrel in this batch with the hue changed from purple to bone. There is no water, no waterline, no reeds, no mud, nothing aquatic. The stem is a dead-straight olive hairline with no taper that vanishes behind the sphere mass. There is one flower, a tiny 6-point white star of uniform triangular points at the very top — the reference requires WHORLS of three-petalled flowers spaced up the stem, and a dark purple centre, neither of which appears.
rows.fix: Replace the sphere cluster with 4-6 true sagittate blades: broad triangular apex plus two long divergent basal lobes, each on a long triangular spongy stalk rising vertically out of a shallow waterline, with a couple of blades tilted so their underside shows. Add the water: a dark reflective plane with the stalks cutting through it and a soft ripple where each enters. Rebuild the flower stem as a tapering scape carrying three or four WHORLS of three broad rounded white petals with a dark purple centre boss, spaced up the stem, and add the exposed knobbly tuber cluster in the mud if it is to read as the harvest.

rows.readsAs: a generic hosta or lotus rosette — the leaf icon from a gardening app
rows.defect: Two of the three mustRead features are simply missing: there are no white asymmetric flowers anywhere in the frame, and there is no knobbly pale scaled rhizome at the base — the base is a hard flat cut-off line at the bottom of the leaf fan with a blur shadow, so the plant does not appear to enter the ground at all. There are also no stalks: every leaf blade converges directly to one point, so 'long sheathing stalks' is unrepresented. The blades are pointed rather than broad lance-oval, arranged in a mirror-symmetric fan, and rendered in a neon acid green with an internal glow that reads as backlit plastic rather than a matt leaf. Each blade carries one perfectly straight ruled midrib line and no other venation. It is the same rosette build as Arnica in this batch with the flower stem deleted.
rows.fix: Add the missing harvest: a cluster of pale, jointed, scale-ringed rhizomes breaking the soil at the base, partly exposed, with fine roots — this is the whole point of the species. Add a slender side stem carrying a few small asymmetric white flowers. Give each leaf a distinct sheathing petiole so the blades attach at staggered heights along a short stem rather than at a single hub, broaden the blades and blunt their tips, kill the internal glow and drop the saturation to a matt mid green, and curve the midrib with faint pinnate side veins branching off it.

rows.readsAs: a clip-art olive tree with black cherries, standing on a tongue depressor
rows.defect: The trunk is a perfect parallel-sided rectangle with rounded caps — a popsicle stick. No taper, no root flare, no branch division, no bark; it simply disappears into the canopy with a hard vertical edge on both sides, the classic stuck-on seam. The canopy is not a crown at all but a circular grey-white FOG blob with ~30 small identical pointed-ellipse leaves scattered around its rim, all the same size, none overlapping, none drooping — sprayed on rather than grown. The reference calls for large leathery drooping leaves; these are tiny and radiate outward like a dandelion clock. The fruit is the biggest failure: five perfectly ROUND dark spheres with a specular highlight and a short stick on top, where the species requires pear-shaped pebbled fruit. Fruit and leaf are also nearly the same value, so the fruit barely reads.
rows.fix: Rebuild the trunk with taper, a widening root flare at ground level, and at least two forking limbs that carry the canopy so the join is structural rather than a butt-end. Replace the fog blob with an actual leaf mass: large elliptic blades, 3-4x the current size, overlapping in depth-sorted clumps, hanging tip-down from the branch tips so the crown reads as drooping. Reshape the fruit to a pyriform silhouette — narrow neck at the stalk swelling to a heavy rounded base — hang it so the neck is genuinely attached to a stout short peduncle on a branch, darken it against the foliage, and stipple the skin for the pebbled texture.

rows.readsAs: a firework burst or an ornamental fountain grass in brass
rows.defect: Nothing in this picture reads as bamboo. The culms are thin gold strands that ARCH outward from a single ground point into a symmetric fountain, so the whole thing is wider than tall — the reference asks for aspect 0.5, i.e. tall culms, and a bamboo culm is straight and rigid, not a whip. The nodes are represented by short horizontal dashes floating across the image, and many of them sit in empty space touching no culm at all, which makes them read as scratches on the canvas rather than as rings on a stem. There is not one leaf in the entire frame — the leafy sprays at the top are absent. The brown-sheathed pointed shoots at the base, which the note identifies as the actual harvest item, are also entirely absent. The colour is metallic gold, not mid green, and the strands have a hard specular ridge running down them that reads as brass wire.
rows.fix: Straighten the culms: 5-8 near-vertical rigid stems of differing heights, thick at the base and gently tapering, with only a slight outward lean at the top, in a tall composition. Draw nodes as a swelling ring drawn ON each culm — a slight bulge in the silhouette plus a darker band — never as a free-floating dash, and clip them to the culm path. Add sprays of narrow lance leaves on short branchlets in the upper third only. Add two or three fat pointed cones at the base, overlapping brown hairy sheath scales, pushing up out of the soil — that is the harvestable item and it must be the focal point. Recolour culms to green with a straw cast at the nodes and remove the metallic highlight.

rows.readsAs: A generic willow or bamboo sprig — one stick with leaves. Nobody would say Devil's Club.
rows.defect: The picture is one straight brown stick with six plain almond-shaped leaves alternating off it — nothing else on the canvas. Every mustRead is absent: no yellow needle spines anywhere on the cane (the cane is a smooth clean dowel with a soft brown gradient and not a single spine pixel), no palmate lobed 'open hand' leaves (the leaves are simple entire lanceolate blades with one centre vein), and no scarlet berry cone above the leaves at all. The cane is also perfectly straight, not thick and crooked, and each leaf meets it as a hard butt-joint with no petiole and no swelling into the stem.
rows.fix: Rebuild the leaf as a 5-7 lobed palmate blade on a long petiole radiating from the node, sized to roughly a third of canvas width (giant is the point). Add the spine layer: short yellow bristles distributed along the cane and along the leaf veins, dense enough to fuzz the cane's silhouette. Add the harvest: an upright cone-shaped panicle of small flattened red berries emerging above the top leaves. Give the cane a crooked path with 2-3 direction changes and taper it, and grow petioles out of the cane with a widened base so no butt-joint seam is visible.

rows.readsAs: Three garden stakes or bamboo canes with pinwheel windmills tied to them.
rows.defect: Three identical vertical green rods, uniform width top to bottom with rounded caps, floating parallel and unconnected — they touch neither each other nor the ground shadow. They are capsule primitives: perfectly straight machined edges, one smooth cylindrical highlight down each. No three-ribbed triangular cross-section, no scrambling or hanging, no spine clusters. The 'fruit' is two flat 2D pinwheel stars of pink triangles with green tips, pasted flat onto the middle of two rods with a hard outline and zero volume — it is a sticker on a pole, not an oval fruit with upcurled scale fins. The huge white strap-petalled night flower is entirely missing.
rows.fix: Replace the cylinder stems with 3-winged segments: a triangular section drawn as three scalloped wavy-edged ribs, jointed every so often into segments that arch and droop rather than standing rigid; add small areole spine tufts on the rib crests. Make the fruit a 3D oval body with a shaded pink surface and green scale fins peeling off its skin, hanging off a stem, not centred on it. Add at least one white trumpet flower with long strap petals and a spray of stamens. Anchor the stems to a common base or a support so the composition is one plant.

rows.readsAs: Three mints or pebbles on a small navy plate — or, at full size, a flying saucer.
rows.defect: Three fat teal ellipsoid blobs resting on a dark navy dish that has a thin white perfect-ellipse rim and a pedestal foot beneath it. The water surface has been drawn as a hard-edged saucer primitive, so the whole thing reads as tableware. Only three fronds — not a carpet — and they are thick puffed 3D lozenges rather than tiny flat discs. Not one hair root hangs anywhere, and the fronds do not bud off each other in pairs and threes; they just overlap. Aspect is wrong too: the row states 2.5 wide, but the mass occupies a small central island with huge empty canvas around it.
rows.fix: Delete the saucer and its rim ellipse entirely; render the waterline as a soft dark wash with no outline. Scatter 30+ small flat discs across the full canvas width in irregular clumps, each disc nearly flat-shaded bright light green with a faint reddish underside where it tips. Draw one fine hair root trailing down into the dark from each disc. Join discs into 2-3 frond families with a visible bud notch so they read as budding, not stacked.

rows.readsAs: A clump of chives or eelgrass. It also reads as a lighter cousin of the Elderberry's green stalk in this same batch.
rows.defect: The blade colour is BRIGHT SPRING GREEN. Dulse must be deep purplish-red to brick red — the single most identifying feature of the organism is wrong, which alone makes it unshippable. The form is also wrong: instead of a flat hand-shaped lobed blade it is a fan of about ten narrow uniform-width tube-straps with rounded tips, all radiating from one point. No lobing, no ear-like flaps along the margins, no disc holdfast — the straps just converge to a pencil point on the ground shadow. Each strap has the same cylindrical highlight, so they read as solid rods, not flat leathery sheet.
rows.fix: Recolour the whole blade to deep purple-red with brick-red translucency where it thins. Replace the strap fan with one broad flat blade that splits into a few wide hand-like lobes of varying width, drawn flat with translucent light through it rather than tube shading. Add small ear-shaped flaps budding from the blade margins. Put a small hard disc holdfast on rock at the base with a very short thick stipe, so the blade grows out of a gripped foot instead of tapering to nothing.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon nut tree — walnuts or acorns on a lollipop trunk.
rows.defect: A lollipop tree. The trunk is a flat tan capsule — the same width at the ground as it is at the canopy, both ends rounded, no taper, no root flare, no bark texture — and it terminates inside a grey-green cloud blob with a hard-ish boundary. The four fruits are smooth brown spheres with longitudinal grooves and a little stem knob; there is not one pyramidal spike on them, so the defining armour of a durian is absent. They also sit inside the cloud rather than hanging on a visible stalk from a branch — no branches exist anywhere in the crown. Leaves are pale sage flecks with no bronze-gold underside.
rows.fix: Taper the trunk and flare it into roots at the base; add vertical bark grooving so it is not a solid fill. Draw real major branches out of the trunk into the crown and hang each fruit from a thick stalk on one. Rebuild the fruit surface as a field of sharp pyramidal spikes reading in silhouette (the outline must be prickly, not round). Break the cloud canopy into leaf clusters and flip a share of leaves to a coppery-bronze underside.

rows.readsAs: A single small pink daisy stuck on top of a fern or vetch stalk.
rows.defect: The flower is tiny — roughly a tenth of the plant's height — and completely flat: eight short pink petals sticking straight out in a wheel around a flat brown dot. There is no drooping backswept petal and no raised domed bristly cone, which are the two things that make a coneflower recognisable. The foliage is wrong in three ways: the leaves are arranged in nine neat opposite pairs (must be alternate), they are smooth cyan-teal (must be dark green, coarse and hairy), and they are so regular the stalk reads as a fern frond. The stem is a hairline-thin smooth green line with no bristle and no thickness.
rows.fix: Scale the flower head up several times so it dominates the top of the plant; give it long narrow ray petals that angle downward and back from the disc, and replace the flat dot with a tall domed orange-brown cone built from small bristly scales. Re-space the leaves alternately with irregular gaps, recolour to dark green, and add a coarse stipple for the bristly surface. Thicken the stem and give it a rough hairy edge instead of a clean line.

rows.readsAs: A small silver agave or a frosted yucca with a flower spike.
rows.defect: The woolly bract star has been built as a basal rosette of long pointed silver blades at ground level, with a single bare stalk rising well above it to a tiny white six-point star at the top. That is backwards — the star of bracts belongs at the flower head, framing the flower heads. And the mustRead yellow buttons are simply not present: the little top star has a plain white centre, no yellow at all. The blades are also smooth and glassy, with a clean gradient from white tip to pale grey base and a crisp edge; nothing about them reads as felted wool. The bare stalk is a hard thin line entering the rosette with a visible seam where it passes through.
rows.fix: Move the bract star to the top of the stalk so the blades radiate around the flower cluster, and put several small yellow-ochre button heads in the middle of that star. Kill the smooth gradient: give every bract a fuzzy broken edge and a woolly noise texture so the silhouette looks fibrous rather than cut. Keep a small low rosette of narrow woolly leaves at the base if a rosette is wanted, but make it clearly subordinate. Thicken the stalk and wool it too, so it merges into the rosette instead of piercing it.

rows.readsAs: A fern or asparagus-fern bush with a few grape-like caterpillars on it.
rows.defect: The plant sits on one thick tapered solid-green wedge of a trunk — elder is a woody shrub with several brown-grey canes, and here there is one smooth green cone with a hard edge where the foliage mass starts. The foliage is not pinnate elder leaflets: it is a dense bush of narrow fronds lined with tiny sharp comb teeth, which reads as fern or asparagus fern, and the units are far too small and too numerous to register as 5-7 toothed pointed leaflets. The big flat plate-like heads of creamy white flowers — a mustRead — are completely absent. The berries appear as four or five knobbly caterpillar-shaped purple lumps poking up and out of the mass; they neither form flat drooping plates nor nod under their own weight, and the crimson stalks are not visible.
rows.fix: Replace the green wedge with two or three woody grey-brown canes branching from the base. Rebuild the leaf as a proper pinnate frond: 5-7 broad pointed leaflets in opposite pairs with a terminal one, each large enough to read individually, with saw teeth on the margin, not comb needles. Add at least one big flat-topped creamy-white corymb held above the leaves. Rework the berry heads as wide flat sprays of many tiny dark purple spheres on visible crimson stalks, tilted over so they hang and nod.

rows.readsAs: a young coconut palm or a sago cycad
rows.defect: This is a palm/cycad, not a banana. The fronds are narrow PINNATE feathers — a spray of ~20 thin lance leaflets radiating off each rachis, drawn with a comb-tooth serration along the edge. Banana's mustRead is HUGE undivided paddle blades that tear into ribs; there is not one paddle blade anywhere in the image.
