The false stem is two flat kelly-green capsules meeting in a hard Y-fork at mid-height: perfectly parallel straight sides, semicircular cap on the lower stem base, and a visible hard seam line where the fork splits — a machined primitive, not rolled leaf sheaths. The harvest is a 6-blob cluster of pale yellow circles tucked INTO the crown at the fork, sitting upright; there is no hanging bunch, no arching stalk, and no purple-red bud at all — two of the three mustReads are absent.
rows.fix: Replace the pinnate frond generator with 6-9 large single-blade paddles (blade width ~35% of blade length) spiralling off ONE thickening false stem, and cut each blade with 3-6 wind tears running perpendicular from margin to midrib. Kill the Y-fork — the pseudostem must be a single tapering column whose sheath layers overlap visibly (offset arcs, no straight sides, no capsule end-cap). Rebuild the harvest as an arching stalk emerging from the crown and bending DOWN past the stem, carrying 3-4 stacked tiers of curved yellow-green fingers and terminating in a large teardrop purple-red bud.

rows.readsAs: a generic storybook fruit tree with pumpkins in it
rows.defect: The defining feature — the enormously swollen grey barrel trunk — is missing entirely. What is drawn is a flat pale sage-green vertical bar of constant width (~30px across its whole height) with a rounded pill cap at the bottom: a capsule primitive, no taper, no swelling, no bark, wrong hue. Where the trunk enters the canopy there is a hard straight edge with the leaf mass simply overlapping it — a stuck-on seam, no branch structure at all, so the 'short stubby root-like branches at the top' mustRead is absent. The canopy is a soft mint-green cloud blob with spiky maple/cannabis-like serrated leaflets scattered over it, not palmate 5-7-leaflet sprays, and the whole thing is bathed in a blurry pale halo that reads as fog rather than foliage. The three pods are perfect striped spheres sitting flat on the leaf mass like pumpkins, with no stalks and no long cords — they are painted on top, not dangling.
rows.fix: Rebuild the trunk as a bulging asymmetric barrel: base width ~45% of image, pinched in near the top, silhouette built from irregular noisy curves in warm grey (#9a9c92-ish) with vertical fold shading — no constant-width column, no pill cap. Grow 4-6 short thick tapering branches OUT of the trunk crown, each continuing the trunk's grey and splitting into stubby root-like forks; the canopy must hang off those, sparse and see-through, not as an opaque cloud. Swap the maple leaflets for palmate whorls of 5-7 smooth oval leaflets on a common point. Suspend each pod on a long visible cord from a branch so it hangs BELOW the foliage, and make the pod an elongated velvety ovoid, not a striped ball. Remove the halo bloom.

rows.readsAs: a blue rocket or a spiky blue traffic cone
rows.defect: Colour and shape are both wrong to the point of unrecognisability: this is a tall narrow ROYAL BLUE cone, roughly 4x taller than wide, tapering to a sharp point at the apex. The reference calls for a fat squat grey-green barrel at aspect 0.9 with a FLAT crown; nothing here is squat, nothing is grey-green, and the crown is a spike. The ribs are rendered as straight vertical gradient stripes — perfectly parallel, machine-ruled lines with no accordion depth or bulge. The spines are the worst offence: short white rectangles floating in the black background, clearly detached from the silhouette with visible gaps, not one of them curved or hooked, and they sit only along the left and right outlines rather than on rib crests all around. The harvest reads as a single yellow daisy flower plus a 3-blob cluster stuck on the upper right — there is no ring of scaly yellow barrel fruits crowded at the crown.
rows.fix: Re-derive the body from the cactus form, not a spire: width/height ~0.9, a bulging barrel with a slightly domed FLAT top, silhouette scalloped by the rib crests so the outline itself is wavy. Recolour to desaturated grey-green with red-brown areoles. Draw ribs as 3D accordion folds (lit crest, shadowed valley) that follow the barrel's curvature and converge at the crown, not as straight stripes. Attach spine clusters to areoles ON the rib crests across the whole visible face, each cluster radiating short spines plus one long flattened central spine with a hook at the tip, rooted in the body with no gap. Replace the daisy with a dense ring of 8-12 scaly yellow ovoid fruits crowding the flat crown.

rows.readsAs: a pink ornamental twig arrangement or a dried floral display
rows.defect: The leaves are bright MAGENTA-PINK. The reference demands very dark glossy green leathery lance leaves; the render is the opposite end of the colour wheel, so the single most identifying property of a bay laurel is inverted. The leaf shape is a flat pink triangular shard with straight machined edges and a sharp corner point — a geometric primitive, not a leathery blade, and there is no rippled margin anywhere (mustRead absent). The 'dense conical evergreen shape' mustRead is also absent: this is a sparse open vase of five bare brown sticks, mostly empty black space between them, with leaves attached as isolated pink chevrons at hard angles. Every leaf meets its twig at a visible hard junction with no petiole and no thickening. The flower clusters are grey-white pom-pom balls perched on the very TIPS of the bare stems like lollipops, whereas the reference calls for cream flowers at the leaf joints (axils).
rows.fix: Recolour foliage to near-black glossy green (#1c3a24 range) with a specular highlight streak along each blade. Replace the triangular shards with elongated lance ovals, widest at the middle, tapering at both ends, and give the margin a low-amplitude sine ripple so the edge is never straight. Raise leaf density hard — the canopy must close into a dense conical outline that reads as a solid evergreen mass, not five visible sticks. Grow each leaf from a short petiole that swells into the twig so there is no hard seam. Move the flowers off the stem tips into small cream clusters tucked at the leaf axils, and replace the pom-pom spheres with tight bunches of tiny four-petal florets.

rows.readsAs: an autumn ornamental shrub with berries — reads as a red-leaved sibling of the Bay Laurel in this same batch (identical vase-of-sticks skeleton and identical shard leaves)
rows.defect: The foliage is bright coral RED, not the dull dark green the reference specifies, and every leaf is the same flat pointed shard shape used in Bay Laurel with no toothing on the margin at all. The silhouette is a narrow upright vase clearly TALLER than wide, directly contradicting the 'dense low thicket wider than tall' mustRead. The 'smother of small white five-petal blossom' mustRead is entirely absent — there is not one white flower in the image. The five purple plums are perfect spheres with a specular dot, each perched alone on the bare tip of a stem like a pin head, floating clear of the foliage, instead of clustered tight against the twigs. All stems radiate from one point at a brown trunk base in a symmetrical fan, which reads as machine-generated rather than a thicket.
rows.fix: Recolour leaves to dull dark green with a paler downy underside on the leaves that turn, and cut fine serrations into the margin so the outline is toothed rather than a smooth triangle. Rebuild the silhouette wider than tall (aspect ~1.2 as width:height) as a tangle of many short crossing twigs from multiple ground points, not one symmetric fan from a single trunk. Add the flowering state: dense small five-petal white blossom scattered through the twigs. Move the plums into tight clusters of 3-5 pressed against the twig sides, mid-canopy, and dull the specular highlight into a dusty waxy bloom.

rows.readsAs: a bunch of white grapes or a string of pearls
rows.defect: There is no flower and no leaf in this image. It is eight near-perfect white spheres, each with a hard specular hotspot and a horizontal seam line across the middle, strung along a thin olive stem that zigzags diagonally up the frame — it reads as a bunch of white grapes or a string of pearls. All three mustReads fail: no funnel-shaped pink-magenta flower with a dark star throat, no two-lobed goat's-foot leaf notch (there is no leaf blade at all — only tiny grey wire loops on the stem where leaves should be), and no long straight runner creeping FLAT across sand. The aspect is also inverted: the reference asks for 2.8 (a wide horizontal creeper) and the render is a vertical diagonal column. The spheres are geometric primitives painted on top of the stem, each meeting it with no pedicel and a visible overlap edge.
rows.fix: Lay the runner horizontally across the bottom third of the frame — a long, nearly straight stem with occasional rooting nodes, so the silhouette is wide and low. Replace the spheres with 3-4 open funnel flowers drawn as a flaring trumpet in pink-magenta with five faint fold lines and a dark five-pointed star throat, seen at varying angles, each on its own short pedicel rising off the runner. Add the leaves the render is missing entirely: thick waxy deep-green blades whose tip is notched into two rounded lobes, alternating along the runner, with a glossy highlight following the blade curvature.

rows.readsAs: a dead autumn locust or mimosa branch
rows.defect: Wrong colour and wrong posture. The leaflets are burnt ORANGE-RED where the reference calls for waxy blue-green, and the stem is dead brown — the whole plant reads as a dried autumn twig. The 'purple-blue pea flowers' mustRead is completely absent; there is no flower and no pod anywhere in the frame, so the harvest is unrepresented. The 'low sprawling mat, not upright' mustRead also fails: the vine is a tall vertical S-curve occupying the full height of the canvas with nothing horizontal about it. The pinnate sprays are stuck onto the stem as flat fans of identical stamped ellipses, all the same size and angle within a spray, meeting the stem at a hard right angle with no rachis and no visible attachment; the tendrils are tiny dark circular curls drawn as separate loops floating beside the stem rather than continuing out of a leaflet pair.
rows.fix: Recolour foliage to waxy blue-green with a pale glaucous bloom, and the stem to a live green. Reorient the whole plant into a low sprawling mat: stems running mostly horizontally, overlapping, spilling wide rather than climbing. Give every leaflet spray a visible rachis growing out of the stem at a node, with leaflets in true opposite pairs that vary in size along the rachis and end in a tendril that is the rachis tip continuing and curling — not a detached loop. Add the missing harvest: clusters of 4-8 purple-magenta pea flowers (standard, wings, keel readable) fading to blue, plus a few flat green pods.

rows.readsAs: a clump of ornamental grass with a brass screw stuck in it
rows.defect: The head is far too small and reads as hardware, not grain. It is a single thin gold rod about 1/8 the image height with regular chevron notches ratcheting up it — the profile of a wood screw — capped by a small flared fan. The mustRead is 'extremely long fanned awns, LONGER than the head itself'; here the awn fan is roughly 1/3 the head length, so the proportion is inverted. 'Head nods over when ripe' also fails — the spike stands bolt upright on a perfectly straight vertical stalk. The grains are not readable as plump rows; they are just the notch pattern on the rod. Only one head is present for a whole clump of foliage. On the credit side the basal foliage is genuinely good: the blades fan and arch with real variation, taper to fine points, and grow out of the base with no seam.
rows.fix: Enlarge the spike to ~25% of image height and rebuild it from discrete overlapping plump grains in staggered vertical rows so the rod silhouette becomes lumpy, not a smooth notched cylinder. Draw the awns as 15-25 individual fine bristles springing from each grain tip and fanning upward past 1.5x the head length. Bend the culm's top third over so the head nods and hangs, and add 2-3 more heads at differing heights above the tuft. Warm the ripe head toward straw gold with a green-to-gold gradient down the culm.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon lollipop tree with watermelons in it
rows.defect: The canopy is a soft green fog-blob with ~14 small spiky star-rosette clusters floating on top of it — nothing resembles a big deeply-cut hand-shaped leaf, so the primary mustRead is absent. The trunk is a flat ochre capsule: constant width top to bottom, a perfectly rounded stadium end at the base sitting above the ground shadow with no root flare, and it terminates inside the foliage blob with a hard edge — no branches emerge from it, so the canopy is stuck ON the trunk rather than growing out of it. The 4 fruits are spheres carrying bold dark vertical stripes with a pinched dark polar dimple; they read as watermelons or striped gourds, not fine pebbled breadfruit skin, and they hang in mid-air with no visible stalk. The whole crown also has an unmotivated yellow-green glow halo bleeding past the leaf shapes.
rows.fix: Replace the star-rosette leaf sprite with a large single-blade leaf silhouette cut by 5-7 deep sinuses into broad finger lobes, sized ~3x current so 6-8 leaves fill the crown instead of 14 tokens. Give the trunk a taper plus a flared root base and 3-4 forking limbs that carry the leaf/fruit clusters, so leaf and fruit attachment points are on wood. Kill the vertical stripe pass on the fruit and swap to a dense fine bump/pebble noise, and add a short thickened peduncle from twig to fruit. Delete the crown glow halo.

rows.readsAs: an acacia or mimosa tree with three eyes in it
rows.defect: The leaves are pale khaki pinnate fronds — narrow midrib with many small side leaflets — i.e. fern or mimosa foliage, the opposite of the huge deeply lobed hand-shaped leaf the row requires. The 4 fruits are perfectly smooth grey-tan spheres with a single specular highlight and zero spines; the three sitting in a horizontal row at the same height read unmistakably as eyeballs staring out of the canopy. No milky sap cue anywhere. The trunk is again a straight brown capsule of constant width with a rounded end, no root flare, no branching — it just disappears into the foliage mass at a hard seam. Whole plant is desaturated straw-yellow rather than dark glossy green with pale veins.
rows.fix: Swap the pinnate frond sprite for the same deeply-lobed hand leaf as Breadfruit, add pale vein strokes down each lobe, and push leafColour to a dark saturated green. Rebuild the fruit: soft outward-pointing spine bristles densely covering the sphere silhouette so the outline is fuzzy, not circular; remove the single hard specular dot; scatter the fruit at different heights and depths instead of a level row of three. Add a tapered branching trunk with root flare, and a small white sap bead at one broken leaf base.

rows.readsAs: a white agave or yucca with a red caterpillar on a wire
rows.defect: This is a flat, near mirror-symmetric fan of 13 dead-straight triangular blades radiating from one point — machined edges, ruler-straight sides, no arch, no curl, no thickness. There is no vase: the leaves converge to a single vertex, so there is no cup and nothing holding a pool of water, which is the number-one mustRead. No grey scurfy banding and no red flush; the leaves are ghost-white/pale-blue, badly wrong for a green bromeliad. The bract spike is a hairline dark-green wire with a small red beaded sausage on top, floating clear of the leaf mass and clearly drawn on a separate layer — it neither emerges from a cup nor widens into bracts, and the beads read as a caterpillar. Colour and blade language are also nearly identical to Buckwheat's pale-blue palette in this same batch.
rows.fix: Curve every blade with an outward S-arch and taper, vary length and azimuth (no mirroring), and give the base a short wide funnel of overlapping leaf sheaths with a dark water meniscus disc at the centre so the vase reads. Recolour to mid green with horizontal grey scurf bands and a red flush toward the leaf bases. Rebuild the inflorescence as an overlapping stack of broad red/pink bracts rising from inside that funnel, with small purple-blue florets peeking between them; anchor its base below the leaf tops so it grows out of the cup.

rows.readsAs: a fern frond or a wheat sprig with one blue star stuck on the tip
rows.defect: Rendered as a single strictly erect vertical stem with 11 identical leaf pairs stepped up it at perfectly even spacing — a fern-frond / wheat-sprig ladder, not a sprawling water plant. Aspect is inverted: the row asks for 1.8 (wider than tall, sprawling with rooting stems) and the render is roughly 0.35 (tall and narrow). No water, no sprawl, no rooting nodes. The leaves are flat grey-violet lozenges with no gloss and no toothing — not fleshy glossy green. Flowering is wrong twice over: there is exactly ONE flower, sitting on the apex like a topper, when the row calls for loose sprays rising from the leaf joints; and it is a geometric 6-point star primitive with a plain blue centre, not a 5-lobed corolla with a white eye. Image is also so underlit the plant is nearly invisible against the background. Shares its exact stacked-ladder skeleton with Buttercup and Buckwheat in this batch.
rows.fix: Rotate the growth habit to a low sprawling mat: 3-4 decumbent reddish stems running mostly horizontally with tips turning up, root hairs at the lower nodes, and a shallow water line across the base. Fatten the leaves into short succulent ovals with fine marginal teeth and a glossy specular band, recoloured fresh mid-green. Replace the single apex star with several short axillary racemes of 4-6 small flowers each, four rounded lobes plus a white centre eye. Raise overall luminance ~40%.

rows.readsAs: an ear of corn or a white hyacinth
rows.defect: Zero arrowhead leaves — the defining mustRead is entirely missing. What is drawn is a tight vertical column of ~11 pairs of pale blue-white glossy ovoid pods packed in two overlapping rows along a thin green wire, which reads immediately as a corn cob or a hyacinth spike. No red-flushed jointed stem (the stem is a plain olive hairline). No three-sided pyramid seeds; the only harvest element is a tiny cream fan blob perched on the very top. Aspect is badly off: the row says 0.8 and the silhouette is roughly 0.35 tall-narrow. The pale blue-white palette is the same one used on Bromeliad in this batch and belongs to neither.
rows.fix: Rebuild from the leaf up: alternate arrowhead/sagittate leaves with two backward-pointing basal lobes on short petioles, mid-green, spaced irregularly on a branching stem. Recolour the stem red-flushed with visible swollen nodes and papery sheaths at each joint. Replace the pod column with loose airy terminal clusters of tiny 5-lobed white-pink florets, plus a few hard brown seeds rendered as sharply three-angled pyramids with visible edge highlights. Widen the whole silhouette to ~0.8 w/h.

rows.readsAs: a sea anemone or an orange feather duster / paintbrush
rows.defect: The single most important mustRead — one round onion-like bulb float at the top of the stalk — is absent. There is no bulb anywhere. Instead the picture is an upright bouquet of ~9 straight strap blades all converging to a sharp point at the BOTTOM, with three small orange lozenge pills floating loose in the middle of the fan, unattached to anything. There is no whip stipe: the blades run the full height themselves, so there is no stalk-below / blades-above structure at all. Colour is salmon-orange to brick red throughout, not dark olive-brown with a lighter glossy bulb. The blades are ruler-straight with rounded capsule ends and uniform width, so they read as plastic strips, and the bottom convergence point sits on a hard ground shadow as if this were a terrestrial plant, not a holdfast in water.
rows.fix: Restructure vertically: a holdfast clump at the base, one long slightly-curved whip stipe of constant slim width rising ~60% of the frame, swelling smoothly into a single glossy round-to-pear bulb, and the blades fanning out only from the top of that bulb, drooping under their own weight with wavy ripple edges and tapering tips. Recolour the whole plant dark olive-brown, with the bulb a lighter glossier tan. Delete the three floating pills. Remove the terrestrial ground shadow ellipse and let the blades trail.

rows.readsAs: a yellow bottlebrush or an acacia flower spike
rows.defect: No buttercup flower exists in the picture. The mustRead five glossy lacquered rounded petals appear only as a tiny 5-6 point star, maybe 20px, jammed on the apex; the body of the image is a tall yellow column of ~10 pairs of pointed lance leaves stacked in an even ladder up a thin stalk, which reads as a yellow bottlebrush or a mimosa spike. Palmate deeply-cut leaves are absent entirely — the leaves are simple entire spearheads, all identical, all the same yellow as the supposed flower so leaf and bloom are indistinguishable. Aspect should be 0.9 (near square, low basal habit) and the render is roughly 0.35 tall-narrow. It is built on the identical stacked-ladder skeleton as Brooklime and Buckwheat in this batch — three species, one shape.
rows.fix: Drop the ladder skeleton. Draw a low basal clump of green palmate leaves each cut into 3-5 deeply toothed segments on hairy stalks, occupying the lower two thirds, then 2-3 thin branching flower stems rising above it. Each terminal flower: five broad overlapping rounded petals forming a shallow cup, saturated golden yellow with a strong tight specular sheen to read as varnish, and a small green-gold stamen boss at the centre. Petal diameter should be roughly a quarter of the frame width, not 5%.

rows.readsAs: a cauliflower, or a green rose with an egg in the middle
rows.defect: The head does not read as a head. It is a flat cluster of ~8 near-circular leaf blobs arranged like rose petals around a pale mint-white SPHERE at the centre; that sphere is a different material and value from everything around it and reads as an egg sitting in a nest, or a pearl, not as the innermost furl of a cabbage. The bold white midribs mustRead is missing — there are only thin pale outline strokes tracing each blob's edge, which read as rim-light, not as thick ribs branching across the blade. Colour is dull olive-brown-green with no blue cast and no waxy bloom. The outer leaves that do point outward are simple pointed darts stuck flat behind the mass with hard straight edges, no wavy margin. Overall silhouette is a lumpy circle rather than a ball with a distinct base.
rows.fix: Replace the central sphere with 3-4 tightly furled inner leaves whose curled edges spiral toward the centre, in the same material and hue family as the rest. Add a thick pale midrib running from each leaf base up the blade with 3-4 branching side veins, drawn under the leaf's own shading so it is not an overlay line. Shift leafColour to blue-green and add a soft desaturated waxy bloom pass on the upper surfaces. Give the outer leaves wavy undulating margins and let them cup and flare, curling outward and downward rather than lying flat.

rows.readsAs: An ornamental pink-leaved twig bouquet — a florist's dried arrangement, not a ground-hugging evergreen
rows.defect: Rendered as a tall UPRIGHT vase-shaped bundle of straight brown sticks fanning out of one trunk — the reference calls for aspect 2.4, a flat TRAILING MAT. Nothing in the picture trails. Leaf colour is hot magenta/violet, not 'dark glossy green'; the leaves are pointed almond shapes, not blunt spoon/paddle leaves. They sit as separate floating ovals beside the twigs with no petiole and no join — you can see clear dark gaps between leaf and stem, so the foliage is stuck on rather than growing out. Two mustReads are entirely absent: no white-pink urn flowers, and the fruit is a few small brown-maroon knobbly clusters at the twig tips, not dull red berries among the leaves. The reddish peeling stem note is the only thing half-present.
rows.fix: Rebuild the skeleton as a prostrate mat: stems near-horizontal, spreading left/right from a low centre, crown height ~40% of width to hit aspect 2.4. Recolour leaves to dark glossy green (winter bronze as accent only) and change the leaf primitive from pointed almond to a short blunt spoon with a rounded tip and a visible thickened edge. Attach each leaf with a short tapering petiole that shares the stem's colour ramp so there is no gap. Move berries to sit AMONG the leaves as individual matte red spheres, not tip clusters, and add small nodding white-pink urn flowers.

rows.readsAs: An agave or a flame-coloured aloe — a spiky desert succulent, not a root vegetable
rows.defect: The single most important mustRead is missing outright: there is NO root. The whole picture is a rosette of salmon-orange spiky blades and nothing else — no round dark red root half out of the soil, no soil line, no tail. Leaf shape is wrong too: sharp pointed lance/spike blades, not broad wavy heart-shaped puckered blades, and they are flat with a plain airbrush gradient rather than puckered. There are no crimson STALKS at all — the blades spring straight from a point, so the crimson-stalk mustRead cannot read either. Colour is uniform orange-salmon; the reference dark-green-flushed-maroon is nowhere. Silhouette is identical to Bitterroot in this same batch minus the flower stem.
rows.fix: Add the root as the dominant mass: a top-shaped deep purple-red bulb occupying the lower ~45% of the frame, its upper third above a soil line, with a slender tapering tail below. Give every leaf a distinct long crimson petiole that visibly emerges from the crown of that root, then a broad rounded heart-shaped blade in near-black green with crimson midrib and side veins. Replace the flat gradient with puckered blistering between veins. Break the shared rosette template so it no longer matches Bitterroot.

rows.readsAs: A generic purple frond or a decorative fern stalk — no berry, no bell, no nightshade
rows.defect: A single dead-straight grey stick with seven perfectly regular, perfectly symmetrical OPPOSITE pairs of identical violet leaves — a machined ladder. The reference asks for a coarse BRANCHING herb with alternate, unequal leaf pairs (one large, one small); the render has no branching at all and every pair is a mirrored clone. Both remaining mustReads are absent: no dull purple-brown drooping bell flowers anywhere, and no glossy black berry in a flared green star — the only fruit is three tiny grey pinhead dots at the apex, unreadable at any size. Leaf colour is bright lilac-violet, not dull dark green. Each leaf meets the stem at a hard V-notch with no petiole. Aspect is a narrow vertical spike, not the 0.8 bushy herb.
rows.fix: Branch the stem at two or three points so the plant is broader than tall. Randomise the phyllotaxy to alternate, and make each node carry one large and one small blade with different lengths. Recolour to dull dark green. Hang two or three drooping tubular bell flowers in purple-brown from short curved pedicels in the leaf axils, and give at least one large glossy black berry seated in a five-point green star calyx at readable scale (10-14% of frame width). Add petioles that blend into the stem.

rows.readsAs: A wheat or golden fern stalk with a small pink daisy stuck on the tip
rows.defect: Same machined ladder skeleton as Belladonna and Black-Eyed Susan in this batch — one straight stick, eight identical opposite leaf pairs — recoloured gold/amber. The headline mustRead fails completely: instead of a ragged firework head of narrow tubular flowers on a domed head, there is one tiny tidy pink DAISY with a smooth round disc, about 8% of the frame. It is a rayed composite, exactly the wrong flower family. No leafy bracts under the head. The square stem does not read — the stem is a thin uniform round line with no facets or ridges. Leaves are gold, not grey-green, and are smooth pointed blades rather than toothed lance leaves. Aspect 0.6 asks for a fairly broad plant; this is a narrow vertical wand.
rows.fix: Replace the daisy with a domed receptacle carrying 30+ long slender curved TUBES radiating outward and upward in lavender, unequal lengths, deliberately ragged in outline, at 3-4x the current head size. Ring the base of the head with a whorl of narrow leafy bracts. Give the stem two visible parallel edge highlights so the square section reads. Branch the stem and add a second flower head to break the wand silhouette, recolour foliage to grey-green, and saw fine teeth into the leaf margins.

rows.readsAs: A frosted or silvered ornamental sprig with elderberry-style fruit clusters — closest to a blueberry, which is the one thing it must not be
rows.defect: Upright tall vase of green stems — the same skeleton as Bearberry recoloured — where the reference asks for a low dense MOUND at aspect 1. It is roughly twice as tall as wide. The note's own distinguishing feature is contradicted: the berries are in tight CLUSTERS of five to seven at the stem tips, which is exactly the blueberry trait the row says to avoid; nothing is borne singly in a leaf axil. Leaf colour is pale silvery white-blue, not bright fresh green, so the plant reads as frosted or dead. No pink-green globe flowers. Stems are smooth round lines with no angular ridging. Leaves float beside the stems with visible dark gaps, no petioles.
rows.fix: Compress the silhouette to a wide low mound (width >= height), with many short twigs rather than a few long ones. Recolour foliage to bright fresh green. Break every berry cluster apart: place single blue-black berries with a dusty pale bloom individually where a leaf meets a twig, one per axil. Give the twigs a flat-sided ridged profile with a highlight down each angle so they read as green and angular. Add a few small nodding pink-green globe flowers, and join the leaves to the twigs with short petioles.

rows.readsAs: A child's lollipop tree, or a walnut/cocoa tree — brown fruit balls on an orange post
rows.defect: Every mustRead fails. The trunk is a rusty terracotta-orange CAPSULE — a rounded rectangle with the same width top to bottom, rounded ends, no taper, no root flare, no branch junctions — a machined primitive, and the crown simply overlaps it with a hard boundary rather than growing from it. There is no white bark and no black diamond scars anywhere. The crown is not narrow or airy: it is a broad opaque brown blob built from about twenty-five near-identical spheres, each with a hard drawn crease arc, packed edge to edge; behind them is a diffuse tan glow that reads as fog. No fine drooping twigs, no triangular leaves at all. The white bead-chains hanging in the crown are the only vertical detail and read as caterpillars.
rows.fix: Rewrite the trunk: slender, tapering, with a root flare at the base and two or three branch forks visible, painted chalk-white with grey-black horizontal lenticel dashes and black diamond scars under the branch collars, plus curling peel flaps at the edges. Rebuild the crown from many fine drooping twig lines rather than blobs, keeping the crown narrower than tall and letting background show through so it reads airy. Replace the sphere clusters with small triangular toothed leaves in light fresh green. Delete the tan glow. If sap is to be shown, put a single tap and a clear bead run on the trunk.

rows.readsAs: A flowering agave or aloe — a spiky rosette with a flower spike, which is the opposite of the stemless ground-hugging bloom intended
rows.defect: Directly contradicts its own mustReads. 'No visible stem' and 'flower sitting FLAT on bare ground' — the render puts a single tall bare stem up through the whole upper half of the frame with the flower perched at the very top, further from the ground than anything else in the picture. The flower is also small (about 10% of frame) where the row calls for a LARGE many-petalled bloom, and it is a tidy even-rayed disc daisy rather than a many-petalled star. The rosette leaves are flat sharp orange-salmon blades, not short fleshy grey-green cylinders, and none of them is shrivelling. No gravel or ground texture. The rosette is pixel-for-pixel the same construction as Beet in this batch.
rows.fix: Delete the stem entirely and seat the flower directly on the ground at the rosette centre, scaled up to 35-40% of the frame width, built from 12-15 narrow overlapping pink petals in two offset rings around a small pale centre. Replace the flat blades with short fat grey-green cylinders that taper to a blunt tip and have visible thickness, several of them browning and curling to read as withering. Add a scatter of gravel pebbles at the base. Differentiate the rosette geometry from Beet's.

rows.readsAs: A generic yellow daisy on a fern-like stalk — a coreopsis or sunflower sprig rather than a black-eyed susan, since it has no black eye
rows.defect: The nearest miss in the batch, but the defining mustRead is absent: the centre is a small AMBER-GOLD flat button barely distinguishable from the rays, not a deep chocolate-brown raised DOME. Without that contrast it is just a yellow daisy. The rays are short, stiff and evenly radiating like gear teeth with no droop. Nothing is bristly or hairy — the stem is a smooth thin line and the leaf surfaces are clean airbrush gradients with hard edges. The leaves are in perfectly regular opposite pairs, but the row specifies alternate on a rough stem, and it is the identical seven-tier ladder used by Belladonna and Bergamot in this batch, only recoloured green. Leaves join the stem at a bare V-notch with no petiole.
rows.fix: Make the centre a dark chocolate-brown hemisphere with visible shading top-lit and a stippled floret texture, sized to about a third of the head diameter so it dominates. Lengthen the rays, vary their lengths, and angle them downward from the disc so they droop. Add short bristle strokes along the stem silhouette and the leaf margins and a rough matte leaf surface. Switch the phyllotaxy to alternate with irregular spacing, add petioles, and branch the stem so it stops matching Belladonna and Bergamot.

rows.readsAs: a lollipop cartoon tree with sunflowers glued to it
rows.defect: The trunk is a literal capsule — a uniform-width green rounded rectangle with a domed bottom that floats above a black ellipse shadow and never tapers or branches. The crown is a soft round dark-green cloud blob, not a flat-topped umbrella; leaf sprigs are pasted radiating outward from the blob's outline like spokes on a pincushion, each one a flat 2D ferny stamp with a hard edge where it meets the cloud, and none of them grow out of any visible limb. The five yellow flowers are 8-petal daisies with pale centres — sunflower stamps, not acacia puffballs. Zero of the three mustReads are present: no flat top, no paired white thorns at nodes, no horizontal layering. No seed pods either.
rows.fix: Kill the capsule: tapering trunk that forks into 3-4 ascending limbs, bark texture, base flaring into the ground rather than hovering over an ellipse. Crown becomes a wide flat-topped shape — several overlapping horizontal plate-layers with a straight/slightly convex top edge and a wider-than-tall footprint. Sprigs must be attached to and emerge from the visible limbs inside the crown, not radiate from its silhouette. Replace the daisy stamps with small cream spheres of radiating filaments (puffballs), and hang a few curled brown pods. Add paired white thorns at the sprig nodes.

rows.readsAs: a dead twig, or a single wheat/bamboo shoot
rows.defect: This is not a palm and barely a plant. The whole image is one thin brown leaning stick with three small golden-amber pointed leaves stuck alternately along it, over a black ellipse. Nothing about the reference row survives: no clump of stems, no ringed grey trunks, no stilt roots, no feather crown, no drooping berry brooms, and no green anywhere. Aspect is also wrong — it renders as a single tall stick, not a palm silhouette. The leaves meet the stick at a hard seam with no petiole or sheath.
rows.fix: Full rebuild against the palm form. Draw 3-5 slender stems of differing heights rising from a shared base, thin and grey with faint horizontal ring scars and stilt roots splaying at the bottom. Top each with a small crown of long arching pinnate fronds whose leaflets droop, and hang broom-like sprays of many small near-black-purple berries on a pale rachis below the leaf crown.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon fruit tree with chestnuts
rows.defect: Same capsule trunk as Acacia — a flat green rounded-rectangle with a domed bottom hovering over a shadow ellipse, no taper, no ridged bark, no crooked limbs at all. The crown is a round green cloud roughly as tall as it is wide, not a broad heavy crown wider than tall. The leaves are deeply cut spiky star/maple shapes with sharp points, the opposite of oak's rounded lobes and shallow bays, and they sit on the cloud's rim as flat stamps. The four 'acorns' are perfect brown circles with a single specular dot — spheres, not ovoid nuts, and with no scaly cup whatsoever. Reads as the same tree as the Acacia entry in this batch with a different leaf stamp and different fruit dots.
rows.fix: Crown must go visibly wider than tall and sit on 3-4 massive crooked forking limbs that are drawn, not implied. Retexture the trunk with deep vertical ridges and taper it into a buttressed base. Redraw the leaf as an oak leaf: rounded lobes with shallow rounded bays, no sharp points. Redraw the fruit as an ovoid nut sitting in a textured scaly cup on a short twig, in pairs, and drop the specular circle highlight.

rows.readsAs: a dried palm frond or a golden agave — indistinguishable from the Agave, Air Plant and Aloe images in this batch
rows.defect: A perfectly mirror-symmetric fan of straight-sided amber triangles radiating from one point — machined geometry, both halves identical. These are spikes, not broad lance-shaped parallel-veined blades; each has a single straight central crease instead of veining. Colour is gold/orange, nothing like bright mid green. No sheathed pseudostem, no knobbly rhizome, and the mustRead mauve-pink ground-level flower is absent — instead a ruler-straight vertical stalk rises from the centre topped by a tiny yellow bead spike. This is the identical shape used for Agave, Air Plant and Aloe in this same batch, recoloured.
rows.fix: Stop sharing the rosette primitive. Build a leaf shoot: overlapping tubular leaf sheaths forming a pseudostem, with broad lance blades fanning off it, each blade showing multiple parallel veins running tip to base and a slight independent twist so the two halves are not mirror copies. Recolour to bright mid green. Remove the tall bead stalk; place a mauve-pink flower low at ground level beside the shoot, and expose a pale knobbly rhizome with a cone tuft of roots at the base.

rows.readsAs: a green paper fan or a palmetto leaf
rows.defect: Pixel-for-pixel the same fan as African Ginger, recoloured emerald green, with the same ruler-straight stalk and the same tiny yellow bead spike on top. The blades are flat 2D triangles with a straight centre crease and zero thickness — nothing about them reads as a rigid succulent sword. All three mustReads fail: no black terminal spine at any tip, no teeth anywhere along the edges, no bud-imprint lines on the faces. Colour is bright green, not blue-grey. Perfect bilateral symmetry.
rows.fix: Give the leaves volume — a lit upper face and a shaded under-curve so each sword has thickness, with a slight outward arch and varying lengths so the rosette is not mirrored. Recolour to dusty blue-grey green. Add the hard black terminal spine on every tip and a row of small hooked teeth down both margins. Score faint pale bud-imprint lines across the faces. Either remove the thin bead stalk entirely or replace it with a genuinely massive branching panicle.

rows.readsAs: a small dried yucca or a spiky sunburst ornament
rows.defect: Third recolour of the same symmetric triangle fan (tan/orange, slightly narrower spikes), with the same central stalk carrying a purple bead spike. Every mustRead fails: the leaves are straight rigid spikes rather than narrow curling recurved ones, there is no silvery frosted furring — the surface is a smooth flat gradient — and there is no flat pink bract paddle or tubular violet flower. Worst, it sits on the same ground shadow ellipse as every other plant here, which directly contradicts 'no soil and no real roots'; nothing indicates an epiphyte.
rows.fix: Break it off the shared rosette shape. Draw narrow leaves that taper to a whisker and curl and recurve in different directions so the rosette is loose and spidery, none mirrored. Give the surface a fine pale stippled fuzz so it reads silvery and frosted rather than glossy. Remove the ground shadow and perch the plant on a bark fragment or a wire loop with its base gripping it. Replace the bead spike with a flat pink paddle-shaped bract with two or three tubular violet flowers pushing out from between its scales.

rows.readsAs: a fern frond, or a fossil imprint of one
rows.defect: A single vertical stem with about eleven machine-regular horizontal pairs of pale ice-blue ovals stepping evenly up it — the regularity is mechanical, every pair the same size and spacing. That is a pinnate frond, not alfalfa: the mustRead trifoliate clover-like leaf of three narrow leaflets is completely absent, as are the corkscrew-coiled pods. Colour is near-white silver-blue rather than grey-mid-green, so it reads frozen or fossilised. The only nod to the row is a small purple bead spike at the tip — the same bead primitive used on the Air Plant.
rows.fix: Rebuild the leaf architecture: several slender branching stems, each carrying trifoliate leaves — three narrow oval leaflets, the centre one on a short stalk, with a few teeth at the leaflet tip. Randomise leaf angle and spacing to kill the ladder regularity. Recolour to a slightly grey mid green. Replace the bead spike with short dense racemes of small violet pea flowers (banner and keel readable), and add two or three tight corkscrew-coiled brown pods.

rows.readsAs: a white paper fan or an origami flower
rows.defect: Fourth recolour of the identical mirrored triangle fan, this time in flat bone-white/ivory — a colour no aloe has. The blades are thin flat wedges with a straight crease and no fleshy volume, no toothed margins, no flecking and no red edge tinting, so the whole rosette reads as paper rather than succulent. The blades splay outward and downward instead of curving upward. The one thing that works is the tall bare stalk rising well above the leaves, but its flowers are a short column of round orange beads rather than packed tubular downward-hanging blooms.
rows.fix: Recolour to grey-green with pale flecks and reddish leaf margins. Rebuild each blade as a thick triangular succulent — lit top face, shaded rounded underside, tapering to a soft point — curving upward from the centre rather than flopping flat, with small pale teeth along both edges and varied lengths so the rosette stops being mirror-symmetric. Turn the bead column into a raceme of elongated tubular orange-red flowers hanging point-down, densest at the top of the spike.

rows.readsAs: a white-flowered alien vine or a string of edelweiss blooms
rows.defect: This is not a grapevine. The picture is an S-curved green stem carrying seven white star/daisy rosettes — spiky white petal whorls with grey shading — plus one small dark-purple stippled lump the size of a thumbnail sitting where the stem bends. Zero of the three mustReads land: there are no palmate 3-5 lobed toothed leaves (the 'leaves' are white flower-like starbursts), the single berry lump is stuck against the stem edge rather than hanging as a tight conical bunch below the foliage, and it has no chalky bloom — it is a matt maroon speckled blob. The only tendril evidence is a handful of tiny grey-blue hoop rings floating beside the stem that are not connected to anything and read as artifacts. Every rosette is the same stamped shape rotated, and each meets the stem at a hard point-contact with no petiole, so the parts sit ON the stem instead of growing OUT of it.
rows.fix: Rebuild the leaf primitive as a broad palmate blade: five pointed lobes radiating from a basal notch, coarse saw-teeth on the margin, a visible petiole 20-30% of blade length attaching with a shaded junction swelling. Recolour foliage deep green with a paler underside on back-facing blades, not white. Replace the stray hoop rings with actual tendrils: a thin stem-coloured line leaving the node OPPOSITE each leaf, running straight for ~30px then forking into two helical coils. Promote the fruit from one lump to a pendulous conical bunch hung below the lowest leaves — 30+ overlapping spheres tapering to a point, blue-black base colour with a low-opacity pale grey bloom pass over the upper-left of each sphere and a specular dot punched through the bloom.

rows.readsAs: a string of pink water balloons or a cartoon crab-apple branch
rows.defect: Eight identical salmon-pink spheres with a hard vertical highlight seam down each are strung in pairs along a brown S-curve stalk, with one small grey-white stippled clump near the top. Nothing here is Piper nigrum. No heart-shaped leaves exist at all — the 'foliage' is balloons, so the ribbed cordate blade mustRead is entirely absent. There is no support to cling to and no root pads, so the climber mustRead is absent. The pepper spike is one static grey clump wedged into a stem fork, not a drooping catkin-like string of berries. The spheres are perfect geometric circles with a mirrored gradient, and each touches the stem at a single tangent point — a textbook stuck-on part with a visible seam and no attachment tissue. Colour is wrong end to end: salmon pink where the reference calls for dark glossy green.
rows.fix: Delete the sphere primitive from this species entirely. Draw cordate leaves: a broad blade with a notched heart base clasping the petiole, 5-7 curved parallel veins arcing from base to tip, dark green with a glossy sheen band, alternate along the stem. Add a vertical rough-barked support column behind the vine and attach the stem to it with short bristly adventitious rootlet pads every 40-50px. Replace the grey clump with 2-3 slim pendulous spikes 100px+ long hanging clear of the stem, each strung with 20-30 small round peppercorns graded green at the tip to red at the base.

rows.readsAs: a clump of electric-blue alien reed or a neon sea-fan
rows.defect: An upright fan of teal-green stems rising from a single cone-shaped base, hung with roughly forty electric-blue zigzag chevrons, topped by five grey-brown bobbled heads. The blue is a saturated cyan-blue that appears nowhere on a bramble. Leaves fail completely — a chevron/lightning-bolt zigzag is not a palmate leaf of 3-5 toothed leaflets, and they are all one stamped shape at three sizes. The form is wrong: this is a stiff vertical bouquet, not long arching canes that root where they touch down, so that mustRead is absent. There are no hooked prickles anywhere on the stems. The berry heads are grey-brown, not glossy black, and there is no red unripe fruit alongside, so the mixed-ripeness mustRead fails too. The stems all converge into a smooth machined cone at the base with a hard seam where the fan meets it.
rows.fix: Change the whole armature to arching canes: 3-4 stems that leave the base, bow over past the horizontal and dip back toward the ground, with a rooting tip touching down. Recolour stems reddish-green and stipple hooked prickles — small backward-curved triangles — along their length at 15-20px spacing. Replace the chevron primitive with a compound leaf: a rachis bearing three to five separate ovate leaflets, coarsely toothed, dark green above with a grey-green wash on tilted undersides. Rebuild the fruit as drupelet clusters — 12-20 small glossy spheres bunched into each berry with individual specular dots — and paint a mix: black ripe, red half-ripe, pale green unripe in the same cluster. Dissolve the cone base into individual stems entering the soil.

rows.readsAs: a red tulip bud or a stylised rocket fin
rows.defect: A single closed crimson-red teardrop bud, wider at the top and tapering to a sharp point at the ground, striped with vertical dark red lines, with three pale pink lozenges spaced down its centre and two short rounded red horns at the crown. Not one mustRead survives. There is no Y-forking of straps whatsoever — the whole organism is one unbranched closed volume. There are no paired round bladders either side of a midrib; the three pink lozenges are single, centred, and read as painted-on pills rather than gas-filled swellings inside tissue. There are no swollen warty fertile tips — the top is two smooth rounded nubs. Colour is catastrophically wrong: brilliant scarlet where the reference specifies olive-green to yellow-brown. The silhouette is a perfect smooth teardrop with machined edges and mirror symmetry, and it stands upright on a drop shadow as if it were a terrestrial bud, with no holdfast and no sense of water.
rows.fix: Discard the teardrop primitive. Build the frond procedurally: a small knobbly holdfast at the base, then a flat leathery strap that dichotomously forks into two equal straps, repeated 4-5 times, each generation slightly shorter, splaying into a fan. Give every strap a raised centre midrib with a lighter highlight ridge, and place bladders in symmetrical PAIRS straddling that midrib — bulges that push the strap outline outward so the silhouette swells at each pair, not discs drawn on a flat surface. Recolour to olive-brown with yellow-green tips and darker near-black patches. Terminate the outermost forks in inflated, pimpled, warty receptacles noticeably fatter than the strap. Curve the whole fan as if buoyed by water.

rows.readsAs: a generic green ornamental shrub with purple flowers; a boxwood or a pot plant rather than a blueberry
rows.defect: The most readable image in the batch, but mechanical. A fat glossy green trunk-cone splits into six stems, each carrying identical pointed oval leaves in a perfectly regular alternating herringbone — the same stamped leaf repeated about sixty times at one size and two mirror rotations, which makes the foliage read as machine-tiled rather than grown. Two mustReads are missing outright: there are no white urn-shaped bell flowers anywhere, and the seven blue fruits are flat purple pom-pom rosettes with radiating petal lobes, showing no five-point crown scar and not reading as berries at all. The bush is not dense and twiggy — the stems are wide, smooth, plastic-looking and all identical in width, and each meets the central trunk at a hard-edged seam. Berries appear only in the top 20% of the crown, which leaves the lower two thirds an empty leaf mat.
rows.fix: Break the herringbone: randomise leaf size ±35%, angle ±25 degrees, and skip nodes so gaps appear. Thin the stems to fine twigs, taper them along their length, and tint them green-to-red as the reference specifies. Add a fillet/shading swell where each twig leaves the trunk so it grows out rather than being welded on. Redraw the fruit as individual spheres, powder-blue with a matt bloom, and punch a small dark five-point star scar into the top of each; scatter clusters throughout the bush, not only at the apex. Add drooping white urn-shaped bells — narrow-mouthed pitcher outlines nodding downward — in small clusters near the shoot tips.

rows.readsAs: a red-leaved ornamental grass or dwarf autumn bamboo
rows.defect: Structurally the closest hit in the batch — stiff upright brown twigs fanning from a base, with pale yellow-green cylindrical catkins standing at several tip positions. But the leaves are wrong in shape and colour: they are sharp lance-shaped orange-red spikes, pointed at both ends, arranged as regular opposite pairs like bamboo or a red ornamental grass. The mustRead calls for small BLUNT-tipped grey-green leaves broadest near the tip with a few teeth only at the end; nothing here is blunt, nothing is grey-green, nothing is toothed, and the leaves are opposite rather than alternate. The catkins are also the wrong colour — pale yellow-green instead of brown-orange — and they coexist with a full flush of leaves, whereas the mustRead specifies stubby catkins on LEAFLESS stems. Every leaf is the same stamped spike, and each meets its twig at a single point with no petiole or junction shading.
rows.fix: Reshape the leaf to a spatulate blade: narrow at the base, widest about 70% along, blunt rounded tip, with two or three small teeth only on the outer third. Recolour grey-green with a dusty desaturated wash and speckle small amber resin dots across the surface. Switch the arrangement from opposite pairs to alternate, with variable spacing. Recolour catkins to a stubby brown-orange cylinder, shorter and fatter, and either strip leaves from the catkin-bearing twigs to sell the spring state or drop the catkins to a few and keep them at the very tips. Add a small swelling at each leaf base where it joins the twig.

rows.readsAs: a bundle of dead willow twigs with pussy-willow buds
rows.defect: The plant has NO LEAVES. The image is a bundle of bare straw-tan sticks crossing each other in a lattice, rising from a smooth tan cone at the base, with about nine small pale-pink capsule blobs perched on the stick tips. The single most important mustRead — narrow inrolled leathery leaves flashing chalky white undersides — is entirely absent, and with it the dark blue-green colour that gives this species its name. The flowers fail too: they are upright flat-topped pink pills, not nodding urn-shaped bells, and they sit ON the tip of each stick like a bead on a skewer rather than dangling from a curved pedicel. Nothing indicates a bog — no moss, no wet ground, just a drop shadow. The stems are uniform-width straight tan lines that cross without any junction, so the whole thing reads as an assembled wire frame rather than a grown bush, and the base cone is a machined shape with a hard seam.
rows.fix: Add the foliage first: narrow strap leaves 3-4x longer than wide, edges visibly rolled under so the outline is a tight cylinder-like blade, dark blue-green on the upper face, and on every downward-tilted or reversed leaf paint the chalky white underside so the bush flickers white. Recolour stems from straw-tan to thin dark reddish wiry lines and taper them. Rebuild flowers as nodding urn bells: a curved pedicel arcing over so the flower hangs mouth-down, body pinched near the mouth, soft pink with a darker throat, in clusters of 3-5 at shoot tips. Replace the base cone with individual stems entering a mossy hummock.

rows.readsAs: a lollipop tree or a cartoon olive tree on a broom handle
rows.defect: A perfectly straight tan dowel of constant width, with a rounded pill-cap bottom that floats above the drop shadow, supporting a soft airbrushed yellow-green ball of foliage with three brown spheres. The trunk is a machined capsule primitive: no taper from base to crown, no buttress or root flare, no bark texture, and its rounded lower end is exactly the same rounded end as its top, so the tree does not enter the ground so much as rest on it. The mustRead 'flat crown of branches only at the very top' is unmet — there are no branches at all; the dowel simply continues up into the leaf ball and the leaves are pinned around the outside of a glowing blurred sphere with a hard-edged pointed-oval leaf shape repeated about thirty times. The crown is a globe, not the flat spreading emergent crown the reference and note demand. The nut pods are plain brown balls with a highlight dot, showing no woody rind texture and no hole at one end, and they hang against the leaf blob with no visible stalk.
rows.fix: Taper the trunk: wide flared base swelling into the ground, narrowing steadily to the crown, with vertical bark striation and a slightly irregular outline. Push the aspect further — the bole should be 70-75% of the image height for an emergent giant. At the top, split into 4-6 real branches that spread outward and slightly upward, and hang leaf tufts at the branch ENDS only so the crown reads flat and umbrella-like instead of spherical. Kill the airbrushed glow blob behind the leaves and let the crown silhouette be made of leaf clusters with sky gaps between them. Redraw pods as heavy woody spheres with a rough pitted rind, a darker circular operculum hole on the underside, on a short thick stalk that visibly attaches to a branch.

rows.readsAs: A generic cartoon orange tree — a green lollipop with four oranges. Nobody would say cashew.
rows.defect: A textbook lollipop tree: a flat mid-green capsule (rounded top AND rounded bottom, uniform width, machined vertical sides) plugged into a soft-edged elliptical green blur-cloud. Not one mustRead is present — no low wide spreading crown (the crown is a tall vertical egg, taller than wide), no pear-shaped fleshy false fruit, and no grey kidney nut anywhere in the image. The 'harvest' is four identical perfect orange-yellow spheres with a specular dot, indistinguishable from oranges or apricots. The trunk is GREEN, not woody, and its rounded bottom cap floats clear of the cast shadow so the tree does not meet the ground. The trunk/crown junction is a hard vertical edge sliding behind a blur — no branching, no taper, no seam-free growth. Leaf slivers are scattered inside and outside the blur with no twig connecting any of them.
rows.fix: Rebuild the harvest as a two-part organ: a pear/bell-shaped swollen false fruit shading red at the top to yellow at the bottom, with a separate curved grey-brown kidney nut hanging from the fruit's LOWER end on a short stub — the nut outside and below, per the reference note. Recolour the trunk to grey-brown fissured bark, taper it, and split it into 3-4 low ascending scaffold limbs that fan into the crown so there is no trunk/crown line. Squash the crown to ~1.6:1 wide-to-tall and flatten its top for the spreading habit. Replace the blur-cloud with clustered leaf masses of blunt-tipped leathery ovals showing parallel veins, some flushed reddish at the shoot tips. Extend the trunk base below the shadow ellipse.

rows.readsAs: A bunch of cut white lavender or hyacinth stems in a vase. Definitely not a root crop.
rows.defect: The whole plant is pale lilac-white, not green — it reads as a bouquet of small white flowers, not foliage. The palmate leaves have collapsed into tiny 5-7 pointed white starbursts about 25px across scattered on olive stalks; at this size each one reads as a bloom, and there is no leaf blade, no long narrow finger-lobes, no petiole colour distinction. Zero of the three mustReads survive: the hand-shaped leaf of narrow pointed fingers is illegible, the red petioles are absent (stalks are dull olive-green), and the fat tapering tubers radiating from the base are completely missing — the base is a plain green tapered wedge sitting on a shadow ellipse. The stem bundle is a flat triangular cone with straight machined sides and no knobbly leaf-scar cane texture.
rows.fix: Recolour blades to mid/dark green and enlarge them 2.5-3x so the seven narrow lance-shaped lobes read individually with a visible midrib each. Recolour every petiole and the young stem tops to strong red-pink so the classic cassava red-stalk signal dominates. Add the harvest: 4-6 fat brown-skinned tapering tubers splaying out from the stem base at ground level, partly exposed in soil. Replace the triangular cone base with knobbly cane-like stems carrying raised leaf scars.

rows.readsAs: A red Japanese maple sprig, or a poinsettia bouquet — and at a glance it is the same picture as Cassava in this same batch.
rows.defect: Structurally this is the SAME render as Cassava in this batch — identical bouquet skeleton, identical starburst leaf tokens at identical scale, identical tapering triangular base cone — only the hue changed to salmon-red. That duplication alone is disqualifying. On its own terms: the mustRead 'upright spikes of bristly red seed capsules above the leaves' is entirely absent (the only things above the leaves are three bare olive stick-ends), so the harvest does not exist. The leaves are far too small for 'very large palmate' and are not peltate — every stalk attaches at the lobe notch, not at the blade centre. The stems are opaque brown-olive, not hollow red-tinged. The base is a flat brown triangle with two perfectly straight machined edges meeting the shadow at a hard line.
rows.fix: Differentiate the skeleton from Cassava outright: castor is one or two thick hollow stems, not a fan of many. Scale the leaves up 3-4x to dominate the silhouette, hold each blade peltate (stalk meeting the underside at the blade's centre, visible radiating veins) and put teeth on the 7-11 lobe margins. Add the harvest as a dense upright terminal raceme of soft crimson spiny capsules standing clear ABOVE the foliage. Keep a bronze-red flush but push blades toward deep green so the red stems and red capsules read as accents rather than the whole plant.

rows.readsAs: Ornamental pampas or fountain grass. The brown spike is too slight to be recognised as a cattail head.
rows.defect: Reads as a silver fountain grass, not a cattail. The blades are pale white-blue and arch outward and DOWN in a symmetric fountain, where cattail strap leaves stand near-vertical from the waterline. The signature organ has failed: the brown spike is a thin (~8px) knobbly stick barely longer than a leaf, not a dense velvety cigar — it has no girth, no volume, and the thin male-flower spike above it is not distinguishable from the female sausage, so two of three mustReads are illegible. Worse, there are roughly a dozen small white horizontal DASHES floating free in the middle of the plant, unattached to any blade or stem — off-body artifacts. There is no waterline at all; the plant sits on a dry drop-shadow ellipse.
rows.fix: Thicken the spike to a genuine cigar (roughly 8-10x its own width, ~60-70px tall, ~18px wide) with dark chocolate velvet shading, and put a distinctly thinner paler male spike directly on top of it with a small gap. Recolour the foliage to mid/grey-green. Steepen the blades to mostly vertical with only the tips flopping, and reduce the number so the crown is not a symmetric spray. Delete the floating white dashes or attach them to blades. Add a waterline: cut the bases off at a horizontal water plane with a reflection instead of a dry shadow.

rows.readsAs: A red-orange sea creature — a feather-duster worm or a soft coral fan. In a plant context, a tropical ornamental, never a cave fern.
rows.defect: The frond architecture is genuinely the best in this batch — pinnate fronds arching from a single crown, one small fiddlehead curl at the base — but the colour is completely wrong: the whole plant is bright salmon-orange. The mustRead calls for 'thin soft shade-green pinnae, thin enough to look translucent'; this is opaque, saturated and warm, which is the exact opposite read. The second mustRead, 'arching fronds spilling from a rock crevice', is also missing — there is no rock, no crevice, no substrate at all, just a drop shadow. Craft-wise the pinnae are hard-edged isoceles triangles of uniform size repeated along each rachis, giving a sawblade/comb edge rather than soft foliage, and the aspect is landscape (~1.5 wide) where the reference asks for 1.1 tall.
rows.fix: Recolour to deep shade-green with reduced opacity at the pinna tips so light reads through them; keep some warm brown only in the stipes. Replace the triangular sawteeth with soft-shouldered pinnae that vary in length along the rachis and shorten toward the frond tip. Add the rock: a dark crevice wedge behind and beneath the crown with the rhizome gripping it, fronds spilling out and down over the lip. Rotate the composition to portrait ~1.1 and add faint rows of brown sori dots on the visible underside of one or two upcurled pinnae.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon broadleaf lollipop tree with pine needles glued on and four brown screws stuck in the leaves.
rows.defect: Same lollipop skeleton as Cashew and Cherry in this batch: a flat green capsule trunk with rounded top and bottom, plugged into a soft green blur-cloud. That is a broadleaf silhouette, and it contradicts all three mustReads at once — the crown is a tall round egg rather than a broad flat-topped crown, there are no tiered horizontal branch plates (no branches at all are visible), and the needles are single straight green sticks radiating individually, not tight rosette clusters on spur shoots. The needles clearly overshoot the crown blur, sticking out into empty background with no twig behind them. The cones are four small brown ribbed screw/bolt shapes that read as machine hardware, and only two of them stand upright; the others lean and one hangs. The trunk is bright green rather than grey fissured cedar bark, and its rounded lower cap floats above the shadow ellipse.
rows.fix: Discard the lollipop. Build a bare, thick, taper grey-brown trunk that divides into strong horizontal limbs, and hang flat cushion-shaped foliage plates along the tops of those limbs with sky gaps between the tiers — the tiered-plate silhouette IS the cedar read. Replace the individual needle sticks with small radial rosette tufts clustered on short spurs along the limb tops. Redraw the cones as smooth barrel/egg forms with a flat resinous top, seated upright directly on the upper surface of the foliage plates. Recolour foliage to dark blue-green with silvery grey-green highlights. Extend the trunk into the ground.

rows.readsAs: A teal aquarium fern or a stylised wheat sprig with a single daisy stuck on the tip.
rows.defect: Machine-stamped, not grown. A single dead-straight vertical stem carries eleven leaf pairs at exactly equal vertical spacing, each pair mirror-identical, each made of the same repeated leaflet token — the repetition is visible as a grid and the two sides of the plant are perfect reflections. The colour is bright cyan-turquoise, not the bright light green called for, which pushes it into aquarium-plant territory. The mustReads fail: the foliage is rows of fat rounded leaflets, not wispy thread-fine segments; and there is exactly ONE flower, a small flat white disc with a flat pale-yellow centre, so 'hollow domed yellow centre taller than it is wide' and 'white rays folding back and down' are both absent — the rays are stubby, in-plane, and radially perfect like a clip-art asterisk. Chamomile is a branching many-headed herb; this is one unbranched spike.
rows.fix: Break the symmetry and the grid: randomise leaf spacing, angle and length, and let the stem bend. Split the plant into several branching stems each ending in its own flower head — a chamomile plant should carry 5-15 heads at different heights and angles. Recolour foliage to bright yellow-green and thin the leaflets down to hair-fine thread segments so the mass reads feathery and see-through. Rebuild the flower head in three dimensions: a tall domed yellow cone standing proud of the ray plane, with white rays reflexed backward and downward past horizontal, and vary the head tilts.

rows.readsAs: A dead grey tree hung with four red apples — reads closer to a winter/ashen tree than to a cherry, and shares its exact skeleton with Cashew and Cedar in this same batch.
rows.defect: Third instance of the batch's lollipop skeleton — capsule trunk with rounded ends into an elliptical blur-cloud. The crown is desaturated grey-brown and the leaf slivers are pale grey-white, so the whole tree reads as dead or ash-covered; nothing here is 'mid-green'. All three mustReads are missing: the bark is a flat maroon capsule with no horizontal lenticel banding and no gloss; there is no blossom of any kind; and the fruit are four isolated perfect crimson spheres with a single specular dot, sitting singly and unattached inside the crown — no pairs, no long slender stalks, nothing dangling. The trunk's rounded bottom cap floats above the cast shadow, and the leaf slivers spray past the crown boundary into bare background with no twigs behind them.
rows.fix: Recolour the crown to mid-green foliage with visible saw-toothed oval leaves. Give the bark its signature: glossy red-brown with horizontal rows of pale lenticel dashes wrapping the trunk, and branch it into ascending limbs so the crown grows out of it. Rebuild the harvest as pairs of glossy near-black-red cherries hanging from a common point on long thin visible pedicels, clearly below the twig they hang from. Add clusters of five-petalled white-pink blossom on long stalks. Sink the trunk base into the ground plane.

rows.readsAs: A young palm frond or a fern pinna — a leaf, not a flowering herb
rows.defect: The plant is a single, almost perfectly bilateral frond: ~11 pairs of teal-cyan lance blades set in EXACTLY OPPOSITE pairs, evenly spaced and smoothly graded in length, on a bare straight stem. The reference wants alternate, crowded mid-green leaves — these are opposite, evenly spread, and the colour is teal/turquoise, not green. The 'pyramid plume arching to one side' is a straight vertical chain of about a dozen tiny yellow beads at the very tip, maybe 8% of the plant's height, dead centre and not arching at all; it reads as a bud spike, not a plume. Every blade is the same lens shape flipped and scaled, and each meets the stem with a hard dark point rather than tapering out of it.
rows.fix: Recolour blades from teal to mid green (#5f8a3e range). Offset the leaf pairs into a true alternate arrangement with irregular spacing and crowding toward the base. Replace the bead-chain with a proper panicle: a triangular/pyramidal mass 30-40% of plant height, built of many small radiating flower heads on short side-branchlets, the whole mass tipped and curved to ONE side so it arches.

rows.readsAs: A Japanese maple bonsai or a coral-leaved ornamental acer
rows.defect: Every leaf is bright coral orange-red, not mid green, and the lobes are long thin pointed straps radiating like a Japanese maple / cannabis fan, not small crinkled 3-5 lobed palmate tufts. There are no spines anywhere — no thorn at any node. The berries are pale green knobbly balls sitting ON TOP of the bare stem tips, above the foliage, like flower buds on a stalk; the reference requires them hanging SINGLY BENEATH the branch, and none of them hang. No longitudinal stripes, no translucency — they are opaque matte spheres. The brown trunk stops in a hard flat brown wedge where the stems emerge.
rows.fix: Recolour foliage to mid green. Shorten and crinkle the lobes into a rounded 3-5 lobed maple-ish outline. Add a pair of sharp spines at every leaf node. Re-anchor the fruit: hang each berry on a short pendulous pedicel from the UNDERSIDE of a stem, and give it pale vertical veins over a translucent skin with a rim-light showing the interior.

rows.readsAs: A purple flowering vine or a string of anemones — nothing about it says grape
rows.defect: The 'leaves' are magenta-violet fans of six or seven straight straps radiating from a single point — a flower or a sea anemone, not a large palmately lobed toothed vine leaf, and the colour contradicts the mid-green reference outright. The tendrils are tiny flat dark ellipses stuck to the stem, drawn as closed loops seen edge-on; nothing coils and nothing forks. The berry bunch is a single small clump of grey-lilac balls pressed flat against the stem at mid-height, roughly the same size as one leaf, and it does not hang or taper into a cone. The stem is a smooth S-curve of uniform width with no woodiness or node swelling.
rows.fix: Recolour foliage to mid green and rebuild the leaf as a broad five-lobed cordate blade with a toothed margin and radiating veins. Redraw tendrils as forked, spiralling filaments that grow out of the node opposite each leaf, with real 3D coil overlap. Enlarge the bunch to 2-3x, hang it on a visible peduncle clear of the stem, and taper it into a conical cluster of many overlapping berries with a waxy bloom.

rows.readsAs: A green wine glass, or a single Caulerpa blade — not a cell colony
rows.defect: This is a solid, opaque, flat-shaded green vase or tulip shape on a thin stalk. The top is cut off by a PERFECTLY STRAIGHT HORIZONTAL LINE across the widest point — a machined edge, and the body below it is a smooth funnel with three straight pale seam lines running down it. It fails all three mustReads: it is not a sphere, there are no cells on the surface at all, there are no daughter colonies inside, and it is fully opaque with no jelly or translucency. It also has a stalk and a basal holdfast, which a free-floating colony should not have.
rows.fix: Discard the vase entirely. Draw a translucent sphere: a soft rim-lit circular boundary, no hard edge; stipple 60-120 small bright-green cells evenly over the surface with perspective foreshortening toward the limb; show 3-5 smaller daughter spheres suspended inside, dimmed and blurred by the intervening jelly; remove the stalk and holdfast.

rows.readsAs: A lollipop tree diagram, or a smoking olive branch — the trunk alone reads as a wooden craft stick
rows.defect: The trunk is a flat pale-olive rectangle with rounded ends and parallel straight sides — an ice-lolly stick. It does not taper, it has no bark texture, no flaking copper mottling, and it terminates in a blunt rounded cap that is simply overlapped by the canopy: a hard stick-into-blob seam with zero branching. The canopy is a pale grey fog cloud with individual small leaves floating around and outside it, unattached to anything; several leaves hang in empty space with no twig. Leaf colour is a washed-out silvery grey-green, not dull mid green, and the veins read as one central line, not sunken parallel ribs. The three fruits are plain olive spheres with a dark dot; no papery calyx crown.
rows.fix: Replace the stick with a tapering trunk that splits into 3-4 visible branches, and paint the flaking copper-over-green bark patchwork the reference calls for. Attach every leaf to a twig in opposite pairs and delete the orphan floaters. Kill or greatly reduce the grey fog layer and warm the leaf colour. Add a small dried star-shaped calyx crown at the fruit apex and give the skin a slightly bumpy pale yellow-green.

rows.readsAs: A dried palm fan, a golden pheasant tail fan, or a sea fan coral
rows.defect: Colour is completely wrong: the whole plant is saturated golden orange-yellow, reading as dead or dried, where the reference asks for deep glossy green with brown scaly bases. Posture is wrong too: instead of an upright shuttlecock the fronds splay outward and DOWNWARD into a fan much wider than it is tall (roughly 340x230 of used canvas, so aspect ~1.5 wide where 0.9 upright was specified) — several fronds point sideways and one droops below horizontal. The pinnae are hard-edged isoceles sawteeth of identical size marching along each rachis, machined and repetitive, and they are once-cut only — there is no second division, so 'twice-pinnate' fails. No scaly brown stalk bases are visible; the crown is a dark knot.
rows.fix: Recolour to deep green with a glossy specular sheen along each rachis. Rotate the fronds up into a true vase/shuttlecock: outer fronds arching at ~45 degrees, inner ones near vertical, and make the silhouette taller than wide. Subdivide each pinna into 5-8 pinnules with rounded, slightly irregular lobes instead of triangular teeth. Add brown papery scales clustered on the lower third of each stipe.

rows.readsAs: A bunch of grapes, or a blackberry — and inside this same batch it is easy to confuse with Grape, which is the actual grape entry
rows.defect: The body of the plant is a triangular pile of roughly 40 PERFECT GREY-BLUE CIRCLES, all the same radius, overlapping like a heap of ball bearings. They have no toothed margin, no heart-shaped base, no petiole, no vein — they are geometric primitives, and the desaturated blue-grey is not 'mid green, softly matt'. The whole mass sits on ONE thin green stalk that vanishes into the pile with a hard seam; the multi-stemmed stool from the mustRead is absent. The five gold objects on top are on thin straight wires standing UPRIGHT above the foliage — catkins must dangle, and the nut husks are not frilled, they are smooth acorn shapes.
rows.fix: Replace the circles with real leaf blades: broad rounded-cordate outline, abruptly pointed tip, visibly doubly-serrate margin, pinnate veins, matt mid green, each on its own short petiole off a twig. Split the base into 4-6 stems rising from one stool. Hang the catkins as long limp yellow tassels pointing DOWN from the twigs. Rebuild the nuts as clusters of 2-3 wrapped in a ragged, torn-edged green husk longer than the nut.

rows.readsAs: Lavender, or a thorny purple bramble
rows.defect: There are no leaves in this image. What should be minute scale leaves hugging the stem in four ranks are instead long straight purple SPIKES, 20-40px each, projecting at roughly 45 degrees from bare stems like barbs on a bramble — the opposite of the mustRead, and they are magenta, not dark green. The stems themselves are straight rigid line segments joining at hard angles; nothing curves or twigs. The silhouette is a tall narrow upright vase, not the specified 'low wiry twiggy mound' — it is clearly taller than wide. The pink flower spikes at the tips are the one right element, but they are only five, all at the very top, and they are not one-sided.
rows.fix: Delete the projecting spikes and replace with dense tiny scale leaves appressed along the whole stem length so the stems read as thickened and dark green, not naked. Curve and subdivide the stems into many fine twigs. Widen and flatten the silhouette into a spreading cushion. Multiply the flower spikes and place the tiny bells along one side of each spire.

rows.readsAs: A clump of aquarium ribbon-weed (Vallisneria) or a stylised green-and-teal flame
rows.defect: It is not floating and it is not a blanket. The render is three upright teal ribbon-blades standing on a ground shadow ellipse, rooted at the bottom of the frame — the opposite of "formless floating blanket with no stem or holdfast". Zero of the three mustReads are present: no hair-fine tangled filaments (the forms are broad solid slabs), no trapped gas bubbles anywhere, and there IS an implied holdfast/base plus a drop shadow that plants it on a floor. The blades are built from hard straight polygon segments with visible faceted corners (sharp angular notches along both silhouette edges and a flat-cut chevron top on each blade) — machined edges, not organic. Aspect is also inverted: the row asks for 2 (wide mat) and the picture is roughly 0.75 (taller than wide).
rows.fix: Stop routing this to the upright-seaweed-frond generator. It needs a horizontal-mat primitive: a wide, low, irregular-perimeter mass occupying the upper-middle band of the frame with a waterline, built from hundreds of overlapping hair-width filament strokes (1px, high count, random curl) rather than filled polygons, with 8-15 small translucent highlight-topped bubble discs embedded in and lifting the mat. Delete the ground shadow ellipse and the basal attachment entirely. Round or feather every polygon corner — the current faceted silhouette is the single most artificial thing in the picture.

rows.readsAs: A small green fern frond with a few pink buds stuck on the tip
rows.defect: There is no flower spike.
