The entire harvest is three tiny pink triangular blobs perched above the topmost leaf pair — not "a tall one-sided spike of hanging bells", not hanging, not one-sided, and no dark speckled throats (mustRead 2 and 3 both absent, mustRead 1 absent as a recognisable spike). The foliage is wrong too: neat opposite pinnate lance leaves running evenly up the whole stem, fern-frond fashion, instead of a basal rosette of large soft downy ovals with smaller leaves ascending. Leaf colour is a bright saturated mint green, not "dull grey-green, felted" — no felting or nap in the fill at all, just a flat gradient per leaflet. Every leaflet is the same lens shape mirrored at a fixed angle, so the plant reads as a mechanical repeat rather than a grown thing.
rows.fix: Add a real racemose inflorescence primitive: a bare vertical spike occupying the top ~40% of the height carrying 10-14 pendant tubular bells, all rotated to hang from one side of the axis, each bell a flared-mouth tube (not a triangle) with a speckle pass of dark maroon dots inside the visible throat. Rebuild the foliage as a wide basal rosette of broad downy ovals at the base with leaf size decaying up the stem, desaturate the green heavily toward grey and add a fine light rim-fuzz to sell the felted surface.

rows.readsAs: A spider plant or pampas-grass tuft with a tiny white mushroom growing out of it
rows.defect: The bulb — the single most identifying feature and an explicit mustRead — is entirely absent. The leaf fan simply narrows to nothing and disappears into a shadow ellipse; there is no white papery bulb and no clove divisions. The scape is a dead-straight vertical line with no curl or loop (mustRead 2 missing), and it terminates in a hard-edged flattened white ellipse that reads unmistakably as a small mushroom cap on a stalk, not a garlic umbel. The leaves are wrong in kind: 20-plus very thin grass blades in a tuft, where the row asks for flat folded strap leaves in a narrow fan — and they are near-white/silver, not "grey-green, waxy". Several blades on the left end in fine wispy scribbles that break the drawing's own weight.
rows.fix: Add the bulb: a rounded off-white mass at the base with 4-6 vertical seam lines dividing visible clove lobes and a translucent papery outer sheath, seated in the soil so the leaf bases emerge from its neck. Curl the scape — give it a full loop or a strong S-bend before the head, which is the classic hardneck garlic silhouette. Reduce blade count to 8-10, widen each into a flat strap with a visible central fold crease, and shift the fill from white to waxy grey-green. Replace the ellipse head with a spherical umbel of small bulbils.

rows.readsAs: A dead bracken frond or an autumn-coloured fern sprig
rows.defect: This is the Foxglove render with a colour swap — identical pinnate skeleton, identical leaflet shape, identical leaflet count and spacing, identical tiny-blobs-on-top inflorescence. The defining feature is missing: there is no deep-blue trumpet with a flared 5-lobed mouth, only four small blue rectangular specks above the top leaf pair, and the row demands the flower be LARGE relative to a low plant when here it is perhaps 3% of the image. Leaves are rust-orange/salmon, flatly contradicting "dark green", and they are pinnate along a tall stem rather than smooth pointed leaves in opposite pairs on a low plant. Aspect asks 0.6 and the render is a narrow tall column near 0.3.
rows.fix: Route this away from the shared pinnate-frond skeleton. Build a low plant (height ~60% of width) with 2-3 pairs of smooth untoothed lance leaves in true opposite pairs, dark green, and put a single upward-facing trumpet at the apex that occupies at least a third of the frame height: a tapering tube opening into five rounded lobes, filled with a saturated ultramarine-to-cobalt gradient and a paler striped throat. Fix the leaf colour lookup — orange here is almost certainly a palette index error.

rows.readsAs: A shaving brush or a bundle of bone-coloured feathers with three pills glued to it
rows.defect: The gas bladders are three flat white ROUNDED RECTANGLES painted on top of the blade surfaces — pure geometric primitives with uniform fill, no shading, no attachment, floating over the strap edges rather than swelling out of a blade base. That is a stuck-on part with a hard seam, and there are only three of them for a dozen-plus blades when the row requires one at the base of EVERY blade. The holdfast is missing entirely: the whole bundle tapers to a single sharp point at the bottom, so nothing anchors it. Colour is bone-white/cream, not "amber to olive-brown, translucent". The blades are smooth-edged straps with no wrinkling, and the bundle silhouette is a symmetrical teardrop.
rows.fix: Model the bladder as a pear-shaped swelling that is part of the blade path — widen the blade at its base into an ovoid with a shaded belly and a highlight, then narrow into the stipe, so there is no outline crossing. Emit one per blade. Add a branching root-claw holdfast at the base: 6-10 splayed forking haptera gripping a rock. Recolour to amber/olive-brown with alpha so blades overlap translucently, and add crosswise wrinkle ripples along each blade. Break the left-right symmetry of the bundle.

rows.readsAs: A purple water lily or a magenta agave rosette
rows.defect: Reads as a flower, not a plant. The render is a wide low rosette of ~18 broad pointed magenta-purple petal-blades radiating symmetrically from a central point, with a thin bare stalk carrying a small knobbly yellow spike. All three mustReads are absent: no clump of reedy leafy canes, no two-ranked narrow strap leaves (these are wide triangular petals in a radial fan, not two ranks), and no rhizome — the base is a bare point on a shadow, with nothing knobbed or fingered exposed. Leaf colour is purple where the row says mid green. Aspect asks 0.7 (taller than wide) and the render is about 1.6 (much wider than tall). The radial symmetry is near-perfect, which is the giveaway that it is a generic flower primitive with the petal count turned up.
rows.fix: Switch the form from radial-rosette to a cane clump: 3-5 slender vertical reed stems of differing heights, each carrying narrow strap leaves alternating strictly LEFT-RIGHT in one plane (two-ranked) and arching down at the tips. Recolour foliage to mid green. Add the rhizome as a horizontal knuckled buff-yellow mass half-buried at soil level with 3-4 finger lobes, with the canes visibly emerging from its top so there is no seam. The yellow spike inflorescence is fine but should sit on a short separate stalk from the rhizome, not tower over the plant.

rows.readsAs: A red bottlebrush, a celosia plume, or a small orange conifer sapling
rows.defect: The count is wrong by an order of magnitude: the row asks for A SINGLE stem topped by ONE whorl of five-fingered leaves, and the render stacks roughly twelve identical whorls of narrow spiky leaflets up the entire stem into a dense column. The leaflets are simple pointed spears, not toothed palmate leaflets, and there are far more than five per whorl. The berry cluster sits ON TOP of the column instead of in the centre of the whorl, and the pale forked man-shaped root — the whole reason anyone recognises ginseng — is absent; the stem just meets a shadow. Leaf colour is red-orange, not mid green. The regular vertical repetition makes it look extruded rather than grown.
rows.fix: Reduce to one whorl at the apex of a single bare stem: five long-stalked leaves radiating horizontally, each divided into five toothed leaflets (a palmate compound primitive, not spears), in mid green. Place the tight scarlet berry head at the whorl's centre, below the leaf plane so leaves frame it. Expose the root: a pale forked bifurcating taproot with rootlet hairs and a slight anthropomorphic two-leg fork, emerging seamlessly from the stem base.

rows.readsAs: A red rocket nose cone, a traffic cone, or a single chilli pepper standing on end
rows.defect: It is one smooth unsegmented cone. The defining mustRead — leafless ARTICULATED fleshy stems, jointed like stacked tiny sausages — is completely missing; there is not a single joint, constriction or node anywhere on the form. There is no branching at all, let alone "opposite pairs like small candelabra". And the colour law is inverted: the row says bright translucent green reddening only on OLDER segments, while the whole plant here is a uniform crimson from tip to base. The surface decoration is vertical parallel ridge stripes running the full height, which reads as machined fluting, and the silhouette is a perfect symmetrical cone tapering to a needle point. Aspect asks 1.2 (roughly as wide as tall) and the render is about 0.35.
rows.fix: Rebuild from a segment primitive: stack 6-9 short barrel-shaped joints per stem with a visible pinch between each, each joint slightly fatter in the middle. Branch in opposite pairs from the joint nodes, 2-3 tiers, to give the candelabra shape and widen the plant to roughly its own height. Fill the base and mid segments with bright translucent green and apply the crimson only as an age gradient on the lowest/oldest joints and stem base. Remove the vertical fluting stripes entirely — replace with a soft waxy specular highlight per joint.

rows.readsAs: A cycad or young palm — a pole with a radiating burst of fronds on top.
rows.defect: The trunk is a flat terracotta capsule — two perfectly straight parallel sides with a rounded cap — that plunges into the crown with no branching, no fork, no root flare, and it is a single uniform brown gradient with zero mottled grey flaking bark. The crown is a brown fog blob with ~20 stiff pinnate spokes radiating from a single point around its rim; the spokes attach to nothing (no branch structure between trunk and leaf), so every frond is stuck ON the fog rather than growing OUT of wood. The four fruits are perfect glowing circles with identical specular dots floating over the foliage, and the ground under the tree is completely bare — the mustRead 'yellow fruit littering the ground' is entirely absent.
rows.fix: Replace the capsule trunk with a tapered, buttressed bole that forks into 3-5 visible scaffold limbs before the crown, and paint mottled grey-buff bark with irregular flaking plates instead of the flat brown gradient. Attach leaf clusters to the ends of those limbs so the crown is built from twigs, not sprayed onto fog. Replace the perfect fruit circles with slightly irregular matte yellow spheres and scatter 8-15 of them in a heap on the shadow ellipse beneath the tree.

rows.readsAs: An ornamental purple cordyline or phormium, not a meadow grass.
rows.defect: Every blade is saturated violet-purple, not fresh green or blue-green. The seed head is a single short stiff vertical spike of stacked beads on a bare stalk — there is no pyramid, no whorled branches, no airy structure at all, so two of the three mustReads ('airy open pyramid of a seed head', 'fine whorled panicle branches') are missing outright. The blades are all identical smooth tapering ribbons fanning from one point with a hard-edged highlight down each, machine-uniform with no boat tips and no variation.
rows.fix: Recolour blades to fresh green with a blue-green cast. Replace the beaded spike with a true open panicle: a central rachis with 3-4 whorls of thin branches, each branch splitting again and carrying a few small spikelets at the tips, occupying a triangle wider at the bottom. Vary blade width, curvature and length, and give the tips the flattened boat hood.

rows.readsAs: A purple flowering climber — clematis or passionflower — with a bud on it.
rows.defect: The leaves are purple pinwheel stars of six sharp pointed petals — nothing rounded, nothing lobed, nothing hairy, and the wrong colour entirely. The vine is a thin grey S-curve floating in mid-air with the plant occupying the vertical centre of the frame; there is no ground-trailing runner, and the tendrils are two tiny closed grey ovals that read as rings rather than coiled springs. The single fruit is a small ribbed sphere pinned at a stem joint halfway up the picture, hanging in air rather than resting on the ground, and the star leaves meet the stem at hard butt joints.
rows.fix: Rotate the composition to a horizontal ground-runner along the lower third, recolour to a slightly grey hairy mid-green, and replace the star leaves with broad rounded palmate blades with five shallow lobes and a scalloped rough edge. Draw tendrils as open helical coils springing off the node. Move the fruit down onto the ground line, enlarge it, and give it tan-green netted rind rather than a smooth ribbed ball.

rows.readsAs: A generic lollipop tree — indistinguishable from Marula in this same batch apart from hue.
rows.defect: It is the same asset as Marula recoloured yellow: identical flat capsule trunk with straight parallel sides and no low branching, identical fog-blob crown with stiff ladder-notched spokes radiating from one point. None of the three mustReads land — the foliage is coarse spokes, not fine feathery bipinnate lace; there are no paired thorns anywhere at the nodes; the trunk is straight and vertical rather than crooked and low-branching, and the crown is a round dome rather than wide and flat. Two dark grey ellipses sit inside the crown reading as holes or smudges rather than seed pods, and no straw-coloured pods hang anywhere.
rows.fix: Break the trunk into a short crooked bole that splits below mid-height into two or three leaning limbs, and flatten and widen the crown envelope. Rebuild the foliage from many tiny paired leaflets on fine rachises so it reads as lace at 440px rather than a comb. Add paired straight white thorns at the nodes. Replace the dark ellipses with clusters of long pale straw pods hanging clear of the foliage against the dark background.

rows.readsAs: An ear of wheat or a golden fern frond — the same template as Mint in this batch.
rows.defect: The whole plant is orange-gold, not dull grey-green, and the silhouette is a narrow vertical spire roughly a third as wide as tall — nowhere near the stated 0.6 squat herb. The leaves are eleven pairs of small identical almond shapes stamped up the stem in a perfectly regular ladder with no size gradient and no visible pale midrib; they meet the stem at hard points with no petiole or leaf base. The flower is a single tiny pink half-disc capping the very top like a pinhead — there is no domed umbel, and the warty silk-bursting pod is completely absent, so two of the three mustReads are missing.
rows.fix: Widen the plant and cut to 4-6 pairs of large oblong leaves that get smaller upward, each with a thick pale midrib and a short clasping base, drooping slightly. Recolour to dull grey-green. Replace the pink cap with a nodding hemispherical umbel of many small dusty-pink florets on visible pedicels, and add at least one warty spindle pod split open with white silk streaming out.

rows.readsAs: A pink ornamental grass or dwarf phormium with a seed spike.
rows.defect: Every blade is hot magenta-pink instead of mid green — the plant is entirely non-green. The composition is a straight recolour of Meadow Grass in the same batch: identical fan of smooth uniform tapering ribbons from a single point, identical thin bare stalk rising from the centre. The seed head does read as a beaded bottlebrush, but it is thin and short rather than the thick heavy spike the reference calls for, and it does not nod or bend under any weight.
rows.fix: Recolour blades to mid green. Thicken the seed head to two or three times its current width and lengthen it so it dominates the top of the frame, and let it lean or nod slightly. Give the cane visible nodes and joints, and differentiate the blade fan from Meadow Grass by making the blades broader, longer and arching over more steeply.

rows.readsAs: A burger, or a bowl of glowing lava — nobody would name any plant.
rows.defect: This is not a plant at all — it is a horizontal cluster of six overlapping soft red circles with a yellow rounded rectangle sitting in the middle, heavily blurred, occupying only the bottom half of the frame. There is no stem, no leaf shape, no flowers, and none of the pale fresh-green colour. Both mustReads fail completely: there is no circular leaf pierced by a stem and no white flowers standing out of it. The yellow centre is an obvious geometric primitive with straight sides and rounded corners; the red lobes are perfect circles.
rows.fix: Rebuild from scratch: a slender upright stem carrying one roughly circular pale-green disc leaf viewed at a slight tilt, with the stem visibly passing through the centre of the disc and continuing upward; add a small loose spray of five or six tiny white flowers on thin pedicels rising above the disc, and a couple of long-stalked spade-shaped basal leaves at ground level. Kill the red/orange palette entirely.

rows.readsAs: A fern frond or a young ash sapling with a lavender tip — visually a hue-swap of Milkweed in this same batch.
rows.defect: It is the Milkweed asset recoloured teal: the identical eleven-pair ladder of small uniform leaves up a perfectly straight thin stem, with a small bead column at the tip. None of the three mustReads land — the stem is a plain round hairline with no square section or edge shading; the leaves are narrow smooth lance blades with completely untoothed margins, not oval and toothed; and the pairs are all drawn flat in-plane, so there is no decussate crossing at the nodes. Leaves join the stem at hard points with no petiole. The lilac tip is a stack of identical circles rather than whorled flower rings.
rows.fix: Cut to 4-5 pairs of broad ovate leaves with clearly serrated edges and sunken veins, and rotate alternate pairs 90 degrees so successive pairs cross when seen from the front. Redraw the stem thick enough to show two shaded faces and a corner so it reads square. Replace the bead stack with two or three whorled rings of tiny lilac flowers with visible stamens at the stem tip, and set the shoot in a small clump rather than as a single isolated stalk.

rows.readsAs: a grey feather-duster or dandelion clock stuck on a brown lollipop stick, with four yellow marbles glued on
rows.defect: Nothing in this picture is a lemon tree. The trunk is a flat maroon capsule — a rounded rectangle with no taper, no bark, no branching, no root flare — and it stops dead at a hard horizontal edge where the crown blob begins, a visible seam between trunk and canopy. The canopy is a radial pinwheel of ~30 near-identical pointed blades all fanning outward from one centre point, and they are GREY-lavender, not 'mid to dark green'. Behind them sits a grey smoke puff that reads as fog, not leaf mass. The four fruits are perfect circles with a single specular dot — no nipple, no pore texture, no stem, and they are pasted flat over the leaves rather than hanging among them. mustRead fails on all three: no pointed nipple end, no thorns anywhere, no purple-flushed buds.
rows.fix: Kill the capsule trunk: draw a tapering bole that splits into 3-4 visible scaffold limbs which the crown grows out of, so there is no seam. Recolour foliage to real citrus green (dark glossy #2d5a2a-ish) and break the radial fan — leaves should hang in clumped sprays at branch ends with varied angles, not spoke out from a hub. Give the fruit an ovoid body with a small drawn nipple bump at the lower pole and a stem dimple at the top, and hang two of them below leaves so they occlude. Add short straight thorns at the leaf axils.

rows.readsAs: a corporate sunburst logo, or a half-open teal folding fan
rows.defect: This is a flat teal sunburst: sixteen straight, hard-edged, machine-perfect tapered spokes radiating from a single point at the bottom centre, all one flat #2fb5a0 with no shading, on empty background. It is a vector logo, not an organism. Every mustRead is absent — there is no flat crusty rosette, no rock or bark substrate at all, no lobed edges, no chalky pale margin, and no cup discs. The note explicitly says 'never as foliage' and 'drawn as a crust or antler-tuft on a substrate'; this is neither — it is a fan of stiff rays springing from one hub, the exact opposite of a crust.
rows.fix: Rebuild from scratch as a substrate piece: paint a mottled grey rock or bark slab occupying the lower two thirds, then grow an irregular crustose thallus over it with a ragged non-radial outline, overlapping leathery lobes with a raised chalky-white rim, sage/grey-green body with rust-orange and sulphur-yellow blotches, and a scatter of small raised apothecial cups (dark centre, pale rim) on the surface. If the antler-tuft variant is wanted instead, use irregularly forking round branchlets with blunt swollen tips — never straight rays from a common origin.

rows.readsAs: a golden wheat or barley sprig, or a decorative brass laurel branch
rows.defect: A perfectly straight brown stick with five exactly mirrored pairs of large glossy GOLD lens-shaped leaves and three tiny yellow spheres at each node. Colour is flat wrong — reference says 'mid-green, dull' and this is metallic gold. Leaf architecture is wrong: these are ten simple opposite blades, not pinnate leaves of 9-17 leaflets — there is no rachis, no terminal leaflet, no compound structure at all. No pale blue-violet pea flower spike exists; the yellow beads at the nodes read as berries. No roots or runners are drawn, despite the harvest being the root. The bilateral symmetry is machine-exact — every left leaf is the mirror of its right partner at identical angle — which kills any sense of a grown plant.
rows.fix: Recolour to dull mid-green. Replace each simple blade with a true pinnate leaf: a side rachis carrying 9-13 small oval leaflets in pairs plus one terminal leaflet. Break the mirror symmetry — jitter leaf angle, length and node spacing. Replace the yellow node beads with slim upright racemes of small pale blue-violet pea flowers (banner + wings visible on the largest ones). Add the harvest below a soil line: two or three long straight ropey yellow-fleshed roots with horizontal runners.

rows.readsAs: a purple ornamental palm or cycad, or a feather boa
rows.defect: A bright MAGENTA/orchid fan of fronds. leafColour says 'bright yellow-green'; this is pink-purple, so the species reads as an alien ornamental. Frond shape is wrong too — the pinnae are long sharp needle-teeth cut nearly to the rachis, giving a comb/palm look, where the reference demands 'blunt lobes joined at the base along the stalk'. All three mustReads fail: there is no mossy branch or trunk for the fronds to sprout from (they emerge from nothing at the bottom of the frame), no wing fusing the lobes along the stalk, and no green rhizome running through moss. The note says it grows on bark and mossy rock, not soil — no substrate of any kind is present, so the epiphyte identity is lost entirely.
rows.fix: Recolour to bright yellow-green. Draw a mossy horizontal branch or rock across the lower third and have the fronds and a visible knobbly green rhizome emerge from the moss — the fronds must attach to something. Reshape the pinnae: rounded blunt tips, cut only two-thirds to the midrib, and joined at their bases by a continuous green wing running down the rachis. Reduce frond count and let a couple arch and overlap so it is a tuft on bark rather than a symmetrical hand-fan.

rows.readsAs: a dried autumn twig jammed into a lump of blue plasticine
rows.defect: A thin straight pale-lilac wire with six tan-ORANGE lens leaves alternating up it, spearing into a bright ROYAL BLUE blob sitting on the ground. Two colour failures: leaves should be mid-green, and the harvest root should be yellow woody — the blue lump reads as a rock or a puddle of slime, not a root. The lump is a hard-outlined separate primitive with a crisp seam where the stem enters it; nothing grows out of anything. Leaves are simple, not pinnate — no locust-tree leaflet structure. No pea flowers at all. The 'long straight ropey yellow root' mustRead is entirely absent.
rows.fix: Recolour leaves mid-green and convert each to a pinnate leaf with 9-13 oval leaflets on a side rachis. Delete the blue blob; replace with a cutaway soil line under which two or three long straight ropey yellow-fleshed roots descend and one horizontal runner travels sideways, drawn continuous with the stem base (fibrous rootlets crossing the soil line so there is no seam). Add a slim upright spike of pale blue-lilac pea flowers near the top.

rows.readsAs: a child's apple tree — a green lollipop cloud on a green post; nearly indistinguishable from the Lemon render in this same batch
rows.defect: Same skeleton as Lemon in this batch, recoloured — the trunk is again a flat straight capsule (rounded rectangle, uniform width, rounded bottom cap floating above its shadow), and it is the SAME green as the leaves, so the tree has no bark and no woody read at all. The crown is a soft airbrushed green cloud with small leaf flecks sprayed on top of it rather than composing it; several stray dark hooked scribbles float inside the cloud with nothing attached to them. Fruits are three perfect spheres bunched at the top-left plus one at the right, all rendered yellow-olive with a highlight dot — they read as apples, not limes, and they sit on the canopy surface instead of hanging in it. Both foliage mustReads fail: no spines in the leaf joints, and no winged petiole below any blade.
rows.fix: Give the trunk a tapered brown bole with root flare and 3-4 branches that push into and structure the crown, replacing the cloud-blob-plus-sprayed-flecks with actual clumped leaf sprays hung off those branches. Delete the loose hook scribbles. Recolour fruit to true lime green, slightly smaller than the current spheres, with a dimpled pore texture and a nub, hung low in the canopy so leaves overlap them. Add short sharp axillary spines and, on the nearest few leaves, the diagnostic wing on the petiole below the blade.

rows.readsAs: a turquoise plastic aquarium plant with red beads clipped to it
rows.defect: An upright bouquet roughly two and a half times taller than wide, with bright CYAN/turquoise lance-shaped pointed leaves — the reference calls for dark glossy green, small, thick, leathery and box-like, and none of that reads here. The habit is the biggest failure: mustRead demands 'a low creeping evergreen mat barely a hand high', and this is a vertical vase-shaped clump reaching for the sky. The stems all rise out of a solid flat-shaded green wedge at the base that has a hard outline and visible comb-tine notches cut into it — a separate primitive the stems are plugged into, with an obvious seam and no transition into the soil. The berry clusters sit perched on top of the shoot tips like little flower heads rather than nodding beneath them.
rows.fix: Rebuild the habit: a wide low mat under about a third of the frame height, stems creeping sideways and arching up only slightly, rooting where they touch. Delete the green base wedge entirely and let stems emerge from moss/soil litter. Recolour leaves to dark glossy green with a paler underside showing where they curl, reshape to small rounded ovals with rolled-under edges, and pack them tightly along the stems. Hang the scarlet berry clusters nodding under the shoot tips so they read as fruit weight, not blossom.

rows.readsAs: three floating tealight candles, or poached eggs in a blue dish, with a pink sticker between them
rows.defect: Three flat cream-white ellipses lying on a dark blue ellipse. The note is violated head-on: the pads FLOAT FLAT on the water surface — the water-lily error the row explicitly forbids — with no stalks whatsoever, so 'leaf held high above water on a central stalk' fails outright. Colour is wrong: they are ivory/bone, not blue-grey green with a waxy bloom, and each has a plain crescent shading line instead of radiating veins or an upturned rim. The bloom is a tiny flat 6-pointed pink star about a twentieth of a pad's area, nothing like a 'large pink cupped bowl' of many petals. There is no shower-head seed pod at all. The pond itself is a mathematically perfect ellipse with a thin uniform stroke around it — a geometric primitive, not water.
rows.fix: Redraw completely: raise two or three peltate pads well clear of the waterline on tall visible stalks that attach at the pad CENTRE underneath, with the rims turned up into a shallow bowl and radial veins running from the central attachment. Recolour to blue-grey green with a matte waxy bloom. Add a large pink many-petalled cupped bloom on its own tall stalk, roughly a third of frame height, plus one flat-topped green receptacle showing sunken wells with loose seeds. Replace the outlined ellipse pond with a soft irregular water plane, reflections and a broken horizon rather than a stroked shape.

rows.readsAs: A purple bottlebrush or a Liatris/lavender spike — or, honestly, a fuzzy purple caterpillar on a stick
rows.defect: A bright magenta-purple spiky column on a thin brown pin. Every mustRead fails: there is no silver-white underside anywhere (the whole plant is one saturated purple with no bicolour flip at all), no reddish grooved stem (just a 4px dull brown line), and the 'drab greenish-grey spires' are instead a floor-to-ceiling wall of showy purple petals — exactly what the note forbids. The only drab element is a tiny cream beaded stub poking out the top. Leaves are not cut or pinnate: they are flat isoceles triangles arranged in perfect mirrored pairs down a rigid axis, a stamped repeat, not foliage. The whole spike ends abruptly at a hard horizontal line where it meets the bare stem, and the stem is a stuck-on stick, not a stalk the leaves grow from.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a branching herb, not a spike: alternate (not paired) pinnately cut leaves with 3-5 pointed lobes per side and a real midrib, painted dark green on the upper face with a distinct pale grey-white wash on the reversed/curled leaves so the silver flicker reads. Recolour the stem to reddish-purple with vertical groove striping and taper it into the leaf bases instead of butting them. Delete the purple bloom entirely; replace with several narrow, loose, grey-green spires of tiny buttons at the top only, occupying the upper ~25% of the plant.

rows.readsAs: A generic sand-coloured lollipop tree hung with blackberries — closest to Nutmeg in this same batch, same capsule trunk and ball crown
rows.defect: The crown is a beige-tan cloud of ~25 identical almond/nut-shaped pods, each with a hard central crease line, floating over a brown fog blob. Nothing in it reads as a leaf: no teeth, no lobes, no mix of heart-shaped and lobed forms, no green — the whole canopy is a matt sand colour where the row asks for mid green. The trunk is a flat orange-red rounded rectangle with perfectly straight parallel machined sides and a rounded bottom cap; it enters the crown at a hard seam with zero branching, and no crooked branches exist anywhere. The berries are four purple lumps that read as square knobbly clusters glued flat onto the canopy surface, not elongated and not hanging from or staining any branch. Crown is also a compact ball, not broad and low-spreading.
rows.fix: Repaint the canopy mid-green matt and reshape the leaf stamp into two real variants used together — a broad heart-shaped toothed blade and an irregular 2-3 lobed blade, both with visible serrated edges. Replace the capsule trunk with a tapering, forking bole plus 3-4 crooked limbs that carry the leaf masses so the crown grows out of the wood; widen the crown to ~1.4x its height and lower it. Make berries elongated cylinders in white/red/near-black hanging on short stalks below the twigs, with a dark stain smudge on the branch beneath.

rows.readsAs: A frosted bottlebrush or a small white fir sapling — and structurally it is the same picture as Mugwort and Nettle in this batch
rows.defect: This is the Mugwort render recoloured: the exact same rigid mirrored spike of flat triangular points down a single axis, here in icy pale blue-white. The leaf colour is wrong in kind, not degree — mid to yellow-green becomes near-white with a blue cast. All three mustReads fail: the yellow flowers are a single 20px yellow crescent smear balanced on top like a hat, not a flat-topped raceme of four-petalled crosses; there are no seed pods at all, slender/beaked or otherwise; and there is no big lyre-shaped lower leaf — the lowest leaves are the same triangle as every other. The plant is unbranched where the row calls for a branching stem, and the green thread stem is a separate stuck-on line, hard-terminating at the base of the spike.
rows.fix: Start over as a branching cruciferous herb: a few splaying stems, big lyre-shaped lower leaves with an oversized rounded terminal lobe and small side lobes at the base, narrowing to plain lance leaves higher up, all in yellow-green with a slightly bristly edge. Put a flat-topped corymb of individual 4-petal yellow crosses at each stem tip, and hang 6-10 slender upward-angled pods with a pointed beak off the stem just below each flower head.

rows.readsAs: A palm or dandelion-shaped firework tree with Christmas baubles on it; shares its flat green capsule trunk with Oak in this batch
rows.defect: The trunk is a flat, uniform, straight-sided green capsule with a rounded foot — a machined primitive, and it is the same green as the leaves so the tree has no wood. It plunges into the crown at a hard seam with no branching. The crown is not a broad rounded shady canopy: it is a starburst of about a dozen isolated pinnate sprigs radiating outward like a firework or a dandelion clock, with a hollow blurred green fog disc showing through the gaps in the middle. The leaflets are drawn as tiny straight ovals in neat rows with no sickle curve and no teeth, and the sprays point outward and upward rather than drooping. The white flower sprays are entirely absent — a whole mustRead missing. In their place are three perfectly circular yellow-gold balls with a hard specular dot, which read as glass ornaments hung on the tree.
rows.fix: Give the tree a brown tapering bole that forks into 4-5 limbs, and hang the pinnate sprays off those limbs so they droop with gravity rather than radiating from a point. Curve each leaflet into an asymmetric sickle with a toothed margin and a glossy highlight along the upper blade. Fill the hollow crown centre with overlapping foliage to make a solid rounded dome. Add loose airy sprays of tiny white star flowers among the leaves, and reduce the fruit to small dull olive-shaped ovals with matt green-to-yellow skin — no specular sphere highlight.

rows.readsAs: A green feather or a plain pinnate fern frond; identical construction to Mugwort and Mustard in this batch
rows.defect: Same stamped spike template again, this time in flat jade green. The leaves are smooth blunt-ended sausages/ovals laid in overlapping mirrored pairs — no heart shape, no coarse teeth, no pointed tip, and no bristles or hairs anywhere on leaf or stem, which kills the single most identifying feature of a nettle. The stem is a thin green thread, perfectly round in section with no square edges or hair, and it simply stops at the bottom of the leaf mass at a hard line. The flower strings are wrong in both form and place: one small cream beaded stalk sticking straight UP out of the apex, where the row calls for trailing green tassels drooping from the leaf axils down the sides. Tiering is mechanical, ~11 identical rungs at equal spacing.
rows.fix: Rebuild the leaf as a cordate blade — wide notched base, sharp drawn-out tip, deep sawtooth margin — and set opposite pairs at 90-degree rotation between tiers with clear internode gaps so the tiers read as a real plant. Give the stem visible flat faces/edge ridges for the square section and stipple fine bristles on stem and leaf edges. Move the flowers into the axils as several limp green catkin strings hanging DOWNWARD, and remove the upright cream spike entirely.

rows.readsAs: A cycad or an autumn-coloured tree fern — the salmon crown plus brown trunk reads as an ornamental palm, not a mangrove nipa
rows.defect: It has a big obvious forked TRUNK — a thick brown Y-shaped column running from the ground to the crown, occupying the lower two-thirds of the frame — when the first mustRead is explicitly 'no visible trunk, fronds erupting directly from water and mud'. That is a direct contradiction, not a shortfall. Second, the fronds are salmon/coral orange-red, not glossy mid-to-dark green; the plant is the wrong colour entirely. Third, the fruit is wrong in size, colour and position: a small knot of pale cream-white pebbles about 40px across tucked into the fork up in the crown, instead of a large brown woody spiky cannonball sitting at ground level. The trunk is also a smooth flat-shaded shape with hard straight edges and a rounded foot, and the fronds sprout from it at a single hard seam.
rows.fix: Delete the trunk outright — fronds must spring straight out of a muddy waterline at the base of the frame, splaying from one hidden point. Recolour fronds glossy green and make them tall, stiff and upright rather than arching over. Replace the cream knot with a big brown woody ball of tightly packed angular faceted fruits, roughly 1/4 of the image width, seated in the mud at the base among the frond bases, and add a wet mud/water suggestion at the ground line.

rows.readsAs: An olive or generic peach tree; shares Mulberry's capsule trunk and blob crown almost exactly
rows.defect: Two of three mustReads are simply absent. The fruit are four intact pale peach spheres with a hard specular highlight — none is split, there is no scarlet lacy mace and no brown seed showing anywhere, so the one thing that makes nutmeg identifiable is missing. The crown is a round olive-yellow ball, not a dense conical dark crown, and the leaf colour is a dull yellow-olive rather than dark glossy green with a grey reverse; leaves are plain pointed ovals scattered thinly enough that the brown fog blob shows through the middle. The trunk is a flat medium-brown rounded rectangle, straight parallel sides, rounded bottom, no taper, no bark texture, meeting the canopy at a hard seam with no branches. The spheres read as beads pinned onto the leaf layer rather than fruit hanging on stalks.
rows.fix: Reshape the crown to a tall conical dark-green mass and repaint the leaves dark glossy elliptic with a highlight streak and a pale grey underside on the turned leaves. Replace at least two of the fruit with halves split open along a vertical seam — pale yellow leathery rind gaping, a bright scarlet net of mace lacing over a glossy dark brown nut inside — and hang them on short stalks with a shadow where they attach. Taper the trunk, add bark, and fork it into limbs inside the crown.

rows.readsAs: A maple sapling with chestnuts on it; the trunk is the same flat green capsule used on Neem in this batch
rows.defect: Nothing here says oak. The leaves are sharply pointed star/palmate shapes with spiky teeth — they read maple or cannabis, the exact opposite of oak's rounded deeply-cut lobes. The crown is a donut: a ring of foliage around a large empty blurred green disc in the middle, and it is roughly as tall as wide rather than the broad spreading canopy the row demands. The trunk is a flat bright-green capsule, straight-sided, uniform, with a rounded foot — it is the same colour as the leaves, has no bark at all, let alone rugged deep fissures, and it is a stuck-on stick that meets the crown at a hard horizontal seam with no limbs. The acorns are three plain brown spheres bunched together with no scaly cup on any of them, so they read as chestnuts or berries.
rows.fix: Redraw the leaf outline with 5-7 ROUNDED lobes cut deep toward the midrib and no sharp points, clustered at twig ends. Widen the crown to about 1.3x its height, fill the hollow centre with overlapping leaf clumps and let a few dark branch lines show through. Replace the green capsule with a thick brown bole that flares at the base and forks into heavy crooked limbs, textured with deep vertical fissures and cast shadow in the grooves. Give each acorn an oval nut with a textured scaly cap covering its top third, and sit them on short twigs, not floating in the leaf mass.

rows.readsAs: a bundle of asparagus spears or scattered pick-up-sticks in a green cone
rows.defect: About a dozen short green rod segments float completely free of the plant — they cross the picture in mid-air with no attachment at either end (the pair at upper-left around x=150,y=175 and the two on the right at x=255,y=190 and x=265,y=215 touch nothing at all). The base is a solid flat green triangular wedge with two dead-straight sides and a hard seam where the individual stems disappear into it, so the stems read as sticks pushed into a cone rather than emerging from a crown. Every rod is a straight, uniform-width line with no nodes, no swellings and no scale sheaths anywhere, so the defining jointed character is absent. The red 'cone-berries' are five flat clusters of small circles sitting at the very stem tips, not at the joints.
rows.fix: Kill the off-body segments — every rod must trace back to the crown; clip strokes to the stem graph instead of scattering free line segments. Replace the solid triangular base with overlapping stem bases that splay and taper so the silhouette is made of the stems themselves. Add a visible node every ~18px: a slight diameter bulge plus a tiny dark scale collar, and jog the rod angle a few degrees at each node so the stems read as jointed rather than ruler-straight. Move the red berry clusters from the tips down onto the nodes and give them a fleshy 3D shading rather than flat discs.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon lollipop tree with daisies stuck in it
rows.defect: This is a lollipop: a single straight olive-yellow bar for a trunk topped by a round blurred ball of foliage. Three mustReads fail outright. (1) The leaves radiate OUTWARD from the ball like a dandelion clock or sunflower burst — they point up, sideways and diagonally; none hang vertically, so the sparse open crown is instead a dense opaque blob. (2) The bark is one flat olive-yellow tone with a soft gradient — no ribbon peel, no cream/grey/orange patchwork. (3) There are no gumnut capsules; the harvest is shown as four white daisies with dark button centres and separated petals, which read as chamomile, not a stamen-burst blossom. The trunk also terminates in a rounded capsule end that stops short of the ground shadow, so the tree appears to hover, and its edges are two parallel machined lines.
rows.fix: Rebuild the crown as pendulous: draw each adult leaf as a long sickle blade hanging near-vertical from its petiole, with gaps of background showing through — the crown outline should be ragged and see-through, not a filled circle. Recolour foliage from olive-yellow to matt grey-blue-green with a waxy bloom, same tone on both faces. Replace the daisies with clustered woody cup gumnuts (small hemispherical capsules with a rimmed top and 3-4 valve teeth) plus, optionally, hemispherical fluff pom-poms of fine cream filaments and no dark disc centre. Repaint the trunk with vertical peeling ribbons revealing cream/grey/orange patches, flare the base into roots that meet the shadow, and vary the trunk edge so it is not two straight lines.

rows.readsAs: a blue feather, or a stylised wheat/fern stalk — nothing about it says fennel
rows.defect: The foliage is not feathery at all — it is two rigid vertical columns of discrete teardrop leaflets stamped in near-perfect rows either side of a straight grey stem, giving a hard rounded-rectangle silhouette roughly 90px wide by 180px tall. The colour is saturated cobalt/periwinkle BLUE, not blue-grey green; nothing in this picture is green. The umbel is a single small solid yellow crescent (a filled arc primitive) balanced on the stem tip — no spokes, no rays, no individual florets, and it is much too small relative to the plant. The stem is a flat grey rod with no ribbing and no blue bloom.
rows.fix: Replace the stamped leaflets with 3-4 orders of recursive branching ending in hair-fine 1px threads, drawn in a soft irregular cloud that overlaps and dissolves at the edges rather than filling a rectangle. Recolour to desaturated blue-tinged sage green. Rebuild the umbel as a wide flat disc of 10-20 visible rays springing from one point, each ray ending in a tiny cluster of yellow florets — draw the rays, do not fill an arc. Add 2-3 lateral umbels at different heights so the top is not one lonely shape, and put fine vertical ribs and a glaucous highlight on the stem.

rows.readsAs: a white bottlebrush or Banksia flower spike, or a feather
rows.defect: There is no fenugreek here. The plant is a dense column of overlapping pure-WHITE pointed petals stacked in regular tiers up a stalk — a capsule silhouette about 100x250px. The mustRead trifoliate clover leaves are entirely absent: there is not one group of three toothed oval leaflets anywhere, and there is essentially no green in the image except a 40px stub of stem at the bottom and two small tips at the crown. The pea flowers are absent. The sickle pod is represented by one small grey-brown speckled blob near the apex that reads as a caterpillar sitting on the plant rather than a beaked pod. It also reuses the same stacked-column template as Fennel in this batch, recoloured white.
rows.fix: Discard the column template. Build an upright branching green stem with alternate trifoliate leaves: three oval leaflets on a short common petiole, each leaflet widest past the middle and toothed only toward the tip, in light fresh green. Tuck small pale yellow-white pea flowers (standard/wing/keel, not radial petals) singly or in pairs into the leaf axils. Draw the pods as long thin green-to-tan sickles curving upward with a fine pointed beak, several per plant, clearly attached at an axil. Remove the white petal mass entirely.

rows.readsAs: a cyan agave rosette or a sea anemone
rows.defect: The mustRead croziers are effectively missing — I can find exactly one tiny thin circle (about 12px, at roughly x=232,y=278) buried in the middle; there is no group of tight coils standing in the centre, and no papery brown scale husks anywhere. The colour is electric cyan/turquoise, not vivid spring-green. Each frond is a machined comb: a smooth bar with identical sharp triangular teeth on one side only, all the same length and spacing, which reads as a saw blade rather than pinnae. Several frond tips end in a blunt flat grey-blue chisel cut (right side around x=395,y=210 and upper-left x=95,y=145) — a hard squared-off edge no plant has. The overall shape is a flattened fan, not a vase.
rows.fix: Put 4-6 prominent croziers upright in the centre at varied heights: a spiral of 2.5+ turns, thickening from the tip outward, each wrapped in ragged papery brown scales. Recolour the whole crown to spring green with warmer yellow-green in the new growth. Rebuild the fronds as once-pinnate blades — pinnae on BOTH sides of the rachis, shortening toward the tip, each pinna with a curved leading edge rather than a straight-sided triangle, and vary length and spacing. Taper every frond to a fine point; remove the flat chiselled tips. Raise the outer fronds so the crown is a vase/shuttlecock rather than a fan.

rows.readsAs: a frosted Christmas-ornament tree, or a snow-dusted lollipop tree with baubles
rows.defect: The colour is wrong at the root: the foliage is pale ice-white/blue and the trunk is mauve-purple, so nothing reads as a fig. The canopy is another lollipop ball built from small spiky many-pointed star leaves — the mustRead big hand-shaped 3-5 lobed leaf with rounded lobes appears nowhere; these leaves are pointed and tiny, closer to a chrysanthemum. The four fruits are perfect spheres with a hard specular highlight dot, reading as glass Christmas baubles, and they hang out in the foliage away from any branch instead of sitting stalkless at a leaf axil; they are also round, not pear-shaped with a neck. The trunk is a straight-sided bar ending in a rounded capsule bottom that hovers above the ground shadow, with no bark texture and no root flare. Same lollipop template as the Eucalyptus in this batch.
rows.fix: Recolour leaves to mid green with a rough matt surface and the trunk to smooth pale grey. Redraw the leaf as a large palmate blade with 3-5 broad ROUNDED lobes and deep sinuses, sized so 8-12 leaves fill the crown — big leaves are the fig's signature. Break the crown out of the circle: fewer, larger leaves on visible branches with sky between them. Reshape fruit to a pyriform body with a narrow neck and an ostiole dimple at the fat end, kill the specular dot in favour of a soft bloom, ripen green to purple-brown, and anchor each fruit directly against a branch at a leaf axil with no visible stalk. Flare the trunk base into roots meeting the shadow.

rows.readsAs: a purple fern frond with a beaded stalk
rows.defect: The skeleton is right — one poker-straight stem, leaves all the way up, spike on top — but the paint is wrong. The leaves are violet/purple, not mid green, and they carry no pale midrib. They are also set in perfectly regular OPPOSITE pairs at identical intervals, producing a mechanical fishbone; fireweed leaves spiral alternately. The flower spike is a narrow vertical stack of small magenta circles about 12px wide — it reads as a string of beads or a caterpillar rather than a tapering raceme, the individual flowers show no four-petal shape, and it is far too slim next to the 70px-wide leaf zone. There is no bottom-up bloom gradient (all beads are the same colour and size) and no seed pods.
rows.fix: Recolour foliage to mid green with a visible pale midrib and a hint of red at the tips. Change the phyllotaxy to alternate/spiral with a slight rotation and shrinking leaf size up the stem, and break the even spacing. Rebuild the spike three times wider and tapering to a point: individual four-petalled magenta flowers with visible petal gaps and a protruding style, open and larger at the bottom, closing to tight buds at the apex. Add a few long slender split seed pods below the open flowers to sell the bottom-up sequence.

rows.readsAs: an autumn rowan or sumac sprig with one blue flower stuck on top
rows.defect: The leaves are burnt ORANGE-rust, which kills the identification outright — flax must read grey-green and sparse. They are also broad lance blades in perfectly regular opposite pairs marching up the stem, another mechanical fishbone, when the reference calls for small narrow pointed leaves set alternately and THINLY up a very slender wiry stem; the stem here is a thick brown bar, not wiry, and there is only one of it where the mustRead asks for a slender clump. The single flower at the apex is a small blue star with six visible points and a white centre, not a flat five-petal disc, and it is the only bloom in the picture. No round seed capsules appear at all. The plant is also barely 30% of the frame width, so it reads as sparse-by-accident rather than by design.
rows.fix: Recolour foliage to grey-green and cut leaf width by two thirds so they are near-linear; set them alternately with wide irregular gaps so the stem shows through most of its length. Replace the single thick stem with a clump of 4-6 very thin wiry stems of varied height leaning slightly apart. Redraw the flower as a flat five-petal sky-blue disc with faint darker veining, petals overlapping at the base, and put several of them plus a couple of buds across the tops of different stems. Add 2-3 round pea-sized capsules with a small apical point on stems that have already flowered.

rows.readsAs: A yucca or agave clump with a single wheat/barley head planted in the middle of it
rows.defect: The exact thing the row forbids is what got drawn: a single COMPACT golden ear with a dense bristling herringbone of short awns running up a stiff central spike. There is no open panicle, no spreading branchlets, nothing dangling on fine threads. Below it the plant is a dense fountain of ~20 broad, near-WHITE silvery blades (leafColour says light green ripening cream-gold) that are far too wide and too pale for a cereal culm — they read as succulent straps, not grass blades. The whole ear is a hard-edged decal pasted onto the top of one central stem: the yellow spike simply begins where the green stem ends, no sheath, no droop, no flexion. Silhouette is a stiff Y and the base is a solid opaque white wedge where all blades fuse into one mass with no visible individual origins.
rows.fix: Replace the compact spike-with-awns generator with a panicle router: 6-10 alternating branch whorls off the upper culm, each branch a thin curving filament ending in ONE teardrop spikelet that hangs pendulous under gravity, so the harvest silhouette is airy and wider than it is dense. Kill the awn hatching entirely. Cut blade count to 6-9, halve their width, recolour to light green with cream-gold only at the tips, and give each blade its own attachment point on the culm with a wrapping sheath instead of merging them into a white pedestal.

rows.readsAs: A blue-leaved ornamental aster or a cut bouquet of gerbera-like daisies
rows.defect: Leaves are flat blue-violet lozenges stuck onto the stems at hard points — each one is a sharply-tipped slab that meets the stem at a visible hard junction with no taper, no petiole and no midrib, and several float clear of any stem entirely. The colour is wrong in a way that changes the plant: vivid periwinkle/blue-violet where the row asks for dark grey-green leathery foliage, with teal stems. Leaves are scattered singly and in loose pairs; the whorls-of-three mustRead does not read anywhere in the picture. The five flowers are 8-10-petalled flat daisies with a dark centre disc, sitting as isolated singles on bare stem tips — not the five-petal pinwheel, and not the dense terminal head the row requires. Two of three mustReads fail.
rows.fix: Recolour foliage to dark grey-green (desaturate the blue out completely) with a pale midrib line down each blade, and grow each leaf from the stem with a narrowing base rather than butting a lozenge against it. Enforce the whorl: emit leaves in triplets at 120 degrees at each node. Rebuild the flower as five broad overlapping petals with a pinwheel skew and a small pale corona throat, and cluster 5-9 of them into one dome at each shoot tip instead of one lone daisy per wand.

rows.readsAs: A dead thistle head or a dandelion clock on a stick
rows.defect: The trunk is a perfectly straight, parallel-sided orange-brown capsule with rounded ends — a geometric primitive, no taper, no gnarl, no fissure, no root flare, no branching whatsoever. It disappears under the canopy at a hard seam with no crotch or limb structure. The crown is a brown/tan fuzzy cloud with short straw-coloured spikes radiating outward like a burr — it reads DEAD, and there is no grey-green, no silver underside, and no two-tone leaf anywhere. The four olives are perfect circles with identical specular dots, sitting ON the front of the cloud rather than hanging in sprays, and each has a hard outline against the fuzz. All three mustReads (gnarled fissured trunk, two-tone leaf, open airy crown) fail.
rows.fix: Rebuild the trunk with a procedural gnarl: irregular sinuous centreline, variable width, bark fissure striping, a widening root flare at the soil, and 2-3 limbs that split off and carry into the canopy so the crown has visible structure. Replace the radiating straw spikes with narrow lance leaves in opposite pairs, drawn twice — grey-green face and a silver-white flipped subset — and break the crown into 3-5 separated leaf masses with sky gaps between them. Hang the fruit in sprays of 2-4 on visible pedicels, vary the radii, and lose the identical highlight dot.

rows.readsAs: A blue ornamental fountain grass or a liriope clump
rows.defect: There is no bulb. The single most important mustRead — swollen papery bulb sitting on the soil with a fringe of wiry roots — is completely absent; the leaves converge to a thin point at ground level and vanish into a flat shadow ellipse. No roots either. The leaves are flat tapered blades with a visible flat face and highlight ridge, not hollow round tubes, and they splay in a full 360 fountain rather than the flat two-ranked fan the row specifies. Colour is electric periwinkle blue, not waxy blue-green. The flower is a tiny flat white disc, disproportionately small and hovering on a hairline stem far above the foliage — an allium umbel should be a dense spherical head. Silhouette is essentially identical to the Oats and Pampas Herb renders in this same batch.
rows.fix: Add the bulb as the dominant mass: an onion-shaped swollen body at the base, papery cream-brown layered skin with vertical striations, a narrowed neck the leaves emerge from, and a fringe of thin wiry white roots below it. Render leaves as tubes — round the cross-section with a centre highlight running the length and a blunt, not pointed, tip — and restrict them to one flat fan plane, alternating left and right. Desaturate the blue toward grey-green with a waxy bloom. Replace the white disc with a spherical umbel of many small florets.

rows.readsAs: A generic green lollipop tree with orange beads glued on — closer to a persimmon or apricot cartoon than a citrus
rows.defect: The trunk is a literal pill: a flat GREEN parallel-sided capsule with rounded top and bottom, no bark, no taper, no branches, no root flare — and it is the same grey-green as the foliage, so the tree has no woody element at all. It meets the canopy at a hard seam. The crown is a pale grey-mint fog blob with small mint slivers scattered over it; the row asks for dark glossy green, and nothing here is glossy or dark. The white five-petal flowers required by mustRead are entirely absent. The four oranges are perfect circles with a smooth gradient and one identical highlight each — no pitted rind texture, no calyx, no stalk, and they read as pasted-on beads floating in front of the fog rather than hanging among leaves.
rows.fix: Recolour the trunk to grey-brown bark with vertical texture, taper it, flare the base, and split 3-4 branches into the canopy so leaves have something to attach to. Darken and saturate the foliage to deep glossy green with specular streaks along each leaf, and give the leaf its winged petiole so the shape is diagnostic. Add clusters of white five-petal blossoms with yellow stamen centres among the fruit. Give each orange a stippled/pitted rind shader, a small green calyx, and a short pedicel connecting it to a branch, with one or two partly occluded behind leaves.

rows.readsAs: A dried fern frond or a fish skeleton
rows.defect: There are no pods. The defining mustRead — clusters of long bean-like green pods hanging from the stem — is absent, as are the thick fleshy leaves, the vining habit, the aerial roots and the waxy flowers. What is drawn is a single straight rust-ORANGE stick with about twelve pairs of identical rusty chevrons arranged in a perfectly regular ladder up its length, all the same size, all at the same angle. Nothing is green. Nothing climbs or grips anything. The chevrons are flat facets with straight machined edges meeting the stem at a hard V. It is visibly the SAME generator as the Oregano render in this batch — identical stem, identical node spacing, identical paired-leaflet ladder — with only the colour and leaflet outline swapped.
rows.fix: Rebuild from the vanilla reference: a thick green vining stem that leans and curves against implied bark, thick fleshy OBLONG leaves (broad, rounded, waxy — not chevrons) alternating singly along it at irregular intervals, pale aerial roots emerging at the nodes and curling downward, and the harvest as a hanging hand-cluster of 5-8 long slender green pods radiating from one point on the stem. Recolour the whole plant flat mid-green. Break the mechanical node spacing with per-node jitter in spacing, angle and scale.

rows.readsAs: A purple ornamental foliage stalk — Persian shield, coleus, or a stylised feather
rows.defect: Nothing about this reads as oregano. A single unbranched vertical stem carries about eleven pairs of LARGE magenta-purple leaves in a perfectly regular stacked ladder, each pair identical in size and angle, edges overlapping like roof tiles. The row asks for SMALL oval mid-green leaves; these are big, pointed, and violently purple. The stem is a plain dark brown line — no square section, no reddish tone, no hairs. There is no branching, so the airy flat-topped flower spray cannot exist; instead there is a single tiny white smudge at the apex, which is the whole floral contribution. Every mustRead fails. Structurally it is the identical template used for Orchid Pods in this batch.
rows.fix: Branch the plant: 4-6 stems from the base, each forking twice near the top so the flowers can form flat-topped corymbs. Shrink the leaves to roughly a quarter of their current size, round them to true ovals, recolour to greyish mid-green, and space opposite pairs at 90-degree decussate rotation with jittered spacing. Draw the stem square in section with a reddish tint and fine hairs along the edges. Replace the apex smudge with loose sprays of many tiny white-pink florets subtended by dark purple bracts.

rows.readsAs: A fibre-optic lamp or a bound sheaf of straw / a broom
rows.defect: The silver-white feather plume — the single feature that makes pampas grass recognisable — is not present. There is no plume, no seed head, no stalk holding one. The entire render is a fan of ~18 hairline orange-tan WIRES radiating from a solid, flat, opaque orange triangular wedge at the base. The wires have uniform width end to end, no taper, no saw edge, no blade face and no thickness; they are strokes, not leaves. They are also perfectly evenly spaced, giving a machined comb look. The base wedge is a hard-edged geometric triangle with a visible straight-line boundary where the wires terminate into it. Colour is warm orange throughout where the row calls for blue-grey green foliage and a silver-white plume. Both mustReads fail.
rows.fix: Add the plume first — a tall bare culm rising well clear of the clump topped by a large silver-white feathery panicle with soft translucent edges, ideally two or three at varied heights. Convert the wires into real blades: give each width that tapers from a broad base to a fine tip, a centre fold highlight, a fine serrated edge, and a natural arch that droops at the end. Recolour foliage to blue-grey green. Dissolve the solid triangular base into overlapping individual blade bases with jittered spacing and angles so the clump has depth instead of a flat wedge.

rows.readsAs: a dandelion clock / a dandelion seed head on a stick, or a firework burst
rows.defect: The picture is a grey-white airbrushed fluff-ball on a bare pink-brown stick, with ~40 straight white needles radiating out of it like a firework and four small tan cone shapes floating inside the fluff. Not one of the three mustRead marks is present: there are NO finely-cut fern-like leaves (no leaf geometry at all, just a soft smoke blob), NO flat white umbel heads (the white is a diffuse cloud, not a flat-topped disc of tiny florets), and the stem is a single uniform dusty-rose colour with NO purple-red blotching and no hollow/ridged read. The stem is a machined capsule — two perfectly straight parallel edges and a rounded cap — and it meets the fluff at a hard seam with nothing growing out of it: the canopy simply sits on top of the stick. Aspect is also wrong: the row asks 0.6 and this is a narrow ~0.35 lollipop.
rows.fix: Abandon the lollipop-tree template for this herb entirely. Build the stem as a tapering, slightly kinked green tube with irregular dark purple-maroon splotches painted INTO the stem gradient (not overlaid dots), branching into 2-3 side stems. Replace the fluff blob with 3-4 discrete flat-topped umbels: each a compressed disc of radiating thin ray-stalks each ending in a tiny white floret cluster, drawn as geometry not as a blur. Replace the radiating white needles with tripinnate leaf sprays — a triangular leaf outline subdivided three times into fine green segments, attached at a sheathing base that widens into the stem so there is no seam.

rows.readsAs: a symmetrical spruce/Christmas tree, or a young sago palm
rows.defect: A perfectly bilaterally symmetric Christmas-tree: one dead-straight vertical stem with eight opposite pairs of identical palm-fan leaves that shrink in uniform steps toward the tip, plus a terminal fan. It reads as a conifer or a young palm/cycad. The mustRead 'dense green flower clusters bunched at the top' is entirely ABSENT — the top of the plant is just three more leaf fans, no bud/seed-head mass anywhere. The leaflets are smooth lance blades with NO serration on any edge. Every fan attaches to the stem at a single hard point with a visible dark seam and no petiole, so the leaves are stuck on rather than growing out. Nodes are evenly spaced by ruler, and the leaflets in each fan are laid out on a perfect radial protractor. Rendered aspect is roughly 0.7, not the 0.4 the row asks for.
rows.fix: Break the symmetry: alternate the upper nodes (opposite only at the base, per the row), vary node spacing and fan size non-monotonically, and tilt the stem. Give each leaflet a saw-toothed edge and a pale midrib, and taper the leaflet base into a short petiole that fuses into a swollen stem node. Add the missing crown: dense knuckly green bract/flower clusters packed in the upper leaf axils and massed at the apex, with fine hair fuzz — that mass is what identifies this plant. Ridge the stem with vertical striations.

rows.readsAs: a decorative purple houseplant sprig — Tradescantia 'purple heart', or a heraldic wheat motif
rows.defect: A single straight stem with eight mirrored pairs of identical smooth magenta-purple almond ellipses and, at the very top, a small white beaded caterpillar after a bare gap of stem. The colour is wrong — the row wants mid green often purple-flushed, and this is uniformly saturated magenta with no green anywhere, so it does not read as a basil. Two mustReads fail: the leaves have NO teeth (perfect unbroken almond outlines) and the stem shows no square section and no hairs; the third, tiered whorls, is only half-present — the spike is a lumpy white bobble, not tiered whorls of tiny flowers separated by bracts. Every leaf is the exact same size and shape, joined to the stem at a point with a hard dark seam. The flower spike also floats: there is a bare stretch of naked stem between the top leaf pair and the bobble, so the inflorescence looks glued on. Rendered aspect is ~0.3 against the row's 0.8.
rows.fix: Recolour the leaf body to mid green with a purple flush concentrated on the veins and margins. Cut a small toothed scallop into every leaf edge, vary leaf size (larger below, smaller up the stem), and give each pair a short petiole that swells into a node. Make the stem visibly square by shading two faces differently, and add a soft hair rim on the silhouette. Rebuild the spike as 5-7 stacked whorls, each a ring of tiny purple-pink florets above a pair of small bracts, and start the whorls immediately above the top leaf pair so there is no bare gap. Widen the plant with side branches to reach aspect 0.8.

rows.readsAs: an elderberry spray, or a bundle of red-twig dogwood cuttings
rows.defect: A tight bundle of brown twigs rising from a solid brown cone base, hung with small crimson leaves, and topped by four tight BUNCHES of grey-blue berries clustered at the twig tips. That directly contradicts the defining mustRead — berries must be borne SINGLY in the leaf axils, and here they are grape-like clusters of 5-8 sitting at the shoot ends, which is exactly the blueberry/elderberry read the note says to avoid. The 'sharply angled green stems' mustRead also fails: the stems are round, uniformly brown-red and dead straight, with no green and no zig-zag angles. No pink urn-shaped flowers are present anywhere. Berries are flat grey-lavender spheres with a single highlight dot, reading as painted beads rather than fruit. The base is a smooth machined cone with a hard rim where the twigs enter it.
rows.fix: Recolour the young stems to yellow-green and give them a visible zig-zag with sharp angular ridges at each node. Break every berry cluster apart: place single dark purple-red berries one per leaf axil, spaced down the shoot, each with a small calyx dimple at the tip. Add a few pink-white urn-shaped nodding flowers on the lower shoots. Let the leaves be mid green with only some crimson tips rather than uniformly red, and dissolve the cone base into splayed woody stems and litter.

rows.readsAs: a speckled bird's egg, or a microscope slide of blood cells
rows.defect: A near-perfect pale blue-grey ELLIPSE, centred and symmetrical, with an airbrushed vignette darkening at the rim and salmon/red circular dots scattered across it. All three mustReads fail. The colour is pink-salmon on white, not the golden-brown/olive-tan/amber the row specifies — nothing here is brown or gold. There are NO stringy mucilage strands trailing anywhere; the bottom edge of the ellipse is a clean geometric arc with nothing hanging from it. And there is no read of 'the underside of ice' at all — no ice mass, no brine channels, no direction, no up or down. The dots are perfect circles of uniform size stamped on top of the surface, which is the textbook 'pattern sprayed on' failure: the speckling does not belong to the surface, it sits above it.
rows.fix: Shift the whole palette to golden-brown, olive-tan and deep amber. Replace the free-floating ellipse with an actual ice slab: an irregular pale blue-white mass filling the top of the frame with a ragged lower edge, dark water below. Paint the algae as staining that follows the brine-channel network — branching, uneven, denser in the channels, bleeding into the ice rather than sitting on it. Hang irregular tapering mucilage strands of varying length from the ragged edge, drifting sideways in current. Kill the perfect circles: use irregular blotches at multiple scales.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon lollipop tree, or a green dandelion clock
rows.defect: The same lollipop template as Hemlock and Jackfruit in this batch: a flat olive-tan capsule trunk with two perfectly straight parallel sides and a rounded cap, meeting a soft airbrushed pale-green cloud at a hard horizontal seam — nothing branches, the canopy just balances on the post. The feathery pinnate sprays are present, which is good, but they radiate straight OUTWARD from the blob like pincushion spines rather than arching or DROOPING, so the 'drooping twigs' half of the mustRead fails. The fruit reads wrong too: instead of pale green globes sitting almost stalkless spaced ALONG the branches, there are three tight grape-bunch clumps of 4-6 small yellow dots floating in the canopy with no branch under them. The globes have no vertical ridging and no translucency — they are flat mustard circles.
rows.fix: Replace the capsule trunk with a tapering trunk that forks into 3-4 main limbs which continue up into the canopy, so foliage grows out of visible wood instead of resting on a post. Re-aim the sprays downward and outward with a curve so they hang, and thin the airbrushed cloud so the individual sprays carry the canopy silhouette. Break the fruit clumps up: single pale translucent green globes pressed one per node in a row along the drooping twigs, each with faint vertical ridge lines and a bright rim highlight to sell translucency.

rows.readsAs: a spray of white daisies, or an edelweiss garland
rows.defect: An S-curved olive stem carrying six WHITE fans of narrow petals, plus a few tiny dark curled rings on the stem. This is not recognisable as ivy by any mark. The colour is inverted — the row demands very dark glossy green with pale grey-green veins, and the foliage here is cream-white. The lobed leaf is completely absent: there is no 3-5 lobed triangular leaf anywhere, only radial petal fans, and consequently no pale vein network. The spherical black-berry umbels are absent. The clinging rootlet mats are reduced to about eight small dark curls that read as snail shells or wire clips rather than dense brown fibrous pads, and there is no surface for the vine to be clinging TO — it floats in space, which kills the whole climber read. The fans are also the same primitive used on Hemp in this batch, just recoloured, so the two pictures share an obvious family shape.
rows.fix: Throw out the fan primitive here. Draw actual ivy leaves: a palmate outline with 3-5 triangular lobes and a heart-shaped base, filled very dark green with a glossy specular sheen, and a pale grey-green vein network running lobe-to-lobe drawn as part of the leaf, not on top. Alternate them along the stem on distinct petioles. Add a wall/bark plane behind so the vine has something to grip, and give the stem a continuous dense mat of short brown rootlets on the contact side. On the upper shoots switch to unlobed diamond leaves and add 2-3 spherical umbels of green-black berries on radiating stalks.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon tree with three pumpkins or pomegranates sitting in it
rows.defect: The lollipop template again — a flat sage-green capsule trunk with straight parallel sides, cut off by a hard horizontal seam under a pale grey-green airbrushed cloud with small white lance leaves stuck around its rim. The single most important mustRead is violated: the fruit does NOT hang off the trunk or main limbs. Three small brown-orange ribbed balls sit up IN THE CANOPY, and they are round and pumpkin-sized relative to the leaves rather than an enormous knobbly oblong barrel. Their surface is smooth vertical ribbing like a pumpkin, not the dense hexagonal spiny bumps of a jackfruit. The 'dense dark glossy crown' also fails — the crown is a pale, washed-out, desaturated blur and the leaves are near-white, not dark glossy green. No milky sap is indicated at any point. Nothing about the picture reads tropical or heavy.
rows.fix: Move every fruit onto the trunk and lowest limbs, attached by a short thick stalk that visibly bends the wood under the weight, and make them large — a third of the trunk height — and oblong/barrel-shaped, not spherical. Cover them in tight hexagonal knobbly bumps, dull yellow-green, with irregular dents. Recolour the crown to dark saturated glossy green with hard specular highlights on individual large leathery oval leaves, and let the leaves define the crown silhouette instead of a blur. Replace the capsule trunk with a tapering grey-brown trunk with visible bark, forking into heavy limbs, plus a white sap bead or two at a fruit stalk.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon orange or apple tree
rows.defect: The fruits are three perfectly round yellow-orange balls with a plain radial highlight — there is no pear taper anywhere in the picture, which is the one thing the row demands. No blossom of any kind (no white five-petalled flowers, no dark anthers). The crown is a wide, squat green fog-blob wider than it is tall, the opposite of the 'upright narrow oval crown, taller than an apple tree' called for. The trunk is a flat mid-green capsule of constant width with rounded ends — a lollipop stick — with no taper, no root flare and no bark; where it enters the crown it simply vanishes into the fog rather than dividing into branches, and the only 'branches' are a few dark hairline scratches painted over the blur. The ~40 leaves are all the same almond stamp at random angles, floating free in the haze with nothing connecting them to a twig.
rows.fix: Replace the ball fruit primitive with a true pyriform silhouette — narrow shoulder swelling to a fat base, with a long stalk hanging off a twig rather than pinned into the canopy fog. Rebuild the trunk as a tapered woody form with a flared base and 3-5 real forking limbs whose tips are the anchor points every leaf and fruit attaches to. Compress the crown horizontally and stretch it vertically to a narrow upright oval. Add white five-petal blossom clusters with dark anther dots.

rows.readsAs: an alien blue-grey tree with oranges on it — indistinguishable in kind from the Pear in this same batch
rows.defect: This is pixel-for-pixel the same tree template as Pear with a colour swap — same constant-width capsule trunk, same squat blob crown, same scattered almond-leaf stamps, same round fruit balls. Specific misses: the trunk is a flat slate-blue slab with zero texture, so the 'dark blocky checkered bark' mustRead is entirely absent; the fruit are plain orange spheres with no four-lobed green calyx cap at all; the tree is fully leafed rather than the classic bare-branch look, and the leaves are pale ice-blue-grey, not dark glossy green nor blazing orange. Two of the three fruits are half-buried inside the leaf mass instead of hanging clear on branch tips.
rows.fix: Give the trunk a rectangular-plate cracked bark texture in near-black brown. Strip the canopy to bare grey branches (or a sparse remnant of orange leaves) so the fruit hangs exposed. Add a stiff four-lobed green star calyx sitting on the shoulder of each fruit with a short stalk above it. Recolour any remaining leaves dark green/orange — the blue-grey leaf makes it read as an alien plant.

rows.readsAs: a golden scallop shell, or a segmented pumpkin — nobody would say plant, let alone water plant
rows.defect: The picture is a huge fan of about eight overlapping golden-yellow spheres filling the bottom two-thirds of the frame, each a smooth shaded ball with a perfect circular outline and a specular hotspot, cut by two straight ruled lines. Above it a single hairline stalk rises with a tiny blue bead-string on it. Nothing here is aquatic: no water line, no wet surface, no emergent stalks. There is no heart-shaped or arrow-shaped leaf blade anywhere — the 'leaves' are geometric spheres. The flower spike is a stack of ~10 identical small blue circles the size of a fingernail, nowhere near a dense violet-blue spike, and it sits far above rather than just above a leaf. Colour is completely wrong: brilliant gold instead of dark glossy green. Every element is a machined primitive with hard-edged arcs.
rows.fix: Discard the sphere-fan entirely. Build 3-4 thick cordate blades — broad rounded lobes at the base narrowing to a blunt point — each on its own long upright petiole rising out of a rippled waterline drawn across the lower third. Colour dark glossy green with a wet sheen. Rebuild the flower spike as a dense cylindrical mass of many small overlapping violet-blue tubular florets, wider than the stalk, terminating just above the tallest leaf.

rows.readsAs: a dark clump of dead grass or bracken
rows.defect: The render is so dark and so small it barely separates from the background — it occupies maybe a quarter of the frame and the darkest stems are near-black against near-black. The structure is a bundle of perfectly straight dark-olive rods fanning out from one point like chopsticks in a pot, with no woody taper or branching, and every rod ends bluntly in mid-air. The 'leaves' are pale grey comb rows — a straight midrib with ~12 identical short tick-marks at right angles — which reads as pinnate/fern or a fishbone, not the required trifoliate three-lance-leaflet arrangement. There are zero yellow red-streaked pea flowers and zero pods, so two of the three mustReads are entirely missing. The comb-leaves also float beside the stems rather than joining them at a node.
rows.fix: Raise overall brightness and scale the plant to fill the frame.
