Replace the pinnate comb stamp with true trifoliate units — three narrow lance leaflets on a short common petiole, mid one on a longer stalklet, grey-green above with a paler downy underside where they twist. Attach each petiole at a visible node on a stem that tapers and branches. Add clusters of yellow standard-petal pea flowers with red-brown streaking, and flattened green pods with visible seed bumps and a hairy edge.

rows.readsAs: a dandelion seedhead or an exploding firework on a stick
rows.defect: The crown is a round yellow-olive pom-pom of glow with dozens of straight pale-yellow lines radiating outward from its centre like a firework burst — that is a sphere, not the 'broad umbrella crown' the row and the note both insist on, and the note explicitly warns against the wrong crown shape. The needles are single ruled straight strokes emanating from one central point; there are no bundles, no sheaths at the base, no two-to-five grouping. The trunk is the same flat ochre capsule primitive used on Pear and Persimmon — uniform width, rounded pill ends, no bark, no reddish plating, and it terminates inside the fog with no branch structure. The three cones are small brown ribbed teardrops pinned onto the outside of the blur, not stout rounded cones sitting on branches, and one is clipped by the crown edge.
rows.fix: Flatten the crown into a wide, shallow parasol — a broad horizontal mass sitting on top of clear bare trunk, with a few thick limbs visibly spreading outward and upward to carry it. Draw needles as short fascicle tufts, 2-5 lines emerging from a common brown sheath at a twig tip, not lines from the crown centre. Give the trunk orange-red plated bark and a taper. Make the cones fat, blunt-topped and woody, seated on a branch.

rows.readsAs: a pineapple — recognisable, but the netted texture also invites 'a decorative gourd'
rows.defect: The fruit body reads as a pineapple, but it is defeated by a machine-perfect crosshatch: a flawless diamond lattice of ruled straight lines laid over a smooth gold ovoid, identical cell to cell, with no relief, no individual fruitlet bumps, no bracts and no shadow — the pattern is sprayed on top rather than being the fruit's own skin. The crown tuft is a bundle of straight flat blades all converging to a single point, reading as a paintbrush, and it meets the fruit at a hard flat line with no visible socket. Worse, the fruit has no stalk: it simply rests on the ground rosette, so it looks stuck on rather than growing out. The rosette leaves are flat rounded green noodles of constant width with blunt tips, lying almost horizontally — no stiff sword taper, no spiny margins, no red edge flush, and none of them is more than half the fruit's height.
rows.fix: Replace the ruled lattice with individual raised hexagonal fruitlets — each with its own shading, a small bract scale and a dry fibrous tip — so the pattern has depth and slight irregularity. Give the fruit a short stout stalk continuous with the rosette centre. Rebuild the rosette leaves as long stiff swords that taper to sharp points and arch upward before curving down, with sawtooth marginal spines and grey-green tone flushed red at the edge. Fan the crown tuft outward with individually curled leaves rather than a converging brush.

rows.readsAs: the same firework-on-a-stick as Pine Nuts in this batch, in a different colour
rows.defect: This is the Pine Nuts render recoloured pale sage — same round pom-pom crown, same firework of long straight radiating needle lines, same flat capsule trunk, same two brown teardrop cones stuck on the fog. That directly contradicts the row and its note: needles are LONG straight spikes when they must be short and blunt in pairs, the crown is a tall floating ball when it must be a low wide rounded bush, and the trunk is a perfectly straight pill with no taper when it must be crooked. The trunk also has no bark and no branches; it just enters the glow and stops. The cones are pointed teardrops with fine ribbing, not squat eggs with thick blunt scales, and no nuts are visible in them.
rows.fix: Shorten the tree, widen and lower the crown so it sits close to the ground and is broader than tall, and give the trunk a visible bend plus a couple of gnarled forking limbs breaking the silhouette. Cut needle length by two-thirds and draw them in tight paired tufts densely clothing stubby twig ends rather than as rays from a centre. Redraw the cones squat, near-spherical, with thick rounded scale plates and fat brown seeds showing between open scales. Differentiate the palette from Pine Nuts.

rows.readsAs: a champagne flute or a pink cocktail glass
rows.defect: What is on screen is a champagne flute. One smooth magenta-pink cone, widest at the top and narrowing to a point, sits on a bare dark-brown stick of uniform width, capped by a flat cream ellipse — a perfect geometric ellipse used as the mouth. There is no hood arching over the mouth (mustRead missing), no red vein network on the throat (mustRead missing), and the tube does not flare at the top, it just ends. There is a hard seam where the pink cone meets the brown stick — the pitcher is stuck onto a stem rather than being a rolled leaf that rises from a ground rosette. Colour is wrong: flat magenta rather than yellow-green with crimson veining. Only one pitcher exists, with no clump, no ground-level base and no separate flower stalk.
rows.fix: Build a clump of 3-4 trumpets rising directly out of a low ground rosette, each swelling from a narrow base to a flared mouth. Give each an operculum hood arching over and partly shading the open mouth, with the mouth drawn as a rolled ellipse in perspective, not a flat disc. Repaint the surface yellow-green with a dense crimson vein reticulation that intensifies toward the mouth and hood. Add one separate tall bare scape carrying a single nodding umbrella flower so the flower is not confused with the traps.

rows.readsAs: three slices of raw tuna or three red rubber pads on a blue plate, with a tiny white flower as garnish — sushi, not a plant
rows.defect: Not a plant at all in the pixels: three flat red-pink lozenges the colour of raw tuna sit overlapping on a dark blue-grey ellipse, with one tiny white six-point star flower perched on the middle one. Nothing else is on the canvas — no stalk of any kind, no rhizome chain, no holes. All three mustReads fail: (a) the round dish leaf is not held high on a prickly stalk, it is a red pad lying flat, and lotus pads are never red; (b) there is no sausage-linked pale rhizome anywhere; (c) no ring of cut-root holes. The blue ellipse behind the pads is a hard-edged perfect ellipse with a thin outline stroke — a geometric primitive reading as a serving dish, and the pads sit ON it with a visible seam rather than floating in water.
rows.fix: Recolour the pads to blue-grey green (#7d9b82) with a paler waxy bloom and a radial vein fan from the central petiole attachment, and give at least one pad an upturned bowl edge. Kill the outlined ellipse primitive — replace with a soft dark water plane with no stroke and a wet reflection under each pad. Then add the actual harvest, which is currently absent: a horizontal chain of 3-4 fat pale-tan rhizome segments pulled from mud along the lower third, each segment pinched at the joints, with one segment cut to show the ring of 8-10 round holes. Raise one leaf on a visible speckled stalk out of the water so the plant is not all at one height.

rows.readsAs: a green lollipop or a cartoon palm sapling with red flowers stuck to it — could not be called a fruit tree, let alone a lychee
rows.defect: A flat green capsule for a trunk — literally a rounded rectangle with parallel straight sides and a semicircular cap top and bottom, no taper, no root flare, no bark. It is the classic lollipop-stick primitive. Where it enters the crown there is a hard seam: the capsule's outline just disappears under a soft green fog blob, nothing branches out of it. The crown is a glowing mint-green cloud with feathery pinnate fronds scattered on top of it like confetti; the fronds float free and none of them connect to a branch. Fruit are four flat rosettes of red dots that read as poinsettias or scab clusters, not as round pebbled-rind lychees, and they are pasted flat on the fog rather than hanging in drooping sprays. The dense rounded DARK crown mustRead fails — this crown is pale luminous mint, not dark glossy green.
rows.fix: Replace the capsule with a tapered trunk that flares at the base and forks into 3-4 boughs that carry the crown, so leaves grow out of wood instead of out of fog. Kill the glow-cloud fill; build the crown from overlapping dark green (#1d3a24) leaf masses with grey-green undersides showing on the drooping edge. Make the fruit spherical with a terminal-hang: 3-5 fruit per pendant spray on a common wiry rachis, radius ~14px, strawberry-red, with a fine tubercled bump texture on the sphere itself (not dots painted on a flat disc) and a shaded underside.

rows.readsAs: a purple sea fan / gorgonian coral, or a decorative purple palm — nobody would say fern, and certainly not maidenhair
rows.defect: The whole thing is VIOLET-PURPLE. Not a hint of green anywhere. Every mustRead fails: the stems are thick purple midribs, not glossy wiry jet-black wires; the leaflets are hard sawtooth triangles cut straight off the midrib like a comb or a fish bone, not fan-shaped wedges with scalloped outer edges; and the mass is a dense overlapping shuttlecock fan, the exact silhouette the reference explicitly forbids, rather than an airy open lacy spray with dark space between the sprigs. The fronds all converge to a single dark wedge at the bottom with a hard machined V edge — the fronds are stuck INTO that wedge, not growing from a crown of rhizome and scales. The sawtooth pinnae are also perfectly repeated in size and angle, which reads as a stamped pattern rather than growth.
rows.fix: Recolour: stems to near-black (#0d0b10) with a hard specular wire highlight along one side, blades to fresh apple-green (#8ec95f). Replace the sawtooth comb pinnae with individual wedge leaflets — wider at the free edge than at the stalk, outer edge scalloped into 4-6 shallow lobes, each on its own hair-thin black stalklet so black gaps show between neighbouring leaflets. Cut leaflet density by roughly half and randomise spacing so the spray is open and lacy; break the single fan into 3-4 arching fronds that branch dichotomously. Replace the hard basal wedge with a small tufted rootstock of brown scales.

rows.readsAs: a generic cartoon orange tree — the round orange balls say citrus, not mango; and it is the same picture as Lychee with the colours swapped
rows.defect: Same lollipop primitive as Lychee: an olive capsule trunk with dead-straight parallel sides and a rounded cap, no taper or flare, meeting the crown at a hard seam where its outline is simply swallowed by a pale fog blob. The crown is a luminous pale sage cloud, not a dense DARK dome, and the leaves are small pale sage slivers sprinkled on top of the fog with no branch structure behind them and no drooping whorls — they point in random directions including upward. The fruit fail outright: four perfectly round orange balls with a single specular dot, evenly spaced, sitting flat on the crown with no stalk at all. The mustRead 'fruit dangling on long wiry stalks' is entirely absent, and 'kidney-shaped' has become a geometric circle.
rows.fix: Give the trunk taper and a buttressed base, and fork it into boughs that carry the leaf mass. Darken the crown to a deep glossy green (#1a3319) with a few red-bronze new-growth flushes at the shoot tips, and hang the leaves — long lance blades, 4-5x longer than wide, all angled downward in whorls at branch ends. Redraw the fruit as an asymmetric kidney/ovoid with a beaked shoulder, green flushed red-yellow with a soft gradient, each on a long thin pendulous stalk 40-60px that visibly leaves a branch and lets the fruit swing clear of the foliage.

rows.readsAs: a generic tree with plums or dark grapes on it — the missing green star cap means no one would name mangosteen; it is also almost pixel-for-pixel the Mangrove Leaves card
rows.defect: Identical template again — an ochre capsule trunk, straight-sided rounded rectangle, hard seam into a yellow-green glow cloud. The crown is a wide ROUND ball, not the 'dense narrow conical crown' the reference demands. Leaves are small yellow-green lance slivers scattered on the fog, alternate and random-angled, not large thick leathery ellipses in OPPOSITE PAIRS, and there is no parallel venation. The purple fruit are there and are the one thing that lands, but they are flat circles with a smooth airbrushed highlight and only a tiny brown nub on top — the four-lobed green star calyx cap, which is the single most identifying feature of a mangosteen, is missing on all four. Foliage colour is also wrong: yellow-green and glowing, where the reference calls for very dark glossy green.
rows.fix: Add the calyx: four fleshy green lobes splayed over the top of every fruit, plus the woody stalk, drawn so the lobes overlap the fruit's shoulder in perspective. Rebuild leaves as large opposite pairs — two blades emerging at the same node on either side of a twig, 3x longer than wide, thick-edged, with 8-10 fine parallel side veins; darken to #16301c with a yellow-green underside on the flipped ones. Narrow and heighten the crown into a cone. Replace the capsule with a tapered trunk forking into boughs. Give the fruit a matte thick-rind shading with a broad soft terminator instead of the single glossy dot.

rows.readsAs: a generic yellow-green shrub-tree; without the stilt roots it is indistinguishable from the Mangosteen card minus the purple fruit
rows.defect: The defining feature of a mangrove is simply not drawn: there are NO stilt roots. The trunk is a single ochre capsule that runs straight down into a flat elliptical ground shadow — no arching prop roots, no water, no lifted trunk. That is a mustRead missing outright. The propagules also fail: instead of long pencil/cigar seedlings hanging vertically, there are three or four short dark-brown slivers roughly the same length as the leaves, lying at random angles inside the crown (two are nearly horizontal), so they read as dead leaves or debris, not as seedlings. Leaves are scattered singly on a yellow-green glow blob, not thick glossy pairs bunched at branch tips, and there are no visible branch tips for them to bunch at. No flowers. The crown fog has visible circular soft blobs in it that read as lens bokeh rather than foliage.
rows.fix: Draw the stilt roots — 6-10 arching legs springing from the trunk at 1/3 and 2/3 height, curving out and down to enter a water line, crossing each other, thinning toward the tips; lift the trunk base clear of that water line and add a reflection. Make the propagules 3-4x longer, uniformly pendulous (straight down, slight sway), pale green with a darker tip, hanging BELOW the leaf clusters where they are silhouetted against the dark. Group leaves into terminal rosettes of 4-6 opposite pairs at the end of each visible twig, thicken them, and add a specular sheen band on the upper surface plus a pale yellow-green flipped underside on one or two. Scatter small pale-yellow flower clusters at the same nodes. Remove the bokeh circles from the crown.

rows.readsAs: a glowing green cannabis bush on a stick — the spiky star leaves and total absence of a tap or bucket mean nobody would say maple, let alone maple sap
rows.defect: The harvest is missing entirely — no spile, no bucket, nothing on the trunk. That is one of three mustReads gone, and it is the one that makes the card 'Maple Sap' rather than 'Maple'. The trunk is the same flat green capsule primitive: parallel straight sides, rounded cap, no bark texture, no taper, hard seam where it vanishes into the mint-green fog crown, and no opposite branching visible anywhere. The leaves are not maple leaves: each is a spiky star of 7-9 narrow pointed spikes radiating from a point, which reads as cannabis or a chestnut palmate, not five broad smooth-sided lobes with deep U notches and a broad basal lobe. Colour is uniform glowing mint with no mid-green body and no flame orange-red. And there are the same stray dark cigar slivers floating in the crown as on the Mangrove card — leftover propagule geometry on a maple, an off-body artifact.
rows.fix: Add the spile and bucket: a metal tap driven into the trunk about 100px up, a galvanised pail hanging from it, and a bright sap drip/streak on the bark below the tap — this is the identity of the card. Redraw the leaf as a true palmate: five lobes, the middle three long, sides shorter, smooth (not toothed) lobe margins, deep narrow sinuses between them, wider than tall, with a red petiole. Make the leaves paired opposite along each twig. Replace the capsule with a taper-and-fork trunk in grey furrowed bark, opposite branching. Shift the crown to mid green with a graded flame orange-red on the sunlit outer edge. Delete the dark cigar slivers.

rows.readsAs: a bundle of dry twigs, a besom broom or a dead shrub in winter — with tiny pink buds it might pass for a bare cherry sapling; sea lavender is not readable at all
rows.defect: It is a bundle of bare dead sticks. Perfectly straight ochre-brown rods, each one a hard-edged line of constant width, radiating up from a slightly wider bundle at the base, with short straight spurs stuck on at regular angles like thorns. All three mustReads fail: there is NO basal rosette — nothing at ground level but the bundle's cut ends; the flower stems do not fan out level on top, they splay upward in a V so the outline is a vase/broom, not the flat table-top of a sea lavender; and the florets are about eight tiny pale-pink tick marks perched on the stem tips, nowhere near a dense mist of blue-violet, and pink rather than violet. The colour of the whole plant is dead brown with no green anywhere. The side spurs meet the main stems at hard T-junctions with a visible overlap seam — stuck on, not branched out.
rows.fix: Build the rosette first: 7-10 spoon-shaped basal leaves lying flat on the ground, broad rounded tip narrowing to a long stalk, dull dark green with bronze/salt-crusted edges, drawn in near-plan view as a flat disc of foliage. From its centre send up 3-5 wiry stems that are slightly bowed and taper, branching by dichotomous forks at shallow angles (not right-angle spurs) so all the tips arrive at nearly the same height — flatten the top of the mass into a level corymb. Then replace the pink ticks with a dense haze of a hundred-plus 2-3px papery florets in blue-violet (#7b6bc4) with paler dry calyces, packed thickly enough along the upper branchlets to read as a mist. Warm the stem colour slightly toward olive-brown and vary the widths.

rows.readsAs: A red bottlebrush or a Celosia 'plume' cockscomb - most people would say 'some kind of red feather-plant', nobody would say monkshood
rows.defect: The picture is a single vertical stick carrying ~14 pairs of long hot-pink/scarlet pointed blades in a strict herringbone, ending in three or four tiny violet dots the size of a pinhead at the very tip. None of the three mustReads are present: there is no hooded flower anywhere (the violet specks are unshaped dots, no helmet over anything), the leaves are neither dark, glossy, green nor palmately cut - they are flat coral-pink lance blades, and the 'flower spike' is actually the LEAF column. Colour is inverted from the reference (foliage should be dark green, flowers deep blue-purple; here foliage is pink and the flowers are nearly invisible). Every blade is a mirrored copy of one shape rotated a fixed angle, and each meets the stem at a hard flat butt-end - a visible seam, not a growing petiole. Silhouette is a symmetrical bottlebrush cylinder.
rows.fix: Rebuild as two distinct organs. (1) Foliage: dark glossy green (#1d3a22-#2a5230), basal and mid-stem, each leaf palmately split into 5 narrow toothed segments radiating from a common petiole junction - kill the pink entirely. (2) Flowers: replace the pinhead dots with 10-14 deep blue-violet (#3b2f8f) flowers ranked up the top third of the stem, each drawn as a large arched hood/helmet overhanging two small lower petals, the hood at least 8-10% of image height so it reads. Stagger flower spacing and vary hood tilt; taper the spike so the top buds are smaller. Attach leaves with a curved petiole that widens into the stem instead of a flat butt.

rows.readsAs: A dead winter shrub someone tied pink plastic pine needles onto - or a barberry twig with berries; nothing about it says a green leafless Ephedra
rows.defect: The plant is a fan of BROWN woody twigs with bright magenta/violet straight sticks laid across them at fixed angles, plus five clusters of small orange-brown spheres. mustRead 'upright broom of bare GREEN jointed stems' fails outright - there is no green pixel in the image; the main stems are dead-brown and the only saturated colour is magenta. mustRead 'swollen nodes with a paper collar of scales' fails - the stem joints are unmarked, no swelling and no collar. mustRead 'no foliage at all' also fails in effect, because the magenta sticks read exactly as needles/foliage. The magenta pieces are perfectly straight machined line segments of uniform width that terminate in flat cut ends and simply cross over the brown stems with a hard overlap seam - they are stuck ON, not growing OUT. The berry clusters are perfect circles of identical radius.
rows.fix: Recolour the stems yellow-green to olive (#8f9b45-#6f8a3a) and delete the magenta sticks entirely - this species has no leaves. Build the broom from 12-20 slightly flexing rush-like rods rising from a common base, each rod visibly segmented every ~25px by a slightly SWOLLEN node with a small brown papery collar of two opposite scales at each node. Give the rods a subtle longitudinal ridge/stripe. Replace the sphere clusters with small pale papery cones (elongated, layered scales, straw colour) sitting in the node axils, not spherical berries.

rows.readsAs: A silver-leaved ornamental such as Russian olive or a dusty-miller with blue fruit; it also sits on the exact same skeleton as Mountain Cranberry in this batch, only recoloured
rows.defect: Leaves are silvery WHITE with a metallic sheen, not 'mid green' - the leafColour row is contradicted on every leaf. The berries are not carried singly in the leaf axils; they are gathered into four tight grape-like bunches of 5-7 balls at the shoot tips, and they have no pale bloom - they are glossy with a specular highlight. Leaf margins are perfectly smooth, so 'finely toothed' fails, and there is no hint of red autumn colour. The habit is a tall upright vase spray, not a 'low compact bush' - it stands ~1.6x taller than wide. Leaves are one repeated pointed-oval stamp attached at a hard flat angle along each cane; the canes emerge from a flat olive-green cone base that meets the stems with a visible straight seam.
rows.fix: Recolour foliage to mid green (#3e6b34) with a warm scarlet variant for the autumn state; keep the highlight subtle and matte, not chrome. Break the berry bunches apart: place berries SINGLY, one per leaf axil, dusty blue-purple (#4b5b8a) with a soft matte powder bloom - kill the specular dot. Squash the whole plant so it is at most as tall as wide, with shorter, wirier, visibly ANGLED (zig-zag) green twigs rather than long smooth canes. Add fine teeth to the leaf margin and vary leaf size/rotation. Blend the base into the soil rather than ending in a hard-edged cone.

rows.readsAs: An aquarium plant - Anacharis or a plastic fish-tank fern with red beads; the cyan makes it read as underwater, not alpine heath
rows.defect: Foliage is bright turquoise/CYAN, which contradicts 'dark glossy green' so hard it stops reading as a land plant. mustRead 'low evergreen creeping MAT' fails - this is an upright vase-shaped spray, clearly taller than wide, when the row asks for aspect 1.5 (wider than tall). Leaves are flat pointed ovals with straight smooth margins and no rolled-under edge, no notched tip, no dark dotting. The berry clusters are three small bunches of perfect red circles, and they are not nodding at the stem ends - two of them sit mid-cane. The plant is the SAME repeated leaf stamp on the same repeated cane array as Mountain Blueberry above, and each leaf meets its cane at a hard flat butt with no petiole.
rows.fix: Recolour to a deep glossy green (#1f4a2c) with a waxy highlight along the leaf midline only. Flatten the whole habit: spread it into a low mat wider than tall, with stems that run horizontally and turn up only at the tips. Redraw leaves small, thick and leathery, with edges rolled visibly under (a darker rim) and a distinct NOTCH at the rounded tip, plus fine dark dots on the shaded undersides. Move all berries to tight nodding clusters at the shoot TIPS only, scarlet, with a slight pear shape and a small dark calyx dimple instead of perfect circles.

rows.readsAs: A purple fern frond or an ornamental grass seed-head - nothing in it says mint, since the square stem, corymbs and bracts are all missing
rows.defect: A single unbranched stem with 11 pairs of PURPLE lance leaves in rigid herringbone, topped by a narrow vertical string of small white beads. mustRead 'square BRANCHING stems' fails - there is exactly one stem and zero branches. mustRead 'flat domed clusters of tiny white flowers' fails - the flowers are a thin vertical bead-chain, the opposite of a flat-topped corymb, and there are no purple speckles. mustRead 'pale silvery bracts under each flower head' is entirely absent. Leaf colour is violet, not mid green with whitish dusting. The bead chain is a stack of identical circles on a straight line; the leaves are one mirrored stamp with flat cut bases meeting the stem at a visible seam.
rows.fix: Branch the stem 2-3 times in opposite pairs so it forms a candelabra, and make the stem visibly square (two-tone shading on the flat faces, a fine edge line down each corner). Recolour leaves mid green, and dust the topmost pairs and the bracts with silvery white. Replace the bead chain with 3-5 FLAT-TOPPED domed heads, each a disc of 20+ tiny white lipped florets speckled with fine purple dots, and set a rosette of pale silvery-white bracts fanning out beneath each head. Vary leaf length down the stem instead of a constant stamp.

rows.readsAs: A purple palm tree or a cycad in a stylised game-asset style; the Y post plus feather crown says 'palm', not papaya
rows.defect: A flat grey-brown Y-shaped post with capsule-rounded ends carries a huge PURPLE feather-frond crown and one yellow ball wedged in the fork. The crown is pinnate (feather-shaped fronds with comb teeth along a central rachis), not 'deeply lobed PALMATE leaves' - it reads as a palm/cycad, the wrong leaf architecture. mustRead 'slim scarred trunk with a SMALL tuft crown' fails twice: the trunk is a thick flat slab with zero leaf scars, and the crown is enormous, roughly 3x the trunk width and about 40% of the whole image. mustRead 'small ribbed yellow fruit CLUSTERED on the stem' fails - there is exactly one fruit, and it is a near-perfect sphere with ribs painted on rather than a five-angled body. The trunk is a flat untextured fill with hard straight sides and no join to the crown - the fronds simply overlap the top of the post.
rows.fix: Recolour the crown mid green. Rebuild the leaves as palmate: a long stalk ending in a single blade cut into 5-7 deep lobes radiating from one point, each lobe itself notched - no central rachis, no comb teeth. Shrink the crown to a small tuft of 6-8 such leaves and lengthen/slim the trunk so it holds a 0.6 aspect. Cover the trunk in staggered crescent LEAF SCARS and give it bark tone variation, curvature and a flared base instead of a flat capsule-ended slab; drop the Y fork (papaya is single-stemmed). Replace the single sphere with a cluster of 5-8 small fruits hugging the trunk under the crown, each with five visible flat FACES meeting at ridges, so the cross-section reads pentagonal.

rows.readsAs: A brain coral, or a cluster of green balloons/succulent bubbles - a viewer would guess 'coral' or 'fungus' before 'alpine herb'
rows.defect: The body of the plant is a fan of about ten enormous overlapping INFLATED spheres in mint green, each shaded as a 3D ball with a bright specular highlight, packed into a brain-like dome that fills the lower two thirds of the frame. They do not read as leaves at all - they are balloons, and the thin dividing lines between them look like seams in a moulded object. mustRead 'kidney-shaped succulent basal leaves' fails (no kidney notch, no flat blade), mustRead 'red leaf stalks' fails completely (there is one thin GREEN stalk and no petioles are visible at all), and mustRead 'cluster of flat winged crimson seeds' fails - the seed spire is a narrow vertical chain of ~10 identical orange beads, round not flat, and unwinged. Scale is also wrong: the leaf mass dwarfs the seed spike, which is a thread by comparison.
rows.fix: Flatten the leaves: draw each as a thin kidney-shaped BLADE seen at an angle, with a clear basal notch, a slightly wavy margin and visible palmate veining, overlapping loosely with dark gaps between them rather than fusing into a solid dome. Cut the specular ball shading down to a soft sheen. Give every leaf its own long RED petiole running back to a common crown at the base, and let some petioles show through the gaps. Rebuild the seed head as a branched spire of flat, disc-shaped papery winged fruits - round translucent crimson discs seen edge-on and face-on at varying angles - and enlarge it to about a third of the plant height.

rows.readsAs: A stylised arrow or a wheat/barley pictogram with a flower on top - it reads as a diagram, not a plant, and certainly not a creeping thyme
rows.defect: A single straight grey vertical rod with eight purple V-chevrons crossing it and one lone pink daisy at the top. mustRead 'low creeping mat, WIDER than tall' fails completely - the plant is roughly 4x taller than wide, the exact inverse of the required 2.0 aspect. mustRead 'very small paired leaves' fails - there are no leaves, only straight purple line segments of uniform stroke width with flat cut ends laid across the stem; they are geometric primitives, not foliage. mustRead 'purple-pink flower heads at EVERY shoot tip' fails - there is one flower, and it is a symmetrical radial daisy with a brown centre disc, which is a composite/Asteraceae flower, not a dense head of tiny lipped labiate flowers. The stem is a flat grey untextured line with no woodiness and no branching.
rows.fix: Turn the whole thing on its side: build a low sprawling mat of 6-10 thin WOODY brown stems creeping outward and turning up only at the tips, occupying about twice the width of the height. Replace every chevron with pairs of tiny dark grey-green oval leaves, crowded so densely along each stem that the stem is half hidden, opposite pairs rotated 90 degrees between nodes. Delete the daisy and put a small rounded flower HEAD on each of the upturned shoot tips - each head a tight cluster of 15-25 minute rose-purple two-lipped florets with green bracts beneath, no yellow/brown disc.

rows.readsAs: a sago palm / cycad, or a young tree fern
rows.defect: This is not a banana-architecture herb. The crown is a fan of ~14 pinnate FERN fronds — each one a thin rachis lined with dozens of tiny sawtooth pinnae — in a pale mint/teal that is nowhere near 'mid green with reddish midrib'. mustRead 'torn paddle leaves' fails: a paddle blade wind-split into a few broad ribs is a completely different shape from a comb of 30 leaflets. mustRead 'heavy hanging bunch of straight green fingers' fails outright — the only harvest present is a ~15px cluster of four pale-yellow dots sitting in the crotch of the stem, reading as a small flower, not a bunch of plantains. The 'false trunk' is two smooth flat-colour green capsule bars forked into a Y; a banana pseudostem is a single unbranched sheathed column and never forks. Both stem bars are untextured solid #3a7a3a rectangles with rounded caps, and the fronds attach at one hard point with a visible seam where the frond bases cross the stem top.
rows.fix: Replace the pinnate-frond generator with 6-9 whole elliptical paddle blades ~2.5x longer than wide, each with a thick pale midrib and 3-6 tear splits cut perpendicular from the margin inward (splits, not repeated leaflets). Kill the Y-fork: one unbranched pseudostem with vertical sheath overlap lines and a slight taper. Recolour blades to mid green with a reddish-brown midrib wash. Replace the yellow dot cluster with a real infructescence: a downward-arcing peduncle carrying 4-6 stacked hands of 8-12 straight angular green fingers, sized ~30% of crown width, hanging below and in front of the stem.

rows.readsAs: a purple lotus or magnolia flower on a stick
rows.defect: Zero of the three mustReads are present. This is an upright PURPLE FLOWER on a bare brown stick — a lotus or magnolia bloom of ~9 overlapping violet petals tilted at 40 degrees at the top of a plain 8px brown pole. mustRead 'flat rosette pressed to the ground' fails: there is no ground rosette at all, the leaves are gone and everything sits at the top of a 250px stalk. mustRead 'parallel ribs running the length of the leaf' fails: the petals are flat untextured purple with no venation of any kind. mustRead 'thin upright rat-tail spike' fails: the only thing near it is a small teal barrel of 4 stacked crescent bands wrapped around the stalk beneath the flower, which reads as a decorative collar, not a slender seed spike. The stalk is also the wrong colour — bare woody brown for what should be a green scape — and it meets the purple mass at a hard butt joint with a visible seam.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a rosette: 7-9 broad oval leaves radiating from a single ground crown, drawn nearly flat with strong foreshortening so the outer ones lie almost horizontal, each carrying 5-7 curved parallel ribs that converge at both tip and base. Colour mid green, no purple anywhere. Then add 2-3 thin green scapes rising from the rosette centre, each topped with a narrow cylindrical rat-tail spike of fine packed brownish florets, roughly 1/4 the scape length and no wider than 3x the stalk.

rows.readsAs: an olive tree, or a generic storybook fruit tree
rows.defect: Reads as a generic fruit tree, and the canopy is a painted blob rather than a crown. The foliage mass is a soft yellow-olive cloud with a bright glow bleeding well past the leaf edges into the background; individual leaves are then stamped ON TOP of that cloud as ~30 identical pointed almond shapes at scattered angles, several floating clear of the mass in empty space with no twig connecting them. Leaf colour is khaki-yellow, not the specified mid green. mustRead 'twiggy sometimes thorny crown' fails: there are no visible branches whatsoever — the trunk vanishes into the blob and nothing forks out of it. mustRead 'white blossom before the leaves' is absent entirely. The fruit half-works: five purple-violet spheres with a highlight, but they are perfectly round rather than oval and carry a glossy specular dot instead of a matte pale bloom. The trunk is a plain brown capsule primitive — constant width, rounded top cap — that terminates inside the canopy with a hard edge.
rows.fix: Draw an actual branch armature first: trunk splitting into 3-5 primaries and then twiggy secondaries that reach the canopy edge, with the leaves and fruit attached to those twigs so nothing floats. Tighten the glow radius so it does not exceed the leaf silhouette. Shift leaf fill to mid green with a purple-tinged rim, taper the trunk and give it bark striation instead of a flat fill. Make the fruits ovals on short stalks, swap the specular dot for a soft desaturated bloom haze over the upper surface, and add a scatter of small white five-petal blossoms on the bare inner twigs.

rows.readsAs: a date palm or a dry thistle-headed tree hung with cherries
rows.defect: Form is specified as 'shrub' but this is rendered as a single-trunk tree — one straight brown capsule bar with a rounded cap running the full lower half of the frame — so the twiggy multi-stemmed habit is gone. The crown is a spiky starburst of ~40 narrow tan/khaki blades radiating from a centre, which reads as a palm or a thistle, not as small glossy opposite-paired leaves; the colour is dry straw-tan with no green in it at all. mustRead 'crown of stiff points at the top of the fruit' FAILS: the three red fruits are plain glossy spheres with a single small dark nub, no calyx points anywhere. mustRead 'vivid orange-red trumpet flowers with crumpled petals' FAILS: no flowers in the image. mustRead 'small glossy narrow leaves on twiggy spiny branches' fails on both colour and branch structure — there are no branches, the leaf blades emanate from a fog blob and several hang detached beyond it. The fruits are also perfect circles with a specular highlight and read as cherries.
rows.fix: Rebuild the habit as a multi-stemmed shrub: 4-6 slender stems from the base, arching out, with fine spine-tipped twigs. Replace the starburst blades with dense small oblong leaves in opposite pairs along those twigs, glossy mid green with bronze new growth. Redraw the fruit as a slightly flattened leathery globe in red-gold with a matte skin, and crucially add the calyx — 5-6 stiff triangular points standing up off the crown of each fruit. Add 2-3 orange-red flowers with crumpled, irregular-edged petals emerging from thickened tubular hypanthia.

rows.readsAs: an ear of wheat or a fern frond with a single red daisy stuck on top
rows.defect: Wrong plant and wrong proportion. The reference aspect is 0.6 (wider than tall) but the render is a tall narrow column roughly 1:2 — a single vertical stem with 22 tiers of small identical pinnate leaflets stacked in strict horizontal rows all the way up, giving a symmetrical feather/wheat-ear silhouette. mustRead 'four thin crinkled tissue-paper petals' FAILS: the flower is a tiny ~35px red disc with about 10 short stubby radial petals and a dark centre, i.e. a daisy, and it is the only flower present. mustRead 'nodding hairy bud that lifts as the petals open' FAILS — no bud anywhere. mustRead 'round pepper-pot seed capsule with a flat ribbed cap' FAILS — no capsule. The leaves are the wrong shape (poppy leaves are deeply lobed and toothed, basal, and irregular) and the wrong colour: they render as pale ice-blue-white, not grey-green. The regimented row-on-row leaflet placement is machine-regular and gives away the procedural template. This is the SAME silhouette as Potato in this batch, differing only in leaf hue and flower colour.
rows.fix: Break the shared column template for this species. Crush the height to aspect 0.6 with most foliage in a low basal clump: irregular deeply-lobed grey-green leaves with bristly hair fringing the margins, sizes varying, none in aligned rows. Send 2-4 thin hairy stems up out of that clump at slightly different angles and lengths. Put a real poppy flower on the tallest: four broad overlapping crinkle-edged scarlet petals filling most of the bloom's width, black basal blotch, dark boss of stamens. On a second stem add a nodding hairy bud, and on a third a spent stem carrying the round green capsule with its flat ribbed lid.

rows.readsAs: a wheat ear or a bottlebrush plant with one white flower on top
rows.defect: Structurally identical to the Poppy render in this same batch — the same tall narrow vertical spine with ~20 tiers of small leaflets in strict horizontal rows and a single flower planted dead centre on top — recoloured mint-green with a white flower. mustRead 'compound leaf of uneven-sized leaflets' FAILS: every leaflet is the same small oval, mechanically repeated, so the diagnostic potato pattern of a big terminal leaflet with tiny ones interleaved between the pairs is absent. mustRead 'clusters of white or purple star flowers with a yellow cone of anthers' FAILS: there is exactly ONE flower, not a cluster, and it has six thin spiky petals with a plain white centre — no yellow anther cone. mustRead 'knobbly tubers hanging on stolons at the base' FAILS COMPLETELY: the stem just meets the ground shadow, nothing below or around it. Form is declared 'tuber' and the tuber is missing. The stems are also drawn as one ruler-straight vertical line rather than the sprawling angular stems specified.
rows.fix: Kill the shared feather-column template. Build a sprawling low bush of 3-5 angular stems leaning at different angles. On each, draw true pinnate leaves with a large terminal leaflet, 2-3 pairs of medium laterals, and small extra leaflets tucked between the pairs — matt dull green with a slightly rough edge. Replace the single top flower with 2-3 nodding cymes of 4-6 five-pointed star flowers, each with a clear yellow-orange anther cone at the centre. Then add the harvest that defines the species: a cutaway of 4-6 knobbly brown-skinned tubers of varying size hanging on pale stolons at the stem base, with shallow dark eyes.

rows.readsAs: a white water lily or lotus flower
rows.defect: None of the three mustReads survive. The plant is a wide fan of about 14 overlapping cream-white pointed petals splayed symmetrically from a single low point — a water-lily bloom, not foliage — with a hairline stalk running straight up through the middle carrying a small pale-lilac beaded spike. mustRead 'five-fingered palmate leaf' FAILS: there are 14 undivided petals, not leaves in groups of five, and no leaf division of any kind. mustRead 'dense hairy stems' FAILS: the single stalk is a bare 3px line with no hairs and no other stems. mustRead 'swollen turnip-like root on a thin thread' FAILS: no root is drawn at all, and the species is defined by that root. Colour is bone-white, not the specified silvery grey-green. This is also the same fan-rosette-plus-spike template as Plantain Herb in this batch, just white instead of purple.
rows.fix: Rebuild from the reference: 3-5 hairy stems rising from a crown, each ending in a palmate leaf of exactly FIVE narrow leaflets radiating from one attachment point, grey-green with a silvery hair fringe rendered along every margin. Add a short dense spike of blue-purple pea flowers on the tallest stem. Then draw the harvest below the ground line: a fat spindle-shaped brown tap root, wide at the shoulder and tapering to a point, hanging from a thin thread-like neck that connects visibly up into the stem crown.

rows.readsAs: a cluster of green eggs, or a smooth succulent such as a jade plant
rows.defect: An off-body artifact sits in empty space: a small yellow flower floats roughly 60px ABOVE the plant with nothing connecting it to any pad — a hard blocker on its own. The body is five smooth bright-green egg/teardrop shapes fanned out from a common base, each with a soft airbrush gradient and a clean unbroken outline. mustRead 'areoles with tufts of fine glochids and long spines' FAILS COMPLETELY: the pads are perfectly bare — not one spine, not one areole dot on the whole plant, which removes the single feature that names this cactus. mustRead 'magenta tunas ringing the pad edge' FAILS: there are no fruits. mustRead 'flat overlapping paddle pads' half-fails — they overlap, but they are plump ovoids rendered with a centre-bulge gradient that makes them read as inflated eggs rather than flat paddles, and the tips are rounded rather than the broad blunt end of an opuntia pad. Colour is a saturated emerald, not the specified blue-grey green.
rows.fix: Ground the flower: seat it on the upper rim of a top pad, growing from an areole. Reshape the pads to true opuntia outline — widest above the middle, blunt-topped, narrowed to a short neck at the joint, with a slight irregular waviness to the margin instead of a clean ellipse. Flatten the shading to a broad soft plane with a rim light so they read as slabs, not eggs, and shift the hue to dusty blue-grey green. Then add the defining detail: a regular diagonal lattice of areoles across every pad face, each a small buff tuft with 2-3 long pale spines and a halo of fine glochids, denser along the margins. Finally ring the top pad rims with 3-5 upright barrel-shaped magenta tunas, each with a sunken navel at the top.

rows.readsAs: A stylised cycad or a green feather-duster on a stick
rows.defect: No prop roots at all — the required cone of stilt roots is entirely absent, and the trunk instead ends in a blunt rounded capsule tip floating above the drop shadow. The trunk is a flat, uniform-width mid-green capsule with one stubby dead-end side branch, giving a crude Y; there is no bark texture, no taper, no root flare. The crown is a perfectly radial fan of cyan-teal pinnate feather fronds — pinnate, not strap leaves, and radially symmetric rather than spiralling in a screw around the stem. The fruit is a ~24px orange bead with painted-on vertical stripes sitting in the dead centre of the crown where the fronds meet, not a big segmented ball hanging below the crown. Fronds meet the trunk at a hard line at the Y fork — a visible seam, nothing grows out of anything.
rows.fix: Add the stilt-root cone as real geometry: 5-8 tapering roots leaving the trunk at 40-60deg from a point ~40% up and planting into the ground plane, each with a widened foot. Replace the pinnate frond generator with long unbranched strap blades carrying saw-tooth edge notches, and drive their emission points up a short helical path around the crown axis so the spiral reads. Kill the Y branch stub or extend it into a second true crown. Recolour blades grey-green/blue-green (desaturate the cyan ~40%). Scale the fruit to ~3x and hang it on a visible peduncle BELOW the leaf bases, and build its knobbly surface from packed hexagonal drupe cells, not painted stripes.

rows.readsAs: A yellowing palm or the same cycad as the Pandanus card, painted a different colour
rows.defect: This is the exact same render as Pandanus_Fruit in this batch, recoloured yellow-olive — identical Y trunk, identical radial pinnate frond fan, identical tiny striped bead at the crown centre. Every mustRead fails: the trunk is BRANCHED (papaya has no branches) and has no leaf-ring scars; the crown is feather-pinnate fronds instead of huge deeply lobed palmate blades; and there is no fruit cluster on the trunk — just one bead the size of a marble sitting in the crown. Aspect is roughly 1:1, not the specified 0.55 tall-and-slim. The leaf colour is sulphur yellow, not mid green, which reads as a dying plant.
rows.fix: Fork papaya off the palm/cycad template entirely. Single straight unbranched grey-green column, slightly tapering, with a ladder of crescent leaf-scar rings up its length. Crown = 7-9 huge palmate blades, each a disc cut into 5-7 pointed lobes with a secondary lobe cut, held out on long thin petioles that arc down. Recolour blades mid green. Add a ring of 6-10 overlapping ovoid melons pressed directly against the trunk immediately under the petiole bases, green shading to orange at the lower ones.

rows.readsAs: A clump of dry ornamental pampas grass or a wheat sheaf
rows.defect: A wide fountain of arching golden-brown blades springing from a single point — no tall bare stems, no triangular culms, and crucially no firework umbel: not one of the ~20 blades terminates in a burst of fine drooping rays, they just taper to points. The silhouette is roughly 1.4 wide-to-tall when the row asks for 0.5 (tall and narrow); the plant sprawls sideways more than it stands up. Colour is dry straw gold, not bright green. Scattered through the interior and floating clear of any blade are ~15 short yellow horizontal dashes and tick marks with air on both sides — off-body artifacts that read as debris sprayed over the drawing. There is no water, no rhizome mass.
rows.fix: Rebuild as vertical culms: 8-12 near-straight stems rising to 80-90% of frame height, each with a faint three-sided shading break (light left facet, dark right facet) so the triangular section reads. Cap every culm with a real umbel — 30-40 thread-fine rays radiating from one node then drooping, with small brown spikelets at the ray tips. Strip leaves off the culm entirely and put short brown sheaths only at the base. Recolour to bright green. Delete the free-floating dash primitives (they are unparented to any blade path) and add a dark waterline with a thick rhizome clump at the base.

rows.readsAs: A teal spider-plant or sedge clump; indistinguishable from the Papyrus card in the same batch
rows.defect: The same fountain-grass template as Papyrus above, recoloured cyan-teal and thinned to ~12 blades — no visual distinction between the two cards beyond hue. All three mustReads fail: the stems are curved tapering grass blades, not bare triangular culms; there is zero starburst at any tip; and there is no water surface, the clump just sits on the same generic ellipse shadow as every other card. The identical floating cyan dash artifacts from the Papyrus card are present again, hanging in empty space beside the blades. Aspect is wide-spreading, not the specified 0.55.
rows.fix: Same culm-and-umbel rebuild as Papyrus, then differentiate: make the shoots shorter, fewer, and strictly vertical with the umbels still tight and half-unopened (rays short and clumped rather than fully spread), and add the pale cream young shoots at the waterline that this card's harvest calls for. Add a real waterline with reflection so the aquatic form reads. Remove the floating dash primitives. Recolour to bright mid green — the cyan is a palette default, not a plant colour.

rows.readsAs: A generic yellow star-flowered creeper, nothing that names passionflower
rows.defect: An S-curved bare olive stem carrying six IDENTICAL yellow spiky rosettes, each a flat starburst of ~9 pointed blades clipped onto the stem at an obvious junction. The signature flower is absent: no flat disc bloom, no fringe of fine radiating corona filaments, no raised central column with stamens and styles — the yellow bursts are leaf-shaped stars, not flowers. No palmate 3-5 lobed leaves anywhere. No fruit. The small dark coils at the nodes do read as tendrils, which is the one mustRead that lands. The whole plant occupies maybe 35% of the frame and every rosette is a copy-paste of the same asset at the same scale.
rows.fix: Split the parts: draw real leaves as 3-5 lobed palmate blades on short petioles, and draw the flower ONCE or twice at 2-3x the leaf size as a distinct object — flat pale disc of 10 sepals/petals, then a dense ring of 60+ hair-thin filaments banded purple-white-purple laid over them, then a green androgynophore column rising from the centre bearing 5 flat anthers and 3 hooked styles above. Vary rosette scale and rotation so no two are the same stamp. Grow leaf petioles out of the stem with a swelling node rather than butting the shape against it. Add an egg-shaped purple fruit. Fill more of the frame.

rows.readsAs: A blue alien creeper with one berry — reads as the Passionflower card in a different colourway
rows.defect: Same S-vine template as the Passionflower card, recoloured periwinkle blue, with one maroon sphere added mid-stem. The blue-violet leaves are wrong on the row's own terms (dark glossy green) and read as alien, not earth flora. The leaves are pointed multi-blade starbursts, not the required deeply three-lobed glossy leaves. The corona flower with radiating filaments is entirely missing. The fruit is a single flawless circle with a smooth radial gradient and a specular hotspot — an obvious geometric primitive pasted onto the stem with no peduncle, no stem scar, no wrinkle. Tendril coils are present and are the only correct feature.
rows.fix: Recolour to dark glossy green with a hard specular streak along each blade. Replace the starburst leaf with a true three-lobed blade: one wide central lobe and two swept side lobes off a common base, serrated margin. Add at least one corona flower so the vine is identifiable. Rebuild the fruit as a slightly oblate purple ovoid with a dimpled, faintly mottled rind, hung from a short green stalk that visibly leaves a leaf axil, and add a second fruit at a different depth so it does not read as a single stuck-on bead.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon lollipop tree with oranges on it
rows.defect: The trunk is a literal capsule — constant width from top to bottom, semicircular cap at the bottom, no taper, no root flare, no bark — and it disappears into the canopy along a hard horizontal edge. There are no branches whatsoever; the crown is a single soft green blob with short pointed leaves radiating outward like a sea-urchin's spines, so the leaves stick OUT of a cloud rather than hanging off twigs. The required drooping willow-like narrow leaves read instead as stiff outward spikes, and the low spreading vase-shaped crown is a round puffball. The three fruit are perfect circles with a plain pink-orange radial gradient: no suture cleft, no velvety fuzz, no red-over-yellow blush break.
rows.fix: Give the trunk a taper and a flared base that meets the ground, break the outline with bark ridges, and split it into 3-5 upward-and-outward scaffold limbs at about 30% height so the vase crown is built from actual wood — then hang leaves off those limbs. Rotate leaf blades to droop downward from their attachment and lengthen them to a 5:1 lance shape with a visible folded midrib and a toothed edge. Add the suture: a darker crease running pole-to-pole down one side of each fruit, offset from centre, plus a soft noise/fuzz pass on the fruit rim and a yellow-to-crimson gradient break rather than a uniform tint.

rows.readsAs: A blue fern frond or a young monkey-puzzle sapling with a nut balanced on top
rows.defect: This is a tall ramrod-straight vertical spire — one perfectly straight blue-grey stem, drawn as a constant-width line with a rounded cap, carrying about eleven evenly spaced opposite pairs of pinnate fronds, each frond made of a dozen tiny tick-like blue leaflets. The four-leaflet mustRead fails completely (dozens of leaflets per frond); the low spreading habit fails (this is a 1:3 vertical mast); the small yellow pea flowers are absent. Worst, the single tan ovoid pod is drawn hanging at the very TOP of the stem, in the air, which the reference row explicitly forbids — peanut pods form underground. The blue-violet colour is not mid green. The spacing of the frond pairs is metronomically regular, machined rather than grown.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a low, wide, sprawling herb: several stems fanning outward from a crown at soil level, height well under width. Each leaf must be exactly four oval leaflets in two opposite pairs with no terminal leaflet — draw them large enough to count. Recolour to mid green. Add a few small yellow butterfly-shaped pea flowers in the leaf axils. Delete the aerial pod entirely; instead draw a soil line across the lower third and put two or three netted tan pods BELOW it, connected up to the plant by thin pegs driven down into the soil. Jitter node spacing and stem curvature so nothing is evenly ruled.

rows.readsAs: A brown wooden garden fork with four green firework sparklers glued to the prongs — or a bare sapling decorated with plastic pom-poms. Not a Joshua tree.
rows.defect: The rosettes are flat radial asterisks — 10-14 identical straight green spokes fanning from a single point in near-perfect rotational symmetry, sitting on the branch tips like clip-art sparkles rather than dense three-dimensional bristling heads of daggers. Only four of them on the whole plant. The trunk is a flat mid-brown tapered strap with a smooth airbrush gradient and completely smooth edges: no shaggy grey bark, no packed dead-leaf-base texture, not even a value break — a mustRead is simply absent. The second mustRead, the skirt of dead grey-brown leaves hanging below each rosette, is also absent; there is no grey or brown anywhere in the foliage. The branch forks are hard seams — at the main Y the two arms are separate tapered strips laid over the trunk with a visible straight-edged overlap line and no swelling or crotch where they grow out. The upper arms are straight sticks with a single elbow, not contorted. The harvest (creamy club of waxy flowers) is missing entirely. Silhouette is far too sparse and thin for a Joshua tree — a real one is a heavy, top-weighted mass.
rows.fix: Rebuild the rosette as a spherical bristle head, not a 2D star: 60-90 short stiff daggers on a hemisphere, each with width and a light/shade side, varied length and jitter so the outline is ragged, and add the required grey-brown dead skirt as a downward-drooping collar of desaturated leaves under each head. Thicken the trunk substantially (roughly 2x current width at the base) and clad it in the shaggy bark: overlapping small downward-pointing scale marks in warm grey, dark in the recesses. Kill the fork seams — draw trunk and arms as one continuous tapering spline mass with a widened crotch fillet where the arms leave. Bend each arm at two or three points instead of one. Add the club-shaped creamy flower cluster at one arm tip.

rows.readsAs: A child's lollipop tree or a generic cartoon olive tree with cherries. Nobody would say jujube.
rows.defect: The trunk is a literal capsule — a flat olive-yellow bar of constant width with a semicircular rounded cap at the top, exactly a popsicle stick, and it terminates INSIDE the canopy at a hard rounded line with no branching whatsoever. Zero of the three mustReads are present. There are no zigzag thorny twigs — there are no twigs at all; the leaves float unattached in a soft olive fog cloud that has a visibly airbrushed, soft-edged boundary quite unlike foliage. The leaves are plain untextured pointed almond shapes with a single central highlight, no three strong veins, and they are not in two ranks. The fruit are three perfect hard-edged circles in flat maroon with a specular dot, sprayed on top of the canopy — no oval date shape, no wrinkling, and one of them (upper right) overlaps a leaf with a razor-straight cut edge. The canopy fog is a different colour family (yellow-olive) from the leaves drawn on it, so it reads as a separate painted blob behind the leaves rather than the mass they belong to. Trunk-to-canopy is one of the hardest seams in the batch.
rows.fix: Replace the capsule trunk with a tapering trunk that splits into 3-5 branches which then split again into the characteristic zigzag twigs — each internode kinking left-right with a small paired spine at every node. Attach every leaf to a twig with a visible short petiole; no floating leaves. Draw the three arcuate veins on each leaf (one midrib plus two curving from the base) and give the leaf a glossy top-lit sheen instead of a single dot. Remake the fruit as ovals with the long axis along a short stalk, ripening gradient green-to-red-brown, and add wrinkle shading on the shoulders. Delete the airbrushed olive cloud, or reduce it to a very low-opacity shadow mass tinted the same green as the leaves and confined behind them.

rows.readsAs: A clump of ornamental grass or a plastic aquarium plant with blueberries stuck on. Indistinguishable from the Lavender and Labrador Tea in this same batch — all three are the identical armature recoloured.
rows.defect: This is not a needle shrub, it is a bundle of green drinking straws. Every 'needle' is a thick straight rod of uniform width with a rounded cap on the end, roughly 25-35px long and 5-6px wide, set at a repeating ~45 degree angle off a handful of vertical stems — a machined, repeated primitive, and there is nothing prickly about a blunt rounded-ended rod. Colour is a bright emerald/grass green with a light-green highlight stripe, not the required blue-green; the mustRead white band on the needles is absent, and no needle is grouped in a whorl of three. The bush is not dense — you can see straight through to the dark background nearly everywhere, so the mustRead 'dense prickly bushy or columnar form' fails; it is a thin splayed spray. The base is a solid flat green wedge with straight sides and a hard edge where it meets the ground shadow. The berries are five tight clusters of small perfect grey-blue circles with a single white highlight dot each, floating at stem tips with no visible attachment — glued on, not growing, and there are no green unripe berries mixed in as the reference requires.
rows.fix: Replace the rod primitive with a real needle: tapered to a sharp point, slightly curved, roughly half the current length and varying, with a pale silvery stripe painted down the upper face. Cluster them in whorls of three around the twig rather than as single sticks, and increase count by 4-6x so the mass is opaque and the silhouette is a prickly cloud rather than a wire diagram. Shift the whole palette to blue-green (desaturate and cool it hard). Give the berries a short pedicel and a dusty matte bloom instead of a specular dot, break the perfect circles with slight ovality and the characteristic four-part apex scar, and mix in green first-year berries. Dissolve the flat wedge base into a woody stem with bark.

rows.readsAs: The same green grass clump as the Juniper card next to it. A stranger would not connect it to the spice.
rows.defect: Near-identical to Juniper.png in the same batch — same procedural armature, same straight rounded-cap rod 'needles' at the same repeating 45 degree angle, same bright emerald green, same flat wedge base, same grey-blue perfect-circle berry clusters. The only visible differences are that the spray is slightly wider and one berry cluster sits further out on the left. Since this species is supposed to FEATURE the berries, the failure is worse here: the berries are five small clusters of flat circles with white highlight dots, occupying maybe 3% of the image, glued at stem tips with no stalk and no dusty bloom (they are shiny, the reference says matte waxy bloom). All three mustReads fail — no white stripe, no whorls of three, no bloom on the berries, no green unripe ones, and the bush is see-through rather than dense/scruffy/conical.
rows.fix: First, make it visually distinct from Juniper.png — this card should be a close-in, berry-forward composition: fewer, larger berry clusters at 2-3x current size, pushed to the foreground, with the foliage as supporting mass. Then apply the same needle fixes as Juniper (tapered pointed needles in whorls of three with a silvery upper stripe, blue-green palette, 4-6x density). Render the berries with a matte dusty bloom — desaturated pale-blue haze over a dark blue-black body, no specular dot — plus the four-part star scar at the apex, a visible short stalk into the twig, and a mix of green first-year fruit alongside the ripe blue-black.

rows.readsAs: A sea anemone, a rocket fin, or a feather-duster tubeworm. Several people would guess it is a fungus. Nobody would say kelp.
rows.defect: This does not read as a plant at all. The image is a single upright rust-orange/terracotta teardrop — narrow rounded top, bulging middle, tapering to a point at the ground — with vertical stripes down it and THREE glowing hot-orange oval dots spaced down the centre line. All three mustReads are absent: there is no root-like claw holdfast (the shape just comes to a point and stops at the ground shadow), there is no stiff stipe stalk (nothing distinguishable as a stalk), and there is no wide flapping brown blade (the form is tall and narrow, roughly 1:3.5, which is the inverse of the specified aspect 0.35 reading — a broad blade should be the dominant mass). The colour is wrong: warm rust-orange/salmon, not olive-brown or dark chocolate. The glowing dots look like bioluminescent alien organs and belong to no earth seaweed. The surface reads dry and matte, not glossy and rubbery. The vertical stripes are evenly spaced straight lines — a machined gradient repeat, not the ripple of a blade.
rows.fix: Restart this one. Build it in the three canonical parts, bottom-up: a knotted holdfast of intertwined haptera gripping a rock at the base, drawn as overlapping finger-like roots with real overlap shading; a smooth cylindrical stipe rising from it with a slight bend and a highlight running its length; and at the top a broad strap-like blade at least twice the stipe's width, splitting into 4-7 finger-like segments that curve and flap sideways so the silhouette is asymmetric and water-moved. Repaint entirely in olive-brown to dark chocolate with a wet glossy specular sheen and translucent light through the thin blade edges. Delete the three glowing dots — they are alien-flora artifacts leaking into an earth species.

rows.readsAs: A generic vine sprig carrying two burdock burrs or two spiky seed pods. Reads closer to a cocklebur or a rambutan than a kiwifruit.
rows.defect: Two of three mustReads fail. The leaves are small plain dark-green ovals with a faint central highlight — not large, not round, not heart-shaped, no basal notch, no point — and their stalks are the same brown as the cane with no red and no hairs. There is no support and no twining: the cane is a lone brown S-curve standing in empty space, so 'twining woody cane wrapping its support' is absent; nothing tells you this is a climber. Scale is inverted — the fruit are drawn as big as or bigger than the leaves, whereas a real kiwi leaf dwarfs the fruit, and that inversion alone destroys the read. The fruit themselves are pale tan/khaki rather than russet-brown, and the fuzz is rendered as an outline of stiff radiating spikes around the perimeter only, which reads as a burr or a sea urchin rather than dense velvet nap; the interior of each fruit is smooth and untextured. The fruit hang singly, not in the specified twos and threes. Leaves join the cane at a hard butt-joint with no swelling at the node.
rows.fix: Multiply the leaf size by roughly 3x and reshape to a broad round leaf with a heart-shaped notched base and a short abrupt point, with palmate venation and a faintly felted pale underside visible on any leaf that turns. Recolour every petiole to a distinct rusty red and give it visible bristle hairs. Add a support — a wire, post or host branch — and wrap the cane around it so the spiral is unmistakable. Move the fuzz from the silhouette to the surface: an all-over dense short-hair nap in russet-brown with soft rim lighting on the hairs, no spiky outline. Hang the fruit in pairs and triples from a shared node on short peduncles, and swell the node where each leaf and each fruit stalk leaves the cane.

rows.readsAs: A clump of dead golden wheat or barley with tiny white mushrooms growing on it. Nobody would say Labrador tea; the third guess would be dried ornamental grass.
rows.defect: The entire plant is gold/ochre — stems, leaves, everything — so the mustRead 'dark green above, rust-orange felt underneath' is not a contrast at all, it is a monochrome dead-looking shrub. There is no green anywhere. The rusty fuzz mustRead therefore cannot read as fuzz: it reads as autumn dieback, and there is no felted/woolly texture on any surface, just a smooth gradient on flat shapes. The leaves are stiff pointed daggers with straight edges and sharp tips — the opposite of the required narrow leathery leaves with edges rolled UNDER, which should show a thick soft rounded margin and a cylindrical profile. The flowers are five flat white ellipses laid horizontally on stem tips, reading exactly as tiny mushroom caps or pushpin heads; the mustRead 'domed white flower clusters' fails because there is no dome, no cluster and no individual florets — each is a single opaque blob. Structurally it is the identical procedural armature as both Juniper cards and Lavender: same vertical stem fan, same repeated rods at 45 degrees, same solid flat wedge base with straight sides.
rows.fix: Recolour to a strong two-tone: dark matte green upper leaf surfaces, and let the rust-orange appear ONLY on the visible undersides and on the young stems, so the contrast itself carries the identification. Reshape the leaf — narrow, blunt-tipped, with the margin visibly rolled under (paint a darker rolled edge line down both sides so each leaf reads as a half-tube), and hang the leaves downward-drooping rather than radiating as stiff spikes. Replace each white blob with a real corymb: 8-15 small five-petalled white flowers packed into a dome, with visible protruding stamens and shading on the underside of the dome. Add a woolly texture pass — short soft fibres breaking the silhouette of stems and leaf undersides. Break the shared armature: this should be a low sprawling bog shrub, not the same upright spray as the junipers.

rows.readsAs: Lavender — correctly, from the spikes alone. But the teal foliage makes a viewer hesitate and second-guess toward an aquarium plant or a sea-lavender.
rows.defect: The violet spikes are recognisable and this is the only card in the batch a stranger would name correctly, but the foliage is wrong in a way that fights the read. The leaves are bright teal-cyan straight rods with rounded caps — not silver-grey-green, not narrow, not downy, not in opposite pairs — and the cyan is a colour lavender never shows; it makes the plant look aquatic. The mustRead 'long naked stalk with a short dense violet spike at the tip' fails: the flowering stems are clothed in these rods right up to within a few pixels of the spike, so no bare stalk is visible on any of the seven stems, and the stalks are round-profiled with no hint of the four-sided section. The mustRead 'tight rounded bush' of low silvery leaves also fails — the base is a splayed open spray you can see straight through, on a solid flat green wedge with straight sides, not a dense mound. The spikes themselves are decent bumpy purple columns but they sit at slightly varied heights on stems that are otherwise identical, and the whole armature is the same primitive shared with Juniper, Juniper Berries and Labrador Tea in this batch.
rows.fix: Recolour the foliage from teal to a soft silver-grey-green and add a fine downy bloom over it. Replace the rods with narrow tapering linear leaves in opposite pairs, and confine them to the lower third so each flowering stem rises as a genuinely NAKED stalk for its upper half — that bare-stalk-then-spike rhythm is what makes lavender readable at a glance. Give the stalk a squared four-sided cross-section by running a highlight edge and a shade edge down it. Compress the base into a tight rounded mound of dense silvery foliage instead of an open splay, and dissolve the flat wedge into woody stems. On the spikes, add the whorled calyx bracts so the bumps read as stacked florets rather than generic lumps.

rows.readsAs: a young fern frond or a generic aquarium plant sprig — nobody would say sesame
rows.defect: Two of three mustReads are simply absent: there are no tubular white-pink flowers in the leaf axils and no ribbed upright seed capsules anywhere on the stem. What is drawn is a bare olive-green stick with seven pairs of perfectly opposite, identically-sized pointed lens leaves — no size grading, no switch to alternate/narrower leaves up the stem. Leaf colour is pale ice-blue/white, not mid green. Every leaf is the same mirrored lens primitive rotated a few degrees, and each meets the stem at a hard point with no petiole or swelling, so they read as pasted-on rather than grown. Construction is identical to Solomon's Seal in this same batch (same straight stem, same opposite lens leaves) — the only difference is a flower on top.
rows.fix: Add the missing harvest and flower geometry: upright ribbed oblong capsules pressed tight against the stem in the upper axils, and small tubular foxglove-like white-pink bells nodding from the lower axils. Recolour leaves to mid green (drop the blue-white tint currently shared with Solomon's Seal and Star Anise). Grade leaf size down toward the tip and go alternate above the midpoint. Give each leaf a short petiole and a stem-node bulge so it grows out of the stem instead of touching it.

rows.readsAs: a speckled bird's egg, or a petri dish of pink mould — not snow with algae in it
rows.defect: The whole organism is a single hard-edged perfect ellipse of pale grey-white filling the frame — a geometric primitive with a soft airbrush gradient, not snow. The snow has no granularity at all: no crystal facets, no grain, no texture breakup, just a smooth radial blend. The cysts are flat salmon/dusty-pink discs at very low opacity, not the deep crimson-red the row calls for, and they never stain the surrounding snow watermelon pink — the field between them stays neutral grey. Zero cells show a green chloroplast core, so a full mustRead is missing. Cells are uniform flat circles with no thick wall rendered.
rows.fix: Kill the ellipse silhouette — let the snow field run to the frame edges or break its outline with crystal clumps. Paint granular snow: clustered angular crystal facets with directional highlights. Push cyst colour to deep crimson with a darker thick wall ring, and put a distinct green chloroplast blob off-centre inside roughly a third of the cells. Bleed a soft pink stain into the snow around each cyst cluster so the field itself reads watermelon-tinted.

rows.readsAs: a generic wildflower — bedstraw or a stylised chamomile stem
rows.defect: The defining feature — a single smooth ARCHING stem with bell flowers dangling in a row along the underside — is absent. The stem is dead straight and vertical, and the only flower is one 6-petalled star-shaped daisy sitting on top of the stem tip, which is the opposite of the plant's identity. Leaves are pale ice-blue lens shapes in five opposite pairs, not broad ribbed ovals, and carry no parallel veining whatsoever. Aspect is tall-narrow, not the wide 1.3 arching habit. Leaves attach at a hard point with no petiole. Structurally it is the same asset as Sesame in this batch with a flower added at the apex.
rows.fix: Rebuild the stem as a single smooth arc leaning to one side, leaves alternating along the top of the arc and held flat in one plane. Move flowers to the UNDERSIDE as a row of small green-white tubular bells hanging in pairs beneath each node, and delete the terminal daisy entirely. Widen and round the leaves, add clean parallel longitudinal veins, and recolour to mid green.

rows.readsAs: a red flax/phormium clump with a wood screw driven through the middle of it
rows.defect: The seed head is a literal machined screw: a tapered flat funnel-head on top of a cylinder with regularly spaced horizontal thread rings, perfectly straight-sided and hard-edged. It reads as hardware, not grain. The stem is a thin bare rod, not a stout jointed corn-like cane, and it does not thicken toward the base. Every blade is rust-orange/red rather than mid green, and none has the whitish midrib the row requires — blades are flat gradients with faint darker streaks only. The blades all radiate from one point at ground level like a phormium clump instead of alternating up a tall cane, so the corn-like architecture is missing. Blades meet the ground at a single hard convergence with no sheath.
rows.fix: Replace the threaded cylinder with an organic panicle — an irregular clumped mass of small red-brown grains, wider at the middle, with a soft broken outline. Thicken the stem into a jointed cane with visible nodes and attach broad blades ALTERNATELY up its length via wrapping sheaths, not from a basal rosette. Recolour blades mid green and paint a pale white midrib running the full length of each.

rows.readsAs: a small red agave or aloe rosette with a flower spike
rows.defect: The mustRead arrowhead leaf with backswept basal lobes does not exist — every leaf is a plain straight-sided triangular spike radiating from a single basal point, with no lobes at all. Leaf colour is salmon-orange, not fresh mid green. The spikes are hard-edged geometric wedges arranged in a symmetrical fan, and they all converge on one point rather than each rising on its own petiole. The seed spire is a bare wire-thin stalk with a tiny beaded pink caterpillar at the very top and nothing below it. In silhouette and colour this is essentially the same picture as Sorghum in this batch — orange radiating blades plus one thin central stalk with a small terminal head.
rows.fix: Redraw the leaf as a true arrowhead: broad blade with two distinct backward-pointing lobes flanking a petiole, and give each leaf its own petiole rising from the crown so they do not all meet at one point. Recolour to fresh mid green. Extend the rusty-red flower spire down its stalk as many small whorled florets rather than a single bead cluster at the tip, and add a second shorter spire so it does not read as one antenna.

rows.readsAs: a lollipop tree with watermelons hung in it
rows.defect: The fruit is wrong in every respect: four small perfectly spherical balls with vertical dark stripes — they read as watermelons. No heart shape, no soft curved spines, and they are tucked inside the canopy rather than hanging heavily from trunk or thick branches. The trunk is a capsule primitive — a straight-sided rounded rectangle with an obviously rounded bottom cap floating above the shadow — and it disappears into the crown at a hard seam with no branching whatsoever, so the crown is a separate object sitting on a stick. The crown itself is a circular airbrushed blob with small lens leaves sprinkled over and around it, several floating detached in empty space at the edges. Leaves are small yellow-green lances, not large dark glossy leathery oblongs.
rows.fix: Replace the striped spheres with one or two large asymmetric heart/kidney-shaped green fruits, surfaced with soft curved recurved spines, hanging on a short thick peduncle directly off the trunk or a main limb and heavy enough to bend it. Break the trunk into 3-4 real limbs that fan into the crown so there is no seam, and taper/flare the base into the ground. Enlarge the leaves, darken to glossy green, and remove the detached floating leaves.

rows.readsAs: a dandelion clock or a green firework on a lollipop stick
rows.defect: The crown is a round green cloud puff on a stick — the exact opposite of the narrow spire crown with tiers of stiff branches the row demands, so the headline mustRead fails. There are no branches at all inside the crown, just an airbrushed blob with straight teal sticks radiating outward like pins in a pincushion; those needle-sticks are perfectly straight uniform-width line primitives that start in mid-air and are not attached to any twig. The four cones are small orange ribbed cone-shapes that read as screws or traffic cones, they point UPWARD/outward and are stuck in random spots in the cloud rather than hanging downward from branch tips — the note explicitly calls for downward-hanging cones. There is no contrast between vivid light-green new tips and dark old growth; the crown is one flat green. The trunk is the same capsule primitive as Soursop and Star Anise, with a rounded bottom cap and a hard seam into the crown.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette as a tall narrow spire with whorled tiers of branches drooping slightly, foliage massed along the branches rather than a spherical cloud. Grow needles off drawn twigs in dense clusters instead of scattering straight lines from the blob centre. Hang the cones downward from the underside of upper branch tips and restyle them as papery scaled cones, not smooth ribbed cones. Add pale yellow-green candle tips at the branch ends against darker blue-green older foliage.

rows.readsAs: a generic grey-blue shrub-tree with seed pods — no viewer would say star anise
rows.defect: The whole identity of this plant — the woody eight-armed star fruit — is completely absent.
