What hangs in the crown are three small dark elongated pods/slivers that read as seed pods or dead leaves. There are also no flowers of any kind, so a second mustRead is missing. Leaf colour is cold blue-grey, nothing like deep glossy green, and the leaves are small pale lens shapes scattered loose around the crown with a dozen floating detached in empty background. The trunk is the identical capsule primitive used by Soursop and Spruce Tips — straight parallel sides, rounded bottom cap sitting above the shadow, no branching, meeting the crown blob at a hard seam. The crown is a grey airbrushed cloud.
rows.fix: Draw the fruit as the subject: one or two large woody eight-armed stars in warm red-brown, each arm a boat-shaped follicle split along the top to show a glossy tan seed, hung prominently at a branch tip. Recolour foliage to deep glossy green, enlarge leaves to leathery elliptics clustered at branch ends, and delete the floating unattached leaves. Add a few small many-petalled pink-yellow flowers. Split the trunk into real limbs entering the crown so the seam disappears.

rows.readsAs: a bundle of dried spaghetti or a shaving brush stood on end
rows.defect: Not an alga at all. The picture is a tight sheaf of ~8 smooth, unbranched, tapering rods in warm tan/apricot orange, all converging to a single point at the ground and fanning slightly at the top. Every mustRead fails: there is ZERO forking — not one branch splits anywhere in the image, let alone 'finely and repeatedly'; the colour is orange-tan with no red, crimson or purple anywhere; and there is no disc holdfast, just a pinched vertex where the rods meet. The rods have hard rounded pill ends and identical stroke width, so they read as extruded tubes rather than seaweed tissue. Silhouette is a plain teardrop/capsule.
rows.fix: Re-colour to deep crimson-to-purple (#7a0f2e → #3d0a2a) with a cool iridescent rim light, and replace the straight-rod generator with a recursive dichotomous frond routine: 4-5 levels of forking with the fork angle narrowing and stroke tapering at each level so the tips are hair-fine. Widen the flattened fronds into blade-like ribbons rather than round tubes. Terminate the base in a small lumpy encrusting disc holdfast that spreads sideways onto the substrate instead of a converging point.

rows.readsAs: a yellow star-flowered climbing vine — someone would guess a jasmine or an ornamental creeper, never a grapevine
rows.defect: A zigzag olive stem carrying five bright canary-YELLOW star rosettes and a single pea-sized purple berry cluster. The leaves are the failure: they are narrow-petalled 7-point stars radiating from a centre, which reads as a flower head, not the big palmate 3-5 lobed toothed vine leaf the row demands — and they are yellow, not mid-green. The berry bunch is present but is a tiny knot of 5-6 grains roughly one-tenth the size of a single leaf, with no conical taper and no hanging; it is glued to the side of the stem like a wart. Tendrils exist but are drawn as perfect flat circles/spirals of uniform stroke stuck beside each node — a geometric primitive, not a forked coiling tendril growing out of the stem.
rows.fix: Recolour blades to mid-green with paler downy undersides. Replace the star rosette with a true vine leaf mask: broad cordate outline, 3-5 pointed lobes separated by deep sinuses, a coarse-toothed margin, and palmate veins radiating from the petiole notch. Grow the bunch to 1.5-2x leaf size, hang it BELOW its node under gravity, and give it a conical taper (wide shoulders, pointed tip) built from overlapping shaded spheres in crimson-red. Redraw tendrils as tapering forked filaments whose spiral pitch loosens toward the tip, emerging from the node opposite a leaf rather than as a closed circle.

rows.readsAs: a dandelion clock, or a lollipop-shaped cartoon tree
rows.defect: This is not a tree of any kind. A short, wide pale grey-green CAPSULE — a flat-filled rounded rectangle with hemispherical caps, no taper, no bark texture, no root flare — supports a fuzzy round cloud of pale mint green from which straight pale sticks radiate in every direction like pins in a pincushion. Aspect is roughly 1:1, not the required 0.3 tall narrow column. The trunk/crown junction is a hard seam: the capsule simply disappears into the blur with a visible edge. Needles are individual straight line segments sprayed outward, not flat two-ranked feather sprays. Worst of all, four brown ribbed cones are drawn at 1/6 the crown width, hovering unattached in the blur — the reference note explicitly warns that large cones read wrong, and these are enormous.
rows.fix: Set aspect to a genuine 0.3: crown width ~130px against a 400px height. Rebuild the trunk as a tapering fluted column with a flaring buttressed base that spreads into the ground, and paint fibrous cinnamon-red bark as deep vertical ridge-and-furrow striping with warm highlight on the ridges. Replace the radial needle spray with pendant feather-shaped sprays: a central twig axis with short flat needles set in two opposite ranks, sprays hanging and overlapping to build a narrow conical crown. Shrink cones to 6-8px olive-sized ovoids and attach them to spray tips, or drop them entirely. Remove the soft blur cloud, which is doing the work the foliage should be doing.

rows.readsAs: a stand of bare winter trees, or a white coral head — nobody would say lichen
rows.defect: The branching itself is genuinely good — fine, repeatedly forking, tapering to hair tips, in the right pale ash-cream. But the structure is wrong: below the branch zone there are eight or nine long, clear, bare vertical TRUNKS rising from the ground before any branching begins, which turns a spongy ground cushion into a miniature grove of bare winter trees. The crown is capped by a smooth opaque cream dome that fills the upper third solidly, hiding the branch structure and reading as a hard mushroom cap or a mushroom cloud rather than a springy open mat. The result has a strong flat-topped mushroom silhouette. Branch tips also radiate evenly in all directions rather than all nodding one way, so the mustRead 'tips drooping and all nodding one way' is not met.
rows.fix: Cut the clear trunk height to near zero — start forking within the first 10-15% of height so the mass sits on the ground as a cushion. Reduce the crown opacity so the twig lattice reads through it instead of a solid dome, and break the flat top into an irregular lumpy cushion profile. Bias every terminal fork 15-25 degrees toward one side so the tips collectively nod in a single direction. Add a few darker interstitial shadows inside the mat to give springy depth.

rows.readsAs: a bunch of helium balloons on strings
rows.defect: Five near-perfect salmon-orange CIRCLES on thin red sticks, all converging to a single sharp point at ground level. The circles are geometric primitives with a faint single crease line drawn across them as the only nod to a leaf; there is no heart shape, no triangular blade, no crinkling, no puckering, no wavy margin, no veining, and no green anywhere — blade and stalk are the same salmon-red family, so the vivid-red-stalk-against-deep-green-blade contrast that IS rhubarb is entirely absent. Blades are also too small relative to stalk length; the row asks for leaves far larger than expected and these are modest discs. The five stalks meet at a knife point rather than a crown.
rows.fix: Recolour blades to deep green with a red-veined underside and keep the stalks vivid pink-red so the two-tone contrast carries the read. Replace the circle mask with a broad triangular-cordate blade: notched heart base at the petiole, wide shoulders, wavy undulating margin. Add puckering via a bumpy displacement between the main veins plus paired highlight/shadow ridges so the blade reads quilted and crinkled. Scale blades up ~1.8x so they dominate. Splay the stalk bases apart into a short thick crown at ground level instead of a single vertex, and thicken the stalks so they read fleshy rather than wiry.

rows.readsAs: a pink ornamental grass or cordyline with a bottlebrush flower — closest to a garden phormium
rows.defect: Colour is the immediate blocker: the entire leaf fountain is hot MAGENTA-PINK shading to violet, with no green or ripening gold at all, so it reads as an ornamental garden phormium rather than a food grain. The seed head is the second blocker — it is a single stiff, perfectly VERTICAL, compact bristled spike sitting on top of a rigid straight central stem, exactly the 'compact ear' the row says to avoid, with no nodding, no arch, no weight and no loose branched panicle. There is only one central culm, not a clump of several tillers, and no water, wet ground or reflection anywhere. The spike's regular chevron ribbing looks machined, like a screw thread.
rows.fix: Recolour blades to bright green ripening to golden-yellow at the tips. Split the single culm into 4-6 separate tillers rising from a common clump. Rebuild the seed head as a loose panicle: a curved rachis that bends over past horizontal under load, with 8-12 secondary branchlets each carrying spaced plump grains, so the whole head droops. Add a dark waterline ellipse with a soft reflection at the base to place the clump in flooded ground. Replace the uniform chevron ribbing with irregularly sized, individually shaded grains.

rows.readsAs: an ear of white corn, or a caterpillar climbing a stem
rows.defect: A single thin stem carrying about ten tightly stacked pairs of pale bluish-WHITE smooth ovals, packed edge to edge into a solid column with a tiny cream bristle at the very top. It reads as an ear of corn or a segmented grub. Every mustRead fails: the leaflets are featureless egg shapes with no heart base, no point, and no saw teeth of any kind; the colour is near-white lilac instead of dull dark green; there are no stinging hairs visible on stem or leaf; and there are no dangling flower tassels at the leaf joints — the single bristle sits at the apex, in the wrong place and the wrong form. The overall silhouette is a rounded rectangle. Aspect is also inverted: the row calls for 0.5 (wider than tall) and this is roughly 1:2.5 tall and narrow. The leaflets are so tightly packed they overlap into a continuous mass with no stem visible between pairs, so nothing grows OUT of the stem — they are stuck on in a column.
rows.fix: Recolour to dull matt dark green. Space the leaf pairs out to 3-4 well-separated decussate nodes with visible square stem between them, and enlarge each leaf several times so the plant is broader than tall. Give each blade a cordate base, a drawn-out point, and a coarse sawtooth margin cut into the outline itself, with impressed veins. Add fine pale hairs as short strokes along the stem edges and leaf margins. Hang small drooping catkin tassels of tiny green flowers from each leaf axil, not from the apex.

rows.readsAs: a bouquet of frosted white ferns or dried baby's-breath with cherries stuck in it
rows.defect: The foliage is the blocker: every leaf is a white/pale-grey HERRINGBONE comb — a bare rachis with dozens of identical short straight teeth set at a regular angle, repeated identically across the whole bush. That is a fern or a frost crystal, not pinnate rose foliage; there are no discrete oval leaflets, no toothed leaflet margins, no impressed veins, no quilted rugose surface, and the colour is white-grey rather than rich glossy dark green. Four bright red spheres sit on top of upright bare stalks like cherries: no flask shape, no dried sepal star crown at the tip, and they perch on the stem end rather than terminating a branch. Prickly bristly stems do not read — the stems are smooth, and the whole clump converges into a flat solid olive-green triangular wedge at the base with straight machined edges.
rows.fix: Recolour foliage to rich dark green with a glossy specular highlight. Replace the comb generator with true pinnate leaves: 5-9 separate oval leaflets with visibly toothed edges, paired along a rachis with a terminal leaflet, and paint deep impressed lateral veins with a bumpy quilted surface between them. Reshape the hips into fat flask-shaped ovoids in scarlet-orange and add a 5-point dried blackened sepal crown at the free end. Scatter fine prickles and bristles as short dark hooked strokes along every stem. Break the base wedge into individual arching canes emerging separately from the ground.

rows.readsAs: A fan palm seedling or a spider plant with one flower spike
rows.defect: The picture is a fan of about eleven straight, flat, hard-edged green blades radiating from a single point on the ground, with one pencil-thin vertical stem rising ~150px above the fan carrying a single tiny magenta star-flower at the very top. Every mustRead fails: there is no low cushion or mat (the silhouette is a tall upright fan, taller than wide, when aspect 2.2 asks for a wide low mound); the flower is emphatically NOT stemless — it is on a long bare stalk, the exact opposite of "flowers resting on the foliage"; there is one flower, not a scatter; and the foliage is not tiny paired scale-leaves but long machined capsule blades with uniform width and rounded ends. The blades all converge to one hard point where they overlap the shadow — a seam, not growth. No lime-crusted tips.
rows.fix: Discard the fan-rosette primitive entirely. Build a wide low dome (width:height about 3:1) out of many short, thick, opposite-paired scale leaves packed along creeping stems so the outline is lumpy and mossy, dark grey-green with lime speckling on the leaf tips. Scatter 10-16 five-petalled magenta flowers with pedicel length zero, sitting directly on the dome surface and partly sunk into it, a few overlapping the silhouette edge. Add a hint of rock the cushion is hugging.

rows.readsAs: A purple lupine spike, or a stacked ornamental succulent
rows.defect: A tall vertical column of lavender-white rounded lobes arranged in eight mirrored opposite pairs up a bare thin grey stick, topped by a 20px chain of orange beads. Colour is wrong at the family level — the leaves are pale violet/periwinkle, not mid green or red-gold. No goosefoot leaf anywhere: the lobes are smooth teardrops with no toothing, no duck-foot outline, and they are opposite-paired when quinoa is alternate. No grooved striped stem — the stem is a featureless grey capsule barely visible behind the lobes. The seed head is a tiny bead string, not a chunky branched panicle; it is far too small to read as the harvest. Each lobe pair meets the stem at an identical hard point, a visible repeated seam all the way up the axis. The whole thing is the same lobed-ladder template as Rainforest Nettle in this batch, recoloured.
rows.fix: Retarget the leaf primitive to a broad alternate goosefoot blade — widest near the base, three shallow angular lobes, irregular coarse teeth, dusted mealy grey-green with red flushes. Space them alternately with real petiole curvature so no two joins repeat. Rebuild the harvest as a dense branched panicle occupying the top third of the frame, chunky and clustered, in hot magenta/cream/orange. Give the stem visible longitudinal grooves and a red stripe. Break the shared template with Rainforest Nettle.

rows.readsAs: A dead tarweed or a dried sunflower weed
rows.defect: Ochre-brown branching stems with five separate small yellow daisy heads, each with clearly drawn radiating ray petals, sitting on top of long bare stalks at five different heights. Three mustReads fail: the stems are brown, with no white-felted or woolly quality at all, so it reads dry and dead rather than silvery; the flowers are discrete rayed daisies at staggered heights, not "solid gold flat-topped masses" (and the row explicitly says NO ray petals); and the leaves are short, stiff, hard-edged brown darts stuck onto the stems at sharp right angles like thorns, not thread-like grey-green filaments. Each dart meets its stem with a hard straight join. The crown is not a rounded broom — it is a sparse open V.
rows.fix: Recolour stems to pale white-grey with a soft felted fuzz along the edges and desaturate the leaf strokes to grey-green. Replace the dart leaves with many fine hair-thin curving filaments that taper into the stem instead of butting it. Merge the five daisies into two or three broad, dense, flat-topped corymbs of tiny discoid florets — a solid gold plateau of texture, no visible ray petals — and pull the whole crown into a rounded broom outline by adding more stems of even height.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon red starfish, or a five-petalled poster flower
rows.defect: Five russet-red lobes around a central dark dome does get the basic gesture, but the execution fails the row and the shape rules. The mustRead "deep central pit ringed with spikes" is absent: the centre is a smooth convex bulge with a soft radial gradient, reading as raised, not as a pit, and there is not a single spike or ramenta. The cream spots are perfect hard-edged circles with a bloom glow, several of them overlapping or crossing the lobe outline into the background — sprayed on top of the shape rather than being warts in the skin. Each lobe is a pure ellipse capsule that meets the central ellipse along a hard curved seam; the five joins are identical. The flower hovers above a detached oval shadow with no ground contact and no host vine, contradicting "flat on the forest floor".
rows.fix: Sink the centre: replace the convex dome with a dark concave well using an inner shadow ring, and rim it with a ring of pale fleshy spikes pointing inward. Clip all spots to the lobe silhouette, kill the glow, and vary them into irregular raised warts with their own shading rather than flat circles. Give each lobe an individual asymmetric outline with a fleshy thickened rim and blend it into the central disc so no seam is visible. Seat the flower on the ground with soil contact and a knobbly host vine emerging beside it.

rows.readsAs: An ear of green corn, or a stack of hosta lobes on a stick
rows.defect: Identical geometry to Quinoa in this same batch — a vertical stem with eight mirrored pairs of smooth rounded mint-green lobes stacked in a ladder, topped by a small cream bead spike. Every mustRead fails: there are no oversized heart-shaped leaves (the lobes are small smooth teardrops, no cordate base, no toothed margin, no visible venation), and there is no haze of stinging hairs anywhere on the stems or veins. The harvest is a bead spike at the apex rather than clusters of pale fruit in the leaf axils. The form is not a shrub at aspect 1 — it is a narrow vertical column. Every lobe joins the stem at the same hard point, repeated sixteen times.
rows.fix: Rebuild as an understorey shrub: three or four thick soft-wooded stems carrying a handful of very large heart-shaped leaves — deep cordate notch at the base, coarse teeth on the margin, strong palmate venation, pale mid-green with a felted paler underside showing on the tilted ones. Add a fine pale hair fringe rendered along the leaf margins, veins and stems to read as the stinging haze. Hang small pale fleshy fruit clusters where the petioles meet the stem. Stop sharing the lobed-ladder template with Quinoa.

rows.readsAs: A papaya or a tree fern
rows.defect: The trunk is a literal rounded rectangle — a flat-topped brown capsule with two perfectly parallel straight machined sides and no taper, root flare or bark, exactly the capsule silhouette that is called out as forbidden. It disappears behind the crown with no branching whatsoever, so the crown is stuck on top of a stick. The crown is not a dense dark rounded mass: it is a flat radial spray of grey-sage feathery pinnate fronds with a grey smoke blob painted in the middle, so it reads as a fern or palm rosette rather than a broadleaf tree. Leaf colour is desaturated grey-green, not dark green, and the leaflets are many tiny herringbone slivers rather than 2-4 pairs of large leathery ovals. The fruit clusters are bunches of smooth flat red circles with no hairs at all, so the single most identifying feature of a rambutan is missing.
rows.fix: Replace the capsule trunk with a tapered trunk that flares at the base and splits into three or four ascending limbs which carry the foliage, so there is no seam between trunk and crown. Fill the crown as a dense overlapping dark-green rounded mass rather than a flat radial fan, and swap the herringbone leaflets for a few pairs of broad glossy leathery ovals per leaf. Redraw the fruit as red ovoids covered in soft outward-curving green-tipped spines breaking the fruit silhouette, and let the clusters hang under branches rather than sit on the leaf plane. Delete the grey haze blob.

rows.readsAs: A magenta thistle or an astilbe
rows.defect: This is the Rabbitbrush render recoloured — the same brown branching stem skeleton, the same staggered heads, the same stroke leaves — now in magenta. Consequences: the harvest reads as five pink pom-pom flower heads, not fruit; there is not one thimble-shaped berry in the picture, so "hollow-cored red berries" is missing outright. The leaves are violet-magenta feathered combs, not pinnate groups of 3-5 toothed green leaflets, and there is zero white-grey underside flashing anywhere. No bristly prickles on the canes. The habit is a branching shrub crown rather than upright biennial canes. Each comb leaf meets its stem as a hard perpendicular bar.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a clump of straight upright canes rising from the base with a fine bristle texture along their length. Give each cane trifoliate/pinnate leaves of 3-5 coarsely toothed green leaflets, with a good number tilted to expose a bright white-grey felted underside. Replace the pom-pom heads with drooping clusters of red thimble berries built from visible individual drupelets, at least one showing the hollow core. Drop the shared skeleton with Rabbitbrush.

rows.readsAs: A frosted feather-boa vine or a silver fern sprig
rows.defect: An olive S-curving cane does deliver the snaking climber gesture, and that part is right. Everything else fails. The fronds are stark white/silver, not mid to dark green, so the plant reads as frost-covered; there are six of them and all six are the same fanned comb of straight white strokes, rotated. Each tuft attaches to the cane at a single hard point with a visible seam and no rachis continuing into the cane. The mustRead whip-like hooked flagella trailing off the leaf tips is entirely absent — nothing trails. The spiny sheaths are drawn as flat dark-grey doughnut rings that sit beside rather than around the cane, several of them detached from it in empty space, and they carry no spines. Nothing indicates the cane is climbing anything.
rows.fix: Recolour the leaflets to mid-dark green with straw-brown sheaths. Give each frond a real rachis that emerges from the cane and continues its curve, with narrow leaflets spaced unevenly along it and varying frond length. Add long thin whip flagella trailing off two or three frond tips, with tiny recurved hooks along them. Replace the doughnut rings with sheaths that genuinely wrap the cane at each node, banded and studded with outward black spines. Add a suggestion of a host trunk or branch the cane hooks around.

rows.readsAs: a marijuana plant or a chrysanthemum — a palmate-leaved bush with flat pink daisies stuck on top
rows.defect: The harvest is missing and mis-drawn. The reference is explicit that the read is a fat waxy scarlet CALYX hugging the stem, and the note warns against drawing the flower — but the render shows exactly what the note forbids, and even gets that wrong: six flat pink-red daisy heads with visible narrow ray petals and a pale centre, floating on top of the foliage. There is no swollen fleshy body anywhere. The stems are also plain mid-green, not red — the mustRead 'upright red-stemmed stalks' does not read at all, and neither do the red petioles/veins the leaf row calls for. Leaf shape is wrong in a way that changes the species: instead of three-to-five broad maple-like lobes, every leaf is a rosette of 7-9 identical narrow finger-lobes radiating from one point, which is a palmate cannabis/Virginia-creeper leaf, not a hibiscus leaf. The green is an acid neon lime with no tonal range. Construction: the whole crown is one flat cluster of stamped leaf rosettes on a single smooth green cone trunk that terminates in a hard horizontal line where the foliage begins — a visible stuck-on seam between trunk and canopy.
rows.fix: Replace the daisy flowers with 5-8 bulbous ribbed scarlet calyces sitting directly against the stem in the leaf axils, each with the pointed epicalyx bracts flaring at the base and a matte waxy highlight. Recolour every stem and leaf stalk to deep red-maroon and run red veins into the blade. Rebuild the leaf as 3-5 BROAD lobes with sinuses cut halfway to the midrib (maple silhouette), not 7-9 narrow fingers. Darken the green off neon toward mid forest green. Kill the trunk/canopy seam by letting individual red stems continue up through the mass rather than a cone ending in a flat line.

rows.readsAs: lavender, or an aquarium plant — a teal wire-brush bush with lilac bottlebrush spikes
rows.defect: The needles are not needles — they are straight, uniform-width, flat-ended teal line segments, all the same length, laid down in a crossing X lattice so the bush reads as a woven wire trellis rather than foliage. Real rosemary needles crowd DENSELY up each stem in whorls; here the stems are nearly bare and the 'needles' are sparse spokes with big dark gaps between them, and they overlap each other in a mechanical grid pattern. The mustRead 'white underside to the needle' is entirely absent — every needle is a single flat teal with no two-tone flip, so the defining silver-felt read is gone. The flowers are wrong too: four fat lilac-white bottlebrush cones sitting only at the very tips, which is a lavender/veronica arrangement; rosemary's pale blue lipped flowers should be small and scattered ALONG the stems. Colour is a cool aquarium teal, not the dark grey-green of rosemary. Construction: the base is a smooth solid green trapezoid/cone with a hard edge, and the stems appear on top of it rather than out of it — a clear seam. No woody brown anywhere despite 'upright woody bush'.
rows.fix: Rewrite the needle primitive: taper it to a point, vary the length, and paint a lighter silver-white stroke down one edge for the rolled-under white underside. Increase needle density 3-4x and attach them in tight ascending whorls hugging each stem so the stem is barely visible, instead of sparse crossing spokes. Break the X-lattice by giving each stem its own slight curve and its own needle phase. Replace the four terminal bottlebrushes with many small two-lipped pale-blue flowers scattered in the upper leaf axils. Shift palette from teal to dark grey-green, and make the lower stems woody brown emerging from a ragged root flare rather than a solid green cone.

rows.readsAs: pampas grass or a silver ornamental fountain grass — possibly a spider plant; nothing about it says rush
rows.defect: The harvest is completely absent. The mustRead demands a brown flower cluster bursting SIDEWAYS out of the stem with the tip continuing past it — there is no flower cluster of any kind in this image, nowhere, so the single feature that identifies a rush is missing. Colour is the second blocker: the row calls for glossy mid-to-dark green with straw-brown at the base, and the render is near-white silver-grey from tip to base with a faint blue cast — it looks frosted or dead. The blades are also flat and ribbon-like: each one widens in the middle and tapers, with a visible flat face and a bent droop at the tips, which is exactly the flat-grass-blade look the note warns produces a sedge read, not the smooth round leafless cylinders rushes actually are. Several outer blades bend into a hard arc and go nearly horizontal, giving a fountain silhouette rather than the stiff needle-straight upright tuft specified.
rows.fix: Add the inflorescence: a tight dark-brown scaly cluster attached to the SIDE of several stems about three quarters up, with the green stem visibly continuing above it as a sharp point — this is non-negotiable for the rush read. Recolour the whole tuft to saturated glossy mid-green with a warm straw-brown wash on the bottom fifth. Change the blade primitive from a widening ribbon to a constant-diameter cylinder with a single specular highlight running its length, tapering only in the last 15% to a needle point. Straighten most stems to near-vertical, keep only 2-3 outer ones leaning, and remove the horizontal fountain arcs.

rows.readsAs: an ornamental autumn grass or a decorative pampas clump with a single wheat sprig stuck in the middle
rows.defect: The proportion is inverted. The reference calls for aspect 0.22 — a very tall, very thin plant, taller and thinner than wheat — but the render is a low fountain that is markedly WIDER than it is tall, with blades sweeping out to the horizontal on both sides. It is the opposite of the required silhouette. The whole plant is also a single foliage clump carrying exactly ONE ear on one thin culm; rye should read as a stand of tall culms each topped by an ear. The ear itself fails its mustRead: it is a short, stubby, upright, rigidly symmetric zipper of stacked chevrons with a tiny fan of stiff bristles at the very top, where the row demands a long slender ear that NODS over at the tip with very long hair-fine awns spraying the full length. The awns here are short, few, and confined to the crown. Colour is wrong in both stages at once — the whole plant is uniform hot amber-orange with no blue-green waxy bloom anywhere and no grey in the straw. Critically, this is the same fountain template as Rush Shoots in this batch with a different hue and one ear pasted on.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette vertical: 3-6 tall thin culms rising well above a narrow basal clump, total aspect near 0.22, with only short narrow blades clasping the lower culm rather than a wide radiating fountain. Lengthen the ear to roughly 3x its width, curve it so the top third leans over, and replace the bristle crown with 20+ hair-fine awns twice the ear's length fanning from every spikelet along the whole ear. Recolour foliage to distinct blue-green with a dusty waxy bloom and let only the ear and lower culm go grey-straw; drop the orange entirely. Differentiate the base geometry from the Rush Shoots template so the two do not share a silhouette.

rows.readsAs: a red-leaved dracaena or a coral-thorned twig shrub — closest to an ornamental spike plant; it is unrecognisable as sage
rows.defect: The colour is not merely off, it is the opposite of the spec. The mustRead says grey-green not bright green, and the leaves here are SALMON-RED / coral pink — a colour sage never has. The leaf form is also wrong: these are narrow, sharply pointed, flat spear blades radiating like thorns, where the row calls for thick oblong pebbled leaves; there is no pebbling, no wrinkle, no velvet nap, no thickness, and no visible opposite-pair arrangement — they scatter singly along the stems. The stems are bare rust-brown rods with big empty gaps, so the plant reads as leafless twigs with red spines rather than a leafy herb. The flowers are four fat lilac-white bottlebrush cones sitting only at the stem tips, identical to the primitive used on Rosemary in this same batch, instead of separated whorls of violet-blue lipped flowers spaced up a spike. Square woody-based stems do not read — the stems are round and smooth. Construction: a solid brown cone base with a hard top edge where all stems suddenly appear.
rows.fix: Recolour every leaf to muted grey-green with a silver bloom on the young ones — remove all red/coral. Rebuild the leaf as a thick blunt-tipped oblong roughly 3:1, drawn in opposite pairs at right angles up the stem, with a fine puckered network of veins and a soft matte edge for the velvet. Triple the leaf count so foliage, not bare stem, dominates. Rework the flowers into distinct spaced whorls of violet-blue two-lipped flowers on an emergent spike, and stop reusing the Rosemary bottlebrush cone. Flatten the lower stems to read square and let them merge into a ragged woody crown rather than a smooth cone with a seam.

rows.readsAs: a teal aquarium bamboo or a cyan willow shrub with cream catkins
rows.defect: Silver-grey is the entire identity of sagebrush and this render is bright cyan-teal — the mustRead 'silver-grey felted foliage' fails outright. The leaf is a plain narrow pointed lance with a smooth entire margin; the three blunt teeth at the tip, the single most diagnostic feature in the row, are absent on every leaf. There is no felting or hair texture — the leaves are flat filled shapes with a hard clean edge. 'Twisted gnarled woody trunk with shredding grey bark' also fails: the base is a smooth symmetric green cone with a hard rim, no bark, no twist, no grey. The flower wands are cream-yellow lumpy catkins, acceptable in placement but far too pale and bulbous for tiny dull yellow heads. Structurally this is the same X-lattice-of-crossing-stems-plus-terminal-spikes template as Rosemary and Sage in this batch, recoloured — the three sit side by side as the same plant in three hues.
rows.fix: Recolour foliage to pale silver-grey with a soft dusty edge (feather the leaf boundary to suggest hair) and drop the cyan completely. Cut three blunt lobes into the wide tip of each leaf so it reads as a wedge with a toothed end, not a lance point. Replace the green cone base with a short thick trunk that kinks and forks, painted in grey-brown with vertical shredding bark strips, and let the stems grow out of that fork instead of appearing above a rim. Thin the flower wands into slim sprays of many tiny dull-yellow heads. Give it a distinct branch structure from Rosemary and Sage.

rows.readsAs: a wheat ear, a decorative feather, or a stylised fern-frond icon — a symmetrical ornament, not a berry bush
rows.defect: This is not a shrub at all — it is one perfectly straight vertical brown rod with seven identical pairs of gold lens-shaped leaves at exactly equal spacing, mirrored left and right with machine precision. The silhouette is a rectangle. Every mustRead fails: no upright canes (there is one rod), no shreddy golden-brown bark texture (the rod is a smooth gradient stick), no prickles, no magenta-pink five-petalled flowers anywhere, and no orange-pink thimble berries anywhere — the entire harvest is missing. The leaf is wrong twice over: it is a simple pointed ellipse with a smooth untoothed edge, not a trifoliate group of three toothed leaflets with an enlarged terminal one, and it is amber-gold, not bright mid green — there is no green pixel in the image. The leaves also butt into the stem at a hard point with a visible junction rather than growing out on petioles. The regular spacing and perfect bilateral mirroring make it read as a stamped icon rather than a grown plant.
rows.fix: Rebuild from scratch as a multi-cane shrub: 4-6 arching canes of varying height with peeling golden-brown bark and scattered fine prickles. Recolour all foliage to bright mid green. Replace each single ellipse with a true trifoliate unit — one large toothed terminal leaflet plus two smaller side leaflets on a short petiole — with serrated margins. Add the two missing harvest reads: several magenta-pink five-petalled flowers and several orange-pink drupelet-clustered thimble berries hanging from the upper canes. Randomise leaf spacing, angle and size, and break the left-right mirror.

rows.readsAs: a dried autumn twig, a sheaf of wheat, or a sprig of sea buckthorn — a golden dead-looking bush
rows.defect: The mustRead 'chalky white-grey foliage' is the defining feature and the render is warm amber-gold-brown throughout — it reads as a dead or autumn plant, the exact opposite of the salt-frosted white this species needs. There is no mealy/bladder-hair texture: leaves are hard-edged flat gold slivers with a clean outline and no chalky bloom. The papery fan-shaped seed bracts, the second mustRead, are entirely absent — nothing in the image is papery, winged or fan-shaped. The leaf shape is also wrong: the row specifies small THICK OVAL leaves, but these are narrow pointed slivers. Silhouette fails the 'dense stiff rounded twiggy mound' — the mass is a lopsided upward-leaning wedge biased to the upper right, not a rounded mound, and it is small in the 440px frame with a lot of dead space. Construction: a smooth tan cone trunk with a hard rim from which all the twigs sprout — a stuck-on seam — and the twigs themselves are the same crossing-lattice primitive used on Rosemary, Sage and Sagebrush in this batch.
rows.fix: Recolour everything to near-white chalky grey with the faintest green undertone, and add a mealy speckled bloom over the leaf faces so they look salt-dusted. Change the leaf to a small thick blunt oval with a slightly puffy silhouette. Add clusters of translucent pale papery fan/wing bracts hanging among the upper twigs — this is the harvest and it is missing. Rebalance the mass into a symmetric dense rounded dome filling more of the frame, with short stiff twigs radiating in all directions rather than an upward-right lean. Replace the cone base with grey woody stems that branch from ground level.

rows.readsAs: An agave or spider plant sending up a flower spike
rows.defect: The picture is a dense fountain rosette of ~25 broad teal-green arching blades, all radiating from one point at the soil, with a single thin gold spike rising out of the middle. Wheat's mustRead 'single unbranched straw with a few flat leaves' is absent — there is no visible culm at all, no nodes, no widely-spaced clasping blades; the leaves outnumber and outweigh the ear about 30:1. The ear itself is a ~10px-wide gold cylinder with tiny hatch marks and a small tuft at the very top; the 'long straight awn bristles fanning out' read as a short brush on the tip only, not a fan running the length of the ear. Colour is a saturated aquarium teal, not blue-green cereal foliage, and there is zero straw-gold in the leaves. The blade mass is also a symmetric mirrored fan — the left half is nearly a reflection of the right.
rows.fix: Cut leaf count to 4-6 and attach them at intervals ALONG a visible jointed culm (draw the culm as the dominant vertical, ear-to-soil, with swollen nodes where each blade clasps). Widen the ear to ~3x its current width, build it from overlapping spikelet lozenges in two ranks, and emit 15-25 long straight awns from the spikelets fanning up and outward over the ear's whole length. Shift leaf hue from teal to desaturated blue-green with straw-gold tips.

rows.readsAs: A blue-flowered climbing bellflower or clematis
rows.defect: Nothing in this image is a grape. It is an S-curved dark stem carrying five large BLUE-VIOLET star-shaped flowers with 6-8 pointed strap petals each. The mustRead 'big lobed vine leaf silhouette' is completely missing — there are no palmate leaves, no lobes, no teeth, no green foliage of any kind. The mustRead 'forked coiling tendrils' is missing — the small dark curls behind each flower are calyx/bract shapes, not opposite forked tendrils. The only nod to fruit is one thumbnail-sized cluster of ~6 flat yellow-ochre discs at mid-stem; they are opaque, uniformly round, and read as pollen dots, not translucent amber-green berries. Colour direction contradicts the row entirely (blue/purple against a spec that says green to gold).
rows.fix: Replace the blue star flowers with 3-5 palmate leaves — five pointed lobes, coarse marginal teeth, mid-green with a paler underside on the reflexed ones. Route the stem as a woody gnarled cane and spring a forked, coiling tendril from the node OPPOSITE each leaf. Rebuild the fruit as one tapering conical bunch of 25+ overlapping ellipsoid berries in pale amber-green, with rim-light through them so they read translucent.

rows.readsAs: A cut-flower bouquet of an upright herb standing in a green vase
rows.defect: The mustRead 'low sprawling twiggy mat well under knee height' is inverted — this is a tall narrow upright bouquet, taller than it is wide, with every stem shooting vertically. Worse, all the stems vanish into a solid opaque mid-green tapered wedge at the base: a hard-edged trapezoid with a straight left edge, a straight right edge and a flat crisp boundary where the stems disappear into it. That is a machined primitive with a visible seam, not a plant crown — it reads as a florist's foam or a vase. Leaves are not 'small oval'; they are sharp teal lance/dart shapes attached at a uniform angle in near-perfect opposite pairs up every stem, giving a stencilled, sprayed-on repetition. The berries are only 5 small grey-purple clusters, all crowded at the top rim, with no pale bloom and no five-point crown visible.
rows.fix: Delete the wedge base entirely and let each wiry stem taper into the soil independently, splaying outward so the silhouette is wider than tall (aspect nearer 0.5 relative to its spread). Swap the dart leaves for small rounded ovals with a short petiole, alternate rather than paired, and jitter angle and size per leaf. Scatter berry clusters through the mid and lower canopy as well as the top, add a dusty pale-blue bloom overlay and a small dark five-point calyx star on the berries facing the viewer, and put scarlet in a few leaves.

rows.readsAs: A dead or autumn-brown palm/broom on a wooden lolly stick
rows.defect: The trunk is a flat rounded-rectangle capsule — constant width from soil to crown, straight parallel sides, a domed cap at the bottom, filled with a plain orange-brown vertical gradient. No taper, no root flare, and critically none of the mustRead 'shiny red-brown bark with horizontal lines of pores peeling in bands'. The crown is a soft brown-tan cloud of straw-coloured spiky slivers — dead grass colour, not the specified mid-green foliage — with a blurry glow halo around it that makes it look out of focus against the sharp trunk. The mustRead 'clusters of white blossom on bare wood' is entirely absent. The four cherries are perfect hard-edged circles with a specular dot, sitting flatly ON the fuzz with no stalk whatsoever, contradicting 'on long stalks'. Where the trunk enters the crown it simply terminates in three straight spikes — a stuck-on join.
rows.fix: Taper the trunk and flare it at the base, then paint horizontal lenticel dashes in bands across a red-brown bark with a satin sheen. Replace the tan fuzz with layered mid-green oval toothed leaf clumps built from actual leaf shapes; branch the trunk into 3-4 real limbs that carry those clumps so the crown grows out of the wood. Hang each cherry from a visible 12-20px pedicel in stalked clusters of 2-4, and add white five-petal blossom clusters on the inner branches.

rows.readsAs: A leafless autumn rosehip or holly twig bundle
rows.defect: This is the Wild Blueberry image recoloured — the exact same upright bunch of parallel stems, the same opposite-paired dart leaves at a fixed angle, the same solid tapered opaque wedge base with hard straight edges, the same 5 fruit clusters ringing the top. Only the palette differs. The mustRead 'mid green' leaves fail outright: every leaf is salmon-orange/rust. The mustRead 'small white star flowers' is absent — there are none. The fruits are large perfect glossy spheres with a highlight dot, sitting at the very tips of bare stems like rosehips, not 'pea-sized' among the foliage, and their scale relative to the leaves is roughly 3x too big. 'Scrambling wiry many-branched bush' fails too — the stems are near-parallel verticals that barely branch.
rows.fix: Break the shared skeleton: make the stems zigzag and cross at wide angles so the bush scrambles, and remove the wedge base so each stem meets the soil separately. Recolour foliage to mid green and enlarge the leaves to smooth pointed ovals. Shrink the fruits to about a third of current diameter, make them slightly bullet-shaped rather than perfect spheres, and multiply them to 15+ standing upright on short pedicels ABOVE the leaf layer. Add small five-lobed white star flowers among them.

rows.readsAs: An ornamental teal fountain grass with a single aster flower
rows.defect: Reuses the Wheat rosette wholesale — same count, same splay, same teal gradient, same mirrored left/right fan — so the two are indistinguishable at silhouette level. The mustRead 'hollow tube leaves, round in section' fails: every blade is a flat tapered ribbon with a hard highlight down one side and a knife-edge tip, exactly the flat blade Wheat uses. The mustRead 'tight lilac pompom' fails: the flower is a small flat 2D daisy — a ring of ~12 separate rounded petals around a pale disc — which reads as an aster, not a dense spherical umbel of many florets. Colour is wrong in both directions: leaves are bright aquarium teal rather than blue-grey green, and the scale of the flower head to the leaf mass is about a quarter of what a chive shows. No clustered bulbs are visible at the base.
rows.fix: Render the leaves as narrow cylinders — constant width most of their length, a rounded blunt tip, and a centred soft specular stripe with dark on BOTH edges so they read as tubes not ribbons. Cut them to a tighter vertical tuft, desaturate to blue-grey green. Replace the daisy with a globe: 40+ small six-petal florets packed onto a sphere in lilac-magenta, sized 2-3x the current head, on one bare hollow stalk thicker than the leaves. Show 2-3 pale bulb shoulders where the tuft meets the soil.

rows.readsAs: A generic cartoon plum tree on a stick
rows.defect: Same lollipop template as Wild Cherry: an identical flat rounded-rectangle trunk, constant width, straight parallel sides, plain ochre gradient, no taper. The mustRead 'massive spreading crown on buttressed pale trunk' fails on both counts — the trunk is a narrow stick with zero buttressing and the crown is a modest fuzzy oval barely twice the trunk's width. The mustRead 'hanging aerial roots' is completely absent. The mustRead 'figs studding the bark of trunk and limbs' is inverted: the only three fruits are dark purple perfect spheres with specular dots floating in the canopy fuzz, not one is on the wood, and they read as plums. The crown is a yellow-green haze of tiny spiky slivers with a blur halo — no leathery oval leaves, no drip tips, no gloss.
rows.fix: Rebuild the trunk as a fused lattice of vertical root strands with visible gaps and a wide flaring buttressed foot in pale grey. Drop 6-10 thin aerial roots from the branches to the ground. Widen the crown to 3-4x the trunk width, spreading and layered, built from large dark glossy leathery ovals each ending in a short drip tip. Move the figs onto the bark: 10+ small round green-to-red figs pressed directly against the trunk and limb surfaces on tiny stubs.

rows.readsAs: An ornamental purple fountain grass or purple cordyline
rows.defect: The whole plant is mauve-purple — every blade, root to tip — where the row calls for fresh bright green; nothing in the picture is green. The mustRead 'broad lily-like leaves' fails: these are the same narrow tapered grass ribbons used by Wheat and Wild Chive in this batch, roughly a fifth of the width ramsons leaves need, and the rosette layout is the identical mirrored fountain. The mustRead 'starburst of white flowers' fails badly — the flower is a single small white crescent/lozenge about 20px across, essentially a blank capsule with no discernible florets, no radiating star petals, no umbel structure. The stalk carrying it is a thin round green line, not a three-angled scape, and it is so slender the head looks pinned on top of it.
rows.fix: Widen the leaves to 4-5x current width into broad flat elliptic blades with a pointed tip and a visible central rib, cut them to 5-7 total, and have them rise separately from the soil rather than fanning from one node. Recolour to fresh yellow-green. Thicken the scape and give it a triangular cross-section read (two shaded facets plus a lit edge). Replace the white lozenge with 12-20 individual six-petal white stars radiating on short pedicels from a common point, sized 3x the current head, plus a pale bulb and papery tunic at soil level.

rows.readsAs: a sago palm / cycad rosette, or a bundle of palm fronds stuck in the dirt
rows.defect: There is no trunk at all. Every frond springs from a single point on the ground, so the mustRead 'fibrous brown trunk of matted old frond bases' is entirely absent and the plant reads as a ground-level rosette, not a tree fern. The fronds are only once-divided: each rachis is a hard straight line with identical triangular sawtooth pinnae stamped along it at even spacing — machined regularity, no twice- or thrice-divided lacework. Every frond converges on one pixel-tight vertex, a visible hub seam where nothing grows out of anything. Only one tiny crozier spiral is legible (a small green curl near the vertex, plus a faint one at the upper right); the mustRead 'coiled croziers at the centre of the crown' does not carry.
rows.fix: Add a stout upright fibrous trunk occupying the lower ~45% of the height, textured with overlapping brown scale/frond-base chevrons, and start the frond rachises from a crown at its top rather than from a shared ground vertex — stagger the emergence points around a crown ring so no single hub is visible. Subdivide the pinnae one more level (each pinna becomes a small lobed pinnule strip with varied length, not an isosceles tooth) and jitter pinna length and angle 15-25% along each rachis. Enlarge the croziers to 3-4 clearly visible brown-scaled spirals sitting at the crown centre above the trunk.

rows.readsAs: an alien candyfloss tree with red berries glued on top
rows.defect: The canopy is a lavender-purple cotton-wool cloud blob with no leaves in it — the mustRead 'big soft heart-shaped leaves' is unreadable at any size, and leafColour is specified mid green but rendered violet. The fruits are three flat, perfectly smooth red ellipses lying ON TOP of the cloud with a hard edge against it; they are not hanging, not stalked, and not below the foliage, so 'long-stalked pendant egg-shaped fruit' fails. Two bare brown twigs poke straight up out of the cloud like antennae with nothing on their tips. The trunk-to-canopy junction is a straight brown stick that simply disappears into the puff.
rows.fix: Replace the cloud fill with discrete overlapping heart-shaped leaf blades in mid green (paler felted undersides on the down-facing ones), each attached to a visible short petiole off the limbs. Move the fruit to pendant clusters hanging BELOW the canopy edge on visible thin drooping stalks, and give each fruit an egg taper plus a small green calyx at the stalk end instead of a flat ellipse. Kill the two naked twigs or terminate them in leaves.

rows.readsAs: a golden lotus/water-lily bowl, or a decorative crown ornament
rows.defect: Colour is entirely wrong — the whole plant is amber/gold where the row calls for fresh mid green. The leaves are not broad lance blades: they are jagged saw-toothed maple-like flaps arranged in a perfectly mirror-symmetrical bowl, left half an exact reflection of the right, which is the single most machined-looking thing in the batch. The result is a cupped rosette, not the mustRead 'fountain of broad upright ribbed leaves from ground level' — nothing is upright, everything droops outward. The 'cone of pale green-and-pink bracts at the base' is absent; instead a single bare wire-thin stalk rises from the exact centre carrying a tiny yellow beaded spike at the top, floating well above the leaves with a visible seam where it crosses the leaf mass.
rows.fix: Recolour to fresh mid green. Replace the toothed flaps with smooth-margined long lance blades, each with a strong central midrib and fine parallel ribbing, and make them rise steeply upright before arching, on visible sheathing stalks. Break the mirror symmetry — vary blade count, length and angle per side. Move the inflorescence down to a squat cone of overlapping pale green bracts tipped pink sitting AT the base among the leaf sheaths, not on a bare stalk overhead, and expose a knobby orange-fleshed rhizome at soil level.

rows.readsAs: an ornamental purple fountain grass or a sea-anemone spray
rows.defect: Two mustReads are simply not present. There is no 'dense pedestal mound of old dead thatch at the base' — the blades converge into bare ground with only a cast shadow ellipse beneath them, so the tussock has no tussock. And there are no seed panicles: every element in the picture is an identical smooth blade, nothing thin or feathery stands clear above the fountain. Colour is lavender-purple throughout with none of the specified straw/tan dead thatch. The subject is also small in frame, occupying roughly the middle third, leaving the render mostly empty background.
rows.fix: Build a raised dome of tan/straw matted old leaf bases at the base, wide enough that the green blades visibly emerge from within it rather than from a point. Add 5-8 thin wiry culms rising 20-30% above the tallest blade, each ending in a loose feathery panicle. Recolour blades mid-green with straw tips grading into the tan mound, and scale the whole plant up to fill more of the 440px frame.

rows.readsAs: an upright ear of wheat or a standing feather duster
rows.defect: The bones are right — one unbranched stem, opposite pinnate leaves in a ladder, a small pale domed head on top — but the execution is stamped. Every leaflet is the identical small chevron, repeated at identical spacing and identical angle for the entire stem length, so the foliage column has perfectly straight parallel left and right edges: a rectangle of leaflets, not a plant. There is no taper toward the tip and no size gradient, and the leaf ladder runs all the way to the soil with no bare lower stem. Colour is olive-yellow/gold rather than mid green. The flower head is a tiny white puff that reads as detached from the stem top, and it is white rather than the specified pale pink-white.
rows.fix: Vary leaflet length along the stem — longest at mid-height, shortening toward the crown — so the foliage silhouette tapers instead of forming a column. Jitter each leaflet's angle and size by 10-20% and add visible toothing on the leaflet margins. Recolour to mid green. Clear the lowest 15% of the stem to bare grooved green stem. Widen the terminal flower head into a flat-topped corymb of many tiny florets tinted pale pink, with visible short pedicels fanning up from the stem so it grows out of the stem rather than sitting on it.

rows.readsAs: a red pepper vine or a bougainvillea sprig
rows.defect: Colour is wrong across the whole plant — the leaves are hot red/salmon, not mid green fleshy matt. The leaves are narrow pointed flame shapes, not the mustRead 'flat fleshy oblong' blades. The mustRead orchid flower is absent: the only other feature is a scattering of small dark-red open rings along the stem, which read as sucker discs or scabs, certainly not a pale greenish-yellow orchid bloom. There is no bark, tree or support of any kind, so 'aerial roots gripping bark' cannot read — the vine S-curves in empty space and its lower end just terminates in the ground shadow. No hanging cluster of green pods anywhere.
rows.fix: Recolour stem and leaves to matt mid green. Replace the flame leaves with wide flat oblong blades (roughly 3:1, blunt tip) lying flat against the picture plane, alternating strictly left/right. Add a vertical trunk or bark column behind the vine and turn the red rings into pale aerial roots that visibly clasp it. Add one pale greenish-yellow orchid flower with a distinct trumpet lip at a leaf axil, and a hanging bundle of 4-6 long slender green pods below it.

rows.readsAs: a blue tulip on a long stem, with red sparks above it
rows.defect: This does not read as a flytrap in any respect. There is no low ground rosette — a single bare brown stick runs the full height of the frame and the trap sits on top of it like a flower, which is the exact opposite of the reference note. The two lobes are periwinkle BLUE, smooth, and meet in a V like tulip petals; there is no hinge, no clamshell, and no red glandular interior. The teeth are the worst failure: they are a row of short red dashes floating in empty space ABOVE and BETWEEN the lobes, not touching the lobe margins at all — detached off-body artifacts that interlock with nothing. No flat winged petioles, no soil-level growth, no flower stalk distinct from the trap.
rows.fix: Drop the traps to a low rosette at ground level on short flat green winged petioles radiating outward. Rebuild the trap as two green clamshell lobes hinged along a visible midrib, opened maybe 60 degrees, with the inner faces flushed deep crimson and fine trigger hairs. Attach the teeth as tapering spikes growing directly off each lobe's outer margin and interdigitating with the opposite lobe — they must originate on the lobe edge, never in open space. If a flower is wanted, put small plain white five-petalled flowers on a separate thin stalk rising above the rosette.

rows.readsAs: a cluster of blueberries or a pile of soap bubbles with a tiny flower on a wire above it
rows.defect: The leaves are rendered as eight or nine large smooth blue spheres/balloons overlapping in a mound — perfect circular primitives with specular shading, no heart shape, no scalloped edge, no petiole, no vein beyond a single hairline seam bisecting the mound. Colour is cornflower blue, not mid-to-dark green. A single hair-thin dark stem rises from behind the mound to a tiny purple five-petal flower sitting way up in the empty upper quarter, so 'flowers held just above the leaves on curved stalks' fails on count (one, not several), on height (far above, not just above) and on the curve (dead straight). No backward spur is visible. The stem visibly passes in FRONT of the leaf mound as a drawn-over line rather than emerging from within it.
rows.fix: Replace the spheres with heart-shaped blades — notched base, pointed tip, scalloped margin — each on its own visible arching petiole rising from a common crown at soil level, and recolour to mid-dark green with paler veins. Add 3-5 flowers on thin stalks that curve over at the tip so the bloom nods, held only slightly above the leaf tuft, and give each a clearly drawn backward spur behind the lower petal. Route the stalks so they emerge from between the leaf bases instead of being overlaid on the mound.

rows.readsAs: a shaving brush / bundle of grey cables
rows.defect: There is no blade at all. The picture is a tight bundle of ~10 smooth grey-blue tubes, all the same width, splaying slightly at the top and pinched to a point at the base — a shaving brush or a bundle of cables. None of the three mustReads are present: no lobed wings, no flattened midrib, no ruffled sporophyll frill. The colour is cold blue-grey with a metallic sheen, not olive-brown/green-brown, so it does not even read as a plant. Each tube is a separate stroked cylinder with its own highlight, so they read as stuck-together rods rather than one organism.
rows.fix: Replace the tube bundle with a single flat blade: draw one dark olive-brown midrib strap from base to tip, then attach broad wing lobes to each side by cutting deep V-notches into a continuous membrane outline (lobes must share the midrib's outline, not be drawn as separate shapes). Add the sporophyll as a densely convoluted ruffled collar of small overlapping wavy folds bunched at the bottom 15% of the stipe. Recolour to olive-brown → deep green-brown and kill the specular highlight on the strands.

rows.readsAs: a palm tree, or a dandelion clock with brass beads
rows.defect: The trunk is a flat salmon-pink capsule with perfectly rounded ends and constant width top to bottom — a geometric primitive with no taper, no bark, no root flare, and no branches at all; it simply ends inside a grey fog blob with a hard silhouette-free stop. The crown is that fog blob plus ~12 pale feathery fronds radiating out of the centre like wheat ears or palm fronds — the leaflets are tiny, numerous and same-sized, the opposite of 5-9 big smooth-edged leaflets. No grey furrowed limbs anywhere. The three nuts are perfect brown spheres with a hard specular dot, reading as metal ball bearings hovering in the fog rather than husks hanging on twigs.
rows.fix: Give the trunk a tapering, slightly irregular outline with a widening root flare and grey furrowed bark texture, and split it into 3-4 heavy ascending limbs that continue into the crown so the branch/crown junction is grown not overlapped. Drop the crown fog layer entirely. Rebuild the leaves as pinnate sprays of only 5-9 LARGE oval leaflets each (leaflet length ~1/4 of the frond, smooth edges), mid green with bronze on young tips, hanging with gravity rather than radiating like a starburst. Replace the spheres with slightly ovoid, matte, dull-green husks with a faint suture line, attached at the tip of a visible twig.

rows.readsAs: a bottle brush or a horsetail stalk — and it is nearly the same drawing as Water Mint in this batch
rows.defect: A perfectly straight, uniform-width green rod runs floor to ceiling with pale blue-white leaflets stamped in machine-regular mirrored rows down both sides — the spacing, size and angle repeat identically, which reads as a bottlebrush or a printed pattern, not foliage. Leaflets are pale ice-blue, not mid green, and are simple smooth teardrops with no sharp teeth and no twice-pinnate structure. The stem is plain green: no hollow look, no purple streaks or blotches, so the single most diagnostic mustRead is absent. The umbel is a tiny dark disc capped by a white crescent, smaller than the leaf mass and reading as a nail-head, not a flat-domed umbel of many small flowers. No chambered root is shown.
rows.fix: Break the regularity: vary leaflet length, spacing and angle, and build true twice-pinnate structure (each side branch carrying its own row of leaflets) rather than leaflets straight off the main axis. Recolour leaflets mid green and give them sharp saw-teeth with veins running into the notches. Add purple blotching/streaking as irregular mottling on a stem that swells and tapers. Enlarge the umbel to 2.5-3x its current width, build it from many visible individual pedicels fanning up from one node into a flat-topped dome of tiny white florets, and expose a swollen chambered rootstock at the base.

rows.readsAs: a water lily — correct, but it looks like a paper cutout on a dish
rows.defect: The read is basically right, but everything is a primitive. The water is a hard-edged perfect ellipse with a crisp outlined rim, so the plant sits on a grey dinner plate rather than in water. The three pads are perfect flat ellipses with a smooth airbrushed radial gradient and no venation and no red-purple underside; the notch is a single hairline slit rather than a wedge cut to the centre. The pads simply overlap each other with hard edges and no contact ripple. The flower is a tiny 6-point white star sitting on the middle pad, closer to a daisy sticker than a lily bloom, and it has no visible relationship to a stem or pad.
rows.fix: Replace the elliptical water plate with a soft, irregular, edge-fading surface (no rim stroke) and add a small ripple/meniscus ring where each pad meets it. Cut a real wedge notch (angular, reaching the pad centre) instead of a slit, add radiating veins from the notch apex and let a sliver of red-purple underside show on the raised pad lip. Give the pad outline a slightly wavy, non-elliptical edge. Enlarge the flower 2x and build it from layered pointed tepals with a yellow stamen boss, seated in the water with its own reflection.

rows.readsAs: an aster or a purple daisy on a willow shoot — and the stalk is the same template as Water Hemlock in this batch
rows.defect: The flower is a purple DAISY — a ring of separate radiating strap petals around a distinct orange-brown centre disc — not a rounded lilac pompom head, so the key mustRead is contradicted, not merely missing. The leaves are narrow lance/willow blades with perfectly smooth edges (no teeth), bright teal-green with no purple-bronze flush, and they are pinned to the stem in a regular herringbone that reads as machine-repeated. The stem is a single hairline of constant width with no square-section shading or edge lines. Every leaf meets the stem at the same angle with a hard little join.
rows.fix: Rebuild the flower head as a dense spherical pompom of many tiny lilac-pink tubular florets with protruding stamens, no central disc and no separated petals. Change the leaf shape to short toothed OVALS in clearly opposite pairs (pairs at 90 degrees to the pair below), flushed purple-bronze along the edges and midrib. Render the stem as a square section — two shaded faces with a visible corner ridge — and thicken it with slight taper. Vary leaf size down the stem.

rows.readsAs: a generic bamboo or willow sprig with green washers threaded on it
rows.defect: An upright S-curved vine standing out of a ground shadow — there is no water, no floating habit, and no trailing runner, so the whole 'aquatic, floats and roots at the joints' read is absent. The leaves are narrow pointed lances, not arrowheads or heart shapes, and none of the three white funnel flowers with purple throats appear anywhere. In their place are flat dark-green rings — literal donut outlines — stuck along the stem at intervals; they have no depth, no attachment point and no plausible botanical identity. The stem is a single flat ribbon of constant width with no joints or nodes.
rows.fix: Lay the stem horizontally as a trailing runner on a water surface, thicken it and articulate it with swollen nodes, and drop white threadlike roots into the water from each node. Reshape the leaves to arrowheads with two flared basal lobes on visible petioles, alternating along the stem. Replace the flat rings with proper funnel flowers: a five-lobed white trumpet seen in slight perspective with a dark mauve-purple throat and a visible tube joining the node.

rows.readsAs: a red coral sea fan, or a sumac in autumn colour — the same radial-frond template as Walnut in this batch
rows.defect: The whole plant is CRIMSON RED against dark brown rachises — the reference calls for dark glossy green, so the colour is not off-tone, it is a different plant. The layout is a perfectly symmetrical radial peacock fan of ~14 stiff brown spokes each carrying identical red blobs, mirrored left/right about the centre line. There is no floating mat, no water, no succulent hollow stems, and no white threadlike roots at the nodes — all three mustReads absent. The leaflets are featureless red lozenges, all the same size, so there is no larger terminal leaflet. A single vertical brown stalk rises from the fan centre topped by a white nail-head cap that does not resemble tiny four-petal cress flowers.
rows.fix: Recolour the entire plant dark glossy green and the stems to pale succulent green-white. Destroy the radial fan symmetry: sprawl a few thick hollow stems roughly horizontally across a water surface at varied angles and lengths. Make each frond a short pinnate spray of 5-7 ROUNDED leaflets with a noticeably larger terminal leaflet at the tip. Add tufts of fine white roots hanging from the stem nodes into the water. Replace the white cap with a loose cluster of tiny four-petal white flowers on thin pedicels.

rows.readsAs: a cannabis plant with a blue-green bowling ball
rows.defect: The leaves are unmistakable cannabis leaves — five to seven narrow, sharply pointed, serrated fingers radiating from one point — instead of deeply cut leaves with ROUNDED lobes and wavy edges. Five of them stand bolt upright at even spacing along a dead-straight horizontal stem like pickets in a fence, all the same size and same angle. The melon is a perfect circle in flat teal-cyan with four dark stripes painted across it as arcs; the stripes are clearly sprayed on top and do not follow the fruit's curvature at the poles, and teal-cyan is not a watermelon colour. The fruit floats against the stem with no attachment peduncle and no contact deformation with the ground. Only one tiny tendril spiral is present.
rows.fix: Reshape the leaves to broad blades with 3-5 ROUNDED, wavy-margined lobes, grey-green and matte-hairy, and let them flop at varied angles and sizes rather than standing upright in a row. Curve and branch the runner so it wanders rather than ruling a straight line, and add several branched coiling tendrils at the nodes. Recolour the melon to warm mid green, make it a slightly flattened oval rather than a circle, seat it into the soil with a contact shadow and slight flattening at the ground line, and draw the stripes as wavy bands that converge at the poles so they wrap the volume. Attach it with a short thick peduncle to the runner.

rows.readsAs: A dried ornamental fountain grass or a pampas-grass clump — or, because of the bone colour, a spray of white feathers.
rows.defect: Reads as grass, which is more than most of this batch manages, but it fails the reference on two counts. The whole tuft is bone-white / pale cream with a faint warm cast — not the specified blue-grey green, and not any colour a living grass is; it looks bleached or dead. And there is NO seed head. The mustRead calls for a 'compact narrow seed head' and nothing in the picture is a head: the only granular detail is a fine speckled stipple scattered along the upper third of the long arching blades, which reads as noise on the blade, not as spikelets gathered into a spike. The blades also radiate in a full 360-degree fan from a single point rather than sitting stiffly in two ranks like little combs, and there is no runner, stolon or spreading turf — it is one isolated fountain-shaped clump floating over an elliptical drop shadow. Blades are long, soft and gracefully arching, the opposite of 'short stiff narrow'.
rows.fix: Recolour the blade gradient to a desaturated blue-grey green (roughly #7d9484 base to #a8bcae tip) with a thin chalky salt-crust highlight only on the upper margins, not the whole blade. Add the missing harvest: a single narrow straw-coloured spike, 3-4 blade-widths tall, standing above the tuft on one stiffer culm, built from small overlapping spikelet lozenges. Shorten blades to roughly 60% current length, stiffen the arc so tips only just bend, and re-order the blade angles into two opposing ranks (left set and right set, near-zero blades pointing at the viewer) so the comb reads. Add two or three low side-tufts joined by a near-ground runner to sell the spreading turf.

rows.readsAs: A rocket nose cone, a blue crystal shard, or a closed umbrella — nothing organic.
rows.defect: This is not a plant. The image is a single solid royal-blue cone — a smooth bullet or nose-cone silhouette, wide flat base, perfectly straight-tapering sides, one sharp apex point — filled with vertical ribbed stripes of alternating light and dark blue. There are no leaves of any kind, no finger-lobed segments, no umbel, no clump, no branching, no rock. The outline is a pure geometric primitive with machined straight edges and bilateral perfect symmetry; the interior stripes are evenly spaced flat bands, clearly a procedural fill rather than plant tissue. The colour is vivid electric blue, not blue-grey green. Every one of the three mustRead features is absent.
rows.fix: Discard this render entirely — the form router has handed a 'spike/cone' primitive to a herb. Rebuild as a low bushy clump: 4-6 sprawling stems radiating from a base wedged against a rock lump, each stem carrying 2-3 orders of THICK blunt cylindrical finger segments (rounded ends, no points), swollen at the middle. Recolour to glaucous blue-grey green (#8fa89a with a waxy pale bloom). Crown two or three of the stems with flat-topped umbels: a short umbrella of 8-12 rays each ending in a tiny greenish-yellow floret cluster. Aspect should be wider than tall at the base, not a vertical spire.

rows.readsAs: A badminton shuttlecock, a pendant lampshade, or a turquoise paintbrush held bristles-up.
rows.defect: Also not a plant. It is an inverted cone — narrow at the bottom, flaring wide at the top, cut off by a flat horizontal top edge — made of about ten identical bright-cyan/turquoise ribs that all converge to a single point at the ground. The top is capped by a few short dark grey stubs. Nothing branches; nothing tangles. There are no gas floats at all (the mustRead's defining feature — 'small round pea-like gas floats on short stalks' — is completely missing), no toothed leaf-like blades, and no bushy mass. The colour is saturated aqua/teal, about as far from 'golden olive-brown to tan' as the palette allows. The silhouette is a hard geometric funnel with straight edges and radial symmetry, and each rib is a flat two-tone stripe with a hard-edged specular line down its centre.
rows.fix: Rebuild from scratch on a branching frond skeleton: one holdfast, a main axis, then 3-4 orders of irregular side branches with random splay so the mass reads tangled rather than radial. Hang small elliptical toothed blades (serrated margins, visible midrib) alternately along every branch, and stud the branch axils with 10-20 small spherical floats, each on its own short stalk so the bead sits clear of the branch. Recolour the entire mass to olive-brown / tan (#8a7038 to #b99a52) with darker branch cores. Aspect 1:1 as specified — currently it is a tall funnel.

rows.readsAs: A bunch of purple grapes, or a cluster of plums on a skewer.
rows.defect: Reads as a bunch of grapes, not a cress. The picture is dominated by six or seven enormous overlapping PURPLE spheres, each nearly a third of the canvas, packed into a wide lobed mass. They are smooth shaded balls with a visible hard seam line running horizontally across the largest one on the right — a straight machined edge cutting a perfect circle in half. Through the exact centre runs a dead-straight thin brown stick, ruler-perfect from top to bottom, passing IN FRONT of the spheres with a hard silhouette edge and no join, no taper, no attachment point at either end — a part stuck on, not grown. At the very top of that stick is one tiny white crescent, presumably the flower head, at maybe 1/40th the scale of the leaves. Colour is wrong (purple, spec says glossy mid-green), leaf shape is wrong (perfect spheres, spec says heart/kidney-shaped stalked plates), scale is wrong, and the 'small white cross-shaped flowers' mustRead is reduced to an unreadable white smear.
rows.fix: Kill the sphere primitive — the leaf generator is emitting spheres where it should emit flat blades. Draw leaves as small flat cordate plates with a notched base and a short curving petiole that visibly meets the leaf blade at the notch; scale them to roughly 1/8 of current diameter and scatter 15-25 of them in a low sprawling cushion. Recolour to glossy mid-green (#4e7a3e to #7fae5c) with a soft specular sheen, not purple. Replace the straight stick with 3-4 short curved flowering stems that emerge from between the leaves and taper. Enlarge the flowers into visible clusters of four-petalled white crosses, 6-10 per head.

rows.readsAs: A poinsettia, or a red water-lily / dahlia bloom.
rows.defect: This reads as a flower, not a leaf rosette, and the colour is the loudest error in the batch: the entire plant is bright crimson-pink with a pale white-pink glow at the centre. The spec calls for 'very dark glossy green' leaves. Leaf shape is wrong too — every element is a sharp-tipped lanceolate spear with straight edges, arranged in a tidy radiating symmetrical fan, where the reference asks for thick triangular-to-diamond blades with WAVY margins. There is not a single wave in the picture; every edge is a straight line from base to point. No red stems are visible (they would be invisible anyway against red leaves), and the mustRead 'wiry ropes of green flower spikes trailing outward' is entirely absent — no spike, no seed knob, nothing. The silhouette is a clean symmetric mound with hard faceted panels and a flat gradient fill per petal; it looks like a vector logo.
rows.fix: Recolour to very dark glossy green (#1c3a20 to #2f5b2c) with a strong wet specular highlight, and give each blade a red-purple midrib and petiole so the red reads where it belongs. Replace the pointed spear silhouette with a broad triangular blade, blunt tip, and drive a sine ripple along both margins plus a matching ripple in the shading so the leaf reads as buckled, not flat. Break the radial symmetry — a basal rosette sprawls unevenly and some leaves fold under. Add the harvest: 3-5 long thin wiry stems trailing sideways out of the rosette, beaded along their length with tiny green flower knots.

rows.readsAs: A bunch of dried yarrow, fennel or golden-rod — a florist's dried arrangement.
rows.defect: There are no berries. The mustRead's first and defining feature — 'orange berries crowded directly on the thorny branch' — does not appear anywhere. Instead each of the five upright stems terminates in a small yellow-ochre pom-pom floret cluster held at the tip, which reads as an umbel of flowers, not fruit, and puts the harvest in the wrong place (buckthorn berries clothe the stem, they do not cap it). There are also no thorns: the stems are smooth, unarmed, and unbranched. The leaves are wrong — small flat yellow lens/almond shapes stuck onto the stems at regular alternating angles with a visible hard join where the leaf edge meets the stem edge; they read as separate decals rather than growth, and they are yellow-gold, not silver-grey. The whole plant is monochrome yellow-olive with no woody bark tone, and the bundled stems fuse into a solid trunk-blob at the base that has no visible root or branching logic. It is a herbaceous bouquet, not a shrub.
rows.fix: Move the harvest onto the stems: pack 30-60 small spherical orange berries (#e8801c to #f4a83a, each with an offset highlight) tightly in clusters directly against the twig along the middle and upper stem, overlapping so they crowd. Add sharp woody thorns — short rigid spurs at a steep angle off the main branches, a few carrying berries. Recolour leaves to silver-grey-green (#93a396) with a pale scaly stipple on both faces, narrow them to willow proportions (roughly 6:1), and taper their base into the stem so there is no seam. Give the stems grey-brown bark, real woody branching, and aspect 0.9 (wider than tall) rather than the current tall vertical bunch.

rows.readsAs: A fern frond, a bottlebrush, or a stylised conifer sapling.
rows.defect: The render is the exact thing the reference note warns against. It is a single ruler-straight vertical green rod, dead centre, running the full height of the frame, with dozens of tiny identical pointed leaflets in strict evenly-spaced rows down both sides — a feathery, pinnate, machine-repeated pattern. The note says explicitly 'its leaves are fat and fleshy, quite unlike the fine hair-like foliage of true fennel', and the mustRead says 'thick succulent finger-shaped leaf segments, NOT feathery threads'. Every leaflet is the same size, same angle and same flat green fill, with a hard join line where it meets the stem — stuck on, not grown. There is no clump: one stalk, no branching, no rock. The umbel is a tiny flat yellow half-disc perched on the stem tip like a cap, with no visible rays or florets, at maybe 1/12 the width it should be. Aspect is roughly 3:1 tall where the spec asks 1.1 and a LOW clump.
rows.fix: Replace the pinnate leaflet generator with fat segments: 3-5 blunt cylindrical fingers per leaf, each rounded at the tip, swelling at the middle, no points anywhere, and only 2-3 divisions deep.
