Break the single stalk into 5-7 stems fanning out low and sideways from a base wedged into a rock, total height about equal to width. Recolour to glaucous waxy blue-green (#7d9c8c) with a pale bloom. Rebuild the flower head as a proper umbel: 10-14 visible rays radiating from one node, each ending in a small greenish-yellow floret ball, forming a flat plate 3-4x its current diameter. Vary leaflet size and angle so nothing repeats identically.

rows.readsAs: A bouquet of statice or everlasting flowers — a dried florist's posy, not a coastal shrub.
rows.defect: Wrong plant entirely, and it is a recolour of Sea Buckthorn in this same batch — identical construction: the same bundle of straight stems fused into a solid base blob, the same small flat lens-shaped leaves stuck alternately along them at identical angles with hard seams, the same pom-pom cluster capping each stem. Only the palette changed (cream-white leaves, dusty pink-purple pom-poms). Against the reference: there are no dinner-plate round leathery leaves — the leaves here are tiny slivers roughly 1/20 the required area, elongate not round, with no heart-shaped base and no red veins at all. There are no dangling grape strings — the fruit reads as upright flower heads at the stem tips, the exact opposite of hanging. There is no windswept spreading shrub habit; it is a narrow vertical bouquet. All three mustRead features fail. The cream-white leaf colour is also wrong against 'glossy deep green'.
rows.fix: Route this off the herb/bouquet template onto a woody shrub. Draw 6-10 LARGE circular leathery leaves, each 100-140px across at 440px canvas, held nearly flat and overlapping, with a notched cordate base, a thick pale midrib and 5-7 bold red-pink lateral veins fanning to the margin; recolour to glossy deep green with one or two older leaves shifted to orange-red. Build a stout low branching trunk that spreads sideways wider than tall. Replace the tip pom-poms with 2-3 pendulous strings hanging DOWNWARD from leaf axils, each strung with 12-20 round fruits graded green at the tip to purple-red at the base.

rows.readsAs: a dead pampas/spider-plant rosette with a nail hammered through it
rows.defect: A squat fountain of pale grey-white ribbon blades with a single short central stalk topped by a tiny gold cylinder and a flat triangular fan. Three mustReads fail: there is no water at all (no surface line, no reflection, no emergent stance), the plant is short and wide rather than 'very tall emergent', and the seed head is a closed 2mm-wide bottlebrush stub, not an open branching panicle — no branch arms, no separated dark grains, nothing purple-brown. Blade colour is desaturated white-grey, not mid green, so the whole thing reads as a dead ornamental grass. The blades are identical mirrored crescents fanning from one point, with a visible pinch where every blade converges into the same node — a stuck-on rosette rather than a tussock of separate culms.
rows.fix: Draw water: a horizontal surface band across the lower third with the culms cutting through it and a soft reflection. Raise aspect so the culm is at least 2x the leaf mass. Replace the bottlebrush with a real open panicle — 6-10 thin branch rachillae splaying alternately off a central axis, each carrying separate elongated purple-brown grains with awns. Recolour blades to mid green. Stagger blade origins along a short vertical culm base instead of one convergence point.

rows.readsAs: a teal agave or spider plant — and specifically the same plant as Wild Rice in this batch
rows.defect: This is the same picture as Wild Rice with the hue rotated: identical mirrored-crescent blade fountain, identical convergence pinch at the base, identical thin central stalk with a small gold bottlebrush and a flat fan cap. Side by side the two are indistinguishable in silhouette. The spike is far too small and too smooth to read as 'stiff bristly' — the awns are a fringe of tiny even ticks about 8px long confined to the very top fan, not 'long straight awns like whiskers' projecting past the spike. Blade colour is saturated tropical cyan-teal, nowhere near blue-grey green, which pushes it towards an agave/aloe. There is no tufted clumping base — one point, one rosette, no separate tillers.
rows.fix: Differentiate from Wild Rice at the silhouette level: give rye a dense multi-culm tuft (4-6 distinct shoots each with their own base) and shorter, stiffer, more upright blades. Enlarge the spike to 25-30% of total height, build it from overlapping two-ranked spikelets, and extend awns as long straight hairs 1.5x the spike length radiating past its outline. Desaturate the foliage heavily toward blue-grey green.

rows.readsAs: an ear of wheat or a golden fern frond
rows.defect: A single straight gold-orange stem with about eight pairs of small pointed lance-shaped leaflets angled upward in perfect herringbone symmetry. Every mustRead fails. The stem is a smooth tapered line with no square section, no facets, no edge highlight. The leaves are narrow pointed slivers, not big paired broad ovals, and they have completely smooth edges — no teeth — and flat gradient fill, no crinkling, no vein network, no purple backing. There is no flower or seed spike anywhere. The colour is wheat-gold, not mid green. The leaflets are identical stamped copies at identical angles, attached by a hard butt joint against the stem with no petiole and no swelling where they meet.
rows.fix: Rebuild as perilla: 3-4 pairs of large broad ovate leaves, each 3-4x current area, with a visibly serrated margin, a sunken pinnate vein net and a bumpy quilted surface, on short petioles that flare where they join. Give the stem a square profile by drawing two lit faces and a shadowed corner ridge. Recolour to mid green with purple undersides on the back-facing leaves. Add a one-sided terminal raceme of tiny pale capsules.

rows.readsAs: a wild strawberry — correct
rows.defect: Genuinely readable — red berry with white surface seeds, two white five-petal flowers with yellow centres, and a long runner trailing right to a plantlet bud. But the leaflets are smooth-edged ovals with a single painted midrib: the mustRead 'toothed leaflets' and 'sunken veins' are simply absent, and only four leaflets exist in total so the trifoliate grouping never reads. The berry is a flat symmetric heart with seeds placed as an even grid of identical white dots sprayed on the surface rather than sitting in dimples. The flowers are perfectly regular five-petal decals — identical petal width, identical spacing, no overlap or tilt. The runner is a single clean bezier of constant width ending in a lollipop ball, with no roots, no nodes and no leaf on the daughter plant.
rows.fix: Add sawtooth serration to every leaflet margin and press 3-4 lateral veins in as darker sunken creases. Group the leaflets explicitly in threes on a shared petiole. Give the berry an irregular cone shape, a green calyx, and set each achene into a small shadowed pit with a highlight. Break flower symmetry — vary petal widths and let petals overlap. Taper the runner, put a visible node with thread roots and a small trifoliate rosette at its tip.

rows.readsAs: a cluster of oyster mushrooms or a stack of pearl-white balloons
rows.defect: Not a plant. The image is a fan of roughly twelve overlapping pale blue-white semicircular discs, each a perfect half-circle with a smooth radial gradient and a thin hairline crease across it, radiating from a point at bottom centre. There is no stem, no stalk, no petiole, no green anywhere, and nothing arrowhead-shaped. It is built entirely from geometric primitives — literal perfect circles clipped in half — and the hard hairline seams between discs are the only structure. Every mustRead fails: no downward-pointing arrowhead leaves, no long erect stalks, no ground clump.
rows.fix: Complete rebuild. Draw 4-6 individual peltate leaves as true arrowhead blades — a broad rounded body with two rearward basal lobes and a notch between them — each hanging with the tip pointing down and slightly cupped, on its own long erect purple-flushed stalk that attaches inside the blade (peltate) rather than at the edge. Stalks all rise from one crown at soil level. Colour mid green with pale radiating primary veins and a few beaded water highlights. Add a brown fibrous corm half-exposed at the base.

rows.readsAs: a fishbone diagram, or a single stem of aster/echinacea
rows.defect: A single tall vertical stalk with about eleven pale blue chevron strokes stacked up it and one flat purple daisy on top — it is the Wild Sesame template with line-strokes instead of leaflets. The aspect is inverted: the mustRead demands a ground-hugging mat much wider than tall, and this is roughly 1:3 tall and narrow with a single stem. The 'leaves' are bare straight lines with no width, no oval form and no pairing you can perceive as leaves. There is one solitary flower, not dense domed heads, and it is a flat radially perfect daisy with a brown button centre — nothing two-lipped, nothing mint-family about it. No woody stems, no bronzing, no mat.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a creeping mat: several thin woody stems running horizontally and radiating outward across the ground plane, filling far more width than height. Populate them with hundreds of tiny paired oval leaves — actual filled shapes a few pixels across in opposite pairs — in dark grey-green with bronze tips. Cap the stem ends with several domed clusters of small two-lipped pink-purple corollas, each cluster a mass of overlapping tubular florets rather than one flat daisy.

rows.readsAs: a bunch of grapes or a string of purple berries on a vine
rows.defect: An S-curved grey stem carrying eight glossy purple spheres arranged in pairs, plus a few small dark spiral tendrils. The 'leaves' have been rendered as inflated three-dimensional balls with specular highlights — there is not one heart shape and not one vein anywhere, so two mustReads die outright. There is no support to twine around, so the stem just floats in an S with nothing spiralling; and there is no tuber at the base at all, the stem simply ends in mid-air above the shadow. The spheres are near-perfect circles of two repeated sizes, each meeting the stem at a hard tangent line with no petiole, and the colour is uniform violet — nothing green.
rows.fix: Replace every sphere with a flat cordate leaf: broad rounded lobes, a basal notch, a drawn-out tip, and 5-7 veins arcing from the base to converge at that tip. Recolour mid green. Add a vertical support (a cane or trunk) and wind the stem around it in a real helix, passing behind and in front. Attach each leaf on a short petiole with a visible swelling at the node. Add a large knobbly brown tuber, part-buried, at the stem base.

rows.readsAs: an olive tree or a generic lollipop shrub on a stick
rows.defect: A lollipop tree: a straight tapered brown wedge of a trunk with a spiky ball of stiff, dark, narrow leaves radiating outward from its top like a palm or olive. The defining mustRead — a mass of long slender drooping whip-like twigs — is entirely absent; nothing hangs down, every leaf points up and out. There are no visible twigs or branches at all, only leaves stuck directly onto the crown mass, and they meet the trunk top at a hard flat silhouette junction with no branching transition. The trunk is a smooth featureless taper with zero fissuring or bark texture, and it reads as a paddle handle. Leaf undersides are all one dark grey-green — no silvery pale flicker. The catkins are four vertical strings of identical evenly spaced circles floating flat over the foliage, unmistakably sprayed on top rather than hanging from anything, and a grey haze blob sits behind the crown unattached to any form.
rows.fix: Rebuild the crown from pendulous structure: a short trunk that forks into 3-4 rising limbs, from which dozens of thin whips fall in long catenary curves reaching most of the way to the ground, and hang the narrow lance leaves alternately along those whips so the outline is vertical streamers, not a ball. Alternate leaf fills between mid green and a much paler silver so the crown flickers. Cut deep vertical fissures and colour variation into the trunk, taper it less mechanically, and lean it. Attach catkins to individual twig tips with a visible peduncle and vary their size and angle; delete the free-floating grey haze.

rows.readsAs: a lump of turquoise brain coral, or a Pac-Man ghost, with a TV aerial stuck in the top
rows.defect: The whole plant is a bright turquoise/cyan mound of smooth glossy balloon-lobes, split by two hard straight seam lines (one vertical down the centre, one diagonal across the right lobe) that read as machined cuts, not leaf edges. Reference calls for DARK GLOSSY GREEN — nothing on screen is green. The critical mustRead is inverted: the maroon flower is NOT hidden at ground level under the foliage, it is a row of four tiny pink squares floating on a perfectly straight 1px green line that rises ~80px ABOVE the top of the leaf mound, like an antenna stuck into the blob. There is no soil-level cup flower, no hairy stalks, no kidney-leaf notch — the lobes are featureless spheres with an airbrush highlight.
rows.fix: Recolour the leaf mass to dark glossy green (#1d3a24 body, #4a7c4f specular sheen) and kill the cyan entirely. Kill the vertical mast: move the flower to the base — a single dark maroon-brown three-lobed cup sitting ON the ground plane at the front, partly occluded by the leaf edges, with a short (8-12px) fuzzy stalk. Replace the sphere-lobes with two paired kidney leaves: add the basal sinus notch and a curled outer margin so the silhouette has a heart cleft, not a bubble outline. Remove the hard seam strokes — separate the two leaves by an overlap shadow instead of a drawn line.

rows.readsAs: a red cordyline or a ti-plant/bromeliad in a pot, with a few unripe crab apples wired on
rows.defect: The foliage is bright crimson-pink, not matt mid-green — nothing in this picture is a guava leaf colour. Every leaf is the same identical pointed lozenge stamped in a rigid herringbone ladder up the branches (perfectly regular alternating angle, machine-repeated), with no quilted parallel side-veining at all. The mustRead flaking copper-and-grey mottled bark is entirely absent: the trunk is a flat brown geometric cone with two straight machined edges and a hard-cut horizontal top where the foliage begins. The four fruit are small hard green spheres with a black stalk dot on top — no calyx crown, no yellow-green ripening. No white flowers with stamens anywhere.
rows.fix: Recolour leaves to matt mid-green with a paler downy underside on the reversed ones. Draw 5-7 impressed parallel lateral veins per leaf and dent the leaf surface between them for the quilted read. Replace the cone trunk with an irregular tapering bole and paint the mottled bark: patches of copper-orange peeling off over grey-green, soft-edged, no straight silhouette lines. Enlarge the fruit ~1.8x, shift to pale yellow-green, make them pear-shaped, and add the dried five-point calyx crown at the far tip. Add 2-3 white flowers with a visible burst of stamens.

rows.readsAs: a child's drawing of an orange tree, or a peach tree — not a mango
rows.defect: Generic lollipop fruit tree. The trunk is a flat ochre-yellow stick with parallel straight sides and no taper, and it vanishes into the canopy at a hard horizontal cut — no branching, no root flare, a clear stuck-on seam where trunk meets crown. The crown is a soft olive-green airbrushed CLOUD with individual leaf dashes sprayed on top of it rather than growing from twigs; you can see the blurred blob edge behind the leaves. The mustRead 'tall dense DARK crown' fails twice: it is neither tall (a wide mushroom cap, wider than high) nor dark (pale yellow-olive). The mustRead 'fruit dangling on long stalks' is absent — five orange-brown spheres sit flat on the canopy surface with no stalk, no pendulous drop. Leaves are short flecks, not long leathery lance leaves.
rows.fix: Darken the crown to deep green with bronze flushes and make it a tall narrow forest-tree ellipse (height ~1.5x width). Replace the airbrush blob with layered leaf masses and visible interior branch structure so leaves attach to twigs. Give the trunk taper, a root flare at the base, and 2-3 branches that enter and divide inside the canopy instead of a flat cut. Lengthen the leaves into drooping lance shapes clustered in whorls at shoot tips. Re-hang the fruit: 15-25px pendulous stalks so the fruit hangs BELOW the foliage edge, and reshape them from spheres to slightly ovoid green-yellow.

rows.readsAs: a cyan aquarium plant or a spiky bromeliad vine with a single gourd tied on
rows.defect: Reads as an aquatic or tropical ornamental, nothing melon-like. Leaves are electric CYAN — the reference asks for grey-green and bristly. Their shape is a symmetrical pointed star/rosette (like an aloe or an anemone), not a deeply cut rough cucurbit leaf with a heart base. The mustRead 'ground-running vine' fails: the stem is a vertical S-curve climbing UP the frame with a shadow puddle beneath it, so it reads as an upright plant, not a sprawler. Only ONE fruit is present, and it is a tan-gold ribbed sphere sitting in a leaf socket rather than a green globe mottled with pale stripes. Tendrils are present but drawn as perfect flat spirals — identical machined curls, no varying pitch.
rows.fix: Recolour foliage to dull grey-green with bristly stipple; kill the cyan. Reshape the leaves into palmately 5-lobed cucurbit leaves with a basal sinus and rough irregular margins — no radial star symmetry. Reorient the whole composition horizontally: run the main stem left-to-right along the ground plane at the lower third to satisfy aspect 2.4, with leaves and fruit sitting ON the ground. Add 2-3 more fruit and repaint them as small hard green globes with pale longitudinal stripes, one flushing yellow. Vary the tendril coils — different radii, one uncurled and searching.

rows.readsAs: a stalk of wheat or a lavender stem — the gold colour makes it read as dried grass
rows.defect: Nothing about this is mint. Leaves are GOLD-YELLOW, not mid green, and they are smooth pointed almonds with completely clean margins — the mustRead 'toothed' is absent from every single leaf. The mustRead 'square stem' is absent: the stem is a plain round tapering yellow line with no visible facet or edge highlight. The mustRead 'flowers in rings around the stem, not just at the tip' is directly violated — the ONLY flowers are a single lilac bobble-spike at the very apex; the leaf axils below are bare. Leaves are also perfectly evenly spaced up the stem in a mechanical ladder, and the aspect is a tall narrow spike rather than the specified 0.9 near-square bushy herb.
rows.fix: Recolour leaves and stem to mid green. Add 6-9 saw teeth per leaf margin and shorten/broaden them to a toothed oval. Render the square stem literally: two parallel edge highlights with a shaded flat face between them, and show the corner at the base. Move flowers into whorled rings — a dense ball of tiny pale lilac florets encircling the stem at each of the top 3-4 leaf axils, plus a terminal one. Broaden the whole plant to aspect ~0.9 with a second and third stem branching from the base and irregular internode spacing.

rows.readsAs: a red bottlebrush or a celosia plume — or, unkindly, a caterpillar skewered on a stick
rows.defect: A solid salmon-RED bottlebrush column. Both flower mustReads fail outright: there are NO four-petalled yellow flowers in a cross anywhere — the only yellow is one tiny crescent smudge balanced on top like a hat — and there are NO slender beaked seed pods held out from the stem. The entire body is one dense repeating stack of identical red triangular spikes with perfect radial symmetry, machine-stamped at a fixed interval, giving a straight-sided rectangular silhouette. Foliage colour is wrong (spec: mid green, rough-hairy). The specified 0.7 aspect (wider than tall) is rendered as a tall narrow column. The stem is a bare brown toothpick at the bottom with a hard join where the red mass starts.
rows.fix: Rebuild from the reference: green rough-hairy foliage — big-end-lobed leaves at the base grading to narrow toothed leaves up the stem, irregularly spaced. At the apex put a real corymb of yellow flowers, each drawn as four petals in a visible cross. Below the flowers, hang slim green pods angled OUT from the stem at ~45 degrees, each ending in a pointed beak — that stage transition (flowers above, pods below) is the whole identity of the plant. Widen and branch the plant to aspect 0.7 and break the radial symmetry so no two leaf ranks match.

rows.readsAs: purple fountain grass or a cordyline with a white mushroom cap floating over it
rows.defect: The mustRead 'ball of tiny flowers' is not rendered as a ball or as flowers — it is a single flat white LENS, a perfect geometric half-ellipse disc, sitting on the stalk like a mushroom cap or a satellite dish. No individual florets, no pink, no spherical volume. The mustRead 'papery membrane bursting under the flower head' is absent. The leaves are vivid MAGENTA-PURPLE where the spec says grey-green, and they are flat tapering ribbon blades, not tubular or channelled — no fold-line down any blade. There is no bulb at the base; the blades just converge into a dark point. The one thing that works is the tuft gesture and the bare stalk.
rows.fix: Recolour the leaf tuft to grey-green with a waxy bloom; the purple should live only in the flowers. Rebuild the umbel as a sphere of 25-40 individual six-tepalled pink-white florets on short radiating pedicels — visible gaps between them so the silhouette is bumpy, never a smooth disc. Add the split papery spathe as two translucent tan flaps hanging just below the head. Give each leaf a channel: a darker centre groove and a rolled edge so it reads tubular. Add the pale bulb swelling where the blades meet the soil, with a hint of papery outer tunic.

rows.readsAs: a white lotus blossom, or a paper snowflake — and it is a near twin of Wild Ginger in this batch
rows.defect: Pure WHITE leaves — the spec says dark green with red-flushed veins, so the colour is not merely off, it is inverted. Leaf shape is a sharp-pointed maple/star with long straight machined edges and flat facets; the mustRead 'huge puckered rough-textured crinkled leaves with WAVY margins' fails on every count — the margins are ruler-straight and the surface is a smooth flat gradient with zero pucker. The mustRead 'stout red-tinged ribbed stalks springing from a crown at ground level' is entirely missing: there are no petioles at all, the leaf mass just floats as a mound, and the single thin GREEN line running up the middle is a flower stem, not a stalk. Worse, this is compositionally the same drawing as Wild Ginger in this same batch — identical bilobed mound plus a dead-straight central mast topped with a beaded pink spike; only the leaf tips and hue differ.
rows.fix: Recolour to dark green with red flushing along the main veins. Replace the star-maple leaf with a broad triangular-heart blade: wavy undulating margin, deep palmate venation, and a puckered/blistered surface between the veins (bump-shade the interveinal panels). Draw the stalks — 3-5 stout ribbed petioles, red at the base fading green, radiating from a visible ground-level crown, each carrying one leaf so the leaves are clearly held UP rather than piled. Thicken the flower spire into a tall foamy cream panicle instead of a thin beaded wire, and offset it from dead centre. Then re-check against Wild Ginger: these two must not share a skeleton.

rows.readsAs: a stubby brown lollipop-tree with four glowing lemon-coloured baubles in a cloud of dust — a generic fruit tree, closest guess 'lemon' or 'orange'
rows.defect: The fruit — the one thing that names this species — is four perfect glowing yellow-green spheres with a soft bloom halo. There is not a single rib, wing, angle or star-section on any of them; they read as light-emitting berries, not carambola. No lilac-pink flower clusters anywhere on the trunk or old wood, so a second mustRead is simply absent. The trunk is a flat brown capsule: constant width top to bottom, semicircular cap at the bottom, no root flare, no taper, no bark texture, and it terminates in a hard rounded line where it enters the canopy — a visible stuck-on seam rather than branches growing out. The canopy itself is a brown-grey airbrushed haze blob with pinnate leaflet sprigs radiating out of it like pins in a pincushion; the sprigs are all near-identical stamped copies at even angular intervals and none of them connect to a visible branch.
rows.fix: Rebuild the fruit as a five-ribbed prism: draw each fruit as a tapered body with 3 visible longitudinal wings (2 full-face, 1 edge-on) meeting at sharp crests, waxy pale-yellow faces with darker green-brown crease shadows in the valleys, and kill the radial glow entirely — replace with a specular highlight on the wing crests only. Add small clusters of 4-6 tiny lilac-pink flowers directly on the trunk and thick branches (cauliflory). Replace the capsule trunk with a tapered trunk that flares into surface roots at the base and splits into 3-4 real branches whose bases blend into the trunk (draw branch and trunk as one path, no butt-joint). Delete the brown haze blob and let the canopy read as overlapping pinnate fronds hanging on those branches, with leaflet size varying and rachis curvature randomised per frond.

rows.readsAs: a fern frond or a conifer seedling with a few red berries at the tip — nobody would say tulip; closest guess is 'yarrow' or 'a young pine'
rows.defect: This is not a tulip in any respect. It is a tall thin vertical green stem carrying about twelve pairs of narrow V-shaped chevron leaflets marching evenly up its entire length, topped by three or four tiny flat red heart/blob shapes about 10px across. Every mustRead fails: there is no cup flower (the red bits are small flat lozenges, no petals, no pointed tips, no cup volume), there are no broad grey-green basal strap leaves at all, and the stature is the opposite of short — the plant is roughly 2:1 tall where the reference asks for aspect 0.5 with the flower close to the ground. The leaflet pairs are identical stamped chevrons at perfectly even spacing, and each one meets the stem as a hard straight line with no petiole or base swelling. Colour is a saturated emerald, not blue-grey.
rows.fix: Discard the current geometry and rebuild as a bulb form: 2-3 broad channelled strap leaves emerging from ground level, each 8-12x wider than the current leaflets, blue-grey-green with a waxy sheen, wavy-edged and curving outward and down; a single bare stem no more than ~1.5x the leaf height; and one cup flower at the tip built from 6 tepals with narrow pointed recurved tips, scarlet with a dark basal blotch, showing interior shadow so it reads as a cup and not a flat blob. Remove every chevron leaflet from the stem — a tulip stem is bare.

rows.readsAs: a sheaf of wheat, or a lit torch — an upright bundle of golden straw, not a seaweed
rows.defect: The blade is split into six or seven separate parallel fingers running the whole length of the plant, with dark gaps between them — this directly violates the 'one unbranched ribbon blade, never split into fingers' mustRead. Margins are perfectly smooth: no crinkle, no frill, no ruffle anywhere on the outline, so the second mustRead also fails. There is no stipe and no branching holdfast; all the fingers converge to a single sharp point that just touches the ground shadow. The whole thing stands bolt upright and is taller than it is wide, where the reference asks for aspect 0.25 (a long horizontal drifting belt). Three glowing yellow rounded lozenges are pasted flat on top of the blade at intervals — they have no relation to kelp anatomy and read as applied decoration. Colour is a hard saturated gold, not warm olive-brown.
rows.fix: Collapse the fingers into ONE continuous blade of roughly uniform width and re-lay the composition horizontally to hit aspect 0.25. Build the frill into the silhouette: displace both margins with a low-frequency sine plus noise so the edge undulates in and out, and paint the resulting ruffles with alternating lit/shadowed bands so the blade reads as physically buckled rather than outlined. Add a dimpled bullate central band (irregular dark puckers in two loose rows) down the midline. At the base add a short cylindrical stipe splitting into 5-8 finger-like haptera gripping a rock. Recolour to olive-brown with a wet glossy specular streak, and delete the three yellow lozenges.

rows.readsAs: an unopened tulip bud on a wire, or an abstract logo of a sprouting seedling — no viewer would say carnivorous plant
rows.defect: Nothing carnivorous is visible. The plant is a perfectly straight machine-drawn dark purple line — constant width, ruler-straight, no taper — with two smooth green almond leaves in a V at the very top and a row of nine short grey vertical tick marks floating in an arc above them. All three mustReads fail: there are no red tentacle hairs and no dew droplets (the grey ticks are flat opaque bars with hard ends, no gloss, no bulb, and several of them float clear of any leaf with a visible gap between tick and leaf — parts sitting in space rather than growing out of tissue); there is no ground-level rosette of paddle leaves at all (the two leaves are held ~300px up in the air); and there is no arching scorpioid flower stalk. The two green leaves are mirror-image copies of one identical almond shape, and each meets the stem at a hard point with a bright bloom used to hide the join.
rows.fix: Rebuild from the ground up: a flat rosette of 6-9 round-to-spoon paddle leaves seen from above/three-quarters, each on its own slender petiole, radiating at uneven angles, leaves overlapping and foreshortened. Cover each paddle with 20-40 crimson tentacles drawn as fine tapering hairs that emerge from the leaf surface (start them inside the leaf outline, no gap), each terminating in a small translucent sphere with a bright specular dot and a dark refracted core so it reads as glue. Add one slender flower stalk that rises from the rosette centre and curls over in a scorpion-tail crozier, carrying 3-5 small five-petalled white flowers. Recolour leaves green flushed crimson toward the margins. Never draw the stem as a straight constant-width line — give it taper and a slight bend.

rows.readsAs: a lavender flower spike, or a purple caterpillar climbing a stick, with a small daisy stuck on top — the yellow head is read as an unrelated ornament
rows.defect: The picture is dominated by a tall column of about eighteen stacked lavender-purple pillow lobes — smooth, identical, inflated, arranged in two mirrored files up the stem — with a single tiny yellow daisy about 45px across perched on the very top. This inverts the species: the mustRead is 'one huge head on a thick single stalk', and here the head is the smallest element in the frame while the foliage is a giant purple caterpillar. The leaves are not heart-shaped, not green, and not coarse — they are featureless mauve balloons with airbrushed highlights, no veins, no serration, no sandpaper texture, and each one meets the stem at a hard notch. The seed disc is a plain dark dot with no spiral packing and no visible striped seeds. The stalk is a thin pale grey pole, not thick and bristly, and it is visibly too slender to carry the mass above it.
rows.fix: Invert the mass budget: the head should occupy 35-45% of the frame width. Rebuild it as a broad disc with two interleaved Fermat spirals of individual striped seeds, a fringe of maturing florets at the rim, and a single ring of long yellow ray petals with notched tips and slight droop/curl variation. Recolour foliage to mid-green and reshape to large cordate leaves with a pointed tip, basal lobes flanking the petiole, visible pinnate veins, toothed margins, and a stippled matte texture for the hair; alternate them up the stem rather than stacking mirrored pairs, and vary their size and droop. Thicken the stem to 3-4x its current width, give it green colour, longitudinal grooving and short bristles on the silhouette edge, and blend each petiole into the stem with a swollen base instead of a notch.

rows.readsAs: a lavender or a purple ornamental fern frond — 'mint' would not be anyone's guess, and it is easily confused with the Steppe Tulip render in the same batch
rows.defect: The flowers are wrong in position and form: instead of ring-like whorls of lilac florets clustered at the leaf axils, there is a single narrow white-grey beaded spike sticking out of the very tip of the stem, with a visible bare gap of stem between it and the topmost leaves — it reads as a separate object skewered onto the plant. The leaves fail the 'toothed oval' mustRead entirely: they are long narrow smooth-edged lance blades with perfectly clean margins, no serration anywhere, and they are violet-purple rather than mid green. The stem shows no square cross-section — it is a flat dark grey line of constant width with no facet shading or ribbing. The leaf pairs are all drawn in a single flat plane rather than decussate, and each pair is a mirrored copy of the same stamped shape, giving an even ladder that reads mechanical. Silhouette is nearly identical to Steppe Tulip in this same batch: same tall thin central stem, same evenly-spaced paired blades.
rows.fix: Re-shape leaves to short broad ovals about 2:1 with clearly serrated margins (cut 6-10 forward-pointing teeth into the outline, not painted lines), sunken pinnate veins, and recolour to mid green keeping only the stem and petiole purple-flushed. Rotate alternate pairs 90 degrees so pairs cross at each node, and foreshorten the pairs that point at the viewer. Give the stem a square section by shading two visible faces differently with a crisp corner ridge down the middle. Delete the terminal spike and instead place tight ring-shaped whorls of small two-lipped lilac flowers wrapped around the stem AT the upper leaf axils, so the flower ring and the leaf pair share the same node.

rows.readsAs: pink pampas grass or a cordyline / phormium ornamental — a decorative fountain grass, not sweet flag
rows.defect: Colour is completely wrong: the leaf fan is hot magenta-pink shading to dark plum, where the reference calls for bright yellow-green — nothing about this reads as a wetland plant. The leaves are not upright sword blades; they are thin arching whip-like strands that curve outward and droop, several of them bending past horizontal, so the 'fan of upright sword leaves' mustRead fails. Margins are smooth outlines with no crimp or wave at all. The spadix is in the wrong place: the yellow-green beaded finger sits vertically at the very TOP TIP of the central stem, directly contradicting the note that it must jut out sideways at an angle partway up the flat stem — and it sits above a stretch of bare dark stem with a hard colour change where the two meet, reading as a bead-string glued onto a pole. All the blades converge to a single knife-point at the ground with no rhizome or basal sheathing.
rows.fix: Recolour the entire fan to bright yellow-green with paler translucent edges. Straighten the blades: keep them mostly vertical with only the outermost 20% of the length falling away, and give each a flat sword profile with a visible off-centre midrib and a twist so some show face and some show edge. Crimp the margins by displacing the outline with a small-amplitude wave along its full length and shading the resulting undulations. Move the spadix down to roughly 45-55% of the stem height and angle it out at 30-45 degrees from a flattened green scape, rendering it as a dense stubby cylinder of tiny diamond florets that emerges continuously from the stem tissue rather than butting against it. Add a thick pinkish-cream rhizome with ring scars at the base and sheathing leaf bases wrapping it.

rows.readsAs: a bunch of green grapes, or a string of glass marbles on a vine — the shape says grape cluster before it says root vegetable
rows.defect: The tubers are seven near-perfect glossy spheres of identical size, each with a hard straight equator line ruled across it — they are exactly what the note forbids ('smooth and tapered, never round'), and the equator line plus the plastic specular highlight makes each one read as a moulded bead or a Christmas bauble. They are also bright teal-turquoise, which is neither orange nor purple-red. There are no ground-hugging runners: the whole composition is a single stem running diagonally across the frame with the spheres bunched along it like grapes, and it floats in the middle of the picture rather than spreading wide along the ground. The leaves are effectively missing — only a handful of tiny dark curl glyphs a few pixels across sit beside the stem, with no heart shape, no three lobes, no petioles of any length. Every sphere touches the stem at a single tangent point with a visible dark gap, so the tubers read as beads threaded onto a wire rather than growing from anything.
rows.fix: Reshape every tuber to an elongated spindle: 2.5-3.5x longer than wide, tapered to a point at both ends, with subtle asymmetric bulges, fine longitudinal skin wrinkles, a few thread roots at the narrow ends, and NO eyes and no equator line. Recolour to coppery orange or deep purple-red with earth-dusted matte skin. Move them below a ground line so they read as buried, and connect each to the plant by a visible stolon that widens continuously into the tuber body. Above ground, replace the diagonal bunch with 2-4 runners spreading horizontally and low, wide enough to hit aspect 2, carrying full-size cordate or three-lobed leaves on long petioles, mid-green with purple veins and purple-flushed stems. Vary tuber size — a real crop yields a range, not seven clones.

rows.readsAs: A lit tiki torch, or a feather-duster / sea pen with three glowing eggs in it
rows.defect: Nothing in the picture is sea grapes. It is a tall orange-to-brick-red inverted teardrop made of ~10 straight vertical strands that all pinch into a single point at the bottom, with THREE glowing orange pill-shaped lozenges stacked on the centre line. The mustRead colour (translucent bright emerald green) is absent — the render is warm orange/rust. There are no beads: the three lozenges are stretched capsules on the midline, not clusters of tiny stalked spheres. There is no horizontal creeping runner at all; the whole thing converges to one pinch point on a black ground ellipse. The strands are perfectly regular parallel ribbons with machined edges, and the outer silhouette is a smooth symmetric teardrop with no organic variation. Worst of all it is pixel-for-pixel the same template as Seagrass in this same batch, recoloured orange instead of amber.
rows.fix: Rebuild the form entirely: lay a horizontal creeping stolon across the lower third of the frame, root it with fine rhizoids at 3-4 irregular points, and send up 5-7 upright shoots of DIFFERENT heights from it. Clothe each shoot in dozens of tiny (4-8px) spheres on short individual stalks — the beads must be many and small, not three big pills, and must sit around the shoot's circumference so the shoot reads as bumpy in silhouette. Recolour to translucent emerald with a bright specular dot on each bead. Delete the parallel-ribbon fill and the shared teardrop envelope, and break the template link with Seagrass so the two do not share a routine.

rows.readsAs: A lotus or water lily, or an agave, with a map pin stuck behind it
rows.defect: A bilaterally perfect lotus/water-lily rosette of ~11 smooth SHARPLY POINTED lance leaves in glowing turquoise, plus one tiny white half-disc on a long naked wire stem floating high above the foliage. Two mustReads fail outright. (a) 'cabbage-sized crinkled blue-grey leaves': these leaves have hard straight taper edges and a single straight central vein, no crinkle, no undulation, no lobing, and the colour is a saturated tropical turquoise, not glaucous blue-grey with waxy bloom. (b) 'white flower cloud on top': there is no cloud — a single 26px mint hemisphere sits on a bare stalk like a pinhead or a mushroom cap. The flower stem also does not grow from anything; it drops behind the leaf mound and its base is hidden, so the harvest part reads as a separate object planted next to the plant. Perfect left-right mirror symmetry makes it read as a decal rather than a grown plant.
rows.fix: Replace the pointed lance leaves with broad ovate blades whose margins are driven by a low-frequency noise-warped outline (deep rounded lobes plus a high-frequency crinkle on top), and add cross-vein puckering so light pools in the crinkle troughs. Shift leafColour to desaturated blue-grey green with a pale waxy bloom highlight and a purple tint on the inner young leaves. Flatten the mound (wider than tall) so it spreads. Replace the single hemisphere with a broad froth of 60-100 tiny four-petalled white florets on a visibly BRANCHED corymb, and root that inflorescence in the centre of the rosette so the branch structure emerges from between leaf bases rather than appearing above them. Break the mirror symmetry.

rows.readsAs: A fern frond or a horsetail with a lollipop / map-pin on top
rows.defect: A single perfectly straight vertical stem carrying eleven identical, evenly spaced OPPOSITE pairs of pointed turquoise leaflets, topped by one small mauve hemispherical cap. All three mustReads fail. There is no flat-topped cloud of tiny papery flowers — just one solid purple half-dome primitive with a visible hard rim where it meets the stem. There are no wiry BRANCHING flower stems: the axis is unbranched and, contrary to the row, it is leafy right up to the flower head. There is no basal rosette of leathery spoon-shaped leaves pressed to the mud at all — the stem simply enters a black ellipse. The leaflet pairs are stamped at a fixed angle and fixed spacing with a hard seam at each attachment point, so they read as stuck onto the stem, not grown out of it. This is also the same skeleton as Sea Rocket in this batch (straight rod + stamped opposite leaf pairs + one flower primitive), just teal/purple instead of brown/white.
rows.fix: Delete the leafy spike entirely. Build a flat basal rosette of 7-9 leathery spoon-shaped (spathulate) dark-green leaves lying almost flat on the ground, then send up 2-3 wiry LEAFLESS stalks that fork repeatedly (3 levels of branching) and flare outward so the tips all terminate at roughly one height, making a broad flat-topped spray. Populate the tips with hundreds of 2-3px papery violet-blue florets with a paler chalky calyx, drawn as a dusty cloud with irregular density, not a solid dome. Vary branch angles per-instance. Break the shared skeleton with Sea Rocket.

rows.readsAs: A wine glass or a champagne flute; failing that, a calla lily
rows.defect: A single opaque, near-symmetric goblet — the silhouette is literally a wine glass: a perfectly STRAIGHT horizontal top edge with two sharp square corners, sides that curve down and pinch into a stem, and a small green disc at the base. That flat machined top edge is the single most damning thing in the frame; nothing organic terminates in a ruled line. 'Ruffled lettuce-like frilled margins' — the headline mustRead — is entirely missing: the margins are smooth arcs with zero frill. 'Paper-thin translucent' fails too: the sheet is a flat opaque sage-green fill with three faint straight radiating lines and no background showing through, no overlap darkening, no light passing edge glow. Colour is dull grey-sage, not the vivid almost-glowing grass green called for. The disc holdfast is the one mustRead that lands, but it is a perfect flat circle primitive.
rows.fix: Drive the whole outline with a high-amplitude, high-frequency sine/noise warp so the margin is deeply frilled and self-overlapping — the frills are the species. Build it from 3-5 separate overlapping sheets at different angles rather than one blob, and render each with alpha ~0.55 using additive/multiply overlap so crossings read darker and the sheet reads as one cell layer thick. Recolour to vivid saturated grass green with a bright rim where light passes through a fold. Kill the straight top edge outright — the upper margin should be the most ruffled part. Replace the circular holdfast with a small irregular knobbly pad gripping a pebble.

rows.readsAs: A scallop or clam shell, or a barrel-cactus cluster, with a pink asterisk sticker floating above it
rows.defect: Off-body artifact: the pink star flower is FLOATING free in the black void roughly 80px above the plant, with no stem, no pedicel and nothing connecting it to anything. That alone is a blocker, and it directly contradicts the mustRead 'pink star flower TUCKED AGAINST THE STEM' — it could not be further from the stem. The body below is five fat smooth teal egg/balloon shapes fanned in a symmetric rosette; they are not narrow, not paired, not opposite, and they have no stem — there is no visible stem anywhere in the frame, so 'sprawling reddish stems' and 'rooting at the nodes' both fail, and the 'mid green with red-purple stems' colour is a uniform tropical teal. The mustRead 'low mat sprawling flat' fails: this is a compact upright clump, and the reference aspect of 2.4 (a wide flat mat) is not honoured. Each blob is a clean gradient ellipse with a hard outline — obvious geometric primitives, and the fan arrangement makes it read as a scallop shell.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a prostrate mat: 3-5 reddish-purple stems radiating outward and lying flat, each with a slight zigzag and visible swollen nodes with root hairs dropping from them into the sand. Hang plump but NARROW (roughly 4:1) succulent leaves in true opposite pairs along those stems, mid green, with a fleshy translucent rim highlight rather than an outline. Then attach the pink five-point flower in a leaf axil, small, half-hidden between a leaf pair and the stem — it must be drawn as a child of a stem node so it can never detach. Ensure the flower's anchor point is validated against the body mask before compositing so no future roll can strand it in the void.

rows.readsAs: A generic olive or herb sprig, or a plastic aquarium plant
rows.defect: A dead-straight dark brown dowel running the full height of the frame, with five identical evenly-spaced opposite pairs of pale blue-white almond leaves clamped onto it, and one white six-petalled flower. Every mustRead fails. 'Fleshy lobed leaves with rounded lobes': the leaves are perfectly smooth pointed lens shapes with no lobing whatsoever. 'Sprawling zigzag branching over sand': the stem has zero zigzag and zero branches — it is a ruler-straight vertical rod that continues bare well above the topmost leaves and simply stops in mid-air. 'Lilac cross-shaped flowers with jointed pods': the single flower is WHITE with SIX petals (not four, not lilac, not cross-shaped) and there is not a single seed pod anywhere. The leaves are also alternate in the reference but stamped as strict opposite pairs here, at a fixed identical angle, each with a hard dark seam where it meets the stem. Same skeleton as Sea Lavender in this batch.
rows.fix: Replace the straight rod with a low sprawling stem that changes direction at every node (a real zigzag) and throws 2-3 side branches, all leaning across the ground plane rather than standing vertical. Cut the leaves in pinnate rounded lobes down each side of a midrib and thicken them so they read succulent (soft internal glow, no hard outline), and stagger them alternately with varied angle and size. Rewrite the flower to four petals in a cross, pale lilac fading to white, in small terminal clusters of 4-6, and add the diagnostic fat two-jointed corky pods below the flowers along the stem — the pods are what make this species identifiable. Trim the bare stem overshoot above the last leaf.

rows.readsAs: A lit torch or a wheat sheaf; identical to Sea Grapes Algae in this same batch
rows.defect: This is the SAME IMAGE as Sea Grapes Algae in this batch with the hue shifted from orange to amber/gold — same inverted-teardrop envelope, same ~10 straight parallel ribbons converging to one pinch point, same three glowing pill lozenges stacked on the midline, same black ground ellipse. As seagrass it fails on every count. Colour is golden brown, not mid-green darkened by silt. The blades are not flat ribbons with rounded tips — they are hard-edged strips that taper to points and are bundled into a single closed cone, so there is no meadow and no sense of separate shoots. 'All leaning one way with the current' fails: the bundle is bilaterally symmetric and dead upright. 'Horizontal creeping rhizome with shoots at intervals' is completely absent — everything converges to a single point. The reference aspect of 0.7 (wider than tall) is inverted: the render is roughly 1:3 tall and narrow. The three glowing lozenges are pure invention for a species whose harvest row says nothing is visible.
rows.fix: Draw a horizontal rhizome running across the frame just under the sand line, with fine roots below and 4-6 shoots rising from it at irregular intervals. Give each shoot a flattened fan of 3-5 long ribbon blades of even width with ROUNDED tips, and bend them all in the same direction along a shared current curve with slightly different phase and amplitude per blade so they cross and overlap. Widen the composition to the 0.7 aspect so it reads as a meadow, not a torch. Recolour to mid green with darker silt/epiphyte mottling toward the blade bases. Delete the three glowing lozenges. Critically: this species must not share a draw routine with Sea Grapes Algae — one of the two is being routed to the wrong generator.

rows.readsAs: A potted cyan houseplant, or a blackberry / elderberry bush
rows.defect: The closest to shippable in the batch — it does read as a multi-stemmed shrub with berry clusters — but three things break it. (1) The base is a solid flat green TRAPEZOID with a ruled straight top edge, sitting under the shrub like a plant pot or a wedge of turf; the stems visibly poke out of the top of that block with a hard seam, so the trunk zone reads as a separate object the branches were pushed into. It also contradicts 'slim GREY multi-stemmed trunks' — the trunks are a single green mass. (2) leafColour is specified mid green (bluish when young) but rendered as a hot neon cyan-turquoise that looks lit from inside, and every leaf is the same small pointed lens at the same size, giving a sprayed-on texture rather than foliage. (3) The berries are near-black maroon knobbly clusters that read as blackberries or elderberries; the mustRead calls for round BLUE-PURPLE pomes with a starry five-point crown scar, and there is no crown scar visible on any of them. The white strap-petalled flowers of the mustRead are simply not present.
rows.fix: Delete the trapezoid base and replace it with 4-6 slim GREY-BARKED trunks that continue as tapering lines down into the ground, splaying slightly from a common root crown, with the branch tapering continuous from trunk to twig so there is no seam. Desaturate the foliage to a true mid green with a bluish tint on the youngest tip leaves, vary leaf size 0.7-1.4x and angle, and thin the density so gaps of dark sky show through. Repaint the berries as separate round pomes in blue-purple with a pale waxy bloom and a small dark five-point star scar drawn on the tip of each — the crown is the diagnostic. Add a few sprays of white narrow strap-shaped petals on the outer branches to satisfy the flower mustRead.

rows.readsAs: a hot-pink plastic sea anemone, or a magenta cycad/palm fan — nobody would say fern, and certainly not a native green one
rows.defect: The whole plant is hot magenta-pink — every frond, rachis and leaflet. The row asks for dark glossy green and this is a saturated fuchsia with pale pink highlights; nothing in the image is green. Form is also wrong: instead of a tight upright shuttlecock the fronds splay into a low sideways fan roughly 1.6x wider than tall, several arching almost horizontally past the pot line, so the silhouette reads as a spreading palm rosette. Four or five fronds terminate in a bare rounded pink club — the leaflet comb simply stops ~30px short and leaves a naked capsule tip, which is a machined primitive poking out of the foliage. The leaflets themselves are identical straight triangular spikes stamped at even spacing along both sides of every rachis with no size falloff toward the tip, and there is no basal hook on any of them. No rust-brown sori anywhere.
rows.fix: Set the leaf palette to dark green (~#1d4023 base, #2f6b34 lit face, glossy specular streak along each leaflet) and delete the magenta ramp. Narrow the crown: raise the frond emergence angles to 60-85 degrees from horizontal so the outer fronds arch up-and-out rather than sideways, and bring the aspect to ~1.1 tall. Run the leaflet comb all the way to the frond apex, tapering leaflet length to near zero at the tip so no bare rachis club is left. Give each leaflet an asymmetric base with a small forward-pointing auricle/hook on the upper edge, and shorten leaflets progressively toward the frond tip. Add two rows of small rust-brown sori dots on the fronds whose undersides face the viewer.

rows.readsAs: a dandelion clock or a glowing fuzzy lollipop on a popsicle stick
rows.defect: The trunk is a flat brown capsule — two perfectly parallel straight vertical edges and a semicircular rounded top — pasted over a blurred ball of olive fog. Where it disappears into the canopy there is a hard-edged seam: the crisp brown rectangle just ends inside the soft blob with no branching, no flare, no boughs. Nothing grows out of anything. The canopy itself is a radial-gradient yellow-olive smudge with about twenty small yellow caterpillar-like combs scattered on its surface, all the same size and all pointing outward from the centre like pins in a pincushion; they sit ON the fog rather than being lit by it, and the fog has no leaf structure of its own. There is not one hanging pod in the picture — no cinnamon-brown, no crook, nothing pendulous at all, so the harvest mustRead is entirely absent. The overall glow makes it read as a light source rather than foliage.
rows.fix: Replace the capsule trunk with a tapering trunk that splits into 3-5 ascending boughs which then divide into twigs inside the crown, so the canopy is carried on visible structure. Kill the radial glow blob: build the crown from many overlapping small pinnate sprays in mid green (#4c7a2e / #6a9c3d) at varied scale and rotation, densest at the top and ragged at the silhouette edge, rather than a blur with combs stuck on. Add the missing harvest: 8-12 curved, knobbly cinnamon-brown pods (#7a4a22) hanging vertically from twigs at the lower edge of the crown, in loose clusters of two or three, drawn in front of the foliage so they read.

rows.readsAs: a bundle of dead twigs or a straw broom with a few pink pipe-cleaners tied on
rows.defect: The plant is entirely bare — there is no foliage of any kind. What should be feathery scale-clad twigs is a bundle of about forty straight, hard-edged orange-tan sticks of uniform width, crossing each other at sharp angles like a besom broom or a pile of dropped matchsticks. Every stem is dead straight; not one arches, so the 'slender arching wind-blown branches' mustRead fails, and the blue-grey green of the row appears nowhere — the whole plant is warm ochre, the colour of dead wood. The pink flowers are present but as only six small isolated pink caterpillar-shaped spikes floating at the top on otherwise naked sticks; they are nothing like 'clouds of fine plumes', and each attaches to its twig with a visible blunt butt-joint. The base is a solid tan trowel-shaped wedge with straight sides that the sticks emerge from as a hard seam.
rows.fix: Clothe every twig: draw each branch as a soft blue-grey-green (#7d9184) feathery cord built from many tiny overlapping scale marks along its length, so the branch line itself becomes the foliage and no bare ochre stick is visible except on the lower main stems. Curve the branches — apply a consistent gravity/wind bend so the upper thirds droop and sweep to one side. Multiply the flower plumes to 25-40 and cluster them densely over the outer third of the crown, letting them overlap into a haze of pink at the silhouette rather than sitting as six separate objects. Replace the wedge base with a short flaring multi-stemmed trunk whose stems continue upward into the branches instead of terminating at a seam.

rows.readsAs: a pile of tangerines, or a croissant — no viewer would call it a plant at all
rows.defect: This is not a plant. The image is a heap of eight or nine overlapping orange spheres and half-spheres, each a clean radial gradient with a crisp circular outline, piled into a fan-shaped mound; a single thin straight line runs across the right-hand lobe like a scored crease. There is no stalk, no petiole, no stem, no root, no corm, and no green anywhere in the frame. Every mustRead fails: no elephant-ear leaves, nothing pointing downward, no peltate stalk attachment, no brown ringed corm. The forms are perfect geometric circles with hard edges where they overlap, the definition of stuck-together primitives, and the colour is pumpkin orange against the row's dull mid green.
rows.fix: Rebuild from scratch as a herb: 4-6 thick upright pale-green petioles rising from a common base, each carrying one enormous heart-shaped blade tilted so the pointed tip hangs downward, blade colour dull mid green (#3f5f34) with a matte waxy sheen and a few beaded water droplets, pale radiating main veins from the point where the stalk meets the blade. Attach the stalk INSIDE the blade a short way up from the notch (peltate) with the two basal lobes overlapping behind it, not at the notch edge. At ground level add one brown corm with concentric ring scars and coarse fibrous hairs. Remove every sphere primitive from the recipe.

rows.readsAs: a dried sprig of chamomile or a generic gold wildflower posy
rows.defect: Not a bush. It is a thin sparse V-shaped spray of maybe six stems rising from a small trowel-shaped base, with roughly twenty leaves total and a lot of empty background between them — the 'dense twiggy rounded bush' mustRead fails outright. The colour is wrong in a way that dominates the picture: every leaf and stem is dry wheat-gold/tan, not dark glossy green, and there is no hint of a pale new shoot because the whole plant is already pale. Leaves are identical symmetrical pointed lens shapes duplicated at two sizes, all with perfectly smooth outlines — no serration is visible on a single one — and each meets its stem at a hard point with no petiole. The five flowers are flat vector daisies: a perfect circle of eight identical white petals around a perfect yellow disc with radial spokes, drawn face-on and upright rather than nodding, with no boss of stamens.
rows.fix: Recolour to dark glossy green (#20401f base with a #4a7a3a lit face and a hard specular highlight) and tint the top two leaves of each shoot pale yellow-green so the harvest reads. Triple the stem count and shorten internodes to build a dense rounded twiggy mound roughly 0.9 aspect, filling the silhouette so no large background gaps remain. Cut fine sawtooth notches into each leaf margin and vary leaf outline, tilt and curl per instance. Rebuild the flower: nod it downward on a short pedicel, give it 5-7 slightly irregular cupped white petals and a dense tuft of individual yellow stamen filaments rather than a spoked disc.

rows.readsAs: an electric-blue barbed-wire bush, and unmistakably the same plant as the Tea card in this batch, just recoloured
rows.defect: It is the Tea render again with a different palette — same trowel base, same V-spray of stems, same five flat white-and-yellow spoked daisies in the same arrangement at the same heights. Here the stems and leaves are electric periwinkle blue (#4a5bd0-ish), which matches nothing in the row: no bright fresh green, and the papery white peeling bark mustRead is completely absent — the single short trunk is a plain grey-blue tapered wedge with no texture at all. The foliage is not fine or soft: it is about fifty straight blue dashes of uniform length stuck at fixed angles onto straight stems, reading as barbed wire rather than needle leaves. There are no bottlebrush spikes anywhere — the creamy cylindrical flower spikes are replaced by the same daisies used on the Tea card, so the most identifying feature of the species is missing.
rows.fix: Recolour foliage to bright fresh green (#6fa04a) and the trunk to off-white. Give the trunk real papery bark: layered irregular pale sheets with curling dark-shadowed edges peeling away from the surface. Replace the straight dashes with very fine soft needles, several per node, drawn short and slightly curved and dense enough that the twig masses into a soft plume with a fuzzy silhouette. Delete the daisy flower primitive from this species entirely and replace it with cylindrical bottlebrush spikes — a 30-40px stretch of twig ringed with dense creamy-white filaments radiating in all directions, with the twig continuing out the far end — plus a few clusters of small woody grey seed capsules gripping older twigs. Also diverge the branching structure from the Tea recipe so the two cards are not the same drawing.

rows.readsAs: a fishbone diagram or a schematic pine sapling with one aster stuck on top
rows.defect: There are no leaves in this picture. The plant is one perfectly straight vertical green line with eight pairs of straight green line segments angling up from it — a fishbone or herringbone diagram, or a schematic conifer. Every element is a zero-width stroke: nothing has a blade, a width, a fill or an outline, so 'tiny paired oval grey-green leaves' and 'leaf edges rolled under' both fail with nothing on screen to judge. The colour is bright mint green, not grey-green. The habit is exactly inverted from the row: it is a single tall narrow spire about 2.5x taller than wide, where thyme must be a low spreading mounded subshrub (aspect 1.6, wider than tall), and there is no woodiness anywhere — no branching, no wiry tangle, one unbranched stick. The one flower is a flat purple daisy with a ring of identical petals and a perfect circular centre, an obvious geometric primitive, and it is a single large bloom where thyme carries dense clusters of many tiny florets.
rows.fix: Replace the line-segment leaves with actual filled blades: tiny grey-green (#8a9c7d) ovals 4-6px long in opposite pairs, with a darker rim on the long edges to read as rolled-under margins. Rebuild the habit as a low mound — 10-15 wiry woody stems fanning outward and drooping at the tips, wider than tall at ~1.6 aspect, with visible thin brown woody bases and green herbaceous tips. Crowd the leaf pairs at short intervals so the mass reads as fine-textured. Swap the single purple daisy for several rounded clusters of many minute pale lilac two-lipped florets sitting at the shoot tips.

rows.readsAs: a large-leaved herb — comfrey or foxglove; tobacco is a plausible guess, which no other card in this batch earns
rows.defect: The structure is right — one stout unbranched stem with six large ovate leaves stepping up it, biggest at the bottom, smallest at the top, and a terminal cluster of pink flowers — so this is the only card in the batch that reads as its own species. What fails is surface and colour. The leaves are dark blue-green, near-black in the shadows, where the row calls for pale yellow-green and matt; the plant reads as a comfrey or a rubber plant. Each leaf is the same perfectly symmetrical pointed lens shape duplicated at five scales, with a ruler-straight midrib and perfectly straight herringbone side veins that all leave the midrib at the identical angle — machined, not grown. The 'sticky hairy' texture is a scatter of about twenty pale straight tick-marks lying on top of the leaf faces and edges, clearly sprayed on rather than emerging from the surface, and none appear on the stem. The leaves butt into the stem at a hard point with no clasping base and no petiole flare, leaving a visible junction line on the two right-hand leaves. The flowers are short pink clubs on straight radiating spokes — a neat umbel of matchsticks; no flared five-lobed mouth is drawn on any of them, so that half of the harvest mustRead is unmet.
rows.fix: Shift leaf colour to pale yellow-green (#8fa04f) with a matt, slightly translucent finish and drop the near-black shadow. Vary each leaf: different outline, asymmetric halves, some droop and curl, and give the veins a curved course that fans and forks toward the margin. Make the leaf base clasp the stem — widen and wrap the base around the stalk with a shadow underneath, deleting the point-contact seam. Replace the sprayed tick-marks with a dense fine fuzz along the leaf margins and up both sides of the stem silhouette, plus a faint sheen on the blade to read as sticky. Lengthen the flowers into slender tubes 3-4x their current length and open each into a five-lobed star mouth facing the viewer, with the tubes nodding outward instead of radiating as straight spokes.

rows.readsAs: a stylised dahlia or agave sunburst — an ornamental gold rosette logo, not any real herb
rows.defect: This is not a wood sorrel at all. The picture is a flat, perfectly mirror-symmetric fan of ~15 pointed lance/petal blades in GOLDEN ORANGE, radiating from one exact point at the bottom centre, with a single ruler-straight olive stem rising out of the seam to a tiny 6-point cream star. Every mustRead fails: there is no low carpet, no trifoliate grouping, and not one heart-shaped or notched leaflet anywhere — the blades are plain tapered spearheads. Colour is wrong (must be fresh light green; rendered gold/amber). The single 'flower' is a flat 6-point star stamped on the end of a line, not a nodding five-petalled cup, and it has no purple veining. The stem is a 2px straight line with a hard butt-join into the leaf mass — a classic part-stuck-on seam. Construction is a geometric primitive: identical triangles rotated about a pivot, left half an exact mirror of the right.
rows.fix: Abandon the radial fan router for this species. Build a low sprawling clump: 6-10 SEPARATE thin arching petioles rising from a shared crown, each ending in THREE distinct heart-shaped leaflets (broad, notched apex, splayed at 120 degrees) — the notch is the whole identification and must be visible at 440px. Recolour foliage to fresh yellow-light green with a darker fold-crease down each leaflet midline. Replace the star with 2-3 nodding five-petalled cups on hair-thin curved pedicels, white/pale pink with fine purple veins radiating from the throat. Break the mirror symmetry entirely and taper/curve the petioles so they grow out of the crown instead of meeting it at a point.

rows.readsAs: a single fern frond, or a frosted horsetail — certainly not a bushy grey shrub
rows.defect: A single ruler-straight vertical green stem with two perfectly opposed ranks of silvery-white leaflets, plus a pale beaded caterpillar spike at the top. This reads as ONE fern frond, not a shrub. mustRead 'woody-based bushy clump' is entirely absent — there is no woody base, no branching, no clump, just one stalk on a flat black ellipse of shadow. Aspect is badly wrong: the row calls for 0.8 (wider than tall) and the render is roughly 1:3 tall and narrow. The leaflets are stamped decals — the SAME comma shape repeated at identical spacing on a grid, each meeting the stem at a hard dot with no petiole and no thickening, so the whole rank looks glued onto the line rather than grown from it. 'Silky felted' does not read: the leaflets have crisp hard outlines and a flat cool-white fill, more like frost stencils than downy foliage. The yellow button flowers are missing — the terminal spike is a fused beaded rod, not small nodding buttons.
rows.fix: Route this to a multi-stem shrub, not the single-frond template. Emit 7-12 stems fanning from a short thickened woody base with brown flaking bark, heights varying, each leaning outward. Make foliage twice-pinnate — the current single-order pinnae must themselves be subdivided into blunt-tipped lobes — and soften the leaflet edges with a fuzzy low-alpha halo so the silky felt reads. Vary leaflet size/angle/spacing per node so the stamped-grid repetition disappears, and give each pinna a short curved rachis so it grows out of the stem. Replace the beaded rod with sprays of separate tiny drooping dull yellow-green spheres hanging off fine lateral branchlets. Widen the whole clump to aspect 0.8 and delete the perfect-ellipse ground shadow.

rows.readsAs: the same plant as Wormwood two entries earlier, in a different colourway — or an aquarium plant with a pill stuck on top
rows.defect: This is the SAME asset as Wormwood in this batch, recoloured. Identical straight vertical stem, identical two-rank stamped leaflets at identical spacing and identical angle — the only differences are a cyan-teal palette instead of silver and a flat white half-disc cap instead of the beaded spike. Two organisms sharing one silhouette is a batch-level failure. Beyond the clone: the colour is bright turquoise/cyan, not grey-green — it reads alien. The flower head is a single solid white SEMICIRCLE, a perfect geometric primitive with a clean straight bottom edge, so 'a flat dense plate of MANY TINY WHITE DAISY FLORETS' fails — no florets are resolvable at all. Aspect must be 0.6 (broad) and the render is tall and thin. Stems are singular, not 'stiff hairy upright stemS' plural, and are perfectly smooth with no hairs. Leaflets attach at hard dots on the straight stem — stuck-on seam.
rows.fix: First, force a different silhouette from Wormwood — Yarrow is a loose clump of several upright stems, each ending in its own corymb at slightly different heights. Recolour foliage to dull grey-green, not cyan. Rebuild the flower head as an actual corymb: 30-60 individual 5-rayed white florets with pale yellow centres, packed on short pedicels that all reach the same plane, with visible gaps and an irregular outer boundary — never a filled half-disc. Subdivide the foliage a second order to get true feather-fine ferny texture and let the leaflets clasp the stem (widen at the base into a sheath) rather than dotting onto it. Add short stiff hairs along the stems and widen the clump to aspect 0.6.

rows.readsAs: a florist's bouquet of white willowherb with rowan berries stuck in — a cut arrangement, not a tree
rows.defect: The row says TREE and the picture is a hand-tied bouquet. A dozen thin stems fan up from a bundled base that has a hard horizontal seam where the stems merge into a solid green sheaf — a bound broom handle, not a trunk. No trunk, no branch structure, no crown: mustRead 'dense evergreen small-tree crown' fails outright. The leaves are WHITE and narrow-lanceolate with smooth edges; the row demands dark GLOSSY leathery OBOVATE leaves with shallow blunt teeth — wrong colour, wrong shape, wrong margin, no gloss highlight. mustRead 'small greenish-white flowers clustered at the leaf joints' is absent; the only reproductive parts are red berry clusters at the stem TIPS, whereas mate berries sit in the leaf axils. The berries are perfect uniform circles in tight rosettes. Leaves attach to stems at hard points with no petiole taper.
rows.fix: Send this through the tree router, not the herb-bundle one. Build a single tapering trunk with root flare and grey bark, dividing 2-3 times into a rounded dense evergreen crown at aspect 0.9. Recolour foliage to dark green with a specular sheen streak along each blade to sell 'glossy leathery'. Reshape leaves to obovate — widest above the middle, blunt rounded tip — and cut shallow rounded teeth into the margins. Move the red berries into the leaf axils along the twigs in small stalked clusters, break their perfect circularity, and add small greenish-white flower clusters at those same joints. Kill the bundled-sheaf base entirely.

rows.readsAs: a dandelion seedhead on a popsicle stick, or a mimosa/wattle in bloom — nothing about it says ancient churchyard yew
rows.defect: A lollipop. The trunk is a mustard-yellow CAPSULE — perfectly parallel machined sides, zero taper, a rounded bottom that floats above the shadow, no branches, no bark texture, no root flare. mustRead 'massive fluted trunk of fused stems with red-brown flaking bark' fails on every word: it is thin, smooth, uniform and the wrong colour. The crown is a translucent hazy yellow-green cloud stuck onto the top of that stick, with a visible seam where the stick disappears into it. mustRead 'dense very dark heavy crown' fails — the render glows bright chartreuse and you can see the background through it. The 'needles' are single-width perfectly straight line segments radiating outward from the centre like a sea-urchin or a dandelion clock; real yew needles are flat and set in two ranks along horizontal twigs, so both the geometry and the arrangement are wrong. The four aril clusters are flat clumps of small perfect red circles with white speckles — closed dots, not the open-ended cup with a dark seed showing that the note explicitly calls out.
rows.fix: Rebuild the trunk as a fluted column of several fused stems: irregular vertical grooves, strong taper into a wide flared base, red-brown bark broken into flaking vertical plates. Grow real branches out of it — 3-5 heavy limbs splitting and carrying the foliage, so the crown is supported rather than balanced on a point. Recolour the crown to near-black green at high opacity and give it weight (dense overlapping sprays, dark interior, no background showing through). Replace the radial straight-line needles with short flat needles arrayed in two opposite ranks along curved drooping twiglets. Rebuild the arils as individual open-topped scarlet cups, each showing a dark seed in the opening, scattered singly on the underside of the sprays instead of in four symmetric dot rosettes.

rows.readsAs: a decorative sunburst or a folded palm-frond fan logo — an agave at best, and it matches Wood Sorrel's construction closely enough to be mistaken for it
rows.defect: A flat sunburst of ~13 perfectly straight isoceles triangles in golden orange, all radiating from one exact pivot point, with the left half an exact mirror of the right. These are geometric primitives, not leaves: dead-straight edges, no curvature, no keel, no thickness, no overlap depth — the rosette is a 2D fan with no front-to-back reading at all. Colour is wrong: the row calls for blue-grey green and the render is amber/tan, which also makes it a visual sibling of Wood Sorrel in this same batch (same gold fan construction). mustRead 'curly white threads along the leaf edges' is completely MISSING — every edge is a clean unbroken line. The inflorescence is a single ruler-straight stem with FIVE tiny white bells stuck on near the top; that is not 'a tall panicle', it is a line with five decals, and the stem emerges from the pivot seam with no sheathing.
rows.fix: Recolour to blue-grey green with a paler waxy bloom. Rebuild the leaves as true swords: slight S-curve and outward twist, a visible central keel with a lighter highlight, thickness at the base narrowing to a hard brown terminal spine, and randomised length/angle so the rosette is asymmetric and layered — some leaves crossing in front of others, some flopping down. Add the diagnostic curly white fibres: 3-6 fine peeling threads springing off each leaf margin, curling loosely. Rebuild the flower spike as a real panicle — a thick stalk with 10-15 short lateral branches, each carrying 3-6 pendulous waxy cream bells, densest in the middle — rising from inside the rosette centre with a few small bracts, not butt-joined at the pivot.

rows.readsAs: Two burnt matchsticks, or a pair of tapered candles with green wax caps — not a fungus at all
rows.defect: Two of the three mustReads are simply absent: there is no white egg sac (volva) at the base — each stalk ends in a flat, perfectly elliptical disc that reads as a machined lamp base or a candle holder — and there are no flies anywhere on or near the head. The olive head is a solid flat-green thimble sitting ON the stalk with a hard, unbroken dark seam line across the join; on the left specimen the seam is a straight horizontal cut, and the cap even reads as a separate opaque object with a small notch of stalk poking through it. The head has no slime: it is flat matte olive with a single soft highlight, no glisten, no drips (the left specimen has a faint drip but the right has a hard-edged pointed lobe hanging down that reads as painted-on, not flowing). The stalk is a straight-sided tapering cone with mathematically clean edges and a uniform vertical gradient — no pitting/honeycomb texture, only a handful of soft grey blotches sprayed on the lower half that read as mildew stains rather than the pitted spongy chambers stinkhorn stalks have.
rows.fix: Grow a torn white egg sac at the base — an irregular lobed cup with ragged lip and soil clinging to it — and delete the elliptical disc plate entirely. Blend the cap-to-stalk transition: draw the head as an ovoid cap whose lower rim overhangs and drips down over the top 15-20% of the stalk with 3-5 irregular slime runnels of varying length, and give the head wet specular highlights plus a darker rim shadow rather than one flat olive fill. Replace the sprayed blotches with a real pitted network — a lattice of small elongated pits following the stalk's curve, denser near the top, so texture reads as the surface's own chambering. Add 2-4 small dark flies as silhouettes on and around the head. Break the stalk's straight silhouette with slight curvature and a bulge below the cap.

rows.readsAs: Salmon fillets or orange feathers pinned to a wooden post — or a row of willow leaves
rows.defect: Nothing about this reads as Turkey Tail. The substrate is a perfect vertical RECTANGLE with straight machined edges and sharp 90-degree corners in flat dark brown — it is a plank, not a log. The brackets are six identical pointed lanceolate blades in a single flat salmon-orange, each an exact clone of the one above it, spaced at even intervals and all pointing the same direction. The mustRead concentric banding is entirely missing: there are no rings of any kind, let alone bands varying in hue — the whole fan body is one orange gradient with two faint darker curved contour lines inside it that read as leaf venation, not growth zones. No cream wavy outer rim; the outer edge is a sharp point with a thin dark hairline. No rust/ochre/blue-grey/near-black. Not "dozens of small fans in overlapping rosettes" — six large evenly-stacked blades that barely overlap. Each blade meets the plank at a dead-flat vertical cut, a visible hard seam, so they are stuck on rather than emerging. Aspect and posture are wrong too: real turkey tail is wide and short, these are long narrow tongues wider than tall by a lot in the wrong way.
rows.fix: Rebuild from scratch. Substrate: an irregular bark-textured log cylinder with knots and a broken end, never a rectangle. Brackets: replace the six clones with 15-30 small semicircular fans of varied size, angle and overlap, clustered into rosettes with edges meeting and fusing. Each fan needs 6-10 concentric bands, alternating in HUE not just tone (rust brown, ochre, blue-grey, near-black) with a cream band nearest the rim, band widths irregular. Outer margin must be thin, wavy/lobed and pale cream, not a point. Add fine radial velvet striation across the bands.
