Kill the vertical seam by having each fan's attachment point narrow into the bark with a shadow pocket and slight upward flare so it grows out of the wood.

rows.readsAs: A potato, or a speckled rock/asteroid in space
rows.defect: This is one single monolithic blob, and yeast's entire mustRead is about multiple discrete cells. There are no rounded oval cells, no smaller bud swelling off one side, no loose cluster — just a lumpy olive-khaki mass with a few concave dents in its outline. The white dots are sprayed on top: they sit at uniform brightness with soft glows, ignore the form entirely, and crucially dozens of them float OFF the body in the black background as a halo of loose specks, which is an off-body artifact blocker. They read as dust or snow, not as bud scars (bud scars are ring-shaped craters on the wall, not bright dots). Colour is wrong — the row asks for translucent pale cream to buff, this is opaque olive-grey mud with no translucency and no internal light. The silhouette is a rock outline with faceted straight segments on the lower left and a flat-ish bottom.
rows.fix: Delete every speck that lies outside the silhouette. Rebuild as 4-7 discrete ovoid cells in a loose non-touching cluster, each with a smaller daughter bud swelling off one flank with a visible constricted neck at the join. Give each cell a translucent pale cream to buff wall: bright rim light, a darker interior with a soft nucleus-like inclusion, and light bleeding through the thin edges. Replace bright dots with a handful of shallow ring-shaped bud scars — small darker annuli with a raised lip — placed only on the cell wall and foreshortened to follow curvature. Keep it filament-free.

rows.readsAs: A generic glowing purple videogame toadstool / Alice-in-Wonderland mushroom
rows.defect: Three saturated violet-purple toadstools on bare black. The glow is a white hotspot painted on the TOP of each cap dome — exactly the opposite of the reference note, which says the light comes from the gills. There are no gills at all: the cap undersides are a plain darker purple band with zero radial lines. No rotting-wood substrate, only a flat black ellipse shadow. The colour is wrong twice over — not pale grey-cream by day, and the glow is white-lilac, not cold green-white. Construction is geometric: each stem is a straight-edged truncated cone (two perfectly straight converging lines) that butts into the cap with a hard horizontal seam, so the caps read as parts stuck on. The caps themselves are half-ellipse primitives.
rows.fix: Move the emissive source under the cap: paint a green-white radial gradient centred on the gill plane so the underside is the brightest part and the cap top is only rim-lit. Add 14-20 radial gill blades cut into that underside, each catching the light so the glow reads as coming through them. Drop cap/stem base albedo to pale grey-cream (#d8d4c6) and let ONLY the emission be green (#9ff2c0). Replace the cone stems with a slightly curved, unequal-width stalk whose top flares into the cap flesh (shared silhouette, no horizontal seam), and put the cluster on a mossy rotting-log form rather than a bare shadow ellipse.

rows.readsAs: A golf ball next to a sliced dinner roll, or a puffball
rows.defect: Both bodies are BONE WHITE, not coal-black — the single most identifying property of a black truffle is missing. The cut face is a white disc scored with about fourteen straight, near-parallel dark lines that read as a barcode or a scored bread roll; the reference asks for a lace of fine WHITE veins on DARK flesh, so the value relationship is exactly inverted. The 'warts' are small white triangular spikes sitting on top of the surface like sprinkles rather than pyramidal facets of the rind itself. The whole-truffle body is a lumpy but smooth-shaded blob with no rind texture. The background is a brown vertical gradient panel whose top edge cuts a hard straight horizontal line across the frame at roughly y=145 — a visible machined rectangle behind the subject.
rows.fix: Re-key the palette: rind to near-black (#141110) with warm brown micro-facets, flesh to purple-black (#2a1c26). Redraw the veins as branching, non-parallel, tapering white capillaries that fork and rejoin across the cut face, never straight and never evenly spaced. Build the warts as displacement on the silhouette (the outline should be visibly bumpy with pyramid tips) instead of light-coloured triangles drawn over a smooth blob. Kill the hard-edged brown gradient rectangle — either extend the soil field to the full frame with a soft vignette or remove it.

rows.readsAs: Four kitchen knives, or leaves, stuck into a fence post
rows.defect: A perfectly rectangular dark-brown bar (straight vertical sides, flat square top and bottom, hard machined edges) stands in for the trunk, and four IDENTICAL cream lens shapes — pointed at both ends, like knife blades or leaves — poke horizontally out of it. Each blade meets the bar at a hard vertical cut line: the brackets do not grow out of the trunk, they are pasted over it. None of the three mustReads is present: no concentric growth bands on the top surface, no pore layer underneath (the undersides are just a thin dark sliver), and no hoof form — these are flat two-dimensional blades. The batch note explicitly says a bracket must read as ONE thick woody hoof to distinguish it from the shelf; this renders four thin identical tiers, i.e. it renders the shelf.
rows.fix: Replace the four clones with a single large hoof-shaped mass: a thick half-dome bulging out and downward from the trunk, deepest at the attachment and thinning to a blunt rounded margin. Sculpt 5-8 concentric ridges into the top crust following the arc of the margin, each a raised band with its own shading, and colour-zone them grey-brown to rust. Show a pale cream flat underside stippled with fine pore texture. Make the trunk an irregular bark cylinder with a broken silhouette, and swell the bracket's base into the bark with a flared collar so no vertical seam is visible.

rows.readsAs: A generic golden cartoon toadstool — indistinguishable from the Death Cap in this same batch
rows.defect: This is the Bioluminescent Mushroom render recoloured gold — same three-mushroom staging, same half-ellipse cap domes, same straight-sided truncated-cone stems, same black shadow ellipse. Every distinguishing chanterelle feature is missing: the caps are smooth convex domes with a clean elliptical margin instead of a funnel with a wavy, irregularly lobed edge; the undersides are flat plain olive discs with no forking ridges and nothing running down onto the stem; and the profile is a parasol, not a vase. Stem and cap are also different colours (gold cap, olive-brown stem shading) where the reference asks for one egg-yolk yellow throughout, and the cap/stem junction is a hard horizontal seam.
rows.fix: Rebuild the silhouette as a vase: cap margin turned UP and outward, centre depressed into a funnel, margin cut into 5-7 irregular soft lobes so no two are the same width. Replace the flat underside with fat blunt ridges that fork as they descend and continue visibly down the outside of the stem (decurrent), rendered as rounded ribs with soft shadow between, not blade gills. Merge cap and stem into one continuous tapering solid of the same egg-yolk hue so there is no junction line. Reduce to one large plus one small fruiting body so it stops matching the Death Cap and Bioluminescent staging.

rows.readsAs: Blue ice shards or feathers stuck into a wooden post
rows.defect: The colour is catastrophically wrong: the shelves are pale ICE-BLUE and white. Chicken-of-the-woods is defined by brilliant sulphur-yellow to salmon-orange, and none of that hue is anywhere in the image. Structurally it is the exact same asset as the Bracket Fungus in this batch — the identical brown rectangle post with the same four identical pointed lens blades, only re-tinted. The blades are thin and sharp-edged rather than thick and fleshy, the margins are smooth and pointed rather than suede-soft and wavy-lobed, and there is no yellow pore surface underneath (just a dark sliver). Each blade meets the post at a hard vertical cut with no attachment tissue.
rows.fix: Re-key to the actual species colour: orange (#e8762c) upper surface graduating to a bright yellow (#f5c518) margin and a saturated yellow pore underside. Make the shelves thick and fleshy — the margin should have visible depth, not taper to a knife point — and cut the outer edge into overlapping soft wavy lobes of uneven length. Stack them as overlapping rosettes of different sizes at different heights rather than four evenly spaced clones. Fuse each shelf into the bark with a swollen base so the attachment reads as growth. Also break the shared geometry with Bracket Fungus so the two are not the same mesh.

rows.readsAs: A cluster of bare orange winter saplings or a leafless shrub
rows.defect: The branching is genuinely good — junctions fork out of the parent rod rather than being pasted on, and the ochre-orange is right. But the overall reading is a stand of bare winter saplings, not a fungus: three separate thin trunks rise from the ground and open into a wide crown that is broader than it is tall, with branches sweeping laterally and even drooping downward at the outer edges. The reference asks for a dense upward cluster from ONE thick base; here the base is three pencil-thin stems. Tips are fine and pointed like twigs rather than blunt or antler-forked, and every branch is a uniform-diameter rod with a rounded cap, which gives the whole thing a machined tube-and-joint feel.
rows.fix: Merge the three stems into a single fat fleshy base — a broad rounded foot at least 3x the width of any branch — and let all branching originate from it. Change the growth vector to vertical: branches should rise and stay inside a narrow upright cone, with almost no lateral sweep and nothing drooping below horizontal. Taper each branch continuously from base to tip and end it in a blunt swollen or two-pronged tip, never a fine point. Increase branch density near the top so it reads as a packed coral head, and pale the tips to cream against the ochre body.

rows.readsAs: Matchsticks or corn dogs stuck upright in a puddle of mud
rows.defect: The host insect is not there. What sits on the ground is a featureless flat brown ellipse with a handful of tiny tick marks along its edge — no head, no thorax, no abdomen segmentation, no legs, no antennae. Per the batch note this makes it 'just a club fungus', which is exactly how it reads. The six stalks are perfectly straight, uniform-width hairline rods that pierce the ellipse at a hard puncture point instead of erupting through a carapace, and two of them cross in an X that no fruiting body would make. The orange heads are separate speckled ovals sitting on the pin tips with a visible neck seam, so they read as stuck-on beads rather than a swollen continuation of the club.
rows.fix: Build a real host: a segmented ant or caterpillar in side view with a distinct head capsule, visible legs curled under it, and body segments, lying on the substrate and rendered dark brown with the fungus mycelium creeping over its joints. Have the clubs burst from specific points — the head, the thorax, the abdomen joints — with the cuticle visibly split and lifted around each exit. Give each club a continuous taper from a thick emergent base to a swollen roughened fertile tip so there is no neck seam, and add a slight organic curve so no two stalks are parallel or crossing. Reduce the count to 3-4 so the insect stays the dominant read.

rows.readsAs: The same golden cartoon toadstool as the Chanterelle in this batch — no viewer would separate them
rows.defect: Bright egg-yolk gold caps and gold stems — the species is olive-to-yellowish GREEN cap with pure WHITE gills and WHITE stem, so both of the colour anchors are wrong. The two features the note calls identifying are entirely absent: there is no white skirt-like ring on the stem, and there is no sac-like volva at the base — the stems just spike straight into the shadow ellipse. No free white gills either; the cap undersides are flat olive discs. Geometrically it is the same asset as the Chanterelle and the Bioluminescent Mushroom in this batch: three half-ellipse caps on straight-sided truncated cones, same staging, same hard horizontal cap/stem seam.
rows.fix: Re-key the cap to olive-green (#8a9a4e) shading yellow-green at the margin, and drive the stem and gills to near-white (#f2efe6) so the value split is the read. Draw a pendulous white membranous ring hanging loose around the upper stem with a slight droop and irregular edge. Most importantly add the volva: a torn, cup-shaped white bag at the base with 3-4 uneven lobes, the stem emerging from inside it and part of the cup half-buried in litter. Add faint radiating fibrils streaked across the cap surface, no warts. Flare the stem apex into the cap flesh to kill the seam, and vary the staging away from the Chanterelle's.

rows.readsAs: a lump of raw dough or a scorched potato lit from inside
rows.defect: An opaque warm ochre-brown lump floating on black, hard-edged and amorphous, dusted with orange speckles and a soft orange glow halo. Every mustRead fails: there is no leaf or fabric substrate at all, so nothing can be 'still visible through the film'; the mass is solid and volumetric rather than a thin superficial patch; and the colour is caramel-brown where the row calls for chalky white to pale grey. The silhouette is an amorphous pebble blob that is pixel-for-pixel the same shape as Mold in this same batch — only the hue differs.
rows.fix: Stop drawing mildew as a free-floating body. Paint a substrate first (a leaf blade or cloth weave filling the frame) and render mildew as a low-opacity chalky-white bloom over it, alpha 0.35-0.6, so leaf veins/weave read through the film. Kill the volumetric core shading and the orange glow entirely; palette to #e8e6df / #c9c6bb with grey-brown ageing only at patch centres. Patch edges should be ragged fractal fringes advancing along the substrate, never a closed pebble outline.

rows.readsAs: a grey asteroid or a snow-flecked river stone
rows.defect: A slate-grey amorphous blob with white speckle dots and a faint glow, identical in silhouette to Mildew. The single most identifying feature — upright stalks each topped by a dark round spore capsule — is completely absent; the white dots are flat sprayed specks with no stalks under them and they sit inside the body rather than standing off it. There is no tangled hyphal fuzz (the surface is a smooth airbrushed gradient) and no circular colony patches. It reads as a rock, not a colony.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a mat, not a body: a low field of fine white hyphal filaments drawn as many thin overlapping strokes, then 30-60 sporangiophores rising OUT of that mat (each a 1-2px pale stalk terminating in a dark blue-green or black sphere 4-8px), silhouetted above the fuzz line so the capsules break the outline. Ground it in 2-3 overlapping circular colony discs with soft concentric tone rings. Remove the pebble outline and the interior speck scatter.

rows.readsAs: a red argyle-knit gnome hat, or an Amanita with a patterned cap
rows.defect: Bright crimson-red conical head on a cream stalk. Colour is flatly wrong — the row asks tan to dark grey-brown and this is fire-engine red. The pit texture is a perfectly regular repeating diamond lattice of uniform cells laid over a smooth gradient: it reads as printed argyle wallpaper, not recessed chambers with sharp raised ridge walls, because there is no per-pit shadow, no ridge highlight, and the grid never distorts with the surface curvature. There is a hard horizontal seam where the red cone meets the cream stalk, so the head sits ON the stalk exactly as the reference forbids. Cone silhouette is a smooth unbroken dome — no ridge bumps break the outline.
rows.fix: Repalette to tan/olive-brown honeycomb with pale cream ridges. Replace the tiled diamond overlay with generated pits: irregular quadrilateral cells that shrink and skew toward the apex and the silhouette edge, each with a dark occluded interior and a lit ridge lip, so ridges catch light and pits read recessed. Break the outer contour with the ridge bumps. Delete the horizontal cap seam — flare the cone base outward and let it merge continuously into the stalk with shared shading, since a morel head is fused down to the stalk base.

rows.readsAs: gold leaves or canoes pinned to a fence post
rows.defect: A dead-straight-sided dark brown rectangle (the 'trunk') with four identical golden pointed lens shapes attached along a hard vertical line. This is machined geometry: the trunk has perfect parallel edges and square corners, and each cap is a symmetric almond with a sharp point at the outer tip. Where each cap meets the bar there is a flat vertical seam — the caps are stuck on, not growing out. None of the three mustReads land: no white gills (the undersides are a thin dark line, nothing more), no off-centre stubby stem, no inrolled wavy margin. Colour is saturated marigold gold, not pale grey to fawn. It is the same template as Shelf Fungus in this batch with only a hue change.
rows.fix: Replace the rectangle with a painted bark cylinder — irregular edge, vertical fissure texture, tone falloff at both sides. Change the cap primitive from a pointed almond to a fan/oyster shell: broad rounded outer margin, wavy and inrolled, narrowing back to a short lateral stem stub that visibly swells into the bark (blend 8-12px of shared shadow there, no seam). Tilt the caps so the pale undersides show on the lower tiers and draw radiating white gill lines converging on the off-centre stem. Repalette to fawn-grey #b9ada0 caps with #f2efe6 gills.

rows.readsAs: glowing alien toadstools from a bioluminescent-forest asset pack
rows.defect: Three turquoise-teal parasols. Colour is not in the reference range at all — chestnut/bun-brown cap and buff stem are specified and nothing here is brown. The proportion is inverted from the key diagnostic: stems are slender straight-sided tapered cones markedly THINNER than the cap is tall, where a porcini's defining feature is a fat barrel stem far thicker than the cap height. The underside is a flat teal disc with a single hard edge — it is neither pores nor gills, just a cut plane. No white reticulate net on the stem. Every cap is a clean half-ellipse dome with airbrushed shading, and the cap-to-stem junction is a hard tonal step.
rows.fix: Repalette: cap #7a4a26 to #4a2c15 with a slightly greasy sheen, stem #ddd0b4. Rebuild the stem as a bulging barrel — widest at mid-to-lower height, wider than the cap is tall, tapering in at the cap. Give the underside real depth: recess it into the cap and stipple it with fine dark pore dots over an off-white-to-olive ground; add cast shadow so it reads as a sponge slab, not a disc. Overlay a fine raised pale mesh of interlocking hexagonal lines on the upper stem. Merge cap into stem with continuous shading, no step.

rows.readsAs: a bonsai or a bare winter tree canopy under frost
rows.defect: The best render in the batch — genuine repeated dichotomous branching, fine hairlike tips, correct pale ash-white colour, no leaves or flat lobes. Two things stop it reading as lichen. First, the base resolves into about six thick, clean, near-parallel vertical trunks that rise well clear of the ground before branching, which is tree anatomy; a reindeer lichen cushion has no trunk, it is a dense mass of equal-sized podetia crowding from the substrate. Second, the branched mass is bounded by a smooth perfect ellipse — the canopy top is a machine-cut dome with a uniform outer arc, so it silhouettes as a mowed shrub rather than a springy irregular cushion. The mustRead 'tips fine, drooping and all nodding one way' is not met: tips radiate evenly in all directions with no shared lean.
rows.fix: Cut the six trunks down to near zero — start branching within the first 10-15% of height and multiply the number of independent podetia to 20-30 so the base is a crowded thicket, not a colonnade. Perturb the bounding envelope: vary each podetium's terminal height by 20-30% so the top edge is lumpy and open rather than a clean ellipse, and let a few stragglers poke above the mass. Add a consistent 15-20 degree lean plus tip droop to all terminal branchlets so the whole cushion nods one way. Slight hollow-tube shading (bright rim, darker core line) on the thicker stalks would sell the tubular podetia.

rows.readsAs: red feathers or fish fillets nailed to a post
rows.defect: The identical template to Oyster Mushroom, recoloured crimson: a straight-edged dark brown rectangle bar with five pointed almond shapes attached at a hard vertical seam. The shelves are not semicircular and have neither a flat top nor a flat underside — they are lens-shaped with a sharp outer point. No concentric ochre/umber banding anywhere (the caps are a smooth two-stop red gradient), no pale buff pore surface below, and the tiers are stacked vertically in a flat column rather than stepping outward like a staircase. Against the note in the row, this does not read as a stack of thin plates, and it is indistinguishable in construction from Oyster Mushroom in this same batch.
rows.fix: Diverge the template from Oyster: shelf caps must be semicircular half-discs with a flat straight top plane and a flat underside, viewed slightly from above so both planes show. Repalette to concentric bands of ochre #c08a3e, umber #6b4520 and cream, following the arc of the margin. Add a pale buff pore layer as a visible thin slab under each shelf. Stagger the horizontal projection so lower shelves reach further out than upper ones, forming a staircase. Replace the rectangle with painted irregular bark and merge each shelf into it with a shared shadow wedge rather than a butt seam.

rows.readsAs: a plain red fairy-tale toadstool — a spotless fly agaric
rows.defect: The identical template to Porcini, recoloured crimson: three parasols with straight tapered cone stems and smooth half-ellipse caps. All three mustReads fail. The cap surface is a clean airbrushed gradient with no cracking and no white flesh showing through. The margin is a sharp thin edge, not inrolled, and there are no white veil remnants fringing it. There are no gills — the underside is a flat plane — and the stems are dead-centre and smooth rather than off-centre and fibrous. Colour is bright red where umber to tea-brown is specified.
rows.fix: Repalette cap to #5a3a24-#2e1c10 tea-brown, stem tan #c2a97e, gills cream. Fracture the cap: overlay an irregular crazed network of cracks with pale #efe7d4 flesh exposed in the fissures, wider at the crown and closing toward the margin. Roll the margin under and hang torn white veil flakes off it that break the silhouette. Thicken the cap and show crowded radial white gills beneath on the tilted specimens. Make stems off-centre, slightly curved, with vertical fibrous striations, and merge them into the cap with continuous shading instead of a tonal step.

rows.readsAs: a purple cartoon toadstool from a children's game icon set — nobody would say 'Amanita', and certainly nobody would say 'white'
rows.defect: The single most important fact about this species — that it is PURE WHITE, cap gills stem and all — is absent. All three mushrooms are saturated violet-purple with a lilac gradient. Both other mustReads are also missing: there is no ring on any stem and no sac-like volval cup at any base; the stems are smooth truncated cones that simply stop at a flat bottom edge where they meet the ground shadow. Construction is pure geometry: each cap is a half-ellipse with a hard straight chord along its underside, each stem a perfect linear-taper cone, and the cap/stem junction is a hard horizontal seam — the stem is plugged INTO the cap rather than flaring out of it. The whole thing is a vector logo, not a painted organism. It is also indistinguishable in silhouette from the Jelly Fungus render in this same batch.
rows.fix: Repaint the entire body in whites — cool white gill shadow, faint ivory warmth only at the cap crown — and delete the purple hue entirely. Add the two missing anatomical parts: a thin white pendulous ring about two-thirds up the stem, and a deep ragged white volval cup swallowing the stem base so the stem emerges FROM the cup rather than being cut off by the frame's shadow ellipse. Break the cap silhouette off the ellipse — give it an ovate/conical crown with a slightly wavy, unevenly-thin margin — and blend the cap-underside into the stem with a shared shading pass so no straight chord line survives.

rows.readsAs: a naval contact mine, or a coronavirus diagram — a spiked ball, not a fungus
rows.defect: The rays are not rays. What is drawn is a grey sphere with about eight thin needle-sharp triangles poking out sideways from its equator — they read as spikes ATTACHED to the ball, not as a thick leathery outer skin that has split and peeled backward under the sac. There is no star: the points are too few, too thin, all in one flat equatorial plane, and they emerge with a hard seam at the sphere's outline. The spore sac is a perfect circle with a symmetric radial gradient, and the apical pore is a perfect black dot punched in dead centre. The whole organism is also rendered far too small and far too dark — it occupies maybe a fifth of the 440px frame and its greys sit only a step or two above the background, so it barely resolves.
rows.fix: Rebuild the rays as a separate peeled outer layer: 6–9 BROAD triangular flaps of tan leathery skin, thick at the base and tapering, curling downward and backward beneath the sac so their pale inner faces show, with the sac visibly seated in the cup they form rather than floating in front of them. Vary ray length and curl per ray. Replace the perfect-circle sac with a slightly squashed, softly irregular papery sphere in warmer grey-brown, and turn the pore into a small raised fringed beak with a puckered darker aperture, not a filled circle. Raise overall value and scale the organism up to fill ~70% of the frame.

rows.readsAs: a cluster of small pale mushrooms — a viewer would plausibly say enoki, so the identification succeeds even though the craft does not
rows.defect: This is the closest to shippable in the batch — the bouquet reads, the stems are genuinely long and thin, and they converge to a fused base. But the base is a machined artifact: it is a row of six or seven IDENTICAL rounded-rectangle capsules of the same width, same height, same flat top, lined up side by side like a row of piano keys. That is a repeated primitive, not a mycelial clump. The caps are perfect hemispheres — an exact half-disc with a straight bottom chord — and each sits on its stem with a visible hard seam, a bead threaded onto a wire, with no flare where the stem should widen into the cap flesh. Several caps are also too broad relative to the needle stems (the reference asks for 'pinhead caps barely wider than the stems'), which pushes it toward generic-small-mushroom. Colour has drifted from ivory to a cold electric blue-white.
rows.fix: Delete the capsule row: replace with one irregular fused clump of unequal, softly-lobed stem bases packed at different heights and angles, some overlapping, some shorter. Shrink the caps by roughly 40% so they read as pinheads, and make each cap slightly ovate/asymmetric with a small downturned margin instead of a half-disc. Fuse cap to stem with a short flare and a continuous shading gradient across the junction so no chord line is visible. Warm the palette from blue-white to ivory/cream, and let a couple of the tallest stems bend slightly rather than all being straight.

rows.readsAs: a fly agaric — the species is correctly identifiable, which is why the missing ring and volva are the whole problem: it is the right organism rendered as clipart
rows.defect: Two of three mustReads are simply absent: there is no white pendulous ring skirt anywhere on the stems, and there is no bulbous scaly volval base — each stem is a straight-sided tapered box that terminates in a flat horizontal cut, with hard perfectly-straight vertical edges down both sides. The white warts are painted-on flat blobs of uniform pure white, clumped almost entirely on the LEFT half of each cap with the right half bare, so they read as a decal misapplied rather than as veil remnants scattered over the whole dome. Cap meets stem at a hard horizontal seam. All three specimens are also rendered very small against a large empty field, and the caps are near-identical scaled copies of one another.
rows.fix: Add the missing anatomy: a white ring skirt hanging from the upper stem with a torn lower edge, and a swollen ovoid stem base carrying two or three concentric scaly volval belts, sitting into the substrate rather than being cut flat. Redistribute the warts across the full cap dome with irregular spacing and give them dimension — small pyramidal bumps with their own lit top and cast shadow, a few tiny, a few larger, one or two near the margin. Curve the stem outlines (fibrous, slightly uneven) instead of straight vertical rules, and flare the stem into the cap underside. Scale the group up to fill the frame and vary cap shape between the three, not just size.

rows.readsAs: two purple balloons or bath bombs — a pair of spheres, with no reading as fungus at all
rows.defect: Colour is wrong to the point of misidentification: the reference calls for chalk-white to buff, and both balls are saturated lavender-violet. Worse, they are two mathematically perfect circles — no deviation from a compass arc anywhere on either outline — each with a bright arc of specular rim light along its upper-left, joined by a clean overlap with no fusion or squash at the contact point. The dark speckles are scattered dots sitting flat on top of the gradient with no relation to any surface curvature or crack; they look sprayed on. Nothing about the surface says 'leathery kid-glove skin' — it is a plastic sphere shader. No sign of the aged split/spore-puff state.
rows.fix: Change the base colour to chalk white ageing through buff to olive-brown. Break the circles: puffballs are slightly flattened and irregular, wider than tall, with a puckered flattened underside where they sit and a faint sterile-base pinch at the ground contact — no arc of the outline should be a true circle. Where the two touch, flatten and merge them so they deform against each other. Replace the sprayed dots with a fine kid-glove texture — shallow polygonal cracking that follows the sphere's curvature and widens over the crown — and on the larger specimen open a small ruptured tear with a dusty brown spore plume escaping.

rows.readsAs: a group of white mushrooms — the same picture as 'Destroying Angel' in this batch, recoloured
rows.defect: Wrong organism entirely. The reference asks for a stemless gelatinous mass of brain-like folds sitting directly on bark, amber-orange and translucent. What is rendered is three CAP-AND-STEM mushrooms — domed caps with straight-chord undersides on tapered cone stems, in cold white-silver. Every one of the three mustReads fails: no convoluted lobes, no translucency (the caps are opaque and lit like ceramic), and a prominent stem on all three when the species must have none. There is no bark or substrate. It is the same geometry as the Destroying Angel card in this batch with a different palette — the two are interchangeable.
rows.fix: Discard the cap-and-stem construction for this species and route it to the jelly family renderer. Build a single low sprawling mass of soft interlocking gyri — irregular convoluted folds with rounded crests and deep shadowed valleys — spreading laterally along a bark surface it visibly adheres to and drapes over the edge of. Paint it amber-orange to golden with genuine subsurface behaviour: the thin lobe edges should glow warm and brighter than the thick centres, with light bleeding through. No stem, no cap, no straight chord anywhere.

rows.readsAs: a cluster of eggs, or a cauliflower head — a pile of spheres with a few short drips, not a mane
rows.defect: The defining feature is almost missing. The mass is a heap of roughly thirty overlapping PERFECT CIRCLES in cream, and the icicle spines appear only as one small band of short stubby drips in the middle of the mass — they do not cascade, they are not long, and they hang from the interior rather than from the whole rounded body. The reference's 'rounded pom-pom of long hanging icicle spines' is therefore unmet. The bubble mass itself is naked geometric primitives: every lobe outline is a circle arc, so the surface reads as foam or a bunch of eggs. The body also floats — the cast shadow ellipse sits a clear gap below the mass with nothing connecting them, so the organism is not attached to anything.
rows.fix: Invert the construction: the spines ARE the organism. Build a compact rounded body mass, then cover its entire lower two-thirds in dense, long, slightly-wavy pendulous teeth of graduated length — longest at the bottom centre, shortening toward the top and sides — all hanging plumb downward so the silhouette is a shaggy fringe, not a bubble cluster. Replace the perfect-circle lobes with irregular soft lobes whose edges dissolve into the spine origins, so there is no visible boundary between mass and spines. Warm the tips toward tan. Attach the mass to a substrate — a short bark/branch anchor at the top — and bring the shadow up to contact so it stops hovering.

rows.readsAs: a tree canopy, or a mushroom-cloud explosion — a brown crown floating above a white mound, definitely not a hen-of-the-woods
rows.defect: The frond mass is physically DETACHED from its base: a lumpy brown cloud hovers with a clear empty gap of background between it and the small white dome sitting on the ground below. Whatever connects the two is simply not drawn, so the rosette floats. The white base itself is a plain smooth dome — there is no branched white stalk system, so the 'fronds all springing from a single branched stalk' mustRead fails outright. The fronds are not fronds: they are flat mid-brown blobs of uniform value, outlined and internally divided by thin lighter pen strokes, with no overlap depth, no spoon shape, no visible pale undersides, and no rosette organisation. The whole silhouette is a symmetric canopy on a stalk.
rows.fix: Close the gap: grow a visible branched white stalk system out of the base dome — a short trunk splitting into three or four thickening arms — and hang the fronds directly off those arms so mass and base are one continuous body. Rebuild the fronds as individual overlapping spoon/tongue shapes, each with a lit grey-brown upper face and a pale creamy underside catching light, layered in a tight rosette with real occlusion and cast shadows between tiers so the mass has depth. Make the outer margins wavy and irregular per frond and drop the uniform thin-stroke outlines. Squat the overall mass down and wider so it sits like a hen at a tree foot rather than standing like a tree.

rows.readsAs: A radar sweep screen or a target reticle / dartboard. Nobody would say 'living organism'.
rows.defect: It is a perfect mathematical circle overlaid with a polar coordinate grid — 4 evenly-spaced concentric rings and ~12 straight radial spokes, all identical 1px pink-red strokes — glowing over a dark red radial gradient. The lattice is not a shell, it is graph paper wrapped on a disc: every cell is a perfect quadrilateral of the same construction, with none of the irregular hexagonal/pentagonal fenestration a silica test has. Two mustReads are simply absent: there are ZERO spines radiating out (the outline terminates cleanly at the circle, nothing crosses it), and there are no nested inner shells — the inner rings are drawn ON the same disc, not as a shell inside a shell. The colour brief says clear glassy silica, faintly iridescent, with a dark central capsule; the render is saturated crimson with a BRIGHT centre, the exact inverse of the dark central capsule. It also reads flat: no refraction, no glass thickness, no highlight anywhere on the sphere.
rows.fix: Rebuild the shell as an actual sphere of silica: generate an irregular geodesic/Voronoi mesh on the sphere (varied pentagon/hexagon cells, bar thickness varying with a slight taper at each node, and bars on the FAR side of the sphere drawn thinner and dimmer so the form reads as hollow and 3D rather than as a flat wheel). Break the perfect circular outline — the rim must be the mesh bars themselves, slightly lumpy, not a drawn circle. Add 12-20 spines of clearly varied length (0.4-0.9 of the shell radius) growing OUT of mesh NODES, tapering to hair points, not stuck onto the rim. Nest one smaller mesh sphere inside at ~0.45 radius. Repalette to near-colourless: pale cyan-white glass with thin iridescent magenta/green edge tint on the bars, and put a DARK olive-brown central capsule at the core instead of the current bright bloom.

rows.readsAs: A cluster of soap bubbles, or a generic 'bacteria under a microscope' stock icon in the wrong colour. Reads as the SAME organism as Sulfur-Oxidizing Bacteria and Thermophile in this batch — identical circle-plus-dark-dot template, only the hue differs.
rows.defect: The colour is flatly wrong — this is TEAL/cyan, and the reference (and the species name) require brick red to rust brown. That alone kills identification. Beyond the palette: this is ~8 overlapping translucent perfect circles, each with a single dark round dot at centre, on plain black. None of the three mustReads are present — there is no girdle groove and no armour plating (the cells are unfeatured discs with a rim stroke, no thecal plate boundaries at all), the surrounding water is NOT discoloured (the background is the same dark navy as every other card in the batch), and there are no surface streaks or swirls of concentrated cells. 'Packed at huge density' is contradicted by eight sparse cells with wide black gaps. The circles are geometric primitives with hard uniform rim strokes; where they overlap you see clean intersecting arcs, so they read as soap bubbles stacked in front of each other rather than a bloom.
rows.fix: First repalette to rust: cell bodies brick-red/ochre-brown, and flood the background with a rust-brown water wash (radial density falloff) so the water itself is stained — that single change does most of the identification work. Then give each cell dinoflagellate anatomy instead of a disc: an epitheca/hypotheca split by a horizontal GIRDLE GROOVE (a recessed band with a shadow line, cell slightly waisted at it), plate sutures scribed across each half, and an apical horn on some cells. Raise count to 60-150 cells at varied scale, densest in curving streaks so swirl structure reads at thumbnail. Drop the uniform bright rim stroke — shade cells with an internal light direction instead.

rows.readsAs: A speckled bird's egg, or a granite pebble. Nobody unlabelled would say 'snow'.
rows.defect: The silhouette is a single closed, perfectly regular ELLIPSE with an airbrushed vignette edge — a 'field of many' scattered through snow has been rendered as one egg-shaped object floating in black. The snow inside it is a smooth featureless grey-white gradient: the mustRead 'granular snow crystals' is entirely missing, there is not one crystal facet, grain boundary, or sun-cup shadow anywhere. The mustRead 'faint green chloroplast still showing at some cell centres' is also missing — I can find no green pixel in the image; every cell is the same salmon-orange. The cells themselves are flat uniform-opacity circles of two or three sizes rubber-stamped across the surface with no rim, no wall thickness, and no shadow into the snow, which is the textbook look of a pattern SPRAYED ON TOP rather than objects sitting in a substrate. Colour is also off-brief: the brief says deep crimson-red, the render is a pale salmon/terracotta that never reaches watermelon saturation.
rows.fix: Kill the ellipse — let the snow fill the frame edge to edge (or break the boundary with an irregular drift line and shadowed pits) so it is a field, not an egg. Texture the snow: overlapping granular crystal clumps, blue-shadowed interstices, a few specular sparkle points. Give the cysts a THICK WALL — a darker crimson rim ring around a slightly lighter interior — and seat each one with a small blue-grey contact shadow in the snow so they sit IN it. Push ~15% of cells to a visible green chloroplast core inside the red envelope. Deepen the red toward crimson/magenta and add a diffuse pink bleed into the snow around the densest clusters so the snow itself is stained, not just dotted.

rows.readsAs: A bunch of purple soap bubbles, or a clump of grapes / budding yeast colony. Nobody would say bacteria.
rows.defect: It is not a rod field at all — it is a clump of ~10 overlapping violet spheres, each a perfect circle with a thin hard 1px lilac stroke and a perfectly circular flat dark dot pasted inside. Aspect of every cell is 1.0, not 2.2. Nothing in the picture is acidic: no rust-red fluid, no orange iron precipitate flocking, no corroded mineral or pyrite grains — the background is the same neutral dark navy vignette used on every other card. Three mustRead features out of three are absent. The dots are stuck ON the spheres (no shading interaction, they sit at flat alpha over the sphere gradient), and the cells sit ON the background rather than in a fluid.
rows.fix: Rebuild as a field of many slender rods at 2.2+ aspect, capsule-ended but with irregular hand-drawn contours, colourless/pale so the medium reads through them. Flood the whole field with a rust-red/ochre acid-water wash and dust warm orange iron-oxide floc granules clustering onto and around each rod. Add 3-5 angular corroded mineral chips and one or two brassy pyrite fragments in the mid-ground. Delete the perfect-circle + centre-dot cell primitive entirely — it is the shared template that also produces Bioluminescent Plankton and Cryophile.

rows.readsAs: A coffee bean, an avocado, or a potato. Not a living cell.
rows.defect: Zero pseudopods. The silhouette is a smooth opaque brown teardrop/kidney with one small pointed kink on the right that reads as a beak, not a blunt finger. The defining mustRead — 'blunt finger-like pseudopods' — is entirely missing, and so is the clear outer rim: instead of an ectoplasm band there is a hard machined gold hairline stroke tracing the whole outline. Interior is a flat brown radial gradient with no granularity. The nucleus is a perfect circle with a soft drop-shadow and the two 'vacuoles' are perfect translucent circles pasted at flat alpha over the body — all three float on top rather than sitting inside cytoplasm. Colour is opaque milk-chocolate brown, not translucent colourless grey.
rows.fix: Drive the outline with a low-frequency noise-warped radial contour and pull 3-5 blunt lobed pseudopods OUT of it — different lengths, asymmetric, one clearly leading. Feather the limb/body junction so there is no waistline. Replace the hairline stroke with a 6-10px lighter hyaline ectoplasm band that follows the same warped contour. Fill the endoplasm with dense fine granule stipple. Recolour to translucent grey-green with the background faintly reading through the thin edges. Give the contractile vacuole a bright rim and a darker core so it reads as a bubble in the cell, not a disc on it.

rows.readsAs: The same purple bubble cluster as Acidophile — grapes or fish eggs. Nothing about it says plankton or bioluminescence.
rows.defect: This is pixel-for-pixel the same construction as Acidophile in the same batch — the identical overlapping-violet-sphere-with-a-dark-dot template, only the sphere arrangement shifted. That alone is a blocker. On its own terms: the light is violet/magenta-white at the centre pile, never the cold electric blue-cyan the note calls non-negotiable, and it is a continuous soft bloom rather than discrete sparks. No cell has a trailing tentacle, and no cell has a cleft — the mustRead 'single stout trailing tentacle from a cleft' is 100% absent. The cells are perfect circles with thin hard strokes, not translucent buoyant balloons; you cannot see through any of them.
rows.fix: Differentiate hard from Acidophile: make the cells genuinely large and translucent (background visible through the body, bright specular crescent top-left, thin bright rim). Cut a visible cleft in the lower pole of each and grow one short stout tapering tentacle out of it, thicker at the base and blending into the cell wall with no seam. Recolour bodies translucent pink-grey. Replace the continuous violet bloom with sparse cold #40E0FF point flashes on a subset of cells plus short cyan wake streaks, so the light reads as agitation-triggered.

rows.readsAs: Amber bubbles, fish roe, or a yeast colony. Reads as a warm organism — the last thing anyone would guess is a cold-lover.
rows.defect: Warm gold-yellow, the exact opposite of the required cold blue-white cast — the whole field is amber. It is also the third instance of the Acidophile sphere template: same perfect circles, same hard thin stroke, same flat dark centre dot, only hue-rotated to yellow. Family is wrong (spheres at aspect 1.0 instead of rods at 2.0). No ice anywhere: no faceted crystal boundaries, no brine veins, no polygonal grain junctions. All three mustReads absent.
rows.fix: Recolour the entire field to blue-white/pale cyan on a near-white frozen ground. Replace spheres with small slender rods. Build the ice first as the structural layer: hard-edged faceted polygonal crystal cells filling the frame with brighter refraction edges, and thread dark thin liquid brine veins along the crystal boundaries — then place the rods INSIDE those veins only, so their distribution is dictated by the ice. Add a cold blue-white overall grade and faint refraction caustics.

rows.readsAs: Glowing centipedes, or four zippers / measuring tapes laid on a table.
rows.defect: Colour is bright yellow-gold. The organism whose name means 'blue-green' is rendered with no blue or teal anywhere — that inverts the single most identifiable property. The filaments are not beaded chains: each is a smooth flat ribbon with straight ruled tick marks stamped across it, a machined ladder/zipper pattern, so the cells read as printed divisions on a strip rather than individual bodies strung end to end. The one enlarged pale cell per filament is a perfect sphere with a visible hard seam where it meets the ribbon — it is stuck ON, not set INTO the chain. Layout is four near-parallel arcs stacked in even horizontal rows with clean gaps; that is a stripe pattern, not the loose tangled mat the reference calls for.
rows.fix: Recolour to blue-green/teal with the denser overlaps going inky blue-black. Rebuild the filament from actual discrete cells: draw each as a short barrel with a rounded end, butted against its neighbours so the chain silhouette bulges and pinches at every junction — the beading must be visible in the OUTLINE, not painted on a smooth ribbon. Kill the ruled tick marks. Make the heterocyst a slightly larger, paler barrel of the same construction sharing the chain's outline, not a sphere with a seam. Then tangle the layout: crossings, loops, varying curvature and thickness, filaments running behind each other.

rows.readsAs: A dragonfly wing, a rugby ball, or a comb.
rows.defect: No glass, no gold, no lattice. It is a flat purple ellipse with straight ruled violet hairlines running top-to-bottom, all in one direction, stopping raggedly short of the outline — they read as combed hair or an insect wing's veins, not as a repeating pore array. There is no two-halves construction: nothing suggests a pillbox and lid, no girdle band, no suture. The horizontal element through the middle is a hard straight rod with three round nodes on it that reads as an armature or a skewer, not a raphe. The golden-brown chloroplasts are completely absent — there is nothing inside the shell at all. The silhouette is a mathematically perfect ellipse with a thin uniform stroke. Two of three mustReads missing, and the note's 'precisely ordered repeating pore pattern is the whole read' is not delivered — random-length straight strokes are not a lattice.
rows.fix: Recolour the frustule to near-transparent cool glass with a bright refractive rim and a specular sheen, and put 2-4 golden-brown lobed plastids inside showing THROUGH the silica. Replace the hairlines with an actual pore lattice: rows of small punched dots (areolae) in evenly spaced striae that fan perpendicular to the valve edge and follow its curvature all the way to the margin. Draw the pillbox: a straight girdle band across the cell with a visible overlap edge where the epitheca lip sits over the hypotheca. Make the raphe a fine slit with terminal and central nodes, not a rod with beads. Break the perfect ellipse with slightly asymmetric, faintly faceted valve ends.

rows.readsAs: A dartboard, a radar screen, or a wagon wheel. Not an organism.
rows.defect: The equatorial girdle groove — explicitly the non-negotiable feature — is entirely absent. So are both flagella. What is drawn is a perfect circle with a polar spoke-and-ring grid: 16 evenly spaced radial spokes crossing 3 concentric rings, mathematically regular, reading as a dartboard or radar sweep. That grid is not 'interlocking polygonal cellulose plates' — real thecal plates are irregular, differently sized, with visible suture ridges, and are never arranged as a radial pie chart. Aspect is 1.0, not the specified 0.8. Silhouette is a geometric primitive: an exact circle with a uniform gold stroke. Body is a flat brown radial gradient with zero surface relief. Two of three mustReads missing.
rows.fix: Cut a deep transverse girdle across the equator first and let it define the shape: a recessed band with a shadowed floor, the epitheca above overhanging it slightly and the hypotheca below stepping in, so the silhouette itself pinches at the waist. Add the sulcus groove running down from the girdle on the ventral face. Re-plate the armour as irregular polygons of varying size and count, laid out separately on epitheca and hypotheca, each with a raised suture ridge and its own specular highlight. Add the transverse flagellum as a ribbon sitting inside the girdle and a longer longitudinal one trailing from the sulcus, both emerging from the groove floor with no seam. Squash to 0.8 and break the circle with an apical horn or two.

rows.readsAs: A Paramecium — or, honestly, a green kiwi slice with a face.
rows.defect: This is a Paramecium. The body is a symmetric green ellipse fringed with short cilia hairs around the ENTIRE perimeter — a ciliate's coat, and it actively points the viewer at the wrong organism. There is no flagellum: not one long whipping strand anywhere. There is no red eyespot: the only interior marks are a dark grey oval and two circular outlines that together read as a cartoon face with a nose and glasses. The spindle shape is missing too — both ends are equally rounded, with no drawn-out tail point. All three mustReads fail. The two interior circles are hard outlined rings pasted at flat alpha over the body, and the cilia are uniform straight stubs planted on the stroke line rather than growing from the pellicle.
rows.fix: Delete the cilia fringe entirely. Reshape to a true spindle: broad rounded anterior, tapering to a fine point at the posterior. Grow one long flagellum out of an anterior reservoir invagination — thick at the emergence, whipping into 2-3 curves, thinning to a hair, with the base blended into the body so there is no attachment seam. Place a small saturated orange-red eyespot immediately beside the flagellar base. Fill the body with many discrete lens-shaped grass-green chloroplasts rather than a flat green gradient, add faint diagonal pellicle striations following the body curve, and put one paraflagellar contractile vacuole near the anterior instead of the two pasted rings.

rows.readsAs: a radiolarian or heliozoan — a bunch of green grapes stuck in a pincushion
rows.defect: Closest thing to a real organism in the batch, but three failures. (1) The pseudopodia are ~100 DEAD-STRAIGHT dark rays of near-identical length fanning out in a perfect sunburst from a point in the middle of the shell — they are darker than the background, never branch, never anastomose into a net, and do not issue from the aperture; they pass behind and around the chambers, so they read as a pin-cushion sprayed on behind the shell rather than cytoplasm streaming out of it. (2) mustRead 'shell walls pierced by fine pores' is entirely absent — the chambers are smooth glossy balls. (3) The chambers are perfect circles with a ball-bearing specular highlight each, joined by hard circular outlines where they overlap, so it reads as stacked spheres rather than one continuous calcite test. Colour is pistachio/mint green, not the specified chalky white to honey-tan calcite. The coil (7-8 chambers, each larger, dark elliptical aperture on the largest at lower right) is genuinely correct and should be kept.
rows.fix: Redraw the threads as bright, pale, tapering filaments that ORIGINATE at the aperture ellipse only, fan into a narrow cone, and split 2-3 times with a few cross-links so they form a net; vary length heavily and drop the opacity so they are lighter than the shell, not black. Stipple the chamber walls with fine dark pore dots that follow each chamber's curvature. Kill the per-chamber outline stroke and the per-chamber specular dot — one shared light source over the whole test, with the chamber sutures as soft depressed grooves, not rings. Recolour to warm chalk-white with honey-tan shadow.

rows.readsAs: a half-filled green marble, or a planet icon with a sea
rows.defect: This is a geometric primitive, not an organism: one perfect circle with a thin 2px grey stroke, an olive-to-dark-green vertical gradient fill, a single large white specular dot upper-left, three 3px white dots, and a hard straight horizontal chord across the lower third with a darker green cap under it — it looks exactly like a liquid fill line in a glass ball. All three mustReads fail: no cells studded over the surface (the three tiny dots are not a colony), no daughter colonies inside, and no translucency or jelly — the fill is opaque. The straight chord is a machined edge with no biological reading at all.
rows.fix: Build the sphere out of ~60-90 discrete cells on the surface, densest at the rim where the shell is seen edge-on and sparse/enlarged at centre, each cell a slightly irregular polygon with its own chloroplast dot — the studding IS the silhouette, so let the outer edge be bumpy from the rim cells rather than a clean circle. Render the interior as see-through: 2-4 smaller daughter spheres floating inside at partial opacity, and remove the opaque gradient and the horizontal chord entirely. Drop the single big specular dot for a broad soft gloss arc.

rows.readsAs: a clump of amber fish eggs or frogspawn — indistinguishable from the Iron-Oxidizing Bacteria card in this same batch
rows.defect: Wrong family, wrong colour, wrong aspect, and it is the same generic template as four other cards in this batch: ~10 overlapping PERFECT CIRCLES, each with a thin ring outline and one offset dark nucleus dot. The reference calls for rods at aspect 2.2 — these are spheres at aspect 1.0. Colour is amber gold / ochre-brown; the specified vivid magenta to carotenoid red-orange is nowhere in the image. No angular salt crystals anywhere, no brine tint, and the cells are sparse against black rather than 'densely crowded staining the whole field'.
rows.fix: Swap the coccus generator for elongated rods — capsule bodies with slightly bowed, unequal sides and blunt but irregular ends, 2.2:1, at scattered rotations, packed shoulder-to-shoulder until they overlap and fill the frame. Add a handful of hard-edged angular cubic/hopper salt crystals as clear facets between them. Recolour to hot magenta-through-orange-red and tint the field itself a dilute pink from cell density. Remove the uniform ring stroke and the single centred dark dot — they are what makes this read as an egg cluster.

rows.readsAs: a cluster of glowing yellow bubbles or amber eggs — a palette swap of the Halophile card
rows.defect: Identical construction to Halophile, Methanogen, Nitrogen-Fixing and Radiation-Resistant: ~9 overlapping perfect circles with ring outlines and offset dark dots, here in bright yellow-gold with a hot glow behind the centre. Every mustRead is missing: no bean-shaped cell, no twisted ribbon stalk trailing behind anything (there is not a single elongated element in the frame), no rust crust, no matted ochre sludge. The family is declared 'filament' and nothing in the picture is filamentous. Aspect reads ~1.4 wide by accident of clustering, not by morphology.
rows.fix: Make the stalk the subject: draw long flattened ribbons that twist along their length (alternating light/dark facets to show the helix), sweeping in curves from lower-left to upper-right and tangling into a mat; crust them with granular rust-orange oxide that clumps unevenly along the ribbon. Put a small near-colourless bean-shaped cell at the leading TIP of each ribbon, narrower where it meets the stalk so the stalk is clearly secreted from it, not butted onto it. Colour must live on the stalk; the cells stay pale.

rows.readsAs: a bunch of purple grapes or a spread of ova — a hue swap of the Nitrogen-Fixing and Radiation-Resistant cards
rows.defect: Same overlapping-perfect-circles template again, recoloured purple: ~11 spheres with ring outlines and offset dark nucleus dots. mustRead 'short blunt-ended rods' fails — these are spheres, aspect 1.0 against the specified 2.0. No gas bubbles rising anywhere in the frame (the biggest identity cue in the reference, called out in the note, is simply absent). No dark anoxic sediment or sludge — the cells float on the same empty dark-navy vignette used by every other card. The purple is also far more saturated than the specified pale grey-lilac.
rows.fix: Convert to short stubby rods, roughly 2:1 with rounded ends and slight length variation, jammed into irregular packets of 4-8 at differing angles rather than an even scatter. Bed the lower half of the cluster in a dark granular sludge that occludes some cells. Add a rising column of clear bubbles of mixed size, small near the cluster and larger/wobblier as they ascend, with a few clinging to the cell surfaces before release. Desaturate to a pale grey-lilac and let the bodies be faintly translucent so overlapping cells show through.

rows.readsAs: teal caviar or a colony of algae cells — structurally the same picture as Methanogen and Radiation-Resistant
rows.defect: The same circle-cluster template a fourth time, in teal-green. Colour is flatly wrong: the reference asks for pale cream rods inside salmon-pink nodule tissue, and there is no pink anywhere — the whole card is cyan. No nodule at all; the cells sit on the standard empty dark background rather than being packed inside host tissue. No rods (spheres at aspect 1.0 vs the specified 2.2), and no swollen irregular Y-shaped bacteroids — every cell is the same circle at a different scale. That means all three mustReads fail.
rows.fix: Establish the nodule first: a soft salmon-pink irregular tissue field filling most of the frame with a slightly lumpy boundary, cells crammed INSIDE it and clipped by it, so the pink is a container and not a background wash. Fill with cream-coloured short rods at dense random rotations, and mix in 4-6 visibly larger bacteroids with lumpy Y and T branched outlines so the shape variety is the read. Remove the uniform ring stroke and the identical central dot from every cell.

rows.readsAs: a ciliate, probably a paramecium — a viewer would likely name it right from the cilia fringe alone, which is why it is worth fixing rather than rebuilding
rows.defect: The best-drawn card here — the dense hair fringe of short cilia around the entire perimeter genuinely works — but the body is a PERFECT ELLIPSE, bilaterally symmetric on both axes, so mustRead 'asymmetric slipper or shoe outline, blunt at one end' fails outright; both ends are identically pointed. The internal features are drawn as literal geometry: two perfect white outline circles for the contractile vacuoles, and the oral groove is a single straight white RULER LINE, horizontal in the frame (so not even parallel to the tilted body axis), stopping dead in mid-cell instead of running in from the side. A grey lozenge sits between them as the macronucleus. Colour is saturated violet-purple; the reference asks for translucent pale grey-green, faintly straw tinted.
rows.fix: Break the ellipse: widen and blunt the posterior, taper and slightly bend the anterior, and push one flank inward so the outline is a slipper in profile, not a symmetric egg. Redraw the oral groove as a shallow tapering DIAGONAL trough that starts at the cell's mid-flank edge and sweeps back to a gullet — shade it as a depression with cilia lining it, never as a stroked line. Replace the two outline circles with soft radially-spoked vacuoles that read as fluid, not as drawn rings. Recolour to translucent pale grey-green and let internal granules and food vacuoles show through the body wall. Give the cilia a directional metachronal lean instead of uniform radial bristles.

rows.readsAs: a scatter of grey fish roe or soap bubbles — the same picture as Methanogen and Nitrogen-Fixing with the hue changed
rows.defect: The circle-cluster template a fifth time, in cold grey-blue. The signature mustRead — a flat packet of EXACTLY FOUR cells — is violated: I count roughly twelve spheres in a loose irregular scatter, which the reference note explicitly says reads as something else entirely. No unusually thick layered envelope: each cell has the same hairline ring stroke as every other card in this batch. Colour is slate grey-blue, not salmon pink to red-orange, and the surface is matte with a single tiny dot highlight rather than glossy.
rows.fix: Drop to exactly four cells arranged as a square tetrad, mutually flattened where they press together so the contact faces are straight-ish and the outer faces bulge — that mutual deformation is what makes a tetrad read as cells rather than as four balls. Draw the envelope as a genuinely thick multi-layer rim, 8-12% of cell radius, with two or three visible concentric layers of differing tone, continuous across the shared walls. Recolour to salmon pink deepening to red-orange with a broad wet specular sweep across the upper-left of the whole packet, not per-cell dots.

rows.readsAs: a climbing pea/bean shoot
rows.defect: The vine reads, but it is assembled from stamps rather than grown. The same sickle leaf appears ~11 times at the same length and curl, mirrored left/right down the stem, so the eye immediately picks up the repeat. Worse, sitting ON the stem are seven dark outlined ELLIPSES (perfect ovals with a lighter rim) at the base of the leaf pairs — they have no attachment, no shading tie to the stem, and read as decals pasted on the stalk rather than buds/pods swelling out of it. The stem itself is a single uniform-width ribbon from base to tip with no taper toward the growing point.
rows.fix: Jitter per-leaf length (0.6-1.4x), curl angle and base width from the node index so no two leaves match; make the node ellipses actual swellings — widen the stem spline locally by 1.3x over ~8px and shade the bulge with the stem's own gradient instead of drawing a separate ellipse path; taper stem width from ~7px at the base to ~2px at the tip.

rows.readsAs: a grey mushroom, or a mop head on a broom handle
rows.defect: A perfectly straight brown dowel with a flat grey pancake balanced on top. The trunk is a machined taper — two straight edges, no bend, no bark, no root flare where it meets the ground. The canopy is a horizontal grey slab: hard flat underside, wide flat top, and the two small forks at the top of the trunk terminate at a visible hard seam under the slab rather than carrying up into it. The canopy colour is a desaturated cloud-grey with no green, and the whole render is so dark the silhouette barely separates from the background.
rows.fix: Curve the trunk spline (2-3 control points, 8-15deg lean) and flare the base into the ground; branch the fork into 4-6 boughs that penetrate at least a third into the canopy mass so the foliage is built AROUND them; replace the slab with clustered blob lobes of varying radii so the underside is broken, not a straight line; raise canopy value/saturation ~30% so it reads at thumbnail size.

rows.readsAs: a patio umbrella or a fibre-optic lamp
rows.defect: Machined regularity. Roughly 18 pale strands hang from the crown, all the same width, all the same length terminating on the same horizontal line, all the same arc, evenly spaced, and perfectly bilaterally symmetric about the trunk. Every strand starts from a single point at the apex, giving a hard convergence knot. The result is a geometric umbrella/dome silhouette, not foliage. The trunk is again a dead-straight tapered dowel with no root flare, and the strands never touch it — they hang in front of it as separate strokes.
rows.fix: Randomise strand length +/-35% so the hem is ragged, vary width and give each strand 2-3 spline points with independent sway; break symmetry (different counts and phases left vs right); originate the strands from 4-6 separate crown boughs rather than one apex point; add a few short interior strands at varying depth so the dome has volume rather than being a wireframe shell.

rows.readsAs: a tiered cake stand or a child's stacking-ring toy
rows.defect: This is not an organism, it is five flat pink ELLIPSES threaded on a brown stick. Each tier is a mathematically perfect ellipse with a uniform flat fill and a single soft rim highlight — no edge break, no leaf, no needle, no texture. The tiers are stacked at even vertical intervals with radii increasing linearly downward, so the eye reads a chart or a stacking toy. The stick is a straight uniform-width line passing IN FRONT of every tier with a hard dark seam at each crossing; nothing grows out of anything.
rows.fix: Replace the ellipse primitives entirely — build each tier from 15-30 overlapping frond/needle strokes radiating from the trunk at that node so the outline is serrated and the tier has depth; let the trunk pass behind the tiers with foliage overlapping it; vary tier spacing and radius non-monotonically; taper the trunk and give it a bend and a base flare.

rows.readsAs: a bundle of pink matchsticks or a pick-up-sticks pile
rows.defect: Every branch is a dead-straight bar of constant width with flat chopped ends, crossing other identical bars at hard angles. No taper from base to tip, no curvature, no leaves at all — the pink is the branch itself. Junctions are simple overlaps: bars lie across each other with a visible dark crossing line instead of forking out of a parent. The brown trunk stub at the bottom is a separate cone that the pink lattice merely sits on top of. Reads as a pile of matchsticks, not growth.
rows.fix: Make branches tapered splines (width shrinking to ~15% at the tip) with 10-25deg curvature; fork children from a point ON the parent, sharing the parent's colour and width at the junction so there is no crossing seam; add foliage/leaf mass at the branch tips so the pink is decoration on structure rather than the structure; continue the brown trunk colour up into the first-order branches so the base stub isn't a separate object.

rows.readsAs: a piece of broccoli/cauliflower on a skewer
rows.defect: A dead-straight dark line of constant width runs the full 440px height of the frame and is drawn OVER the orange canopy, cutting the foliage in half with a hard machined edge. It does not taper, does not bend, does not flare at the ground, and does not branch — the blob is simply skewered on it. The canopy itself is one undifferentiated lumpy orange mass with no internal branch structure and no value variation beyond a soft blur; it is attached nowhere, sitting off-centre to the left of the pole.
rows.fix: Draw the trunk BEHIND the canopy and terminate it inside the mass; taper it (thick base, thin apex) and bend it; flare the base into the ground contact; branch 4-6 boughs into the canopy and let foliage clusters hang off those boughs so the mass has an armature; break the canopy into 3-5 lobes with distinct lighting so it isn't a single blurred blob; centre the crown on the trunk.

rows.readsAs: a snowberry bush with red flowers
rows.defect: Much the best of the batch — it genuinely reads as a berry bush and the green stems do fan out of the base. But the ~35 berries are the same near-perfect circle repeated at two sizes with an identical highlight at the identical upper-left position on every one, which reads as a sprite stamped in a grid rather than fruit at varying depth. The overall berry mass is a clean triangle/heart outline. The green basal stalk is a short flat cone with a visible hard seam where the berry cluster begins.
rows.fix: Vary berry radius +/-30%, squash them slightly along random axes so they are not circles, and rotate the specular highlight per berry with a few berries in shadow behind the front layer; darken back-layer berries ~25% for depth; break the triangular outline with 3-4 outlying berries and a couple of bare stems; let the green stems taper up INTO the cluster and remain visible between berries instead of stopping at a seam.

rows.readsAs: a mushroom or a parasol; indistinguishable from flora-h0-s3
rows.defect: Same failure as s3 and near-duplicate of it: a straight brown dowel with a flat pale slab balanced on top. The canopy underside is an almost perfectly straight horizontal line, the top edge is a flat wedge, and the trunk's small fork ends at a hard seam beneath it. The white 'fruits' are five identical perfect spheres with the same highlight, sitting on the slab surface like beads on a plate rather than hanging from anything. The trunk has no bend, no bark, no root flare, and is unnaturally long relative to a very thin crown (crown depth is ~12% of total height).
rows.fix: Differentiate it from s3 — this seed should not produce the same silhouette; break the canopy underside with hanging lobes and let boughs run into it; hang the fruits from visible peduncles under the crown edge and vary their size and highlight angle; increase crown depth to ~30% of height and shorten/curve the trunk with a base flare.

rows.readsAs: An ornamental grass or spider plant — correct read.
rows.defect: The best picture in the batch, but it still shows engine tells. Every blade converges to a single mathematical vertex at the ground — there is no crown, no root mass, no thickening where the leaves emerge, so the whole tuft balances on a point. The blades are two populations that do not belong to one plant: fat opaque ribbons in the centre and hairline threads sweeping out left and right that are a quarter the width and read as separate wisps. Each blade is a smooth airbrushed gradient from dark base to pale tip with no midrib, no fold, no torn or frayed tip — the arcs are perfectly clean spline curves. The cast shadow is a hard-edged perfect black ellipse floating under the plant.
rows.fix: Add a base crown: widen the bottom 8-12% of every blade and stagger the emergence points across a ~30px ellipse instead of one vertex, so blades grow out of a sheath. Unify blade width distribution (min width no less than ~45% of max). Give each blade a darker centre-line midrib and break 2-3 tips with a split or a bend. Replace the elliptical shadow with a soft irregular blur.

rows.readsAs: A tree — but specifically a low-poly game-asset tree with a broccoli-texture canopy.
rows.defect: The canopy is built from cotton-wool puffs whose outline is visibly stair-stepped in square ~8px blocks all the way round the rim — it reads as a low-resolution mask scaled up, not as foliage. There are no leaves anywhere, just three glowing blue-white blobs. The canopy sits ON the branches rather than growing from them: the branch tips disappear behind a hard scalloped underside line, and the left blob is offset far enough that it overhangs empty air. The trunk and branches are flat grey-lavender ribbons of near-constant width with straight machined edges and hard Y-junctions — no taper into the fork, no swelling at the crotch, and the trunk colour has zero relationship to the canopy colour.
rows.fix: Anti-alias / resample the canopy mask (the blockiness is the real killer) and replace the solid puffs with clustered leaf marks so the rim is broken by individual leaves. Attach foliage per branch tip so each blob is centred on the twig that carries it, and let twigs pass INTO the leaf mass. Taper the trunk from base to fork and add a fillet at each Y so limbs swell out of the trunk instead of butting into it.

rows.readsAs: A purple parasol or a lollipop on a stick, not a living organism.
rows.defect: The stem is a dead-straight brown dowel of perfectly uniform width with parallel machined edges, and it meets the cap in a hard flat T-junction — a textbook stuck-on seam, with four tiny dark tick marks under the cap standing in for gills. The stem has no basal flare and no roots; it is inserted into a perfect black ellipse. The cap is not a mushroom cap: it is a flattened loaf pointed at both ends like a rowboat hull, thicker at the left than the right, and it is a single smooth airbrushed purple mass with pale bumps that read as sprayed-on highlights rather than warts sitting in the flesh. Aspect is also wrong — the stem is roughly 4x the cap width tall, which is a lamp-post, not a fungus.
rows.fix: Give the stem taper and a slight S-curve, flare its base into the ground, and blend the top 15% outward into the cap underside so the two are one continuous surface (kill the T-junction). Rebuild the cap as a radially symmetric dome with a downturned rim and real radial gill lines converging on the stem. Shorten the stem to roughly 1.5-2x cap width. Make the warts displace the cap silhouette, not just paint on it.

rows.readsAs: A paper cut-out Christmas tree icon.
rows.defect: This is not an organism, it is clip art. Five stacked isoceles triangles with dead-straight edges, sharp mathematical corners and flat uniform orange fill, plus a plain brown rectangle for a trunk. Every triangle is the identical shape scaled down, spaced on an even vertical rhythm. There is no needle, no branch, no texture, no variation, no asymmetry and no lighting — the fill has a faint vertical gradient and nothing else. The trunk rectangle has parallel sides and butts into the bottom triangle with a hard line.
rows.fix: This needs a rewrite, not a tweak. Replace the triangle stack with real whorled branches: per-tier draw 6-12 individual drooping boughs with needle clusters, jittered in length and angle, so the tier outline is ragged rather than a straight hypotenuse. Curve the leader, taper the trunk, and let branch bases emerge from the trunk with a widening. At minimum, if a tiered silhouette is kept, perturb every edge with noise and break the corners.

rows.readsAs: A clip-art daisy sticker.
rows.defect: A cartoon daisy assembled from primitives. Eight identical rounded petals in a perfect rotational array about a perfect flat yellow circle — the disc is a true circle with a uniform fill and no florets. The stem is a dead-straight brown line of constant width from the ground to the flower, meeting the bloom at a hard point with no receptacle or swelling. Two leaves are stuck onto the stem at hard contact points with a visible seam; they are pure white almond shapes that share no pigment with either the cyan flower or the brown stem, so they read as debris caught on a wire. The plant is also all stem — the bloom occupies the top fifth and the bare shaft below it is featureless.
rows.fix: Break the petal array: vary petal length, width and angle by 10-20% each, overlap them unevenly, and give a couple of them a notched or curled tip. Replace the flat disc with a textured floret centre and a slight dome. Add a green calyx/receptacle where petals meet the stem and give the stem a bend, a taper and a hair texture. Re-pigment the leaves into the plant's own palette and grow them out of the stem with a widening base rather than touching it.

rows.readsAs: A floor lamp with a beaded shade, or a mop — plausibly a jellyfish before a plant.
rows.defect: The drooping strands are all the same uniform-width neon line, all the same length, all curving with the identical radius, and they terminate on a dead-flat horizontal bottom edge — the hanging mass is a rectangle. That flat hem plus the even spacing makes it read as a fringe or a mop head, not foliage. The strands have no leaves, no thickness variation and no taper to a tip. Where the curtain meets the trunk there is a hard colour and material discontinuity: violet glowing threads and a green glow hotspot sit on top of a flat matte grey-lavender column, with no crown, no bract, no transition. The trunk itself is a straight-sided constant-width post with no taper or base flare, driven into a perfect black ellipse.
rows.fix: Randomize strand length by at least +/-30% so the hem becomes ragged, and taper each strand to a fine tip. Vary the spring/curl radius per strand and let a few cross. Build a real crown at the top — a swelling of the trunk with strand bases emerging radially from it and inheriting the trunk hue at their roots so the violet fades in. Taper the trunk and flare its foot.

rows.readsAs: The same purple parasol as flora-h2-s14 — a stranger would call them one organism.
rows.defect: Effectively a duplicate of flora-h2-s14 — same purple boat-hull cap, same bumps, same brown dowel, same tick-mark gills; only the wart pattern and a couple of degrees of cap tilt differ. On its own merits it carries every s14 defect: a perfectly straight uniform-width stem meeting the cap in a hard flat T-junction with no blend, no basal flare, no roots; a cap that is an asymmetric flattened loaf pointed at both ends rather than a dome; and pale bumps painted on the surface that do not disturb the silhouette. The lower two thirds of the frame is empty bare stick.
rows.fix: Same structural fix as s14 (taper + curve the stem, blend its top into the cap underside, rebuild the cap as a radial dome with a downturned rim and real gills, shorten the stem to ~2x cap width). Separately, the procedural seed needs to differentiate s14 and s18 — push cap silhouette, tilt, bump density and hue apart far enough that they are not read as the same species twice.

rows.readsAs: A clump of dried wheat or sedge — the read is right, but the floating specks make it look like a rendering glitch.
rows.defect: Short bright-yellow horizontal dashes float in empty space between the blades — several near the upper-left and mid-canopy touch no stem at all, so they read as stray artifacts rather than leaflets. The two outermost arms are thick tapered tubes with soft rounded ends and a completely different weight from the thin central spears, so the clump looks like two organisms overlapping. All blades converge to a single point at the ground with no crown or sheath. The two big outer arcs also have suspiciously identical mirrored curvature.
rows.fix: Snap every leaflet dash to a parent stem and give it an attachment angle following the stem's tangent, so nothing floats. Bring the outer arms' width within ~40% of the central blade width, or make the leaflets continue onto them so they read as the same plant.
