Add a basal crown with staggered emergence points, and break the left/right mirror symmetry of the two big arcs.

rows.readsAs: a cyan tree-fern or feather-duster tube worm — plausible as a fern
rows.defect: Best render in the batch, but it is built from one frond stamped ~9 times: every frond carries the identical uniform sawtooth pinnae at the identical spacing and the identical rachis taper, so the crown reads as a repeated brush rather than a grown plant. The whole fan is a single flat cyan hue with only a faint darker underlay — no depth between the front and back fronds. Fronds converge to a tiny dark stub at the base with no rhizome, crown mass, or root flare, so the fan appears to balance on a point. There is also a small hard-edged ring/dot artifact floating on the lower-right frond near centre (~235,270) that belongs to nothing.
rows.fix: Per-frond jitter the pinna length, angle and count (±25%) and vary rachis curvature so no two fronds are congruent; darken and desaturate the rear fronds by 20-30% value to build depth; add a short fibrous crown/caudex mass where the rachises meet the ground so they emerge from something; remove the stray ring primitive on the lower-right frond.

rows.readsAs: a purple parasol or a folded umbrella on a pole
rows.defect: The canopy is a flat purple slab with straight machined edges and sharp angular spike corners — a hard-edged polygon pancake, not foliage. It meets the trunk at a visible hard seam: the brown stem stops and a few dark stick-like struts poke up into the underside of the slab, which is a different material and colour entirely. The trunk is a near-perfectly straight tapered line with no bark, no taper variation and no root flare where it meets the ground shadow. Three lumpy pale blobs sit on top of the slab as sprayed-on decoration. No leaves exist anywhere.
rows.fix: Replace the polygon slab with an actual clustered-leaf canopy built from many overlapping leaf strokes whose outer edge is lobed and broken by sky holes; run the branch strokes THROUGH the canopy so the same colour ramp carries from trunk into leaf mass (no material change at the join); flare the trunk base into the ground and give it a curved, irregular centreline with bark value variation.

rows.readsAs: a clipart sunflower or gerbera daisy
rows.defect: Pure vector clipart daisy. The flower centre is a mathematically perfect circle in flat brown; the petals are ~22 identical scalloped teardrops at perfectly even angular spacing, radially symmetric to the degree. The stem is a dead-straight tapered line. The two leaves are flat lozenge primitives stuck ONTO the side of the stem with a hard seam and no petiole, no midrib, and no continuity of colour with the stem. Nothing in the image has surface texture — every shape is a single flat fill.
rows.fix: Break the radial symmetry: vary petal length/width/tilt per petal and let a few overlap or droop; replace the perfect disc with a textured floret head (concentric seed spiral, value gradient, slightly irregular outline); grow the leaves out of the stem with a tapering petiole that shares the stem's colour ramp, and give them a midrib and a curved, asymmetric blade; curve the stem and thicken it toward the base.

rows.readsAs: a closed purple tulip or a paintbrush — the pills read as beads on a string
rows.defect: Three pale-lilac PILL shapes (perfect stadium/capsule primitives, all identical, all horizontal) plus one at the apex are pasted flat on top of the strand bundle. They cast no shadow, follow no strand curvature, and read as UI capsules sprayed on rather than buds or fruit growing from the plant. The strand bundle itself converges to a single needle point at the ground with no base mass. The whole silhouette is a smooth closed teardrop with very little inter-strand separation, so it reads as one solid object rather than many blades.
rows.fix: Replace the pill primitives with irregular bud/pod forms that are attached to a specific strand — rotate each to that strand's tangent, add a short pedicel, and shade them with the same light direction as the strands; splay the strand tips apart and vary their lengths so the silhouette breaks up; add a fibrous base clump where the strands meet the ground.

rows.readsAs: a flying saucer on a pole, or a desk lamp — not a plant
rows.defect: Same umbrella archetype as flora-h1-s1, and worse for it: the canopy is a flat lens-shaped grey disc with a bright specular hotspot on top that makes it read as brushed metal. Its rim is a hard machined edge with two straight angular spikes. The stem is a perfectly straight, uniform-width lavender column — a capsule — meeting the ground with no flare. The only saving detail is that the branch struts do splay visibly into the canopy underside, but they are dark and disconnected in value from the disc above them.
rows.fix: Kill the specular hotspot (it is what makes this read metallic); rebuild the canopy as broken foliage mass with a lobed, hole-punched outline instead of a smooth lens; carry the branch colour up into the canopy underside so there is no material change at the join; curve and taper the trunk and flare its base. Also differentiate this generator instance from s1 — two umbrella-on-a-pole silhouettes in one batch.

rows.readsAs: a water fountain or a fibre-optic lamp
rows.defect: Off-body artifacts: roughly a dozen small white DASHES float in the empty space between the arcing strands, unattached to anything — most obviously the horizontal ticks stacked up the centre and the two isolated dashes at upper right near (280,130) and (255,150). They are meant to be leaflets but they render as detached ticks crossing gaps. All strands also converge to one exact mathematical point at the ground with zero base mass, and the arcs are smooth uniform-width tubes with no taper or texture, giving a wire/fibre-optic look. Silhouette is a symmetric fountain spray.
rows.fix: Clip leaflets to their parent strand and anchor each one to a point ON the stroke with a matching tangent — nothing should draw where no strand exists; taper each arc from thick at the base to a fine tip; jitter arc lengths and departure angles so the spray is asymmetric; add a fibrous crown clump at the convergence point.

rows.readsAs: an orange firework burst, or a dead grass tussock — nearly identical to flora-h1-s13
rows.defect: The same generator as flora-h1-s13 with an orange palette — same fountain silhouette, same convergence point, same defect. The detached leaflet dashes are even more visible here: a ladder of short horizontal orange bars runs straight up the centre of the spray, crossing empty background between strands, so the middle of the plant reads as a rung ladder. Strand tips are blunt uniform-width tubes; several dark rear arcs end abruptly in mid-air with a flat cut.
rows.fix: Same fix as s13 — anchor leaflets to their parent stroke and clip them to it, taper strands to fine tips, break the symmetry. Additionally, this instance must not be a palette swap of s13: change strand count, arc curvature, and leaflet form so the two are distinguishable as different species.

rows.readsAs: a lollipop or a cotton bud — a green pom-pom on a stick
rows.defect: The trunk is a literal CAPSULE: perfectly straight parallel sides, constant width top to bottom, and a rounded bottom cap that floats clear of the ground shadow so the tree is not standing on anything. Colour is one flat olive with no bark. The canopy is a soft out-of-focus green blur blob — badly over-blurred against everything else in the batch — with about 30 elongated diamond leaf primitives arranged in a sunburst around its rim, all pointing radially outward, none attached to a branch. The trunk simply enters the bottom of the blur with a hard edge change; no branches exist between trunk and canopy.
rows.fix: Give the trunk a curved irregular centreline, taper it toward the top, and flare the base into the ground contact; drop the heavy blur on the canopy and rebuild it from resolved overlapping leaf clusters; grow visible branches out of the trunk top and hang the leaves off those branches with varied orientation instead of a radial sunburst of identical diamonds.

rows.readsAs: A large feather, or a carved wooden quill/paddle. Nobody would say 'plant'.
rows.defect: An inverted-teardrop orange-brown body with straight vertical ribs converging to a single hard point at the bottom, and THREE identical orange capsule/lozenge shapes stacked dead-centre on the midline. Those three pods are perfect rounded-rectangle primitives with a hard unlit edge — they are painted on top of the ribbing, not growing out of it (the ribs pass behind them unbroken, and the pods cast no shadow onto the body). The ribs themselves are straight machined lines fanning from a vanishing point, not organic veins. There is no stem, no root, no ground contact other than the tip poking at the drop shadow, and no leaf/branch structure of any kind.
rows.fix: Kill the three capsule pods or re-form them as swellings of the body itself — interrupt the rib lines where a pod sits, give each pod a different size/angle and an occlusion shadow onto the surface beneath. Curve the ribs (they should bow with the body's surface, not run to a mathematical vanishing point) and vary their spacing. Give the base a taper into a stem/root rather than a needle point.

rows.readsAs: An agave / aloe succulent — correct read, but drawn as a geometric fan rather than painted.
rows.defect: A teal rosette of radiating pointed leaves — the most legible piece in the batch, it genuinely reads as an agave. But every leaf is a perfectly straight-sided isoceles triangle: two ruled edges meeting at a sharp apex, with one straight crease line down the middle. No leaf curls, bends, twists or tapers unevenly; they are flat facets of a single flat teal gradient with no skin texture, no vein network, no serration and no thickness. The fan is also near-mirror-symmetric about the centre.
rows.fix: Give each leaf a bowed spine (sigmoid, not straight) so the outer ones arch and droop under their own weight; vary length, width and apex sharpness per leaf rather than repeating one triangle; add a rolled-edge highlight along one side of each leaf so it reads as a 3D channel rather than a flat facet; break the left/right symmetry.

rows.readsAs: A floor lamp with a fringed shade, or a mop head on a pole. Also a hue-swap twin of flora-h2-s11 in this same batch.
rows.defect: A perfectly cylindrical brown trunk — uniform width top to bottom, straight ruled sides, no taper, no bark, no root flare, cut off flat where it meets the ground — with a magenta 'weeping' canopy that is not attached to it. The strands hang from a small hoop floating ABOVE the trunk top; the trunk simply disappears behind that hoop with no crown, no branch junction, no thickening. Every strand is the same width, the same length band and evenly spaced, and they are pure hairline strokes with no mass, so the canopy reads as a wire frame rather than foliage.
rows.fix: Grow the canopy out of the trunk: flare the trunk into a crown, split it into 3-5 real boughs, and originate each strand from a bough with a thick-to-thin taper. Vary strand length, spacing and droop; let some cross and clump. Taper the trunk and flare its base into the soil instead of ending in a flat cut.

rows.readsAs: A dandelion clock or a bottle brush on a lollipop stick.
rows.defect: The stem is a literal capsule primitive — a flat mid-green rounded rectangle of constant width with a domed cap at the BOTTOM that sits on top of the shadow instead of entering the ground. It is a single flat fill with no shading, no taper, no fibre. The head is a soft green cloud with straight needle-spikes sprayed radially out of it; the spikes are uniform-width straight lines of a lighter green than the cloud, clearly drawn over the blur rather than emerging from it, and several float detached in the haze with no visible origin.
rows.fix: Replace the capsule stem with a tapered, slightly curved stalk that widens at the base and disappears into the ground plane; shade it (lit side / core shadow). Anchor every spike to a common receptacle at the stem top so they read as radiating florets, curve them, and vary their length so the head silhouette is irregular rather than a disc of quills.

rows.readsAs: Cotton candy on a stick, or a lichen/fungal bloom on a fence post.
rows.defect: A dead-straight uniform-width dark brown stick runs from the very top edge of the frame (where it is cropped) all the way to the ground, and a single amorphous pink cloud blob is laid over its middle-left. The blob has zero attachment to the stick — the stick passes cleanly behind it and re-emerges above with no branch, no node, no thickening, no leaf. There are no secondary branches at all, and the blob's edge is a uniform soft airbrush lump with faint circular dabs on it that read as sprayed-on stippling rather than leaf mass.
rows.fix: Stop the trunk inside the canopy and branch it — the foliage mass must sit on visible boughs. Taper the trunk, curve it, flare the base. Break the pink blob into overlapping clumps with silhouette notches and a few individual leaves at the edges so it reads as foliage, and drop a contact shadow from the mass onto the trunk.

rows.readsAs: A ceramic vase with two sprigs in it, or a lit candle.
rows.defect: The body is a tall, flat, unlit dark-purple capsule/vase — straight parallel sides through most of its height, rounded shoulders, a rounded base, one flat fill with essentially no value modelling. That is the capsule silhouette in its purest form. Two small pale-lilac cloud blobs are parked on the flat top with a hard horizontal seam where they meet it, and a blown-out white glow dot sits between them for no structural reason. The whole image is so dark that the trunk barely separates from the background.
rows.fix: Give the trunk a real profile: taper, curvature, a base flare into the ground, and directional lighting with a rim on one side. Originate the two flower heads from short peduncles that visibly emerge from the trunk tip rather than resting on it, and occlude the seam. Raise the trunk's value so it reads against the dark plate; remove or motivate the white glow.

rows.readsAs: A scallop shell, or a flat firework/sunburst logo. Reads as UI iconography, not an organism.
rows.defect: Completely flat vector art — a single solid red with no gradient, no texture, no lighting, no shadow modelling anywhere. Roughly a dozen straight tapered spikes radiate from one point at the bottom in an almost perfectly symmetric arc; each spike is a ruled two-edged wedge with a hard point. There is no stem, no ground attachment other than the ellipse shadow, no base structure at all — the spikes converge to a mathematical apex. This violates the painterly-canvas look every other card in the batch at least attempts.
rows.fix: Bring it into the painterly engine: per-frond gradient shading with a lit edge and a core shadow, overlap/occlusion where fronds cross, and a fleshy base or holdfast at the convergence point instead of a point. Curve the fronds (splines, not straight wedges), vary their length and thickness, and break the radial symmetry.

rows.readsAs: A teal-fringed floor lamp. Indistinguishable in form from flora-h1-s8 in this batch.
rows.defect: Structurally identical to flora-h1-s8 with the canopy recoloured teal — same perfectly cylindrical untapered brown trunk cut flat at the ground, same detached hoop of evenly-spaced hairline strands floating above the trunk top with no crown or branch junction, same wire-frame canopy with no mass. The two images differ only in hue, so the batch ships the same plant twice.
rows.fix: Same as h1-s8 (flare a crown, real boughs, tapered strands, tapered/flared trunk) AND differentiate the two seeds structurally — different canopy width, strand count, droop depth, trunk lean and height — so a hue change is not the only variation the procedural router produces.

rows.readsAs: a generic green four-legged lizard-antelope; hard to name any real animal
rows.defect: The back is a perfectly straight machined line running from the base of the neck all the way to the tail root — a ruler edge, not a spine. Below it the flank carries a fan of thin straight 'vein' strokes radiating from a single point mid-body, which read as a decal sprayed onto a flat green wedge rather than musculature. The four legs are straight tapered cones that butt into the underside with a visible hard seam; there is no shoulder or haunch mass at all, the body just ends and a cone begins. The neck is a separate cone stuck onto the front of the torso, again with a hard boundary. Head is far too small (roughly 1/9 of body length) and sits on the neck like a bead.
rows.fix: Replace the straight dorsal edge with a curved spine profile carrying a withers rise and a croup dip. Delete the radial vein strokes; if flank marking is wanted, use blobs that follow body curvature. Blend limbs into the torso with shoulder/hip masses so the outline is continuous where they meet — no straight line across the join. Enlarge head ~40%.

rows.readsAs: a purple caterpillar or slug wearing a shell fin — a toy, not an animal
rows.defect: The body is literally a row of five or six overlapping spheres (perfect circles with radial shading) plus four more circles used as feet — obvious geometric primitives, no unified silhouette. The large dorsal fin/carapace terminates on its left side in an abrupt straight vertical cut, as if the shape was clipped by a bounding box, and it overlaps the sphere-chain with a hard edge and no attachment tissue. The head is a lump carrying six eyes arranged in a perfect 3x2 grid on a rounded-rectangle dark patch — a sprayed-on sticker, not eyes set in a skull. Tail spikes are four identical straight triangles stuck along the top edge.
rows.fix: Union the sphere chain into one metaball/spline silhouette so individual circles are not readable; vary radii and offsets. Fix the clipped fin edge (it is being cut by a draw bound) and root it into the back with a fairing. Scatter the eyes at varying sizes on the head's own curvature instead of a grid on a rectangular patch. Make the spikes emerge from the tail contour with basal thickness.

rows.readsAs: a giraffe or a llama — the ID lands
rows.defect: Reads correctly as a giraffe/llama-like browser, and the neck-to-body transition is the best in the batch. But the four legs are perfectly straight parallel-sided rectangular columns with no taper, joined to the belly by a hard horizontal seam, and each has a darker hoof block and a mid-leg knee segment that read as separate stacked parts rather than one limb. The torso is a plain capsule. The dark spots are evenly scattered ellipses that do not wrap or compress near the body's silhouette edges, so they sit on top of the form rather than on skin.
rows.fix: Taper the legs (thick at the haunch, thin at the pastern), curve them slightly, and merge their tops into hip/shoulder mass so there is no straight seam. Break the capsule torso with a belly sag and rib/chest swell. Foreshorten and clip spots near the silhouette so the pattern follows the surface.

rows.readsAs: a horned green antelope-lizard; visually the same creature as fauna-h0-s6
rows.defect: Same rig as fauna-h0-s6 recoloured — identical straight dorsal ruler line along the back, identical cone legs with hard belly seams, identical tiny bead head. On top of that, two separate pattern layers are stacked on the flank: dark blobs and white outlined diamonds, neither of which follows the body's curvature, so it reads as two decal sheets applied over a green wedge. The tail carries a dark segmented band that looks like a different object slid onto the tail. The face 'whiskers' are four straight green rays fanning off the cheek with no root in the skin.
rows.fix: Curve the dorsal line. Pick ONE marking system and warp it to the body's surface normals. Delete the tail band or make it a continuous ringed taper. Root the facial rays in a fleshy base so they grow out instead of being pasted beside the head. Differentiate the silhouette from h0-s6 (currently the same animal in the same batch).

rows.readsAs: a generic fish-shaped icon; possibly a flatfish or a leaf, no species readable
rows.defect: Rendered tiny — the animal occupies roughly a quarter of the 440px frame with a huge empty margin, so it reads as an error rather than a portrait. The silhouette is a near-perfect lens/almond: two symmetric arcs meeting in sharp points at both ends, a pure geometric primitive with no head, no mouth, no gill line, no tail peduncle. A dark grey crescent sits over the upper half with a hard curved boundary line right across the body — a pasted-on dorsal patch, not counter-shading. Vertical light bands are evenly spaced and identical. Fins are one-pixel hairlines that barely exist, and the caudal end is two stray hairline strokes floating off the point.
rows.fix: Scale the render to fill the frame like the rest of the batch. Break the lens symmetry — give it a distinct head end with a mouth line and jaw, a narrowing caudal peduncle, and a real tail fin with area. Feather the dorsal dark region into the flank instead of a hard edge. Give the fins actual membrane width and root them into the body.

rows.readsAs: a dark donkey or hare-eared mule with glowing dots
rows.defect: The bioluminescent spots are perfect radial-gradient circles composited over the animal, and at least two of them are OFF the body entirely — one glow hangs below the belly line between the hind legs and another sits past the flank contour — floating in empty space. They also do not dim or distort anywhere near the silhouette edge, so the whole pattern is sprayed on. The back is again a dead-straight ruled line from shoulder to tail. The ears are two flat leaf shapes butted onto the top of the skull with a hard seam, and the tusks are two flat white triangles overlapping the muzzle with no socket. The bristle tail is a bundle of straight radiating lines terminating in a lone pale circle.
rows.fix: Clip all glow spots to the body mask and vary their size/intensity; kill the two that render outside the silhouette. Curve the dorsal line. Merge the ear bases into the skull with a continuous contour. Set the tusks into the jawline. Give the tail bristles a tapering, slightly curved growth from a fleshy root.

rows.readsAs: a turtle — the ID lands, but it reads as a clip-art turtle logo
rows.defect: The shell is a mathematically perfect half-disc: concentric arcs and straight radial spokes forming an even pie chart, with a dead-straight horizontal line closing its bottom rim. The head is a perfect ellipse that simply overlaps the shell edge — no neck, and a hard crescent seam where ellipse meets shell. Only TWO legs exist, both identical blunt brown ovals with no feet, no toes and no knee, each meeting the shell with a hard straight cut. Nothing grows out of the body; every part is a primitive laid on top of another primitive. No tail.
rows.fix: Warp the shell into an irregular dome and replace the even radial grid with scutes of varying size and slightly irregular boundaries; curve the plastron rim. Add a real neck that tapers out of the shell opening. Draw four legs with elbow/ankle bends and toe forms, emerging from under the carapace rim rather than clipped to it. Add a short tail.

rows.readsAs: a golden deer or stag; visually the same animal as fauna-h1-s1 recoloured
rows.defect: Same off-body glow defect as fauna-h1-s1: the luminous spots are perfect radial circles and one sits clearly BELOW the belly outline near the centre bottom, detached in empty space, with another small one past the flank. The antlers are two flat forks with four straight parallel tines of equal length and squared tips — they read as combs or hands, not bone, and they meet the skull as flat overlapping shapes. The tail is a fan of perfectly straight yellow lines radiating from a point. The dorsal line is the same ruled straight edge as the rest of the batch. Body is otherwise the identical rig to fauna-h1-s1, recoloured yellow.
rows.fix: Mask the glow spots to the body silhouette and remove the detached one. Rebuild the antlers with tapering, curving, unequal tines and pedicles that emerge from the frontal bone. Curve and taper the tail hairs into a tuft. Curve the spine. Vary the rig from h1-s1 so the two are not the same animal in two colours.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon stegosaur-sauropod hybrid toy with a decorative racing stripe
rows.defect: A perfectly straight, ruled horizontal line runs the full length of the flank from shoulder to hip, with four flat pink/blue discs threaded onto it like beads on a wire. It is a machined straight edge laid over the torso and does not follow the body's curve at all. The dorsal spikes are separate hard-outlined triangles sitting ON the topline rather than emerging from it — the left-most two float clear of the back over a lump that reads as a second head. All four legs are identical straight tapered pills that butt into the belly with a visible seam; no shoulder or haunch mass anywhere. The rear of the animal ends in a rounded knob with no tail, so the silhouette is head-at-both-ends ambiguous.
rows.fix: Delete the ruled lateral line and the disc row entirely; if a lateral organ is wanted, paint it as a curved band that follows the belly arc with soft-edged, irregular blooms, not circles on a ruler. Grow the dorsal spikes from the back contour — the back outline itself should deform into each spike (shared silhouette, no separate outline), taper them front-to-back, and jitter spacing/height. Add scapula and pelvic bulges where the legs meet the torso and give each leg its own angle and joint bend. Resolve the rear: add a tapering tail so the head end is unambiguous.

rows.readsAs: A dead fish with two chicken legs stuck to it
rows.defect: There is no head and no face. The right end of the body is an unresolved series of bulges from which two thin stick limbs with club-shaped tips project sideways into empty air, giving the whole thing the read of a dead fish floating belly-up rather than a living animal. The tail is a pure geometric arrowhead — three perfectly straight-edged flat triangles meeting at a point, with hard machined edges and no membrane, ray, or taper. The body is a horizontal capsule with a smooth unbroken outline. A hard-edged rhombus outline is scribed on the flank like a decal. The limbs meet the body at abrupt seams with no hip mass.
rows.fix: Give it a head: a distinct cranial mass at the anterior end with at least one eye and a mouth line, and a neck/shoulder transition that widens into the torso. Rebuild the tail as a curved caudal fin — arced trailing edge, visible ray striations, soft membrane between lobes, base blended into the peduncle rather than a hard triangle junction. Break the capsule silhouette with a dorsal ridge and a belly curve of different radius. Remove the rhombus decal or replace it with skin-following texture. Root the limbs in a swelling of the body wall.

rows.readsAs: A striped cat-lizard, roughly a small dimetrodon crossed with a housecat
rows.defect: The dorsal sail is a separate cut-out shape sitting on the back with a hard straight base line where it meets the topline, and it is filled with perfectly straight parallel ribs — a printed fan, not tissue. The tiger stripes are sprayed on top: they run as flat dark bands that ignore the leg cylinders and stop dead at the body outline. The torso is a smooth lozenge with no ribcage or shoulder, and the legs are thin uniform tubes ending in hard dark ankle 'socks' with an abrupt tonal cut. Only two legs on the near side are drawn with any weight; the animal has no visible hip where the thin curling tail attaches.
rows.fix: Merge the sail into the back silhouette — the spine contour should rise continuously into the sail and the ribs should be curved, unevenly spaced, and taper to the sail's edge. Make the stripes wrap: bend each band along the barrel of the torso and carry a few onto the upper leg so they read as pigment in skin. Add a scapula bump, ribcage swell, and a haunch at the tail root; vary leg thickness and put a bend at each joint. Soften the ankle sock into a gradient rather than a hard band.

rows.readsAs: The same dead fish as s3, in green
rows.defect: Same defect set as fauna-h1-s3 and visibly the SAME organism recoloured — identical horizontal capsule body, identical flat triangular arrowhead tail on the left, identical pair of thin stick limbs with club tips on the right. Again there is no head and no eye anywhere. The scales are a perfect repeating grid of identical crescents in ruler-straight rows, sprayed across the body without changing size, spacing, or orientation over the curve of the flank, and they stop at a hard line at the body edge. The tail triangles are flat facets with straight machined edges.
rows.fix: Differentiate it from s3 at the silhouette level, not just the palette — different body depth, fin count, and tail shape. Add a head with an eye and mouth. Make the scale field respond to the form: shrink scales toward the tail and the belly, curve the rows to follow the body's cross-section, break the rows with irregularity, and fade them out at the contour instead of clipping. Replace the arrowhead tail with a rayed, arced caudal fin blended at the peduncle.

rows.readsAs: A purple deer or kangaroo with a firefly swarm accidentally baked into the layer
rows.defect: Bright white glowing dots are scattered as free-floating artifacts — at least four sit in empty background above and in front of the back, touching no part of the animal, and others straddle the body outline half on and half off. The body is two separately drawn masses: a large bulbous rear blob on the left overlaps the torso with a visible hard crescent seam, so the creature reads as an abdomen glued to a chest rather than one animal. The darker polka-dot rows are laid over the top in even ranks, unaffected by the form. Legs are thin uniform tubes with hard black hoof socks and no haunch or shoulder.
rows.fix: Clip every glow to the body mask and anchor each one to a skin feature; delete the ones in open space. Fuse the rear mass into a single continuous silhouette with the torso — one outline, with the rump and ribcage as swells of the same contour, not two overlapping ovals. Make the spot rows follow the barrel of the body and vary spot size with distance from the light. Build a haunch and a scapula where the legs attach and vary leg length and bend.

rows.readsAs: A glass toy turtle on two wheels
rows.defect: The legs are two flat grey circles floating underneath the shell — they touch nothing, have no thickness, no foot, no joint, and sit at exactly the fore and aft positions of wheels. The picture reads as a wheeled trolley. The shell is a perfect geometric half-dome with a dead-straight flat bottom edge and a ruled fan of radial spokes plus concentric arcs, like an umbrella diagram. The head is a perfect circle with a single dot eye, joined to the shell by a stubby neck with a hard seam and no jaw, mouth, or skull shape. There is no tail, no plastron, and no body between shell and ground.
rows.fix: Replace the circles with actual limbs: columnar forelegs and hindlegs emerging from under the carapace rim with visible shoulder/thigh mass, toes, and ground contact. Break the dome — give the carapace an irregular scute pattern with varied polygon sizes, a curved lower rim rather than a straight line, and a slight front-to-back asymmetry. Rebuild the head with a wedge skull, a beak/mouth line, and a wrinkled neck that widens into the shell opening. Add a short tail at the rear so the animal has direction.

rows.readsAs: A sea urchin, or more honestly a cartoon sun
rows.defect: The body is a mathematically perfect circle and the spines are ~26 identical straight tapered rods radiating at near-uniform angular spacing — a child's sun drawing, or a geometric primitive with a stroke pattern. Every rod is the same length and the same straightness; none bend, cross, or vary. The rods emerge from behind the circle with a hard occlusion edge rather than growing out of the skin. The only features are three tiny green dots on the right, which give no orientation, no mouth, and no read on which way the animal faces. A flat tonal band cuts horizontally across the sphere with a hard edge.
rows.fix: Deform the body off-circle — flatten the oral side, add lumps and an irregular contour. Vary spine length, thickness, curvature, and angular spacing substantially, let some cross and some be broken/stubby, and seat each spine in a visible tubercle on the skin so it grows out rather than being occluded by the disc. Add a mouth or oral opening to establish orientation. Replace the hard tonal band with a soft terminator that wraps the sphere.

rows.readsAs: A jellyfish — the one image in the batch whose organism is identifiable, but rendered as a lampshade with wires
rows.defect: The bell is a geometric half-ellipse with a dead-flat straight bottom edge and a uniform bright rim arc, with three thin ruled arcs drawn across it. Three pale grey perfect circles are stuck onto the bell margin like bolts — they are flat primitives with a hard outline, sitting on the surface rather than in it. The tentacles are near-straight vertical rods of constant width with rounded tips; they hang stiff, all roughly parallel, and are cut off abruptly at the bell rim with no visible attachment. Two darker tentacle masses behind read as flat silhouettes.
rows.fix: Curve the bell margin — scallop or ruffle it, drop the straight base, and let the bell asymmetry suggest a pulse. Sink the three circles into the bell as translucent gonads/organs seen through the tissue (soft edge, tone continuous with the bell) or remove them. Make tentacles taper from a thick base to a fine tip, curve each one differently, and let them originate from visible margin points so they read as growing from the rim. Add oral arms of a different, frillier character to break the uniform rod field.

rows.readsAs: a spiny caterpillar or hairless grub
rows.defect: Legless spiny grub in dark sage green. The head is a discrete rounded-triangle lobe with its own closed outline drawn ON TOP of the neck arc — a visible seam ring where head meets neck. The thin tail at the left emerges from the body mass at a hard joint with the same outline break. The seven dorsal spikes are flat isoceles triangles set on the back line with no base flare, so they read as stuck-on rather than grown. The single swept horn off the skull is a separate hairline triangle floating clear of the head at its tip. Body itself is decent — overlapping scalloped lobes with a warm rim light that genuinely read as segments.
rows.fix: Union the head lobe into the neck before stroking so only ONE silhouette outline exists; taper the spike bases into the dorsal contour (widen base 2x and blend the fill) instead of butting triangles onto the line; fuse the horn root into the skull mass.

rows.readsAs: a toy turtle on wheels, or a wheeled pull-along cart
rows.defect: This is built from geometric primitives, not anatomy. The shell is a clean half-ellipse with concentric arcs plus radiating spokes drawn over it like a wagon wheel. The shell meets the plastron along a perfectly straight horizontal brown bar. The two legs are FLAT PERFECT CIRCLES in solid brown, unattached to the body and hanging below the bar — they read as cartwheels, not limbs; only two are present and there is no toe, ankle or shoulder anywhere. The eye is a perfect circle with a perfect white catchlight. The cast shadow is a perfect ellipse. It is also drastically smaller in frame than every other organism in the batch.
rows.fix: Replace the circle legs with tapered limbs that flare out of the shell margin with an elbow and toes, and show four of them (two near, two far, far pair darker); break the straight shell/plastron line into a scalloped scute margin; replace the radial spoke overlay with irregular polygonal scutes that follow the shell curvature; scale the whole organism up to match the batch framing.

rows.readsAs: a blue zebra-striped toy dinosaur
rows.defect: The torso is a plain capsule — parallel top and bottom edges with hemispherical caps. Five identical vertical ellipses sit on the dorsal line as back plates, each with a visible arc where it crosses the back outline, i.e. pasted on top rather than emerging. The blue banding is a flat sprayed overlay: the bands cross the leg/body junction unchanged and go semi-transparent where limbs overlap, so you can see straight through the legs. Legs are four straight tapered sticks that terminate in a hard line against the belly with no shoulder or haunch. The tail is a fan of straight bristles like a paintbrush head, meeting the rump at a flat vertical cut.
rows.fix: Deform the torso spline (deepen the chest, tuck the flank, arch the spine) so it is not a capsule; give the dorsal plates a fused base that widens into the back silhouette and vary their height along the spine; render limbs opaque and paint the band pattern per-limb so it wraps rather than showing through; build shoulder/hip masses where the legs meet the trunk; taper the tail bristles from a fleshy tail base instead of a flat brush cut.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon green deer or jackalope
rows.defect: Green long-necked browser. Neck and head grow out cleanly and the ears are convincing, but the four legs are uniform-width tubes with rounded caps that simply intersect the belly — the front leg shows a hard elliptical seam at the shoulder and the knee is a straight-edged offset joint rather than a bend. The tail is a string of five separate dark beads projecting straight back and up, each bead a distinct circle with its own outline, clearly a chain of primitives rather than a tail. Dark spots are a uniform sprayed blotch field that ignores body form — same size and density on the flank, the neck and the haunch.
rows.fix: Add haunch and shoulder masses that swell out of the trunk and swallow the leg tops; taper the limbs (thick at hip, thin at ankle) and give the knee a curved contour; replace the bead chain with a single continuous tapering tail whose lumps are bulges in one outline; grade the spot field — larger and sparser on the flank, shrinking toward the neck and legs.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon giraffe or llama with fireflies floating past it
rows.defect: Off-body artifacts: six soft white glow blobs are scattered across the frame and several are clearly OUTSIDE the silhouette — two hang in the empty air in the gap between the fore and hind legs beneath the belly, and one sits off the shoulder over background. They have soft round halos and no skin attachment, so they read as dust motes composited over the picture rather than bioluminescent organs. Beyond that the morphology is a straight palette-swap of fauna-h0-s19: same lozenge torso, same tube legs with the hard shoulder seam, same five-bead chain tail, same round ears, same sprayed spot field, only orange instead of green.
rows.fix: Clamp emissive spots to inside the body mask and seat each one in a skin socket (dark ring + gradient into the hide) so it belongs to the animal; then differentiate this genome from s19 — change torso depth, neck length, ear shape and leg proportion, not just hue, or the two read as the same species.

rows.readsAs: a red six-legged caterpillar-cow with floating lights
rows.defect: Off-body artifacts again, and worse: at least four white glowing orbs float in empty background ABOVE the dorsal line, unconnected to the body, plus smudged white haze clouds around them. The six legs are identical thin sticks in three pairs, each butting into the belly at a hard point with no hip. The torso is a fat capsule whose only shaping is a lumpy underside. The dark dot rows are a regular polka grid sprayed over the hide — the rows run straight across the shoulder and the head at the same spacing, ignoring the form. The pale horn on the muzzle is a flat quadrilateral with straight machined edges pasted over the cheek.
rows.fix: Mask all emissive/haze layers to the body silhouette and anchor each orb in a pore; give each leg pair a hip bulge growing out of the trunk and vary the pairs in length; make the dot rows follow the body's curvature and compress toward the head; rebuild the horn as a curved tapering cone rooted in the skull rather than a straight-edged flat plate.

rows.readsAs: a dachshund-bandicoot or long-bodied jackrabbit
rows.defect: The best-integrated picture in the batch — neck, muzzle and ears genuinely flow out of one mass and the mottled hide has believable size variation. Two real defects remain. First, the limbs are vestigial: the forelimb is a single hairline stick and the hind pair are short thin pegs, all far too slight to carry the heavy body, and the forelimb meets the chest at a flat cut with no shoulder. Second, a pale grey rim highlight runs along the spine and then STOPS dead in mid-back with a visible hard terminus, reading as a pasted stroke rather than light. The tail is again a chain of discrete dark lumps.
rows.fix: Thicken and taper the limbs and grow shoulder/haunch masses over their tops; fade the dorsal rim highlight out with a gradient at both ends instead of ending it on a hard cap; merge the tail lumps into one continuous tapering outline.

rows.readsAs: a red plated caterpillar-dinosaur, essentially the blue s18 recolored
rows.defect: Structurally the same build as fauna-h0-s18 recolored red: capsule torso, five identical vertical ellipse plates seated on the dorsal line each showing an arc where it crosses the back outline, wide dark bands sprayed across the body. The bands and plates are semi-transparent — you can see the darker band continue straight through the legs and through the plate overlaps, so the whole animal looks like layered cellophane rather than solid flesh. Six thin stick legs meet the belly at hard points with no hip. The head is a small pinched cone with a dark tuft blob sitting on top of it as a separate shape, and the tail is a bare hairline curve with no root.
rows.fix: Render body, limbs and plates opaque and composite in depth order so nothing shows through; fuse the plate bases into the back contour and vary their size along the spine; deform the torso off the capsule (chest, flank tuck, rump); root the tail in a fleshy base that tapers; blend the head tuft into the skull. Also re-roll this genome away from s18 — as shipped they are one species in two colors.

rows.readsAs: a brown suppository or bowling pin with two heads of broccoli balanced on it
rows.defect: The trunk is a smooth almond/lens capsule — widest at mid-height and NARROWING as it reaches the ground, which is backwards for any woody stem (no root flare, no base widening). It is filled with a single flat brown airbrush gradient: zero bark, zero grain, zero silhouette break. The canopy is two separate cotton-wool teal puffs dropped onto the top-left and top-right of the trunk; between them a small fan of 3-4 straight brown branch strokes pops out of the trunk top and terminates abruptly at the puff edge, leaving a visible hard line where canopy meets wood. The puffs also overlap each other with a crisp cut edge instead of interleaving.
rows.fix: Invert the trunk taper — widest at the base with 2-3 root buttress lobes breaking the outline, narrowing upward, and break the silhouette with bark ridges/knots so it is not a lens primitive. Grow the branch fan out of the trunk as a continuous tapering fork (same paint pass, no butt-joint), and let branch tips penetrate INTO the foliage so leaf clumps read as attached to twigs rather than balanced on top. Replace the two smooth cotton puffs with a single irregular canopy mass built from overlapping tonal clumps with a ragged, non-convex outer edge.

rows.readsAs: a purple palm or cycad clump — recognisable as a fern/palm, but plastic
rows.defect: The pinnae are a machine stamp: every barb along every frond is the same isoceles triangle at the same angle and the same spacing, running full-size right to the frond tip with no taper, no shortening, no gap variation. Each rachis carries an identical hard-edged bright centre stripe. All ~14 fronds live in one flat plane with no depth ordering or foreshortening, and the crown is a single point at bottom-centre with no sheath, no stipe bases, no emerging croziers — fronds simply converge on a dot. There is also a small isolated ring/spiral floating near the base right of the crown that reads as an artifact. Critically it is the SAME plant as flora-h1-s3 in this batch, pixel-structure for pixel-structure, only recoloured purple.
rows.fix: Taper the pinnae along the rachis (long at mid-frond, short at base and tip) and jitter length/angle/spacing per pinna; curve the pinnae so they are scythe-shaped rather than straight triangles. Build a real crown: overlapping fibrous stipe bases with a widening trunk-let, so fronds emerge from a structure not a point. Vary frond arc and out-of-plane rotation so back fronds foreshorten. Reseed s17 off a different frond count/arc/curl so it is not a palette swap of s3.

rows.readsAs: a supermarket bouquet of white-leaved stems with red berry sprays
rows.defect: The base is a florist's bunch, not a plant: eight perfectly straight stems run parallel into a solid flat pale-green wedge that sits on the soil like a cut bouquet dropped into a vase — no root spread, no divergence at ground level. Every leaf is the identical almond shape with the identical crisp vector outline and the identical single specular highlight, mirrored in pairs; they meet the stems at a clean point with a visible junction, reading as stickers rather than as growth. The stems themselves are hard polylines with sharp angular kinks. The whole render is flat vector fill with a linear gradient — no painterly tooth at all, which is off-engine for this project.
rows.fix: Splay and curve the stems at the base so they emerge from separate points in the soil with a visible crown; kill the solid wedge. Randomise leaf length, width, curl and rotation per leaf and taper leaf size toward the stem tips; draw a short petiole that thickens into the stem so the join is a fillet, not a point. Replace the polyline kinks with smooth nodal bends and add internode swelling at each node. Re-render through the painterly pass so edges carry brush texture instead of vector crispness.

rows.readsAs: a dried yellow bamboo-ish shrub with tiny red flower heads
rows.defect: Same skeleton as flora-h1-s18 recoloured olive/yellow — identical bundled-wedge base, identical stem topology, identical red flower cluster placement — so the two do not read as different species. The stems are extreme zigzags: hard straight segments meeting at sharp acute angles that read as cracked glass or lightning bolts, not as plant growth. Leaves are thin identical slivers, and on the outer left and outer right at mid-height several slivers sit clear of any stem they could be attached to, reading as off-body artifacts. The base is again a solid tapered pale wedge like a paintbrush ferrule.
rows.fix: Reseed the whole silhouette rather than recolouring s18 — different stem count, branching order and inflorescence type. Smooth the zigzag into gentle nodal curvature with a swollen node at each direction change, and clamp the bend angle so no segment turns more than ~25 degrees. Re-anchor every leaf to an explicit stem node with a short petiole and cull any leaf whose anchor is offscreen or occluded. Break the base wedge into individual splayed culms with a soil-contact flare.

rows.readsAs: a floor lamp, or a blue side table with a fried egg on it — nobody would call it a plant
rows.defect: This is a set of geometry primitives, not an organism. A perfectly straight 3px dark brown line, no taper and no texture, runs floor to mid-frame; a mathematically perfect blue ELLIPSE sits horizontally on top of it; on the ellipse sits a lumpy red-orange blob wrapping a perfectly round pale yellow CIRCLE. Everything is heavily airbrushed and out of focus. There is no growth logic anywhere: the stem meets the ellipse at a bare intersection with no receptacle or flare, and the red blob sits on the ellipse surface with a hard seam. Colour-wise the blue disc, red blob and yellow circle share no palette relationship.
rows.fix: Delete the perfect-ellipse cap and the perfect-circle centre. Rebuild as a real structure: a tapering stem that thickens toward the base and flares into a receptacle, and a cap/bloom whose outline is irregular and non-elliptical with radial ribbing that visibly continues down into the stem. Anchor the red element as petals or bracts that spring from the same receptacle rather than resting on the disc. Sharpen the focus — every edge here is blurred to mush — and pull the three colours into one harmony.

rows.readsAs: a green palm or tree-fern crown — correct family, but reads as moulded plastic
rows.defect: Structurally the strongest render in the batch, but it is the exact same asset as flora-h1-s17 recoloured mint green — same frond count, same fan arc, same crown point, same stray small ring artifact near the base. The pinnae are a repeated stamp: uniform triangles, uniform spacing, full size all the way to the frond tip with no taper, so each frond reads as a saw blade rather than a leaf. Every frond has the same hard bright rachis stripe and all of them sit in one flat plane with no depth. The crown converges on a bare point with no stipe bases or trunk, so the fan is not attached to anything.
rows.fix: Taper and jitter the pinnae per-frond (shorter at base and apex, slight scythe curve, varied gaps) and soften the rachis highlight into the leaf. Give the fan a real crown — overlapping fibrous stipe bases widening into a short caudex so fronds grow out of a body. Vary per-frond out-of-plane rotation for depth. Remove the stray ring near the crown. Then differentiate s3 and s17 by structure, not palette.

rows.readsAs: a thermometer or a plastic measuring ruler — a manufactured object, not a living thing
rows.defect: This is not an organism at all. The silhouette is a literal rounded rectangle: two dead-straight vertical parallel sides, a perfect semicircular dome on top, cut flat where it meets the ground. It is filled with a single pale bone/grey vertical gradient, no texture. Six short horizontal ticks of identical length stick out on the left side and six on the right at perfectly regular vertical intervals — a scale of graduation marks, machined and evenly spaced. One lone small curved leaf shape hangs on the upper left, the only organic mark in the frame, and it is stuck ON the column with a hard edge, not growing out of it. Nothing tapers, nothing branches, nothing varies.
rows.fix: Total re-render. Break the rounded-rectangle silhouette — taper the column, add irregular ribbing or segmentation that bulges the outline, flare it at the soil. Replace the regular tick marks with spines or leaf scars that vary in length, angle and spacing and that visibly emerge from a rib rather than being pasted to a flat side. If the intent is a columnar succulent, add multiple offset arms of different heights and a fluted cross-section shading; if it is a stalk, add real leaves at the nodes. As it stands, no parameter tweak saves this shape.

rows.readsAs: an out-of-focus photo of cotton buds or matchsticks stuck into a purple eraser
rows.defect: The entire image is rendered out of focus — every edge is a soft bokeh smear, unreadable at 440px. Beneath the blur the parts are bare primitives: a hard-edged horizontal purple rounded BAR laid across the bottom like a UI progress bar or an eraser, and six thin dark straight sticks with perfect white circles on their tips. Five sticks cluster left of centre, one taller pair sits isolated far right with a gap of empty frame between the two groups, so the composition does not read as one organism. There is no stem taper, no leaf, no branching, no attachment detail where the sticks meet the purple bar, and the bar itself has no soil, root or body character.
rows.fix: Fix the focus first — this looks like the blur/glow pass ran at full strength with no sharp base layer; restore crisp silhouettes before judging anything else. Then replace the purple bar with an actual body (a rosette, pad or bulb) whose outline is irregular, and grow the stalks out of it with a visible thickened foot. Taper the stalks, curve them, vary their heights continuously instead of in two separated clumps, and give the heads irregular sporangium/bud shapes rather than perfect circles.

rows.readsAs: blurry photo of five dandelion/cotton-grass seed heads standing behind a glowing turquoise canoe or bathtub
rows.defect: The entire 440px render is out of focus — every edge in the frame (stalks, heads, the teal shape) is soft-blurred by ~8-10px, as if a depth-of-field pass was applied to the whole canvas with nothing left sharp. On top of that the composition is three disconnected pieces: six perfectly round white balls, five thin straight brown sticks in a clump at left plus one lone stick at right, and a bright teal lens/eye shape lying across the bottom whose top edge is a dead-straight horizontal line with symmetric pointed ends. The sticks do not meet the teal shape at all — they terminate in mid-air ~20px above it with a hard cut, and the lone right-hand stick stands entirely off the teal shape's right end over bare background. The ball heads are geometric circles pasted on stick tips with a visible seam; no calyx, no receptacle, no thickening where head meets stalk. There is also no visible connection between the left clump and the right stalk, so the picture reads as two separate objects.
rows.fix: 1) Remove the global blur — this looks like a canvas-wide filter/shadowBlur left on; the organism must render sharp with only intentional soft shading. 2) Root the stalks: extend each stalk down INTO the teal basal pad and grow the pad's silhouette upward around each insertion point so the outline bulges where a stalk enters, instead of a straight-edged lens sitting under floating sticks. 3) Break the teal pad's straight top edge — give it an irregular, lobed rosette outline rather than a symmetric lens primitive, and lose the pure-cyan flat fill in favour of value variation. 4) Swap the perfect-circle heads for slightly irregular ovoid capitula, and taper the stalk into the head over 6-10px so there is no seam. 5) Bring the outlying right stalk into the same rosette or drop it.

rows.readsAs: clip-art Christmas tree / a paper cut-out holiday decoration
rows.defect: This is a vector Christmas-tree icon, not an organism. Five brick-red isoceles triangles are stacked in a perfect size progression down a straight brown vertical bar, plus a sixth narrow triangle as the apex. Every edge is dead straight and machined; every triangle has the same apex angle and the same flat colour with a single smooth top-to-bottom gradient. The tiers do not overlap or interleave, they simply stack with clean air between them. The trunk is a constant-width rectangle with parallel sides that vanishes behind each triangle and reappears below with a hard horizontal seam at every crossing — no flare at the base, no root spread, no branch stubs anywhere. Under the tree is a flat black ellipse for a shadow. There is not one curve, not one irregular contour, and no needle, leaf or branch texture at any scale.
rows.fix: Replace the triangle-stack with actual branch geometry: generate 5-8 whorls of individual boughs, each a curved tapering spline with downward droop and slight per-branch angle/length jitter, then clothe them with needle/frond marks so the silhouette edge is ragged rather than a straight hypotenuse. Flare the trunk into a root buttress at ground and let branch bases swell into the trunk (no hard crossing seam). Vary tier spacing non-uniformly and let adjacent whorls overlap. Drop the flat black ellipse for a soft contact shadow that hugs the root flare.

rows.readsAs: a goldenrod or yarrow flowering shrub — a bouquet of yellow star flowers jammed into a stick
rows.defect: The best-reading image in the batch — a dense head of yellow star florets with a few dusty-pink berry clusters — but the plant is a flower-ball impaled on a stick. The olive trunk is a bare tapered wedge that rises ~50px with nothing on it, then the flower mass begins at a hard, almost horizontal boundary; no branches, twigs or peduncles are visible anywhere between trunk and blooms, so the canopy is stuck ON rather than grown OUT. The trunk edges are two straight converging lines. Inside the canopy every floret is the same stamped 8-point star at nearly the same scale and the same yellow, tiled to fill the mass, which makes it read as a repeated sprite rather than a population of flowers at different ages and depths. The pink berry clusters sit only on the top-right rim and are not carried by any visible stem.
rows.fix: 1) Draw the branching: fan 5-9 tapering stems out of the trunk apex and let each floret sit on the end of a visible pedicel, so the canopy's lower boundary is a scatter of stems rather than a hard line. 2) Give the trunk a curved, slightly irregular contour with a root flare at ground. 3) Jitter floret scale (0.6x-1.4x), rotation and petal count, and darken/desaturate the florets deeper in the mass so the canopy has depth instead of a flat yellow slab. 4) Hang the pink clusters from their own visible stems distributed through the canopy, not only along the top-right silhouette edge.

rows.readsAs: a blue cycad or tree-fern rosette / a peacock-tail fan of fern fronds
rows.defect: A blue pinnate-frond fan that is close to working but is built as a radial primitive. All ~13 fronds converge on one exact mathematical point at bottom centre with near-even angular spacing across a 180-degree sweep — there is no crown, caudex, rhizome or stem mass at the convergence, just a pinch, so the plant has no base and the silhouette is a clean half-disc. Along each rachis the pinnae are identical straight triangular teeth at uniform spacing and uniform length, machined rather than tapering toward the frond tip. Behind each blue frond sits a dark navy copy offset by a few pixels in the same shape — it reads as a duplicated stamped shadow layer, not as form shading or as a frond behind. There is also a small light ring / circle artifact roughly 20px above-left of the convergence point sitting on top of the fronds and belonging to nothing.
rows.fix: 1) Add a base: a short thickened caudex or crown of overlapping leaf scars at the convergence, and start each frond from a slightly different point on that crown rather than one shared vertex. 2) Randomise the inter-frond angles and lengths so the outline is not a perfect semicircle; let one or two fronds cross in front of others. 3) Taper pinnae length from mid-rachis to tip and curve them toward the tip; jitter their spacing. 4) Replace the offset dark duplicate with real shading — darken the underside half of each frond along its own rachis instead of drawing a displaced copy. 5) Track down and remove the stray circle artifact near the crown.

rows.readsAs: a red-leaf dogwood or bamboo twig arrangement — flat pink leaf stickers on straight brown sticks
rows.defect: Leaves are pasted on top of the stems rather than attached to them. Several of the pink lance-shaped leaves run straight ACROSS a brown stem and continue out the far side, forming visible X crossings (clearest in the mid-left and centre of the bush) — the leaf is a lens primitive drawn over the stem with no petiole, no junction swelling and no occlusion, so it reads as decal on a line. The stems themselves are perfectly straight constant-width brown bars radiating from the base with no bend, no taper along their length and no branching; they simply end in blunt tips. The base is a solid brown triangular wedge with a hard boundary where the stems begin. Every leaf is the same shape and roughly the same length, rotated at arbitrary angles, and their pink is a flat fill with a single gradient — no midrib, no edge variation. Sparse coverage leaves a lot of visible bare background between elements, so the silhouette does not resolve as a shrub.
rows.fix: 1) Attach the leaves: give each a short petiole that meets the stem at a swollen node, clip the leaf so it never crosses to the far side, and orient leaves along the local stem tangent instead of at random angles. 2) Make the stems organic — curve each with a spline, taper from base to tip, and let secondary twigs fork off primary stems rather than all rays leaving the base. 3) Dissolve the triangular base wedge into the stems with a root flare so there is no hard boundary line. 4) Add a midrib and per-leaf shape/scale jitter, and raise leaf density so the canopy reads as mass rather than scattered marks.

rows.readsAs: a stack of orange pancakes on a skewer, or a wooden toy pagoda — not a living thing
rows.defect: Five orange ellipses of increasing width threaded onto a straight brown vertical pole. That is the whole image. Each tier is a mathematically perfect ellipse with a uniform flat orange fill and one soft gradient; the edges are smooth machined curves with zero irregularity, zero leaf detail and zero silhouette break. The pole is a constant-width bar that passes in FRONT of the ellipses at the top and BEHIND them lower down, producing a hard straight seam at every crossing and no attachment structure at all — the discs are not growing from the stem, they are skewered on it. No branch, no petiole, no bark, no texture, no root. This is also structurally the same object as flora-h0-s13 (same tiered-cone-on-a-pole topology, triangles swapped for ellipses), so the two collide inside one batch.
rows.fix: This one needs to stop being a disc-stack. Convert each tier into a whorl of individual radiating boughs drawn from the trunk outward, with foliage clumps at the ends so the tier's outline is lobed and ragged, not elliptical. Make the trunk taper and curve, flare it into roots at ground, and swell each branch base into the trunk so there is no crossing seam. Randomise tier spacing, tier tilt and tier diameter so the progression is not a clean linear ramp. Give the foliage internal value variation and a few gaps you can see sky through. Also diverge the archetype from flora-h0-s13 so the two do not share a silhouette.

rows.readsAs: a thermometer or a graduated measuring cylinder / a UI slider widget — if generous, a very stylised saguaro
rows.defect: The silhouette is literally a rounded rectangle. A flat teal capsule ~70px wide and ~350px tall, with dead-parallel vertical sides and a semicircular cap, standing on a black ellipse. Seven grey horizontal tick marks are drawn across it at regular intervals — and they OVERSHOOT the body on both sides, extending 15-20px into the bare background left and right, so they are off-body artifacts floating in space rather than ribs on a surface. They are straight lines of uniform grey with no thickness variation, sprayed on top instead of being the plant's own ridges. The single 'arm' at upper left is a flat teal crescent with a hard chord edge that stops short of the trunk entirely — there is a visible gap of background between the crescent's inner edge and the trunk, so the limb is not attached to anything. No areoles, spines, taper, or ground contact — the trunk's bottom edge is a straight horizontal cut.
rows.fix: 1) Kill the capsule: rebuild the trunk as a fluted column whose outline undulates with the ribs, wider at the base, narrowing and rounding to a domed apex — the rib count must be visible in the silhouette. 2) Clip the rib marks to the body and replace the flat grey lines with shaded rib valleys that follow the trunk's curvature and converge at the apex; ribs must never cross the outline into background. 3) Reattach the arm — grow it out of the trunk with a continuous outline and a filled elbow so trunk and arm share one silhouette, and curve it upward like a saguaro branch rather than leaving a detached crescent. 4) Add a root flare and soft contact shadow instead of the straight bottom cut on a black ellipse.

rows.readsAs: a gold sunburst / sunrise logo — at best an agave or palmetto rosette
rows.defect: Reads as a vector sunburst emblem rather than a plant. Fifteen gold blades radiate from one exact point at bottom centre in an even 180-degree fan; each blade is a straight, needle-perfect lance with two machined straight edges converging to a sharp point, and lengths step smoothly from short at the outside to long at the top so the outline is a clean symmetric arc. There is no crown, no stem, no basal rosette mass at the convergence — the blades just meet at a vertex sitting on a flat black ellipse. Every blade carries the identical linear gradient (dark at base, bright gold at mid, pale at tip) applied at the same angle regardless of blade orientation, which is what makes the whole thing read as a printed logo. No midrib, no fold, no serration, no per-blade damage or curl. It is also the same radial-fan archetype as flora-h0-s15 in this same batch, differing only by pinnae.
rows.fix: 1) Build a base — a short fibrous crown or bulb at the convergence, with blades emerging from distinct points on it and a few dead/brown outer leaves at ground. 2) Curve the blades: each should arc and droop under its own weight, with the outer ones bending nearly to the ground; straight lances are the core tell. 3) Randomise angular spacing, length and width so the outline is asymmetric and a couple of blades cross in front of neighbours. 4) Give each blade a midrib crease with shading that follows ITS OWN axis (not a global gradient direction), plus edge serration or fibre texture and a little per-blade colour drift. 5) Differentiate it from flora-h0-s15's fan silhouette.

rows.readsAs: A mushroom cap with strings hanging off it — or, on a second look, a jellyfish, but a toy-shaped one.
rows.defect: The bell is a literal geometric primitive: a near-perfect half-disc whose bottom edge is a dead-straight horizontal chord running the full width of the cap, with a pale rim stroke drawn along it like a ruled line. Every tentacle is a uniform-width capsule rod with a rounded cap, and all ten of them terminate abruptly at that chord — a hard, unbroken seam where the whole tentacle array is stuck onto the underside of the cap rather than growing out of a bell margin. Four flat, perfectly circular discs (two pale blue, one red, one blue) are pasted across the seam line as though airbrushed on; they have no relationship to the bell's volume and read as decals. The tentacles are also all the same thickness top-to-bottom and hang as a parallel picket fence with no taper, no crossing, no flow.
rows.fix: Replace the half-disc with an asymmetric bell profile: a domed apex whose sides curve inward and then flare into a scalloped, wavy margin (8-12 lobes) so the lower boundary is never a straight line. Grow the tentacles from that margin — each one should start at the width of its lobe and taper to a point over its length, with per-tentacle length jitter (0.6-1.4x) and a lateral drift curve so they cross and bunch instead of hanging parallel. Delete the four circle decals; render gonads as soft translucent horseshoe/petal masses seen THROUGH the semi-transparent bell (draw them before the bell fill, at 40-60% alpha), not as opaque discs on top of it. Add a translucent oral-arm cluster in the center, shorter and frillier than the marginal tentacles, so the underside has interior structure instead of a flat edge.

rows.readsAs: A fish — a generic red minnow or trout-shaped fish. Correct family, but posed like a clip-art fish.
rows.defect: The most legible piece in the batch — it does read as a fish — but the fins are appliqué. The dorsal fin is a dark triangular flap whose base is a straight line lying flat along the top of the back, with a visible tonal step where it meets the body: it sits on the fish, it does not emerge from it. The caudal fin has the same problem at the peduncle — a hard vertical boundary where the wedge is butted against the body with no narrowing of the body into it. The eye is a perfect white circle with a black pupil dot, a cartoon sticker overlapping the head outline rather than an eye set into a socket. There are no pectoral or pelvic fins at all and no gill opening or mouth line, so the head is a blank point. The internal pale chevron/streak markings float over the body with soft airbrush edges and do not follow the body's curvature.
rows.fix: Taper the body into a narrow caudal peduncle and let the tail's rays fan out from that neck, so the join is a width transition and not an edge. Build the dorsal fin from individual rays whose bases sink into the dorsal contour, with the membrane between them slightly translucent and the body's color bleeding a few pixels up into the fin base. Add a pectoral fin on the near flank and a small pelvic fin — a fish with only two fins reads as a decal. Add a short curved gill slit behind the head and an angled mouth line at the snout. Shrink the eye ~35%, drop the pure-white ring, and seat it with a darker orbital shadow. Re-draw the flank markings as chevron myomere bands that follow the body arc and are clipped to the body silhouette.

rows.readsAs: Nothing real. A lumpy sausage or caterpillar with a separate fin object resting on its back — closest guess would be a chewed-up plastic dinosaur toy.
rows.defect: This does not resolve into any organism. The body is a horizontal chain of eight or nine overlapping dark-red spheres — a visible string of blobs with the individual ball outlines still readable, a metaball chain that never fused. Sitting on the back is a large leaf-shaped plume with its own hard continuous outline and a completely different, glossier shading pass; it is glued to the top of the blob-chain with a visible seam along its entire base and nothing about the body deforms to accept it. Three flat grey/pink perfect circles are spaced along the flank at even intervals like buttons. The tail end degenerates into a machined zigzag sawtooth of identical triangles. The head is a small lump with straight radiating hairline whiskers and a row of orange dots. There are no legs and no belly line — the creature has no way of standing on the ground shadow beneath it.
rows.fix: Stop this silhouette from being a bead chain: run a single tapered spine spline from head to tail and skin it with one continuous outline, using the blob field only to modulate the width, not to emit visible circles. The back plume must grow out of the body — narrow its base to a root a third of its current width, sink that root below the dorsal contour, and shade the plume from the body's own color ramp instead of a separate glossy pass. Replace the three flank circles with segmental structures that wrap the body's curvature (paired spiracles or overlapping plate edges), never head-on discs. Replace the sawtooth tail with a tapering fluke or a set of curved, unequal spines of varying length. Add at least one pair of visible limbs or a distinct ventral foot so the animal contacts the ground plane, and give the head a jaw or beak so it is distinguishable from the body lumps.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon sun icon. Second guess: a sea urchin, or a virus particle from a diagram.
rows.defect: This is a geometric primitive, not an organism: a mathematically perfect brown circle with roughly twenty-four straight gold spikes radiating from it at even angular spacing. Every spike is the same length, the same width from base to tip, capped with the same rounded end, and drawn with a bright specular line down its center — they are line segments, not appendages. The spikes stop dead at the circle's edge with no basal swelling, no socket, no darkening; the body outline is continuous underneath them, so they are unambiguously drawn on top rather than growing out. The body has one flat horizontal tonal band across its lower third — a straight-edged gradient stop, not a form shadow. Three tiny yellow dots stacked vertically serve as the only anatomy. The whole thing is bilaterally and radially symmetric to the pixel.
rows.fix: Break the circle: apply low-frequency noise to the body radius so the silhouette is lumpy and slightly ovoid, and offset its center from the frame center. Randomize spike length by at least ±40%, taper each one from a wide base to a fine point, curve them along a slight arc, and jitter both their angular spacing and their emergence angle so they are not a fan. Root each spike with a swollen tubercle that reads as part of the skin, and shade the base with the body's own tone so no boundary line survives. Delete the straight horizontal band and replace it with a curved terminator following the sphere. Give it a mouth, an oral opening, or a definite ventral side so it has an orientation — a radially symmetric ball reads as an icon, not an animal.

rows.readsAs: A red ornamental shrub — something bamboo-like or a red willow. Legible as a plant, but recognizably a procedural stamp job.
rows.defect: Reads clearly as a plant, but it is assembled from stamped clones. Every leaf is the identical narrow lance shape at the identical scale, alternating left and right off each stem at the same fixed angle and the same regular spacing all the way up — the repetition is obvious at a glance and no leaf overlaps, curls, or foreshortens differently from any other. The stems are dead-straight tapered wedges radiating from a common point like a hand of cards, with no curvature and no response to gravity. The base is a smooth cone/triangle with a hard edge and no root flare or ground contact. The berry clusters at the tips are groups of small perfect circles of the same radius, sitting flat with no shading variation. The stems also emerge from the trunk cone at a single point with a visible junction rather than dividing out of it.
rows.fix: Curve every stem — arc each one along a spline with a slight outward lean and droop at the tip, and vary the branch angles by ±20 degrees. Scale leaves by node position (larger at the base, smaller near the tips) and give each leaf independent rotation jitter of ±25 degrees plus a curl along its midrib so some show broadside and some edge-on; let a few overlap and occlude. Break the alternate-at-fixed-interval spacing with node-distance jitter. Give each berry a distinct radius, a specular offset, and slight cluster crowding so no two are the same disc. Flare the trunk base outward into the ground shadow and let the stems divide from the trunk at staggered heights rather than one shared origin point.

rows.readsAs: Cotton swabs standing in a shallow dish. If forced to name a plant: dandelion seed heads, badly out of focus.
rows.defect: Nothing here reads as a living thing, and the whole render is out of focus — the entire subject is smeared under a heavy blur so no edge in it is sharp, which alone makes it unshippable next to the other seven. Structurally: the base is a flat teal lens/ellipse primitive with a hard straight top edge and a smooth arc bottom, floating as a saucer with no soil contact and no root; it looks like a dish, not part of the organism. Seven dead-straight, one-pixel-wide vertical lines rise from it — the same width from bottom to top, no taper, no curve, no lean — and each one is capped with a soft white puffball. The stalks do not meet the base at any visible junction; they just start above it. The white blobs are barely brighter than the background and several overlap into an indistinct smear. Contrast against the dark background is so low the plant nearly disappears.
rows.fix: First remove the global blur — this looks like a blur radius scaled off the wrong dimension; render the subject sharp and reserve blur for background depth only. Replace the lens base with a rosette of low, overlapping basal leaves whose tips break the silhouette, sitting in a shadow that reads as contact with ground. Taper each stalk from a thick base to a thin neck, curve them with independent bend and lean, and let them emerge from between the basal leaves so there is a real junction. Give the seed heads structure — radiating pappus filaments or visible florets — instead of a soft dot, and vary head size and maturity. Raise the value contrast of both stalks and heads at least two steps so the plant separates from the dark background.

rows.readsAs: Cotton candy on a stick, or a lollipop. Not identifiable as a plant species at all.
rows.defect: A featureless pink cloud blob impaled on a stick. The stem is a machined straight rod of perfectly constant width from the ground shadow all the way up, with parallel sides, no taper, no bend, no bark texture, and no root flare — a rectangle with rounded ends. It penetrates the canopy as a straight line and the canopy simply overlaps it, so the two objects never join; there is no branching whatsoever between trunk and crown. The canopy itself is a single metaball mass with a large concave bite out of its right side and a few soft lighter dots scribbled inside; it contains zero leaf shapes, zero twigs, and zero internal silhouette detail, so it reads as vapor rather than foliage. The blob's boundary is uniformly soft everywhere, which flattens it — no side of the crown is lit differently from another.
rows.fix: Taper the trunk from a wide, flared base to a narrow top and curve it; give it a bark value break and a root spread that dies into the ground shadow. Most importantly, branch it: split the trunk into 3-5 primary limbs that fan into the canopy volume, and let a few of those limb tips be visible against sky at the canopy's edge so the crown is clearly supported. Break the crown into 4-6 overlapping foliage clumps at different depths and values rather than one blob, and cut leaf-scale notches into the outer silhouette so the boundary is serrated, not soft everywhere. Light the crown directionally — bright on the upper-left masses, deep shadow under the lower-right ones. Remove or motivate the large right-side concavity; as drawn it reads as a bite taken out of the shape.

rows.readsAs: A tree — a generic broadleaf or maple. Family is right, but it reads as a game-asset placeholder tree, and its blob-on-a-stick construction is the same recipe as flora-h0-s10 in this batch.
rows.defect: It reads as a tree, but the construction is exposed. The trunk is a capsule primitive: constant width from ground to top, parallel sides, and a clearly visible ROUNDED CAP where it terminates inside the canopy — you can see the dome of the capsule through the foliage haze. It has no taper, no root flare, and it is the same green as the leaves, so it reads as an extruded shape rather than wood. There is no branching at all between trunk and crown; the leaves float unsupported. The canopy is a ring of clone-stamped identical star/maple leaf shapes at a single scale, distributed around the perimeter with an obvious hollow donut hole in the middle where only a flat green haze shows — the crown has no interior. The stamped leaves also all sit at the same depth with the same value, so the crown has no volume, and several near the outer edge are cut off flat by the sprite boundary.
rows.fix: Taper the trunk to ~60% of its base width at the top, give it a slight lean and curve, flare the base into buttress roots, and shift its color to a desaturated brown-grey so it separates from the foliage. Terminate it not in a cap but in a fork of 3-5 branches that spread into the crown, with visible secondary twigs where the leaf clusters attach.
