Fill the donut hole: distribute leaf clusters through the crown's interior at varying scale (0.6-1.4x) and value, darkening the ones on the shadow side and behind, so the canopy has front-to-back depth. Give each leaf stamp independent rotation and a small shape variation so the maple-star silhouette does not repeat identically ten times around the ring. Pull the outermost leaves in from the sprite edge so none are clipped flat.

rows.readsAs: A courgette with a paper fin taped to its back — at best a generic cartoon fish
rows.defect: The body is a bare olive ellipse — a capsule silhouette with no head/trunk/caudal transition at all. Everything else is stuck onto it: a row of pale-outlined triangular spikes sits on the back along a clearly visible hard line (the spikes do not grow out of the dorsal ridge, they are a zigzag polygon pasted over the ellipse edge), and a dead-straight, uniform-width needle projects horizontally out of the right end at belly level like a length of wire. The tail is a tiny pale striped triangle on a thin peduncle, far too small for the body mass it has to move. Two cyan dots sit side by side on the right flank, so a strict side view shows both eyes. A small square tab hangs off the underside of the belly with no anatomical reading. Zero skin texture across a 440px canvas.
rows.fix: Replace the ellipse body with a profile spline that has an actual head taper and a caudal peduncle. Grow the dorsal spikes from the back contour — displace the body outline itself into the spikes rather than compositing a separate spiked polygon over it, and kill the pale stroke that draws the seam. Delete the straight rostrum needle or rebuild it as a tapered snout continuous with the head. Drop to one eye for a lateral view and enlarge it. Scale the caudal fin up ~2.5x. Remove the belly tab. Add a scale/mottle field driven by body UV so it wraps the form.

rows.readsAs: A mackerel holding a grey spoon in its mouth
rows.defect: A grey PERFECT ELLIPSE floats at the snout, tilted ~15deg, overlapping the nose but never merging with it — a paddle-shaped blob stuck onto the head with a hard boundary. The body is a symmetrical almond/lens with a dead-straight lateral line ruled down the middle. The single pectoral fin is a hard-edged grey triangle with straight radial rays, sitting on top of the flank with no root. The eye is a cartoon white ball with a black dot, in a completely different rendering language from the rest of the painting. The drop shadow is a detached dark ellipse floating roughly 70px BELOW the animal with nothing connecting them — an off-body artifact. The creature also occupies only about a third of the frame.
rows.fix: Merge the snout blob into the head — either extend it as a continuous rostrum/bill built from the head spline, or remove it. Bow the lateral line to follow the body curve and soften it into a gradient rather than a stroke. Root the pectoral fin with a fleshy base and taper its trailing edge. Restyle the eye to match the painterly shading (iris gradient, lid, no pure-white sclera). Move the ground shadow so it sits under the body, or remove it for a swimming pose. Increase subject scale to fill the frame.

rows.readsAs: A paper dart or a stingray propped up on two chopsticks
rows.defect: The torso is a flat horizontal WEDGE — a triangle with dead-straight upper and lower edges converging to a sharp needle point at the left, bolted to a rounded bulb at the right. That is a geometric primitive, not an animal. The dorsal sail is a hard-edged dome with straight ruled ribs, meeting the back along a visible line. Only TWO legs exist on what is posed as a quadruped, and each is a straight thin tube of constant taper with a single sharp bend and no musculature, joining the underside at an abrupt seam. Straight-line whiskers radiate from the head like drawn spokes. Everything is one flat cyan with a single soft highlight.
rows.fix: Rebuild the torso as a closed organic spline with a belly curve and a real tail taper — no straight edges. Grow the sail from the spine by displacing the back contour, and curve the ribs so they follow the sail's own surface. Give it four legs with visible near/far pairs, thicken them, and add a fleshy shoulder/hip mass so the limb emerges from the body instead of docking onto it. Replace the straight whiskers with curved tapered barbels. Add surface texture.

rows.readsAs: An ankylosaur body with a bolt cutter or a bucket excavator for a head
rows.defect: The head is a machine part: a straight tapered BAR rises from the shoulders to an angular hooked box containing a grid of eight identical square orange teeth in two neat rows — perfect squares in a rectangular array, which is the most obviously synthetic element in the whole batch. The bar-neck has no widening where it meets the torso, just a butt joint. The scale texture is a single uniform stamped diaper pattern applied at constant scale over the torso, the neck bar and the tail alike, so it reads sprayed on rather than being skin that stretches with the form. The dorsal spikes are pale-outlined triangles pasted along a visible seam on the back. Only two twig-thin legs support the whole mass, meeting the belly at a hard line.
rows.fix: Replace the square-tooth grid with individually varied conical teeth of unequal length along a curved jaw line. Rebuild the head as a skull form with a snout and a jaw hinge, and flare the neck into the shoulders so the taper is continuous. Vary the scale cell size by body region and shrink it toward the limbs and tail tip so it deforms with the surface. Grow the spikes out of the back contour and delete the outline stroke. Thicken the legs and add haunch/shoulder masses; show all four.

rows.readsAs: A dachshund or a spotted hyena pup — correctly legible as a dog
rows.defect: Closest to shippable in the batch, but a razor-straight pale highlight line runs from the rump forward along the entire top of the back to the shoulder — a perfectly ruled machined edge across an otherwise soft, well-shaded animal, and it is the first thing the eye catches. The spot pattern is a uniform scatter of hard-edged dark blobs at constant size and density; it does not compress toward the flank silhouette or wrap the barrel of the ribcage, so it reads as spray applied over the top. The legs terminate in rounded stumps with no paw, ankle or toe articulation, and the front pair are barely longer than they are wide. Both ears are near-perfect dark circles.
rows.fix: Replace the straight spine highlight with a curved rim-light that follows the back contour and fades at both ends. Make the spot field perspective-aware — shrink and crowd the spots toward the silhouette edges, vary their size and softness, and let a few break over the contour. Add feet: a paw mass and a toe break at each leg end. Reshape the ears from circles into asymmetric leaf/triangle forms with a base that flows into the skull.

rows.readsAs: An okapi or young deer with a bottle brush stuck in its backside
rows.defect: The tail is a literal bottle brush — an ellipse core with straight bristles radiating uniformly around it, sitting at the rump behind a hard colour seam, and it reads as a paintbrush inserted into the animal rather than hair growing from a tail. The antlers are tan/beige on a saturated teal body, a colour with no relationship to any other pigment on the creature, and they sprout from two hard-edged sockets on the skull. The dark stripes are flat blobby bands laid over the flank at even spacing; they do not narrow or bend as they run over the ribs, so they read painted on. A straight diagonal crease marks the neck-to-shoulder join. The eye is again a cartoon white ball with a black dot, off-style from the shading.
rows.fix: Rebuild the tail as a tapered fleshy tail with directional hair strands that all sweep one way and fade at the tips, growing out of a rump mass rather than butting against it. Tint the antlers toward the body palette (pale teal/bone-teal) and blend their bases into the skull with a fur or velvet transition. Make the stripes follow the barrel: narrow them at the spine and belly, widen at mid-flank, soften the edges. Remove the neck crease and blend the neck taper into the shoulder. Restyle the eye to match the painterly shading.

rows.readsAs: A jellyfish — correctly identifiable, but a diagram of one rather than a painting
rows.defect: The bell is a geometric half-disc: a mathematically perfect circular arc closed by a DEAD-STRAIGHT horizontal bottom edge, with the tentacles simply starting at that flat line. Real medusae have a curved, ruffled margin, so this reads as a primitive rather than a body. Three flat pink PERFECT CIRCLES sit on the bell — one loose on the left flank, two straddling the rim where they act as tentacle roots, and they look like decals rather than gonads or bulbs. The tentacles are straight tapered strokes with almost no curl, all falling at similar angles, and each meets the bell at an abrupt end-cap with no root swelling. The subject also reads as flat — the bell shows one soft highlight and no sub-bell interior structure.
rows.fix: Give the bell a curved, slightly scalloped margin — no straight closing edge — and let the tentacle roots emerge from lobes in that margin. Make the tentacles curl with varied phase and length and add a swelling where each meets the bell. Replace the perfect-circle spots with soft irregular gonad masses seen through translucent tissue. Add interior structure (oral arms, a darker sub-umbrella) visible through the bell to sell translucency.

rows.readsAs: A string of grey pearls on stilts with a leaf resting on it — vaguely insectoid, no specific organism
rows.defect: The torso is an unmerged CHAIN OF SPHERES — you can count roughly five individual balls, each with its own separate specular highlight and each showing the crescent overlap line where it intersects the next. It is metaball geometry that never got blended into a single skin. A large smooth leaf-shaped plate rises off the back with a hard outline and a single straight midrib; it makes contact with the sphere chain along a clean line and reads as a leaf or a shell laid on top, not a wing or elytron growing out of the thorax. The six legs are perfectly straight constant-width sticks with one sharp bend each and no joint mass. The neck is another straight rod to a small ball head, and both the head and the tail tip emit identical bursts of straight radiating line-whiskers.
rows.fix: Union the body spheres into one continuous surface — smooth-minimum blend with a shared shading pass so there is one light source and one skin, then re-add segmentation as soft grooves rather than sphere boundaries. Root the dorsal plate into the thorax with a fleshy base and curve its midrib; taper its trailing edge. Give the legs varying thickness with swollen femur/tibia joints and slight curvature. Replace the straight whisker bursts with a small number of curved, tapered, unequal antennae, and remove the duplicate burst on the tail.

rows.readsAs: a bundle of dried wheat or a corn husk with three glowing amber lozenges laid on it — or a stylised paintbrush
rows.defect: Three glowing amber lozenges sit ON the stalk bundle as perfect rounded-rectangle capsules — flat, uniform, no attachment, no shadow onto the stalks beneath, no swelling of the tissue around them. They read as UI pills composited over the plant, not as pods, fruit or nodes belonging to it. The stalks themselves are ~14 identical constant-width ribbons that converge to a single hard point at the ground with no root flare, basal sheath or ground contact — the plant is a paintbrush stood on its tip. Morphology is byte-for-byte the same shape as flora-h2-s5, only recoloured amber instead of green.
rows.fix: Replace the three capsule primitives with organs that grow out of a specific stalk: give each an asymmetric ovoid outline with a narrow attachment neck, occlude it behind the two or three ribbons that pass in front of it, and cast a short contact shadow onto the ribbons below. At the base, splay the ribbon terminations outward into 3-5 root/sheath flares over ~30px instead of converging to a point. Then break the shared shape from s5 — vary ribbon count, curl a few tips outward, and change the overall taper.

rows.readsAs: a flowering cherry or lilac sapling — genuinely legible, just soft
rows.defect: The strongest image in the batch, but the trunk is a straight constant-width brown rod from ground to first fork — no taper, no root flare, no bark texture, and it meets the soil as a cut-off rectangle. The three flower masses are heavy gaussian-blurred cotton blobs with no petal structure, no calyx and no visible attachment: each branch tip simply disappears into a cloud, so the flowers hover rather than emerge. There are no leaves anywhere on the plant. The lower-left branch meets the trunk at a bare corner with no fillet.
rows.fix: Taper the trunk (thicker at ground, ~60% width at the fork) and splay 3-4 root buttresses into the soil ellipse. Give the flower heads an actual outline — a ring of overlapping lobed petals with a darker centre — and terminate each branch inside a small green calyx that overlaps the petal ring so the join is occluded rather than blurred. Add a fillet where each branch leaves the trunk, and hang 4-6 leaves on the branches.

rows.readsAs: a Christmas-tree icon, or a stack of dinner plates on a dowel — a clip-art logo, not a plant
rows.defect: Five perfect flat ellipses of increasing width threaded on a straight brown stick. They are unmodified geometric primitives: zero silhouette noise, zero foliage edge, no thickness, no branch supporting any of them. The stalk is a dead-straight constant-width line that visibly passes in FRONT of and BEHIND the ellipses at the same time, a hard intersection with no integration. There is no bark, no needles, no leaf detail — the whole thing is an icon, not an organism.
rows.fix: Rebuild the tiers as foliage masses, not ellipses: perturb each outline with 20-40 irregular lobes, give each tier vertical thickness (a lit top face and a shadowed underside), and drop each tier's centre slightly so it drapes. Grow a visible branch whorl out of the trunk to support each tier and let the foliage occlude the trunk between tiers. Taper and bend the trunk and flare it into the ground.

rows.readsAs: a green sea anemone or a bunch of spring onions, glowing — most viewers would call it an animal
rows.defect: The same asset as flora-h2-s2 in green: identical ribbon count, identical taper, identical single-point base, identical three glowing capsules at identical heights. The three green lozenges are again perfect rounded rectangles laid over the ribbons — flat fill, no shading, no attachment, no occlusion by the ribbons in front of them. The bundle converges to a needle point at the ground with no roots. Because of the flat mint fill and the pointed base it reads as an underwater animal, not flora.
rows.fix: Same structural fixes as s2 (attached ovoid organs with necks and contact shadows, splayed root base), plus this instance must NOT share s2's geometry — drive ribbon count, curvature and node placement from the species seed so the two hue variants are different plants. Add value range inside the green ribbons; right now several are a single flat colour.

rows.readsAs: a thorny bramble or rose cane — plausible, but too dark to be sure at a glance
rows.defect: Dangerously underexposed — the dark-olive stem is barely separable from the near-black background and half the plant disappears. The red thorns are straight-edged isoceles triangles jabbed into the stem at hard angles: each one meets the stem as a flat cut with no basal swelling, so they read as stuck-on spikes rather than growths. The small dark-red rings scattered along the stem are flat decal ovals with no relationship to the surface curvature — sprayed-on pattern. Stem is the same S-curve spline used by s7 and s9 with the same tendril nodes.
rows.fix: Raise stem value ~35% so it separates from the background. Rebuild thorns with a curved concave profile and a swollen base that blends into the stem silhouette over 6-8px instead of a straight join. Make the ring markings follow the stem's cylindrical shading (compress them toward the silhouette edges, brighten on the lit side). Vary the stem spline off the shared vine curve.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon fern or a stylised cannabis vine — clearly a plant, but clearly an illustration
rows.defect: Leaves are hard-edged flat triangles arranged in perfect radial fans of 5-7, filled with one uniform mint colour — no veins, no midrib, no value shift, no curl. Each rosette attaches at a single point on the stem with no petiole, so the fans look pinned on. Every rosette is the same fan repeated at a different rotation. The stem is the same S-curve spline and same ring-tendrils as s6 and s9, confirming decoration-swapping over a shared skeleton.
rows.fix: Give each leaflet a curved lanceolate outline with a midrib and a lit/shadow half so it turns in space; stagger leaflet lengths within a rosette instead of a symmetric fan. Add a short petiole that emerges from a thickened node on the stem. Vary rosette leaflet count and droop per node. Differentiate the stem curve from s6/s9.

rows.readsAs: a neon Christmas-tree icon or a stack of glowing lily pads on a pole
rows.defect: The teal recolour of flora-h2-s4 — same five perfect ellipses, same sizes, same straight stalk. Identical primitive problems: flat ellipses with no foliage edge or thickness, and a straight constant-width stalk drawn both in front of and behind them. Additionally the stalk has a purple bloom/glow at the top-third that is a soft vertical gradient with no source object, floating over the trunk. Nothing about the silhouette distinguishes it from s4 except hue.
rows.fix: Same rebuild as s4 (lobed foliage tiers with thickness and supporting branch whorls, curved tapering trunk, root flare). Then give the glow an emitter — a bioluminescent node, sporangium or bud that the light comes from — instead of an unattached vertical gradient, and reseed the tier count and spacing so it is not s4's silhouette.

rows.readsAs: a strand of gold beads or a brass jewellery chain with metal leaves — more ornament than organism
rows.defect: The 'leaves' are perfect ellipses filled with a smooth radial gradient and a specular highlight — they read as polished gold beans or metal eggs, not foliage: no tip, no midrib, no vein, no edge irregularity, and the machined highlight makes them look manufactured. Each ellipse butts straight into the stem with no petiole and no occlusion, and the topmost one on the left overlaps the stem awkwardly as if floating in front of it. Stem is again the shared S-curve spline with the same ring-tendrils as s6 and s7.
rows.fix: Replace the ellipse primitive with a leaf outline that has an asymmetric base and a drawn-out tip, a midrib splitting a lighter and darker half, and a slightly wavy edge; kill the circular specular in favour of a broad sheen following the midrib. Attach via a short stalk from a node so the leaf reads as growing out. Reseed the vine curve away from s6/s7.

rows.readsAs: Two lavender gumballs or a purple snowman — a candy render, not an organism
rows.defect: Two mathematically perfect purple spheres, the big one ~135px across and a smaller one overlapping it on the right, freckled with small darker dots. There is no stipe, no cap/underside distinction, no gills or pores, no substrate — the spheres just float over an elliptical drop shadow. Where the small sphere overlaps the big one you can see the small sphere's full circular outline drawn straight across the large one's shading: a hard arc seam, not a fused merge. The dots are uniform round speckles scattered at random and read as sprayed-on paint rather than skin.
rows.fix: Kill the circle primitive: build the cap from a noise-warped closed path (radial radius modulated by 2–3 octaves of fBm, ±12% radius) so the outline is lumpy. Boolean-union the two heads into ONE silhouette path before filling so no internal arc survives, and add a shared shadow-valley in the crease instead of an outline. Give it fungal anatomy — either flatten the top and cut a gilled/pored underside with a stipe rooted into a substrate patch, or convert to a puffball with a wrinkled ostiole at the apex. Replace the random dot spray with warty scale-plates whose lighting follows the same normal as the body (each wart gets a lit top edge and a shadow underside).

rows.readsAs: A naval contact mine, or a one-eyed cartoon virus
rows.defect: A perfect mauve sphere with six straight, hard-edged triangular spikes radiating from it, plus one dark circular dot dead-centre that unavoidably reads as a single EYE. The spikes are flat isoceles triangles with machined straight edges and no taper variation, each terminating abruptly at a visible straight seam where it meets the sphere — they are stuck ON, not grown OUT. The two horizontal spikes sit at exactly opposing angles, and the whole spike set is close to radially even, which reads as CAD, not growth. Body is featureless: no cap, no stipe, no gills, no texture at all.
rows.fix: Remove the centre dot entirely (it is a cyclops eye on a fungus). Rebuild spikes as curved, tapering spines drawn as a continuation of the body outline — extend the cap's boundary path outward into each spine so the silhouette is one continuous stroke, add a slight S-curve and per-spine length/angle jitter (±30%), and thicken the base into a fleshy swelling that shades continuously into the cap. Warp the sphere into an irregular fruiting body and add fungal read: gilled or pored underside plus a stipe meeting a substrate.

rows.readsAs: Two teal beanbag chairs, or a pair of rubber bath toys
rows.defect: Two teal blobs, large and small, each with a bright cyan outline stroke running all the way round the silhouette — a uniform vector-sticker keyline, not a lit edge. The large body's outline is visibly faceted: I can count roughly six straight segments with rounded corners, so it reads as a rounded polygon. Interior is a single soft radial dark smudge with no flesh, fibre or gill texture. Tiny black bristles fringe the underside rim; they are all the same length and stop dead at the rim in a hard line, reading as glued-on eyelashes. There is no stipe on either body — the caps rest directly on the ground.
rows.fix: Drop the constant-width keyline; replace with a rim-light that varies with the light direction (bright top-left, fading to nothing bottom-right). Subdivide and noise-displace the cap outline so no straight facet survives. Add a real stipe growing out of the cap's underside — same fill, no seam, thickening where it joins. Turn the bristles into radiating gill plates or a hymenial fringe whose bases blend into the cap's underside shadow, with varying length and slight curvature, and let a few overlap the silhouette so they read as part of the body.

rows.readsAs: A banyan or dragon tree in silhouette
rows.defect: This is a TREE, not a fungus. Pale multi-trunk stems fan up and out into a dense dome of thin dichotomous twigs with visible terminal branchlets — the exact silhouette of a banyan or a dragon-blood tree. No cap, no stipe/cap distinction, no gills, no pores, nothing fungal anywhere in the picture. It is also a near-duplicate of fungi-h0-s2 in this same batch: same trunk count, same canopy dome, same proportions, differing only in tint and a couple of trunk angles — two rolls of the same generator with almost no variation.
rows.fix: Route fungi away from the tree/canopy branch generator entirely. If a branching fungal form is wanted, use a coral/Ramaria-style model: thick fleshy coralloid branches with blunt rounded tips (no fine twigs, no terminal fans), branching only 3–4 levels, all emerging from one common fleshy base — and no canopy dome fill. Otherwise give this seed a cap-and-stipe body. Separately, widen the per-seed variation so s19 and s2 do not land on the same silhouette.

rows.readsAs: A backlit tree — the same tree as s19
rows.defect: Same defect as s19 and effectively the same picture: a pale branching tree, ~8 trunks fanning into a solid dome canopy of fine twigs. Zero fungal anatomy. The canopy top is a smooth, near-perfect elliptical arc — a geometric dome the twigs are drawn inside rather than a mass the twigs create; you can see the twig tips get clipped flat against that arc on the upper-left and upper-right shoulders. Near-identical to fungi-h0-s19 in the same batch.
rows.fix: Same routing fix as s19 — fungi must not use the tree/canopy generator. If kept as a branching organism, remove the ellipse clip and let the canopy boundary emerge from where the branch tips actually land (union of tip discs with noise), so no clean arc appears. Then rebuild as a coralloid fungus: fleshy blunt-tipped branches from a single basal mass, no fine twig fans.

rows.readsAs: A bunch of grey grapes or soap bubbles hanging from a stick
rows.defect: A flat brown curved lozenge (the 'branch') spans the frame with a plain unshaded brown fill and no bark texture, and a cluster of five or six translucent grey-blue perfect spheres hangs below it. Each sphere is a true circle with a small white specular ellipse — glass-marble shading. The spheres' full circular outlines are visible through each other where they overlap, so the cluster reads as stacked soap bubbles, never as one fused mass. Critically the cluster does not attach to the branch: it overlaps the branch's lower edge with no stalk, no join, no shared shadow. The whole image is also badly underlit — the subject is barely brighter than the background.
rows.fix: Union the sphere cluster into a single outline before filling (kill the internal circle arcs) and warp each lobe off-circle so no perfect radius remains. Grow an actual attachment: a short tapering stalk or a broadening holdfast that starts inside the branch silhouette and swells into the cluster, plus contact-occlusion shading on the branch where the mass presses into it. Give the branch bark — longitudinal fibre strokes, an irregular outline, and a lit top / shadowed underside. Raise the body value ~30% so the subject separates from the background.

rows.readsAs: An orange, a peach, or a small terracotta planet
rows.defect: A single perfect orange sphere, ~120px diameter, with random small brown freckles and a thin white crescent rim on the right side. That crescent is a hard-edged constant-width arc that terminates abruptly top and bottom — a stroke, not a light. There is no fungal feature of any kind: no cap, no stipe, no gills, no pores, no substrate. It floats above a plain ellipse shadow. Radial gradient plus freckles is decoration applied to a geometric primitive.
rows.fix: Replace the circle with a noise-warped puffball path (irregular radius, slightly flattened base, a wrinkled crease where it meets the ground). Add fungal identity: an apical ostiole/pore with radial wrinkles, or convert to a cap with a visible gilled underside and a stipe rooted into a mycelial mat. Make the rim light wrap and fade with the surface normal instead of being a drawn arc. Replace the freckle spray with raised warts that cast their own micro-shadows and get denser toward the apex.

rows.readsAs: A bunch of yellow grapes, or three soap bubbles stuck under a twig
rows.defect: Identical construction to fungi-h0-s3 with the hue swapped to yellow: flat brown lozenge branch, three translucent yellow spheres clustered below it. Each lobe is a perfect circle, and their complete circular outlines cross visibly through one another — I can trace three full circles inside the mass, so it reads as stacked bubbles rather than one body. The cluster again does not attach to the branch; it simply overlaps it, with a gap of dark background visible between the topmost lobe and the branch on the left. Branch is a featureless tapered capsule with no bark and no shading.
rows.fix: Same as s3, plus break the duplication: union the lobes into one silhouette, deform each off-circle, and vary lobe count/scale per seed so s3 and s5 do not read as one asset recoloured. Attach with a real stalk emerging from within the branch and add contact shadow. Texture the branch (irregular outline, fibre strokes, lit/shadow sides). Damp the glassy specular highlights — fungal flesh is matte-waxy, not glass.

rows.readsAs: a grey asteroid or a rock/boulder — the same read as the space-rock thumbnails, not an organism
rows.defect: Not a fungus at all — a single grey-blue amorphous lump, wide dome on a flat bottom edge, filling the middle of the frame. Zero fungal anatomy: no stipe, no cap margin, no gills/pores, no volva, no mycelium, no substrate. The only 'detail' is a scatter of small pale dots, and a large number of those dots sit OUTSIDE the silhouette in the empty background (a halo of stray specks across the whole upper-left/right), which is an off-body artifact. Surface is a single flat vertical gradient with a soft interior blush — no shading that describes a form, so it reads as a flat cutout. There is no shadow or ground contact.
rows.fix: This seed is rendering the generic 'blob' fallback; route fungi-h0 to the actual fungal builder. It needs the two-part cap+stipe construction the s12/s14 seeds use (cap growing out of a tapering stipe with a flared, curved margin — not a flat base line), or a bracket/shelf form fanning off an implied trunk. Clip the spore/speck scatter to the body mask so no dot paints outside the silhouette, and add a contact shadow.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon virus particle next to a striped barrel/wheel — closest guess a microbe or a coral polyp, nobody would say mushroom
rows.defect: Two hard-edged teal objects floating side by side on a brown gradient band: a lumpy sphere studded with small triangular spikes, and a smaller disc whose face is filled with perfectly straight, evenly spaced horizontal lines. Those 'gills' are ruler-straight parallel strokes on a flat facing disc — machined, drafted geometry, not organic lamellae (real gills radiate from a stipe and curve with the cap dome). The two objects have no connection to each other or to any substrate — the disc's rim is stuck ON as a spiked collar with a visible hard edge where it meets the striped face. The spikes are identical repeated triangles pasted on the sphere surface rather than growing from it. Both bodies are flat-filled single-hue with almost no form shading. The background band ends in a hard horizontal seam across the frame.
rows.fix: Kill the straight-line gill hatching entirely: draw lamellae as radial curves converging on a stipe, foreshortened by the cap tilt, with varied spacing and short/long alternation. Replace the two free-floating primitives with one connected fruiting body (cap continuous into stipe, no seam). Vary the spike geometry per-instance and grow them from the surface with a shared base tone instead of pasting uniform triangles. Remove the hard horizontal background seam.

rows.readsAs: nothing — an empty dark card with dust on it
rows.defect: Effectively an empty frame. All that is present is a very faint dark navy oval haze in the centre and roughly a dozen barely-visible grey dots, most of which are darker than the intended body. There is no silhouette, no cap, no stipe, no readable edge anywhere — the organism is either not being drawn or is drawn at near-zero contrast against the near-black background. As a portrait card this is unshippable at any zoom.
rows.fix: Find why this seed produces no body — either the palette resolved to a value within a few units of the background or the form pass is being skipped. Enforce a minimum luminance contrast between body fill and the card background (clamp the value channel), and add a rim/backlight pass so every fungus reads as a shape even on the darkest palettes.

rows.readsAs: a purple rock or a slime blob; and within this batch it is indistinguishable from fungi-h0-s0 apart from colour
rows.defect: A palette-swapped clone of fungi-h0-s0: the exact same wide dome-on-flat-bottom lump, same proportions, same speckle scatter, only recoloured purple. No fungal anatomy whatsoever — no stipe, no cap margin, no gills, no mycelium. The speck field again bleeds well outside the silhouette into the empty background on all sides (off-body artifact). Flat gradient fill with no form shading and no ground contact.
rows.fix: Same as s0 — this seed is hitting the blob fallback rather than the fungal builder. Build a genuine fruiting body (cap continuous with stipe, curved flaring margin, visible hymenium under the cap) and make s0 and s11 differ in morphology, not just hue. Mask the spore scatter to the body.

rows.readsAs: a mushroom — specifically a shaggy/conical ink cap, so the family read is correct; it just reads as a vector icon of one rather than a painted organism
rows.defect: This one is actually legible as a mushroom, but the construction gives it away. (1) The cap meets the stipe on a dead-straight horizontal line — a hard seam where the cap bottom is simply cut off and the stipe is pasted underneath; nothing tucks under or flares. (2) The stipe is a straight-sided trapezoid, two perfectly straight ruled edges, no taper curve, no basal bulb, no flare into the ground. (3) The cap pattern is a repeating diamond/lattice tile laid flat across the cap with no perspective wrap, no scale falloff toward the margin and no interruption at the silhouette edge — it reads as wallpaper sprayed on, not the cap's own scaly cuticle. (4) The ground shadow is a perfect hard-edged ellipse detached from the stipe base. (5) No gills or margin visible at all under the cap.
rows.fix: Curve the cap's lower margin so it overhangs and the stipe disappears into it (draw the stipe first, then the cap over it with a soft dark occlusion band at the join). Give the stipe a subtly curved profile with a widened, root-flared base. Project the cap pattern along the cap's surface normals so the diamonds compress and darken toward the margin, and break the tiling with per-instance jitter. Soften the shadow to a diffuse gradient anchored at the stipe base.

rows.readsAs: a golf ball, a pearl, or an egg — a ball, not an organism
rows.defect: A mathematically perfect white circle with a smooth radial gradient, a handful of small grey dots sprinkled across it, and a hard-edged perfect ellipse of shadow beneath it. The silhouette is a pure geometric primitive with zero contour variation — no lobing, no wrinkling, no basal attachment, no substrate contact (the sphere floats clear of its own shadow). The grey dots are uniform flat circles sitting on top of the surface rather than pits or warts in it. A puffball is a defensible fungal read, but a puffball has a rooted, gathered base and a warted or leathery skin; this has neither.
rows.fix: Break the circle: perturb the outline with low-frequency noise so it is a swollen irregular ball, gather and pinch the bottom into a rooted base that touches the shadow, and replace the dot sprinkle with warts that have their own highlight and cast shading so they read as skin texture. Add a hint of substrate/mycelium at the base and soften the shadow ellipse.

rows.readsAs: a mushroom, morel-ish — correct family, but a flat illustrated icon of one; and within the batch it is the same picture as fungi-h0-s12 in a different colour
rows.defect: Structurally the identical asset to fungi-h0-s12 recoloured orange/tan — same conical cap, same stipe, same diamond lattice, same ellipse shadow — so the batch contains a palette swap rather than two species. All of s12's construction faults are present and MORE visible here because of the higher contrast: the cap bottom is a dead-straight horizontal cut with the cream stipe pasted under it (hard seam), the stipe is a straight-ruled trapezoid with no basal flare, and the diamond tile runs across the cap at constant scale with no perspective wrap and no interruption at the margin — unmistakably a sprayed-on pattern. The cap's lower-left/right corners come to sharp points where the tile grid meets the outline.
rows.fix: Same structural fixes as s12 (overhanging curved cap margin occluding the stipe, curved stipe with flared base, normal-projected and margin-compressed cap texture, soft anchored shadow), plus differentiate this seed from s12 by morphology — cap profile, margin shape, stipe thickness — not by hue alone.

rows.readsAs: a blue cauliflower or a virus next to a striped drum/barrel; and within the batch it is the same picture as fungi-h0-s1 recoloured
rows.defect: A blue recolour of fungi-h0-s1 — identical geometry, identical layout, only the hue changed. Two disconnected hard-edged objects on a brown gradient band: a lumpy spiked ball and a disc filled with perfectly straight, evenly spaced horizontal lines. The striped disc is the worst offender in the batch — ruler-straight parallel strokes across a flat facing disc, with the spiked rim stuck on as a separate collar with a visible hard boundary against the striped face. The triangular spikes are the same repeated stamp pasted onto both bodies. Flat single-hue fills with no form shading, and the background band terminates in a hard horizontal seam.
rows.fix: Same as s1 — replace the straight-line hatching with radial, curved, foreshortened lamellae converging on a stipe; merge the two floating primitives into one connected fruiting body with no seam at the cap/stipe join; jitter the spike stamps and blend their bases into the surface; remove the hard background seam. Then give s15 a different morphology from s1 rather than a different hue.

rows.readsAs: a handful of matchsticks or cotton swabs stuck upright in a mud patty
rows.defect: Six ruler-straight tan stalks of constant width, each capped by a perfect tilted ellipse, jammed into a flat perfect-ellipse brown pad. Every element is a naked geometric primitive: the caps are true ellipses with no gill line, no underside, no cap/stem junction; the stalks are 3-4px straight segments that terminate at a hard point on the pad with zero basal flare or mycelium — a visible stuck-in seam on all six. The tan speckles on the caps are uniform dots sprayed over the ellipse rather than following its curve. The brown pad itself is a drawn disc with a hard rim and a row of tiny vertical tick marks on its left half that belong to nothing.
rows.fix: Kill the ellipse caps — build each cap as a swept profile (slight asymmetric dome, thickened lower margin, a visible underside/gill shadow where it overhangs). Curve and taper the stalks (bezier with 2-4% width taper, thicker at the base) and flare each one into the substrate with a small mycelial foot so there is no point-contact. Replace the elliptical ground pad with an irregular, feathered-edge substrate blob and drop the orphan tick marks. Vary cap size/tilt/maturity per stalk instead of one repeated ellipse.

rows.readsAs: two moon jellyfish
rows.defect: Two near-perfect semicircular salmon domes with a thin dark arc drawn across the top of each, and a curtain of long, straight, constant-width vertical tendrils hanging from the underside. This is a jellyfish, not a fungus — the domes are bells and the tendrils are oral arms. The dark arc across the crest is a hard graphic seam, not shading. The tendrils all hang perfectly vertical with no taper, no curl, no length logic, and several visibly pass straight through the brown substrate blob instead of stopping at it. Nothing anchors the two domes to the ground: there is no stalk, so both bells float over the substrate.
rows.fix: If this is meant to be a veiled/skirted fungus, it needs a stipe — grow a tapered stalk out of the substrate up into the cap centre and let the cap silhouette deform where it meets it. Break the semicircle: asymmetric cap, uneven margin, a curled or torn edge. Replace the straight tendril curtain with a partial veil / gill fringe that varies in length, curves inward under the cap, and terminates well above the ground. Delete the dark crest arc or convert it into an actual lighting gradient.

rows.readsAs: a banyan grove or a head of cauliflower
rows.defect: Structurally the best render in the batch — the fine branching genuinely grows out of the trunks with continuous taper and no seams. But the read is wrong: eight near-parallel vertical trunks rising from one point and fanning into a canopy is a banyan grove, not a fungus. The canopy boundary is a single unnaturally smooth, near-symmetric elliptical arc with a uniform-density interior, so the twig mass looks like a fill inside a drawn dome rather than a mass of twig tips. The bottom edge of the canopy is a clean concave sweep that no branching system would produce.
rows.fix: Break the dome: let clumps of branch tips overshoot and undershoot the envelope so the silhouette is lumpy and asymmetric, and vary twig density (denser at branch-tip clusters, sparse between). Shorten and thicken the trunk bundle so it reads as a fused fungal base rather than tree trunks, and fuse the lower trunks into one another with a shared flaring foot. Add a hint of fruiting texture (pored/coral surface) on the outer tips to move it away from foliage.

rows.readsAs: a clump of teal grass or an aloe plant
rows.defect: A clump of ten flat teal lens-shaped blades with sharp points — this is grass or an agave/aloe rosette, not a fungus. Each blade is the same mirrored 2D primitive with a single hard specular ridge stroke down its centre that is drawn on top rather than being the surface curving. Every blade is chopped off by the same straight horizontal line at the bottom, a flat butt-cut with no root flare, no widening, and no substrate — the hardest possible seam. The blades are all crescent variants of one shape at different rotations.
rows.fix: This asset is answering the wrong prompt — a fungus does not have leaf blades. Route it to a fungal form (clustered club/coral fungus, bracket, cup). If the tall-blade form is kept, it must taper INTO a shared fleshy base that swells at the ground line, each blade needs a distinct outline rather than one mirrored primitive, and the centre highlight must be replaced by a gradient that follows the blade's twist.

rows.readsAs: a clip-art mushroom with a fabric swatch on the cap
rows.defect: Correctly reads as a mushroom but is an icon, not an organism. The cap is a perfectly symmetric bullet/paraboloid, and it meets the cream stalk along a dead-straight horizontal line — a hard seam with no gills, no annulus, no overhang, no shadow where the cap sits down onto the stem. The cap's diamond-lattice pattern is a flat uniform tile: the diamonds are the same size and orientation at the centre and at the silhouette edge, so it does not wrap the volume at all — it is wallpaper laid over a shape. The stalk is a straight-sided trapezoid with a flat bottom cut and no basal bulb. Shadow is a perfect black ellipse with a hard edge.
rows.fix: Make the cap overhang the stalk and cast contact shading into the junction, with a visible gill/underside band and a torn margin so the cap-stalk boundary is a curve, not a line. Project the diamond texture onto the dome so the cells compress and shear toward the silhouette, and let it fade/stretch near the margin. Give the stalk a slight S-curve, an irregular width profile and a swollen base sinking into the ground. Soften and feather the drop shadow.

rows.readsAs: a virus particle from a textbook diagram, or a caltrop
rows.defect: A perfect cream circle with a radial gradient, eight straight flat triangular spikes radiating from behind it, and one small grey dot floating at the centre. Every spike is a hard-edged isoceles triangle drawn BEHIND the sphere — they emerge at the exact circle edge with no basal swelling, no shading continuity and no deformation of the body, so all eight are visibly stuck on. The body is a mathematically perfect circle with a plain radial gradient and zero surface texture. The centre dot has no context and looks like a stray pixel or an eye. There is nothing fungal here: no stalk, no substrate contact, no fruiting texture.
rows.fix: Spikes must grow out: widen each base into the body wall, shade them continuously with the body, curve/taper them and bulge the silhouette where each one attaches. Break the circle into an irregular lobed sac. Add real surface (pores, wrinkles, a wall texture) instead of a smooth radial gradient. Remove or motivate the centre dot (make it an ostiole with a raised, shaded collar if a puffball pore is intended). Anchor it to the ground with a base or short stipe.

rows.readsAs: two ceramic bowls, or a halved coconut shell
rows.defect: Two smooth off-white bowls, one large one small, with a soft grey gradient inside. They read as manufactured ceramic — the rims are clean rounded-polygon curves, the wall thickness is a constant drawn line, and the interior is one featureless gradient blob with no gill, no spore mass, no depth cue. The only 'organic' element is a fringe of short black bristles that appears ONLY along the lower-left arc of each bowl, a row of identical tick marks laid over the outer wall as a decal rather than hairs emerging from the surface. Neither bowl touches ground or has any stalk or attachment; the small one floats with no shadow of its own.
rows.fix: Wrap the bristles all the way around the visible outer wall, vary their length and angle, and root each one with a slight surface bump so they read as growing out. Give the cup interior real content: a spore mass, peridioles, or a shaded floor with an occluded far rim so the cavity has depth. Make the rim irregular and torn, vary wall thickness, and attach both cups to a shared substrate mat with a tapered foot. Add contact shadow under the small cup.

rows.readsAs: a green coronavirus icon or a sea urchin
rows.defect: Identical to fungi-h1-s1 in the same batch with only a hue change (green instead of cream) and slightly longer spikes — same perfect circle, same eight flat straight triangles emerging from behind the body, same lone centre dot. Two of eight slots in this batch are the same asset recoloured. The spike/body junction is the same stuck-on seam: hard triangle edges meeting the circle silhouette with no basal blend and no bulge in the body. Smooth radial gradient, no surface texture, no stalk, no ground attachment; the drop shadow is a perfect hard-edged ellipse sitting far below the body.
rows.fix: Same structural fix as h1-s1 (spikes fused and shaded into a lobed, textured body, ostiole given a raised collar, base anchored to substrate) PLUS the generator must diverge these two seeds — differ the spike count, spike curvature, body lobing and surface treatment, not just the palette, or the spiked-sphere template will keep restating itself across the fungi set.

rows.readsAs: A blue hockey puck or drum next to a blue spiked ball — a sea urchin toy, not a fungus
rows.defect: Two separate blue objects with no connection to each other or to any substrate. The right-hand one is a hard geometric primitive: a drum/cylinder in three-quarter view whose face is a mathematically perfect ellipse filled with ~14 straight, evenly-spaced black horizontal stripes running edge to edge. The stripes are drawn flat across the ellipse and do not radiate from a centre, do not converge at the rim, and do not follow the disc's curvature — they are a stripe fill clipped to an oval, not gills. Its perimeter also carries a ring of identical small triangular spikes stuck on around the outside edge with visible seams. The left form is a lumpy ball with the same triangular spikes pinned to its outline and small dark chevron flecks sprayed on top of the gradient rather than sitting in the skin.
rows.fix: Kill the ellipse-plus-parallel-stripes gill face entirely. If a gill surface must show, build it as radial lamellae converging on an off-centre stipe attachment, each with its own thickness taper and shadow, and let the outer ones foreshorten into the rim rather than terminating on a clean elliptical boundary. Replace the perimeter spike ring with warts that emerge from the cap silhouette by displacing the outline itself (perturb the cap path) instead of drawing separate triangles over it. Join the two bodies at a shared base or mycelial mat so they read as one clump.

rows.readsAs: A clump of purple ornamental grass or a small aloe
rows.defect: Nine purple blade shapes standing vertically. This is grass or an aloe, not a fungus — there is no cap, no stipe/cap distinction, no gill or pore surface, nothing fungal in the anatomy. Every blade is a flat 2D lens shape with a single straight highlight stripe down its middle, all lit identically, all pointing the same direction with no overlap depth. The bases are all sheared off on one common horizontal line at the same y-coordinate and sit on a flat dark ellipse — the whole cluster looks cut off at a table edge rather than emerging from ground.
rows.fix: This asset needs a different form generator, not a tweak. Route h1 morphology to a cap-bearing or coral/club-fungus builder. If a club-fungus (Clavaria) look is intended, the fingers must be round in section with a swollen blunt tip, splayed at differing angles, varying in length and thickness, and must fuse into a common thickened base that swells out of the substrate — no shared flat cut line, no single central highlight stripe on each.

rows.readsAs: A dark argyle-patterned lampshade on a wooden peg
rows.defect: The cap silhouette is a believable ink-cap bullet, but the surface is covered by a perfectly regular repeating diamond/argyle lattice tile. The lattice keeps identical cell size and identical orientation from the centre of the cap all the way to the outer edge, with no compression toward the silhouette and no wrap around the dome — it is wallpaper pasted over a shape. The stipe is a straight-edged pale trapezoid, flat-shaded with no volume, and it meets the cap at an abrupt horizontal cut with a hard value jump from cream to near-black and no flare, no annulus, no shadow pocket — a visible seam where stalk meets cap. Overall value is also so dark the cap is nearly indistinguishable from the background.
rows.fix: Project the cap texture along the dome's UV so cells compress and skew toward the rim, and randomise cell size/rotation per instance so it stops reading as a tiled pattern; better still, replace the diamond lattice with shaggy longitudinal fibrils that split and lift at the cap margin. Give the stipe a round cross-section (a rim-light down one side, core shadow down the other), taper it and swell the base, and blend the junction with a flared skirt plus a cast shadow under the cap so the two are one continuous body. Lift the cap's base value by roughly 20 percent so it separates from the background.

rows.readsAs: A grey moon or a stone marble floating in space
rows.defect: A single near-perfect grey circle with a smooth centre-lit gradient, hovering above a detached elliptical shadow it never touches. Nothing about it is fungal — no rhizomorphs, no substrate contact, no ostiole, no texture beyond a scatter of small dark dots sprayed randomly over the gradient with no scale falloff toward the limb. A thin white crescent stroke sits on the upper-right edge, stopping abruptly at both ends; it reads as a stray leftover stroke rather than a rim light, because the light on the body comes from the upper LEFT and this highlight is on the opposite side.
rows.fix: Break the circle — puffballs are never round; perturb the outline with a few low-frequency lumps and flatten the base where it presses onto the ground. Sit it ON the substrate: overlap the shadow, add a contact-darkening crease and a few mycelial threads escaping into the surrounding surface. Push the dot texture into the surface with the dots foreshortening and crowding toward the limb. Delete the stray white crescent, or if a rim light is wanted move it to the light-facing upper-left and let it fade out at both ends instead of terminating hard.

rows.readsAs: Two golden ceramic bowls with a brush fringe glued to the underside — a cup fungus on a generous reading
rows.defect: The best of this batch — the two amber cups have believable irregular rims and a real dark interior hollow. But the fringe of hairs is unmistakably stuck on: an evenly-spaced row of identical short dark strokes all the same length, all hanging straight down, all starting exactly on the outer silhouette line rather than emerging from the cup wall, and they appear only along the lower arc and stop dead where the rim turns. The rim itself is traced with a bright uniform-width outline stroke that reads as ink, not as a lit edge. The small cup is a near-exact scaled copy of the large one — same lobed outline rhythm, same fringe, same interior gradient — which makes the pair read as one asset duplicated. Both hover over a soft smear shadow with no ground contact.
rows.fix: Vary the fringe: randomise hair length by two to three times, splay their angles, curl the tips, let some cross in front of the cup body so they clearly originate on the outer wall rather than on the outline, and carry a thinner fringe around the whole rim instead of only the bottom arc. Replace the uniform rim stroke with a varying-width highlight that thins to nothing where the rim turns away. Re-roll the small cup's outline seed and tilt it so it is a sibling, not a copy. Add a contact shadow and a stub of attachment where each cup meets the substrate.

rows.readsAs: Two moon jellyfish drifting over a plank
rows.defect: Reads as two jellyfish. Both caps are smooth half-dome bells with a dark blue-grey band along the top edge exactly where a jelly's bell margin sits, and from under each hangs a curtain of long straight amber threads. The threads are the giveaway: they are near-parallel, nearly all vertical, mostly uniform width, several times longer than the cap is deep, and they hang free in space rather than attaching to anything — that is a tentacle skirt, not gills and not a stipe. They begin at a clean horizontal line under the bell with no attachment geometry. Neither body has a stipe at all. Underneath floats a detached dark brown slab with a rounded-rectangle silhouette and a straight horizontal grain line through it, which reads as a plank rather than a log or ground, and neither cap touches it.
rows.fix: Give each cap a real stipe rising from the substrate and put the cap ON it — the hanging elements must be gills or teeth that are short (a small fraction of cap depth), that fan radially from the stipe outward, that foreshorten toward the cap edge, and that terminate at the cap margin rather than dangling past it. If a toothed Hericium look is intended, make the teeth taper to points and shorten toward the margin. Remove the dark bell-margin band. Replace the floating plank with a substrate the fruiting bodies visibly emerge from: irregular bark silhouette, contact shadow, mycelium at the junction.

rows.readsAs: A cartoon virus particle or a one-eyed spiky ball monster
rows.defect: A perfect salmon-pink circle with a smooth radial gradient, seven long straight triangular spikes radiating from it, and one dark dot placed almost exactly at the centre. The dot reads immediately as a single eye, which turns the whole thing into a cartoon creature. The spikes are flat isoceles triangles pinned over the circle's outline with hard straight edges and no taper curve, no thickness variation, no shading of their own, and no flare where they meet the body — every one is a visible stuck-on seam. The body is also tiny in frame, occupying maybe a fifth of the canvas, and floats above a large detached ellipse shadow.
rows.fix: Remove the central dot entirely, or if an ostiole is intended shift it off-centre, sink it with a dark inner ring and a lit lower lip so it reads as an opening rather than a pupil. Rebuild the spikes as curved spines that grow out of the body: widen their base into the silhouette so the outline itself bulges outward at each spine, taper along a curve, vary length and angle, and light them with the same key as the body. Break the circle into an irregular fruiting body. Scale the organism up to fill roughly 60 to 70 percent of the frame like the other cards, and put it in contact with its shadow.

rows.readsAs: A grey rock or a chunk of ice with snow falling around it
rows.defect: A flat grey-blue polygon with about eight straight machined facet edges meeting at sharp corners — the top-left, top-right and lower-right boundaries are all dead-straight line segments. There is essentially no internal form: one soft light patch in the middle and otherwise an even fill, so the shape has no volume and reads as a cut-out. Over it and spilling well outside the silhouette floats a cloud of soft white dots of varying blur, which sit in front of everything as a particle overlay rather than belonging to any surface. No cap, no stipe, no pore surface, no substrate, no organism of any kind.
rows.fix: Replace the straight-edged polygon with an organic outline — no segment longer than a small fraction of the perimeter should be straight, and corners must be rounded into lobes. Give it actual form modelling: a core shadow, a terminator, a reflected bounce along the lower edge. Decide what this organism is (a bracket shelf, a crust, a puffball) and build the corresponding anatomy — for a bracket, a concentric-zoned upper surface, a thickened attachment where it grips wood, and a pale pore layer along the underside. Confine the spore glints to the body and the immediate air above it so they no longer form a halo larger than the creature.

rows.readsAs: a cartoon cat's head and tail glued to a cloud of purple soap bubbles standing on eight drinking straws — not any organism
rows.defect: The torso is not a body — it is five or six overlapping PERFECT CIRCLES, each with its own rim highlight and its own visible outline arc against the next, so the back reads as a cartoon cloud / bunch of grapes. The dorsal fin is a leaf-shaped lens with a hard stroke outline and a central rib, laid flat on top of the circles with a clean seam across their crowns — nothing grows out of anything. Eight legs, all identical dead-straight tapered pipes, insert into the circle outlines at hard oval seams, and several sprout from the gap BETWEEN two circles rather than from a hip. The tail is a thin tube with a separate ball threaded on it and a flat machined chevron/arrow flag at the tip. The neck is a smooth tube butted against the front circle with a visible edge, and the whiskers are four ruler-straight rays.
rows.fix: Replace the circle-chain torso with a single spine-driven silhouette (one tapering outline sampled along the vertebral curve, lumps as low-frequency perturbation of that outline, never as discrete stamped discs). Kill all per-blob rim strokes. Root each leg in a shoulder/hip mass that swells out of the trunk contour and blend the top 20% of each limb into the body before the limb gradient starts. The dorsal fin needs a membrane base that widens into the back over ~15px rather than an outlined lens. Drop the arrow-flag tail tip and the mid-tail ball for a continuous taper.

rows.readsAs: a golden camel-llama with a fairy-light string draped over it — and a glowing ghost standing behind it
rows.defect: There is a large grey-white luminous smear sitting BEHIND and BELOW the belly, spilling out past the silhouette into the background between the mid legs — an off-body artifact, and two of the white spots sit inside it, off the animal entirely. A dead-straight horizontal line runs the full length of the back, which is where six identical rounded-thumb dorsal plates butt onto the topline: they are a row of repeated stamps, not growths. The white bioluminescent dots are perfect circles with uniform bloom, scattered without regard for the body's curvature — sprayed on. The neck is a separate lighter capsule overlapping the shoulder with a fully visible outline, and a hard-edged dewlap slab hangs under the jaw as its own shape.
rows.fix: Clip every glow/spot pass to the body mask (the grey blob is a light sprite drawn before or outside the silhouette clip — move it inside). Give the dorsal plates a fillet at the base so each merges into the back over several pixels, vary their height/spacing/lean, and delete the straight topline seam. Project the spots onto the surface normal so they compress toward the silhouette edge and vary their radius. Merge the neck into the shoulder with a shared contour instead of an overlaid capsule; remove the dewlap slab or make it a bulge of the same skin.

rows.readsAs: a pink okapi/deer in a knitted argyle sweater
rows.defect: The markings are a rectangular LATTICE — roughly fourteen evenly spaced columns by four evenly spaced rows of identical blurred dark ovals, spanning flank and haunch at machine-uniform pitch. It reads as printed gingham, not as this creature's own coat; it does not follow a single muscle, does not break at the leg, and does not compress toward the silhouette edge. The neck is a distinct paler capsule laid OVER the shoulder with a bright outline where the two overlap — a clear seam. At the tail base the silhouette has a small square bracket-shaped step where the tail shape was pasted onto the rump. Six legs at three stations; the mid pair emerges from flat belly with no hip.
rows.fix: Drive the pattern from a body-space UV field (stripes that bend along the spine, split at the shoulder and hip, taper to nothing at the extremities) with per-mark jitter in size, angle and spacing — never a regular row/column grid. Blend the neck into the chest: same fill, shared contour, no overlap outline. Rebuild the tail as a continuation of the sacral taper so no bracket step appears in the silhouette. Give each leg station a hip/shoulder swelling in the trunk outline.

rows.readsAs: a coiled green snake — correct on first read
rows.defect: Reads correctly and cleanly as a snake — the ventral scute banding follows the body, the head grows out of the neck with no seam, the slit pupil is right. Two things keep it from clean: the outer coil is a mathematically perfect circle (constant radius, constant thickness for most of its run), which reads as a machined torus rather than a resting coil; and the forked tongue is two dead-straight red lines of constant width meeting at a hard V, with no taper and no curve.
rows.fix: Perturb the coil radius by a few percent along its length and let the body thicken slightly at the mid-coil and taper faster into the tail so the ring is asymmetric. Add a small out-of-plane offset where the inner loop crosses so the overlap reads as depth. Redraw the tongue as a tapering curve that thins to a point at each fork tip, with a slight droop.

rows.readsAs: a striped giraffe-donkey with a stegosaurus plate strip and a bottle brush taped to its rear — and it is the same animal as s13 in a different coat
rows.defect: Five identical rounded-thumb dorsal plates sit in a row on the back, all the same height and spacing, and a dead-straight horizontal line runs the entire length of the back where they meet it — a hard seam and repeated primitives. The tail is a whisk: a stubby cone with a fan of straight, untapered bristle strokes radiating from it at even angles, and a white blob where the cone meets the rump. The stripes are hard-edged bands of near-uniform width; on the legs they become horizontal rings that do not line up with the body bands. Both ears are near-perfect ellipses with a smaller ellipse inset. The whole silhouette, dorsal plate row, brush tail and palette duplicate fauna-h1-s13 in this same batch.
rows.fix: Fillet the plate bases into the back and randomize height/lean/spacing; remove the straight topline seam. Rebuild the tail as hair clumps that taper, curve and vary in length, emerging from a rump that narrows into the tail rather than from a butted cone; delete the white junction blob. Soften stripe edges and make leg stripes descend from the body bands. Since s13 shares the skeleton, push at least one of them onto a different proportion/limb plan so the batch does not read as recolors.

rows.readsAs: an umbrella or a dark mushroom cap seen through a window frame; only on a second look, a jellyfish
rows.defect: Three ruler-straight vertical lines and one ruler-straight horizontal line run edge to edge across the bell, making it look like it is behind a window pane. They are perfectly straight — they do not bow with the dome's curvature at all — so they read as a rendering artifact or a UV/tile grid leaking through, not as radial canals. The bell is a half-ellipse clipped flat along the bottom by a straight chord. Three flat, opaque, perfect light-blue circles float at the bell margin. The tentacles are straight tapered slivers whose tops are cut off square against the bell's underside — a hard butt joint, nothing emerging. The whole thing is also near-black against a near-black ground.
rows.fix: Find and remove the straight-line pass — if those are meant to be radial canals they must be arcs that converge on the manubrium and fade before the rim. Give the bell an organic rim: scalloped, thicker at the margin, with the underside vaulting rather than a flat chord. Replace the flat circles with soft gonad/ocellus blobs that pick up the bell's shading. Grow each tentacle from a widened root that shares the bell's fill for its first several pixels, and give each an independent curve. Lift overall value at least two stops off the background.

rows.readsAs: a purple dachshund-otter sausage; closest neighbour in the batch is s14, which shares the same head and neck-capsule construction
rows.defect: The silhouette is a capsule — one long fat sausage with rounded ends and no waist, no ribcage, no rump, and no tail at all; it just stops bluntly at the back. The neck is a separate lighter capsule laid over the shoulder with its whole outline visible against the body, and the snout is a hard-edged cone stuck onto the head with another visible seam. Both ears are flat dark perfect circles. The four legs are tiny thin pegs, far too short and thin to carry that mass — the hind leg is a plain tapered stub with a hard boundary where its upper meets the belly. The dark spots are uniform ellipses of the same size and value spread evenly over the flank, sitting flat on the surface with no curvature falloff, and a thin light stroke traces the top of the back like a drawn contour line.
rows.fix: Break the capsule: narrow the waist, raise the rump, deepen the chest, and either add a tail or terminate the body in a taper. Merge the neck into the chest (shared contour, same fill) and grow the muzzle out of the skull instead of appending a cone. Thicken and lengthen the legs to at least carry the mass, and root them in visible shoulder/hip swellings. Vary spot size and density (denser along the dorsal line, sparse on the belly) and darken/compress them toward the silhouette edge. Remove the topline rim stroke or make it a broken specular, not a continuous outline.

rows.readsAs: a millipede — correct family, but the closed antenna loop makes the front end look like a handle
rows.defect: The overall read is right, but three things are wrong in the pixels. The two antennae do not end — they curve out from the head and MEET, forming one closed hairpin loop hanging off the face. The legs are identical straight unjointed hairs of the same length and thickness, with no coxa, no femur/tibia break and no foot; several along the anterior half start with a visible gap between the hair and the body edge, so they read as detached bristles. The body segments are a stack of identical scallops of near-constant size that do not narrow toward the head or the tail, and the head is an undifferentiated ovoid with a single dot eye — no mandibles, no head capsule. The animal also occupies only about half the frame width and sits well above its shadow, which is a large offset ellipse.
rows.fix: Split the antennae into two independent tapering filaments with free tips and different curves. Give each leg two segments with a knee and a tarsal tip, vary length along the body (shorter at the ends), and anchor every leg so it starts inside the body outline. Taper the segment series so the first and last few are visibly smaller, and give the head a distinct capsule with mandibles or a clypeus. Scale the body up ~35% and sit it on its shadow.

rows.readsAs: a striped goat-antelope with a broom head stuck on its backside
rows.defect: The tail is a household hairbrush, not an organ: a flat cream paddle-lozenge with a hard rounded outline is laid over the rump, and ~40 dead-straight 1px black bristle strokes fan out of it, several of which pass straight THROUGH the paddle rather than out of its edge. Where the paddle meets the rump there is a clean crescent seam — the rump's own rounded end-cap outline is still visible running underneath it. The legs are flat cream rectangles of uniform width with a lighter inner rectangular panel (a visible flat facet) and they butt into the belly at a hard rectangular join with zero shoulder or haunch mass. The head is a small sphere plus a muzzle sphere on a lozenge neck that plugs into the body with a visible rounded terminus. The cream/grey stripes are hard-edged bands clipped straight across the barrel — sprayed on, they do not deform over the hip or the ribs. Large soft cyan glow haloes bleed 30-40px outside the silhouette into the black, reading as camera fog rather than as light coming from the animal.
rows.fix: Replace the tail paddle+bristle-line pass with a tapering tuft built from the body path itself: extend the rump spline into a narrowing stalk, then emit hair as tapered quads (2px root → 0px tip) whose roots are seeded ON the stalk outline, and clip them to never cross back over the stalk. Kill the separate paddle shape entirely. Give the legs a tapered profile (top width 1.8x the hoof) and fair the top 20% of each leg into the belly with a fillet arc so no straight edge terminates at the body outline; delete the inner lighter rectangle. Warp the stripe bands along the body's u/v so they bend over the hip. Drop the outer glow radius by ~60% and clamp glow alpha to the body mask plus a 4px feather.

rows.readsAs: a teal antelope with a bundle of pond weed in its mouth
rows.defect: Same rig as s16 recoloured teal — a batch duplicate. The neck is a uniform-width lozenge whose rounded end-cap is plainly visible sitting ON TOP of the shoulder (clear in the head crop: the tube's own outline crosses the body outline). The corkscrew horns are tan on a teal animal and are cut off flat at the skull surface — no pedicle, no boss, no colour transition, they read as two plastic parts pushed into a hole. The face is blank: two 3px dark dots for eyes with no sclera or lid, and no mouth at all. The whiskers are a fan of straight teal lines plus dark triangular wedges radiating from a single point at the snout tip — they read as a tuft of grass held in the mouth, not as vibrissae. The rear of the body simply tapers to a sharp cone with no tail and no haunch, so the animal appears to be leaking backwards to a point. The dark bars are airbrushed vertical smudges hovering over the teal, clipped at the silhouette.
rows.fix: Merge the neck into the torso with a union/metaball pass so no cap outline survives, and flare the neck base to ~1.6x its mid width. Grow the horns from a raised pedicle painted in the body colour, ramping to horn tan over the first 15% of length. Give the eye a scleral disc plus lid so it reads at 440px, and add a mouth line. Reduce whisker count to 5-6, root them at separate points along the muzzle side (not one shared vertex), and taper them. Either terminate the rump in a rounded haunch or attach an actual tail; a bare cone is neither. Sample the bar pattern in body-space so it wraps.

rows.readsAs: a teal Dimetrodon-llama with a bottlebrush for a tail
rows.defect: The dorsal sail is pasted on, not grown: it is a flat translucent fan with a HARD straight bottom edge cutting across the back, and its support ribs are perfectly straight 1px lines that overshoot the membrane — at the sail's leading edge three ribs continue past the membrane outline into empty black space. The membrane is a different material from the skin (glassy blue-grey against matte teal) with no transition band. The neck is again a constant-diameter tube whose rounded end is visible lying over the shoulder. The ears are teardrops with inner teardrops that float slightly clear of the skull with a gap at the base. The dark blotches are soft airbrushed clouds sprayed on the surface — they have no edge, no scale structure, and they stop dead at the silhouette. The tail is the same detached bristle-brush as s16. Morphologically this is the same rig as fauna-h2-s5 in this batch with a different palette.
rows.fix: Clip ribs strictly to the membrane path and taper them (3px at the base, 0 at the tip) so none escape the sail. Replace the straight bottom edge with a spline that dips INTO the back and share the skin gradient for the lower 25% of the sail so the membrane emerges from the dorsal ridge. Root the ears inside the skull silhouette with a filleted base. Give the blotches a defined edge with a 1px darker rim so they read as pigment cells rather than airbrush. Same tail rebuild as s16. Push the palette/proportion further from s5 (longer neck or shorter sail) so the two are not siblings.

rows.readsAs: a blurry pink-fringed mushroom or a small tree — nobody would call it an animal
rows.defect: This is filed as fauna and it renders as flora — a mauve mushroom or broccoli tree: a scalloped, pink-rimmed canopy over a trunk that splays into 4-5 stubby root-toes at the ground. There is no head, no face, no limb, nothing animal. Three solid pink discs sit in empty black space to the lower-right of the body, completely detached from any surface — the topmost has a dark ring around it and reads as an eye that has fallen off; the other two are pure off-body artifacts. The trunk is a perfectly straight-sided rectangular bar at a 20-degree tilt — a machined primitive with no taper and no root flare where it meets the canopy or the ground. The whole render is heavily blurred and sits at extremely low contrast against the background: the silhouette never resolves and there is no crisp edge anywhere in the image.
rows.fix: First decide the kingdom — if this row is fauna, route it away from the canopy/trunk generator entirely. Delete the three free-floating discs, or constrain the eye/spot emitter to sample points inside the body mask before placing. Replace the straight trunk bar with a tapered spline that flares at both ends into the canopy and the root pad. Raise the base albedo lightness by roughly 25% and add a rim light so the silhouette separates from the near-black background, and drop the blur radius so the canopy scallops read as structure rather than as a soft blob.

rows.readsAs: a blue toy stegosaurus-llama with five thumbs sticking up behind its back
rows.defect: The dorsal spines are behind the body, not part of it. At 3x you can see the torso's top outline running as an unbroken stroke UNDERNEATH all five spines, and each spine is a rounded-top lozenge in a lighter blue than the back — they read as five thumbs poking up from behind the animal. The torso itself is a capsule: parallel top and bottom edges with rounded caps, exactly the silhouette this engine is not supposed to produce. The markings are hollow white-outline rhombi with no fill, all at the same orientation and the same scale, and they do not foreshorten or bend over the barrel or the shoulder — pure decals. The legs are flat slabs with hard rectangular joins into the belly. The tail is a thin straight stick with a bulb on the end, attached at a hard notch.
rows.fix: Build the spines as part of the dorsal path — offset the back spline upward at each spine location and re-solve one continuous outline so there is no stroke passing beneath them — and fill them with the body gradient, not a separate lighter tone. Break the capsule: vary the torso radius along its length (deeper chest, narrower waist, rising hip) so top and bottom are never parallel. Project the rhombus decals through a body-space UV so they scale and rotate with the surface, and vary size and angle per instance. Fillet the leg tops and taper them. Grow the tail out of the rump with a widening base rather than butting a stick onto a notch.

rows.readsAs: a plush dachshund or a cartoon dog
rows.defect: The neck is a separate capsule lying on top of both the head and the body. At 3x its own rounded end-cap is clearly visible resting on the shoulder, and its lighter blue crosses over the skull as a distinct band — a textbook stuck-on part with a seam at both ends. The torso is a rounded rectangle with parallel top and bottom and blunt round caps; there is no tail, the rear just stops. The legs are four tiny nubs with no articulation. The spot pattern is a regular rectangular GRID of soft dots, evenly spaced in rows and columns, unmistakably sprayed on top rather than being skin — and it is clipped hard where the neck overlaps. Several bright glow dots sit in empty black space below the belly, between the legs, touching nothing.
rows.fix: Union the head, neck and torso into a single solved silhouette before shading, so no cap outline survives anywhere; taper the neck so it is widest at the shoulder. Perturb the torso profile so top and bottom are not parallel, and either add a tail or shape the rear into a haunch. Jitter the spot lattice (position, radius, and per-spot alpha) and drive it from a noise field rather than a grid, and let it continue across the neck instead of being clipped. Constrain the bioluminescent emitters to points inside the body mask so none land in open space; lengthen the legs to roughly 1.5x current so it stops reading as a plush toy.

rows.readsAs: a generic yellow aquarium fish icon
rows.defect: Flat vector clip-art, not a painted organism. The body is a lens — two arcs meeting at hard points at the nose and the tail, a pure geometric primitive. The dorsal and anal fins are opaque flat brown slabs drawn BEHIND the body with straight machined ribs and a hard straight bottom edge that simply disappears under the torso — a hidden seam, no membrane taper, no colour continuity with the skin. The caudal fin is a separate flat brown triangle joined to the body point by a thin sliver, so there is no peduncle and the tail reads as detached. The eye is a perfect white circle containing a perfect black circle, sitting half off the body outline. The pectoral fin is a fan of straight lines radiating from one vertex. The lateral line is a dead-straight 1px white stroke. The spots are soft airbrushed blobs floating over the gradient with no scale structure. On top of all that, the animal occupies only about 40% of the 440px frame and the ground-shadow ellipse floats detached, ~80px below a swimming fish.
rows.fix: Rebuild the body from a spline with a rounded snout and a real caudal peduncle instead of a two-arc lens. Draw fins in front of the body with the skin gradient carried into their first 20%, an alpha ramp toward the trailing edge, and a scalloped rather than straight distal margin; taper the rays and root them inside the body outline. Reshape the eye as a slightly ovoid disc with a highlight and move it fully inboard. Break the lateral line into a dotted, curved scale row. Scale the fish up to roughly 80% of frame width, and either remove the cast shadow for aquatic morphs or attach it directly beneath the ventral line.

rows.readsAs: a spotted sail-backed camel wearing Mickey Mouse ears
